Review: Having eaten at another famous Peranakan place that was a great disappointment, my girlfriends and I tried J Manis and were very happy with our choice.Awesome awesome food!The Kueh pie tees are a must order.A tad bit on the pricey side however for its authenticity and great taste, it was well worth it!Show less

Author: rain498Singapore, Singapore
Title: Best Chendol in Melaka! (in our opinion)
Review: On this visit, we wanted to try out a new peranakan restaurant and randomly picked Manis J. The place was cosy and comfy as per other Peranakan restaurant. Diners would likely be regulars or the occasional tourists like us.There was a table of foreign friends and they seemed to have a local guide who was sharing with them the use of spices and the history of Peranakan food etc. Didn't mean to eavesdrop but they were seated rather nearby and we were waiting for our food.The prices here are indeed on the high side, so we were cautious with our orders. As usual, we'd order the Ayam Buah Keluak (a must for us when we wanted to try out any Peranakan place), the Chinchalok Omelette, fried fish and kueh pie tee as appetisers.They will serve you crackers while waiting for the food but the belachan cost us extra.Food was decent and for dessert, we tried the chendol. Wow! All of us felt that the chendol was by far the best in town.Show less

Author: yuanhuikKluang, Malaysia
Title: Overrated, overpriced.
Review: Personally I think it is overrated. Over the years I always go another nyonya restaurant which makes me fall in love in nyonya food. Since this restaurant out rated the usual I go, so let me give it a try. Ordered ayam ponteh, fried kangkung (asked to be non spicy so it was fried with garlic only), telur cincaluk and cendol. Ayam ponteh which is my favourite nyonya food is not well presented by them. The gravy is not smooth and not fragrant enough. Don't wan to comment kangkung because the flavour is not what they usually cook. The cendol cost rm5 per bowl. It's really a small bowl. Only telur cincaluk is accepted. There are better nyonya food out there, if you don't stay long at Melaka, probably could skip this.Show less

Author: susan1819Singapore, Singapore
Title: Only for the kids
Review: The serving sizes are large. That’s probably the best thing if you have a large party and are hungry. Good for kids and those who aren’t into spiced food - by that I do not mean spicy hot but the strong fragrance of spices.The dishes were just warm at the table. We ordered Buah Keluak- standard (South) Peranakan dish that I ate growing up & introduced to my Western partner. He loves Buah Keluak more than I do. We found the chicken dry despite being bathed in gravy. The gravy was thin & lacked flavour. The nuts were old as when scooped out they were dry too. The Prawn Lemak Nanas lacked the sweet sour of pineapple but the gravy was thick from the coconut. There were a number of good sized prawns.The Nonya Chap Chye of cabbage, carrot & dried bean curd was another disappointing dish. The main ingredient of taucheo- preserved beans - was missing. So it was neither salty nor sweet nor fragrant. We had cincalok omelette which seemed more like an onion omelette. We ordered sambal belachan - usually the kick on the table for those who like their tongues on fire. Well... the white bloke at my table ate up the whole plate of sambal in the hopes of pepping up his meal and he didn’t break into a sweat. Dishes only look good.The meal cost 116 Malaysian Ringgit- which is pricey for locals. Not recommended.Show less

Author: viking11
Title: Very Good Food
Review: Just had dinner here. The food was delicious and tasted home-cooked. Ordered the ayam buah keluak and the asam fish as well as a few other dishes as well as cendol. My entire family enjoyed the food. Service was also very friendly and quick

Author: 265felih
Title: Decent but that’s it
Review:
We had a quick lunch there. 
It looks like a typical Chinese restaurant (minimal decoration and mostly round tables).

The food was acceptable but not great. Might be OK for someone who has never tasted Peranakan cuisine before, else avoid.

Author: JasmineL1508
Title: Home-styled cooking
Review: My colleague and I visited this delightful home-styled restaurant, just a short 15-mins walk (following Google Maps) from the bustle of Jonker Street. We met Jennifer, the proprietor who explained that this was a venture by her siblings - all of whom have names starting with J! Her family dropped by for dinner, including her matriarch mother who's the holder of Nyonya secret recipes. We joked about how every Nyonya has her own way of cooking, and each is like a piece of culture, handed down from generations. When we tasted the food she recommended for us that evening, it was simply delightful. I hope to return again to try the many other delights she has, and this time to come with a bigger group so we can order more varieties! What we ordered: ngoh hiang 5-spice chicken lobak roll, steamed fish otak-otak, Assam spicy fish curry, spicy fried chicken, nyonya chap chye -- we started with the cendol to cool off from the hot day! There's a little retail corner, and I also bought Gula Melaka (palm sugar) to bring home.Show less

Author: cpr2exssydney
Title: Peranakan food
Review: Was in the area - Jln Bunga Raya - took a recommendation from a friend to go here. He wasn’t wrong - air conditioned venue with a cheerful host - Jennifer - we had the usual Nonya specialities - telur chinchaluk, kangkung belacan, sambal petai and otak. My favourite was the otak- beautifully spiced. Highly recommended. Show less

Author: meichingl2015London, United Kingdom
Title: Not recommended for local people, this is for tourists.
Review: They charges for the prawn cracker that usually served free, they also charges for the plain water which is unexcetable. The service was excellent, but the food was under the expectation. Not recommand for local people who always having Nyonya food since little. This is for tourist people only.Show less

Author: barbarajilloCheltenham, United Kingdom
Title: Another excellent meal in Malaysia
Review: Visited Manis J on the recommendation of the hotel .It’s a local restaurant serving ‘Nonya’ cuisine. The menu was a mixture of words and photos, very helpful for a foreign visitor .The room itself is fairly large and brightly lit reminiscent of a canteen but the food was excellent , very fresh ingredients and quite subtly flavoured . It’s neither pretty nor romantic but it’s interesting to eat with mostly local visitors and although the serving staff had limited English and I embarrassingly had no Malay we worked it out , towards the end of our meal the proprietress appeared and her English was excellent as was the food .Show less

Author: joannegsp
Title: Best Nyonya Recipes i had ever tried in my life
Review: I had tried a few famous nyonya restaurants in Malacaa City but nothing impressed me so far to consider nyonya food in my subsequent food hunting trips till i tried Manis J on 30 Mar 2019. The food is so yummy, the taste is so unique which you cant get it in any other nyonya restaurants (at least i havent found one). If you like mummy home cook dishes, this is the place you must visit as the recipes are all from the mother of the owner, Jennifer. The food are served with the good quality ingredients. The ponteh chicken taste is so unique. All the different types of belacan sambal are so yummy with different level of spiciness. The cendol dessert is served with pure gula melaka and coconut milk till i can't resist to take it as a person who has no sweet tongue and don't take coconut milk. I have not found any cendol with this quality. You cant miss the specialty chicken roll too. I will definitely go back to try the rest of the items in the menu!Show less

Author: Vivien LSingapore, Singapore
Title: underrated peranakan restaurant
Review: The service was very good. the waiter was eager to share how to eat the black nut with us, showed us how to eat it the peranakan way. Food was lovely, ahem, much better than makko, and i enjoyed it a lot. Loved the paitee, ngoh hiang, black nut stew.Show less

Author: CuriousP
Title: Michelin Worthy Paranakan Restaurant
Review: Service is immaculate and attentive. The food is authentic, tasty, fast, and great portion size. The Assam Fish is fragrant and very fresh. Ayam bua keluak has a rich and thick sauce - well cooked. Otak is fragrant without being wet and soggy or full of red colourings. The Ngoh Hiang can tastes all the 5 spices and comes crispy and fresh. The fried rice is well done and even has fresh prawns. The creme de la creme is none other than the famous Chendol - it’s better than all the ones we have tasted in Malacca. This restaurant is super clean and looks super newFor those who find this restaurant just ok or not up to their standards; well it’s perhaps a matter of personal preference, because the number of people who rated this restaurant with excellent reviews far outweigh the one or two negative reviews. Show less

Author: bhavani3001
Title: Nice prenakan food
Review:
The fried rice was good and the sambal Kang kong. The fried fish was a bit overcooked, so I won’t recommend it. But the sambal sauce on it was really good.
My friend had the chendol which she said was excellent.

Author: nooreyepixtravelJohor Bahru, Malaysia
Title: Excellent Food and Great Service !
Review: We were greeted immediately as we came in. Owner recommended 2 dishes . The Buah Keruak with Chicken was a new dish for us and it was very well prepared and tastes great! I love the Spicy Fish . The drink was delightful. I had Chendol and Wife had Sago. Both desserts were nice. Thank you for your kind hospitality and great food!Show less

Author: mpmilestogo
Title: Great food!
Review: Came here after a few recommendations to try the nyonya food. Very good. Just the right amount of food and it’s nice to eat in a restaurant after a few days in hawker centers.

Author: MattheusAltoDen Hoorn, The Netherlands
Title: Hectic but nice
Review: Dinner for 4During Chinese new year is a challenge. Had to wait in line for a while. The manager was great she was the only one with a little bit of order in the organized chaos. Food was very nice. Had 3 different types of shrimps. Vegetables were good but not super.Show less

Author: JC LAjax, Canada
Title: A Gem - Delicious Food and Top Notch Service
Review: Arrived with my family on a busy Friday night and all tables were full. Jennifer promptly informed us that we could wait for a specific table where the patrons were almost done eating. She also informed us that we could place our order while waiting. This was an excellent option as we were almost immediately served with our order upon being seated. This is perhaps the best run restaurant in Malacca with a high level of cleanliness. The food was extremely delicious, probably the best overall Nyonya food in Melaka. The staff was extremely courteous and professional. What a pleasant experience. We will definitely be back!Show less

Author: stevekyne
Title: A find
Review: It’s as good as everyone says.  Food is awesome, service excellent, and the owner Jennifer is a true professional. This is a find, and we will be returning.  Thank you!

Author: sherbst99
Title: Delicious Peranakan - Totally Satisfying!
Review: By far the best dining experience we had in Malaysia.Jennifer and Jimmy are the kind and welcoming hosts of this authentic family-run Nyonya restaurant in Melaka. The recipes are all handed down - generation to generation - and are made with care and love as part of the families’ cultural heritage.We tried the Ayam Buah Keluak (chicken in curry gravy with whole-cooked keluak nut - rich in flavour and a week in the preparation); Assam Fish (whole fish stewed in tamarind and turmeric gravy, served with okra); Otak-Otak (home made fish cake, steamed in banana leaf); and the light and creamy Sago Pudding (soft tapioca pearls with coconut milk, red bean and palm sugar syrup).Every dish was near perfect, with fresh ingredients and a homestyle richness to the cooking - bursting with flavours. The Otak-Otak was soft and fluffy - easily the best fish cake I’ve ever tasted, and the Sago Pudding will have you returning for a second helping.The restaurant is tastefully decorated with family heirlooms and also featured a variety of yummy hand-made produce from the kitchen (we couldn't resist the palm sugar syrup!). I liked the touch of regional music, which enhanced the meal and made for a relaxing atmosphere.You will love it - just be prepared to return again and again. Thank you Jennifer and Jimmy!Show less

Author: Addy_L_22
Title: One of the BEST Peranakan Restaurants in Melaka!
Review: Ok, so you're in Melaka and you HAVE to try out the local cuisine. Melaka is super well known for their Peranakan (Straits-born) cuisine. Honestly, there are so many restaurants for you to choose from. We've tried many of these and Manis J comes out top. The food tastes so close to home-cooked food, just like grandma's kitchen. It is made with care and love (definitely can taste it in the food!). A must try is the chicken tempra (chicken in vinegar sauce) and the fried fish with chili. It is delicious and it brought me back to my childhood when my grandma cooked these dishes for dinner.This is the restaurant you want to go for your first try in Peranakan food! (Good to call and make a reservation as they can be quite packed during the peak meal times)Show less

Author: Aldert VSouthsea
Title: Superb
Review: We wanted to eat local food and came across this restaurant. It was superb. The signature dish (fish with a spicy paste) was off the planet, so was the prawn curry. And the vegetables in a prawn paste were also special. Although we were already satisfied perhaps the best dish came at the end: the dessert. We tried two and both were superb, one contained ice with a syrup based on palm sugar. We had no experience with this type of food but it did not matter. Jimmy, who I believe is the owner, helped us choosing the dishes. I definitely will go back to this restaurant for my next visit Show less

Author: RuaidahIPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Awesome Peranakan Cuisine!
Review: We were craving for authentic peranakan cuisine and hence, we googled the good restaurants available in Bandar Melaka. This restaurant popped up and so we decided to give it a shot! And boy....we sure glad we did!There were not too many people when we arrived, and we were given a table pretty fast. Score 1!The head waiter (or maybe Manager...) who attended to us politely helped us with our queries when ordering the dishes, friendly guy too...score 2!Next...came the dishes. We ordered chicken, fish, squids, vegetables and the famous Cincalok Omelette...simply delicious! Score 3! We also didn't have to wait that long for our orders...score 4! They have a wide selection on their menu...it was tough choosing the dishes as everything on the menu looked good!The owner....a charming lady came over to our table and asked us how was our meal...and we told her that it was excellent. Score 5 for good customer service!Downpoints?? Well....the parking of course. We parked our car some distance from the restaurant and walked there. However, the awesome food made up for it...kudos!We were very glad we decided to dine here...will recommend to friends, and also will come again! Also, do make a reservation...just in case, so as not to be disappointed.Show less

Author: angelabraccoburnsLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Authentic and delicious nonya food
Review: This excellent nonya restaurant became our go-to local dining haven during a week-long stay in Melaka (staying in Ramada Plaza). Over several visits we 'ate the menu' and each dish was lovely! Especially enjoyed the Sambal fish (Ikan Sambal) and their chicken dish prepared with a local nut (Ayam Buah Keluak).Show less

Author: 253denc
Title: Delicious & Reasonable
Review: Lunched here about 1pm. Service was fast but not rushed. Food was good, better than quite a few other Nyonya eateries in town. Tried and recommends - ponteh chick, asam fish & cendol.

Author: Silverstone90Singapore, Singapore
Title: Visited due to the high rating
Review: We tried three of the recommended dishes which are the chicken, udang and cendol. It took a while to serve and hence he were expecting something hot but unfortunately, it’s a bit disappointed. 2 of us spent about RM95 and it’s really full. We found udang and kangkung were nice, the cendol portion is a bit too small even for one person. Show less

Author: food_travels68
Title: Great Noya Fix
Review:
Traveled to Melaka with family, found the food here great and flavorsome. Service is friendly even when busy made every table feel they were the only people there.
Will go back, no room for the cendel and sago so after reading reviews need to try.

Author: makanagin
Title: Nice Ambience, Authentic Food
Review:
Found this relatively new outlet . Nice ambience with Peranakan artifacts and soft music.
Food quite authentic.  We had Udang Nenas Lemak, Ayam Buah Keluak and Chendol for deserts.
Beware the portions are quite large meant for 2 to 4 persons.

Author: FarAway46140947472
Title: Excellent Peranakan food with good ambience
Review: Very nice and friendly staff. During my recent visit we ordered Ayam Buah Keluak, udang nanas lemak and chendol. Their standard portions were large meant for 3 to 4 persons. So it would be a challenge for 2 of us. In fact we had to pack some of the food we were unable to finish.Quality of food is excellent. Price reasonable : about MYR70+ for 2 persons. The peranakan design setup and soft peranakan music enhance the ambience and dinning experience. Show less

Author: tylerl964
Title: Malaysian Vacation
Review: The food was delicious and the service was excellent. If you're in Melaka then you definitely need to visit the restaurant!

Author: YusnitaA7
Title: It’s allright
Review: Nice place. Clean and cozy. Good service. The food is allright. Cendol is awesome! Would come again for the cendol 🙂

Author: ritzr2017Singapore, Singapore
Title: Good Flavours
Review: Have dinner at this place and service was very personalised. Host was super pleasant and ensured the taste and experience was as expected. Place is clean and food was excellent: tasty and yummy. We ordered fish assam pedas and prawn lemak : food was fresh and delicious. The chap chye and brinjal was good too. Great ambience. The chilli garam dish was good too. Reasonably priced. To top it off: luvly desert. I will recommend this place anyday. A sure revisit.Show less

Author: doublescore27
Title: Not bad but needs to catch up
Review:
The quality of food is not bad. Service is good, better than other nyona restaurants in Melaka.

However, the prices are considerably higher than other well known, and more established, nyona restaurants in Melaka.

Author: Doreen KMalaysia
Title: Delicious authentic nonya fare in Malacca
Review: My husband and I wanted to try authentic nonya food during out recent trip to Malacca so we were delighted we found Manis J Nonya Restaurant! Since it was only a 2 min walk from our hotel Ramada Plaza Melaka we decided to check it out on the 1st night of our visit to Malacca. We had made a reservation for a table for 2 persons at 8pm and we were really thankful we did as the restaurant was full when we arrived. Jimmy came to take our order and we were pleasantly surprised it did not take too long for our food to arrive. We had the Prawn Curry with pineapple, Nonya Chap Chye (mixed vegetables), Otak-otak and Ngoh Hiang (a type of meat roll). We both agreed the lemak prawn curry was the best!! We wanted to try the chicken dish, Ayam Buah Keluak, but Jimmy thought the portion would be too big for the 2 of us so we told ourselves we would have to come back the next day for it!The next day we went back to Manis J again for lunch! This time we brought 2 friends along! We ordered the Ayam Buah Keluak, Sambal Prawn with Petai, Fried squid (sotong) and Sambal four angle beans. Jimmy told us that the Ayam Buah Keluak recipe was from Jennifer's grandmother and also shared with us how they prepare the buah keluak for cooking. He also showed us how to dig out the black contents of the buah keluak and mix it into our rice. It was delicious! We also enjoyed the other dishes and finally a bowl of yummy Cendol was the perfect dessert to finish the meal!Manis J is a lovely nonya restaurant with a nice ambience and friendly staff! Thank you Jimmy and Jennifer for 2 wonderful meals! We hope to be back some day!!Show less

Author: Jenny L
Title: Great nyonya restaurant and best cendol ever
Review: Had dinner there with 5 other friends. Very good selection of food at reasonable prices. We ordered 7 or 8 dishes but favourites were assam fish, prawns petai sambal, chicken buah keluak and cendol and sago for dessert. All of the food was finger licking good and the taste was authentic. The cendol was heavenly !!! This delectable dessert was elevated to heavenly heights by the freshest coconut milk and the intensely favourful gula melaka drizzled on it. A bottle of the gula melaka was put on the table for us to add as much as we liked and it was half finished in record time. Service was great too. The owner, Ms Jennifer, dropped by to chat with us. She was most friendly and gracious and even gave us complimentary servings of sago, which was so yummy. All in, a great dining experience ! Highly recommended.Show less

Author: adrian0714Singapore, Singapore
Title: A great find- Highly recommended, must try
Review: We had lunch yesterday and, personally, we rate it to be one of the best Nonya restaurant in Melaka. We ordered ikan cili garam, sambal petai udang, ngoh hiang, kuih pai tee, nonya chap chai, telur cincaluk, terung tempra and cendol and sago for desserts. Except for the kuih pai tee which needs improvement, the rest of the dishes were excellent. Jimmy, our host, was very hospitable and informative with his suggestions. All in all, a very positive experience and Manis J is definitely the new kid on the block, which is going to give the other more established joints a run for the money. Kudos and keep up the standards.Show less

Author: JimmyKLLangkawi, Malaysia
Title: Yummy,....Just Yummy with reasonable price
Review: Was staying at the Pines hotel to watch Encore Malacca, the restaurant is only 600m walk away. Mr. Jimmy greeted us and we asked if he is the owner since the name of the restaurant has an initial J. He explained, J came from the names of the owner's children, and him Jimmy has a "JOB".Jimmy who shared with us the restaurant best dishes and we ordered fried four angle beans, blanched Ockra and lada garam chicken and lemak udang and nenas. Excellent food and we had a feast. Yummy the food served were fresh and simply spectacular. For dessert, the sago with coconut cream and sugar is a must! We vowed to return again to try the other dishes. The best meal in malaccaShow less

Author: 522cheey
Title: Dinner with my wife. The place is easily found.
Review: Very good selection of baba food in Melaka city Centre. Love the Assam fish and prawn nanas lemak. The price is very reasonable and great service too.

Author: cherlyne88Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Very homely
Review: Celebrated my mother's birthday here and we were delighted when Jimmy's wife bright red birthday eggs out for all of us. It was a very sweet gesture. The food was very tasty and felt like home. The portion of dishes are small which allows you to try a few dishes without having to worry about over ordering. A simple dish (excluding seafood) is between RM20 - 30. Definitely worth a visit. I highly recommend their pineapple prawn dish.Show less

Author: CarolineCHeePuchong, Malaysia
Title: One of the Best Nyonya cuisine in town!
Review: It’s only 600m walk from The Pines Hotel and we were greeted by Mr. Jimmy who shared with us the restaurant best dishes. The food served were fresh and simply spectacular. Yum. For dessert, the sago with coconut cream and sugar is a must! We vowed to return again to try the other dishes. Show less

Author: EdwardT1713Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Family lunch
Review: Outstanding Melaka Nyonya cuisine-we had the house signature dishes& we're not disappointed: garam fish,tender Lady fingers vwith sambal, pineapple & prawn curry and subtly chincalok infused ommelette -went delicious with rice.Add to that the excellent & warm hospitality from Jimmy and Jennifer who were patient & gracious in making us welcome as friends. Their version of chendol surpassed that of the tourist traps of Jonkers Street. This is Nyonya food gem and ranks amongst the best of Nyonya in Malaysia.Show less

Author: sweetaftonSingapore, Singapore
Title: A real gem.
Review: We were looking for another nyonya restaurant other than the usual suspects which have become too commercialized, too crowded, too expensive, too touristy.Our tour driver found this place which opened 2 years ago, run by a group of 5 siblings whose names all begin with J, (hence the restaurant's name Manis J)and with a menu influenced by their mum's recipes.The food was authentic; service was excellent, helpful, prompt . Jimmy Choo was the customer service guy, although he is not family. Jennifer Ngiow was the boss lady.We ordered the usual favourites - buah keluak, assam fish, sambal bendi, gulai pineapple, and a host of others. Desserts that day were either chendol or sago with gula melaka and coconut milk. So yummy  Besides food, the restaurant also sells Peranakan themed handicrafts, inexpensive and sold for a good cause - to support single mums and their families. All the handicrafts were produced by those mums. On sale also were jars of condiments and ready made gula melaka syrup, plus some dried goods for Peranakan cooking. All these also for a good cause.The location was in a quieter part of town. There were 9 of us and we all had a fantastic meal. Fully recommended. We hope success will not make this restaurant go the way of the other too commercialized Peranankan restaurants.Show less

Author: funtraveller989North Yorkshire, United Kingdom
Title: Malaysian Hospitality at its best
Review: We had a family dinner and it happened to be my sister in laws birthday. The food was amazing . Jimmy and his wife were so hospitable. Since it was a birthday ocassion, they served us some boiled red egg, a forgotten tradition. A thoughtful gesture. Definitely a great finding away from the normal tourist trail.Show less

Author: Tennis_Fan123Singapore, Singapore
Title: The most lovely host and owner Jennifer made our dining experience at this quaint Nonya restaurant a wonderful one.
Review: Delicious dishes sampled:Ayam buah kluak, prawn with petai & sambal - spicy & fresh, kangkung belacan, egg with cincalok, and desserts Cendol & Sago Pudding. The chicken were tender and the prawns were very fresh! I really liked the cendol wasn’t too sweet and the red beans in the sago pudding adds a nice texture. A wonderful and clean restaurant to enjoy with friends and family !Show less

Author: Gary FShah Alam, Malaysia
Title: One of the best nyonya food
Review: An upmarket nyonya restaurant serving authentic nyonya food. Prawn sambal with petai is not to spicy and the prawn ls was fresh and cooked to perfection. The lobak is firm and delicious. The lemon grass chicken was a little dry. Cendol was fantastic with additional gula Melaka. Overall the best nyonya food in town.Show less

Author: jacqqqNCL / KUL
Title: We Found A New All Time Favourite
Review: We wanted to save the best for our last day in Melaka. Intended destination was a nyonya kitchen we frequented on all our previous trips. But horror of all horrors. It was closed on that day. Our backup plan was only open for dinner.We decided to break our habit and look for an alternative. My only criteria - good, old fashion nyonya food. None of the fusion nor toned down crap.Yessssssss. And we found just the place in Manis J !!!! So happy !!Ordered the itik tim (the way grandma would have loved it), asam fish (excellent), turmeric chicken, sambal kangkung and sago gula Melaka. Every dish was flavourful.Jimmy, the host, was very accommodating. Couldn’t help but ordered a takeaway of their sambal belacan (hand pounded, no less, and smelled gloriously of belacan). They also sell bottles of their homemade cincalok.I always get asked for recommendations and this one is definitely on my list now.Show less

Author: bucketlisttravellersSydney, Australia
Title: Fine dining nyonya cuisine
Review: This is an upmarket nyonya restaurant with a very welcoming owner. We came here at about 1:30pm for lunch on a Saturday. It wasn’t too busy when we got there so the food came out very quickly. However by the time we left the place was packed. It seems to be quite popular with family groups out for a nice meal.The restaurant is nicely presented and has air conditioning. The tabletops are made from marble and are very nice looking.We were shown to a table and given a basket of crackers called tidbits. In our home country some restaurants sometimes give you bread or crackers for free, but please note that this is not the case in Malaysia. If you eat it they will charge you for it. If you don’t want it you can send it away and you won’t be charged.The owner gave us menus and recommended dishes for us to eat. We had a half and half serving of Otak otak and ngoh hiang, the Kuah pai tee and Ayam Ponteh. The Kuah pai tee was absolutely delicious and pretty as a picture. The Otak Otak and nigh hiang were also really good. We found the ayam ponteh quite mild, but it was a good serving size and came with rice. The meal came to 51 ringgit. They accept cash or credit card, however you need to spend a minimum of 100 ringgit in order to use credit card. We have usually found the minimum spend to be 50 ringgit in other restaurants, so this minimum seemed a bit high to us.Overall this was a very enjoyable dining experience with great hosts and a relaxing atmosphere. This is a great place to come to treat yourself.Show less

Author: BatmanSupermanHong Kong
Title: Excellent, just fantastic!
Review: We have been visiting Malacca regularly and always enjoyed the Peranakan food. Ole Sayang was our favourite for many years but recently new Peranakan restaurants have appeared. We discovered Manis J while walking along the street and decided to try. We were blown away by the great tasting food and the menu. Simply wonderful! This restaurant serves authentic Peranakan fare with their grandma recipe if you know what I mean. That is the X factor that differentiates the good and the really awesome. The service staff Jimmy is very knowledgeable about the menu, he will recommend the best dishes. They also has a corner where the restaurant help support the single women who hand made some of the Peranakan handicrafts for sale. These are great gifts and souvenirs which includes bags, toilet roll holders, tissue box covers, fans etc. All in Peranakan patterns. All proceeds from the sale goes to the single women. Pay in cash though and the bill is separated for the food bill. That is community service with a heart! Therefore this restaurant with its fantastic and authentic Peranakan recipes and its heart for the helping their community win me over as the best Peranakan restaurant in Malacca. It is the new crown jewel of restaurants!Show less

Author: hausofyueneSingapore, Singapore
Title: Lovely restaurant, just that food service is a little slow
Review: The partner and I originally wanted to eat at a nearby nasi kandar stall, but somehow ended up wandering down the road and stumbled upon this restaurant by accident. We'd hoped at some point in our trip to eat some Nyonya cuisine, so it was quite fortuitous. The reviews online were mostly glowing, with the main gripe being the slow service when it came to serving the food.I'm here to say, yes, they are all accurate. We arrived around 8.20pm, nearing the end of the night, and waited till 8.50pm for our food to be served. Be very prepared for a long wait, especially on weekends, when the restaurant is filled with big groups! The service is by table, so they won't cook up your meal until they're done with the previous table's order.Was the wait worth it?OH HELL YES.We ordered the cincalok omelette, nenas udang, sambal kangkong, and otak. By gum, all of them were awesome. My partner especially loved the cincalok omelette and the otak, and I fell head over heels for the nenas udang. Everything was flavorful, the portions generous, and even after 25 minutes of eating, the sambal kangkong was still piping hot. We thoroughly enjoyed ourselves, especially since I had previously eaten rather disappointing Nyonya food in Melaka on another trip many years ago. The only thing which looked small in portion was the cendol, which a neighbouring table had ordered. They weren't kidding when they said the portion was SMALL.The wait staff was also very nice and apologetic about the long wait. Seems like the place is very popular with locals celebrating birthdays (there were 3 tables all celebrating that night!) and turns out that the towkay neo, Jennifer, will prepare a special treat for the table if they're informed beforehand that there's a birthday boy/girl in the house. Nice touch!Everything came up to about RM99, which is around S$33; pretty worth it, in my opinion. I've eaten smaller portions of (admittedly very good) Nyonya food in Singapore for waaaaay more coin. So yes, very much worth the wait, so be patient, and you'll be rewarded with a great meal. Pro tip: try to come around 8.45pm instead, as a Dutch family came in around that time, and because most of the tables had already been served, they did get their food a bit faster (maybe 15-20 minutes instead of 30 minutes?). Try to avoid the peak dinner crowd. Thanks Jennifer, Jimmy and the staff for a wonderful meal; we will certainly be back again.Show less

Author: JeanWNSingapore, Singapore
Title: A lucky find.
Review: Found this Resturant totally by accident. We wondered the area around the Swiss Garden Hotel. Turned the corner and spotted the resturant Manis J. Didn’t order much, rice with ayam buah keluak and chap chye, went down well. As we shared one serving of rice we managed to keep space for dessert. Sago gula melaka and chendol were a superb “chuchi mulut” (amuse buche) in French, really crowned our feast. Show less

Author: Ilya K
Title: Great food
Review: We ordered a few dishes like fried chicken, asam pedas senangin, ladys fingers and sambal udang petai. All food is serve fresh and mert my expectation in terms of its taste. I had a great time with great food :)

Author: Jo22luvTravel
Title: Authentic Nyonya food 👍
Review: The service is good & the lady boss took time to explain their cuisine. Food portion and servings were ok. The ambience was good. Restaurant was located on the main road and easy to find.  Recommended 👍

Author: qi_123singapore
Title: Wonderful food and warm quality service!
Review: Dinner here with my extended family on 9 June and had the most wonderful experience! Called an hour in adv almost expecting to be rejected if it was full, but the lady host Jennifer, was so kind to squeeze us a table and advising us to come early so our kids (2 babies etc) would not be too hungry. Food was delicious, Assam fish was fresh, and the kids thoroughly enjoyed the fishball soup. Service was prompt and friendly, we were always greeted with courteous smiles. Overall a lovely traditional Nonya restaurant in a great location.. just remember to go early before 7 and to book in advance to avoid the crowd! Thumbs up!Show less

Author: jelicias2015
Title: Long wait for the food but overall ok
Review: We went on a Saturday where the restaurant was very packed. We didn’t do much research and just went to a nyonya restaurant near our hotel. We waited about 15min for a table and also 30min for the food. The fried egg and chendol are nice. The rest are average. I wouldn’t come here again to wait 45min for a meal. Show less

Author: KelLy L
Title: 5 Stars Service
Review:
The staff (uncle Jimmy) very friendly, service thumb up 👍

All dishes portion are big except for cendol. Sambal chilli are great !

Author: ChangKaHinkSandakan, Malaysia
Title: The food was interesting...
Review: Firstly, the service! Waiter was very hospitable and warm to us, from opening the door to asking us how the food was.Secondly, the food! It was quite good, and interesting as it was a baba-nyonya restaurant. The salty-sweet ayam ponteh is really a recommended dish to have, as its gravy is quite appetising! The asam fish was alright, sufficient but not much taste of the sourness and lemongrass in it... But the appetiser, kueh that looks like a hat was also great to try out! Other than that, the cencaluk omelette was quite good!Lastly, we had chendol for dessert, which sadly was quite a small bowl compared to its price, so not really worth it as you can a much larger bowl on the streets. Show less

Author: Gui Hua Y
Title: Lovely Nyonya Food
Review: We were searching for a good nyonya restaurant in Malacca but everyone we asked gave us disappointing replies. "There is no more quality nyonya food in Malacca anymore." Luckily, we met a local friend who introduced us to this restaurant. Manis J. We searched it in google and went there for dinner. The nyonya food was good and we were really happy because we have not tried good peranakan food for many years. Jimmy was a great host introducing the dishes that suit to our likes and dislikes. The price was reasonable because we ordered seafood. I would love to have the good old peranakan dishes with pork but it is impossible now. I will probably need to crash into a peranakan home to have that. Haha.Show less

Author: TessahoSydney, Australia
Title: Genuine Nonya cuisine with warm hospitality
Review: We were treated to a delicious Nonya dinner of kangkong belachan, chicken curry and Sambal prawn which were exceptional in that the taste was genuinely home style. Jimmy looked after us beautifully and was delighted when I showed him the reviews on Tripadvisor which mentioned him: he showed them to the owner Jennifer Ngiow who explained how her mother taught all the children how to cook the traditional way. To taste genuine Nonya food in Melaka, this is the place to go to.Show less

Author: 585rolfbGrand Rapids, Michigan
Title: Quality Nyonya cuisine
Review: Good variety of Nyonya dishes on the menu, staff is very helpful in explaining the dishes. Dishes are very tasty and nicely presented. Restaurant is not too big and run as family business giving impression guests are being cared of. Interior decoration is on the spartanic side and restaurant is a bit bare when only few guests are present. Good value for good quality of food. Location is a short walk away from commercialized Jonker Street.Show less

Author: AnnemiekeT19
Title: Manis J excellent restaurant
Review: Traveling with my parents and husband in Melaka. We had a very nice dinner at Manis J. Although we ordered too many dishes. we finished them all. Friendly and attentive staff.

Author: thevisionofying
Title: Wonderful place to enjoy Nyonya food.
Review: You must visit it! Good food with nice service and SUPER clean toilet ( I was surprised with that because It was the most clean toilet I met in Malaysia) haha..

Author: TheWoody
Title: Good Nyonya food in Malacca
Review: Asked a friend in Malacca about good nyonya food and she recommended this place. The food here is very authentic and good. A must try desert is the chendol. Highly recommended and will come again. As for the price is above average.

Author: JoshChuiSingapore, Singapore
Title: Very Delicious food served
Review: It was an accidental find cos more than often I am disappointed with Nyonya food. We ordered Ayam goreng, asam fish, Ngoh Hiang, fried egg, lady's fingers, sambal prawns with petai , chap chye and Chendol. Everything was perfect but the sambal for the lady's finger is not hot. The Chendol was so yummy. Will definitely come back again. Show less

Author: eka c
Title: Tourist
Review: MUST TRY if you finding Nyonya food at Melacca ! Asam Prawn , Cendol is a MUST !!! Everything is just so delicious ! Lady boss super friendly

Author: ck kSingapore
Title: Monday lunch At Manis
Review: Was leaving Malacca on a Monday so thought we'd try (again) to give the Nonya food in Melaka a chance. Googled and saw this nearest to our location. Went for it. Positives - parking is not difficult along the roadnear to Swiss Garden hotel clean place the ayam bakaluak was a winner, authentic enoughNegatives staff not very personal, cold AC and cold servicefood quality average food quantity per serving is a little lackingShow less

Author: JAshraff
Title: Delicious Nyonya Food in Malacca
Review: The food and service were superb.  Special thanks to Jimmy for his in depth knowledge of the menu. Particularly recommended is chicken with keluak. Delicious.

Author: Catherinas L
Title: No halal certificate
Review: We asked whether halal or not, they said its halal and many malay people came. I'm not sure whether they understand about halal or not, or just simply want business. I hope they respect muslim who wants to try the food there and provide halal cert. They keep asking us to shift table, because they prioritise tour group. The price is quite expensive total around RM70 if you order a main dish, kangkung and side dish only. Overall the food is not bad but it is not that addictive as you wont feel like want to come again.Show less

Author: chiewhoon
Title: Good nyonya food near our hotel
Review: We found this restaurant within walking distance from our hotel. The waiter Jimmy was very helpful.  Since we were a large group of 13, we were able to try many of the dishes and choose non-spicy dishes for the children in our group.

Author: Karene HVancouver, Canada
Title: Good food good service
Review: The wait staff here were very attentive and hospitable.The one who took our order offered recommendations, especially seeing we had a young child with us, made sure we had something suitable for him. We enjoyed our meal very much although we would have preferred babi pongteh, I believe this restaurant is halal so they only serve Ayam pongteh, which we ordered and found it sufficiently delicious. My child enjoyed the heepiow soup whilst my favourite was the chapchye.All in all a pleasant experience and would recommend. Show less

Author: Resh_8Klang, Malaysia
Title: Ok food, slow service
Review: We went there abt 2,30 pm for lunch and got a table after waiting awhile. Order was taken quickly but the main dishes arrived abt 20 mins after the rice and appetiser was served. The rice was already coldby then. The fish took the longest tp arrive. They should really improve on this.Show less

Author: Vince-HelenaSingapore, Singapore
Title: Authentic Peranakan Food
Review: Came by this restaurant because it was round the corner from our hotel and we were too lazy to go any further. We were not dissapointed.We ordered ayam buah keluak, chap chye and ngoh hiang. Serving was BIG. 2 of us struggled to finish the food. Food was tasty although we have had better (to our taste) peranakan food. We enjoyed the dinner.Must find some place in your stomach for the desserts. We had the chendol and sago melaka. It was fantastic. Not too sweet and abolutely heavenly. It is so much better than the other chendol stores along Jonker St.Price was reasonable and service was great.Show less

Author: Jean M
Title: Good food takes time to cook
Review: Nice and cosy and environment and the food is top notch in malacca, Beats those in Jonker street, but service is rather slow so make sure you buffer some time for your meal. Highly recommended

Author: LaurenceHay45
Title: AVERAGE
Review: The food is average, slightly better than the other Nyonya Restaurant. Their setback is there is no parking space.Serene atmosphere.

Author: ongkoks2008Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Visiting one of the Unesco World Heritage Site
Review: The most fascinating & exciting place to visit in Malacca is the Jonker Street, the Famosa Fort & the River Cruise(night ride). But of course after all these activities, it is a must that tourists should try to taste the signature local nyonya foods gourmet. My favourite pick restaurant will be none other than the Manis J. This restaurant ambience is cozy, clean & comfortable. The foods were of course quite unique & tasty couple with spiciness(optional) and you could finish off with the local favourite desert called 'cendol'.Show less

Author: kaysa1911

We choose a lot for trying out.

Very deliciouse. This was a great new taste. 
All dishes that they recordmended have been very good.
Shrimp Curry!  
Dessert: Cendol

Author: Thomas T
Title: Always visit whenever we are in melaka
Review:
This restaurant serves authentic peranakan food (straits settlement). The matriach drops in ocassionally to inspect in the quality.

Author: rlsh07
Title: Not good ayam pongteh
Review:
We ordered the following items 

- pie tee , each order comes with 4 . MYR 6, average. 
- ayam pongteh- MYR 25. The chicken is quite dry. Gravy not much flavor.

Author: alistair15
Title: A good lunch with my family.
Review: Well situated restaurant with good home style nonya cooking. Delicious and authentic. Great food for everyone to enjoy.

Author: egidiom331Glion, Switzerland
Title: Authenticity
Review: What a memorable experience ! First of all, thank you for the recommendation from Leong at the Majestic Malacca. This restaurant is offering genuine Nyonya cuisine. Owners are extremely helpful in recommending their best dishes. Their English is excellent... which helps...! Original recipes are from the grandma; do not hesitate to order Ayam Buah Keluak, à specialty made with local nuts. The taste is close to Nyons olives and the waiter will explain and demonstrate how to eat it. We also enjoyed Kangkung Belacan and Terung Tempra. Those aubergines are ... paradise on earth...! We are tempted to return tomorrow and taste many more of their delicious specialties....!Show less

Author: Flai64Singapore, Singapore
Title: Outstanding Malaccan Nyonya Experience
Review: My wife and I had the most satisfying dinner in Malaka. Every dish we ordered was tantalising, bursting with an array of full on, authentic nonya flavours. Our appetizer was a combination of home made otah & ngo hiang, both of which were delicious - light but flavourful. Then came the main dishes. The ayam buah keluak did not disappoint. Clearly the rempah was superb, stuffed with lots of peranakan spieces. The udang Assam was simply divine. A little sweetness with the tinge of sour prawns just filled our palate. Not to mention the fish goreng with the very special balacan which was delightful. Not too spicy but with lots of punch. We also enjoyed the nonya chap chye which had a great broth. As my wife is peranakan, we agreed that this Malaka style nyonya meal had it's distinctive taste, quite different from the Singapore & Penang style nyonya. The Malaka version is less sweet, more savory with greater intensity on it's rempah & flavours. A wonderful finish to our meal was the two deserts we had: chendol & sago pudding. We've had lots of chendol before but this one topped it all as they used fresh san tan coconut with their own recipe gula melaka which was so fragrant. The lady owner Jenifer and her staff were very warm & friendly. Clearly, she's very passionate about nyonya cuisine & has done lots of research, selecting the best ingredients with her mum's recipes for her restaurant. This is a must try if you are in Malaka. You don't want to miss out on this unique nyonya experience. Show less

Author: AngeCrT
Title: Reheated?
Review: We are not impressed with the food served certainly knew the food was packed up in containers to be heated up then served to the customers. If you are a home cook or a chef as a professional, you will know whether the dishes are prepared on the spot or NOT. If dishes are coming out from the wok, it should be "piping hot" but that wasn't the case. For the price, it is on the high side. Service is okay. Other than that...a rather disappointing experience.Show less

Author: 90chewyJohor Bahru, Malaysia
Title: Authentic Peranakan cuisine
Review: Manis J is not a bad choice if you are looking for authentic peranakan cuisine in Melaka. The taste of ayam buah keluah is very unique and my parents prefer to the lady finger with chili. they love their chili so much. Uncle Jimmy is super friendly and courteous. Look for him if you need their food recommendations.Show less

Author: jeannie wSingapore, Singapore
Title: Good location, good service, good food
Review: We arrived at Manis J Nonya Restaurant around 1.30pm after our long drive from Cameron Highlands. We didn't plan to dine at Manis J that day, actually we're gunning for Teo Soon Loong Restaurant for we've a non-chilli eater amongst us. We soon realised that even if we can fly, we won't make it to Teo Soon Loong for they close at 2pm! So we're very grateful that Manis J opens till 3pm. However we're very pleased to dine here for the food turned out to be very good. They even managed to serve the chilli on the side, so that our "non chilli eater" could enjoy the lunch too. Really appreciate that. We're the only ones there but shortly after more people came. Service is attentive, informative and friendly. We like the decor of the place and it is very clean. Yes, the portions are small and a little of the pricey side, but worth it. Definitely will be back the next time we come into Malacca.Show less

Author: cityangel78
Title: Is just ok.
Review: The food ok lah. The food portion quite small and it quite pricy. The staffs and owner are very friendly.

Author: Adrian BOxford
Title: Perfect
Review: Lovely nyonya food, which was tasty and complex as well as light: much less oil seems to be used than is encountered in some other places, and the result is a delight. Nice people as well (and very clean premises), but it is the really excellent food which makes all the difference.Show less

Author: DavyN46
Title: Sambal belachan
Review: The food was good only that you have to pay extra for the sambal. I expected sambal, chili padi, etc will be the basics to be provided. I must thank Uncle Jimmy for being very attentive to us!

Author: YummySum
Title: Sweet Memory at Manis Nyonya
Review:
Food is excellently tasty, service is good.
Tasty authentic nyonya food, good ambience is good, location is excellent and walking distance from Madam King's department stall.

Author: ChrisKurtGabelLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Wonderful evening meal - a must go to in Melaka
Review: This quaint little restaurant is very unassuming from the outside but having only one night in Malaka we really wanted to try the authentic Nyonya food that had been recommended in all our research about the city. We stopped in on the way back to our hotel as we initially thought that it was closed on a Tuesday and normally they are but we got lucky and due to the Malaysian Independence Day holiday they were open this Tuesday. When we stopped in we met Jimmy one of the waiters and his enthusiasm and warmth was one of the reasons we ventured back. The restaurant is spacious with about 10 large tables, the evening we were dinned there were several large family groups. We were again met by Jimmy and given complimentary prawn crackers that were fantastic. We shortly were then served by a lovely lady whom we later found out was Jennifer one the proprietors. As visitors looking at a daunting menu and not having much local knowledge of the cuisine it was great to ask what the restaurant recommended. We were advised to have a selection of three dishes; chicken, prawns and aubergine rice is also served as part of the meal. The service was attentive and quick without being overbearing, just right!When the food came one of the dishes had a nut that is only found in Indonesia and has to be soaked for a week before cooking (all information from Jimmy our waiter). Again, never having eaten this before we had no idea of the what we were meant to do, but never fear the amazing Jimmy was back and politely asked if we needed advice on how to eat this. We readily accepted his kind offer and he then proceeded to show us how to scrape the tamarind like paste from inside the shell to mix with the various dishes on the table. The food was excellently balanced and the portions perfect for the two of us. The fact that the staff were not only knowledgeable about the cuisine but also so proud and wanting to share their cuisine with us made the experience even more pleasurable.Towards the end of the meal Jennifer again came over and we spent some time talking about the her and the restaurant. It has only been open about a year and previously Jennifer was in retail, the restaurant is a joint venture between her and her siblings whose names all begin with the letter ‘J’, a tradition started by her grandfather. She told us that she has three main rules in trying to make this restaurant a success – excellent quality, amazing customer service and fantastic hygiene. From our perspective, she is achieving this and more. This is not the place to go for fine dining but it is an absolute must if you want amazing traditional Nyonya food, with impeccable service and a great family atmosphere. I cannot recommend a visit to Manis J.Show less

Author: hirocmpKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Perfect location and service.
Review: Visit this restaurant at Saturday 7pm, not much diners. Food's taste just average, a bit pricey and small portion. Waiter with very good manners and attentive, after we place order immediately waiter inform us they serve in small portion and advice to order more.Due to we going for next food hunt so we just place the order by informing him the true, but we notice the waiter was murmur with others staff at counter and sniggering. Properly we a group of 8 adult just order 4 dishes and some drinks(end up bill RM 190+), this made us fell unpleasant. Pros: Location. Easy to find.Cons: Price.Show less

Author: KalpanaD101
Title: while in historic melaka do not miss this restaurant
Review: gem of a find  nostagic music a little gift shop all  the dishes need to request to spice it up to your preference just the best otakotak take a platter of the starters

Author: Codeblue79Singapore, Singapore
Title: Delicious food and perfect service
Review: We stumbled into this little gem by chance and we were pleasantly surprised by the authenticity of the nyonya dishes, the top notched customer service and how beautiful and clean the restaurant was. The owners and their team made sure we the customers enjoyed every minute dining in. Our food were deliciously prepared by the chef. Mr. Jimmy and Ms. Jennifer made us feel just at home with their warm smile and the occasional chit chat. It made our day. We will definitely be back and thank you for giving us the best dining experience ever. Show less

Author: WXLWKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: An Absolute Nyonya Food Haven!
Review: Manis J is a quaint little shop tucked away in the street of Jalan Bunga Raya in Malacca. Unlike the many commercialized Nyonya restaurants dotted around Malacca, Manis J had some things my family craved for- authenticity and amazing food! The average sized shop is not too busy during the lunch hour (12-2pm), so it is not necessary to reserve a table. We ordered several authentic Nyonya dishes from our delightful and warm server, Jimmy; including the Chilli Fish, the Lady's Fingers, the Chicken Pongteh, mixed vegetables (Chap Choy), Pai Tee, and a duck soup- Yee Tik Tim.I think it's safe to say that everybody was thoroughly impressed by the authentic, home-cooked, unique tastes ranging from savory to sweet. It truly was like an explosion of delicious flavours on our tongue. One dish I would highly recommend for both locals and foreigners to try is the fried Chilli Fish. It is a truly delectable yet surprisingly simple dish as it just consists of a commendable-sized fried fish and a generous lather of tangy Nyonya Chilli sauce. Another dish that is equally as pleasing is the Chicken Pongteh. My daughter was never a fan of it but the thickness of the brown gravy and the tenderness of the chicken really made her crave for more. Chicken Pongteh is a match made in heaven of delicious chicken and sweet brown gravy. The ambient waiter, Jimmy, serves this all with a wide grin on his face. Another delicious must-try is the chendol that was served to us after our meal. They are quite small so be sure to order at least one for each person! It is extremely refreshing on a warm day and your tastebuds will be as pleased by the fresh coconut milk and the rich Gula Melaka trickled on top of the tantalizing combination of red beans, jelly, and shaved ice.Manis J truly manages to capture the essence of what Nyonya cuisine is while maintaining an authentic, homely feel to it. I would highly recommend this restaurant to everybody and anybody. Last but not least, there are two shelves adorned with gifts and souvenirs you can purchase for your friends and family. Among these are freshly bottled jars of Gula Melaka which can last around two months on the shelf. Colourful batik bags are also available.I can definitely guarantee that you will leave Manis J with a smile on your face and in your stomach! Show less

Author: jentwlJohor Bahru, Malaysia
Title: Awesome! The Real Authentic Peranakan Food in Melaka...
Review: The true-blue Peranakan food they served will not only blow your taste buds, but the hospitality they show are equally as inviting. This restaurant ensures authenticity for a satisfactory dining experience, you will be salivating by the end of this delicious round-up of Peranakan restaurants in Melaka only at Manis J Nyonya Restuarant!Show less

Author: Wijnstijn v
Title: very authentic Baba Nyonya food
Review: Tasty authentic food, warm & friendly staff and host. nice curry dish, even have a quite special dish cooked with Buah Keluak.

Author: Michael WLeopold, Australia
Title: Great Find

The food was excellent, we explained to the waiter we hadn't eaten Nyonya food before and he carefully went through the menu explaining what each dish was and making suggestions. After we had eaten Jennifer, the owner came to talk to us and tell us more about the food.Show less

Author: PaulineAndBearSydney, Australia
Title: Great food with cultural overview !!
Review: Jimmy served us... Great food suggestions along with a brief overview of the culture.Great food in an extremely clean and comfortable restaurant.... a relief from the hawker and street food culture.It's a must try if you want to experience nyonya cuisine. Easy to get to, on the main road approx. 900m easy walking up from Jonker Street area, or just a few minutes down from The Majestic hotel.We had two entrees, one main, noodle dish and two drinks for 65RM. Author: aimantakkisah

Author: ErictherockerSingapore, Singapore
Title: Beautiful, clean, delicious food

The waiter Uncle Jimmy was so nice and recommended great dishes for us to try and he even demonstrated how to eat the famous Buah Keluak. :) excellent service, excellent food! :) made our tummies and our souls full. :)Show less

Author: Song WPort Dickson, Malaysia
Title: Great food
Review: Nice food overall. First time trying authentic Nyonya food in Malacca, and it surprises me by its rich flavour. One little regret is that food is barely warm. Probably because we visited at 3pm when there was no other customers around. Will recommend to friends who wanna try some nice food. Show less

Author: DinaNainggolan
Title: Great Food
Review: The restaurant is near from our hotel (bayview) and it served malay/chinese/peranakan food. Im Indonesian, so these foods are like when i was still a child visiting grandparents and they made us special food to welcome us. Nice and honest food. Dont forget to try the spring rolls !Show less

Author: AcuraMelody
Title: Yummy
Review: Had lunch there before depart back to KL. The restaurant located near to our apartment. Order chicken and also tofu where my son love it! Definitely will be back again

Author: ShengY90
Title: Great food!
Review: The food is awesome, even for me who's not a big fan of sambal balacan. The owner, Jennifer, is also friendly.

Author: k0hk3Singapore, Singapore
Title: Good nyonya cuisine
Review: Having read the good reviews of Manis J, we decide to try it. It is located just about 3 minutes walk from Ramada Plaza hotel. From Ramada Plaza, just walk toward The Shore shopping centre – at road junction – turn left – walk straight – Manis J is on the right opposite a Chinese temple.We were there early, hence it was not crowded. Small family run nyonya restaurant with simple Peranakan décor. Once seated, the addictive keropok was served. Service was friendly and prompt.Luckily we ordered 3 dishes as the portion was big for 2 persons. The ayam buah keluak (MYR30) was well cooked. Portion was too big for us. Uncle Jimmy was kind enough to show us how to dig out the buah keluak fruit. He mentioned it needed to be soaked in water for one week before cooking. The gravy of the chicken stew goes very well with white rice.Next was my favourite – sambai petai udang(MYR35). The prawns were fresh and plentiful. I liked the petai which was slightly bitter in taste.Final dish was the steamed lady finger (MYR15). It was fresh. Sambal belacan came together with this dish. It was spicy but not to me. My level of tolerance for chilli is higher.We were tempted to order the nyonya chendol. But were just too full. Maybe next time.Show less

Author: Janson OSingapore, Singapore
Title: Good food and very knowledgeable staff
Review: Did a search in google and came across Manis J while on holiday in Malacca. Although it is not in main tourist spot it's a short 10 mins walk from Jonker street area. Food is fantastic and service level excellent. Especially love the veg., chicken, chendol and fish dish. Family of 4 cost 160 rm. very reasonable. Show less

Author: RoyThiaSingapore, Singapore
Title: Excellent food, Hidden Gem
Review: Great food and service. I have never tasted such delicious prawn omelette before. The pongteh chicken was also the best I have eaten in Melaka so far. Price is also reasonable. Location though was a bit far from Jonker street but I would highly recommend this place if you want to try great authentic Nyonya food.Show less

Author: ivankct
Title: One of the best nyonya food
Review:

On dessert, chendol is not to be missed, and probably one of the best chendol that I have ever had.

Author: Gilagolf
Title: Best there is in Malacca
Review: I know there might be other more famous nonya food place, but this one is highly recommended. We had our first meal here for our holiday and thru 4 days couldnt find a better restaurant.

Author: 34pangseSingapore, Singapore
Title: Great traditional nonya food
Review: Recommended by friend. So give it try. We need to queue as we have our dinner quite late. We had ayam poteh, fried fish and fish maw soup. The food was great. Price is reasonable. The environment is better than Amy nonya restaurant. Owner is friendly. Nice place. Show less

Author: Michmy
Title: Best Authentic Nyonya cuisine
Review: It's a dinner that's so yummy from 1st dish till the most delicious Cendol in this restaurant. The customer service is excellent with dishes recommendations. This is the best Nyonya restaurant & fully recommended to all. Thank you, Uncle Jimmy of Manis J.

Author: N J
Title: Sincere nyonya
Review: We enjoyed a range of delicious peranakan food. Service was prompt, warm and attentive. Definitely recommended.

Author: TLak S

Author: patrick_tan86
Title: “Authentic nyonya food in a cosy and clean place
Review:
The food is great and the waiter is nice and friendly.

The food is value for money and i will go back again.

Author: Annagan1210
Title: Clean restaurant and nice food
Review: surprise on their cendol..nice service, friendly staff, nice food...clean environment especially toilet...will back again

Author: yilee555Melaka, Malaysia
Title: Authentic nyonya food in a cosy and clean restaurant!
Review: We were staying at the Ramada Plaza Hotel which was a mere three minutes' walk to J. Manis. The staff were welcoming, service was prompt and the Owner, Jennifer, personalises the service by advising us on the combination of nyonya dishes which would best complement. We found memorable the ayam pongteh, fried fish with sambal, prawns in petai, steamed lady's fingers served with a sambal dip and the cendol gula melaka. We were fortunate to have been able to enjoy a variety of nyonya kuehs on the day we were there as a prequel to the Nyonya Kueh Tea Sets which J Manis plans to launch. Having tasted such kuehs when I lived in Malacca in the 1960's and having had access to traditional nyonya kuehs sold around Malaysia and Singapore since, I have to say that the several varieties I had tried at J Manis were top of the class in each of their respective categories. They were less sweet than the ones of the old days, which suit current day palate, and with authentic ingredients like black sesame, pandan juice, fresh young grated coconuts and gula melaka used in the kuehs. Only a perfectionist could have put together this divine ensemble. I hope Jennifer launches the J Manis Tea Sets soon, or at least, offer the kuehs as an option in the Desserts menu for those who might not be there at tea-time. We will be back!Show less

Author: M V
Title: Nice lunch
Review: My family and I very much enjoyed our lunch at this nice little restaurant.  The service is very good, the owner took time to explain interesting things about each dish.  The food is authentic and delicious.  Price is reasonable as well.

Author: danieloR2895ZGSingapore, Singapore
Title: A new option in town
Review: We were walking around for some food along Bunga Raya but they were not (yet) open. By chance we saw this new restaurant. Let's try. A good 6 months into business we were welcomed and the menu was explained. Jennifer who runs the restaurant is on top of things. The food was very well prepared and delicious. The steemed lady fingers came with a mouthwatering chilli sauce. Spicy and sweet. Just perfect. While I prefer Ngoh Hiang made from pork, the chicken version served here is outstanding. The fish maw soup could have been slightly more tasty. It lacked some depth. Everything else was just great. Happy to have a new alternative in an other area of town. Show less

Author: Sincy TKuala Lumpur, Wilayah Persekutuan, Malaysia
Title: Authentic nyonya food with story behind
Review: I came across this restaurant while hunting around for nyonya food around jalan bunga raya... and found out this restaurant opened 6 month ago and it run by a family with 5 siblings.. (the owner will tell you her story ) We order 3 dishes for 2 persons. We are very satisfied with the food especially their Gula Melaka Cendol!!! OMG!! So far this is the best cendol I had in Melaka as the Gula Melaka was super original without add on sugar sweet taste!! Other dishes we order are Ladyfinger with sambal, Asam fish (big portion for 2 person) and Petai prawn sambal.. all food taste good but less spicy for local Malaysian like me. Maybe the chef try to make it mild for foreigners who can't take hot and spicy food. Anyway, the owner will help you on the menu if you can't decide what to order!! Very warm services and high and fresh quality food! I hope they could maintain their food quality and services!! Keep up the good work Jennifer (owner)! I'm so sad I forgot to take photo of the cendol as it is too good!! Show less

Author: maevdbAuckland, New Zealand
Title: Delicious food, fantastic service
Review: We had a lovely lunch here a couple of weeks ago. The food was delicious and had a comfortable "home-cooked with love" feel to it.Jimmy, our waiter, couldn't be more attentive and helpful as he topped up our water, made sure we had ample rice and was nearby in case we needed him.My four-year-old can be a little picky about food at times but she ate the Ayam Buah Keluak, Chap Chye and fried fish with gusto!For those driving, there is limited street-side parking, but a little further up the road to the left is a large outdoor carpark.Will definitely come again on my next visit!Show less

Author: WealdSussex
Title: Wonderful
Review: This family run Nonya restaurant provides authentic Nonya food beautifully cooked as it would be at home. The menu is not vast but the quality cannot be faulted. All the family seem to have a first name beginning with a "J" and are friendly and helpful. The location is close to the Ramada Hotel and the Melaka but not in the Historic Area so if one is not staying in this part of town one needs a taxi Show less

Author: DavidN4471
Title: A definite must for a taste of local food!
Review: We came across this great restaurant by chance and even though it was 30 minutes from closing time, we were given a lovely welcome from Jennifer, the Owner and Jimmy our Waiter. We asked Jennifer to advise us what to choose and we couldn't have been more happy. The food was fantastic and just enough. The Spring rolls were really tasty as was everything else. Jennifer was a wealth of knowledge on Peranakan history and style of food. Would definitely recommend on a visit to Malacca. We will certainly return.Show less

Author: baxR23Midlands

I did not want to review it straight away as it was so new, that I thought they may have been making a special effort to impress! So glad to see that others have said it is still great. Really delicious food, and such a nice change from the standard Malaysian tourist food.Show less

Author: Duskyattire

Review: Sampled outstanding and freshly cooked Nyonya cuisine at this friendly and very good value restaurant. £70 for 4 people got us a starter and main apiece plus sides and drinks. Highly recommended.

Author: barryc1234
Title: Well worth a visit
Review: This restaurant has not been open very long. The staff are extremely friendly and the food great. They explain everything and made us feel welcome. We went on the back of previous Trip Adviser comments and were well pleased we did.

Author: brmateStevenage, United Kingdom
Title: A clean restaurant with lovely food in Malaysia!
Review: First trip to Melaka and we were looking for somewhere to eat (other than a Mamak), and saw this restaurant. The first impression was that it was clean and very well done up. We sat down and the owner came over to us and engaged in a friendly conversation with us. She recommended the Buah Keluak Chicken dish, which was absolutely divine!Another catch, is that is baby friendly. They made sure that the food was not too spicy, as our little one hates spice. To keep the little one entertained they bought out some toys.Good quality food, clean and baby friendly - this is truly a hidden gem in Malaysia.Show less

Author: Steve T
Title: Brilliant, fresh, genuine and super-tasty

Author: X4842AYdavidkHampton, Australia
Title: Peranakan food in clean pleasant surrounds
Review: We wanted to try this restaurant for both the local cuisine and the favourable reviews - also staying at the Majestic so it was very convenient. The service was excellent, staff very charming and overall the meal was enjoyable, but for us the food was not outstanding. To be fair my son and I are so used to very spicy food (nasi kandar, Padang Indonesian food, Manado Indonesian cuisine, Indian, Thai, etc) that we find Peranakan cuisine perhaps a touch overrated. The black nut chicken was interesting without being memorable, sotong goreng was similar and the kang kong perhaps the best dish we had overall. Ayam pongteh would possibly be a better choice to tantalise the taste buds. Having learnt how to prepare this at the Majestic it would be something we would prefer to cook over buah keluak chicken, even if we had access to black nuts, although note others rave about the latter dish. For me the black nut is quite a way from the Asian equivalent of truffles (as has been suggested)....but the preparation of these seeds is so intriguing and exotic that it gets one interested anyway.... check out the 'pangium edule' tree on Wikipedia. Overall this is a good restaurant but perhaps my tastes are possibly not really wildly Nyonya...but don't let that put you off trying this restaurant as we are picky.Show less

Author: LovesToTravelTTTT
Title: Not worth it
Review: This is a combined café and guesthouse.Let me start with the café. The food wasn't very tasty and very small portions. All in all way overpriced for what you end up getting. On a side note - they give people 20 percent of their bill for a good TripAdvisor rating - which honestly is the only thing that explains the high rating for me... The café on it's own I would probably rate 2 stars.However I also stayed in the guesthouse. And I regretted booking three nights in advance. The rooms are right above a café which is open from ten in the until midnight everyday. During that time they play incredibly loud music - the entire day long. The level of noise in my room was incredible - so no sleep or relaxing possible during the opening hours of the café.Staff also wasn't very helpful when I asked for some advice where to go.But the biggest problem was the bathroom - or better the lack of bathrooms. There is only ONE bathroom for the entire place and on top shower and toilet are in the same room. So I had to wait numerous times for people to finish their showers just so I could use the toilets - and sometimes there were several people waiting to get into the bathroom. Technically they did have another toilet downstairs in the café, but for one it was a squat toilet and secondly I don't want to go through a café full of people, especially late at night or in the morning while I'm still in my PJs just to use the toilet.All in all I unfortunately did not enjoy my stay there and recommend you to stay somewhere else!Show less

Author: shounly
Title: Live band

Author: MayN595
Title: Nice place for gathering...
Review: Nice food & nice environment... love their matcha cheese cake. Their nasi lemak spaghetti is special, can have a try!

Author: Shereen T
Title: Birthday cerebration
Review: Nice and clean environment, nice foods and nice songs are highly recomended for family or friends gathering.

Author: CarlyR475
Title: Lovely spot

Author: 999paulj
Title: Best coffee & infusion tea in malacca
Review:
Stumbled upon this clean and humbly managed cafe whilst walking the UNESCO boardwalk opposite side to musical fountain.

If you have had enough of filter/drip coffee in the hotels and are hanging out for the real deal then this is the place to go!

Author: syloh0111Melaka, Malaysia
Title: pet friendly and sweet tooth lover place
Review: Is not easy to find a cafe that you can go with your furry buddy. Luckily found this cafe where i can hang out with my pug. The owner is a pet lover (good looking too) . There is a very cute pomeranian name Kiki own by the cafe owner. The atmosphere of the cafe is very relaxing. Its a great place to have gathering with friend too. If u are sweet tooth lover u can't miss their chocolate souffle. Their chocolate souffle is not like restaurant-style flat top, its risen and hot. Chocolate that melts in your mouth. Way, way better than I predicted! Must try if you are here.Show less

Author: sg790105
Title: Friends gathering
Review:
Lovely environment clean & comfortable,we girls have a good foto shooting at Relish because the design of the place were nice. 
We'll definitely visit again to this cafe plus their food was really delicious & tasty.

Author: Ngaire B
Title: Went to the cafe.
Review: It’s a type of cafe to hang out in for a while. Plugs available at some tables and a section to play board games. The food was surprising! Got the veggie otak and mushroom pizza and both were delicious. The menu selection isn’t very large. The cappuccino was very good also. Had AC and a pleasant atmosphere.Show less

Author: VickyT1901
Title: Smelly toilet
Review: Not enough toilet. There's only two bathroom (one downstairs & upstairs) shared with many people. The toilet upstairs was so smelly even though we stand quite far away from it.

Author: ByyenKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Bad service attitude from the owner
Review: The room was clean except for the toilet are so smelly and dirty. My parents was very uncomfortable for the first impression. Then, we asked if we could cancel the booking in the morning and the boss (Winston) come and show us a displeased face. He disrespect my family member by saying that we are rude and your family are not suitable for dormitory room. We are so shocked by his attitude towards a customer. We do not make noise at the place. We asked you politely but why should we get treated like this from the owner? There's some rude sentences come out from the owner too. I might just skip some of the details. After that, we get two calls from Singapore and US, they apologies on behalf of the owner attitude. But eventually, me and my family never get any single respond from the owner. He even hide my review on his Facebook page. A kind reminder to all the travelers, do not over rely on the review. The owner from Relish The Moment had the bad service and attitude I've never seen before.Show less

Author: FloreGdrParis, France
Title: Great surprise for such a small price!
Review: We were 3 girls and were all amazed by the quality of this hotel ! We paid almost nothing and had more than expected. The café downstairs is very well decorated and the food very good.We slept in a dormitory of 6 people with good air-con. There is a bit of noise from the street but we were not disturb by it. The bathroom is common and its hygiene sufficient. You have 2 bikes at disposal for free ! You have sheets at disposal too.I would 100% recommend this place !! We loved our trip to Malacca thanks to it :)Show less

Author: aaroncoloradoLos Angeles, California
Title: Wonderfully decorated, solid location, cafe/lodging combination
Review: The good things:The family that runs this hostel and cafe are helpful and nice. The decor is wonderful. The dorm room is spacious and beds are comfortable with nice bedding. AC works well. Nice sitting area. Easy access to downstairs cafe. Great location and near to many attractions. Lockers for valuables. Water container. Place to prepare simple meals.Needs improvement: Noisy from street traffic in bedroom at night. Only one shower/toilet combo for the entire hostel floor upstairs. Additional shower/toilet downstairs in cafe area.Show less

Author: Laust S
Title: That home feeling
Review: I am staying here right now. I love it so much. Coffee is perfect, room is nice. Their downstairs area is really comfortable. 5/5

Author: Martins-worldwide
Title: Lovely place in a lovely city
Review: Relish the moment is a cozy and friendly place in Melaka. I had the pleasure to share some time with them and found a family far away from home.In the ground floor you find a cafe/bar where you can enjoy delicious dishes and refreshing drinks such as smoothies, fruit juices or a beer.Going up stairs you have the guesthouse with all the amenities you need. Title: Good

The food was good, albeit it was slightly pricey (understandable given they are on the river and most restaurants there charge around the same price) and the portion was smaller than I expected. Otherwise the place was clean and the staff were very friendly!Show less

Author: CklsqSingapore

Author: yenchie88Melaka, Malaysia

Author: clement871114Singapore, Singapore

Author: Ming J
