I had several meals here and absolute feast would set one back less than $10... The Friday lunch time 10 veg curry deal is brilliant. Exquisite experience to go up to the servery, point to everything you like then go sit - they bring it all out on little dishes followed by the guy with rice and bucket of dahl. Yummy experienceShow less

Author: nilintentum_reliquitMelbourne, Australia
Title: A suprise but a great family experience. Went back for more
Review: We were a little unsure when we first entered but there was no need to be. We were greeted by friendly staff and we only ordered a little to start with to try it out. The food was extremely tasty which launched us into another 3 more orders. The chicken, dosais and lassis were lapped up by us and the many locals who frequented. Food ridiculously good value and had to go back for lunch on our last day.Show less

Author: John S
Title: Great value
Review: Ate vegetarian curry for only RM4, and it was very tasty. The Horlicks was very sweet and the chapatti was nice. Recommended!

Author: sylveskeAntwerp, Belgium
Title: Great food and service!
Review: On recommendation of our travel guide, we ended up here...It's a small restaurant, not fancy or cosy, but... very friendly staff, very yummy (and surely enough) food!!!, very low prices...Here you can eat the real indian food... a lot of locals here too, which is a good sign ;-)We really loved it here!Show less

Author: Denise H
Title: well worth it, especially for the price
Review: I had a vegetarian banana leaf & masala tea.  Very nice and the guy taking our order was super friendly and very accommodating :)

Author: ana192
Title: Nicest place to eat
Review:
Bannana leaf menu, was very nice, the best in town. 

At the counter the woman isn´t nice at all... she should review manners.

Author: SubbaraoKBengaluru, India
Title: Selvam Vegetarian restaurant, Melaka, Malaysia - avoid if you can
Review: If you ask any one in Melaka to suggest a vegetarian restaurant, invariably, it would be SELVAM. But according to me, it is not a clean restaurant. We ordered Lunch. We could not see the way the items were served. Nothing was tasty. If ones criteria is only vegetraian and cheap, then you may go over there. In Holiday Inn, we got an excellent vegetarian curry. The whole sight at Selvam was disgustingShow less

Author: RobynS1962St Kilda, Australia
Title: Breakfast lunch or dinner
Review: I ate here in 1990 and was pleased to find despite many changes in Melaka this place is still the same. I had breakfast here one sleepy early morning Masala Dosai still wonderful I wish I had been able to stay longer to enjoy the entire range at SelvamShow less

Author: pngpcySingapore, Singapore
Title: Awesome Tandoori Chicken
Review: This restaurant serves simply the best Tandoori chicken that I have ever eaten in my life. The drumstick meat is very tender and finger licking good and the skin is crispy and simply juicy. The Naan and sauces are pretty good too but I have eaten better elsewhere. Drinks were ok too. There is not much crowd when we went at 630pm so we didn't had to wait!Show less

Author: JaydcokeBalik Pulau, Malaysia
Title: Good food, clean environment, good value. Love this place.
Review: Selvam is located on the fringe of Little India but close to the historical area. I love the range and quality of food on offer and the taste is unquestionably good too. Friday is vegetarian special day where the basic price includes 14 vegetarian dishes. Even better value!Show less

Author: Hareesh92Singapore
Title: Very tasty and cheap Indian food
Review: If you want to get a taste of tasty and spicy Indian food, catch up on Selvam. There are a lot of choices in both vegetarian and non vegetarian dishes. They are quite tasty too ( by Indian standards too). Very reasonable prices. The ambience can be better.Show less

Author: Muthu C
Title: delcious food
Review: The Restaurent is located closer to the Historical places. The spicy Chettinad food is prepared by the famous Mr. Selvam himself. Once you taste the food you will never want to go to other restaurents..

Author: cochleartraveller
Title: very stuffy!
Review: The place feels uncomfortable but the food is true local indian stuffs!  Getting pricy though! I liked the fired chicken here.

Author: gardenchimeAlor Setar, Malaysia
Title: Good choices available
Review: My favorite Indian restaurant in town. They have the food on display so it saves us the hassle of trying to remember names of dishes and just point and choose instead. Normally rice is served on banana leave. They serve briyani rice on Fridays. Price is quite reasonable for the quality of the food. The downside is the location of the restaurant - it's very difficult to find a parking spot near the place during lunch hours, if you drive.Show less

Author: LoloBoyWoodlands
Title: Tasty and Fresh food
Review: WOW!!!!That is what me and my wife were going like after we had our dinner and were heading back to our hotel....In all the places that we had eaten in SG and MSIA, this was the best we ever got.......it was next best thing to home cooked food.Hygiene wise there were no problems at all...We tried their fried chicken, and curry chicken and mutton as well...we were so happy and satisfied with the food that we actually went back for breakfast the next day. And just as the previous day, we were not disappointed with the breakfast at all. their breads and thosai were freshly cooked. and unlike alot of stall in Singapore and Malaysia, their gravy /curries were not reused or re-heated. Everything was fresh just like the night before. Me and my wife really look forward to going back to Melaka especially for the food at Selvam'sShow less

Author: yogesht49
Title: Slow service
Review: Waited quite long for 2 roti chanai and 2 teh tarik . Place is super crowdwd during public holidays .

Author: Hugh B
Title: Great Indian Food
Review: The food at this restuarant was excellent. We ordered a range of curries and roti etc and it was all delicious and including the drinks for 3 of us the cost was very low. Overall good food and great value. See you next visit.

Author: Vaidehi2012
Title: Good Indian Food
Review: This is at an excellent location.  We had dosai, filter coffee, chicken thali set and all of them were very good.  Their service was very fast and the waiters are very friendly.  It is very cheap food but with excellent taste.

Author: Rhiannonj86
Title: Tasty
Review: Very tasty food for a cheap price. Good banana leaf food and some traditional food on the menu. Good service, they were helpful explaining what stuff was to us.

Author: Xbrit2004Songkhla, Thailand
Title: Great food, and Cheap
Review: This place is right at the entrance to Little India, but not actually *IN* Little India (Look for the fountain with all the pigeons). Go in, sit down, and in a moment or two a waiter will arrive with a Banana Leaf - which is both your place mat AND your plate. "Dahl and Rice is RM 4 and comes with 3 different side dishes included. Add a curry of your choice and a drink and you will still come out with change from a RM10 bill (Unless you opt for something more than the basics offered). If you are in Melaka you have to stop here for lunch at least once.Show less

Author: reena_dwitch
Title: indian food in melaka
Review: its typical indian restaurant (not mamak shop) , with indian varieties, desserts and sweets. Im indian who very particular with indian shops as my mom is a great cook, i dont prefer eat indian shops outside, but selvam taste is good.

Author: Arjunasahayan MChennai (Madras), India
Title: Tasty Indian Food.
Review: I feel the best Tamil nadu food I ever taken.It is a typical Tamil nadu style Hotel . We went for Lunch ,after going through place s in Malakka s heat .Food s are served on Banana leaf .price very reasonable.veg. meal s 2.R.M. cheaper than non.veg meals. very good food.vendaha kulambu (do not miss it) for meal s. serving food take s more time because of crowd.A lady, one of the family member s of owner of the hotel enquire every one and serving the food.Do not expect much comfort and neatness.Show less

Author: raysonraySingapore, Singapore
Title: Not a fine dining restaurant.
Review: This place is a very simple restaurant. Not the posh one. It jas no a/c. The menu is basically white rice and veg and non veg. Briyani only on fridays and weekends. Tiffin only at specific hours. Service is lousy. Some.dishes are cold. Some are tasty.i won't recommend.Show less

Author: Nbichick
Title: Great Indian food
Review: Was missing Indian food after almost 4 months in SE Asia ( there's only so much friend rice and noodles a vegetarian can eat after all ! ) and Selvams was a real treat ! A good selection of authentic food from around the continent, served quickly and pleasantly...and, in good Indian food tradition, tasty and really good value !They also have a small selection of Mithai ( Indian sweets ), which was a lovely treat.Restaurant is totally open at the front and has fans, so is pleasantly cool in the searing Melakan heat.Also, plenty of parking outside if you have rented a bicycle and want to keep an eye on it while you eat.Show less

Author: frances30Malysia
Title: excellent food
Review: eat as much excellent Indian food as you can for a very good price. Not buffet style

Author: Ewan MBristol, United Kingdom
Title: Value for money and a haven for Veggies...
Review: I reapply struggled to find somewhere in Melaka that didn't put fish sauce in just about everything! Not an easy place for a vegetarian, so this place was a welcome find. The food is cheap and tasty and comes in huge portions- try the banana leaf curry, its amazing and I didn't come close to finishing it. Show less

Author: jo_thomsonPlymouth, United Kingdom
Title: Delicious food at a great price.
Review: I visited Selvams about 3 or 4 times whilst in Melaka for a week. We had breakfast, lunch and dinner there and all were very tasty meals for a very reasonable price.Would definitely recommend the masala roti and the Friday special biryani, but then everything I tried was delicious.Strongly recommend you visit this place if you're in Melaka.Show less

Author: Peterjames0Stockport, United Kingdom
Title: Authentic Indian Cuisine- Fabulous-Cheap-Fun
Review: Visited Selvam twice in 3 days because it was that good. Takes a little while to understand the ordering procedure but if you find an english speaking waiter it is fine. The first time I used my fingers like the locals do but found it just too messy for my liking.The second time I used a fork and the waiter wasnt offended by my etiquette.The curries are to die for, I had a mixture of Prawn-Chicken and Mutton, all were really good and the Lhassi is delightful.Average bill was circa £4 which is unbelievable value. Definately worth a visit if your in Melaka.Show less

Author: Mark2011Seattle
Title: Yummy Indian food
Review: Loved this restaurant.  I had the Friday vegetarian special.  Yummy.  The restaurant uses palm fonds as plates.  The chai tea is delicious.  I liked this restaurant so much I went back another day.  Great prices too!

Author: hanspilot
Title: Fabulous
Review: Best banana leaf in Melaka,close to JONKER WALK.drop by if u on a day trip or holiday.ample parking opposite the shop

Author: ScorpionTravellerKuala Lumpur
Title: Love the Curries
Review: I have just moved to Malacca from Kuala Lumpur on work assignment and Indian banana leaf rice is one of my top favourites. Won't consider myself as someone with distinct penchant for Indian food, however I have been many venues in both Kuala Lumpur and Petaling Jaya to satisfy my sinful cravings for banana leaf rice. My colleagues invited me to Selvam one Friday afternoon. It was one of the best lunches I've had. It was vegetarian Friday and we were continuously offered a great variety of vegetarian dishes (I counted - 8 in total). The fish and chicken curries are fresh in taste, I enjoyed every single hint of spice in the mix. We left with a reasonable bill of RM4. It has officially become a favourite haunt of mine.Show less

Author: poopshooterPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: great breakfast joint...
Review: Selvam is my favourite place for breakfast or brunch in Malacca. Parking might be a pain due to where they are located however thats just a minor issue. They serve up awesome tosai, idli and uppuma. Even their banana leaf for lunch is yummy. Along with their rotis and idlis they serve up good dhall and curries. So far been visiting multiple times in the last 4 years and they have been consistant. Service is good and friendly and pricing wise they are pretty reasonable for indian food.Show less

Author: MM2HLondon, United Kingdom
Title: 10 Curry Friday - Noon 'til 2
Review: Every Friday they have their 'Lunchtime Special'. A banana leaf with rice and 10 small helpings of a variety of vegetarian curries. With plain rice its 7RM with Byriani rice its 8.50RM.All the food was delicious. Sure its not haute cuisine but it gives you the chance to taste a variety of different veggie style dishes. Also besides the 'Special' there are loads of other dishes you can choose - meat, egg etc and of course chapatis!The restaurant has recently had a 'refurb' so is in much better condition than just 9 months ago.For something a bit different try the Friday 10 Curry Special. It from noon until 2pm I believe.Show less

Author: Charles HLondon, United Kingdom
Title: I was ill after eating here.
Review: I was ill with diarrhea after eating here. I didnt eat any other food that day - as i had slept in late. It was definitely Selvam that made me ill. When i went to the toilet before leaving i noticed that the restaurant floor was covered in slippery grease. Aside from this not being very safe to walk on, it also showed just quite how dirty the restaurant was.Finally the food didnt taste anything special. Ok sure this is just a regularly priced indian 'dhaba' but others manage to make tasty food at a reasonable price. Not here i'm afraid.Show less

Author: flip-flop88-66Gibraltar
Title: money, money, money !!!!
Review: I've been there a few times !!!each time I ended up arguing about the price.But the straw on camel's back was when they charged us for our 2 yr-old kid, whereas I gave some food from my share.Unbelievable !!!For sure the food is good, but the taste I kept in my mouth was the frustration rather than their food.Show less

Author: nasi_ayam_search
Title: delicious banana leaf curry
Review: lovely food, very authentic and super cheap. I had the vegetarian banana leaf curry, my BF the tandoori chicken, and mango lassi all round. Delicious.

Author: flaviosimonettiThe World
Title: Best Indian restaurant in Malaysia
Review: I stayed Melaka for a week, and everyday I went to Selvam. The food is simply amazing, specially the set menus served after 7 pm. Nice staff and, best of all, really cheap - you can have a decent sized meal for only RM 7! If you're in Melaka, you'll have to go!!!Show less

Author: onlyworldQueanbeyan, Australia
Title: Good food in Cheap price
Review: It is a nice restaurant and typical Tamilnadu (South India) restaurant. You can get all non-vegetarian curries with very good taste and offcourse cheap price. The restaurant atmosphere not bad and it is an old building. You have to wait for the service for a long period. Car parking is available in opposite to the restaurant and you have to pay for the car parking.The restaurant is located in a busy street and you have to be very careful to cross the road. I went with my family (wife and 2 kids) at lunch time. We enjoyed the food and everything. But we were waiting to catch a table for a long time. The service is also not good. Try the following menuMeals – Rice + Sambar + Poriyal + Papadam etc then side dishes try Chicken varuval, Chicken 65, Mutton liver, Mutton curry varuval etc…If you are a tourist from western countries then don’t forget to buy a mineral water bottle. It is recommended in whole Malaysia.Pros: Very good taste, cheap price, using banana leaf for hygienic, car parkingCons: Heavy crowd, you have to wait for a while to catch a table, service, located in a busy streetShow less

Author: gibmow
Title: Excellent roti breakfast
Review: Good old fashioned roti, kopi "o", iced milo. If looking for street food, you will not go wrong here.

Author: MyMsiaReviewsSingapore
Title: Think Again
Review: After reading the reviews in Tripod, I chanced upon Selvam Restaurant and decided to have my dinner there with my family of 8. Being Indian ouselves, we were wary from the outlook of the restaurant but still decided to give it a try.Although priced cheaply, don't expect much for Naans and Tandooris as compared to Singapore standards. Recommended to try the vegetarian food as it was value for money. Overall, cleanliness was disappointing and we decided we had a terrible meal overall.Show less

Author: PinkpowerPinkpower
Title: Good food, simple set up
Review: This is a simple place near Melaka's Little India. We were there for lunch. Lunch consists of plain rice with 3 vegetables on a banana leaf. You are then invited to order extras - there are a huge range of meat dishes and a reasonable range of vegetarian ones. The food was generally tasty. I loved the rasam. Prices were very reasonable. Would want to go back on my next visit to Melaka.Show less

Author: Ashvixen
Title: The ambience and look of the
Review: The ambience and look of the cafe is pretty cool. Food taste was also delicious. Try the salted egg dish! Kudos to the chef!

Author: ElisaNg95
Title: cool café of melaka
Review: food and coffee are good，love the nostalgic environment，and the staff were friendly，will revisit and recommend to my friend

Author: davidalso
Title: Very nice restaurant. The
Review: Very nice restaurant. The food is delicious and the waiters are super friendly. Definatly recommend you to come here and taste the drinks and the food.

Author: Mdbryson1213
Title: Cozy Cafe
Review: Spent an afternoon here catching up on emails while enjoying some unique coffee. The atmosphere is great and the seating in the back is the best with natural light and a mini courtyard. Definitely a nice place for a break and not too far from Jonker Street. The staff is nice and friendly and speak very good English.Show less

Author: hxhxhx
Title: Quaint little cafe
Review: Love their Gula Melaka drink and their salted duck pasta. The smell of the coffee is very fragrant as well. Love the quiet ambiance here. Lovely place for a quiet afternoon.

Author: freckles8_10
Title: Cozy Kaya Kaya
Review: Spontaneously, when seeking shelter from the sudden downpour, we came into the Kaya Kaya Café and were pleasantly surprised. The coffees we tries were very good (Sake Iced Coffee and Hazelnut Latte) and so was the pumpkin carrot soup. Very cozy interior!

Author: jameshonestreviews
Title: Tastey aubergine toast
Review: Tastey aubergine toast meal (TAC) with some hearty local coffee. Staff are friendly and there is a nice ambience! Come here 🦥

Author: SUSAN_711104Butterworth, Malaysia
Title: The best cafe in Melaka City !
Review: Although this cafe is not very big and the food menu doesn't have much choices, but the food was so delicate and super delicious! I ordered a toast with scrambled eggs, spinach and black sesame on top, it was just superb! That was the best toast I have ever had! And my sons had Salted Duck Egg Spaghetti, dessert, all taste fantastic! They even said that will definitely visit again when go to Melaka in future... So we rate this cafe the best in Melaka City!Show less

Author: 901stanleyl
Title: Relax corner
Review:
Friendly staff.
Delicious  food at reasonable price 
Nice place to chill away from the afternoon sun..

Author: Lugosi915Malaysia
Title: Not bad
Review: Came here for a quick lunch before heading to airport, tried their Salted Duck Egg Spaghetti and Kaya/Butter Toast. The Spaghetti was not bad, loved the taste. Kaya/Butter toast one the other hand, wasn't really my taste as i'm not a fan of Gula Melaka. Overall, not bad!Show less

Author: 10elgigisitentaParanaque, Philippines
Title: "Whimsical little cafe, perfect for laid back dining"
Review: First breakfast in Melaka and we wanted some place quiet so we can enjoy our first morning. Surprisingly the place did not disappoint. We were the only diners and I loved it. I looooove the coffee they served - that quaint aroma of the coffee added to the whimsical ambiance of the place. Finally the food serving was large I had to share mine. Food was FANTASTIC. The waiting from the time we ordered our food was commendable. Definitely a rare find along Jalan Tukang Besi.Show less

Author: Christopher_SNZ
Title: Disappointing first visit
Review:
Came here by the recommendation of a friend, unfortunately the air con was broken and most of the menu was sold out.

Cakes were dry and drinks were a bit too sweet. The place is very charming though.

Author: tinsterella
Title: Nice, quaint cafe. Good place for coffee and ice tea.
Review: Nice, quaint cafe. Good place for coffee and ice tea. Drinks are made to perfection. Good place for a nice quiet afternoon.

Author: echelon118
Title: Nice little cafe to visit and relax
Review: Visited Kaya Kaya cafe on the our last day of our weekend trip. The refreshing and pretty-looking drinks did a good job in quenching our thirst. Friendly and helpful staff. Hope to try the food there on our next visit to Melaka.

Author: S7688ZDkatharinakHamburg, Germany
Title: Breakfasr
Review: We had a very good breakfast here! Very nice staff:) we had the French toast and the pancakes. They didn’t have any banana for the pancakes so they offered us apple instead. We also had the iced passion fruit juice and the orange apple juice :)Show less

Author: Y5646FSrachelb
Title: Breakfast
Review: Great breakfast. Both the kaya toast with cheese and the CAT (cheese, aubergine toast) were delicious. Best cappuccino I’ve had so far in Malaysia as well. The staff were lovely and the service was quick. Can not fault.

Author: julietd1234
Title: Lovely brekafast
Review: We had a great breakfast in Kaya Kaya cafe. Their kaya toast with cheese and toast with cheese, aubergine and tomato were amazing! The coffee is delicious. Lovely atmosphere here, highly recommend

Author: Jogkaur
Title: Lovely place
Review: Love the atmosphere and great service from the staffs. Smoothie bowls and avocado on toast were so good.

Author: dagianc
Title: Nice cafe
Review: Good food and ambience for couple hangout . Recommend to all who likes to have great food and ambience for breakfast and lunch

Author: 53pluscountriesWest coast, USA
Title: It was okay
Review: The Kaya toast was good, but not much butter for the price. I ordered a scrambled egg, it was very small and a little undercooked. I asked for a local drink, but the guy working there couldn't really be bothered, I still don't know if I got a local drink. Seemed like a watery bubble tea to me, maybe they were invented here. I'm obviously a visitor, it would have been nice to have gotten some recommendations. Something on the guy's phone was more important I guess. For all the 'amazing' reviews and the western price I really expected better.Show less

Author: T5983QIkarent
Title: Nice environment

Author: Jacky84Singapore, Singapore
Title: Nice retro cafe but do not ordered the welcome to melaka drink
Review: Since we waked up early, we decided to find a good place for some breakfast and this is among some of the cafes that are opened very early. We took a grab from our hotel to this place and surprisingly there is not much of people inside when we have reached the place. We have ordered a breakfast set and a pancake for breakfast, a "welcome to Melaka" and hot milk. They served the drinks first, however to my surprise, the welcome to Melaka drink is actually just soya milk add with grass jelly which is very common drinks in Singapore and available in many hawker centre. The breakfast served a bit slow, but for the price of 26RM, it includes toast, scramble eggs, 2 sausages, chicken ham, salad and mushroom, the price is definitely worth it. The pan cake is good as well, but a bit small portion though and a lot of whip cream. The chocolate blend well with the peanut butter, but banana is not available so replaced with apple instead. Highly recommended to go for breakfast.Show less

Author: marinsulGeylang, Singapore
Title: No Kaya Cafe
Review: A group of 8 went there this morning to have breakfast. First we were told that they run out of kaya, so any dish with kaya on the menu is either not available or will be replaced with something else. We arrived at the cafe at 9:10am and 50 minutes later, only 2 dishes out of 8 were on the table. When we asked how much longer will it take them to bring out the rest of the food, they said at least 20 minutes. Well forget it. Not gonna wait another 20 mins for a mediocre food. Place is cute but didn’t come for the cuteness. Food is average and service is super slow. Will not come again or recommend fellow traveler to come either.Show less

Author: yomamemoSingapore
Title: Overprice, mediocre food
Review: Ambience is ok...in fact if you walk around melaka, you'll find similar cafes...so nothing to shout about.Now, let's talk about the food.Ordered the CAT, grilled chicken chop, mushroom soup and Kaya breakfast. The CAT is a disappointment, just a cheese and tomato dip with slices of white toast.Kaya breakfast's scrambled eggs is just omelette broken into many small pieces. The mushroom sauce for the chicken chop is actually mushroom soup. the black local coffee is weak. All in all we spent RM100 for 3 main courses, 1 side dish and 4 drinks.If you want to benchmark against starbucks breakfast, please at least make sure the quality of the food is the same too.I think the tripadvisor flag that is hung outside the cafe, gives it a "licence" to charge exorbitant prices with mediocre food.Show less

Author: gayathrxSingapore, Singapore

Author: Beck Iskandar MKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Awesome!
Review: Come for the food and ambience, not for the coffee. Although Kaya-kaya Cafe is rated as one of the best cafes in Melaka, there is a need of improvement for its coffee. Let's be fair, they have never brag on their coffee. Instead, the best-selling drinks are See U Again (pandan leaves + lemongrass) and Welcome to Melaka(soy milk + grass jelly + gula melaka). For this visit, our pick were the Kaya Cheese Toast, Carbonara Penne, andMushroom Omelette to try out.  The Kaya Cheese Toast is one of the popular items on the menu. Expect to see the tables around you ordering this as well. The combination of kaya and cheese blend so well together like peanut butter and jelly. As your teeth sunk into the crunchy toast, the rich and creamy kaya melts into your mouth, while the cheese gives a hint of saltiness to balance the taste. For breakfast, do not resist ordering the mushroom omelettes. It may look ordinary but after the first bite, it leaves you wanting for more. The mushrooms are pan seared in butter until fragrant and added onto a fluffy scrambled eggs. The velvety texture of the eggs is in between omelette and scrambled. Served with three pieces of toast of different bread and salad in caeser dressing. As you are sipping your coffee, you can hear the occasional sound of bells ringing from the opposite temple that creates a serene and calm environment. The best spot is at the courtyard where the natural light shines with a small garden on the side. Show less

I would rather be in this café having a meal, chilling out in peace and tranquility compared to the silly patrons queuing for hours in the hot sun for chicken rice balls (at least 20-30 pax in line). Author: KahFuiKuala Lumpur, Malaysia

Author: ashleighb700

Author: PhillfoneWhangarei, New Zealand
Title: Great cafe with excellent food and nice staff
Review: My wife and I are regulars at Melaka restaurants, we saw this one on trip advisor and thought we would give it a try.The staff are very nice and the food is great, a good fusion selection that is very different from the standard fare found around jonker street.Highly recommendedShow less

Author: kai-elsKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Rustic, Nice Atmosphere, Friendly Staff
Review: A slice of history comes alive when you visit this cafe located at Jalan Tukang Besi. This street is named thanks to former metal traders who ply their trade at the particular place. The moment you walk into the cafe, you can see reclaimed wooden tables adorned with antiquated metalwork and also antique dining tables and chairs. At first sight, it may look like a typical hipster cafe, but once you have settled in, it offers nothing but comfort to you. I liked their staff, and they were very friendly. One of the must-try when you visit this cafe is their lemongrass and pandan (screwpine leaves) drink. Of course, without a doubt coffee was aromatic and has a pleasant aftertaste. The food items that we tried were the Malacca Elvis pancakes and Kaya and Cheese Toast. Although there was nothing to shout about for the pancakes, I felt that the cafe was brave enough to take a plunge for the toast - adding a slice of cheese on toast and drizzled it with fragrant kaya. A very courageous move, I'd say.Another interesting fact about this cafe is their artwork that adorned one of the walls in the courtyard. There is a two-storey wall mural which tells the story of how the cafe got its name. In Zulu, “kaya” means “home”, while in Turkish, it means “stone”, which is appropriate for this cafe as it has a lot of exposed brick walls. I would say that this is a pleasant cafe to visit and do drop by if you get the chance. You will not be disappointed for sure.Show less

Author: DolphaniaKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: KAYA TOAST...A MUST HAVE!
Review: A nice cozy little cafe.Signature Drinks:[1] WELCOME TO MELAKA (refreshing herbal jelly with local coconut palm sugar in soya milk) ---> AVERAGE taste[2] SEE YOU AGAIN (homemade pandan leaves and lemongrass drink) This is a drink you should order.For Signature food, we tried the MELAKA 'ÉLVIS' whish is basically pancake stack with combination of sliced bananas, kaya, peanut butter and chocolate. Dont waste your money on this as it is average. The pancakes at THE DAILY FIX is 100times better. You should however opt to try their KAYA TOAST. That would be a better option and it was yummy!Show less

Author: WanderingNekoMelaka, Malaysia
Title: Beautiful cafe but overpriced.
Review: This cafe has a very relaxing ambience and a nostalgic feeling to its ineterior. The menu is quite limited but seems interesting. However, the price is definitely slightly overpriced for the value. I do understand that it is mostly due to its central location in the historic streets. While I see how it is acceptable for tourists, it is definitely not a place locals would go often. If you are craving for some western style cuisines, do go here! Show less

Author: TrueReview94Melaka, Malaysia
Title: A Malacca cafe with a Malaccan spirit
Review: Okay, first of all, this Cafe is not the best cafe to describe Malacca. Malacca is a state full of history and culture, this cafe is new and modern with antique looking furniture. Malacca is unique and one of a kind, this cafe have similar menus found all over hipster cafes everywhere. And yes, this cafe looks like a typical hipster cafe.Even though so, i still think this cafe do represent the Malaccan spirit.What defines a Malaccan spirit? Malaccans are bold and brave, interesting and unpredictable, yet relax and cheerful. What this cafe lacks in describing the Malaccan spirit in their decor,they described them in their food.This cafe serves western food. Although so, their food is the very best description of the malaccan spirit. For example, the salmon on toast. The flavour of this dish is truly bold as the combination of salmon and sesame mayonnaise is one that been describe as weird, but the combination does work out well. This dish consisted of smoked salmon topped with egg, salad served on top of a black charcoal toast and dressed with sesame mayonnaise. At first i paused on the idea of eating such a brave yet weird combination, thinking that it might be some chef trying to be fancy with weird ideas but it turns out i was wrong! this combination worked well. i had a hard time finding any words to describe the flavour except for courageous and interesting. However despite all that, this food is surprizingly comforting. It is packed with flavour, yes, but it does not do it to the extend of "hurting" your taste buds, instead the flavour sits in your mouth. This is due to how the toast balances the strong taste of the sesame mayonnaise and gives your a memorable aftertaste that makes you want to come back for more.Next, I tried the seafood chowder. This dish is very different than the normal seafood chowder i had. This seafood chowder is spicy and tangy compared to other more comforting ones i had in other restaurants. But hey, what can i say, this cafe is really unpredictable. Nonetheless, the taste of the seafood chowder is there and it was the kind of dish that you dont expect it to be but yet pleasantly surprise that you enjoyed it. The chowder was interesting, but for a non-spicy fan like me, it not my bowl of chowder. And for the service. The staff is informative of the dishes, the dishes are served within reasonable time, and are always cheerful. I like the fact they introduce a dish to you like how a friend would, but did not get pushy when you rejected their offer. All in all it makes a very comforting experience dining in this cafe. So how does this cafe flared up in describing the malaccan spirit? The flavour is bold and brave, the food is interesting and unpredictable, and the service is cheerful. As for relaxing, as far as my dining experiences goes, i never felt so comforting in a cafe before. All this while i had went into cafes after cafes with the sole purpose of tasting and reviewing their dishes and services, always serious yet worried in case i miss out on anything important. This cafe is by far the only cafe which i sit down and felt truly relaxed, knowing the fact that nothing would go wrong if i conclude that this cafe had great food and great service. Nothing but this cafe had successfully represents the relaxing nature of the town of Malacca.All in all, great service, great food, great dinning experience. a 5/5. Keep up the great work Kaya-Kaya.Show less

Author: Nicholas TSingapore

Cappuccinos was ok, but quite weak/milky. Juice was ok, served in a cute glass bottle.Atmosphere was quiet, few guests (which we seemed to scare away with our presence).Friendly staff. Over all good, but nothing special and a bit too pricey. Show less

Author: LeeWenJIan

Author: Jiamin_OKuala Lumpur, Malaysia

Author: 128lhrh
Title: Far from the madding crowd
Review: As this shop is at the opposite end of Jonker street where the crowd usually starts from opposite the Red square, the shop was a nice respite for tired feet.The popiah was not well made compared to other tighter looking ones I've seen but tasty enough with pork lard in the turnip filling.Try the 8 treasures tea which is pleasantly sweet and herbal.I bought 2 dumplings to bring back to KL and the lady owner advised not to put in the fridge that very day of buying them but to put in the fridge on the second day. The dumplings cost $6 ringgit and was the most traditional of nonya dumplings I have seen with the blue pea flower staining part of the dumpling. I saw others try the rojak and the laksa which looked a small portion.All in all, this is a quaint place to try local food compared to the over crowded cafes along Jonker street.Show less

Author: simplytravelandeatSingapore, Singapore
Title: Mixed feelings about the food
Review: As the entire family was a big fan of popiah, this place became apparent for us to visit. That’s a private parking spaces for those who are driving right across the street and they charged RM10 for a lot.Crossed over and you will find this small little shop, unassumingly located at the end of the famous jonker street. We ordered the popiah, nyonya dumpling and Rojak to share. The popiah, filled with pork lard which is a trademark of the popiah serves here in melaka. It enhance the taste of the entire popiah not forgetting the texture as well. However, the popiah was loosely held and the turnip was a bit too plain for our liking. The rojak was very average as well. The item that stood out was the good old nyonya dumpling! The glutinous rice was very soft and fragrant. And it totally complemented the very flavorful pork wrapped. As such, a rather mixed bag when it came to the food offered here. They do serve laksa which we didn’t try. The dumpling was good but the rest that we had was really average.Show less

Author: dandygl0betr0tterKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Surprisingly delicious

Author: melmeleats
Title: Poh Piah's skin was too thick!
Review: Didn't really get the hype over this place honestly for the popiah skin was too thick to thoroughly enjoy the ingredients within. Loved the crunchy beansprouts but the boiled radish was not crunchy or flavourful enough for me.

Author: rcck1Pahang
Title: Amazing popiah
Review: After walking throughout the length of Jonker Street we chanced upon this unpretentious shop at Jalan Kubu,a road that intersects Jonker Street at one end. We were greeted courteously by an elderly man who gave us good recommendations on what was available at the shop. We ordered the popiah, Nyonya Laksa, rojak and their Nyonya dumpling. All that we ordered were indeed very good especially the popiah. One bite into it and we could taste the crunchy pork lard that made all the difference in this popiah. Highly recommended.Show less

Author: The_Traveler010710Shah Alam, Malaysia
Title: Nice Poh Piah & Other Local Delicacies
Review: We ordered the famous poh piah, Nyonya chang & fruits rojak after our lunch at The Baboon House. The Poh piah tasted good, can taste the fried lard! The nyonya chang is also worth a try. Do not miss the fruits rojak, the crunchy fruits with very delicious rojak sauce. Show less

Author: 191carolefSwitzerland
Title: Back in time food and ambiance
Review: We really enjoyed their freshly made popiah - they catered to all the different requests regarding spiciness and vegan options. The laksa was simple but delicious and the rojak was also freshly made and tasty. The highlight is definitely the popiah - haven’t had such good ones for years. Show less

Author: Lisa CKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Little shop for popiah
Review: We came here for after lunch and ordered popiah and rice dumplings, rojak. I like the popiah which is similar to the ones in a Seremban, Negeri Sembilan. It has pieces of lard that makes all the difference. The rice dumplings was sweet, didn’t quite like it.Show less

Author: sbf67Brisbane, Australia
Title: Local’s place
Review: We were walking past and I saw they had poh piah so we stopped and it was an inspired decision. We had poh piah, nyonya dumplings and lime juice water. Also served by people who looked like they had been doing it for years but still loved what they do. We will be back for the rojak tomorrow!!Show less

Author: daviddE8348XPMadrid, Spain
Title: Best food of Melaka
Review: We went to Poh Piah Lwee this afternoon for lunch :)It was amazing and cheap. They showed us how to cook it, such a warming people and really nice popiahs. 2€ for the meal/persons. I ate three Popiahs and dumplings. Absolutely Best of the city without doubt if you apprrciate food. #must. Thank you !!!- Local place: don’t expect nothing luxury or fancy- no need resrvation: it goes fastShow less

Author: bucketlisttravellersSydney, Australia
Title: Great nyonya food
Review: We came here for lunch and had the popiah, nyonya rice dumpling and mushroom noodles. The popiah in particular was excellent, which is what we’d hoped for given the restaurant is named after that dish.The owner took good care of us, ensuring we had a good table and recommending dishes for us to try. The food came out super quick and was great value at 13.50 ringgit for the lot. We liked that there were pictures on the walls of the different dishes so we could just point at what we liked the look of.Show less

Author: MrsJMoopPerth, Australia
Title: Best lunch in Malacca
Review: By far the best meal of our trip yet. The lady who served us, chose our meals for us. Noodles and pork for the kids and the rice dumplings and crepes with filling (not too sure of the traditional name) for us. It was so full of flavour! Lovely service, very cheap at only 27 RM for us all. Thank you! Show less

Author: Spotty-LeopardSingapore, Singapore
Title: RM$5.5 Nonya Dumpling
Review: Eat their nonya dumpling which has a unique spice that is subtle and special. Unique taste that is truly Malacca.Show less

Author: AileenChuaKampung Subang Baru, Malaysia
Title: Yummy nyonya dumplings
Review: As the dumpling festival is round the corner, we went to try out the authentic nyonya dumplings here. They did not disappoint. Very nice with the tinge of good old days. Tastes very natural. Highly recommended.Show less

Author: gerarddutchy
Title: Rice dumbling for lunch
Review: I came here twice for a small midday snack. The rice rumblings are their speciality and taste quite original. If you're passing by and would like to have a quick snack this will be your place Show less

Author: 559tany
Title: Popiah and nyonya dumpling
Review: Rm5.50 each for nyonya dunpling. Popiah comes with pork lard but im not a fan so cant comment much. Sells noodles and other dishes too

Author: 901stanleylSingapore, Singapore
Title: Nice laksa
Review: One of my regular place to visit whenever we come to Malacca.There is not much varieties here in a family run business.The laksa and popiah is a must try !!Show less

Author: limwwKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Yummy snacks
Review: Shop is old & small but authentic. A number of food selections. They are known for Poh Piah & Nyonya Dumpling (blue colour stained by a type of flowers). I like their Laksa (slightly spicy noodle with a nice fragrance). To some customers, they may feel it is pricey.Show less

Author: Weemeister
Title: Grandma's Nonya dumpling
Review: We stopped by to try the dumpling even though we were stuffed from breakfast. The blue pea flower is used to tinge the sticky rice, the way my grandma used to do it. None of the artificial colorings of the modern day. Little chunks of dried winter melon add a sweet touch to the savoury meat. N the ketumbar or coriander gives a distinct flavour different from the dumplings of other dialect groups. This is the way my grandma used to make it. Even the meat is finely diced up n not in huge chunks - the mark of the Nonya who prides herself in her genteel cooking ways.Show less

Author: rachellwySeminyak, Indonesia
Title: The Poh Piah worth the visit
Review: As the name of the shop suggests, the signature dish of course is their Poh Piah. I don't usually eat Poh Piah in Singapore but the Poh Piah here is delicious!! Went back twice in two days for the Poh Piah. Tried other dishes tkk - rojak, nyonya laksa and bachormee too. Not bad but not the best I've eaten either. Show less

Author: MarcusTan94
Title: Nothing special
Review: Small place with limited seats, mediocre and overpriced food. Lady there was being a little pushy when selling her food, not the greatest experience.

Author: Isaac L
Title: Lunch
Review: Heard of this shop review. Order their nyona rice dumpling, fruits rojak and poh piah. Rice Dumpling with lots of meat fillings , Rojak was a little wet but overall taste is ok. And the poh piah is unique as they add in crispy pork lard. Overall, nothing special just the local taste. No aircon limited siting space. Need to park a distance and walk as there is limited car park lots. Price is a bit $$$ Show less

Author: Flai64Singapore, Singapore
Title: Incredible Gratifying Nonya Poh Piah, Rojak & Laksa
Review: It's a hole in the wall shop in the famed Jonker walk that sells only nonya laksa, popiah, bachang, and rojak. We had them all for RM30 (2 people). Simply mouth watering, authentic and totally gratifying. The laksa gravy is so fragrant with taste of spices all blended. Very 'lemak' as they would say in peranakan. The rojak reeks of melaka flavors and deliciousness. And the humble popiah was elevated to another level as you bite into crushed crispy pork lard in the midst of the turnip mix. A must go for anybody visiting melaka. You will not regret!!!!Show less

Author: tawjanp
Title: Cheap and delicious
Review: Very nice rojak and poh piah. Dumpling is also impressive. The place is quite far from tourist area but its worth to walk

Author: CarolineCHee
Title: Yummilicious POH Piah and Nyonya Chang
Review: A little restaurant close to Blanc Boutique hotel. Serves real good POH Piah and Nyonya Chang. A must try for all.

Author: nonikuliner
Title: One of the best poh piah in town
Review: The food here is generally good and relatively very cheap. The taste is authentic, price is about half the price at jonker street while only several step away. The location is basically at the further end of jonker street from the river.

Author: segaryputrajaya
Title: Excellent Poh Piah
Review: I truly loved the taste of the Poh Piah, one of the best poh piah ever. The nyonya laksa was good, worth trying...was expecting for a larger prawn...the size of the prawns was too tiny☺ I'm a great fan of Rojak so I can't resist myself from giving it a try. In my opinion, it could have been good if the amount of sugar was less, the sugar actually spoilt the taste of the Rojak. Show less

Author: rnera
Title: Delicious!
Review: Easily in my top 3 best things I ate in Malacca was their poh piah. Crispy pork lard! The menu is literally photos on the wall. Dumplings were really good too.

Author: jen e
Title: Famous popiah
Review:
I am popiah fans 💚
Love the popiah, the ingredients use are so fresh, and special, full with love. The owner are loving too. A must try when you are in melaka, i would say.

Author: Ulun64
Title: Best Poh Piah and Nyonya Dumpling (Bak Chang)
Review: The best Nyonya Bak Chang I ever taste. The poh piah is also fantastic. It's must try if you are in Malacca.

Author: jlamslSingapore, Singapore
Title: Nonya Chang (dumpling) with blue pea flowers
Review: We visited today around 4pm and the owners advised that they only made dumplings this week as it is the Dumpling Festival (Tuen Ng festival). Ate the Chang with Chinese tea and yumz it was amazing. The taste exquisite and unique. We loved it so much we ordered another one to eat in and 7 to take away!!! Yummy visit .....Show less

Author: JeanWNSingapore, Singapore
Title: Desires of the buccal kind!
Review: Visited Malacca for 2 nights. Visited this place twice, does that say it all?Popiah Lwee is located on the right side of street near Northern end of Jonkers Street. Parking not easy so maybe good idea to Uber there n back. Besides if u drive, street parking while next to impossible, requires Malacca parking coupons. Alternative parking cost RM5 located about 100m down from entrance small lane to left of the red Karaoke platform (active at night) this way only in day, at night u have to approach from another side, there are some signs or "jaga kerata" guys aka "valets" for readers from overseas who probably won't need to park!This popiah is "to die for" but definately NOT HALAL for it contains lumps of yummy lard. Yes, not healthy but you're on holiday dispensation and YODO (You Only Die Once) hehe, my version. It's run by a small family led by Mr Choong, his wife Louise (or is it Lwee), son n daughter-in-law. That's them in pic. Check out posted operating hours. While there try their laksa , rojak and Malacca version of what they call "Bak Chor Mee" not the same as the Singapore version (which IMHO is tastier) ENJOY! Show less

Author: svangoh
Title: Yummy and Reasonable Price
Review: We pass by the first time and come again the next day. The laksa, bak zhang, popiah! Really love the popiah. Pipping hot and tasty~

Author: 543kft
Title: warm welcome
Review: The lady owner is very good. When we were there we were full. But the lady told us we were welcome even we had a break with a cup of water. Her heart like that, the shop May cook by heart.

Author: Reyna L
Title: Great Poh Piah and Nonya Dumpling
Review: Serves good pohpiah and nonya dumpling! Tried the rojak and asam laksa but it was soso. Do note that they are closed on Mon and Tue.

Author: nichole2204
Title: Nice Try !!! U will Love it~
Review:
accidentally reach this restaurant during searching for Melaka nyoya Dumpling.
Dumpling and pohpiah selling here are NICE one! u must have a try...

** in fact this is famous recommended on website, i miss for the research before reach here :p

Author: TimothySohSingapore, Singapore
Title: You either like it or hate it!
Review: I felt the Poh Piah was good but my parents thought they were too dry and tasted weird. All I can say is the filling is darker than the ones we normally eat and instead of strong shrimp based taste, the filling tasted overwhelmingly pork lard and more like Teochew duck sauce. Did not taste much prawn. Show less

Author: jojoccbSingapore, Singapore
Title: Brunch b4 heading home
Review: Service was good. Ordered1. Popiah2. Laska3 rojak4. Tabao nonya dumplingI super love the laksa served piping hot! The crispy fried dough in the rojak. And the calories i pile on chompin on the pork lard popiah.Can try! Need to wait as only 1 chef who is responsible to cook all the dishes for u Show less

Author: shiroatkl
Title: Went Twice
Review: basically during each visit to Melaka, without fail must visit this popiah place TWICE. The skin of the popiah is soft and fresh, the ingredients used is fresh and the key to the popiah is the nice fragrant pork lard.

Author: SohH62
Title: The best popiah I ever had
Review: We order 1 popiah, 1 nonya zhang, 1 rojia and 1 laksa. The place was very crowded but the service was still very good and the food still come very promptly. The popiah was so nice that we have to order 1 more, even we are already quite full. The laksa was pretty spicy.Show less

Author: JellyfishismeSingapore, Singapore
Title: Die die must try
Review: My wife and me have been patronising this little quaint shop, the deco is nothing to shout about, but if you have tried all sorts of Singapore popiah, then i suggest you have a go at this version, they have nice fragrant pork lard inside it, together with piping hot fillings, with a option to add more ingredients.Their laksa have a hint of lemon grass to it, and spicyness level will have me wanting to drink it all.Their gula Malacca sold in 1kg bags is weigh by an old scale, and weight varise by few grams, i brought 2 bags, one comes up to more than a kilo another is 986grams. Remember to also pack some handmade nonya dumplings too, for that price, its worth every dollar.Show less

Author: 832phyllis
Title: Nice poh piah & friendly folks
Review: Have been visiting this stall for years but not on regular intervals. Despite that, the friendly chap and his father remember both of us. Nicest poh piah tastes.

Author: raymondp604Metung, Australia
Title: Great little place just off the top of jonker
Review: Limited but what they do they do really well. Menu is 4 photos on the wall PopiahLaksaRojakNyonya dumplingsWe tried three and can vouch for them. Don't go expecting ambience this is just one up from a street stall but food is tasty fragrant and obviously popular. Shop was closing up at one on Sunday as they had sold out. Staff are friendly and good natured. Really like this place and will be back on next visit Show less

Author: CarlosCazorla
Title: Basic and tasty
Review: We discovered this place by chance and don't be deceived by the looks. It's a basic and simple restaurant with very tasty food. Very friendly and helpful staff. Excellent prices. I will definitely go back for more Poh Piah or Laksa

Author: MokisenSingapore, Singapore
Title: Little gem
Review: Decided to try this place as daughter wanted Poh Piah. It wasn't that easy to find as it's not well sign posted and the signage is quite faded and old.However the Poh piah was really yummy. Tasty with lots of lard flavour. Initially ordered two but didn't get enough as the kids finished most of it, so had to order more! The Nonya Chang was really good as well. They use authentic ingredients including the leaves to flavour the filling and the blue flower for the rice. Worth a visit!Please note that they are closed on Monday and Tuesday.Show less

Author: bhcohMelaka, Malaysia
Title: Worth a try
Review: This place sells Poh Piah, Rojak, Laksa and Bak Chang. In my opinion all the dishes are good as it suits my taste. The Laksa is nice and spicy so don't try it if you cannot handle it hot. The Rojak is as how you like it, so you can request for extra or less things in it. The Poh Piah is slightly different but to my taste. The Bak Chang is also to my taste buds as it has more spices than normal which some people may not like. Give it a go I think it is worth a try.Show less

Author: Sabrina_Pat_Ro
Title: Awesome Poh Piah
Review: this was the 2nd time we had come to holiday. We made sure we had come by again to have the Poh Piah, Rojak Buah & the Noodles. Still the same will come again when we come to Melaka.

Author: Joannacheah
Title: Famous But not Honest
Review: Bought 4 prepacked gula melaka labelled as 1 kg each. After weighing it at home, all well below 930gram each. Worst still at 904gram a pack. Unethical...Show less

Author: MrGoh
Title: Extremely Yummy
Review: The poh piah here is very special. They put lard inside. Super yummy!! The coffeeshop is very cramp. It's a eat and go place.

Author: lui_py86Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Yummy laksa
Review: My husband and I arrived before 10.30 a.m. so we managed to park very near to this eatery. We both ordered their famous laksa. It is indeed good. Rich in taste and heavy with aroma. The laksa is served piping hot which I enjoyed much. I find the portion quite small though, even for a small eater like me. Perhaps the cook is just being thoughtful to have prepare their laksa in small portion so that your tummy could have more space to sample their famous popiah, rojak or Nyonya chang. I tried their popiah and Nyonya chang too. Most popiah in Malacca contained pork lard. And this one does too. As I don't usually eat pork lard, I don't take this to my liking. A friendly aunty promoted heavily on their Nyonya chang. So I bought some to eat in the evening. The aunty purposely pack me some freshly made ones as I mentioned I will keep for tomorrow to eat, despite some ready made are hung outside. However, the Nyonya dumpling tasted too soft to my own liking as well.Show less

Author: HoNdaViNcESingapore, Singapore
Title: Nice Laksa & Popiah
Review: The Laksa is better Popiah.Laksa is quite spicy. Non-spicy eaters have to be caution.Laksa is very nice! It has the usual ingredients like cockles, prawns and fish cakes. Highly recommended!Popiah is very unique as it has fried pork lard. This is the key ingredient.Uncle Robert and auntie are very nice and thoughtful people. Non-airconditioned. So be prepared to sweat when eating Laksa.Show less

Author: saradeardear
Title: LOVE LOVE THE FOOD
Review: Great great great Poh Piah, thumbs up even for vegetarian option! Must try the dumpling too ! Will go back again ! Cheap n good food at one end of jonker street!

Author: cityangel78
Title: Very surprised with the popiah ingredients.
Review: I shocked with the first bite of the popiah.. Inside got pork lard. That make the popiah so delicious.. The blue rice bachang aslo taste very nice.

Author: Hannah A
Title: Good Laksa and Popiah!
Review: Nice owners and were very accommodating to tourists that wanted to try local food. Come if you want to experience quality Malaysian food!!

Author: sv628
Title: i'm not sure
Review: i'm not sure but it was being recommended by don't know which page so I went purposefully to try out. Maybe just some accidents on that day so it tastes not really great. I got better recommendation!

Author: AAdrivesingapore
Title: Yummy popiah and Rojak!
Review: Loved the popiah with pork lard bite size hidden in the fillings! And the Rojak is good too. Not impressed w the nonya dumpling. Prefer the other fame stall. This dumpling rice tasted bland and the fillings too "fatty". Real friendly folks who are proud of their creations. Saw other folks enjoying their noodle (laksa and minced pork) but am too filled with other street yummies to taste these noodles.Show less

Author: Xin-FangKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Poh Piah is recommended!
Review: The shop is located away from Jonker Street. Affordable price with tasty food.We strongly recommended its poh piah. The filling was delicious, cooked with lard. Yummy! I am not a poh piah fan, but this dining experience has changed my perception of poh piah. We also ordered laksa. It may look spicy and hot, but to our surprise, it did not. The rojak consists of sengkuang (sweet turnip), cucumber, fried flour dough, and pineapple slices. We ate with its special sauce, and it was appetizing as our brunch.Show less

Author: 309jackiepPerth, Australia
Title: Good popiah but not nyonya Chang
Review: Popiah was quite yummy because of lard in the filling but rather costly at RM4.00 each roll. Almost bought the nyonya Chang but decided to try one first, which was very fortunate I did. The pulut was way too soft and the filling had way too much coriander, could hardly taste the winter melon.....not passable. Don't bother ordering coffee as well, this place does injustice to good old Melaka Kopi O.Show less

Author: myclehoo
Title: Not worth the time
Review: The "famed" laksa was mediocre, at best. Wasn't any good at all. Poh piah (spring roll) was a little better but nothing to shout about. Give it a pass if you have more popular options available to you at Jonker Walk.

Author: 118majat
Title: Tasty!!
Review: The dumpling and the spring roll (nonya Chang and poh piah are the names I think)  are a must try. Staff very friendly.

Author: livelytania
Title: Delicious fresh spring rolls!
Review: We went for the spring rolls and weren't disappointed. Full of fresh ingredients! Just around the corner from Jonker Walk, a little local place to escape from the crowded street.

Author: babyxan88Subang Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Poh Piah Lwee - Yummy tasty poh piah with pork lard
Review: Today, let me tell you about "Poh Piah Lwee" located just along the shoplots (on the right) before turning in to Jonker Walk.The poh piah, RM3, here is really yummy! The jicama is nicely marinated and boiled in a way that it is not too dry, not too sweet and best of all it's just right! Crunchy, fresh, sweet and mix really well with all the other ingredients in the poh piah. What I love most about Malacca poh piah is that you can actually find fried pork lard oil inside! The one I tried at Bunga Raya was very wet and oily, they were really generous on the pork lard oil and sauce but it was abit overwhelming. At Poh Piah Lwee, the amount is just right, just perfect!Show less

Author: 9357MarkYSingapore, Singapore
Title: Absolute super (sinful) breakfast
Review: Brought my work team mates to try out the super breakfast here. All 14 of us. We ate poh piah which has pork belly bits (猪油泡)the pork lard bits you will find in char Kway teow. This made the big difference in taste. Crunchy and fragrant. We also tried the lasksa which is something like curry noodle. After that we ordered nonya changs plus the melaka version of bak chor mee (肉挫面). Everything was yummy and sinful. Wonder what's the effect on our cholesterol..ah but that's not going to stop us from enjoying our breakfast having come all the way from Singapore for our first team building trip. The aunty at this shop is very friendly and keep on recommending us to try more and eat more. It's a traditional kopitiam style setting. People there are friendly and many locals go there for a sat morning breakfast. We even got a customer to take some group photos for us.Also sold me some parking coupons (this is called value added service) as we parked nearby and the traffic police came by to check and issue summons. Singapore plates are a sure magnet for their attention. ☺One thing for sure my team mates will remember this place and will visit it again if they come up to melaka in future. It's at the end of jonker St junction with Jln Kubu. Show less

Author: sibilino
Title: Great popiah and bakchang!
Review: Humble and warm kopi in Melaka with a short but outstanding menu list. The popiah (big spring-roll stuffed with a sort of vegetables and really tasty), the bakchang and the laksa were excelent dishes. Very friendly staff also.

Author: wenaili
Title: Yummy Poh Piah, thumb's up!
Review: Poh Piah was excellent. Old school and robust. Yummy! Laksa was enjoyable too, however the Nonya Zhang was only average. Nonetheless, I will recommend the Poh Piah. Thumb's up!

Author: MxJ1504Singapore, Singapore
Title: Very good nonya zhang!!
Review: If you are looking for a place with good nonya zhang, this is the place! Please call before going down to order! They hardly have enough to sell to walk in customers. Prepared on the day itself, with a lot of fillings! Curry laksa and dry noodles are also good, popiah has got a lot of fried pork lard, really tasty!!! Show less

Author: Liz TLiverpool, United Kingdom
Title: Authentic place to taste popiah and rojak
Review: Great, shady little place to cool off with fresh lime juice and recharge your batteries with tasty popiah (fresh spring rolls containing beansprouts, tofu, pork crackling, coriander, turnip) and sweet and sour crunchy rojak salad. The friendly proprietor wears a distinctive baseball cap pushed back on her head and an apron and she knows what you need to eat! (There are only a few things on the menu anyway!). Let her suggest and don't worry about the price - it won't be expensive! Lunched here twice on my first trip to Melaka and returned again on my most recent trip. Yum. Show less

Author: AgnesW1
Title: Short break
Review: The pop piah was delicious and so was the laksa. There were fried lard inside the pop piah which was  very yummy. Laksa was really nice. The jung was so-so as there were better ones. Excellent place for snack or light lunch.

Author: weiminn2018
Title: Popiah with crackling n laksa
Review:
Popiah is served with egg skin and condiments of pork crackling. Tasty "bangkuang" filling and chili.

Laksa was tasty with cockles but chili hot.  Not for the faint hearted.

Good prices Rgt4 for laksa unlike some other places where they overcharge because it's popular.

Author: KayaToastedSingapore, Singapore
Title: Only nonya chang was great
Review: Went there mid-afternoon so absolutely no crowd. The shop keepers were very friendly. Was there on a Friday so no popiah but had the laksa, rojak and nonya chang. The laksa was not too bad, more like noodles in a light, salty curry sauce but could be I am used to more lemak laksa. The rojak was ok but nothing to write home about. What I really enjoyed (and will go back for when I return to Malacca) is the Nonya chang. It was very tasty - had that great balance of sweet and salty and it was stuff full of meat. I preferred it to the one from East & West Rendezvous Show less

Author: lillopillo
Title: Nice and cheap local food
Review: We had the spring rolls  (popiah), laksa, salad (rojak), dumpling. Everything tasted good and spicy. I recommend!

Author: BilledithBudapest
Title: Best meal in Malaysia, address correction
Review: This place has the travellers triple crown: tasty, local, cheap food.Best laksa we had in Malaysia after traveling here for a month. They also do a great Pohpiah (veg etc rolled in a fresh crepe), and amazing Nonya dumplings ( filled with amazing Bbq pork) Fresh lime juice is good and not sugered up like a lot of others.Owners speak English and were helpful in accommodating my vegetarian wife.Trip Advisor shows it a few blocks north of its actual location. Go south a few blocks and its a small shop on the east side of the road. Does not look like much but don't underestimate it. Hope this helps!Show less

Author: Glampacking
Title: Delicious and great price
Review: We shared a laksa, poh piah and a dumpling for lunch. All the dishes were great but especially the poh piah and laksa, it makes you want more! For under RM 15 this is a great price for budgettravelers.The location is in a small shop right of jonker street. Highly recommendable!Show less

Author: DMbackpackerBury, United Kingdom
Title: Best Laksa ive had in Malaysia
Review: Great little place just off jonker walk. only open until 5pm, so only for lunch. the laksa was amazing, spicy, coconutty and with cockles and shrimps. i could have had another bowl.the friendly staff cook it right there infront of you. the lime juice was excellent too. great value for money. the popiah was very fresh too.go here for lunch, its cheap, fresh, clean and tastes great.Show less

Author: team-sox
Title: Delicious, local food!
Review: This place has amazing local dishes. Laksa for 4 rm - spicy, lemony, fishy coconut broth with noodles and soft biscuitsPoh piah for 3,30 rm - a big fresh spring roll stuffed with veg, crunchy meat and warm cabbageBut the best thing I've eaten in a very long time were the dumplings!They're 4,5 rm a piece and they're totally worth it. They're triangle shaped rice packages cooked in a banana leaf, and one corner they have blue rice that has been coloured with some kind of flower and its filled with a sweet-sour sauce and shredded porkReally if you're in Melaka go there and eat it is yummy beyond description and the staff is lovely too!Show less

Author: cmfchris
Title: Yummy Poh Piah simple and no frills
Review: Their popular food is lard poh piah. I can only say it's delicious and I'll remember the taste for a long time. Their nyonya curry noodles aren't bad either. The nyonya dumpling is also all right. The proprietor and staff were helpful and friendly.

Author: ShiouSingaporeSingapore
Title: Sent to buy nyonya pork dumpling (bak chang) there
Review: This is the place for Rojak, nyonya laksa, Poh Piah and nyonya dumpling. It is our second time there this Sep and we had requests from friends to bring back the dumpling (RM 4.50 ea). I think the dumpling is above average. You can order the dumpling to be ready for pick up before departure. It is a good place for the above comfort foods or to sample them. It is not usually crowded in the morning or lunch time and good to visit at the beginning or end or your Jonker Walk. For children who may not enjoy any of their food, you can order "wan tan" noodle from the stall two shops away to be eaten there. It is at 14 Jalan Kubu at 50m or so beyond the other end of Jonker Street from "San Shu Gong" (supermarket for packaged Melaka/Malaysia food).Show less

Author: Scott BLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Tasty Popiah
Review: A tiny little place on the very edge of China Town, you probably wouldn't stumble across this place without going looking for it. But it's worth finding for the local speciality Popiah. I was also talked into buying a steamed pork dumpling for the road, also very good.Show less

Author: SAWMUK
Title: Authentic street food
Review: This tiny place offers some tasty bites. It's like a mini hawker centre where you can get freshly made popiah, very tasty. We also had dumplings, made from meat and glutinous rice and coloured blue on top. Both of those dishes were the first time for us. The laksa was gorgeous, very rich with coconut milk and very spicy too. There were plenty of grazing locals, always a good recommendation.Show less

Author: Hawker78Burlington
Title: Pohpiah. Rojak. Laksa. Yum.
Review: Now, I'm a huge fan and student of Malaysian food lately, and was very pleased to come across this place. Yes, lonely planet approves, but that means little to me. The pohpiah were particularly good, and this is a dish that really has to be done right to impress. I won't divulge any secrets, but this was one of the better pohpiah on my travels, as well as a great rojak, much better than the Penang rojak that I'd had in similarly lauded spots. PPL's veers towards a sweet-sour (palm sugar-tamarind) and fishy version, with some kangkong (water spinach) thrown in. I chatted with the folks here for a while, too!Show less

Author: LeeSummerSingapore, Singapore
Title: Nice laksa and Nonya dumpling
Review: The shop is at the end of Jonker street, is a small shop with limited seats. The laksa is in metal bowl, the gravy is not as thick but the rich in taste and a bit spicy for those can't take spicy food. Will feel amaze for the nonya dumpling than the poh piah, the glutonous rice is totally cook and soft, the sweet pork inside is tasty. You can pre order the dumpling to take home. Will try the rojak for the visit.Show less

Author: 577brendaa
Title: Good popiah, laksa so-so
Review:
Order the more expensive version of the popiah if u want more pork lard in almost every bite.

The laksa didn't work for us, spicy and not what we expected.

Try the nonya Zhang as well but a bit on the expensive side.

Author: RoscoeHR
Title: This is something you should do if in Melaka
Review: My wife made me go here, she is a Poh piah fan, and I'm glad she did. This is not the poh piah I expected, it's more like a crazy delicious roti wrap made with very thin pastry. Im not sure if that is how they are meant to be and the fried spring roll like versions I have had before are the imitation, but they are both great. We also had a good laksa here. This is a small, sears maybe 15, place just off the main drag and is well worth a thought if you need lunch. Show less

Author: motameus
Title: Amazing
Review: The Poh Piah and Laksa were amazing - easily one of the best meals I've had in the three months I've spent in Southeas Asia

Author: jpk186240Penzance, United Kingdom
Title: Fabulous Poh Pia
Review: We stumbled on this tiny little place, trying to get away from the Jonker tourist trail. the lady who runs the cafe is so lovely and her freshly made poh piah were divine. It was full of locals who obviously all know her well, and they were clearly enjoying her dishes too.Strongly recommend this place, particularly if like us you want to experience authentic Malaysian food. Closed Mondays.Show less

Author: 916SamMelaka, Malaysia
Title: The Best Laksa I Have Ever Had!
Review: I was looking for the long lost taste of laksa that I had forgotten where I had tried before. I could only remember there was some finely chopped greenish vegetable floating in the gravy.Then came one day my Mother wanted to have Popiah and asked me to bring her to the nearest restaurant I could find. So there we were in this tiny little shop.I saw laksa so I ordered one serving for a try. The laksa beehoon was served in a dainty stainless steel wok with shrimps, tau pok, cockles, bean sprouts, thin strips of cucumber and finely chopped greenish vege!! And that was the exact flavour I had been looking for! Yum yum!! The gravy was thick enough and the aroma was irresistible. I couldn't help but take a second serving and promised myself no more other stall of laksa but this one.However, as the gravy is cooked using coconut milk, the calories are high. Consume it with care.The popiah and rojak are also a "must try" when we go there every time.Find out yourself and enjoy!Show less

Author: Farah L
Title: NOMZ
Review: We had the laksa, popiah and rojak! Portions were good to share with a mate. I like the laksa the most! Gravy was just right for me.

Author: Californienne1980
Title: Tasty
Review: Great popiah, great laksa, and great nonya style dumplings. The chef is really friendly too.

Author: shajipapa
Title: it's so different and very,very good.
Review: Located in between little india and chinatown. and the food is excellent and at least you know what ur eating.

Author: Bridget CForfar, United Kingdom
Title: The Best poh piahs in Melaka
Review: The poh piahs are THE BEST - last year we went every afternoon to get our fix. The woman who makes them touts out the opening saying they are the best poh piah and she is not over-boasting - they are!! The laksa is also very good. This year we stayed in Melaka during the week and were disappointed in that she wasn't open every day and then one day (Wed I think) she didn't serve the poh piahs, but we had the other specialty she made - see photo, sorry can't remember the name of them, but glutonous rice with blue colouring and sweet-ish pork in the inside. Okay, but not my cup of tea.Show less

Author: dyganonKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Bye Bye Sid's Pub, Hello GravyBaby
Review: Sid's pub is owned by GravyBaby. Everytime when we visited, The headline of receipt is always Gravybaby for years.GravyBaby has totally taken over the restaurant. No more pork is served. All sausage and bacon is horrible substitution. Look like we have to we have to find new place for drink now.Show less

Author: WatsonMark25Aberdeen, United Kingdom
Title: Unclear that there was a name change.
Review: So, there appears to have been a franchise/name change at Sid's!It is now called 'Gravy Baby'. It appears to be the same menu as Sid's but has a different aesthetic. Firstly, the location, decoration and choice of food is excellent. The quality of food is good too (so much so that we popped back in for cake the next day).My biggest gripe would be that they pride themselves on incredible cocktails and pies but were not serving alcohol while we were there. Just a shame really. That was my only major flaw (that and its generally a little pricey).Show less

Author: bigbrother888888
Title: average
Review: a bit dated now. past its former glory my other half said. food is satisfactory but why pay when you can get better atmosphere in other melaka venues

Author: Rosario_itBelgium
Title: Nice pub on the Malacca river
Review: We went to this pub also because the friend of mine with whom I was visiting Melaka is called Sid and so he was looking forward to make some picture in this pub.We ordered one sandwitch and a beer.The prices are not very cheap but the location is very wonderful.Show less

Author: sHannheSterSingapore, Singapore
Title: Gem of a good o’bar
Review: Was there the last night of the trip. Wished we tried them earlier! Chilling by the Malacca River at Sid’s is what a holiday night out with drinks should be - no overly loud music indirectly leading to a strained throat from raising your voice in order to chat with your friend seated right next to you, comfy and reasonably spaced seating arrangements and good o’single malts on the menu.Show less

Author: RossR908Thames, New Zealand
Title: Really just average
Review: Had lunch here today and were quite under whelmed. My wife got mushroom bruchetta which consisted of fine chopped mushrooms in a white sauce on what looked suspiciously like burger bun lightly toasted and covered with grated parmisan. She ended up only eating the topping. Expensive 3 tbs of mushroom. I had the fish and chips which wasn't to bad apart from the fish being overcooked. Menus are very grubby and unhygienic looking. Would I go back? Maybe!Show less

Author: dnaivaMunich, Germany
Title: Great location, great staff, great food
Review: There is a happy hour until 9pm when the bar is empty. It gets busy later on with life music playing in the background. The stuff speaks great English and is very competent. I recommend the nachos for food - tip top! The beer selection is quite limited, but they have a varianty of cocktails (according to the menu). Show less

Author: PatrickF581
Title: Nice place
Review: We went here for some drinks and snacks. Nice place by the water. Friendly staff. Ordered fries, portion was huge! Looking at the menu and glasses etc. It looks like they our a part of the Gravy Baby franchise, which is good quality food.

Author: RJCF1
Title: Great location with cold beer
Review: A  great place to have a cooling drink overlooking the river. As has been said, no A/C but plenty of open windows giving a cooling breeze. Food was good and the service excellent. Highly recommended.

Author: RandolphCarter1919Australia
Title: British pub, not as bad as it sounds
Review: I would never ever in Australia frequent a British or Irish themed pub, they are tacky with mediocre beers and food. We stopped into Sids as it was really close to our hotel and the thing that turned us was just how friendly and helpful the lads that run the place are. A week in Melaka and we had a few snacks, beers and cocktails here every second day, including one big session and the beer was cold, the snacks were good but the staff excelled. Give these blokes a pay rise.Show less

Author: WranglerdarlesBendigo, Australia
Title: Lovely cool drinks
Review: Lovely spot to sit with a cool drink after walking up and down Jonker Street. Not air conditioned but to sit by the open window over looking the Malacca river was pleasant and restful.We wanted a light lunch so ordered a ploughmans lunch to share, not very good compared to an English ploughmans lunch but satisfied our hunger none the less.Show less

Author: k7cqPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Mutton Varavul
Review: Being Indian, I know how Varavul is supposed to taste. This dish was extremely spicy (they said it was not supposed to be). There was no Indian vegi (2 salad leafs is all we got). The Mutton was mostly gristle and bone, very little meat. The 1 piece of pappadum was stale. The whole dish was terrible. Don't order this dish. The beer and atmosphere was great as usual.Show less

Author: DeathsDragon95Hinckley, United Kingdom
Title: Really good
Review: We saw this place when we were on the boat cruise as we passed it and looked nice, windows open with views of the river and looked busy. We decided to try the place after the river cruise had finished. It is just next to the main bridge in the centre and has a couple of entrances the main entrance which is round the corner on another road from the bridge and the side alley is off of the bridge which can be easier.The place was very dark inside with the lighting being very dim if not much lighting in the building. We were lucky as when we arrived a table in the corner next to the window became available. We ordered our drinks which I had a chocolate milkshake which was really good, it had cream and brownie bits and would have it again. We were a bit peckish so decided to have a snack which we ordered the cheesy chips and gravy. This was really nice and has to be one of the best cheesy chips I have had, the gravy was really nice, thick and had a good strong taste.We saw another table get their food which looked really nice. This place serves British food and has a good choice. The food does sound appealing from the menu and if had been in Melaka longer then would have come back a few times to try different things from the menu. The food and drinks aren't cheap and probably roughly what you might expect for British food and good quality food is not a bit more expensive but this is common for the country. Overall this place is good to go to. It can get busy with people and you might not get a table by the window. The food is really good and the drinks are good too. The place is a bit too dark at night so can be a bit hard to see especially when you're eating it would be good to have a little bit brighter. The decor is nice, quite old feeling, there are interesting things around and there are different phrases hung on the walls which are funny. This place isn't cheap.
