Sadly we went there just before closing and there weren't any fish ball, otah, bean sprout or soup left. Chicken was solid, good tasting and cooked just nice(without blood). The rice balls were smaller than what we had expected as we had eaten the Singapore version which was huge and smooth textured without feeling the individual grain of rice(FYI-the rice balls are machine made to be of equal size). Don't forget to order the assam fish curry. We ordered the tail(there's head, tail or meat) as that was all left at that time. I'm not a fish nor an assam curry person but this I like very much. Sadly there was no bean sprout available but cabbage. Maybe because we were late and they were sold out.Shop is located at the start of Jonker Street diagonal from H&M next to the red building of Sum Sok Kong. Easy to find. Interior is like an antique conservation house and I assume the workers stay upstairs in the living quarters.Very reasonably priced for good quality food that is authentic chicken rice ball.Show less

Author: Nickolas HSingapore, Singapore
Title: Interesting Place
Review: Actually waited about 50 minutes on a Friday afternoon to taste the legendary chicken rice balls, with my 4 and 10 years old son... Sorry but not really to my liking. Chicken not as tender & they actually limit number of rice balls (half a chicken = 3 plates of rice balls) one can purchase. But for novelty, go ahead and try~Show less

Author: phen_poiSingkawang, Indonesia
Title: Queue to get the tasty food
Review: at jonker street , easy to spot because there will be a lot of people queuing at the entrance. after waited for sometimes , we will be greeted with "Rush Method Ordering" (hahaha it shocked me) it will be "for how may person ?" and "cabbage or fish ?" so confusing.(main dish is rice ball and that kind a boiled chicken so that cabbage or fish is side dish) but later the food arrived , it tasted good.Show less

Author: LeeWJ
Title: Chicken Rice ball up to expectation
Review: The chicken rice ball seems more like a novelty. Take that away, we still have a decent chicken rice dish. However, nothing that we could not find else where. The queue here is much better than Chung Wah across the street

Author: Brian194812
Title: Excellent lunch just off Jonkers.
Review: Excellent lunch stop. Chinese. Fast service with good selection of Malacca specialties including steamed rice and sliced pork. Good value for money.

Author: GAHT1
Title: Delicious chicken but....
Review:
the rice ball is overrated.  

The chicken was poached well and very good. 

We also ordered a side order of stir fried bean sprouts.  The simplicity of the dish was delicious. 

Try this as it is synonymous with melaka food culture.

Author: benwolf223
Title: best rice ball
Review: not only they serve rice ball, but also with cabbages and even liver. It's really good and I normally order 5 rice balls and steam chicken with liver

Author: choihoweboonPenang
Title: Not worth the value.
Review: I came from Penang, the food heaven and to rate this shop seems a bit unfair. Chicken rice is something very common in Malaysia (not to mention just Penang). This shop doesn't just sell chicken rice but some nyonya dishes too. Taste wise, it's really nothing can compare to a hawker in Penang. I would say, it's the to eat here is just for the environment....not for the food. So, what you are paying is for the environment. So, I'd rather have my meal somewhere if I have a choice. There's a item in the menu that shocked me. Asam Pedas priced at RM45.00.Show less

Author: JamesKMTanPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: The best chicken ball rice
Review: We went there as a group as part of thhe Photography Society of PJ tour of Melaka. This strategically located shop serves very authentic and delicious chicken ball rice. The rice is done just nice and the chicken was a little tough. Drinks comprising herbal tea and chinese tea was a bit pricey. The service is so fast. The queues are long but worth the wait.Show less

Author: Peter-aus44Perth, Australia
Title: Not $$ - $$$ in price.. good and cheap!
Review: Why does this restaurant get $$ to $$$ in price? We got chicken rice balls for 2 including plenty of chicken, plate of cabbage, Chinese tea for 2, for RM 20-ish. Good deal I think. We went at lunch, no line, got served immediately, food came out quickly. Our first chicken rice balls so not sure how it compares but it was good. Recommended by a local and she said it was her favourite chicken rice balls in Melaka.Show less

Author: Jeremy C
Title: Definately overrated
Review:
The rice ball is perfect, but as for the chicken, it is far below average. 

Considering the queue, I will not recommend.

Author: StefaniAyujakarta
Title: good food, clean place
Review: chicken is very tender and moist. rice ball is full of flavour. if you don't like rice ball you can order loose rice, but the flavour is less than rice ball. vegetable stir is crunchy, it's very delicious. I know there's other restaurant has longer queue, but this restaurant cannot be missed.Show less

Author: reneeSingaporesingapore
Title: Good Choice !
Review: We end up eating in Hoe Kee as there was a long queue at Chung Wah. It was a right choice as the chicken was sweet and tender. The rice ball was just OK for me but the assam fish was good. The restaurant is big and is more airy so it is more comfortable eating here. Show less

Author: elderlywmh
Title: The best steam chicken
Review: One of the best steam chicken in town but rice ball too small. Place too small, hence the queue but worth the wait.

Author: 574samanthag
Title: Local, delicious and simpel
Review: We just Walked in because we were hungry. Its very basic en local, but THE chicken with cumcumber, Rice balls and cabbage were very good. We ate here for lunch for 32RM (including 2 coconot drinks)

Author: JamieTan126
Title: Chicken Rice Ball
Review: Famous restaurant, all stalls are crowded. The meal is special & good taste, just the price may be bit expensive. But worth to have a try.

Author: teep0h
Title: Chicken Ball rice
Review: Came to Ho Kee after seeing crazy queue outside Chung Wah just across the street.It's was just 10am in the morning. We were quickly seated at Ho Kee which didn't have a queue yet but I did notice the railings near doorway which indicates the place will have queue as well.Ordered the chicken ball rice and the lady offered package with cabbage, Assam fish etc which I turned down. Was there to eat chicken ball rice. Drinks were usual herbal tea, soft drinks and Chinese tea. No coffee etc or even barley.Strange thing was that when I wanted to order more chicken balls they're said it wasn't possible due to limited balls and could only order the standard rice....slightly disappointed with that since it's supposed to be a chicken ball rice shop.Anyway the chicken was quite good and rice was decent.....I think the many reviews here are exaggerating that it's terribly bad but that's their opinion. I'd say it's a decent eatery and saves you the hassle of queuing at the Chung Wah but the fact they can't serve more balls is definitely silly on their part.Show less

Author: samanthas792Singapore, Singapore
Review: Melaka is supposedly famous for chicken rice ball. Its just a gimmick sales & marketing that someone has created & made it famous - is to eat rice rolled into riceballs.The chicken is tough and taste just normal. Stir fried veg is tasteless.Don't bother wasting money & calories on this chicken rice balls. U may go try satay celup, cendol, nyonya food, street food - fried oyster etcShow less

Author: Severine BGhent, Belgium
Title: expensive for what you get
Review: We were told to eat the famous melaka rice balls with chicken. They were good but not that special. Maybe they were better at other places. The riceballs are cheap (0,3rm each), but the chicken was a dissapointment. For 14rm we got only a tiny piece of chopped chicken (more bones than chicken). For 1rm we also got a tiny plate of cabbage. The whole was rather tasteless, but we got chilli sause wich made it better. We ate for 23rm but were still hungry. For that money you get much more at other restaurants. The staff was also quite rude.Show less

Author: Fuwa C
Title: Average
Review: Price is affordable. Limited seats inside. Go after 330pm less people and can eat comfortably. During lunch time it's full and had to Q up. Go during weekdays is advisable

Author: Choo N
Title: a must eat
Review: Been there for for lunch few times,never regret to come.Chicken rice、black bean soup and cabbage taste is good.

Author: Leong W
Title: A MUST VISIT in Melacca
Review: After so many year tried different chicken rice (rice ball) in Melacca. This 1 is still the best in town. Never regret to come here everytime.But 1 negative things is, they are shortage of employee recently maybe. They offer rice ball and normal rice to you,mix. Seriously, the normal nice is definitely different taste and texture. Still prefer the rice ball.Show less

Author: VC S
Title: Still the best chicken rice in town
Review: Two hours driving from KL. Very nice town to walk around and the chicken rice is excellent. Worth the trip to Melaka

Author: WidjajaH1
Title: Rice ball
Review: Hainam rice ball i think this one best of many place rise ball in melacca.. delicious.. order white chicken steam slice.

Author: im-young-jaeSingapore, Singapore
Title: Great food albeit long waiting time
Review: Food here was excellent and service at this area was prompt. The chicken rice ball was excellent and brings back old memories of the past. The service was pretty efficient even though there were a lot of customers and it was full house when we were there. Show less

Author: CrystalismKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Just another tourist trap... Below average chicken rice balls
Review: A very average chicken rice shop- just because they roll some chicken rice balls they call themselves famous and silly people like us queue. It's totally not worth the queue- they use cheap grade chicken and the doesn't have much chicken taste to begin with. Don't even start with the Asam fish- they steamed it before hand and placed it a long time before actually serving it. When it arrived at our table it was already cold and the fish is not fresh so it's smelly. So bad we didn't even touch 10% of it. Chicken rice balls just average... Go roll your rice balls into balls and that's all. If you're visiting Melaka for the first time.. Dun fall for this tourist trap and buy their bad service. They make sure you queue before the line otherwise they will scream at you till the whole shop stares at you. Gosh.... Any chicken rice in KL is better than this place!Show less

Author: YuanLiH
Title: Best chicken rice in melaka
Review: Overall is good, but not recommend rice ball, normal rice is nice, chicken taste good. Veggie is also good,no need queue for long time.

Author: Pau Chuan H
Title: Best chicken rice in jonker street
Review: Better than other famous chicken rice. The chicken is fresh. Average is good and the price is reasonable. After eat can visit the jonker street Art place....

Author: wynsum
Title: Overrated
Review: Based on feedback from the internet, this is the best among the three.  I am disappointed.  Chicken is tender but the rice is too wet and missing chicken oil aroma.  I pref the Hainanese chicken rice in Singapore and KK.

Author: Madeline Y
Title: Worth visiting
Review: Didn't have to wait too long as it was still early .the chicken is tender and well flavoured.. my kids simply love the rice balls. Worth the visit .

Author: albeechuaSingapore, Singapore
Title: Great food & service
Review: Tastey chicken & chicken rice ball! Meat was well flavoured and tender. Rice ball too.Service was promptly and good. Staff would also recommend other food to go along if you are unsure what to have other than the signature chicken rice balls.You could make use of the time while waiting for the food, to admire or take picture of the architecture of the shop. Show less

Author: Didier_Cayrac
Title: Simple yet refined tasting food - and a great experience!
Review:
This restaurant has mostly ONE dish: chicken rice balls... but it's DELICIOUS - simple yet subtle... and cheap!
highly recommended for a quick lunch.

Author: Colin C
Title: Just an average restaurant
Review: Had lunch with family and ordered 1 plate of steamed chicken, stir fry cabbage and rice balls. Was attended to fairly fast by the staff, which is good..but taste of the food is nothing special or unique...good for tourists to taste it once when in Melaka.Show less

Author: SalouWLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Wonderful comfort food
Review: We thoroughly enjoyed our meal here. We were worried from the length of the queue that we may have to wait a long time but the owner runs a tight ship and service is fast and efficient - we waited no longer than 15 minutes. This was the first time I had tried chicken and rice balls so I don't have anything to compare it to but we really did enjoy our meal. The chicken was tender and delicious and the rice balls really complimented it and soaked up the juices. It was simple yet comforting food and just what we needed after a few days of far too much gourmet eating! Will definitely go back.Show less

Author: TheresaSeow
Title: Best Chicken
Review: My whole family really enjoyed our meal here. Worth the wait. The chicken is superb, even the chicken breasts was so tender and yummy.

Author: trvkakiSingapore, Singapore
Title: Over rated
Review: This is probably overrated with all the hype about Melaka chicken rice ball. Firstly, the rice ball is nothing to shout about but it does give you a different texture compared to chicken rice. Chicken meat was tough and not smooth.The Assam fish was priced reasonable and tastes fine while the cabbage was considered ok. Place itself though no air con has fans mounted and is quite comfortable.Show less

Author: Wewe_vipPenang, Malaysia
Title: Taste ok, but thumb up for their service!
Review: The taste of the chicken and rice ball is so so, acceptable. But really thumb up for their quick and friendly service. It took not more than 15 mins to be seated and serve with food, although need to queue up and wait. All the menu and price are well stated on the wall outside the shop itself, for customer to have a look while waiting to be serve. Good service, good environment.Show less

Author: StanleyFoo
Title: Cheap and reasonably good
Review: Not expensive, food reasonably good, not super good. Always rum out of rice ball. Rice is nice but rice balls are better. Chicken is only average.

Author: KayJee_123Western Australia, Australia
Title: Great chicken rice served in a relaxing and homely environment
Review: Hoe Kee is our go-to place for chicken rice balls whenever we're in Melaka. We usually try to get there early in the morning (around 10-ish) before the Jonker Street area starts to get crowded.We went as a family of four adults and shared a nice range of dishes: chicken served with cucumber and a few pieces of liver/gizzards on the side, 20 rice balls, a plate of cabbage speckled with carrots and fishcake, a bowl of assam fish and the obligatory complimentary chilli sauce. (Unfortunately, their delicious black bean soup wasn't available at the time we arrived.) All in all, the bill came up to RM 58 with four cups of chilled herbal tea and a can of soft drink. A very reasonable feed!I would highly recommend this place if you are looking to taste some good quality chicken rice balls in a relaxing and homely environment. Service is great and the shop's old-world charm makes it a very pleasant spot to stop for a bite of one of Melaka's famous dishes.Show less

Author: ivorytan88
Title: Best chicken rice in melacca
Review: There are many chicken rice shop in melacca. I personally like their chicken rice ball and tender soft chicken. They have home cooked black bean & chicken feet soup at RM1 a bowl is cheap but delicious.They always our priority choice.

Author: waizhunc
Title: Traditional and local chicken rice
Review: We came here on weekend morning before it got crowded. Personally recommend to come here early morning during weekend or normal weekday. The food here is nice. If you are trying to test some local or traditional Malaysia or Melaka food, here it's one of the place you may try of. The price is a bit cozy for local Malaysian but worth a try if you haven't try it before. Show less

Author: feltroneuGeorge Town, Malaysia
Title: Long queuing for Chicken rice ball
Review: Though chicken rice ball is special in Malacca, the overall taste is still inferior compare Penang Hainanese chicken rice. This was the first time we wanted to try the chicken rice ball but during a hot sunny day and long queuing, it is not worth for the time and money paid for. The service is slightly below expectation maybe due to lot of customers queuing, it seemed that things that we ordered are pricey. With just a half chicken, 10 chicken rice balls, 1 soup, 3 plate of chicken rice and 4 drinks, it costed RM49. In fact I gained a good experience how the chicken rice ball tasted.Show less

Author: Jackson790908
Title: Tasty ayam fish
Review: Walked in for lunch and so lucky there's available seat. Super fast serving. Chicken ball rice so so. Chicken was good. But best will be the ayam fish. Really enjoy the food.

Author: elaina_tanKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Chicken rice ball
Review: They serve chicken rice and asam fish head. Food was good. Paid rm75+ for 3 adults and 1 child. There was a queue during lunch. Rice balls and normal chicken rice are setved together. Rice balls were like sticky rice. Restaurant is set up in an old malacca building so it has a nice ambience.Show less

Author: janny_yap
Title: Not nice chicken rice ball & dishes
Review:
The service is fast. 

Chicken ball rice not really tasty. Not much flavour. The chicken tasteless as well as the vegetables.

Only the environment is unique. Apart of that nothing special.

Title: Original Chicken Rice ball

Their chicken rice balls with steam chicken is the original & the most famous in Malacca. Later, they added assam fish, soup & vegetables. The service is ok but during weekends & festive seasons it is packed with lots of people and the queue is rather very long wait for a table. The prices are reasonable and its great to have your meals here. Show less

Author: JoolesgunSingapore
Title: Wonderful old Peranakan house with yummy food!
Review: We went for lunch here and was surprised when we walled inside the huge house. It's a lovely place to try some of the delicious chicken rice and other treats. The bbq pork was excellent with crunchy crackling! Definitely a must visit when in the area..... both for the food and a peek into one of the old houses! Show less

Author: phatchm
Title: YAYO
Review: Streamed chicken is very tasty and the other ok not bad but recommend by me don't forget order streamed chicken . About Restuarant is very beautiful

Author: lias205
Title: Enjoying chicken rice ball
Review: Wait to be seated during lunch, weekend or high season. Once you have seated, they will ask your order. So simple, but make sure you enjoy the drink first because if it's crowded then you must be really patient to have your meals come. But it's worth. The chicken rice ball and the fish asam pedas is really yummy. Show less

Author: huiyeeg2015
Title: Must eat in Melaka
Review:
I always come to this shop for chicken rice ball in Melaka, at least I don't have to line up under the sun for a long time. 

Love their fast and good service, and most important tasty steam chicken.

Author: HHSGALSingapore, Singapore
Title: Still my fave chicken rice balls in Malacca
Review: My parents and I for as long as I can remember have been patronizing this for many years.. Although the price has increased now, food is still quite good and Im still not sick of eating it. The chicken rice balls are awesome especially with the chilli. I also love their herbal tea. The chicken however sometimes is nice sometimes its average, it depends on luck I guess but I think 8 out of 10 times its still quite yummy. There are 2 chicken rice balls shops at Jonker street. One is this the other is the corner shop... Dont go to the corner shop. The queue is long too but even if you are taking away food you still have to queue the same queue as those who are waiting for the table which is like ages. It just isnt fair... So try Hoe Kee... You will like it perhaps as much as me too :)Show less

Author: FromKluang
Title: Better chicken rice ball
Review:
It is just better chicken rice ball than other stores.
The foods serve by number of person.
It come with standard sets -  chicken, vege and Asam fish.
Long queue during weekend and public holiday.

Author: HihilM03Jakarta, Indonesia

I personally thought the rice ball and steamed chicken was slightly salty. It tasted like normal chicken rice dish, really.Show less

Author: edwintcs
Title: Enjoyed my meal
Review: So apparently the very famous chicken rice ball shop has already got long queue, so I came to this with obviously lesser queue, ought to have little disappointment but turns out to be surprising, it was great with affordable prices.  Highly recommend this.

Author: Patcharalai T
Title: The Best chicken rice ball?...it is not
Review: easy to find...but i went on weekend i must wait for 30min Staff is fast, prompt and systematic even though the Q seems to be very long... But manage to get in to enjoy the food after 30 mins. The taste is so so i think it is not the best nowShow less

Review: Definitely overrated for the quality of the chicken rice. I think the chicken rice ball in Melaka has dropped over the years due to all these hype & the superfluous demand. The folks had to cope with the high demand especially during the peak season, which is a known fact, coz you can't possibly measure up whilst maintaining a high quality of the chicken rice. Was in Ipoh for the chicken rice (Lou Wong) & it miles better, period.Show less

Author: Fpchong
Title: Reasonable chicken rice ball
Review: Went to took dinner at the restaurant to try the chicken rice ball but the rice ball is a bit too small and pricing wise is acceptable.  Best to try is the chicken legs dish too.

Author: Eric_loves_trips

Author: Rex_lee0623

No fight. 200% Malacca better.So far tried before Farmosa Chicken Rice and this one. Surely this one have to be winner. The Chicken is better in quality but most important is the Chicken Soya Sauce this one is outright winner.The only problem I have with them is the ordering. They seem wanted you to get package rather than order what you want to eat. Good as for tourist do not understand what to order and just mentioned 3 people or 4 people. For me I prefer to order how many plate of rice I need versus how many ball of rice versus chicken qty.One more weakness is not much other optional food. This shop just focus Chicken Rice only.Price rather not bad. 15 ball, 1 chicken, 5 drink and 3 people portion of lousy cabbage(LOL! I can cook much better one) RM80. Title: Average... not sure what the hype is a about?
Review: Was highly recommended from a friend back in Singapore. To be honest, not sure what the hype about the Chicken Rice Balls - they're simply just rice balls (no chicken). The chicken rice was good (ask for breast), and so was the fish head in the red/sambal type sauce but honestly, after living in Singapore - this place was okay. I would only recommend it if you have never had chicken rice before. The food is quite greasy, not a lot of vegetables but tasty nonetheless. This food outlet has been overrated all this while and like all humans do , when you see a que , it means that the food must be good especially for Asians . The Chicken rice balla are so small and costly , it's too wet and soft and the texture is not like the real rice that we are used to . The chicken pieces has been flattened so much so that you can't see the beauty of a steamed chicken meat . It's like eating shredded chicken slaps . Author: CarmenJJ

Title: Tasty rice balls and steamed chicken
Review: We passed by this place a few times and it was always crowded with long queue even late in the afternoon. To avoid the crowd, we decided to come in the morning to have brunch instead. The shop has expanded and occupied two shop lots now with additional seating area at the backyard. We ordered steamed chicken, rice balls and barley drinks. The chickens are very tender and juicy, I would rate them 5 stars if they used kampong chicken instead of normal chicken. The rice has perfect texture and nice fragrance. I had my first chicken rice balls in Bradell, Singapore. After trying chicken rice from Hoe Kee, I think I won't go back to the chicken rice ball stall at Bradell anymore. The whole meal costs us below RM20 and we think that is reasonable. Can anyone here shares with us which stall has the longer history, Hoe Kee or Chung Wah? I can't comment which stall serves better chicken rice till I try out Chung Wah's chicken rice during my next Malacca trip.Show less

Author: Anita BSingapore, Singapore
Title: Delicious local fare
Review: We stopped by for a quick, late lunch and we thoroughly enjoyed our meal. We tried the steamed chicken, rice balls and asam fish head, all were delicious and highly recommended. The rice balls had a very nice texture with the perfect amount of flavour, the steamed chicken was tender and juicy, and the fish was spicy, but also very well prepared. Service is quick and efficient, the ambiance inside this old building is pleasant as well. Highly recommended. We went on Saturday and it was closing at 5pm.Show less

Author: stone_soup22Singapore, Singapore
Title: Standards have declined drastically
Review: I used to visit this eatery regularly many years back, when it had not yet expanded and occupied the unit it now does. It still resembled a quaint, family-run business. As it became increasingly popular with visitors, the queues got longer and prices started going up. The final straw came earlier this year when I discovered that they had restricted the number of rice balls each person could order, by pegging it to how much chicken you ordered. What an short-sighted, profit-motivated move when they knew the rice balls were what people were coming for. Their assam fish dish is no big deal. What kept me returning was the chicken rice balls. Sadly this is the last time I will be frequenting this place. Their main competitor, Chung Wah, which is just across the street, isn't any better - the chicken and rice balls are too oily and saltish.Show less

Author: gluttonsaysSingapore, Singapore
Title: Chicken, you won't be missed!
Review: I was very disappointed by how overly-hyped this place is, as evident by the snaking long queues outside the restaurant. There is nothing spectacular about the chicken rice here- apart from the nice interior design of a traditional dynastic chinese house's courtyard. I'm saying in my capacity of as a Singaporean- and i will unabashedly tell you that we have one of the world's BEST chicken rice- If you have tried our Singaporean hainanese chicken rice, you will probably agree with me. FOODThe chicken rice balls were novel, but there was nothing so exceptional about it. The rice was fairly fragrant. The chicken was soft and well-cooked, but its flavour was flat and pretty salty. HOW SHOULD GOOD CHICKEN RICE TASTE?I'm very opinionated on this one, but if you grew up eating as much chicken rice as me, you probably wouldn't blame me!The exceptional plate of chicken rice should be fragrant- You WILL be able to taste the chicken broth, garlic and pandan leaves in every mouthful of the rice. The chicken should be succulent, but the chicken sauce should have a tinge of sesame oil, apart from its soy sauce. It will be salty, but sweet and very fragrant all at the same time. The one sold here was flat and just salty. The cabbage was average too. The tangerine drink was special-i've never had anything like that before. It is a refreshing drink. SERVICEThe service system is orderly and prompt. Due attention is given to all the patrons- the older servers will walk around ensuring that people get enough chilli, while the younger ones are quick to take your order, serve and settle the bill. I won't eat from here again as a chicken rice fanatic and critic, but i will rate this place highly for its efficiency and service. If you are not particular, this may be the place to be for you. Price was fine. We paid RM 23 for two people- Chicken rice + cabbage (add on) + 2 drinks (add on)Show less

Title: Original chicken rice ball in Melaka
Review: This chicken rice ball shop i.e Hoe Kee Chicken Rice shop is one of the pioneer in Melaka. Besides chicken rice with steamed chicken meat, they do offers assam curry fish, pre-cooked sliced cabbage and it is located at prime tourist area where the locals will try to avoid during the weekends coz of the traffic jam & no parking.There is an alternative shop where the locals often go to which is at Family Soya, 46, Lorong Setia 1, Air Keroh Heights, locate beside Klinik Pang X-Ray, similar block with Public Bank Bhd. facing the main road of Lebuh Air Keroh, takes about 10 mins after Air Keroh toll. Instead of joining the crowd down town, this particular shop offers homemade soya drink, tau foo fah and the chicken rice ball per plate cost only RM3.50 ( 8 rice balls and sliced roasted or steamed chicken) plus cucumber slices.The shop operates from 10am to about 1.30 and close on Sunday.Show less

Author: GoforitSingaporeSingapore, Singapore
Title: What is so fantastic about Hainanese chicken rice in Malacca?
Review: Malacca is full of eating places for Hainanese chicken rice. As the name implies, Hainanese chicken rice is a dish originated from the Hainan province in southern China, and we can easily find it from hawker stalls to high class restaurants nowadays. It is a tasty flavored rice served with soft and juicy chicken meat, eat with two different dipping sauces, one is a garlic-chilli paste, the other a traditional ginger paste, and usually complemented with dark soy sauce. Cucumber and cilantro are used as garnish. A small bowl of chicken gumbo is commonly served together with the dish. While on our journey to Malacca from Kuala Lumpur, my stomach was craving for the authentic Malacca’s Hainanese chicken rice I really missed for more than half a decade. Without jeopardizing the road safety, however, I was driving with my mind already on the mouthwatering steamed white chicken that is cut into bite-size pieces and topped with sprigs of cilantro leaf and sesame oil. At the same time, I couldn’t resist the thought of warm aromatic chicken rice balls served with some dark soy sauce and accompanied by delicious ginger and spring onion sauce and tantalizing garlic-chilli sauce.Despite the road closure for major renovations of the Malacca’s popular UNESCO world heritage city monuments, a group of seven of us already made it to the famous Jonker Street (Jalan Hang Jebat), the Chinatown of Malacca just before noon to beat the lunch-time crowds. Among many chicken rice restaurants in the entire Malacca town, there are a number of popular eating places such as Adat, Hainamko, Huang Chang, Heng’s, Famosa, Chung Wah and Hoe Kee, to name a few. Without scouting around, we settled down to dine at the Hoe Kee Chicken Rice Restaurant at Jonker Street. Between the two most popular Hainanese chicken rice eateries located adjacent to each other at Jonker Street, a person might be inclined or mentally lured to join the long queue outside Chung Wah Coffee Shop. As for the Famosa Chicken Rice Ball Restaurant, also located at Jonker Street, I would say that it is catering mostly to tourists in wide varieties of dishes, and not favored by locals for obvious reasons. As such, we skipped this restaurant. However, by looking at the long queue at Chung Wah carefully, we felt that we couldn’t be in the waiting line for 20 to 30 minutes under the merciless scorching sun. Those who picked Hoe Kee had made a wise choice by spending less than five minutes of waiting time under shade. When we were ushered in by one of the Hoe Kee’s waitresses to a table big enough for seven of us, we all felt that the dining atmosphere there was rather spacious, bright, comfortable and windy despite the hot weather outside. For convenience, we simply ordered set meal portions for a table of seven persons as recommended by the waitress. Within five minutes, a large plate of steamed white chicken were served on our table together with two small plates of stir-fried Beijing cabbage, 20 chicken rice balls (each in the size of a ping-pong ball), one plate of loose chicken rice, and seven glasses of herbal tea. Unfortunately, Hoe Kee’s chicken rice balls were not as tasty as its loose chicken rice as the former is moist, soggy, cold and a bit tasteless. Rice was not at all tasty and chicken meat was not tender enough, but it was just alright for our impatient tummies. There was no chicken broth served, but both the chicken rice and chicken meat were reluctantly considered appetizing especially when we were extremely hungry. All of us were happy and satisfied with the recommended dishes that filled our stomachs, although we were billed one-and -a -half.chicken for seemingly less than half a chicken served. Together with the poorly cut pieces of chicken, the plate was also stacked with sliced chicken organs (spare parts), and generously filled up with slices of cucumber to cover up the shortchange.As a matter of comparison, I must admit that I had patronized the nearby Chung Wah’s Hainanese chicken rice balls a few years ago. At Chung Wah, if I can remember correctly, its rice balls were drier, harder, and tastier. Whereas, Hoe Kee’s chicken meat was only slightly more superior in taste than Chung Wah’s. Generally, both the quality of food and service at Hoe Kee were quite standard and basically the same if not better than Chung Wah’s. Frankly speaking, there is no such thing as “best chicken rice” or “best chicken meat” among the reputable eateries, but there is certainly such a thing like “one man’s meat is another man’s poison”. Even if you find the chicken rice or chicken meat tasted somewhat bland, they can in fact taste as good as your well-mixed delicious dipping sauce, a great flavor enhancer. It is, however, the rice and dipping sauces that can make or break the dish. For chicken rice lovers like many of us who can even cook our own chicken rice at home, there is nothing to brag about. The chicken rice balls and the chicken in Malacca were nothing spectacular. Malacca will be a good place to go for Hainanese chicken rice if it is your first time. The real yummy Hainanese chicken rice is indeed in Singapore where you will find it fantastic. Once you know that Hainanese chicken rice is Singapore’s national dish, you will soon know that the highly recommended eateries in Malacca are just over-rated restaurants.Show less

Get to order other food like vegetables unlike Chung Wah who serves Chicken only.This shop has also been recommended on a Taiwanese program called 我們EYE旅行.Show less

Review: Chung Wah Chicken Rice Ball @ MelakaMalaccan's favourite chicken rice ball. Anyway, the crowd is as 'good' as the famous shops Kedai Kopi Chung Hwa and Hoe Kee Chicken Rice located at JonkerStreet. You have to queue and wait as the seat is limited.The rice is shaped into a lump of ball. Given the structure of the balls. Author: hktraveller328
Title: Efficient staff
Review: Only tourists seen. Staff recommended set meals to save time to explain and save their time to wait for you to go through the menu. Taste similar to Chung Wah but half of the rice to be loose rice.

Author: D_JekyllMalaysia
Title: Good chicken rice, but not all served are rice balls
Review: Between the rest of the chicken rice balls eateries in Melaka, this is still the better one. The queue moves fast so no long waiting time to get in or get a table. The food also comes out pretty fast compared to the other restaurant nearby. The seating is spaced out and least claustrophobic or hot.The food here is good, the rice fragrant and the chicken juicy and tender. Sadly due to the speed of service here, they are unable to serve your entire order in rice balls and half of it comes in regular loose form. But still tastes the same at the end of the day.Show less

Author: Aria L
Title: Chicken, Rice Ball and Fish
Review: Just on time we get here before crowded and queue around 11.am, The Food which we order, Chicken, rice ball and fish so delicious and tasty, but order can't much a limited portion will be served.

Author: jackie_a007Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Cop Out on the Rice Ball
Review: No need to line up in the blistering heat for this. The whole attraction to this dish is the fact that the rice comes in tightly packed balls. This was how it was done back in the day. However, you will be hugely disappointed, as there is a notice on the entrance which says that making rice balls is a tedious task and they do not have the manpower to do it thus to keep people happy and to keep to the whole 'rice ball' thing, they throw in a few rice balls per order and give you loose rice to make up for the portions. However, people still flock this place despite the sham that it is. The chicken is steamed and comes in a lovely light soy broth and this is something that can be obtained at most chicken rice shops. Not worth the long and tiring wait. Show less

The Chicken was delicious but not the Rice Balls ( it was average). The most I liked was the Assam Pedas Fish Head which were so soft, tasty and not fishy. You must try it when you go to Melacca. Have fun.Show less

Author: TKWANG168Surabaya, Jawa Timur, Indonesia
Title: Delicious Chicken Rice and Assam Fish Head
Review: We ordered a big portion for 4 people of Chicken and the Rice Ball. The Rice Balls were about average, nothing special, but the chicken was so yummy, One of the best taste in Malay! Also, You must try their Assam Fish Head, it was so soft, delicious and the fish did not taste fishy at all. You must order these 2 dishes. When we arrived there about 12.15pm, there was no queing at all. It's worth a try if you go to Melacca.Show less

Author: ernichan
Title: Average chicken rice
Review: Went here to avoid the horrendous queues at over rated Chung wah, would say the quality is similar, chicken stringy, chicken rice balls squishy, I would say just average run of the mill chicken rice

Author: jeanwsk
Title: Tourist Must Try
Review: Food was average but my friend said this is the best chicken rice she ever eat at Malaysia.$23++ for 2 set chicken rice with 5 rice ball, cabbage and drinks.The homemade chili sauce taste good to dip with the rice or chicken. Service was impressive.Friendly staff even close their door for us to take picture.Overall a good place to start to fill your stomach before explore the Jonker street.Show less

Author: carolX1163SV
Title: Good for Breakfast
Review: This time had breakfast here midweek and could just walk in and not wait. Lunch time queue is very long and standing in hot sun not advisable. Chicken with chicken rice a must. Don't be put off by the crowd. Worth the wait.

Author: shirrrrly
Title: A must try!
Review: The restaurant's wait persons are very efficient! They work so well together. They provide good service for their customers. The food are extremely nice, I like the Assam Fish (but I personally think that it is quite expensive for a small portion) . Their drinks (herbal) are also nice too. Overall, the food here has won over my heart! You won't regret it!Show less

Author: Pixel8Malaysia
Title: Bigger, faster, more comfortable and cheaper option
Review: This is the place to try with faster moving queues and service than Chung Wah. The chicken balls are less lumpier/soggy and can feel the rice grains, tastier than Chung Wah. Chicken is quite similar to Ipoh style, dependent on the soya-based gravy but tasty nevertheless. Better environment too, with shaded area for queues. If coming to Jonker, I'd make this my first choice unless I have plenty of time/patience to brave the sun for Chung Wah.Show less

Author: Sunset116Singapore
Title: Fragrant rice balls...
Review: This is a very unique way of eating chicken rice..in little rice balls. This is one of the 2 famous shops in Melaka and the nice thing is that you queue in the shade and it moves quickly. It opens really early so I suggest you go for breakfast and avoid lunch or dinner if you want to skip the wait. The chicken is a bit too oily for me, but it was pretty nice. Show less

Author: Akanee
Title: Must try..
Review:
First time with chicken rice ball, all is ok quickly service reasonable price for me.

PS. I still no idea why rice ball?

Author: swetling
Title: Overate Restaurant
Review: The chicken and rice are not as good as it is rated. For us, it is average and we think the restaurant is commercialized instead of offering very authentic chicken rice ball.

Author: 948PeterE
Title: Best anywhere!
Review: Really enjoyed the quick service....We ordered our meal during our 5 minute wait for the table and the meal was served in a couple of minutes. The chicken was delicious and the rice balls made the meal extra special. Would definitely recommend it for taste, service and location (right on Jonker Street).Show less

Author: shenpl02Singapore
Title: Lunch for 2
Review: we went for lunch around 12:30pm, and already there was a long Queue. there was no soup on that day, though I wish we could have a try.there is a notice stating they will serve loose chicken rice with some rice balls aside, 'due to insufficient experienced staff'.for 2 pax, we got 2 plates of loose chicken rice and 5 rice balls (each about the size of a Ping-Pong ball)quite contradictory, we find the loose chicken rice more tasty than the mini balls!ordered a plate of vegetables to go with our food, it was average.we queued 1.5 hours, the food is good, but I wouldn't queue a second time for it.Show less

Author: JohnmagfamSingapore, Singapore
Title: Die die must try!
Review: Did ate many varieties in Malacca, so it is a must try to eat Malacca chicken rice if you are here.In conclusion, most outlets selling chicken rice are about the same, so unless you are a food writer or critique, to me most stalls here are very good!Show less

Author: AllyC09Singapore, Singapore
Title: Smaller Portion but Same Price even before GST
Review: The restaurant still look the same but not the service nor the food. The server where like running around like a chicken without head when you call for order. There are some non-local staffs who just stood there too look at the patrons instead of helping out...which is fascinating. They way these workers look as us as if we are alien nor fantasizing...Other than that? The portion of our food goes smaller and smaller from 1 time to another visit. This is surprising because the GST (Good and Services Tax) has yet to kick in. Same price and some slight higher but? Smaller portion. Think twice to eat here again.Show less

Author: WorldGluttonKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Fast service, great food with reasonable pricing !!!
Review: Located along the busy Jonker Street, Hoe Kee Chicken Rice Shop was busy with customers at the front waiting to be seated. We joined in the queue for lunch at 12.30noon, did not have to wait long, staff at the front took our order, Went inside, the interior was spacious and cosy. We love the tasty rice balls and tender chicken with spicy chilli sauce.Fast service with reasonable pricing , it was worth dining here !!!Show less

Author: charlyBranKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Easy Peasy Chicken Rice Ball
Review: Been eating at this place a few times and the taste are quite standard. Best if you are there early, else you will need to queue and wait for a table. However, service are fast. The staff will ask for your order when you reach the entrance, so be prepared to give your food & drink order to the wait staff at the entrance. Once you are seated, the food are serve quite fast.Normally, they will serve you a limited number of chicken rice ball depending on the number of pax. I guess they don't have enough rice ball to serve to all their customer. However, the normal chicken rice will be serve as well. Beside the normal order of hainan chicken, there's assam fish & stir fry cabbage as well if you need some variety in your dishes & some fiber. Both the assam fish & cabbage are nothing to shout about but decent enough to complete a nice meal.Show less

Author: sassyguyKuala Lumpur
Title: NIce rice balls!
Review: Have eaten in this shop a couple of times. The most recent being over the weekend as Chung Wah already had a long line forming up even before 10.30am. Was disappointed that they limit each customer to only 5 chicken rice balls (roughly sized of a ping pong ball) Wanted to add more rice balls but they refused and only offered chicken rice minus the balls. Why call yourself a "chicken rice ball" shop specialist if you cannot satisfy a customers request for more rice balls?? Anyhow the rice tastes good but the chicken was nothing spectacular... normal even. Will try other no frills normal chicken rice ball shops the next time I am here and try to avoid these fancy touristy shops..Show less

Author: HatchsteveBournemouth, United Kingdom
Title: Nice staff, nice chicken rice ball.
Review: You have to try chicken rice ball if you come here and this is as good a place as any to come and do it, less of a queue than Chung way and I thought more delicate rice balls. Did it, enjoyed it, ticked that box.Show less

Author: D_JekyllMalaysia
Title: The better chicken rice in Melaka
Review: The restaurant is dressed up in a lovely authentic traditional facade & it follows through into the interior. It is spacious and hides plenty of nooks and corners. Despite having a long queue of diners waiting to get in, the restaurant staff was very efficient in getting you a table as quickly as possible.Sometimes during peak lunch hours, the restaurant is not able to serve all the rice balls & instead serves half your portion in rice balls & the other half in regular form. Doesn't really matter, its the same rice. The rice & chicken are really good and most definitely trumps those served in Chung Wah. Not forgetting that the service here is by leaps and bound better than the often rude people in Chung Wah.Parking in Jonker street is very limited so park in the nearby open air carparks & walk over.Show less

Author: 924jacquelinedSingapore, Singapore
Title: Lunch
Review: We queued here for 20 minutes. Ordered a whole chicken, 10 rice balls and cabbage for the 2 of us. Chicken is Abit hard not as tender as Tian Tian chicken in Singapore. Chilli dip is Abit too watery. Rice ball is nice. Overall paid rm47 including 2 can drinks. Not bad but overhype.Show less

Author: laurensiavanida
Title: Delicious with reasonable price
Review: We came there before lunch time, it will have long queue if you come around 12. The waitress were super friendly, she gave us good offer for 4 persons. We can try their 2 best menus plus rice ball and additional rice. You must come here when you visit Melaka!Show less

Author: Cynthia Y
Title: Must try in malacca
Review: Never fail to have a satisfying lunch at hoe kee chicken rice ball. Cheap and reasonably good portion. We had their signature chicken rice ball, assam fish, and cabbage. Cooling ambience with natural ventilation. shorter queue than the adjacent chicken rice ball shop.

Author: kevindo76Singapore, Singapore
Title: Tough Chicken Meat
Review: There was short queue of less than 10 people on a sunny Saturday lunch time. The order had to be taken whilst in the queue before being seated in the renovated restaurant, which is not air-conditioned.Each serving of five chicken rice balls came on a plate. The balls were roughly the size of a ping pong ball, and each serving is equivalent to a small bowl of rice. Biting through them, they were a tad sticky and did not disintegrate but still held most of its shape. The rice balls were aromatic with a good amount of garlic and fat. The chilli sauce was watery compared to what we are used to back home. To my relief, it still packed a punch.The chicken was served with a generous serving of sliced cucumber. A lot of the chicken was tough, which is a huge disappointment. The few tender bits were also dry, confirming that it was overcooked. This is a grave misdeed that the poor bird did not deserve to go through to get onto the plate. The sauce was good though, with nice soy and a good balance of fragrant sesame oil which the latter did not overpower the dish. Both the chicken and the chicken rice are important constituents to a chicken rice experience. Sadly, this was a disappointing meal as the chicken failed to make the cut.Show less

Author: Jacqueline FKuala Lumpur
Title: Best of the best!
Review: My husband and I always made sure that we visit this restaurant whenever we visit Malacca. We love it so much! The restaurant has a charming interior and it always felt nice to be eating there. The food was always our favourite! Many would say how great can chicken rice be? After all, it's just chicken rice. But trust me, this is entirely differently in an great way. The chicken is so tender it taste awesome! Every time we are there, we can finish half a chicken between the two of us. The Asam Fish is great too and we tend to go for the tail. Go try it out and you'll see what you've been missing all these while!Show less

Author: Choonfong
Title: Nice Chicken Rice
Review: Chicken rice with the rice served in the form of rolled balls; tasty with authentic chicken flavour and spicy chilli sauce; price is reasonable and service quite prompt without having to wait too long

Author: LCC8585
Title: Nice food
Review:
Enjoyable treat with great foods served.
Comes with various set meals while you headache on what to eat.

Author: HopeLuiHong Kong, China
Title: Yummy authentic chicken & rice
Review: Luckily I did not have to wait to get a table. I initially ordered chicken and rice balls, but they ended up giving me just chicken and rice. Once the owner figured out the mistake, she immediately went and brought me two rice balls without any extra cost. I thought that was quite kind and generous of her. The food was very delicious, and the price would make any budget traveler very happy. Like most posts here, I would suggest you come a bit early. I passed by the restaurant at around 1 and there was a large crowd gathering outside waiting to be seated.Show less

Author: GodfreyLee
Title: Great lunch
Review: I had to wait for 20 mins before i could have a table but it is worthy for waiting. I ordered chicken and fish, both is delicious. the price is quite reasonable and it is a added point for this restaurant.

Author: ksksg21
Title: Best in Melaka
Review: Always come here for lanch on my visit to Melaka, taste of cheken and rice are special.

Author: MouriskaMacao, Portugal
Title: Nice Experience
Review: This restaurant has a nice ambience, u are like eating in the traditional old house with the big hall in the middle. The food is consider worth a visit with tender chicken and the rice ball is indeed better than the other popular shop. Remember to go early as they close quite...Show less

Author: PinXun
Title: Overrated queue
Review: the queue could go up to 30 mins but I personally find the food is quite average not sure of what is with the hype over chicken rice ball in Melaka

Author: NachongJakarta, Indonesia
Title: Dont queue, not worth your time
Review: We were led to this restaurant by our rental driver. At first we wanted to try peranakan food, but we thought the driver must know better although he must get incentive by taking guests there. No soup on that day, as stated in the main door. The rice was given on big plate, not personal portion. It did not taste likechicken rice and also lumpy. Very unattractive. The chicken also lack in taste and presentation. Much of the chicken was undercooked as seen from the blood tingedparts. The assam fish and sauté cabbage were just ordinary. The rice ball was inedible. Yucky consistency and bland. Because of this experience, we did not want to taste any other melaka dishes, such a traumatic experience. I wonder why people still queue to get into this restaurant. Show less

Author: PingAshlynSingapore, Singapore
Title: Go to Singapore for the best Chicken Rice! Most stalls anywhere is better....
Review: For chicken rice lovers like us who even cook our own chicken rice at home, this is nothing to shout about... Rice is not tasty enough, chicken is not tender enough even though it's alright. The rice balls r not as tasty as the loose rice. Will be a good place to eat if it's your first few experience with this dish, u may even find it tasty. But if u want to try real good ones, just go to Singapore... Show less

Author: valerie L
Title: bad, not worth to queue.
Review: Chicken was not so tender . Rice balls were cold. There were no soups on sunday and public holiday. Other then that, they can just hang a sign said no soup for today on any weekdays . We end up with not much choice after a long queue. They only sell white chicken, which not so fantastic, cabbage and Assam fish. As we were 5 persons in an group, we end up eating a small plate of rice balls and a plate of normal rice , all in cold. (They never asked us but just give us a plate of normal rice.) A plate of normal chicken ,and Assam fish. No soup, we don't like cabbage. End up no vegetables. Service was bad, they don't have time to communicate with you. No time to bring their chilli to you. Chilli is not fantastic too..queue for dishes like that. We will not step in in future.Show less

Author: Lance HCaulfield South, Australia
Title: Not too bad but many better options in Singapore.
Review: I have to say that eventually found the place after trying different ones. The best of of the different ones that I tried there. It was ok. The chicken tasted better then the rice balls but overall eating chicken rice in Singapore taste much better. This coming from one of the biggest chicken rice eaters in the world...lol.Show less

Author: EnZZZoSingapore, Singapore
Title: nothing fantastic
Review: This is suppose to be one of the original chicken rice ball started many many years ago. The other one is "Zhong hua". But I do think this stall is too commercialise and over rated though. Chicken is OK and rice not very good. Be prepare to QUEUE if you go during weekends or holiday. I personally prefer the other stall more.Show less

Author: 862bernie168
Title: Over-rated
Review: Chicken was nicely done, but the rice was not tasty and lack of flavour.  Not likely to try again as it seems over-rated.

Author: H3rm3s
Title: Sad
Review: heard from my friend that this is a very famous chicken rice shop in Malacca.. Wanted to hv a try but so many of them is lining up and I was freaking hungry so I went to other place...

Author: Aramena
Title: Nothing to shout
Review: Me & hubby ordered 2 set of chicken rice. The chicken rice taste was good. I personally didn't like the rice balls, because it purely taste nothing. The chicken was tasty. It doesn't ignite my taste buds. But can try. Worth the price.

Author: Adrian D
Title: Not recommended
Review: The rice don't have the chicken rice taste like normal white rice and costly ... totally not recommended ...

Author: TangapushpamKUL
Title: Taste the real chicken rice ball here
Review: Have been visiting this shop since several years. Seriously authentic rice ball and always house full. But they have a really fast service. Despite waiting to get in the shop, once u have got a table, the food are served fast. They also serve fish assam curry which is delicious tooo Show less

Author: Huapatrick
Title: Famous Melaka Chicken Rice Ball
Review:
Waiting time was half an hour or so, good food must wait.
Juicy tender chicken and fluffy rice balls

Author: armani123sg
Title: Nice and affordable
Review: We queued for about 30mins before getting seated. Service was generally fast and friendly. I felt the rice was not fragrant enough but the chicken was great. Price was really good in my opinion.

Author: ChewY165
Title: Not bad
Review: Very fast service and in my opinion very organise service despite tat there is a long queue of customer... The chicken rice is tasty but nothing special~~ Worth a try

Author: evippsrDenpasar, Indonesia
Title: Tasty but nothing special
Review: We went there based on online tips that Chicken Rice Balls is one of the Must Eat in Melaka. To be honest, the food is tasty, but there is nothing special with this dish. It is basically the same dish as any Chicken Rice except that the rice were shaped into little balls. The restaurant is very hectic due to nonstop flock of people coming to try the rice balls (like we did). In term of value it is a good value because the portion is quite generous. Worth a try. But if you are looking for something special with nice ambience, this is certainly not it.Show less

Author: food_heiressMalmo, Sweden
Title: They no longer serve chicken rice balls but still good
Review: In some ways I prefer this to Chung Wah because it's less crowded, we eat in comfort, and the emphasis is on good chicken and fluffy rice without being made into balls. I prefer my rice fluffed rather than balled, I guess. Prices are friendlier compared to Chung Wah too.Show less

Author: LalityaH
Title: The most happening culinary experience
Review: Yes you should try this kind of popular culinary in Melaka. Better you come in the morning and have a breakfast here. Usually people should queuing on lunch time to experience this chicken rice ball.

Author: 512Carmen
Title: Excellent rice balls
Review: Tender soft chicken, excellent rice balls. Normal oily rice is just plain. Service was good. Enjoy queuing under the hot sun!

Author: KokThongSingapore, Singapore
Title: Go there for the food if the more famous shop is crowded
Review: The chicken rice balls were moist and fragrant but as I went during the lunch hour on a Friday afternoon, we were only limited to purchasing a maximum of 10 rice balls for a family of four. If you were there primarily for the rice balls, you would be somewhat disappointed with this imposed limit by the owners. You could still get plates of chicken rice which has the same taste and texture if you don't mind. The chicken is succulent and the soup of the day is surprisingly good. The lady boss is friendly but come across as somewhat quick-tempered and impatient at times. If you are at Jonker Street and the other chicken rice ball shop has a long snaking queue, Hoe Kee might be the next best alternative. You'll just have to eat and go; it's not the type of restaurant where the owners are happy to have customers sit down and take time to enjoy their food. Then again, the experience at other chicken rice ball shops looked pretty much similar.Show less

Author: FlemingC21Koh Phaluai, Thailand
Title: Average taste
Review: This chicken rice ball was our priority when we arrive at Melaka, but after ate, we think the food in here is average. The chicken was nice but there is still blood inside the chicken. The asam pedas fish also average taste and didn't cook well too, there still a part that the fish still rare.The price was fair.Show less

Author: Agape10Hong Kong, China
Title: Long queue, ok food, bit Pricy!
Review: Famous for its rice ball chicken rice. The queue during the mid day sun could be a killer. It will take you around 20+mins to get a table during peak periods. You will find that there are many similar restaurants along Jonker walk but they are all packed during the weekends. So plan to go early.The Chicken was soft but nothing extraordinary. I prefer the normal chicken rice compared to the 'rice balls'. The assam fish was just ok as well.Overall, nothing to rave about.Show less

Author: raspberryanLondon
Title: Fast service, nice interior, average food
Review: Chicken was average. Service was quick although there is a queue. They don't give all chicken rice ball but serve a mixture of regular chicken rice and another plate of rice ball. I personally like the regular rice better than the rice ball. The black beans soup was tasty. The building interior was in the old Melaka house style. Only the two back rooms have air condition. There is fan placed all over the restaurant therefore not too hot.Show less

Author: Kool123934Singapore, Singapore
Title: Original Chicken Rice Ball Restaurant
Review: This restaurant claimed to be one of the earliest chicken rice ball sellers in Melaka. They claimed that their chicken rice balls are handmade right up to these days. We went to this restaurant for early lunch at around 11:30am but their chicken rice balls were not ready and thus, we were served rice instead. Chicken served was tasty and tender and their assam fish was also delicious. We visited the restaurant during the school holiday in December 2013 and were served by some teenagers around 12 to 16 years old (probably their family members). Be prepared to wait in the queue under the hot sun if you visit the restaurant during peak lunch hour.Show less

Author: Dun8HK
Title: More than just chicken rice
Review: Since we have been to Chong Wah so many times, decided to try this place, where the queues were just as long.We ordered chicken and fish. The chicken was very nice and the fish a change from strick chicken menu. Interesting, was served by a young 10 year old - did fell a bit guilt as he carried 5 coconuts on one hand with a tray. Worth trying.The building itself was nice and spacious and quite cool once we sat down.Show less

Author: Indra_HadiwidjajaJakarta, Indonesia
Title: Best Rice Ball in Melaka
Review: One of the most popular food in Melaka is Chicken Rice Ball. It is a variation of Hainamese Chicken Rice, with the rice made like balls.Along Jonker Street, there are several restaurants serving this food, and I recommend this restaurant to try. The queue is quite long during lunch time so maybe it's better to come here not during lunch hours.They don't have many menus so basically you only order dishes for how many person, and whether you would like to order vegetables and drinks. The serving is quick and efficient with the lady in front taking your orders and directing you too your table.Show less

Author: uttercookieness
Title: Favourite place to get chicken rice
Review: Always go back for this. Fast service and the lady boss is loud but friendly. Their fried cabbage is delicious to eat with their tender chicken. Rice balls may run out fast but they do serve loose rice, which is equally yum.

Author: luicbeeKlamath Falls, Oregon
Title: Disappointed
Review: 1. long queue as expected2.chicken meat- ok3. rice---totally disappointed, coz people go there to eat the ball rice, and not the regular oily rice, however you cannot choose ball/regular. it is fixed. ball rice is so much nicer and aromatic. too bad they served lesser ball rice compared to regular rice. what for all the waiting, but less satisfied.4. use "non-recycable" plates, bad for mother nature.Show less

Author: Lejeai
Title: Meh
Review: The standard of rice balls and chicken was pretty average but it was cheap. The portion of the meal was pretty large for its price. Good for those who just want to fill their belly.

Author: 566singapore
Title: Delicious and Filling
Review: We had chicken and rice ball. The chicken comes with the liver tasted good, juicy & tender. Rice ball is too much for the 2 of us, but taste delicious. The chili sauce is great too. We paid less than RM20 for both of us - chicken, rice balls & drinks. Not expensive and reasonable price to us.We like the surrounding. This restaurant is housed in an old shop house with and open court yard and many side roomsWell worth a visit and would definitely be back.Show less

Author: Richard CSingapore
Title: Average food but lovely building
Review: The restaurant occupies a lovely old 2-storey house that has been restored and refurbished. It's located next to the red building occupied by "San Shu Gong" at one end of Jonker Street, but the signboard is not very prominent.We ordered 1/4 chicken, some vegetables, chicken rice and a coconut for brunch. (The chicken rice balls are only available after 12 noon when more kitchen assistants start work.) The food was fairly tasty - not too salty - and very reasonably priced.But I was more fascinated by the building, which was probably home to a rich family many decades ago. A good place to have a quick, simple meal.Show less

Author: 577brendaa
Title: Chicken rice balls qty limited
Review: I feel the chicken was better than Chung wah, it was served warm compared to Chung wah but the Assam fish was disappointing and too expensive.

Author: jeannietstKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Overrated
Review: Personally think it's overrated. The rice taste not bad but the chicken served is disappointing . Almost half of the chicken served appear to to reddish, which is quite spoiling our appetite.. Feeling slightly disappointed since we set quite a high expectation upon seeing good reviews from others..Show less

Author: 1john316Singapore, Singapore
Title: Excellent food in traditional home
Review: My wife and I usually have lunch at this restaurant once a month for the past many years. We like this restaurant because besides chicken rice, they also offer assam fish, black bean soup and vegetables. This suits us very well. It is not true that they no longer serve chicken rice balls. Due to short-handedness (lack of staff) they are not able to produce enough rice balls for the day. So they resort to serving chicken rice in addition to rice balls. This restaurant in a completely renovated old Malaccan house is still very popular.Show less

Author: YukieLilyKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Very, very disappointed
Review: Don't get me wrong, the reason why I am disappointed is not due to horrible tasting food.In fact, the steam chicken tasted good, juicy & tender.The disappointed comes from the fact that they seems to no longer serve "rice ball".If they aren't serving rice ball, they should remove it from their name.The chicken gizzard is out of stock even early in the morning.This is outrageous.Show less

Author: 443barryc
Title: Over rated
Review: This is the first time I try, friend suggest this would be the best among all. Have some queue, service overall are ok. But the chicken taste is really normal, not that delicious for you to queue up. At least in my mind there are few stores that's better than this(not in Melaka). And I can't imagine other store if this is the best among others.Show less

Author: PinkyJane88
Title: Worth a try
Review: Much more better than Famosa Chicken Rice but not as good as Chung Wah Chicken Rice. Nicely decorated and the bosses can speak Hainanese with u!

Author: olivia_s_y
Title: Never order the fish
Review: They do not serve rice ball temporary due to labour shortage, nothing to shout about for the loose rice, the chicken taste so-so, the asam fish which strongly recommended by the waitress taste awful. Overall the food is overrated!

Author: Jeshkp
Title: Good and satisfactory
Review:
I remembered eating there and it was really good and would definitely go back.
As always, when its too popular, service will go down due to high demand/long queue.

Btw, any know if it is halal?  Planning to bring my Muslim friend there...

Author: Bell N
Title: Thumbs up for their rice balls
Review: Best rice balls in the town. Yes, rice balls, not including the others like chicken, chilli sauce...

Author: travelhoneybeeKL
Title: famous chicken rice shop
Review: reached the restaurant after 12pm, there was a queue as usual but luckily did not wait for long time as customer turn over is frequent. unfortunately, some menu items were unavailable including soup and rice balls. we had chicken, loose rice, cabbage and drinks. service was quick and food was good. queue may be shorter than another popular chicken rice shop along the river.Show less

Author: saisaras_sivarajahSingapore, Singapore
Title: I was a little dissapointed
Review: As usual, due to the hype surrounding this place, my friends and I spent nearly 40 mins queuing up at this place. They have a menu with around 10 items but most of it were unavailable including the rice balls. However, not wanting to have wasted our time, we ordered and took our seats. The service was quite fast and neat. However the portions were small for the price we paid. We had loose (chicken) rice with cabbage and steamed chicken. Every dish was tasty, down right to the chili sauce that accompanies the rice. I think I would have enjoyed it better if I had more choices.Show less

Author: Ahmah LOntario
Title: Avid Hainan Chicken Rice Eater
Review: Although they don't sell rice ball, it is the taste that matters most. The chicken and rice are delicious. While the quality of food is important to a restaurant, the environment is equally crucial. Hoe Kee is newly renovated, so it is clean and spacious. You may want to try to their Assam Fish Head and soup of the day. They are also very tasty.Show less

Author: tenderlife
Title: The place for authentic chicken rice ball.
Review: The chicken rice ball here taste good.  you can lower your dining cost by ordering less chicken and more rice ball. Like if you have 5 person, order just 3 person's chicken and more rice balls. Go in the morning to avoid the long queues.

Author: darleneliew2013Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Missing the good old chicken rice ball
Review: We were surprised that there was no queue at all outside the shop. And turned out that they hung a sign written "selling loose rice only". So yea, they were just selling normal chicken rice, instead of the infamous chicken rice ball. Nevertheless, we decided to just went ahead and give it a try since it has been awhile since our last visit. Found out that it wasn't as tasty as my previous visits anymore and its really such ashamed that they do not serve chicken rice ball due to the lack of manpower, according to their staff. And the fact that they don't serve soup on Sunday was also bad. Looking at the number of customers, it has definitely dropped drastically. Really missed the good old chicken rice. I guessed this is our last visit to this shop.Show less

Author: PatrisiusPekanbaru, Indonesia
Title: The Golf Balls on the Plate
Review: It's easy to find this place. it's not too far from the bridges that connect to Jalan Bunga Raya. In the beginning it's quite confusing what should order in here. The owner are able to speak English poorly. It's easy for to speak Malayan or Chinese. The rice balls are so soft, it's look like golf balls. The taste is average, not too salt or sweet. I suggest you to try the dumpling. However it's not available in the early morning.Show less

Author: Humouresque
Title: Busy, so-so food
Review: The food - nothing to rave about. Long queues at lunch time. Service is impersonal. In my view most of the chicken ball rice venues in Jonker St are over-rated.

Author: wmloke13
Title: Chicken rice ball in a local house
Review: The restaurant is set inside a local house along Jonker Walk. It serves excellent chicken rice balls. A good start point to try the local cuisine. Their chilli sauce is excellent condiment.

Author: joeyT_kl
Title: Ok and not ok
Review:
I expect tasty Chicken Rice Balls

And the Rice balls are tasty but not the chickens.

Attendees are not so polite and price is average

Author: DrChristopheSingapore
Title: Yummy Chicken Rice Balls!
Review: Soft lucious hainanese chicken rice balls which go very well with the chicken and the chilli.The line to this Jonker Street establishment moves pretty fast and the customer has to pick which 'set' of items he/she wants. e.g. a set for 3 or 4 people consists of chicken for 4, 15 rice balls, rice etc.The chicken comes with the liver and some gizzard as well, not just chicken like the other places.This restaurant is housed in an old time shop house with and open court yard and many side rooms. This was the nicest of all the chicken rice ball establishments in Jonker Street.The price of the meal was reasonable as well, a party of 7 including soft drinks came to RM65+ only!!Well worth a visit!!Show less

Author: FarnothResidentCairns, Australia
Title: Not the original
Review: Melaka is my home town, I love hainannese chicken rice and I love my rice ball. Came home to visit my parents this year in July/Aug this year and ofcause have to drop in for my comfort food, and man! I was very disappointed! Theres way too many shops and restaurant claim themself as the 'Original' chicken rice ball and I know the fact that they are not but went ahead anyway as the shop that I went has closed for the day, and I was starving! We ordered rice balls and chicken and curry fish as recommended and I wish I never been. Travellers, please be aware, our ORGINAL chicken rice taste nothing like that and I can only tell you most of the restaurant around that area is only aim for tourist, local don't go there! We were out of choice that afternoon and thought we join the tourist, big mistake! Sorry Hoe Kee you don't get my vote.Show less

Author: vzeraphinal
Title: Honestly? Overrated but the lady waitress/owner was an interesting character
Review: Going to Malacca? You have to eat their chicken rice balls before you can truly say you've been to Malacca. I ate here once and i think it is completely overrated. My father is never a fussy eater and is known to neve reject anything given to him. Yet, he rejected the chicken rice ball after one tiny taste. Says a lot huh.It was lumpy, cold and ... I guess, interested. Extremely differently from the chicken rice I get at home. It wasn't at all tasty or fragrant. I felt cheated. >:( however, the chicken was surprisingly delicious. Soft, tender and very yum. We paid 19.80 for half a chicken, 4 rice balls and a plate of vegetables. We went as they were closing. Doubt I would be back again unless I'm here to just eat the chicken. Truly overrated balls. Show less

Author: TEE B
Title: Chicken rice balls
Review: Good to try the rice which is rolled into balls and should eat them together with the chicken and chily.  You be surprise how many rice balls you can eat.

Author: twofivefebSingapore, null, Singapore
Title: Love the chicken
Review: The chicken was really tender and fragrance.. I don't really like the rice ball but I feel that it tastes better than Chung Wah's.. the queue is really long from noon to 2pm.. try to go eat after lunch time if you want to avoid the long queue under the hot sun..Show less

Author: Fiona LSingapore, Singapore
Title: Yummy chicken rice balls
Review: We came here around lunch time on a Friday and managed to get a table without any waiting. Ordered 2 portions of chicken rice balls (5 balls a portion, about the size of ping pong), a plate of chicken and obligatory assam fish head. Chicken is ok but the rice balls are soft and alluringly fragrant. Assam broth is very tasty, with a good degree of sourness. Pity the fish is not fresh at all. If the fish is better, it will deserve 5/5. Show less

Author: Birdie56Canberra, Australia
Title: Specialists in Hokkian chicken and rice balls
Review: This place is known for its Hokkian chicken rice. It serves the rice in rice balls which seems to be the local version of chicken rice. The restaurant caters for tourists and has a fast turn over. I was dining alone and was told by the Chinese woamn who directed me to my table that I would have a serving of chicken rice - she obviously knew that most tourists came to eat their specialty. I had to agtee with her. With Chinese tea, the bill was only 4.50 RM, easily the cheapist meal I had in Melaka. The chicken rice was well cooked but quite bland. I preferred the spicier Nonya food in other restaurants.Show less

Author: WilsonLimPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Good price, average food
Review: The chicken rice here is just average, nothing you can't get in Kuala Lumpur except for the rice balls but its taste was just okay.The black bean soup was really good though.The good thing here is its price - RM26 for 3 servings of rice, half a chicken, a bowl of soup, 2 servings of cabbage and 3 drinks(barley and chinese tea). Pretty decent price considering it's located right in the middle of a tourist area.Show less

Author: mrNanyangSingapore
Title: above-average chicken rice, not expensive.
Review: 5 of us were served their famous chicken, rice balls(饭团） and loose rice（散饭）, 5 black bean soup(RM1.50each), 3 barley drinks, 1 vege dish, bill came out around RM105, which i think is reasonable, esp with their good biz. But, i personally feel some chicken rice in singapore are better, due to softer chicken meat, and i dont really fancy pressing the rice into a ball, which spoilt the texture.Overall, taste is good, and the price is ok. Be prepare to que and wait for food totalling abt 30 mins, depending on the crowds.Show less

Author: mayshalwsSingapore
Title: Taste good
Review: We made order while queue for seat. It took about 15mins for the foods to served. The chicken taste good, quantity enough for 2 persons. Rice ball got the aroma taste. Beside chicken rice ball, their still got other dishes for order. We'll return back if visit Melaka again.Show less

Author: TeikhinKuala Lumpur
Title: Cheap, friendly staff
Review: We went there during school holiday. We had to queue for about 15minutes but I considered acceptable. The staff who took the order was very friendly. The chicken was good but rice ball was ok. I prefered the normal rice than the rice balls. Although it was hot out there, the environment was cold. The price was reasonable. I think the set meal is cheaper but I don't really look into it. I would definitely go there again.Show less

Author: shiroatkl
Title: Good Choice
Review: Good choice of  chicken rice despite the long Q of 30min and another 15min for food to arrive. Chicken meat is soft despite being serve on the breast part.

Author: frolicker_leonSingapore, Singapore
Title: my prefered place for chicken rice
Review: despite having so many stalls here selling similar dish, this is the place i always end up with time and again after multiple visit to melaka. unpretentious food and service, clean environment, and delicious food. i prefer rice served on a plate, rather than in balls. to me, chicken rice balls is just gimmicky.Show less

Author: kennytan19
Title: Decent chicken rice
Review: Chicken is good, rice ball is ok only. I still prefer the singapore hainanse chicken rice. The cabbage is nice too.

Author: memoriezzSingapore, Singapore
Title: disappointed
Review: we were quite disappointed at Hoe Kee. Perhaps coming from Singapore where there's many good chicken rice stalls, we were expecting a little more. The rice was fragrant and nice but the meat just felt too tough for my liking. If you are a fellow Singaporean, I recommend skipping this.Show less

Author: Bridget CForfar, United Kingdom
Title: Hoe Kee - the place on Jonker St for Chicken Rice Ball
Review: This is the 3rd time we've been to Melaka and were always put off by the queue and the fact it was right on Jonker St so we thought it wouldn't be that great (like Famosa) but this time we went and loved it! Before we thought the best was the Chung Wah at the bridge but we enjoyed Hoe Kee much more and in fact went back the next day.
