Review: Just tried out the food in makko nyonya. Food is so so but price is very expensive. Only fish it self aready cost rm100 and they do not display the price for fish. Will never recommend for visit.

Author: 987reginahSingapore, Singapore
Title: Authentic cuisine
Review: Loved the chincalok omelette and ngoh hiang here. The Pongteh chicken small size was insufficient for 3 persons. I found it rather cold and it would be better if served warmer. The ladies finger were a tad old and tough.  We didn't really like the chendol as it was too sweet and too rich with too much coconut milk. We spent RM 91 for all these dishes and drinks for 3 persons. Show less

Author: Stephanieteoh1988
Title: Delicious food
Review: Of the many places I’ve tried the pongteh in malacca, this one has the closest taste and smell to what my late granny makes. You have to make reservations and wait a little while, but it’s worth it.

Author: DianneLim
Title: Satisfied dinner for all - old & young
Review: Glad that we got there by 5.45pm to join the queue. Hence we got seated soon after 6pm when restaurant opened. We dived into the menu to order, including the chendol to be served later. The curry vegetable is amazingly delicious with the fragrance that caught onto us when served. The ngoh hiang & otah otah were so good that our order of large serving weren't enough, and we had to order extra serving. All in, a great dinner enjoyed by all, including the old & young :)Show less

Author: weiyangleeKuala Lumpur
Title: Would have waited if they had better service attitude rather than the "I don't really care for your business" attitude.
Review: Wanted to eat here initially. After a brief interaction with the restaurant staff and their "I don't really care for your business" attitude turned me away from this restaurant no matter how good the food may be. Decided to eat elsewhere instead (Cottage Spices, opposite side of the road) which turned out to be a more enjoyable dining experience with more courteous and helpful waiters and waitresses along with the good food.Show less

Author: MellowsgSingapore, Singapore
Title: Delectable Peranakan Delights
Review: Was visiting Melaka with my family and checked out this top rated Peranakan restaurant. We were very lucky to get a table without booking as we found out that they were fully booked out just a couple of hours before.The ambience is a traditional restaurant with no fuss. Service was efficient and prompt. But the highlight was the food, which was worthy of its top billing!We had the chili sotong (cuttlefish) which was just perfectly done, soft and springy, coupled with a tangy hot sauce that leaves one begging for more.The sambal kangkong was equally delicious, and the Ngoh Hiang hit the spot. Coupled with the rich sambal sauce, and your taste buds would never be the same! The only wish was that the Itek Tim (salted vegetable duck soup) would be a little for full bodied.We polished off the entire meal to the last grain of steamed rice and unfortunately had no room for dessert. That would be the only regret till our next visit!Show less

Author: Cheeps21
Title: Decent food but overrated and priced
Review: The place is quite popular and we waited 15min on a weekday night to get a seat. Overall the food’s good quality, the ngo hiang’s very good, brinjal’s cooked perfectly and sayur lodeh’s excellent. I felt some of the seafood dishes were over priced.

Author: chelva58
Title: Lunch with Family
Review: The cincalok omelette was nice. The chendol was good. Fortunately, there is n more GST! Savings of 6%, we spent on the Otak.

Author: PeaceWalkerzSingapore, Singapore
Title: One of the best place to get Nyonya food in Melaka
Review: Along this place there are several similar store selling Nyonya food. But this place was recommended by a few Malaysian friends of my so I came down to try. Must say by far one of the best place for Nyonya food in Melaka. The environment is old but have this Nyonya place feeling and the staff were in their "house uniform". There are a list of dish and we only tried 3 of them. I must say try the Ngoh Hiang. Is one of my favourite. Will come back and try other dish.Show less

Author: Midnightrainn
Title: Disappointed...
Review: Heard rave reviews about this place and was eager to give it a try Verdict: extremely disappointed...  bland food that doesn’t do justice to the real baba Nyonya experience.. overpriced ... and worst of all rude staff ... Would not revisit and certainly would not recommend it to anyoneShow less

Author: Anne L
Title: Nice nyonya food
Review: Love the nyonya food here especially the pineapple prawn curry and chicken stew.  Most of the time its packed.  Have to make appointment.

Author: PamelaJosephKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Glorious Food
Review: This is the by far the best place for Nyonya food in Melaka. My family and I arrived in the late afternoon and we were thankful we didn't need to wait a long time for seats. 10 minutes later and we were already ordering our food. The food is so much worth each and every Ringgit. Coming from a family whereby my grandmother cooks good Nyonya food, this place serves dishes that are so similar to my own grandmother's cooking - 6 stars for Makko!Show less

Author: AHK2960
Title: Long Queue
Review: It's considered quite popular with long queue, after we parked our car at the back lane, we saw 2 indian men were cooking & stirring a big pot of curry on the back lane outside the restaurant, so we left without trying.

Author: Yew Mun LSingapore, Singapore
Title: Nice Nyonya food in Malacca
Review: I was highly recommended by my friend to must try this nyonya restaurant when I am in Malacca. Indeed the food was very nice especially the petai with sambal ikan bilis and the prawn crackers that came with the meal. The place could be crowded during meal times and the lady that served us wasn't that friendly but the food overrule everything!Show less

Author: DavidOKPSingapore, Singapore
Title: IMHO One of the best nyonya restaurant
Review: Ordered the sambal sotong, sayur lodeh, ayam rendang, ayam buah keluak, otah, ngor hiang and ikan cili. I must say most of them really hit the spot for me. Love the sayur lodeh for its coconut milk flavourfulness, sambal squid for its spices, otah which is fresh and creamy and the rendang for its nicely balanced spices and chilli hotness. Will definitely come back again despite the long wait time.Show less

Author: TrailsOfAnneSingapore, Singapore
Title: Popular restaurant with queues
Review: Came here to try with a recommendation from friends. Waited 30 minutes for a table for 4 during lunch time on a saturday. rather smallEstablishment. Ordered ngor hiang, beef rendang, mixed vegetable, ayam pongeth( in dark sauce) and satay sauce beancurd.didnt think it was fantastic waiting in queue but overall tasty. Sambal at the side to me was the star! Service was prompt. No lingering around after eating as they were waiting to clear the tables Show less

Author: poseidon1430
Title: Interesting taste
Review:
Assam fish sauce tasted more sour than I thought.
The mutton tasted better than expected.
Food is tasty, clean environment, air conditioned and good service

Author: johnnyxtSeremban, Malaysia
Title: Rustic restaurant recommended by locals
Review: No complaints about the dishes we ordered - the ayam pongteh had an great savoury sauce that went well with rice, and the paku masak lemak did not stinge on coconut milk. And the cendol and sago gula melaka were also lovely thanks to the fragrant gula melaka.Service was quick once we were seated, after waiting for about 20 minutes (this was a saturday night at 8pm - could be a longer wait at other times). And we were sharing a big table (they do ask if it was ok to share).Show less

Author: ckthyapKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Expensive
Review: Two of us went for dinner at this restaurant as recommended by friends.. We order Assam fish , petai with prawns ,a vegetable and eggs fried with cincalok . Food was served within minutes . We would rate the fish dish and veggies as 4 out of 10 ,the eggs a 5 and the petai a 7 . When the bill came, we were taken aback. Inclusive of two rice and two Chinese tea ,the total amount we need to pay was rm122.50!!!I think this is too pricey and I would not be recommending this place for food . Even my Malaccan friends told me it is exploiting tourists. The fish cost rm68 and the petai rm24 .Show less

Author: Edmund G
Title: Great Food
Review: The food was great. Satisfied with all the dishes we ordered. Very fast service. Staff are helpful. Good desserts. Must try. Better to make a reservation for dinner.

Author: Julian LSingapore, Singapore
Title: Becoming too popular for its own good
Review: My family have been loyal fans of Makko for as long as I can remember, some 20 years already. We are Peranakans and we would always make our “pilgrimage” to this resturant whenever we are in Malacca. We saw how Makko grew in popularity over the years, and how the crowds of Singaporeans (and tourists) made them rich... and arrogant. Nevertheless, believing that the food was still good, we would queue obediently like everyone else. Some five years ago, we realized that their food just became not as good as before, and the service became less homely (no, they did not become more professional) and friendly. So, we decided to try other nyonya restaurants and as it turned out, there were really better tasting ones besides Makko (check out reviews on TripAdvisor). Today, we thought we give Makko a return visit, for old time’s sake. We booked a table the night before and all excited, we arrived at Makko at 11.35am. And to our dismay, the arrogant and trying-to-be-professional green-uniformed ladies turned us away as we were five minutes late! Their reason - others wanted the table and were waiting. BTW, Makko opens at 11.30am. That was disappointing. I will never go back to Makko ever again. They have become too popular for their own good. Really. Hear it from someone who has followed them for years. Eat elsewhere. You will get better nyonya food and I am sure, better and more friendly service.Show less

Author: KH_LyeKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Authentic and Delicious Nyonya Cuisine
Review: We had to queue about 20 minutes for a table for lunch, and we were told they don't take phone reservation. We soon knew why the :big deal" - the food and service! We were given some minutes to ponder over the menu but we asked for recommendations, preferring less spicy. And the waitress knew exactly what to offer - and all great! Chicken Pong Teh - very delicious gravy and nicely flavoured generous chicken pieces. Nyonya Ngor Hiang (fried spring roll) - flavourful bites. Sotong Goreng Kunyit - the kunyit adds a nice dimension to the fresh sotongs. Sayur Lodeh - a good mix of vegetables, long beans and black fungus in slightly spicy curry, very delicious and go well with rice. Telur Dadah Cincalok - one of the best we had. The service was quick an the price was very reasonable. A very good account of Nyonya food!Show less

Author: Wanderer803971
Title: Second day's dinner out (not Tuesdays)
Review: Must try the chincalok omelette, nanas lemak udang, ayam pongteh and cendol among others, plus get their homemade ubi kayu chips ! Must be willing to wait out outside the restoran though

Author: 556ngkSingapore, Singapore
Title: Dinner
Review: Went makko for dinner. We reached at 6 and the restaurant was already fully booked. We had to wait 40mins for a table. Best to call in advance or to arrive 30mins before to get a table.Food was ok. But somehow lacking that authentic nonya feelShow less

Author: SamuelMo18Singapore, Singapore
Title: great nyonya food
Review: Was looking for nyonya food on the internet while in melaka and decided on this place according to the reviews given. Came for lunch and the restaurant was almost fully packed with customers streaming in steadily at lunch time. I was recommended a spicy prawn curry dish which was fabulous. As recommended by one of their service staff i also ordered otak, chicken roll, fried egg and chendol. The meal was very satisfying and what I believe to be authentic nyonya cuisine. I've eaten at other nyonya restaurants in melaka and this i by far one of the best and one that is highly recommended if you are someone who can take spicy food.Show less

Author: CTSL
Title: Glad to have found out about this place
Review: Really enjoyed our lunch. The quality and taste is authentic and flavourful. This will be a must from now on!

Author: 70SYT
Title: Good Nyonya Food
Review: The restaurant is pack by 7:30 pm. The prawn cooked with pineapple is good. Tofu with dry shrimp is tasty.

Author: HaddyTaY
Title: Will not back again
Review: The staffs are rude and very impatient.  The nyoya foods taste average.  The food served quite fast, and seem it pre-prepared.  Food came in small portion, but enough for us (2 adults and 2 children).

Author: kelvint153Singapore, Singapore
Title: Back again
Review: Have really missed the food here and made a special trip again to savour the foods here.the standard is the same since my last visit and like always busy as usual and have to wait for a couple of minute for a available tableEnjoyed the food and really missed them all especially the friendly staffShow less

Author: doraf435
Title: Tasty Food with a different Flavour
Review: Food are really delicious and pricing are alright for "normal" food items. For food items with seasonal pricing, it can get quite expensive.

Author: ClaraW93
Title: The food is good, but not sure if it is authenic
Review: Seems like it is a must to try Nyonya food when you are in Meleka. However, with no idea what is good or how Nyonya food should taste like, I think the food in this restaurant is good.

Author: andrewchengyc
Title: Foods are good
Review:
The Nyonya food here is good, especially the pineapple prawn.
Price is ok but the chilli fish is really toooooooo expensive.

Author: AFYeng
Title: Popular local restaurant with satisfactory nyonya food
Review: The restaurant was popular for both locals and visitors.  Food was satisfactory standard. Finding the place was not easy. It's good to have the exact full address if taking a taxi or Grab.

Author: 901stanleyl
Title: Nice Nyonya food
Review:
Visit the restaurant in the afternoon and make dinner reservations for dinner on 14  Oct 17.
Food was delicious.
Finished it off with their in house chendol.

Remember to make reservations , else be prepare to queue n weekends.

Author: danielnP7143HP
Title: No big deal
Review:
Just an average Nyonya restaurant with overpriced tag.
Service was fast though. Won't be back unless it is the only restaurant around.

Author: caynanlKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Good Nyonya Food Experience
Review: Slightly crowded upon arriving around lunch time, please make sure to register your name with the staffs in order for them to add you in the queue. Authentic nyonya cuisine, serves good cendol. Cincalok omelette and lemak nanas prawn is a must try. Cendol as dessert to wash down the food completes the meal.Show less

Author: Nylira Y
Title: Family restaurant
Review: Service is not really good but food are average but for decent meal would be enough. Ponteh chicken is good thou. I ordered otak and Ngo Hiang wasn't that nice thou.chendol too sweet for me.

Author: IsaacSutedja
Title: Authentic peranakan food
Review: Won't repeat what others have already said. The bottom line is this: good food, reasonable price, so be prepared to wait if you come late :)

Author: ghimohSingapore
Title: Wonderful Nyonya Feast
Review: Visited this quaint family restaurant in Central Melaka in June with family in tow. Had one of those unforgettable meals that had my family planning for the next trip. Every dishes hit the right spot. A good tip - Book a table a couple of days before going there.Show less

Author: johnxavier
Title: Makko Restaurant
Review:
Makko Restaurant is always full, you have to make reservations.
The food there is very delicious.Good array of food available.Waitresses are pleasant

Author: HudsonNeoSingapore, Singapore
Title: Must try Nyonya Food
Review: We went there some time ago last year but the restaurant was closed. So we tried again this trip and was surprised to see a long queue waiting to have a table. So we placed our name on the clipboard inside the restaurant and was asked to wait outside for our turn.After almost 35 minutes of waiting we were asked to go in and shared a table with another couple.We ordered the Sambal Chilli fish, Ngoh Heong, Chincalok egg omelette, Otak Otak and Chap Choy. In my opinion the food was excellent and worth the wait. We finish off with the famous Melaka desert, Chendol. It was very good.We asked if we could book a table the next day for dinner at six. So we went again and tried the Chicken buah charaus, Garam Chilli fish, Chap Choy and off course the Chendol. This Nyonya restaurant is definitely highly recommend.Show less

Author: karentklSingapore, Singapore
Title: Best peranakan food in town
Review: If you want to sample real peranakan food, try Makko. But word of caution, its always packed so please make a reservation. Parking is limited so take public transport. Everything is delish so it's hard to decide which is my favourite dish. Ayam Buah Keluak is a must try in every peranakan restaurant. Their Keropok with their chilli belachan is to die for. I will always end up buying packets of their keropok home.Show less

Author: smkow
Title: My current favourite Peranakan restaurant
Review: This is my favourite Peranakan restaurant, having tried most, if not all, of the more popular Peranakan restaurants in Melaka. I enjoyed every dish with our table favourite being the chendol. Will definitely be back!

Author: coozeecoozaSingapore, Singapore
Title: No frills, Authentic and value for money!
Review: We took a short walk to this corner shophouse for dinner, less than 10 min slow stroll from where we are staying- Hatten Hotel Melaka. It has a stained glass door and air conditioning inside. We ordered 3 simple Peranakan dish- pucuk ubi (fern leaves) stir fried in belacan, ngor hiong (minced meat rolls) and chicken (ayam) buah keluak. These fusion dishes marry the traditional Chinese dishes with the spices and flavours of the Malay cooking style. Google any of these dishes online and you can find explanations of how flavourful they taste and how they look like. Makko Restaurant does these dishes without any pretentious add ons and served without any fancy cutleries to distract. The way it should be done!! We couldn't resist ordering a traditional chendol dessert(shaved ice) even though we've already burst our calorie quota for the day! We paid a total of Rm55 for the dinner, including a small take away container of "heybeehiam". A savoury spiced shrimp topping, perfect for sprinkling over toast for brekkie. Highly recommended!! Show less

Author: Ice3l
Title: Foods Average
Review: Been to this restaurant many times with family member. I don't really enjoy the foods there. Price consider slightly expensive.

Author: bittymacbethBoston, Massachusetts
Title: Pleasant peranakan restaurant
Review: My friends and I shared several dishes with individual bowls of rice. The ayam pongteh (chicken fermented bean sauce) was a little disappointing, traditionally Peranakans eat babi pongteh (pork) but it seemed this restaurant has decided not to serve pork. The gravy wasn't really the consistency of gravy (I'm not too sure how to describe it) but the taste was pretty much there. I preferred the other dishes, such as their ayam buah keluak (chicken in spicy gravy with Pangium edule seeds) with generous servings of the buah leuak, ngoh hiang (fried meat rolls) and a whole grilled fish with sambal on top. The fish was well-cooked and the sambal was fragrant and flavourful without being overly spicy (even though the chili padis were left in) such that it overpowered your taste buds. The chap chye (vegetables) were pretty authentic as well. The meal came to about 33 SGD / person, which is a little on the expensive side for lunch, but the meal was delicious and very hearty and and mostly authentic.Show less

Author: 3xtraSingapore
Title: Tasty food
Review: We ordered beef rendang, cincalok egg, tong pek chicken and a vege fried wtih sambal. Can't remember the name of the vege butmost importantly, the food is nice.End off with the chendol which is delicious.We came for dinner on a Mondah and it is crowded. Do come early.Will patronise again.Show less

Author: Yv0nneSGSingapore, Singapore
Title: Great Peranakan Food
Review: Came at 12pm on a Saturday and the restaurant was filled but thankfully there was an empty table for us. Ordered and the food came in 10-15 mins with a bowl of crackers as "appetizer".The prawn omelette (medium size) was good though a tad salty and oily. Nice wok hei. My 4 year old ate most of this as she loves it. The fried chicken (medium size) is similar to the one I have at Ivin's Singapore. It's sweet and savory, kids will like this. These are the 2 non-spicy dishes we've ordered cos we have kids around.The star of the meal must be the pineapple prawns. The gravy has a strong coconut and pineapple taste. Very delicious. It was everyone's favorite.My husband specially requested for the Asam fish. There are 2 types of fish, one is in slices, the other option is a whole fish. Have forgotten the names. We ordered the sliced one and it wasn't what we expected. I'd recommend ordering the whole fish one. Overall, I guess this is just ok, we have tasted asam sauce that's more to our liking elsewhere.The ladyfinger dish comes with belachan chili. Nice dish. Ordered this as I missed Atlantic One's version, I still prefer the latter though. We were pretty full after all the food but felt we wanted to try the cendol. It's a pretty big bowl by restaurant's standard. Do take note. It's nice, love the savory sweetness of gula Melaka with coconut milk. Yums.Total damage almost RM150, very affordable. Will suggest reading up on reviews to check out what are their star dishes before heading down.This place is well known with Singaporeans. When we left, there was a rather large crowd waiting for tables outside. Thankfully, we got a table easily.Show less

Author: DreamzSGSingapore, Singapore
Title: Good & afforable Nyonya food.
Review: We didn't get to try this on our previous trip hence we decide to try on this trip. We reached about 5.30pm & there were 1 or 2 families infront of us. They opened punctually & we were also seated & served quickly. The food quality is good & their chendol is good too. Liked the fried egg, ngo hiang & ayam pongteh (^^) Show less

Author: anniec917
Title: Dinner
Review: Can taste that there are reduction of spices in the cooking which make the standard of the food drop.  Lucky for the finale,  the chendol still taste good.

Author: shely45
Title: Worth checking out, despite the queues
Review:
There were many people queuing outside when we reached there, coaches loaded with tourists kept coming too.

The kitchen is very fast, we waited 20 -30 mins.

The food are very original nyonya, not very spicy but full flavored.

Author: riccbcnBarcelona, Spain
Title: Nice Nyonya food
Review: I have to say, I did not really like Malaysian food in general, but Nyonya food it's nice, and at Makko's it's really, really nice. The place it's popular with the locals, so make sure to book in advance or to drop by to put your name on the waiting list before you actually planned to eat. Definitely recommended!Show less

Author: Simon6511
Title: Hidden Tressurea
Review: is not easy to find the restaurant as it is old and not much of signage but the food is pure Nyonya .. old fashioned and good price too

Author: bactrulusSingapore, Singapore
Title: Restaurant may close before the stated closing hour
Review: Don't be misled by the large groups of people hanging around outside of the restaurant, once you reach, send one person into the restaurant to join the waiting list! Then you can spend some time hanging around outside or walking around the vicinity. We reached the place at around 7.30pm, was only seated at 8.15pm. However, the food is served very quickly after ordering (within 5 minutes). Also, while the stated closing time is 9.30pm, we saw that they have flipped the sign to Closed at around 8pm, so as to cater to only those on the waiting list. So be there earlyShow less

Author: LovelynlaiKuching, Malaysia
Title: Best cendol in town
Review: The food here is good and we're served fast. We ordered pongteh chicken, omelette cooked with cencalok(fermented prawn) and makko tofu. All recommended. But the highlight of the dinner is the cendol. The santan is smooth and paired with gula Melaka, they are match in heaven. I can't help but ordered the second serving of cendol and I wish I have room for more. Do come here early or make a reservation.Show less

Author: Diana7737
Title: Food was ok
Review: Staff are quite rude maybe because they've work long there.  Sambal is good. Rendang Chicken served was not hot, taste is below our expectation. Other dishes like sambal fish, kangkung belacan was not bad.

Author: ReggieMcqueen
Title: Need More Cincalok Omelette!!!
Review: well known nyonya family restaurant in downtown melaka - bustling with locals, decent food at affordable prices. waiting time - 15 mins

Author: 987johnt
Title: Great Nyona food
Review:
Great restaurant if you are looking for good Nyonya food.
Must try: Otak, ikan bilis and the samba.
Restaurant has limited space so prepare for Q if you are coming during the peak hours.

Author: mamakleinm
Title: Great food
Review: We tried calling 2 weeks before but no one picks up the phone. Hence we tried our luck the day we arrived into Malacca and fortunately we managed to secure a booking. Went there for lunch the next day. Food was great. We ordered a total of 9 dishes and we all love it. Will be back again for sure.Show less

Author: msnakimSingapore
Title: Quite a Wait
Review: Restoran Nyonya Makko was extremely crowded on a Saturday afternoon. All the tables were occupied and we were told to wait outside. This turned to be quite a long wait. Wonder if we could have called for reservation earlier.The dishes were pretty well done, and prices were reasonable. My only complaint was the rice. Not soft, fluffy and warm...Show less

Author: Lyndsey H
Title: Excellent food
Review: Excellent food and service. Waitress was able to help us to decipher several Malaysian dishes and help us choose. The local fish in a spice sauce was really good, along with sides of mixed veg and big plate of rice. All fresh, excellent quality and really good value for money. We got the last table at around 6.20pm, place absolutely packed with local families and queues in the street to get in after we arrived. Highly recommend in Melaka for Nyonya food. Show less

Author: Jiu Mu XSingapore, Singapore
Title: Can give it a miss
Review: We were told that this restaurant served good nyonya food. So we decided to give it a try. First time i dined in a restautant that turned on its air con at full blast. Everyone was shivering. The waitresses said they needed to circulate the air. Werent they afraid that the food would turn cold very fast?Anyway, we ordered chicken pongteh, makko fried chicken, ngoh hiang, steamed beancurd with fried shrimps, fried fish with chilli, brinjal with chilli and chinchalok fried egg.The chicken pongteh and egg were tasty. The steamed beancurb, brinjal and ngoh hiang were so so. The fried chicken n fried fish were hard and tough. I think we probably ordered the wrong dishes so we didnt find them fantastic. Price was reasonable but i think i ll try other nonya restaurants next time.Show less

Author: DomchongSingapore, Singapore
Title: Awesome Food
Review: Arrived exactly at 6 pm, there was a few people waiting outside already. The restaurant opens at 6 pm. Friendly staffs. Delicious nyonya food. What we loved most was the egg omelette. Super awesome. The other food were great too. Will come back here again next time. Show less

Author: caitlynkhailingKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Average
Review: Dishes are fine but not suitable for those that can't take spicy foods. Those that enjoy spicy foods will recommended. The dishes are well known of its spice and cendol is a must after meal. The services are fast but have to wait outside if there are too many peoples.Show less

Author: Beal08
Title: Authentic Peranakan food
Review: Serving of food are really fast (less than 5 minutes of wait), queuing for table to be seated are long if no advance booking. Overall the food are really delicious and spicy(if you love spicy) and deserve a thumbs up!

Author: DesC133Singapore, Singapore
Title: The first Nyonya restaurant one should visit in Melaka
Review: This is probably the first Nyonya restaurant that one should visit upon arrival to Melaka. The location is good in the heart of the tourists attraction, near to Hotel Equatorial, 3 mins walking distance from Hotel Novotel and Hatten Square. There are ample car park in front of the restaurant. The restaurant opened at 6pm but there already a small queue at 5:50pm. No kidding. I need not have to elaborate how good their food is. For the record, try the assam fried fish, cincalok egg, petai, vegetables.Show less

Author: JBWKohSingapore River, Singapore
Title: Delicious peranakan food
Review: Makko is my favorite peranakan restaurant whenever I visit malacca. I have been a regular here for at least 10 years, the standard & quality of the food have been consistent, fresh and tasty. Service staff are friendly, efficient and kitchen staff are fast efficient in churning out our orders. I always have chendol for my dessert without fail whenever I am here. My favourite dishes: beef rendang, ayam goreng, nanak lemas udang, cincalok omellete and sweet potato leaves with sambal. Show less

Author: EvonneSim
Title: Overrated
Review: This place is parked during lunch/dinner hour. Certainly overrated and the food is mediocre. The standard has certainly dropped compares to many years back. You miss nothing if you have not been to the place.

Author: meeyuleeLos Angeles
Title: Disappointing
Review: Makko Nyonya Restaurant in Melaka was recommended by a Kuala Lumpar friend. Twelve of us arrived at exactly 6 p.m., when they had just opened up. A queue was already being turned away; I overheard that reservation was necessary at least a day ahead--hearing that, imagine my expectation. Inside, historic photos on the wall added charm to the otherwise dowdy dining room. The menu explained the history of Nyonya cuisine, hinting at the restaurant's authentic roots. On-time diners quickly filled the tables. My group ordered a variety of dishes ending with desserts. Native ladies casually took orders and began bringing out food almost instantly. (Here I must admit that the only prior Nyonya restaurant I had enjoyed very much was one in Pasadena, California.) We were excited at the arrival of every dish and ate with gusto. By the end, my friends silently chalked it up as a unique experience. Honestly for me the meal was disappointing. The rice was cold, rough, and tough--if that was the Nyonya way, nevertheless it was awful. Veggie meat and fish dishes were topped with different mush but none has much savory taste. Later a friend said he had peeked inside the kitchen and saw very little active cooking, just pots of sauces ready to be dished. If Makko serves “real” and “best” Nyonya food, then I shall never miss it again.Show less

Author: 956chankSingapore, Singapore
Title: My beloved restaurant
Review: Tried this Nonya restaurant during my recent trip to malacca. Reached there at 6 plus and there were already long queue forming. Managed to get seated near 7 pm. I must say no regret waiting for the seats as the food was one of the best I have tasted in Malacca. Plus their chendol reminded me of my childhood days dessert. I will not hesitant to recommend this place as it is walking distance to Hatten Hotel which I stayed during the trip.Show less

Author: 131pangp
Title: Nonya Makan
Review: Ok and so so. Would find overpriced. Long queue but food serving is fast. I have ordered lady finger, Chilli paddi paste is very very hot. Dun order this in future.

Author: MxJ1504Singapore, Singapore
Title: Still my favorite nonya restaurant
Review: Still the best nonya restaurant I have tried here in melaka. Food is average priced, decent portion food, curry is very nice and they have nice prawn crackers and chilli! Only downside is the restaurant is very small and so need to wait for a long time for a table if u have a large group. Show less

Author: TJLimSingapore, Singapore
Title: Reasonable Price
Review: The restaurant is aways packed with long queues waiting for their turns to dine. Food quality was slightly above average. If you want to eat without waiting then be there before 6 pm to queue. Otherwise make a reservation. Even then you still have to queue to get in when they open at 6 pm sharp no more no less. The nanas udang is worth trying. Buak keluak ayam is average. Show less

Author: JoshuuaaChenSingapore, Singapore
Title: best nyonya food
Review: very crowded, reserve your seats in advance, need to be there when store opens or your table will be filled without notice...Food was ordered promptly and delivered in about 10-20mins (for all to arrive)... Best Lemak Nanas Udang and Cincalok egg, same with the Ngoh Hiang... Bill was affordable which spent about Rm130 for family of 4 with dessert...prawns being the most expensive dish...Show less

Author: lockey1967Havant, England, United Kingdom
Title: Do not bother
Review: We were recommended to this place, the staff were rude and only interested in serving us as quickly as possible to get the next customers in. The food was bland/boring and not to the standard i would have expected from a highly rated store. Please do not waste your money!!!Show less

Author: 1john316Singapore, Singapore
Title: One of our favourite nonya restaurants in Melaka
Review: We're regular customers of this restaurant ever since it opened in 1984. It's still one of our favourite nonya restaurants in Melaka. It is still attracting a good crowd every day. The quality of food is still good although there are inconsistencies sometimes. We always find the staff courteous and helpful in their suggestions. Our favourite dishes are beef rendang, chicken rendang, sayour lodeh, steamed lady fingers with sambal chilli, sambal sotong, and chendol. You can find parking lots along the road in front and behind the restaurant.Show less

Author: 700yeelBatu Caves, Malaysia
Title: Day trip to Melaka
Review: Was there on Sunday morning around 10.30 am and found that still not yet open then we notice that their business hours actually started at 11.00 am. When we went there again by 11.30am, so when we walk and sees that the restaurant was already fill up by 2 buses load of tourists. No one in the restaurant ( i meant the lady boss at the counter and waiter ) have the intention to attend and even look at us. We have to make our way to counter and asked. By then the lady boss told us we need to write down our name for queueing.What really shocked me was when they started to call names for the queueing customers, they actually not calling, they shouted out load in a very rude way. I did tried a few of other nyonya restaurants before this. This is of the bad ones.Their so call signature steam fish, it taste exactly steam the fish then later just put those paste on top. This same goes with the sayur paku belacan.So my rating for this place are below:Services: 2Food: 2Location: 4Show less

Author: MAULEE19
Title: 👍🏻 Good and affordable Nonya food
Review: Second visit to Makko Resturant, food still taste as good. Must try! Good service and affordable price.

Author: Helen641208Singapore, Singapore
Title: Over rated
Review: Melaka is one of my favorite place and I will normally visit this nice little town couple of times within a year. For the past few trips, I went with no plans and just hop into any restaurent that I passed by. Surprisingly, some of them serve very nice nyonya food as well, and price are quite economical. Hence, I have not been looking out for Makko. This trip, we have request from some of our travel mates to visit Makko. The service had improved compared to my past experience. We all agreed that the standard of the food had drop, especially dissappointing with the Chendol. Honestly, nonya food don't really go wrong in this little town, we may want to support the rest, so can reduce queuing time too.Show less

Author: JamesTanSL
Title: Still delicious as ever ... authentic Nyonya cuisine
Review:
I love this place for their authentic Nyonya cooking.  Each time I drop by Malacca, I will have to have a Nyonya food.
Again, the food didn't disappoint.

Author: Stephensyliu
Title: Day trip makan and shopping
Review: Went with my Japanese friend and dear wife to this recommended Nyonya Restaurant by my local friend. The fried Assam prawn, beef rendang was super delicious. Highly recommended nyonya restaurant among the best I have tried in Malacca.

Author: francis_61jbSingapore, Singapore
Title: Very good nyonya food. Not dissapointed.
Review: Had dinner here. There is a queue as in many melaka restaurants offering good nyonya food. This is the third time I had a meal here. The food is tasty and very good. Had prawns, omelette, chicken and chap chai. Please do not skip the cendol @ RM3.80 - The best in town. Wonder what makes the gula melaka here taste so special. The chang is ok.Show less

Author: jeffreyboseSingapore, Singapore
Title: Excelent authentic Nonya food in Malacca!
Review: We've tried many classic Nonya restaurants in Malacca and Makko is one of the best. The decor and furniture is traditional Peranakan and the menu features all the classic Nonya dishes we know. We tried the cincalok omelette, nonya chap chye, angle bean sambal, ngoh hiang, udang nanas and ended the meal with traditional cendol. Every dish was delicious and authentic. Portions were quite generous and prices were reasonable. The staff were knowledgeable and helpful. Our food was served within ten minutes from order placement. It was a truly enjoyable experience and we look forward to our next visit when in Malacca.Show less

Author: Nicholas A S
Title: Overated maybe?!
Review: Food is at average but autheticity is there... Slightly pricey and waiting for a seat is a pain... Wouldn't had tried here because of the previous ratings.

Author: AlchemyRiderKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Tough to get into, but worth the wait.
Review: Makko opens for dinner service at 6pm. We arrived at 6.02pm. The restaurant was already full, and there was a couple at the door waiting for the next open table.If the popularity of Makko is not an indication that it is good, then I don't know what is.Makko serves Nyonya food. Nonya cooking is the result of blending Chinese ingredients with various distinct spices and cooking techniques used by the Malay community.The food is delicious. Especially the chicken pongteh, the lemak nenas prawns, and the sambal squid with petai. Service is fast. Their cendol makes an excellent end to dinner.Show less

Author: BiingWY
Title: Nostalgic food
Review: Have been here for almost 24+ yrs and the cooking is acceptable. Nyonya food has since changed so much as the art of preparation evolved with times. Hence it would be good not to expect toonmuch from what it used to be but to embrace them if your mood is right... Hehehe.Sambal lady fingers always never fails herein.Ayam pongteh was alittle dry on that day but flavour is edible.Itik Tim - still the same consistent sourness to counter the duck broth a good soup to drink on a hot day.Sambal petai passableAsam fish - can be better Overall taste is still good and compared to most local nyonya food makko passed on well.Show less

Author: G0hLJohor Bahru, Malaysia
Title: Makko for lunch
Review: We have been coming to this restaurant whenever we visit Malacca. This restaurant has been around for a long time and it's reputation is highly regarded. At times, there will be a queue and so please wait patiently. The food is worth waiting for. But if there is a queue and it is after 2pm, they might want to take your order before offering you a table or advise you to come back in the evening. Points to note - The staff are not courteous, but they won't act rude in front of you. Price wise, this restaurant is generally more expensive than average.Show less

Author: LilianJoy T
Title: VALUE FOR MONEY RESTAURANT
Review: Very good nonya dishes. Must try their Ayam Ponteh and Nonya Dumpling. The beef rendang too spicy. Veg crackers are very good. Friends bought 2 big packets.

Author: Pieter F
Title: Delicious
Review:
If a hawker in Singapore gets one Michelin star, Makko should have two stars.
Nice people, good atmosphere, delicious meal (chicken rolls, chicken sateh, spinace, rice + not to spicy)

Author: 245daverDungog
Title: Rude Staff
Review: My wife and I were visiting Melaka for three days and we were advised that Makko was a good restaurant. When we arrived we were promptly seated and the menu looked nice and spicy. Shortly after we ordered I heard a waitress say "dumb westerners " in Mandarin. We were the only Caucasians in the room. A short time later another waitress delivered our drinks and she had a plate of prawn chips in her hand. She said in Mandarin "they not want these." She laughed to another staff member who also laughed and took the chips back into the kitchen. I speak enough Mandarin to understand what was being said and the context.Such a shame because the food was good.Show less

Author: cryptofreakSingapore, Singapore
Title: Tasty peranakan lunch
Review: Came here for lunch and had to wait for about 40 minutes before we got a table. As we were one of the last customers before they end the lunch shift (till 2.45pm), we were told to order our food in advance and food was promptly served when we sat down at 2.15pm. Try these: ngoh hiang (deep fried minced pork wrapped in beancurd skin), omelette, chicken rendang and chap chye (braised chinese cabbage). Food was flavourful and dishes go very well with rice. Overall a quaint, clean restaurant serving tasty homecooked peranankan dishes. Show less

Author: joykoo
Title: Nyonya food
Review: Overall food is good. Ambience is a bit noisy, typical of any family restaurant. The fried fish with chilli on top is below expectation.

Author: firerooster2009
Title: Nothing out of the Ordinary
Review: I was hungry when I went there for lunch.Unfortunately, I didn't think the food was exceptionally yummy. I had expected more from the hype I received. It was just ok.

Author: JamieTan126
Title: Best Nyonya Food Served
Review: The service is okay. The food especially sambal/ nyonya favor is the best. The atmosphere is also nice. Highly recommended.

Author: Claudia C
Title: Average Nyonya Eatery
Review:
Was recommended by the taxi driver & we ordered the fried chicken which was not bad. Rendang had abit of a kick in the spice department & assam fish which was fresh.

Place was full with a waiting list.

Average place for nyonya food.

Author: emily_nsl
Title: Full House but food was a disappointing average
Review: We ordered the Tofu, Assam Fish, Buah Keluak Chicken, Otah, vegetables, fried eggs and the only dish I liked was the Otah.

Author: heiolahei
Title: Authentic Peranakan Dishes
Review:
We visited Nyonya Makko on saturday night. We found out about this place from our cab driver. 

The restaurant serves prawn crackers for you to snack before your meal is ready.

Last order is 9:30pm so make sure you come before they close shop.

Author: Shani APuchong, Malaysia
Title: Don't raise your expectations
Review: I was informed that Makko is one of the best restaurant to have Nyonya food and I guess I had my hopes raised a little bit just too high.Everything we ordered tasted very average, no different from home cooked food and considering the quality of the food that is served, it is expensive.Wouldn't recommend.Show less

Author: Selva G
Title: Nothing to shout about
Review: Ordered fish, tofu, sambal petai & vege curry. All the items were super oily. People with heart issues & high blood pressure should stay away!

Author: NIs888Kota Kinabalu, Malaysia
Title: Foods taste normal...a bit disappointed
Review: Regarding the business hours you can refer to there website or google.We are 8 adults heading there and reach there around 7:30pm, at that moment consider full house (there are three tables pre booked by customer).At first we are instruct to write down name on the waiting list. The waitress overall friendly and they are really busy on serving customer. We wait for about ten minutes they gave us the table which reserve by customer(because they are late).My comment on the food overall, if you ask me to rate ( 5 of 10 ).They serve dishes very quick and there are a lot of people keep coming and on waiting list.The price is not cheap but affordable.Show less

Author: serenac499Dover, Massachusetts
Title: Good but would have been better if we had a group
Review: It was just my son and me and there's only so much you can order; deep fried fish, sotong and vegetables. It was good but way too much. I had to bring my cendol to-go. Yes, good meal but not cheap considering what we had been spending. Our bill was 101RM. Not complaining but was surprised! FYI, it's a Wednesday and there was only at few tables at 6pm.Show less

Author: NicolaP942Auckland, New Zealand
Title: Every mouthful a winner!
Review: We found this restaurant on Trip Advisor, so thankyou! We had read it gets busy so we booked a table. The staff were very polite and the service was quick. Our server assisted us in choosing and we were not disappointed. We had a curried prawn dish which was spicy and creamy... Delicious! We also had a fried snapper with sambal which was superb. In fact probably one of the best fish we'd had. Green beans on the side were crunchy and delicious. We finished off with a cendol. I'd had it before in Georgetown but this was different as it had crushed ice in it. I really enjoyed it. The restaurant is clean and efficient, I highly recommend a visit!Show less

Author: Binky1111Porcia, Italy
Title: Authentic Melaka Cousine and Athmosphere
Review: We were looking for a good place where to have an authentic local dinner and found this place just outside the touristic area with traditional home made style dishes with a very efficient service and pretty low cost. Totally reccomend the signature fried chicken and cabbage red curry. Not a fancy place, however clean and with professional staff, just what we were looking for!Show less

Author: lilian2832Staymonth=11
Title: Famous nyonya food
Review: Popular with the locals. Very home cooked like. Easy enough to find. I used the around me app and got there 20 mins before they opened at 11am. The sambal belacan is to die for and one can buy some to take home. Go with an empty stomach to try the ayam pong teh, sambal fish and cendol.Show less

Author: chiachiangSingapore, Singapore
Title: Great Chinese peranakan food
Review: We walked in for lunch on Saturday around 1 and was lucky to get a table in less than 15 minutes. Reservation recommended before 1130am. Food is tasty and service quick. Prawn cracker served as appetizer is nice. Assam fish and chicken curry also taste good. It is a good lunch option given the restaurant is air conditioned.Show less

Author: KBook7Lyon, France
Title: Authentic Nyonya food, locals eat here, petai available!
Review: Restaurant authentique et les gens locals mangent ici bien et pas cher du tout. (Sorry I do not agree with the only negative French review and my French friends ate very well here so I think vous allez l'aimer aussi!)We drove down from KL for a day trip in Melacca and stopped here for lunch first. It's not far from the touristy centre, do get a taxi here if you'd like to try authentic baba nyonya food. We arrived at 12 and the restaurant was empty at first but filled up quickly. Waitress answered us patiently about whether a dish is spicy or not but remember this is a Chinese restaurant and they operate fast, so read up on nyonya food and decide what you'd like to try beforehand, or just order small dishes in a variety and try everything, even petai, the famous smelly bean that locals adore in a sambal chilli sauce. We had the chicken pongteh and a sweet and sour chicken and omelette for the kids, spicy otak otak fish cakes, lorbak, a superb sotong kunyit (stir fried squid with turmeric), sweet potato leaves stir fried with garlic, the petai (ok honestly only one person liked it but at least you can say you've tried it!), and I regret not trying the itik tim (duck in a pickled veg soup). We ate well for around 10-20rm per person, yums!Show less

Author: carroth2016
Title: Worth  a try
Review: Ok the food is relatively good and service speed is swift .   The only "bad' is the itek tim dish - soup was overly salty that it tasted bitter. Did not encounter any rude service staff.

Author: YX_657
Title: Very good
Review: The food was amazing. Very reasonable price. The staff were friendly unlike some reviews says. The chicken spring roll was okay. My favourite is the otak otak. The kunyit sotong is pretty good too.

Author: williamkctMiri, Malaysia
Title: Nice Food but service more room to improve
Review: Nice food but poor service. Recommended to make reservation if want to dine here. There's one staff who can't speak probably till none of our team can understand what she try to said till her colleagues told us that wait outside the restaurant. Till today i'm just wondering what language does that waitress speak?Show less

Author: Jackie_NMLSingapore, Singapore
Title: Yummy Nyonya Food! Shouldn't be missed!
Review: I went there in June. We tried by Nancy's Kitchen & Makko, we preferred Makko. The restaurant is not very big, due to holiday season, there's a huge crowd. Reservations is highly recommended. We didn't get to make reservations hence waited almost an hour for a table. Personally I find that it is worth it. The serving of food is fast.We ordered quite a few dishes. We particularly like the Lemak Nanas Udang. The taste is super good. The beef rendang is good too, very tender. We also ordered this fried sotong which was recommended by their staff, that taste yummy too. Lastly, it is their Chendol! It doesn't look appealing but it is really good.Overall, the food are all very good. Though my friends were very hesitant over the one hr queue, they all find it worth it after the meal.Show less

Author: twln1
Title: Amazing food
Review: Food was really great. Definitely reccomend. Must go if you're in Melaka. Very busy though, must make a booking.

Author: 266Ann
Title: Just for the food
Review: Poor service and opening time is short. (Lunch served from 11.30-2.30 Dinner : 6-9.15pm).  Came here for the food and it was delicious specially the fish.

Author: CrystalismKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Makko pretty good Nyonya food
Review: Nyonya food pretty good. Portions are reasonable. Even better still if they could come up with smaller portions so we can order more. Food arrived within 10 mins of ordering even when the place was packed - very quick! Well some dishes are already pre-prepared hence they probably just heat up and serve. Service is pretty bad- all local staffs and they all come with an attitude. But there was one particular lady which was really nice- she took our orders, patiently recommended some dishes and gave us our bill. She was very smiley and she was not like the rest who looked angry and cranky for no reason. Overall we liked their food and we will definitely recommend! :)Show less

Author: genekhoo
Title: Authentic Nonya food
Review: Good authentic Nonya food. Prior reservation recommended during peak periods. Reasonable menu varieties. Prices above average, about RM20-30 per person.

Author: EdwinLau
Title: Cosy Nyonya Restaurant
Review:
Delicious nyonya food served as mentioned by many.

Do book in advance if your party is big or be disappointed. Their business is good
Restaurant prices.

Food was served pretty fast. 
Would dine here again.

Author: greenestbubbles
Title: Family friendly, big portions, yummy food!
Review: Staff are friendly. Food is as authentic as nyonya food gets. The portions are big and reasonably prized which makes it great for sharing. Family friendly environment. Would definitely recommend and visit again!

Author: bella w
Title: shiok shiok ! miss the cendol
Review:
Had a sedap( maken) meal ,simple chilly n no chilli .
pls either go early or do reservation! no wonder had quite a number of staff around.

Author: happynjoyful
Title: Great yummy place!
Review:
1. Nice little authentic family run restaurant. 
2. It just gets better. Very friendly atmosphere. 
3. Our must cover first stop each visit - for nostalgia n yummy food!
4. Favourite - Assam pedas prawn, fluffy egg, sambal brinjal, chillies ladies finger.

Author: Chrissie2980Singapore
Title: Nice Food
Review: Our friend recommended us this restaurant as she told us that this is the best authentic Nyonya restaurant she tried in Melaka. The food indeed taste delicious and the prices were reasonable. It was worthwhile to wait for 30 minutes as we did not make reservation.Show less

Author: tpshSingapore
Title: Reasonably priced Nyonya dishes
Review: We went on Monday evening at 6 pm. Restaurant was very cold. People streamed in steadily. The waitress attending to us was helpful in her recommendations. Food was good and reasonably priced with no GST and service charged.The 'pon tey' chicken was our favourite. The snapper fish was fresh but a little pricey @ RM $56. The chendol was better than the sago in our opinion. This chendol is all right. I've tasted better ones in Melaka.They are closed on Tuesdays. Dinner starts at 6 pm. Do check out their operating hours. Show less

Author: 652RobertS
Title: Delicious well priced
Review: All are delicious, we came back twice. we love the cendol, its unlike the cendol that we normally tried. This peranakan restaurant i a must try when you visit Melaka

Author: CChanHK
Title: Authentic Nyonya Restaurant
Review: It's just about 5 minutes walk from Hatten Shopping Centre & Equatorial Hotel. Convenient location. Their menu has extensive varieties of Nyonya food to choose. Taste is good and price is reasonable. Its ambience is good too. Highly recommended.

Author: Kathleen_Leong
Title: Good service
Review: First time here for dinner and we have to wait for more than an hour when we arrived at 6 pm. Service was prompt and food served was quick however the Nonya Prawn and Fish we ordered were not fresh.

Author: trvkakiSingapore, Singapore
Title: Place where you could find authentic peranakan food
Review: This may not be the best peranakan restaurant in Melaka but easily one of the top five there. A place where you could find authentic peranakan food but as with a lot of restaurants, they seemed to have refrain from serving pork or lard which meant that their taste is slightly short of the past.Environment inside the restaurant was pleasant and the air con was cooling in the hot weather. In Melaka please do not take the air con for granted as some places with air con turned on feel like without.Pricing was considered reasonable thing though you could likely find cheaper alternatives in the nearby vinicity.Popular place where there is waiting time before your turn to be served.Show less

Author: Sky_Seow
Title: Average Taste, Big Portion
Review:
Slightly over-rated. Taste is alright only, but service is very fast. The restaurant is spacious though, getting a table at lunchtime is not that difficult.
Prefer the Ole Sayang Nyonya Restaurant across the street.

Author: R LSingapore, Singapore
Title: Got To Want To Eat And Be Persistant
Review: The first time we got there late in the afternoon and they refused to serve us. It was disappointing and a little upsetting for us who had traveled a long way and had empty stomachs. But we found food elsewhere and went back another time. Then we learnt of the queuing that is required. The waitress will seem rude and all with all the number of people she has to handle but there's always a nice way to wiggle your way in and get a seat by speaking politely. And after all that effort, the food was worth it! Highly recommend the sotong kunyit and the assam prawns.Show less

Author: SingaporeCatlover88Singapore
Title: After so many decades, food still maintain good
Review: On the last day in historical Malacca, decided to dine at one of the oldest yet famous surviving peranakan restaurant. Restoran Nyonya Mako is one of my favorite peranakan restaurant despite many new restaurants competing in the Melaka Raya but nothing compared to Nyonya Mako.I reached about 7pm to my surprise on Monday evening the restaurant crowded with diners mostly locals dining with family and friends. Managed to get a place and going thru' the menu nothing much has changed the same with signature dishes like ayam pongteh, ayam buah keluak and my all time favorite udang masak lemak nenas. Looking around tha ambience of the restaurant the same like I can imagined myself back then like two decades ago in the early 90s. The food maintained yummy and prices still very reasonable despite stiff competition with the newly opened peranakan restaurants dotting along the Melaka Raya. Going back to Nyonya Mako for authentic peranakan food like walking down my memory lane when I first visited Malacca when there was the kereta lembu ride at the Dataran Pahlawan. So nostalgic that I promised myself going back for more....nyonyalicious nyonya mia.Show less

Author: mgbassSingapore
Title: Average Fare
Review: Wasn't wowed by the food, probably had my expectations too high with all the raves about the restaurant. Perhaps I wasn't used to the flavours of Peranakan food e.g. I find the chilis that were drenched on top of the okra lacking omph in both heat level and flavours. But it was a good experience nonetheless. And a good place to chat with friends after a day of walking around town.Service was good and we waited for a while - around 15 minutes and got ourselves a table for 4 on a Saturday evening, slightly before 8pm.Show less

Author: Bluebunny2046
Title: Delicious foods with good service
Review: Compare others restaurant selling Nyonya cuisine, here price range is more affordable and value for money. My favorite dishes is Ayam Pon Teh, definitely will come back again

Author: billiefunkyjean
Title: Lovely food
Review: We went on a saturday night, we had to wait around 20 minutes to get a table. But it was well worth it. Everything we ordered was delicious. From the asam pedas fish, to their baba nyonya style chicken.

Author: AzmeerSulong
Title: Nice place for Nyonya delicacies.
Review: We had a group dinner of about 30 pax. The service was fast and the foods were very delicious. We had a bowl of chendol as dessert and we enjoyed it very much.

Author: GratefulObserver
Title: Food
Review:
The Hee Pioh soup was tasty. 
Fried scramble eggs with cincalok was surprising good. 
Go for sagu gula Melaka instead of their cendol. It is heavenly yummy!!
Note that they are closed on Tuesday. 
Lunch served frm 11.30-2.30
Dinner : 6-9.15pm

Author: 383sharonlSingapore
Title: Very good food but need to wait a bit
Review: We queued outside the restaurant for 30 minutes. The service was good. We loved the rendang chicken, the fried tumeric calamari, the pineapple prawns were very fresh. We also ordered the chicken pong teh, fried brinjal, Asam fish was average and sambal petai. Overall we enjoyed our lunch here very much. 7 person for $317. Show less

Author: ReubenC1606Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Amazing food
Review: Had a few dishes here and I cannot wait to go back. This place is super busy over lunch and especially dinner, so a waiting list is always used. Best to come early. They close during the mid afternoon and resume for dinner at 6pm. There aren't very many tables inside, but it is a MUST TRY for the food. The cendol, the best I had in Melaka, albeit subjective to taste, but never the less very yummy. I would like to see the staff be a little friendlier though. I without a doubt would recommend this place for dinner. In fact, you must go. Show less

Author: oneserKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Average Nyonya food
Review: Reservation is a must. Otherwise it is a 30-45min wait.The restaurant does not live up to the hype. The dishes were average and not tasty. Some of the dishes we had were:Ayam Pongteh Otak FishOmelette CincalokLobakLady's Fingers with ChilliTheir Sago Gula Melaka was probably the best thing I had there.Service is prompt and efficient. Staff is friendly if overloaded.Show less

Author: tripreview777
Title: Authentic Peranakan
Review: It's our favorite peranakan restaurant as service is fast and friendly. Food is authentic peranakan tho fish may not always be the freshest.

Author: jasonhoeLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Deliciously cheap!
Review: This place is away from Jonker St and situated near the bigger hotels and shopping mall. Very easy to get to and I highly recommend eating here. The food was fantastic if you love foods such as Indonesian and Thai where they use a lot of aromatic flavours (eg chilli, lemongrass). The service was incredibly fast, portions were a great size and the cost was RM70 for 4 dishes and two bottles of water! You are best to make a reservation as the place was full and known to have a queue outside. It also closes early around 8:45pm too! Show less

Author: SherxueSingapore, Singapore
Title: Cheap delicious Nyonya food!
Review: A fan of Nyonya food, this restaurant is a must return whenever I'm back in Malacca. Don't be put off by the run down interior, the food has the touch of homemade goodness and quality has been pretty consistent.My most recent order included Chap Chai, Beef Rendang (must try!), Duck with salted vegetables soup, Omelette and Buah Keluak Ayam (another of my favourite). Finished a whole sauce dish of Sambal Belachan by myself too! Try eating the Keropok with the Sambal Belachan, you will be addicted for sure!If you have a love for Nyonya food, this is a gem not to be missed! Show less

Author: paraplanner15
Title: Poor service with overrated food
Review: Service staffs arrogant and not bother to serve with smile.Food was expensive and overrated.Nothing above average and yet staffs behaved as if customers owe them a living. Maybe because they think business will continue to flourish due to these "good" reviews and start to act arrogantly.Nothing beats having good service.Show less

Author: Shah JSingapore
Title: Nyonya Goodness
Review: Being Singaporean, we trust queues. And we found a really healthy one waiting for their turn outside this restaurant. Luckily we had called ahead for a reservation and speedily found seats.The food was really fresh, and on point. Particular favourites was this turmeric squid dish and steamed lady fingers served with steamed chilli. We were so fond of the keropok that we bought two large packs to munch on!Very quick, prompt service. Paid about RM185 for five peopleShow less

Author: WeeWeiYangMelaka, Malaysia
Title: Freshly Prepared
Review: Had lunch just at this very crowded restaurant and found all ingredients fresh. The recommended dish is the Nyonya otak and sea bass fish. But personally I prefer the babi pongteh to be more rich in flavor and chap chye to be more softer as it was not stewed long enough. Overall happy with the food but do be prepared to wait at least half and hour.Show less

Author: JoshChuiSingapore, Singapore
Title: Average nyonya food
Review: Been to this restaurant a few times. The standards are going down. Sometimes I wonder if the dishes are just reheated and served. However, this round we had very good chendol. It is even better than the ones in Jonker St. Don't think I will come back here again.Show less

Author: KCsgjbChangi, Singapore
Title: amazing food; worth the wait
Review: judging from the crowd waiting for a seat outside the restaurant, you know it is definitely worth the time. locals patron this place too, only goes to prove it isn't a tourist trap. supremely highly marvelously recommended!dishes to try:ayam buah keluak: chicken cooked in soy sauce with a special nutty fruit. u gotta taste it before you say u don't like it.otah: steam fish mashed up with chilli and coconut milk. tastes better than the description sounds. don't worry.sayur lodeh: vegetables stewed in mildly spicy coconut milk broth. heavenly!asam fish: spicy acidic broth, with fish and lady fingers. and don't forget to finish off the meal with a cendol (red beans with green confectionary bathed with generous coconut milk and coconut sugar syrup)!burp.Show less

Author: kudamasKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Interest caught by the long queue outside
Review: Chose this restaurent for some authentic nyonya Melaka food because the long queue outside gave us the impression that it must be good. Went before 6 pm and were the first few to go in when it opened. Ordered fried sotong with tumeric, non spicey chicken with potato gravy, grilled fish with sambal, fried kangkong, prawn omelette and gula melaka cendol. Were impressed by the sotong and the cendol. Others were average. Show less

Author: Actuarial_MathSingapore
Title: Did Not Even Taste Like Nyonya Food. Low Quality, Poor Taste, Expensive, Overhyped.
Review: We read good reviews of this restaurant and decided to try it. When we arrived for lunch, there was an empty table just nice for us. After a while, the queue was 1 hour long.We ordered asam prawns, fried chicken, otah, fish maw soup, and a plate of prawn cracker appetiser. For all the dishes, there was no Nyonya taste of cooking at all; they were at best Chinese cooking and at worst disguised Nyonya cooking. The quality of food is not refined and they were not tasty at all. We have eaten better quality and tastier street food and mall food in Melaka. The highly praised prawn crackers were very starchy; no prawn taste at all. The prices were steep. This is the 2nd worst Nyonya restaurant we have ever eaten at in Melaka over our 10+ years of travelling there. Definitely overhyped on the Internet. Do avoid this restaurant and try some other Nyonya restaurants for more authentic and better quality Nyonya food.Show less

Author: travellerrobbo15
Title: Fantastic local food
Review: Delicious local food in a pleasant setting. Service could be better but on the whole a very enjoyable experience. Worth booking ahead.

Author: GenayeoSingapore, Singapore
Title: Went twice but taste was different
Review: Went there twice over a interval of 3 days but the same dish that we have ordered, pongteh tasted different the second time when we patronised. We don't know whether it's due to change of Chef.The rendang beef is definitely a no no coz it's very hard and the rendang does not taste like the normal rendang sauce.The kangkong & prawn omelette are nice.Show less

Author: Shammy17Kuala Lumpur
Title: Tasteless food!
Review: This place was recommended by some blogs so I decided to give it a try. It was an utter disappointment! I ordered Ayam Goreng Makko, Asam Pedas Fish, Mixed Vegetables and Sotong Masak Lemak with pineapples. The Asam Pedas fish was tasteless, it was neither sour (as claimed by its name 'asam') nor spicy (pedas). And for that, they charged a bomb! The sotong was full of coconut milk and I couldn't taste anything else. I really don't understand why this place is so hyped up. I have definitely tasted better nyonya food in other places around Malacca. Show less

Author: 131pangp
Title: Overprice.. More for tourists
Review: Went to makko when I stay at straits suites. Long queue as there are very little limited tables. Ordered some food but mostly not meant for kids as they are spicy. So we just ordered some non spicy dishes. Personally I find the dishes too salty even on the fried prawn omelette. The price was more costly as compares to other Nyonya restaurant like Nancy 's kitchen, Donald and lily etc. Personally I like and preferred Tong Sheng. Check out my reviewsShow less

Author: Justinlyh
Title: Arrogant
Review: Visited this restaurant for lunch, even you go early to the restaurant, the were always crowded with customers, you need to queue up at outside waiting for call. The service was bad and arrogant. Price rather expensive and the food quality had dropped.

Author: damienchiang
Title: A visit to the closest Nyonya restaurant to our hotel
Review: We ordered a variety of dishes which comes up to under RM80 for three adults and one child. Decent food but with wanting service which comes complete with full service charge and GST. Nice otak otak though.

Author: Gerald KSingapore
Title: Quality of food has dropped
Review: The quality of food at Makko has dropped through the years. I would give the food here with just a pass, and there are way better nyonya food in Melaka. The food and drinks are also a bit pricey. My wife and I ordered the pongteh, rendang and hee paw soup, and the taste of the food was not as flavorful as nyonya food should be. Nyonya food is often rich, flavorful, and has many ingredients that contributes to the explosion with your tastes buds, but sadly, the food here did not do any. It tasted like something I can get at a normal coffee shop. I have eaten at Makko numerous times in the past, but this would likely be the last for me.Show less

Author: K.E. C
Title: Saturday lunch
Review: Pricey overall, otak-otak dish average, standard not maintained. Curry fish overpriced.  Patronised restaurant several times over the year; noticeable fall in quality of food.

Author: WarstelSingapore, Singapore
Title: Nyonya Restaurant with Taste but with Issue
Review: Quality of food ok and taste was not too bad. Price was more for Tourist and local above average man rather than weekly lunch/dinner outing. Had nothing Fancy beside Fish for a meal of 5 people cost almost RM240.Fish with Sambal, Fried Egg, Sambal Kang Kung, Fried Sotong, Petai with Prawn, Chicken Stew and Ngoh Hiang. All small portion.I wanted to visit again can call the Restaurant on Saturday evening around 8:10pm. They told me no reservation and please come and Que..... I acknowledge and reach there around 8:30pm with family. They say no more food and cannot que. I ask them why they not mentioned earlier when I call and advise me of such? They just say nothing they can do and sorry. So you be a judge such Restaurant worth? Food not really great but just good only.Show less

Author: graciepapaSingapore, Singapore
Title: Crowded but wont take too long
Review: There is almost always a dinner queue at this place but they turnover the tables pretty quickly so the wait is quite fast. The nonya dishes had strong flavours as it should be and did not disappoint. Two dishes that to me are must tries - fried squid with tumeric and cendolShow less

Author: TanCK
Title: Ok.
Review: The food taste nice, but there were very little if you order the small size. Prices are at the high side. Have to wait outside the shop until there is a table available for you then you will be called.

Author: ind3cisiv3MY
Title: Delicious authentic nyonya food
Review: Being a Malaysian, I must say that nyonya food is hard to find needless to say authentic nyonya. This is one of the places that actually serves what I would call an authentic nyonya food. Nothing I can complain about. Must try will be of course the cendol - the taste of the palm sugar feels like it's still lingering in my mouth as I'm writing this review after my last visit there - in september. Another must try will be the pineapple prawns. The chap chai nothing special as this food can be well cooked in any other nyonya food places since it's not that hard to make. Oh, how can i miss out the ayam pongteh? Also the sambal ikan bilis and cincalok egg....!!! ok.. cincalok can be an acquired taste. not everyone will like it. In short, it's better to go with a big group and order as much as you can to try at least a bite of everything. you will not be disappointed.Show less

Author: MaxMayaSingapore
Title: Awesome Peranakan Food!
Review: I had my fair share of Peranakan food around Malacca. Nothing can beat this place! The Garam Ikan is a must try for lovers of spicy chilli. The dessert, I have to admit is not the best around especially their Melaka Chendol. Note they only open for approx. 4 hours for lunch and closes thereafter and re-open for dinner. Reservations highly recommended!Show less

Author: babyxan88Subang Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Real nyonya food in Malacca?
Review: Restoran Nyonya Makko serves really good nyonya food. I know there are many others out there but I managed to try this one first! Actually, I noticed every table the orders taken are almost similar. It's like these are the main few recommendations for every tourists that walks in. Hence the taking order part was fast and swift, the serving was pretty quick and served together. It's like they know what we're going to order already.My total bill came up to RM161.75 for 4 pax. Okay~lah for the portion and the meals were almost satisfying except for the fish dish... I should've have tried "Assam Fish" instead! Btw, I can't stand spicy meals, but the dishes here weren't so spicy. It was just right for me. For spicy lovers (like my mom & my hubby) it was more flavorful then spicy to them lolx...Show less

Author: Alison L
Title: Yum.
Review: Nice food. Great ambience. Cendol is a must to eat there.  Definitely miss the food and will be back if I'm gonna be in malacca.

Author: imafulltimemummyPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Restaurant with traditional feel, reasonable price and delicious dishes!
Review: Ambience and environment around the restaurant is cozy and quiet. After we placed our orders, we were served with a plate of tapioca crackers (RM2 per plate) while we waited for our food. Our kiddos seem to enjoy the crackers and when I turned around, I noticed the restaurant sell these crackers too. Dishes we love: prawn omelette, fried fish with salted sambal and the cendol is a must!Show less

Author: Agape10Hong Kong, China
Title: Only Average
Review: Walked by this restaurant one day in Melaka which is just opposite Novotel Melaka.The restaurant was packed when I walked in so I said to myself :"this place must be good then". To my surprise, the food was just average and nothing spectacular.I ordered two dishes: Rendang Ayam and Ngoh Hsiang (five spice beancurd roll).The Rendang Ayam were mainly just bones and hardly any meat attached to the bones! The bones were all pretty soft and fell apart the minute you poke your fork on it! It's quite obvious that it had been cooked for a while.The five spice beancurd roll on the other hand were quite good. The price is rather pricey for the food portions served.Not a must try as I have tried better Nyonya cuisine.Show less

Author: TsogoolyrPutrajaya, Malaysia
Title: Famous Nyonya Restaurant
Review: Lunch time is 11.30am till 2.45pm. We left restaurant at 12.30pm and there were around 20 ppl waiting outside of the restaurant. Friendly waitress made helpful recommendations. Pineapple prawn, fern leaf, lo bak and fried chicken tasted good. Ayam buah keluak is not up to mark though. Overall, an apt place to try Nyonya cuisines withouth having to pay too much. Show less

Author: flhl82Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: just a PASS .......
Review: I came to this restaurant with a group of friend on Sunday afternoon , as expected there are other patrons queueing up for seats.....It took approximately 15 minutes for the queueing !!! Overall the quality of the food is so so as i have try some other places " otak " particularly from Muar which is far better than this restaurant. On that particular day the waitress has actually messed up our order BUT fortunately we are already full so might as well cancel off the order. The food is slightly expensive because of the fame of this restaurant at Melaka. However, this is not the truth........in fact i am very disappointed with their cendol. Their cendol are very poor even some roadside stalls outside of Melaka can beat this restaurant , the portion is little and tasteless !!! Overall the atmosphere & cleanliness is up to standard and it is suitable for a group / family to try out some of the Melaka local delicacy.Show less

Author: rayee2015Singapore, Singapore
Title: Nice food. Can give it a try!
Review: Read about it from other trip advisors. Decide to give it a try. Waiting time was long. Ordered a few dishes. My favorite is the Beef Rendang. The other was the mixed curry Veg. We also ordered the Assam fish. Not too bad but not my favorite. If you are around the area, can consider of giving it a try. Show less

Author: mmc87
Title: Delicious food
Review: Traditional baba nyonya restaurant. Friendly staff, delicious nyonya style food. The food price is not expensive (normal price).

Author: SheenaStReichertshofen, Germany
Title: Hidden jewel
Review: Found this at the recommendation of Family. From outside, you see nothing except some kitschig stained glass Windows. But inside, it is bustling with activity!Food style is Nonya, which is chinese styled with malay and Indian Flairs of spices.I tried the Chicken Rendang, with Soup, and with Fernleave with sambal.Most of the Food is spicy, so ask before if you cannot take spice.They also sell home made Chips, which are so so tasty...Service is simple, fast and Food is extremely satisfying.Show less

Author: EdwinC79Singapore
Title: Cost Friendly Restaurant
Review: we went to cottage spices when we could not get a table at Makko. So the next day, we went at 11am in anticipating for an early lunch. there restaurant opens at 11.30am and a queue already forms up! see picture. when the door opens, everyone tried to rush in forgoing the line that was in place, so whoever is more kaisu, will get a seat. we ordered:Ayam Buah Keluak Salty Duck SoupOtakPetai another green veg. cannot spell it in English. Ayam Buah Keluak not to our liking. the gravy is rather diluted but the part that failed u us its the Buah Keluak. The Kernel is not grind so it taste really bitter. what really good about Makko is the price. we paid RM 75 for 5 dishes! we paid more at Cottage spices for 3 dishes. Overheard walk in customers at 12 noon that the wait for a table is at least an hour. So go early.Show less

Author: Koh M
Title: Good service with nice food
Review: Good service and the food are nice. Not so salty but tasty. Be preapred at weekend or holiday, there will be long queue. But the staff will ask you to leave you contact detail and they will call you when the table is ready.

Author: FriendsOfPeasSingapore, Singapore
Title: Thumbs up!
Review: The food here is really good and affordable. We ordered kangkong belachan, assam fish pedas, ladies finger belachan and cendol. We couldn't try more dishes as there were only 2 of us. As we glanced at all the other diners' tables, we made a mental note of what we shall try the next time we come back, which is very soon. For big groups, I think it's best to make a reservation.Show less

Author: KavinSothyPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Disappointing service
Review: Food is definitely good, only disappointment was the place opens at 630pm and we waiting outside second in line from 6pm waiting to enter but when the doors opened the waitress spoke in mandarin and ignored us who requested her to speak English and totally ignored those who had been queuing patiently to allow people from the behind the queue to enter.
