Very disappointing service. Show less

Author: skylee91
Title: First time here
Review: The food is special. We ordered the egg, chicken, belacan vege. All are delicious. You may refer the others' review. We just based on the review to order the dishes. The lime juice is very refreshing. Mamamiya~ ^^

Author: hsienhuitSingapore, Singapore
Title: Worth the one hour wait
Review: To qualify this review, I have never waited in line for an hour to eat. I just feel that there is better use of my time and ultimately, food is food. However, after having nixed my wife's plans to line up for an hour to eat Putu Piring and for a similar long wait to eat Satay Celup, I agreed to be patient this time although you will probably have an idea as to how I felt and what my expectations were when we finally got a table. I fully expected to be disappointed and was almost eager to run it down.But the quality of the food changed my mind and really lifted my spirits. They served a delicious plate of keropok as an appetizer, small, thin, crispy, yet with sufficient body to make it go perfectly with beer. We ordered sambal petai, ayam buah keluak and ikan assam pedas. The food was prepared superbly and I have to admit that it was the best Nyonya food I have ever had. So inspite of my original intention to say that waiting for the food was a waste of time, I have no hesitation in now stating that the food was well worth the one hour wait! Show less

Author: Powerpuff_GalSingapore, Singapore
Title: Above average Nyonya food
Review: Hub and I had to queue for about 30 mins for lunch but once we were seated, service was prompt and we had our food served to us quite promptly. We ordered the cinchalok egg omelette, stir-fry four wings beans and fried fish with home-made chili sauce. The egg omelette was tasty but there wasn't much cinchalok in it. The four-wings beans were nice and crunchy. The best dish was the fried fish with the home-made chili, it was really delicious! The chili wasn't too spicy yet it delivered enough kick. It was fresh and slightly sweet and it went really well with the fish. We also ordered the Chandol and it was quite pleasant. Personally I had better chandol in Penang, but Makko's chandol was still enjoyable. All in all, I enjoyed my lunch and I would recommend this place. Note that Makko closes by 2 pm!Show less

Author: Caren LKuala Lumpur, Wilayah Persekutuan, Malaysia
Title: Delicious Nyonya dishes
Review: They service is super fast. After order, in around 10 minutes, all dishes is served. I love the cendol, is very tasty with the gula Melaka-thumbs up for it. As for dinner, we order Asam fish, asam shrimp, lady finger, otak-otak and sotong with petai. Overall the food is delicious and nice.Give it a try there.Is advisable to make reservation before go there cause dinner time is pack.Show less

Author: ChinkChongSingapore
Title: Not bad!
Review: Still sitting in the restaurant and writing this review, its got old vintage nonya decor and from the outside it looks closed but just look out for the sign! Pretty ok zi char nonya food. But I tried the 4 angle beans and sayur lodeh and cincalok omelette and they were good! Thumbs up after a long day, value for money !Show less

Author: LillianTeh
Title: Thumbs up Cendol
Review: Thie Nyonya restaurant serves good food. Their cendol was superb. But the Pong Teh chicken was so salty. The other dishes were fine. The service was fast and efficient.

Author: Teddy05
Title: Baba Delight
Review: Great restaurant that is only a stone throw from hatten hotel.  The Ayam ponteh, buah  kualak, Assam fish, wild vegetable, turmeric cuttlefish, Ngoh Hiang, steam toufu were delicious.  Cost myr300 for 11pax.  The keropok cost myr10.70 and great for beer...

Author: limwc78
Title: Excellent Food
Review: All the spicy food is tasty, beside equatorial we finally got other option to eat already. The price is reasonable.

Author: thinksg
Title: Nyonya Dishes
Review: The location was excellent. Stone's throw away from the main shopping belt. Food was excellent, tasty and authentic Nyonya dishes. Will definitely return in the future.

Author: lpchiannKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: homey
Review: one very family style restaurant that serves nyonya food. super homey, reasonable price (not pricey), great cook. Not delicacies, but you'll taste the most local and homey dishes. must try their CHENDOL! if Gelato represents Italy, then Chendol represents Melaka. Icy cold Gula Melaka syrup after hot and spicy Nyonya food, heaven!Show less

Author: Bell NIpoh
Title: Just a perfect taste of spice!
Review: Good service, nice food, nice ambiance. Not like others, to me Nyonya food always have a taste of sweetness despite how spicy it may looks like. We ordered Chicken Pongteh, a curry mix vege, and the Gula Melaka Sago. Chicken Pongteh - the meat was so tender even me who didn't like chicken breast swallow a lot! The curry mix vege has a very mild taste with a touch of coconut milk it gave the dish a well balance between spicy and sweetness, and the sago just brighten up my day!Show less

Author: seijinm82Singapore, Singapore
Title: Delicious Peranakan Food
Review: Went on a Sunday, and I was considerably lucky as I got a seat for two just by walking in. Just a few minutes later, a crowd came in and a queue was formed. Ordered Ayam buah Keluak, Sayur Lodeh, Ngoh Hiong and Cincaluk Omelette - the Ayam Buah Keluak is delicious, better than a restaurant on Jonker Street; the Ngoh Hiong is a bit too salty for me while the other two is considerably tasty. Ended my meal with a bowl of Cendol which is just nice; not too sweet. This restaurant is walking distance from Hatten and Equitorial Hotel.Show less

Author: Annie GKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Not as good as before
Review: Ate here years ago and as i remember it, it was very good. This time around the food is not as pungent and is milder. Asam fish is not sour enough, paku sambal is not spicy, cincalok fried egg not enough cincalok. Pongteh chicken is good sauce is so watery. Curry chicken is good but not spicy enough. Overall is dissappointed. The cendol is still the highlight of the meal.Show less

Author: JALOVE9189
Title: Great food!
Review: The Otak-otak is a must try I'd say. The Makko curry is excellent as well. What is a bit disappointing was the omelette with fu-yu. It was quite salty and can't go solo without rice. Tried the sambal paku vege. That was quite good as well. Overall recommended!Show less

Author: SFJCWongPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: Good food.
Review: We were brought to this restaurant by a close friend and had to wait for a short while as we did not make prior booking (lesson learnt, come early to wait if you did not book, a line started after us). The first waitress was moody and looked angry all the time, but we understood that it could have been her bad day. Another one came to take our order & served us, she was charming and helpful in catering to our tastes. We had pineapple prawn curry, cincaluk omelette, pong teh chicken, chap chye and clear soup, with white rice. The food was flavorful of typical Nyonya dishes and served in good portions. We probably will try out other Nyonya restaurants if we had to wait in line. Prices are exclusive of GST.Show less

Author: 333pennyf
Title: Food indulgence.
Review: The otak2 was good n the tau Foo dish too.too . This place was recommended by a Front Desk Manager at The Settlemen hotel.

Author: satoyurikosingapore
Title: Enjoyed Nonya food to the max!
Review: Finally got a chance to eat at this Restaurant as it's always crowded! We were ushered promptly to our seats and the server recommended their signature to us - so we had rendang chicken, otah otah, ngoh hiang, chap chye, chincalok omelette, and chendol for dessert.I must say that the appearance of the dishes are not fantastic but the taste is wonderful! We enjoyed the food so much and regretted not dining here earlier.Price is really affordable and service was good. We left with a bottle of sambal chilli and 4 pkts of keropokShow less

Author: Eraz7
Title: A very popular haunt
Review:
So tried it bec its popular...long wait , more than 30 minutes, in the humidity of Melaka even at an hour before closing at lunch time...

Good food bec we were rushed ....ordered only basic stuff...

Author: Foodhunterees
Title: Wonderful local food experience!
Review: My local friend took us to this place. This place have the best Malaysia food ever. The restaurant itself people will prob say it needs renovating but I totally disagree. I would not enjoy this authentic local food experience if this place is fully five star decor. It defeats the purpose of the word "Authentic". Me and my two best friends ordered so many dishes and were afraid we couldn't finish but it was so good we ate everything! We had chicken and potato, green veggie, steamed fish, fried sotong(calamari rings), pineapple prawn curry, soup. For dessert we had two cendol and gula Malaka(palm sugar). It was the best meal I've had during the 10 days I was there. My 5th time in Malacca. Would definitely go back again!Show less

Author: highburychampion
Title: Ok food, seems authentic
Review:
Food was tasty and seemed authentic.  We went with a local person and they assured us it was extremely popular.

The decor inside needs updating. Apart from that, the food was pretty good, the service quick, but nothing wow to say about it overall.

Sonya

Author: AndrewTanSingapore
Title: Ok food.
Review: We were recommended by the hotel staff to visit this restaurant. Reached at 11.30am n the place was almost filled. The prawn cracker n chendol was nice. The itek tim soup was overly salty. The beef rending was tough. The chicken was dry.The prawn n fish dish was okShow less

Author: SingLaiSingapore, Singapore
Title: Disappointed after braving the terrible traffic
Review: Had good expectations of the food quality for this restaurant but was terribly disappointed after eating the food.Fish was okay.We ordered a tofu which is fried with some sauce. The oil used for frying the tofu seems to have a stale smell. Should have change the oil more often.The chicken is okay, could be more tender.The chendol was total disappointment. Full of coconut milk that is not fragrant at all but left us feeling bloated. Then again, we just went to Penang to have the most wonderful chendol at kimberly street.Will definitely not be back to this restaurant.Show less

Author: ongjanice1Petaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Nothing to shout about
Review: Apparently this is one of the best places to dine in Malacca and it is within walking distance from Hatten Square & Hatten Hotel. We were staying at Hatten Hotel (5 mins walk), so, the location is superb! My 1st impression of the restaurant; require refurbishment, tables & chairs are "old", no deco whatsoever and the waitresses are not happy serving. Since we pre-ordered a few days before the meeting, our dishes came pretty quickly. We ordered most of their signature dishes (some of the dishes are attached with this review). Of all the dishes, the dish I enjoyed the most is the beef & to my surprise, the chendol is very good!! YUMMY!! Other than that, the dishes are just ordinary (I've tasted better elsewhere) & lastly, the lobak is a waste of time.Show less

Author: Celestar989Singapore, Singapore
Title: Average at Best, Pricey as Well
Review: Felt that the food was just average and a little pricey, perhaps it is slightly better than ole sayang nearby, but none of the dishes were spectacular. I guess this place is overrated. Eggplant dish was a little burnt, the chilli archar was forgettable while the otah I had was slightly raw and served cold. Was just thankful that I didn't get food poisoning after dinner.Show less

Author: jicby2Sydney, New South Wales, Australia
Title: Can't miss this place when in Melaka
Review: Amazing, amazing and more amazing! I've always got to stop by at this restaurant when I'm in Melaka and they've retained their quality. We ordered seven dishes and one cendol between four people and not one was not delicious. Special shout out to their steamed otak-otak, asam fish, egg cencaluk, kacang botel sambal and kerabu timun! Go early though because otherwise it gets packed and is a long wait for a table.Show less

Author: PeggyKohSingapore, Singapore
Title: Worth many more visits
Review: Our family of 8 enjoyed the spicy n non-spicy dishes. Food was tasty n of good value. Double for the chendol n sago gula melaka as ingredients were fresh n generous. The staff were polite n efficient even tho the place was crowded. We were glad we made prior reservation cos there was a queue when we arrived n left. Show less

Author: chew cSingapore, Singapore
Title: Long queue
Review: We were here in the evening of the 8th December 2014. We went in without reservation and have a booked a slot 1 hour later as there was quite a sizable crowd of local people waiting outside. We ordered 4 dishes i.e. ayam pongteh, prawns with pineapple , chap chai and chinchalok egg omelette plus the usual chendol. All dishes were done nicely with the prawns big and fresh.Although the pricing was okay please note that they charged for the paper towels as well as the tidbits served at the beginning.I supposed these can be declined if you dont really want them.All in all a good meal. It is not too far from Hatten Hotel where we stay. Just walk straight down the main road towards Starbucks side.of Datahran Palawan. Only abt 10 minutes walk. Recommended but book in advanceShow less

Author: vinz20
Title: Enjoyed the chendol !
Review:
I ate chendols from 4 different locations in Melaka based on recommendations of malaccans and found this to be the best. Thick and tasty gula melaka and freshly squeezed lemak santan. So good I had two bowls.

Food and Service was so-so.

Author: linnmansingapore
Title: Still as good
Review: We were last at Makko couple of years ago so we headed for this restaurant during our recent trip to Malacca. The place was still as crowded and the food was still good. We especially enjoyed the tenggiri fish in assam pedas, sotong chili garam, beef rendang and chendol (although I must say it still cannot beat the chendol at Madam Kwan's in KL as they are very generous with the gula melaka). The keropok was nice and we bought a few packets (RM11 a packet) to bring home. We also bought their sambal belachan (RM5 a bottle).Service was acceptable considering that all tables were full and the staff was stretched. Makko does not accept reservation by phone but if you are passing by earlier, you can put in your name, phone number and expected time and come back later.We will eat again at Makko next time we are in Malacca.Show less

Author: petaling
Title: Supposedly good food
Review:
but ambience no good.
I cant taste the difference btw this and the much cleaner restaurant at Equatorial Hotel
Cleanliness not up to Western standard.
My local friends think this is the restaurant but to each his own.

Author: yasumi999Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Bad food, bad service
Review: We went to Makko for dinner. We arrived slightly before 9, after circling the area several times before we finally found it - the signboard was not obvious at night.The second after putting menus on our table - I'm not exaggerating, it was really just one second after - the waitress asked us what we wana eat. I said wait, we haven't even looked at the menu yet. To which she replied rudely: our kitchen is closing.Usually with such response, I would've walked out right away. But it was close to 9, & we just spent so much time going round & round the area to get to this place, & it came with high recommendation ... so I went against my usual practice & stayed.Boy that was a huge MISTAKE!!!We ordered two dishes. The pineapple prawn was way too sweet, & the prawns didn't taste very fresh. The belacan four-angled beans, the beans were practically raw. The rice were big gooey rice lumps ... So the food: thumbs down!!!To make matters worse, while we were eating the waitresses (who spoke loudly throughout our stay) started to change out of their uniforms into their daily wear - totally unprofessional. Restaurants usually allocate at least half an hour after kitchen closes for customers to finish their meals, they don't stop operating immediately!And some of them started cleaning up - arranging tables & chairs loudly, even sweeping near us!!!We were told that this place has ppl queuing up outside during weekends. Are you serious???For the kind of food & service, they are definitely overpriced & overrated.This is one of the worse restaurants I've been to in my whole entire life!!!Show less

Author: ChiaBB
Title: Best Chendol in town
Review: Best Chendol in town. Friendly service. Authentic Peranakan food. Reasonably priced - "small" portions more than enough for two (hungry) adults.

Author: SoonhoeLSingapore, Singapore
Title: Absolutely disappointing!
Review: The restaurant was booked for a private function in late Dec 2013, so we dined in Ole Sayang which was above average fare. So I earmarked this restaurant for my future visit to Malacca.We went there for dinner 15th Oct 2015 Among the dishes we ordered were Nonya Chap Chai & Hee Peow Soup. The Nonya Chap Chai was below average; the cabbage was firm and the long beans were still somewhat crunchy! The gravy was a little bland. Clearly the dish was just prepared and no effort was made to check on the quality. The Hee Peow soup was terrible! It was salty & the soup was fishy. It tastes like the fish maw wasn't cleaned properly or something has gone bad. On afterthought, I regret not returning the dish.I don't have high expectations of Makko after experiencing Ole Sayang but the whole dining experience with Makko sucks. Thank goodness this is not our Makko (father's eldest sister, in perankan terms) otherwise we have to tolerate their bad cooking regularly.Show less

Author: sporestrikerSingapore, Singapore
Title: Feels like home cooked food
Review: The place was crowded tonight so we were fortunate to get a table quite fast. We ordered 6 dishes..too much food just for the 3 of us ..so the food must have been good because we finished everything! The best dish was the fried turmeric sotong which was very tasty. The chicken with buah keluak was better than the last time we tried it. Other dishes worth mentioning are the otah otah, steamed ladies fingers sambal and kangkong belacan. The price is reasonable too..everything including the drinks and beers costs less than RM 100.Show less

Author: imehu
Title: Nice food
Review: My husband loves Nyonya Food so we went to have lunch before we check in. The food was great and the staff was friendly.  The order came on time and we enjoy our lunch

Author: LillianTeh
Title: Thumbs up Cendols!
Review: My favourite cendols sold here! Bigger portion and the beans were frozen! It was always full house in this restaurant. Service was good and prompt.

Author: BabyG8787
Title: Family choice
Review: We always love Nyonya food and each time we visit Melaka it is a must for us to go and eat Nyonya Food. We try a lot of place but we still prefer this place.

Author: PoppyJnSingapore, Singapore
Title: Cheap & very good!
Review: We tried many Nyonya restaurants in Malacca over the years. Most of them too busy serving hungry tourists and charged at a price to make you think it's very special. Well, not at Nyonya Makko. The food was authentic like home-cook, tasty, flavourful and the price was great! MR90 for 4 adults and we ordered 'a lot'. We notice many locals come here to eat, proving it is a local favourite. Service is local style too, ie, if you are nice to the aunties, you may get served faster, though it's quite difficult to get attention in a busy restaurant. It's on the same road as Fenix Inn, along the shop houses opposite Fenix Inn and short walk away from Hatten Hotel.Show less

Author: Cynthia CSingapore, Singapore
Title: First visit
Review: Friends tell me that it's a popular restaurant that has a long queue everyday. We were lucky and passed lunch time. There wasn't any queue and we could order instantly. Food was good as other reviews, it's reasonable price too. Will definitely visit again if in malacca. It's worth a visit.Show less

Author: Patrick LSingapore, Singapore
Title: Decent Nyonya food
Review: Restaurant opens at 6pm and it gets filled up pretty fast, so do go early or make a reservation.Arrived on the dot at 6pm and was given a corner table which was great as it was more quiet. The crackers provided were very nice. We ordered the Ayam Pongteh, Ayam Buak Keluek, Omelette, Beef Rendang, Chap Chye soup etc.The portions were good and my family of 7 had some difficulty finishing up all the food. The Ayam Pongteh was not as 'thick' as I like, but I guess every peranakan restaurant/ family cooks it slightly differently. The beef rendang was nice and tender. As we eat, the restaurant was full and people have to wait outside. Before we left, we ordered the cendol which was quite nice although I prefer the one at Jonker 88. All in all, not too bad a meal.Show less

Author: Snoopy6364
Title: Local peranakan fare
Review: Local peranakan fare that is reasonably priced.  If possible, call and make reservation.  Crowded during weekends.

Author: 633ElizabethHSingapore, Singapore
Title: It was ok only; overrated
Review: Ordered the usual Nonya dishes like chap chye, Assam fish, cincalok omelette, otah, ponteh chicken, ayam buah keluak & fried chicken. Dessert: cendol & sago gula melaka. We thought the dishes were a tad too sweet, especially the Assam fish. Couldn't really taste the assam. The fried chicken was too hard. The dessert - was too sweet for our taste. Prices are slightly on the high side. Show less

Author: Ashley1119
Title: Good nyonya food with reasonable price
Review: It is difficult to find good nyonya food in Melaka, this is one of the oldest nyonya food restaurant we have in Melaka, i miss the cendol and otak-otak so much.

Author: poopshooterPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: the best nyonya choice in Melaka...
Review: There are quite a few Nyonya restaurants in Melaka. This is one of the oldest & is the best around. Only issue would be getting in. Gets way too crowded during peak times especially on weekends.Service is a hit & miss. When crowded they can get snappish however food does come pretty fast. They do try to quicken the turnover as business is brisk. The interior is clean & comfy decorated with Peranakan related items.Notable dishes to try would be the Ayam Buah Keluak, Asam Fish, Cincalok Omelette, Nyonya Chap Chye, Ayam Pongteh, Sotong Sambal & Okra Kerabu. All fresh, super yummy & very authentic. The cendol is just so so. Do note they are halal.Overall would definitely recommend as the place for Nyonya food when in Melaka. If you can get through the door that is.Show less

Author: SY_C7Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Authentic!
Review: An authentic Nyonya restaurants with excellent atmosphere. Food served were of good taste and priced reasonably as well. Service was good too. Way way better than the one across the street, Ole Sayang, which we would say overrated, pricy, lousy service and dishes were awful salty. Show less

Author: Boon Ken L
Title: Overrated for Nyonya food！
Review: There is no original taste of nyonya. The food was not okay at all. Overrated！No return in the future，we ordered Chap Chai，Rendang Ayam，Asam Fish and fried eggs and it was not a good choice to choose for Nyonya foods.

Author: RTham
Title: Good food
Review: Tasty peranakan (nyonya) food for the family. Love the Assam fish, Chincalok omelette, Otah otah and Chendol.

Author: corrine6Johor Bahru, Malaysia
Title: Overall ok, but nothing fantastic
Review: A friend recommended this restaurant to us and since we are in the area, the 4 of us decided to have dinner there.They open for dinner at 6pm, and I've been calling since then trying to make reservation, for an hour or so, nobody answer the call. So we head over to the restaurant directly. Due to weekend crowd, we were put on waiting list. Waited an hour for a table.We ordered ayam buah keluak, beef rendang, ngoh hiang, pineapple prawn, chap chai, itik tim & sambal petai. All dishes in small servings as we wanted to taste more varieties. I wanted to order babi pongteh but this is a halal restaurant so they don't serve pork. The itik tim is a total failure. Tasteless soup is a total disappointment!Ayam buah keluak, chap chai and pineapple prawn are just ok. Nothing special. Nothing to rave about. Have tasted better ones elsewhere.The better dishes are the beef rendang, ngoh hiang and sambal petai. Even then, it's not worth the wait and the crazy crowd and the price! We paid RM120 for 4 pax.Show less

Author: maran_maniam
Title: Not so wow about this restaurant
Review: Reach here after read reviews about this restaurant. But feel nothing so special here. Food just ok only. Things are little expensive. Not recommended for first timer who looking for nyonya food (I don't want you feel disappointed).

Author: GNEO
Title: Nice and authentic Nonya dish
Review: Worth a try if u love Nonya dishes. Their signature prawn and pineapple curry dish is really fragrant and smooth. Dishes feel really home cook and not too powering in taste.

Author: Aidanaj
Title: A little disappointed
Review: Fish - Assam fish moderate nothing that could wow its patron Turmeric chicken - Soggy and sweet with Tumeric tasteLadies finger was great but sambal was a bland one Sambal - a disappointment thought it was not really bad but I expect Nyonya sambal to be greatThe only special dish was petai with squid. Overall was just average.Staff was plenty but all serve with no heart. Show less

Author: Yk LSingapore
Title: Just average
Review: My wife and I visited Nyonya Makko as some reviews highly recommended. We walk in around 11.30 with reservation, there are only one table with customers, business is just normal even after we finished our meal 1 hour later. Food taste is also just average and quite salty with some dishes. The only thing I like is the Cendol with quite thick of Gula Melaka, staff is consider friendly, and the Perenakan's decor inside the restaurant. Show less

Author: chin2020Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Over-rated restaurant
Review: Located on a street where almost every other shop is a restaurant, we came here as some of our group have eaten here before. Since we arrived at lunch time, had to wait outside before they could get us a table.We ordered some of the dishes based on their recommendations - pineapple prawns, sambal fish, kangkung belacan, cencalok eggs, ayam ponteh, otak-otak, etc. Overall, it was just average - for an established that is packed with patrons, I expected better-tasting food. Have tasted better ones elsewhere.However, the cendol was the saving grace - it was fragrant and tasty.Overall, a bit pricey. Could have gotten better food elsewhere for the price we pay.Show less

Author: jlnkcSingapore, Singapore
Title: Good
Review: It's not one of the more famous nyonya restaurants in malacca and wasn't our first choice but we ate here as it was located near where we were staying but we were pleasantly surprised. Food was good overall with the buah keluak, fried chicken and sambal seabass being well cooked. Price of the meal was reasonable and I would return in future. Show less

Author: lighthandSingapore
Title: Over-leveraged on their history
Review: Tried this restaurant after recommendation from local guilds. However was very disappointed. The food was over-priced, and the drinks even more so. I still could not get over the fact that they change you for the sambal chili (that's just rude for a Nyonya restaurant).We had the bua kuluak, kang kong, meat ball soup, fried chicken and sambal fish.The bua kuluak was average and the meat ball soup was fine.The star of the night was surprisingly the fried chicken, it was well marinated and fried just right that it's crispy yet retain the juiciness.Biggest flop was the sambal fish. The sambal was weak and the fish have the aftertaste of mud.Service was poor as well (though maybe it's cause it was full house). It took a more than 10mins to get initial service to take our order. Also you get the feeling that they want you to clear off as fast as possible.Show less

Author: malepilot
Title: Over priced, over rated!
Review:
The food was over priced, especially drinks!
The taste was average! Nothing special! 
The sambal fish was not fresh, shocking!

Author: DaliCTSingapore, Singapore
Title: Food is ok.
Review: The food is ok. We ordered the otak otak, fried chicken, ngo hiang, fried calamari and pineapple fish. We had a surprised when we found a few strands of human hair embedded in the fried chicken! The ngo hiang was a disappointment. The pineapple fish was cooked in a diluted coconut sweet soup; we didn't like its taste. In the end, the restaurant didn't charge us for the fried chicken. Show less

Author: travelbug32_00Singapore, Singapore
Title: Our regular "makan" place in Melaka
Review: We have been patronising Makko for more than 10 years already and we eat there on average once a month. Having tried a good number of other Nonya restaurants in Melaka, this is still our favourite peranakan food joint whenever we are in Melaka.Taste is subjective and though not all their dishes are fantastic, there are a few favourites which has become our standard choices whenever we eat there. Their beef rendang, ayam ponteh, chap chai, ngoh hiang, ikan goreng, kang kong and assam mackeral are our regualr order ending with chendol. I am part peranakan and have tried Nonya food in Penang, Singapore, I prefer the Melaka version. Of course nothing beats my late mum's cooking! Service is very fast. I guess they have to be especially on weekends as the place gets pretty crowded at lunch and dinner time. We usually call to make reservations on weekends so as to avoid the sometimes long wait for a table. Weekdays are okay and you can walk in withour reservation. We always enjoy our visit to Makko. Personally I find the prices reasonable and this is one placeI know I get what I pay for. I usually take away 2 packets of their "kropok" (crackers). They sell them for 10 ringgit a pack. Buy them on Friday and Saturday as they are delivered fresh.Show less

Author: sporestrikerSingapore, Singapore
Title: Average at best
Review: Had dinner with my wife there two nights ago. The food was average at best especially with so many choices of good Nyonya restaurants in Melaka. We found keluaks in our Ayam Byuah Keluak disk not properly cooked and prepared. One of the keluaks was not even opened properly. The only saving grace was the delicious chendol. Would probably not come back unless it's just for the chendol.Show less

Author: silkypearl
Title: Delicious
Review: Simple yet delicious with reasonable pricing... Services was good too.  Enjoy the petai dish very much.

Author: PCKK_69Singapore, Singapore
Title: Overrated nonya food....
Review: Decided to go to Makko for Nonya Food..knowing that they are "famous" however me n wife were terribly dissapointed..we ordered the Assam fish ...when dish came ..we went ...What the heck?? few pcs of ladies fingers only (okras for those who do not know) floating in the barely there assam gravy. To top it all off...the fish that we ordered was cold! yes! COLD! imagine 2 pcs of tenggiri fish that is cold to the taste ..think they jus threw it in..boiled for a while n serve..wow!! good quality n customer service i say ..NOT! Complained..took the dish back n returned with another cold fish..sigh! The other dishes were so so only nothing to shout about....think there are other better places for Nonya food n i believe that would be my last visit to Makko... sorry guys!Show less

Author: YukieLilyKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Overrated
Review: One word sums it all, overrated.I've tried their signature fried chicken but the marination is not to my liking.Their Assam fish tasted ordinary.The water convolvulus with belacan is delicious but you can't satisfy a food connouseouir with a single dish.Please let me know if there is some other dish that I should try.Show less

Author: KLOysterManMalaysia
Title: Good Nyonya cuisine, a little less touristy
Review: About a 20 minute walk from Jonker street, well worth it. Some great dishes, especially the beef and chicken rendang. Not over powering nor over priced, a small restaurant with a quick turnover, more geared towards locals it appears. Unfortunately the restaurant is not in an old style Nyonya house, so a bit lacking in atmosphere - best to go with a bigger group of 6-8 to try lots of dishes.Show less

Author: PER468Perth, Australia
Title: Best Nyonya cuisine in lifetime
Review: I have tried many Nyonya restaurants in my lifetime, and this is the best so farYou have to know the cuisine as Nyonya is not for everybody since it is exotic and tasty with full of Nyonya culture in taste - no word could best describeShow less

Author: LTC_SGDSingapore, Singapore
Title: Not that fantastic.
Review: I was there last week with my wife n friend. We order assam fish, kiam chye soup, nonya chap chye and ngngih hiang. Fish too sweet and over fried. The ninya chap chye lack the 'omp' factor. Possibly the lack of pork and black bean sauce. Soup don't tsste enough of kiam chye. Too much of msg in the ngoh hiabg and not enough of fredh water chestnut. Win't go back for second time. RM 100 for the meal with drinks. Don't have the babi poteh or ayam buah klack. So how can it be authentic nonya food!.Show less

Author: Paul YSingapore, Singapore
Title: Authentic Nyonya Fare that defines the Malacca version from its Penang cousin
Review: Trust the Trip Advisor reviewers on this gem! We were happy we chose this place among the many Nyonya restaurants for our dinner on the last night of our trip. It was the best meal we had the entire 3D2N trip. You MUST NOT miss the ladies fingers with sambal (the sambal is awesome!), the nyonya chendol (you'll end up with 2 helpings like me), ponteh chicken and fried egg with cencalok. The restaurant is unpretentious, service is fast, food is great, price is reasonable and there's ample parking behind the restaurant.Show less

Author: BoeyTO
Title: Good selection and offerings, but tastes a bit watered down
Review: Ordered a good spread of dishes. Service was fast. Dishes taste watered down as compared to a while back. Guess the price of commercialism. Cendol is excellent and a must try.

Author: skYap
Title: Mixed rice
Review: Outside look special,old style!  Inside deco also special, many old old stuff,  service is very good , but food terrible,  like eat chinese mixed rice, food serve very fast, feel(own feeling)like ready look time!

Author: Brenda0913Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Fast,fresh n authentic
Review: Got there pass 1.. oredy packed wt hungry customers,but able to get seat in 15 mins... Order the food... And food serve in 20 mins... Munching on crackers while waiting... The food were superb n fresh.... Especially their petai udang n sotong lemak nenas... The cendol was very good too... And i think they cook upon order... Not reheating [--] like one restaurant I went ..Show less

Author: nicodemus88Penang, Malaysia
Title: Good Food & Fast Service
Review: Went there around 6.30 pm, shop was full. But service was fast, waited only 10 minutes for the dishes to arrive. We ordered Ayam Buah Keluak, Pucuk Paku Belacan, Tauhu Satay and Udang Masak Lemak Nanas. Dishes are delicious, especially the Udang Masak Lemak Nanas. Highly recommended...Show less

Author: Andrew KSingapore, Singapore
Title: Home Cooked Peranakan Meals
Review: This Peranakan restaurant is popular, judging from the crowded diners when we visited it during lunch hours. Taste wise, the Nonya cuisine served is average with their typical Peranakan dishes. Meals are served hot straight from the kitchen, but I think most of it are already pre-cooked, such as the Beef Rendang, Ngoh Hiang, Sambal Lady's Fingers, Sambal Sweet Potato Leaves, Sambal Petai and spicy fried chicken. The Assam fish was freshly cooked but did not have that Nonya SEDAP and SHIOK taste. Missing from their menu is the must have Peranakan dish - the Bakwang Kepiting (pork/crabmeat/bamboo shoot) soup. You would expect Malacca which is home and origin of the famous Peranakan cuisine to serve only the best Nonya home cooked meals here...maybe most of them have migrated to Singapore already!Show less

Author: Setay168
Title: Average food..not really fantastic
Review: The food is average, not really fantastic like what other reviewers in their review. The salted veg duck soup - a bit bland. Fried fish with sambal is good!!  The chendol is a bit too sweet...

Author: Michelle TSingapore, Singapore
Title: We went back twice.
Review: This restaurant was recommended by friends and on the day we arrived we popped in for lunch but the kitchen had just closed so we made a reservation for dinner. The dinner did not disappoint. The food was good and the price reasonable. On our last day we had an hour or so to eat and get back to our hotel to wait for our Coach back to Singapore. We did not have a reservation and when we got to restaurant it was full and there were 3 other parties waiting for a table ahead of us. I spoke to the first Waitress I could catch hold off and said I needed to be out of there in an hour. She shook her head but told the Lady Boss at the counter who said wait. She then took my order at the Counter and motioned towards a table finishing up their meal.The table was quickly cleared and food began arriving the minute we sat down. Again everything was excellent and we were done in 50 minutes.We thanked everyone and would definitely recommend this restaurant! Show less

Author: mentisng
Title: Great Taste, not if you are looking for a posh and classy restaurant
Review: second time there, Once you step in. You will see lots of guest waiting at a counter middle of the restaurant. which i think they need to do something about it. So it's best to call and reserve a table.The space wasn't big. So be prepared for a bit of knocking here and there when you move around.The staff there wasn't very proactive. But of course not all of them are like that. so be forgiving.Food was great, sambal sotong is my fav. A must try for chilli lovers. But you have to tell the staff to make it extra spicy. They also sell some home made sauce like "chin chak Lor" and sambal chilli. Listen to me, buy it. you will love it.Show less

Author: JoaquinChannaSantiago, Region Metropolitana, Chile
Title: very homecooked style nyonya food, but not fantastic
Review: nyonya food served in this restaurant is quite good but doesn't blow your mind away.they have authentic nyonya food and a few of those dishes were very well prepared as they require more efforts to prepare.but this is as close to probably homecooked nyonya food rather than prepared really well in restaurant typed food.highlight would be the cendol (local cold dessert), and the ponteh chicken which is prepared well and full of flavours.Show less

Author: Woon29Singapore, Singapore
Title: Not as great as what everyone says.
Review: The food is just average but we love the kangkong best. The food were served very fast. Hence I do agree that the dishes were all precooked. However I am glad that it is extremely cheap to eat here. Most of the staff are very rude. I also spotted them sweeping all the rubbish from the table to the floor while they clear the table for the next person. Hope that they can improve their service and ambience. Show less

Author: Cran B
Title: Good nonya food
Review: Good nonya food is offered here. We ordered steam fish which was quite expensive. However, other dishes were reasonably priced. Service was quick and it is a very popular place judging by .crowd that came during the weekend

Author: kelvint153
Title: Good Nonya food
Review: Must try the ayam rendang and also honey lime juice....shop closed on Tuesday and @ 0830pm daily.better go early and get a seat.

Author: travelbug32_00Singapore, Singapore
Title: My personal favourite...
Review: The restaurant can get very crowded on weekends and expect waiting for a table if you do not have a reservation. If you are looking for ambience, this is not the place for you but if you are looking for good and tasty peranakan food, look no further.My usual selections are the chicken ponteh, assam mackeral, chap chai, beef rendang, fried sea bass with chilli, ngoh hiang and ending the meal with chendol. Prices are reasonable and service is fast. The dishes are served within 10 mins after order. I have tried a few other peranakan restaurants in Melaka and we keep coming back to Makko. These days, we don't bother to try other peranakan restaurants when in Melaka.Show less

Author: beepbeepzSingapore, Singapore
Title: Old Good Flavors
Review: Nyonya Makko is well known for their Peranakan (Chinese mixed with Malay) cuisine. We came in around 8.30 and waited for 10 minutes for our table. We ordered a must-have if you are in a Peranakan restaurant: Ayam Buah Keluak (chicken cooked with Keluak fermented seeds), Udang Lemak Nanas (prawns and pineapples cooked in a mild curry), Nyonya Chap Chye (glass noodle and cabbage cooked in soya sauce), Sambal Sotong (squids stirred with chili paste) and Tahu Makko (steamed bean curd topped with dried prawns). The winner dish for me was the Udang Lemak Nanas. It was so delicious, tangy, sweet and slightly spicy but right in any levels. The prawns were fresh and the pineapples were not overcooked. Overall the dishes were delicious, nice ambience and the prices were affordable. Hingly recommended if you are visiting Malacca.Show less

Author: CristalglaceSingapore, Singapore
Title: Best chendol and lady finger
Review: The chendol here is superb, love the awesome fragrant taste of the authentic gula melaka (palm sugar) used. I reckon this is the best chendol in Melaka that I have tried so far. The lady finger with belachan chili is really good too. We even bought the gula melaka and belachan chili back to Singapore. Read my full review here: http://cristalglace.blogspot.sg/2013/04/melaka-trip-day-2-and-3.htmlShow less

Author: Rian S
Title: food really tastes good
Review:
try beef rendang, it is the best we had so far. the mixed veggie soup is good too.
you can order a small serving of everything if you are sharing with friends.

Author: CarinAshKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Let down
Review: Whenever we visit Melaka, we will definitely have at least a meal at Makko. My kids loved Makko's ponteh chicken, daun keledek and cendol. Fortunately these still tasted great. However, tauhu was just average and the chilli fish (see photo) looks much better than it tasted. Fish was not as fresh and chilli was bland. Not only the fish was the big let down, the price too - it was 50% of our total bill.Show less

Author: Andy LSingapore, Singapore
Title: will visit again
Review: All popular Peranakan restaurants in Melaka need reservation, otherwise be prepared to wait.Although Makko might not be the best Peranakan restaurant, but the food served is tasty and satisfying. Our kids always clean their plates!We recommend :- Chap Chye (vegetable)- Asam Prawn (not spicy for very fragrant)- Potato curry chicken- Ngong Hiang (meat roll)- the sambal fish are also popular but we have to skip (kids)We always end our meal with cendol dessert.Show less

Author: 447daphnetSingapore, Singapore
Title: Ok food
Review: if you havent tried peranakan food, you maybe wowed or impressed. But for the finer tastebuds... You will be disappointed. The belachan is blended not pounded. The flesh of the buah keluak is not removed and checked and mixed with mince pork and stuffed back in. As a result, you are eating it as it is... hard. The rempah was not mixed with sufficient ingredients. .. it tastes neither rich nor aromatic... simply riddled w salt in an attempt to make up for the taste. In short, I felt that took much hype for this place and to cope with the amount of ppl patronising this place., lots of short cuts are taken in their prep.Show less

Author: Alex FSingapore
Title: Best Chendol in Malaka
Review: The restaurant is located 2 mins away from our hotel, Hatten Melaka. The speed of food delivery is amazing. 3 of us ordered ayam buah keluak, prawn omelette, fried chicken and garlic fried sweet potato leaves. My son loves the prawn omelette best. Actually, it really tastes very good. For dessert, we initially ordered 2 chendol as we were disappointed with the chendol that we had in jonker street the day before. When my son tasted my chendol, we finished it so quick that we ordered another one. The gula melaka used in the chendol taste good and so is the green chendol.Show less

Author: WakoPattoBangkok, Thailand
Title: Disinterested & Unhelpfull Staff, Tastless food. Sombre Atmosphere
Review: Went for lunch, All the waitresses sitting around talking disinterested in showcasing there restaurant, food, culture, heritage, traditions ect.Food was fast, But flavourless asked for salt and sweet chilli to add flavour, Salt arrived, Still waiting for sweet chilli... The orange juice was fanta..I will not eat here again.Tip, Wander up a little further to porrige house, Food amazing, People friendly and interesting. There menu is not in english how ever speak with the pleastly plump lady she will suggest menu choices in english.. (dinner only til 2am) Try the Mongolian Pepper Chicken!!Show less

Author: bell_e_lingSingapore, Singapore
Title: Good food, good price!
Review: Place was easy to find, we had a late lunch at about 2pm & luckily there was no Q. Waited about 5 mins before a small table was allocated to us. The waitresses were not smily though. Was very surprised at the speed of the food being served to us. We were so hungry & really appreciate the fast service. We had chincalok egg, sambal kangkong, toufu, ayam buah keluak & chendol. Except for the toufu, the rest was really good!! Spent RM$40+. Show less

Author: MuluvisitorSingapore
Title: Great food, fast service
Review: We were looking for a good peranakan place on our recent visit to Malacca, and happened to come by the Makko when a long queue was starting to form outside just before opening time. We figured the queue was adequate testimony to the quality of the food, so decided to chance it and joined the queue. We were not disappointed. The food was good. Different from the standard peranakan fare we have gotten so used to in Singapore. The menu was wide enough that we had a good selection to choose from. The chilli and sambal were an explosion of flavour. The disappointment was the ngo hiang, which was tasteless without any texture to it. The service was speedy and efficient. So speedy that we are convinced that the food was all precooked, and just dished out. I can understand the stews and curries being precooked, but we got the impression was that even dishes like the chinchalok omelette was precooked. The chendol was also a disappointment. The green worms came out frozen and chewy. Plus the coconut cream was obviously from a can. Fail!Prices were somewhat pricey but way cheaper than Singapore prices. The meal for four of us came to RM120Show less

Author: Simon Koh C
Title: Spicy and delicious traditional food
Review: First time was a bit not sure but after try it, it really taste fantastic delicious and sure to recommend to others who like spicy food ie 'Ikan goring chilli garam'",kangkong Belacan" etc . dessert like cendol is also good. Price is reasonable..

Author: josepho53Johor Bahru, Malaysia
Title: Good Nyonya Food
Review: I have been frequenting this restaurant for quite sometime. Highly recommended for good authentic Nyonya food. I would highly recommend that you try their 'Ayam buah keluak' which is chicken in a slightly spicy sauce; 'Ikan goring chilli garam' which is fried fish with chilli paste; 'udang masak Lemak' which is prawns cooked with pineapple and coconut milk. Another typically Melaka dish is the 'otak otak Melaka style' which is typically different from that of the ones available in Johor or other parts of Malaysia.Another should try is the omellate cooked with cincalok or fermented shrimp. This on top of the normal fare of 'ayam ponteh' chicken on a kind of soya based sauce for those who like less spicy food. Don't forget the famous chendol as the dessert.My advice is to ensure that you have a booking if you intend to visit the place during weekends and public holidays.Highly recommended for a Melaka Nyonya food experience.Show less

Author: JollySheep
Title: Delicious Nyonya Food
Review: Halal Nyonya Restaurant. Love the Bong Teh, Ikan Masak Nenas, Ngu Hiang Rolls, Chap Chai and Gula Melaka Chendol. Reasonable price. Be prepare to queue outside the restaurant. Not open on Wednesday.

Author: ZiadRKuwait
Title: A good atmosphere
Review: We were recommended this restaurant by someone we met at the hotel who said it was off the tourist trail and a genuine nyonya restaurant. We got to the restaurant which had a queue of people waiting to get in and the atmosphere was extremely bustling inside. We waited around 20 minutes and got our table and ordered. The food was good but not what I expected (I thought because it had so many locals and Singaporeans, it had to be special). I thought it was good but not excellent. But, someone did say that we had perhaps missed the specialities of the house and ordered the wrong thing. Perhaps I will try again one day. i loved the atmosphere.Show less

Author: Verona889Hougang, Singapore
Title: Great Service Excellent food
Review: The restaurant lives up to its reputation for food and service. We went there just after 6pm on 29 Dec, Saturday and the place was already packed. Yet, the staff was polite to take down our contacts and put us on the waiting list. We were allowed to place order for our food during the wait. Several families and groups left after learning that they had to wait.However, the wait was worthwhile. My family went for a walk and soon, we got our table served with delicious food. Their signature dish, chilli fish was yummy!!Show less

Author: cowabunga2020Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Pricey but good food. Eat the lemak udang!
Review: It has good traditional Nyonya food. It's packed every day so it is best to make reservation in advance. It's not hard to find and it's located on the busy streets of Melaka Raya. The dish I particularly enjoyed was the Udang Lemak which is basically prawn curry with pineapples. It is literally, to die for. Have fun eating. Oh yes, quite pricey. For a group of 4 - 5 look to spend anything between RM 30 - 60 per person (depending on what you order I guess)Show less

Author: PatToanSingapore, Singapore
Title: Cheap & Good!
Review: Visit this restaurant if you want a taste of basic nyonya food. They are not the best but provides good quality and good spread of food at a reasonable price. Dinning crowd is quite noisy so this is a place where you eat and talk and laugh and enjoy!Show less

Author: simplytravelandeatSingapore, Singapore
Title: Best Chendol
Review: Finally i have the opportunity to visit this restaurant after trying many times while i was in melaka. The atmosphere inside is really warm and perenakan with all the items displayed around the dining hall. As for the food, its hits and misses as some were really good while others were average. And i need to highlight that the chendol here was the best i ever had in Melaka. The rendang beef outperformed as well in my opinion. The seafood dishes that we had were fresh and commendable. Apparently this is one of the restaurant that is run by the family.Show less

Author: Guesswhat229Singapore
Title: Nothing Special
Review: I went there for dinner. The waitress is prompt to take order and they serve you with a plate of crackers to start with.We ordered one ponteh, fried fish with chilli and belachan lady's finger, rice and tea. It cost around 58 ringgit. Amongst all, I find the lady's finger most appetizing, maybe due to the belachan but for the other 2 dishes, I don't find anything Nyongya in it. I did not buy the crackers that cost 10 ringgit per pack because I think it taste better when eating with sambal chilli than on it's own.Overall, I rate Makko average because I expect a lot more from Nyonya food.They close on Tuesday.Show less

Author: Humouresque
Title: Good food, busy place
Review: One of the better places for Nyonya food in Melaka, Very popular & busy, but you will enjoy the traditional nyonya dishes. No pork is served. Certainly worth a visit.

Author: cochleartraveller
Title: Nice food.
Review: I liked the ponteh chicken, curry fish and fired fish with sambal. For veggie, the brinjal, lady fingers and taugeh is what I will go for.

Author: wearethekidssingapore
Title: Great food!!
Review: Totally loved the food served. Also the layout was special, and I find this restaurant very cosy despite the noise from other diners. It is inexpensive and the staff are courteous and polite. try the nonya curry and the otah, which i feel are its 2 best dishes. also try the chendol. u will not regret it.Show less

Author: Gerald KSingapore
Title: Great food! A must try!
Review: Makko is one of my favourite restaurants. We discovered by chance while looking for a nyonya restaurant to eat in. It looked quiet on the outside, and when we pushed open the door, there was a crowd inside and we new we hit jackpot!We tried quite a number of their dishes and they were all good - chicken ponteh, prawns with pineapples, sayur lodeh, chap chye, etc. Lime juice goes well with the nyonya food. They would serve a cracker as you wait for the food and the crackers are really good. You can eat them on its own, or dip it in a little chili. They have these crackers all ready packed for you to buy, and it is a popular take away.They are closed on Tuesdays, so do take note of it. However, when we went on 10 Sep 2012 (Monday), I was surprised to find that they were closed, without any note on their door or why they were closed. My wife and I were disappointed that we could not eat at Makko in September. We did go to another nearby nyonya restaurant, but the food was not as good as Makko.Show less

Author: RenaC82Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Homey, unpretentious Peranakan fare
Review: Growing up with my Nyonya grandmother, I was spoiled with delicious Peranakan food. These days, restaurants and shops claiming to serve "authentic" Peranakan cuisine are a dime a dozen. I was sceptical when my friends introduced me to Nyonya Makko. But the minute I tasted their 'Ikan Goreng Cili', I was sold. Fried to a crispy perfection with an addictive savory chilli paste, I couldn't stop eating it. The "Rendang Chicken" was good but could've used a tad more flavor. But I was sold again when I had the "Lemak Nanas Udang" (prawns in a pineapple and coconut curry broth). We had "Telur Dadar Cincalok" (cincalok omelette) which was a little on the salty side. I really enjoyed the "Tauhu Satay Sauce" (literally that, tofu smothered in a rich, satisfying spicy peanut gravy). Was told by the affable "lady boss" that the modest but charming restaurant was an impressive 27 years old, and the first batch of staff was still mostly intact! Now where else can you find that in this day and age? Service is quick but very basic, so do not expect to be impressed. You get your order taken, your food served and your requests attended to but no extra smiles. Also, do try their famed Cendol Kacang Merah. Decadent and a real treat in the hot Malacca weather. I personally prefer mine without the red beans. All in all, simple/fuss free but highly satisfying Peranakan dishes. If you'd like to make away with snacks or cookies, note that there's a shelf filled to the brim with assorted cookies, sauces and treats for you to take home. Just enquire with the lady boss, who's seated at the counter right next to the shelf. It's notorious for its crowds during peak seasons and weekends, so if you're planning to drop by then, a reservation via phone call would be wise.Show less

Author: biofreshKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Still Authentic fof Years
Review: Well so far I had no question on this restaurant except the price and portion served are not related. Portion are small but price are big!!Taste never change after years but price change so as portion.IF you really want to have the Nyonya feeling do visit this as their setting are still authentically nyonya deco!!Show less

Author: Ethan S
Title: Still as good after so many years
Review: I always remember my parents bringing me to eat Nonya food, so many years on, the taste remain the same and a great place to try Nonya food.

Author: Fabian2625
Title: The Food is great and nice:)
Review: Order a lot of nyonya food, it was nice and delicious, but you have to call before you go, becos there are always full of people..!

Author: JoanLee88
Title: Nice Nyonya Food
Review: If planning to have dinner~~Must visit here~~They provide variety of Nyonya food~~Remember to order their cendol~~it is nice~~besides, they closed on tuesday~~~

Author: amytay46
Title: Poor dishes. Not what we expect of nyonya dishes and the staff are not friendly in servicing.
Review: Nyonya food could be better but since we got recommendations, we decided to try it out but the food was not to our expectation.

Author: Dylan1980
Title: mmmm.......
Review: the food standard didn't reached our expectations, very poor. very lame, kinda disappointed

Author: Nying-jeSingapore
Title: Yummy and Non-pretentious
Review: We had many Paranakan Restaurant to choose from. Not knowing which one is good, we happen to overheard someone mention about Makko so we went in for dinner.We had the traditional Chicken Buakulak, Lemak nanas Prawn, Chap Chai and Omellette. Every dish can be eaten on its own with a bowl of plain rice. Every dish is a star on its won.The food was traditional and simple, no gimmick. Excellent recommendation and service from the waitress who had our interest at heart, they did not oversell.Reasonably price $30 for two.Very satisfying meal. Will return.Show less

Author: SingaporeCatlover88
Title: Good nyonya food very hard to resist...
Review: I remembered first time I patronised this famous nyonya restaurant was in the late 70s. Til today the food (menu) they served never disappointed me. Yummy and made me come back for more and more.

Author: kai_lin001Penang Island, Malaysia
Title: give it a try!
Review: When my friends n i went there, v ordered ayam pongteh, udang lemak nanas> both of them were excellent! v ordered telur cincaluk,sambal kangkung,asam pedas fish > they were average only.v tried other nyonya restaurants around there as well, but found that Makko was the nicest.The price was abit costly for us. It was around rm25 per person.And u might need to do a reservation before u go there as sometimes the restaurant is really flocked by people.Show less

Author: paul360Quezon City, Philippines
Title: A Restaurant from Years Back... And It Shows
Review: Food was okay!It was satisfying enough for 5 hungry tummies :)I enjoyed the crispy fish the mostI like Nyonya flavours and it's not hard to please me with what they had offeredOne thing I could say thoughThe place is quite dated and it showsThough it's not entirely a bad thingI've been told that this place is flocked by people tooSo I guess were quite lucky to immediate be seated once we entered the restaurantFor a restaurant that has a long historyI'm quite optimistic that they can do so much better :)Perhaps bring back the glorious days? I'm willing to give it a second chanceShow less

Author: cttclaire
Title: Commercialize Nyonya food
Review: Commercialize Nyonya food. Nothing special, food tastes normal & costly.

Author: yangxy
Title: Average
Review: I'm not a big nyonya fan. The place is quite full. Food is ok, rice is a bit undercooked.

Author: Jhawk2820Singapore, Singapore
Title: Avoid, better eat somewhere else
Review: Expect a good meal in this restaurant since the reviews is not bad, however was very disappointed with the food quality and taste. ProSambal kankongChendolConService is lousy, and the waitress is very rudeOrder a prawn, but not freshPriceyNoisyOverall, food are not nice.Show less

Author: Kay6388Malaysia
Title: The worst nyonya food that I have taste
Review: Went there after seeing some highly recommended food reviews n proclaim by some saying that It offers one of the best nyonya food. Extremely dissapointed with their food. Ordered 8 dishes namely devil's chicken curry, cencalok egg, rendang beef, chicken pong teh, deep fried fish tengirri with chilli, belacan kangkung, mixed veggies n asam pedas prawn. All d food tat we ordered was tasteless, precooked n reheated with microwave when arrive. The chicken pong teh tastes sweet and were cold. While d devil's curry taste sour which i think they afd 2 much of vinegar. We couldn't even taste d cencalok even though it was called cencalok egg. Mixed vege was boiled n taste bland. Fish was boiled n covered with some chilli paste n all we could taste was d paste.The only dishes tat was edible was d belacan kangkung. Total price is Rm 150 for 7 pax which i feel was expensive given d food tat we consumed. This is d worse nyonya food that I have taste n they even proclaim to have 27 years of experience cooking nyonya food.Show less

Author: nusabahorSingapore, Singapore
Title: If you want good food, go elsewhere
Review: Dozens of time visiting Melaka but have yet to try their famous Nonya food. Do some research from the internet, and coincidently my GPS bring me to this "famous" Nonya restaurant in Melaka. The ambiance is not too bad, but the food quality is bad. I've had much better food than this. Food were serve in a swift manner, but all the food were very hot , I suspect all are pre cooked and microwaved and served it to customers .  Nothing to shout for and the price is expensive. I will not recommend this restaurant if you were to try genuine Nonya food.Show less

Author: mel7155Singapore, Singapore
Title: I have eaten better Nyonya food in Melaka and outside melaka
Review: Food was bland- ayam ponteh sauce was tasteless and chicken was tough. Itik soup was in name only- didn't feel like duck soup, udang Nenas was just as bland, sweet sour chicken was horrible- other food such as chendol and otak was okay- however will not return. Staff was surly- kept changing our place once we settled down because they said that we were blocking them and wanted to plonk us at the corner where they plonked the dirty dishes. That corner was dirty.Show less

Author: ganadelineSingapore, Singapore
Title: Good nonya food but not so good in price
Review: We have visited this restaurant 3 times so far. The food is pretty good but only selectively. We never fail to order dishes like the ngoh hiang, ayam ponteh, crackers, Assam fish and the chendol, of course. The omelette was rather salty and the prawn in coconut milk and pineapple was too overpowering. The bak wan soup and bua keluak dish is okay. The restaurant is always packed durin mealtimes so you have to be there early or be prepared to wait for half hour as seating caacity is quite limited. Service is okay and the staff know their menu well so they can offer good advice. We find the price of their fare rather on the high side. Overall a good nonya dining experience. Show less

Author: Just_my_viewsKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Not worthwhile
Review: This restaurant probably became known after some review by some artistes from Singapoare's MediaCorp, and thereafter is frequented by tourists. During the peak times, ie weekends and/or public holidays, the place is crowded. Success thus beget arrogance and when I visited it, I found the service to be excruciatingly poor. Unfortunately, we had already driven round twice to find parking space near the restaurant, and it would be difficult to get the party of over 10, which included a few old folks, to drive around again to another restaurant. Thus, we stayed on, and, much to our chagrin, were served food which was not at all up to expectation.Show less

Author: ccpy27kuala lumpur
Title: the food in not my favourite
Review: I had my lunch at this restaurant. This restaurant was full of people. The table I took was the last table available in the restaurant.We wait a while only the waitress serve us with a type of cracker and menu. The cracker is very nice but not a special cracker. Then I ordered cendol (a famous dish in this restaurant). The cendol is really nice and will sure miss it.I ordered 3 dishes and 1 soup. I ordered Pong teh chicken, sambal tauhu, belacan paku vege and itik tim. Now the torture start! The itik tim soup was so salty until i unable to finish even half of it. The pong teh chicken also not taste very nice. the sambal tauhu only have spicy and tauhu taste. The only dish preferred is belacan paku. But i have tastes a better paku belacan else where.Show less

Author: hste-leeKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Might return!
Review: The last time we came to this nyonya restaurant was about 10 years back, so during this short visit to Melaka we decided to drop by and reminisce our good old days. Crowd was only a handful when we reached for dinner at 630pm. The interior of the place is almost the same as 10 years back. Not much changes or maybe none at all as far as i can remember. We were pretty hungry and after going thru the menu we decided to place our order.We ordered the following:- 1) Chap Chye Soup @ RM 7.00 (taste like gravy for dish/terrible) 0/102) Prawn Omelette @ RM 9.00 (tasty but too oily) 6/103) Beef Rendang @ RM 12.00 (tasty but lack of presentation) 7/104) Kangkong Belacan @ RM 6.00 (tasty) 9/105) Ngoh Hiang @ RM 11.00 (tasty) 9/106) 3 large rice @ RM 3.00 and 1 small rice @ RM 0.60 8/107) Sambal Belacan with lime (a must try) @ RM 1.00 10/10Overall, i will give this restaurant a rating of 6/10 but the soup is the real spoiler!! Should have ordered the Itik Tim instead. Told the lady boss about the soup and all she did was glooking at me blank!! Hahah! Price is reasonable and might consider coming back again.Located at - No. 123, Taman Melaka Raya, Off Jalan Parameswara (Bandar Hilir), Melaka.Tel. 06-2840737 Operating hours - 1130 - 1445 1800 - 2130Closed on TuesdaysShow less

Author: SusanneWongMalaysia
Title: Wonderful food.
Review: Among the many Peranakan restaurants I've been to, this remains one of my favourites. Friendly lady boss, lovely food and decent atmosphere. Considering the reasonable prices, I have no complaints regarding the ambiance. Absolute must-tries: Ikan Goreng Cili Garam, Pong Teh, Rendang Chicken, Telor Cincalok, Tauhu Satay and of course, their famous Cendol Kacang. I'm not a fan of red beans, but I must say that the ones found in their Cendol are delectable. I've been there no less than 5 times because I always make sure to pay them a visit whenever I'm down in Malacca.Show less

Author: Adrian042Kuala Lumpur
Title: Delicious! Delicious! Delicious!
Review: I enjoy a good Peranakan meal, and have eaten at several "Nyonya" restaurants both in Kuala Lumpur and Malacca. I must say that Makko has to be the best.The "Ayam Buah Keluak" (Chicken cooked with the "keluak" fruit in a slightly spicy sauce; the chicken "Pongteh"; Fish cooked in an "Asam" sauce; Prawns cooked with Pineapple in a "lemak" sauce, the Beef rendang, and all topped off with what has been voted the 2nd best Chendol (a local shaved iced dessert) in Malaysia were awesome. For those who have not tried Nyonya or Peranakan cuisine, it is a very interesting mix of Chinese and Malay herbs and spices in the dishes, which you would not get in typical Chinese or Malay food, and would be hard pressed to find anywhere else in the world apart from perhaps the Straits settlements of Malacca, Penang and Singapore, and Kuala Lumpur of course. Go ahead and give it a try. And by the way, who eats Tom Yam in a Nyonya Restaurant anyway?Show less

Author: LL721Kuala Lumpur
Title: Absolutely the worst Tom Yam Fish soup!!
Review: This place serves the absolute worst Tom Yam Fish Soup. The soup is tasteless.... only tasted spicy, spicy and spicy, thanks to the huge amount of bird eye chillis in the soup!!! We left the soup behind and tried to eat the spicy pieces of fish only.Tried the Ngor Heong. Thought the serving was rather small, and not as tasty as the ones in Penang.Will give this place a miss next time. Only left me with a hot stomach and dissatisfied feeling.Show less

Author: g0_f0r_itSingapore, Singapore
Title: Not worth it at all
Review: Totally disagree with the other 2 reviews. We are not fussy about food but the dishes tasted like any other Chinese dishes cooked by an amateur. We had nyonya chap chai (no different from Chinese chap chai), beef rendang (worse than those cooked by the average hawker or caterer), deep fried fish with chilli (that was not at all cripsy), ayam / chicken ponteh (tasted like most ordinary stir fried chicken with sauce), Ngoh Hiang (like any other you can find in hawker centres/ food courts), Cincaloh eggs (we failed to taste the Cincaloh). Even my kids, who loves eggs, did not finish up the eggs like they usually do. The meal with drinks costs us 137RM. There was no atmosphere or decor in the restaurant to make up for the very ordinary food.We would not recommend it, but if you have to go, the restaurant is along Jalan Merdeka, on the opposite side of Ole Sayang and Fenix Inn. It is within walking distance from the east entrance of Dataran Pahlawan Melaka Megamall. It is opened at 11.30-2.45 for lunch, and 6-9.30 for dinner. It is closed on Tuesdays while Ole Sayang is closed on Wednesdays.Show less

Author: petai
Title: Worth the trip to dine out here
Review: The good food and atmosphere will make you feel your dining a true nyonya food in a local environment,try the fried fish covered in cut-red hot chillies

Author: BenYorkieKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Yuk
Review: We went here in 2017 on a previous visit to Melaka - and thought this place was excellent.We went back this past week and were dreadfully disappointed. Except for a very good prawn omelette, the rest of our food,especially the pork dish, was at best mediocre - if that.Plus the interior is scruffy and towards the back it is very untidy around the cash desk and towards the kitchen Thank you - but definitely a 'no thank you'.Show less

Author: senfaaaMalaysia
Title: Nyonya food
Review: We found it just nearby the jonker street, and luckily we didn't drive a car since there is very limited space to park a car. The food here are not bad and it is air-conditioned (it is very important because the outdoor was super hot that day)!Show less

Author: Alacran24
Title: Our kitchen Nyonya cuisine in Melaka Malaysia
Review: Humble setting with outstanding food.  Must have the pork ribs with black nut sauce as well as whole fish Snapper Assan.  Friendly attentive service.  Inexpensive.

Author: VivekananthaC
Title: Great value for Lunch
Review: It was a great place for a quick lunch break. We wanted to try something new called the “pork rib keluak”, simply superb nyonya style dish. Will recommend. Definitely will come back to this place again.

Author: annisa-mazlan
Title: Great nyonya dishes!
Review: Great nyonya dishes! Homey ambience with a lovely auntie took our orders. Located in a lively alley, parking was a challenge but you can easily walk to the restaurant as the alley is fully shaded.

Author: Amelia J L
Title: Delicious Nyonya food in a homely restaurant
Review: We had pork ponteh, cincaluk omelette and Kangkung belacan and they were delicious. The staff were friendly and the place has a very homely feeling to it.

Author: Kruiza
Title: Enjoyed some traditional nyonya
Review:
Enjoyed some traditional nyonya food and while interesting was not a great example of the local cuisine. The pork ponteh was more like and English hot pot complete with potatoes. 
Just off jonkers though makes it a great place to escape the tourist parade.

Author: JooleelauKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Quiet n gentle service nyonya lunch
Review: My parents and me really enjoyed our nyonya lunch at this restaurant. We just decided to try after seeing the good reviews.We wont disappointed with the taste of the nyonya dishes and their gentle service.Chendol dessert was really good too.Will definately bring my family members to try when we are in Malacca the next time.Show less

Author: yuva906
Title: Reasonable Price
Review: Had lunch here yesterday(6/10/2019).Very crowded.We ordered 1)Pineapple Prawn Gravy-so delicious,2)Kangkung belacan,3)egg omellete and 4)Asam Squid Fried-seriously I won't recommend this dish.The taste of the squid was too bad.I did not enjoy it.Price is reasonable.Otherwise great food to try.

Author: twnteoLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Amazing food
Review: Had dinner, following reviews, 5 of us, we ordered ngoh heang, pork with buah keluah, sambal aubergine, prawns with pineapple sambal and 2 rice.The pork was really good, amazing flavour with the buah keluah, my experience. We all agreed the dishes were very tasty and flavoursome. For me, the ngoh heang was only so so, could be the strong flavour of the rest made this dish quite plain.A place I will return on my next visit to Malacca.Show less

Author: diver260567Singapore, Singapore
Title: Nonya Food Delights
Review: Went to this place after reading about on TripAdvisor. It was packed but we waited. Once in we ordered a few of the typical Nonya Dishes like, 1. Asam Fish2.Sambal Prawn with Petai ( Must Try!)3. Ayam Buah Kuluak ( Must try!)4.Kang Kong BelacanThe food was delicious. Very tasty. A bit spicy...so for those that can't take spicy food, just tell the waitress that you want it cooked less spicy. They will accommodate.The atmosphere in the restaurant is very Peranakan setup and simple. It's not a 5-star restaurant but it's good enough. Overall it a must-eat place to go to. Take note last order is at 915pm. So the best time will be from 730pm to 830pm.Show less

Author: ThengleSingapore, Singapore
Title: Nice little place. Lucky we found it!
Review: Happened upon the place by accident on a Friday night and were lucky enough to get in. The food was great and the atmosphere was fun. Service was typical for a crowded place on a Friday night - they were swamped. Everything we had was quite good especially the Nonya lemak nanas. Really glad we happened in. Show less

Author: uptheladder
Title: Disappointing
Review: We were so looking forward to a genuine Nyonya experience after reading the reviews. The food was average. The service was unfriendly. You have to get your serviettes from a wall dispenser. You get what you pay for.

Author: kamalesaruKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Nyonya Cravings!
Review: What do you eat when you are in Melaka except their best cuisine! So off we went in search of Nyonya food for dinner. Melaka has many restaurants offering Nyonya food but not many have vegetarian options. So it was a lovely surprise to call & find Hazel who said they do have some options & reserved a table for us. This place is just off Jonker St, we walked into a homey place with no bells & whistles. Hazel was very friendly and helpful in explaining the menu and taking our very specific orders. This place is great as they do have different serving sizes, as my husband is a non-vegetarian he often does not order a single dish if it is too big for him alone. So this was perfect! We ordered a pork dish, some vegetables, veg fish asam style, omelette & some drinks. The ice lemon tea & barley lemon tasted home made & perfect. The pork dish, my husband said reminded him of what my mother-in-law used to cook & was delicious, the asam curry was authentic & flavourful. All in all a great meal, we had way more than we should have eaten and then walked it off along Jonker St. One little improvement, tissue/napkins should be placed on the tables and not on the wall dispensers.Show less

Author: Destiny75013
Title: Nice food for Nyonya in a quiet street
Review:
Nice food for Nyonya in a quiet street
In the middle of so many touristics
restaurants
We choice the good one

Author: JoanneHui
Title: Delicious Nyonya
Review: First time tried nyonya cuisine at Our Kitchen.The restaurant located within Jonker Street.Highly recommended.

Author: alpinea2013
Title: A hidden little gem
Review: A great reasonably priced place to eat with great food and friendly staff. Not touristy but just off the most touristy street in Melaka. The Ayam chicken and pork are excellent.

Author: SereneMa
Title: Food not bad
Review: Food was not bad, environment its special, aunty serving us was nice, grandmotherly feel :D order cendol (nice, usually i not very fancy with cendol, but this really nice), babi pongteh (recommend), kangkung belacan & asam sotong.

Author: trvkaki
Title: Best meal in Melaka trip
Review:
This surprise little restaurant tucked at a quiet corner off Jonker street is a gem. Located just behind the Geographer pub in the middle of Jonker walk.

Rendang chicken is recommended.

Author: malabarflyGravesend, United Kingdom
Title: Good foor, good value, good choice.
Review: Not far from the centrally situated Geographers Café on Jonker Street, just up the Jalan Hang Lekira road alongside. There are a number of eatling choices in this short road, so we took a chance on this one. I'm glad we did.There is no outside seating, and the interior is fairly plain, but the service is friendly and the food (Nyonya food) is very cheap compared with more touristy restaurants. For example, we had prawn sambal, ginger chicken, a green vegetable dish and rice, plus a bottle of tiger beer and a soft drink for about 62 MYR (about £12), which can’t be bad. The portions were generous as well.When we were there it was relatively empty (only about four tables taken) but all those who were there were locals (or possibly from Singapore) which has to be a good sign. We would certainly go again if we found ourselves back in Melaka.Show less

Author: MarMar584
Title: Very good food, staff could smile a little more often
Review: We went here twice and enjoyed the food a lot. Very good prices, very good quality and taste. We actually had our best local food from this restaurant. Staff is knowledgeable but for some reason not overly inviting. Compared to the more touristy options like the geographer cafe next door, you get more authentic food for less money here. Don’t be scared by the rather barren environment - it’s worth it.Show less

Author: Jordan LSingapore, Singapore
Title: really cheap and good nyonya food!
Review: We chanced upon this nyonya peranakan plade, which was really good! The food was awesome, with ngo hiang, ayam buah keluah, tofu, omelette was all super flavorful and we loved it. On top of that, its even really cheap. We saw tons of locals there, hence also realised that it was a good sign ...would strongly recommend it.Show less

Author: Michael LSingapore, Singapore
Title: Home cooked style authentic nonya food
Review: Our Kitchen Nyonya Restaurant is located along a small side street off Jalan Hang Jebat ( the main street in Jonker Walk). As you walk along Jalan Hang Jebat towards the less busy end of Jonker Walk, turn left into the side street when you see Geographer Cafe, a popular restaurant and drinking place. Walk for around 50 meters and you will see the restaurant on the right. It's a humble looking restaurant but you will not be disappointed with the food. Our Kitchen serves home cooked style authentic nyonya food at very reasonable prices. You will see many locals there, which is always a good sign.
