Review: I love this eating place. The food is yummy and the service excellent. The price is reasonable too. It makes the waiting worth it

Author: ButtermilkHoHoJohor Bahru, Malaysia
Title: Halal chicken rice ball
Review: Must go place when i visit melaka. The only halal chicken rice ball at the moment i think. Must order item is Nasi Ayam, chicken rice ball, steam chicken, soup. Their asam pedas for me is normal. Not so special. Because i have taste a better chinese style asam pedas at jb. Service is good fast. Restaurant is clean. Location really easy to find. Many parking. Just go for it and u will be love the taste of chicken rice ball. Soft & tastyShow less

Author: Charmaine W
Title: Nothing Special
Review: For me it's nothing special. The place is crowded with tourists and be prepared to queue up for the table during peak time like lunch hour.

Author: studiohausvincent
Title: Nothing special
Review: Its really nothing to shout about with the rice ball and chicken here. Its very commercialize and seems mostly tourist are going.

Author: yunaldocSentosa Island, Singapore
Title: Chicken Rice not as fantastic
Review: I have tried quite a number of chicken rice across Singapore and Malaysia I humbly proclaim . Here is my reviewNormal Chicken rice : 4/5Chicken Rice ball : 2/5Roast Chicken : 3.5/5Soup : no soupSide Vege : 3.5/5Overall Score : 3/5Price : DecentThis restaurant do have other variation of delicacy apart from chicken rice alone which I did not try. My review is based on chicken rice alone.  The 2 downside is that the rice ball is served slightly warm and does not have the fragrant of hot rice when served and without soup makes chicken rice incomplete in my opinion. Therefore the rating 3 is given. Show less

Author: Amira2609
Title: So good
Review: I've always wanted to try the chicken rice ball and found this halal chicken rice. Went back for more the next day.

Author: Jason C
Title: Must Try and won't regret
Review: me and my friend in two, order half chicken and 15 rice balls, with an egg omelette. The rice balls were really the best taste in the town, better than the long q chicken rice near jonker street. The chicken was really smooth, very delicious! The price was reasonable also, it only cost us only RM39.5 with drinks. You must give it a try! Show less

Author: cokataci
Title: Best halal chicken rice ball
Review:
Love the chicken rice ball and the chicken. 
Many customer sometimes need to queue during peak hours and will run out of food early as it is very popular place.

Every time visit melaka we must visit the place.highly recommend.

Author: JulianF584
Title: Chicken  rice balls?
Review:
The chicken itself is very average. The rice itself is rolled into ball.shaped bit it's just ordinary rice and not the authentic chicken rice.

I am sure there are others which tastes better and is more authentic.

Keep looking and avoid this one if possible

Author: shaneeee88
Title: Tasty food
Review: The food over here is tasty and the price is pretty reasonable too. I would recommend trying the sambal udang. The restaurant is situated in melaka center.

Author: ManngaDuaSingapore, Singapore
Title: Good quality
Review: We had late lunch there. The place was pretty crowded with locals.We tried their famous chicken rice. Chicken was tender and tasty with its sauce. The rice ball was tiny, but full of taste. The vegitable was well cooked with simple garlic taste. The price is really reasonable.Will come back.Show less

Author: mayzatulakmarm
Title: Average taste
Review: I thinkthe only Halal chicken rice ball in melaka.town that i hve seen...Taste of the rice ball just ok.for.me.i ordered the roasted.chicken.the chicken is tender.and good but the only.thing is there is still.a blood in the bone ..i do understand that some.chicken rice.shop their.chicken the bone part still can see.the red.of the blood..but this one to.redish for.me..its turn off.my appetite..according to.my friends their chicken rice ball are good from.her last time visit..the.service are good..very attentive waited staff..will be back.again to.try again..Show less

Author: tony12cuKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Great Food at Reasonable Prices
Review: The dishes were great especially the Nyonya Cincalok Omelette and the stir fry Yau Mak (Green Vegie). Although we didn't try their signature Salt Chili Squid, we are determined to have it on our next visit that is already in the planning.The restaurant is FULL HALAL with certificate to proof, and customers are tended mostly by Muslim waiting staff.Show less

Author: Littledingding
Title: Excellent ! You will not regret !
Review: One of the best food in Melaka . Chicken are tender and juicy! Rice balls are soft and fragrant. Price is reasonable and the staff are friendly! Despite the hot weather, it was cooling inside the restaurant as there are many ceiling fans. Very satisfying meal Will definitely go back again Show less

Author: J L
Title: Top place to eat in Melaka!
Review: We went here to try their famous chicken rice balls and it was one of the best meals I had in Malaysia. The friendly staff explained the menu and made some recommendations for us. The food is very reasonably priced and so delicious that we ordered a second serving! Definitely a must-try experience when in Melaka.Show less

Author: LynD827Petaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Halal and Chicken Rice Balls are tiny
Review: We came here because the food is halal. Ordered 2 portions of roast chicken, 10 balls of chicken rice, 1 plate of veg and a bowl of seaweed soup. No complaints except rice balls are a bit tiny (30 sen each). It would also be good if rice came with soup. Would go back again if we had the chance.Show less

Author: Eraz7
Title: Bad Chicken Rice
Review:
Nothing like S'pore's version.

Don't try the roasted chicken - the steamed is much better.

The rice is pathetic and chilli only made the rice better.

Author: LiyanaZAKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Halal chicken rice balls.
Review: It is not easy looking for a halal chicken rice ball restaurant in Melaka. After doing my research online, this is the one that popped up most frequently. We ordered half a chicken, fried vegetables and 20 chicken rice balls with drinks for two people. Total bill came up to around RM36, which is quite pricey in my opinion. Even in KL, its not difficult to find chicken rice for less than RM10 per plate. I guess you are paying for the novelty of eating rice rolled into balls. That and the fact that this is the one of the few halal eateries serving this Melaka specialty.The chicken was moist, the rice a bit on the too mushy side, and the vegetables were delicious. Service was relatively fast, we were served after 15 minutes although the restaurant was full (we went at 4 p.m.). We did enjoy our meal and appreciated the fast service, but the high price may make me think twice about visiting this place.Show less

Author: vinceku76
Title: 1st visit but will come back again!!
Review: the restaurant just nearby Fenix Inn hotel that I stay. First try their chicken rice ball is very delicious! staff service kindly, no need long Q at jonker street also can eat here!! Ee Ji Ban!

Author: NOR AISAH AKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: One of the options for "halal" food
Review: This was my 3rd visit and I had become better in choosing the food. We took: mixed steam and roast quarter chicken (RM12), a good portion for 2 people; small kai lan belacan (RM6), too chary and bitter taste; 2 plates of chicken rice (RM3) and 10 chicken rice ball (RM3), the 2 types of rice became too much for 2.Unfortunetely they don't serve soup with their chicken rice. you have to pay RM9 to get a bowl of fish ball soup.Show less

Author: zsitiSingapore, Singapore
Title: To get Halal Chicken Rice Ball in Malacca!!!
Review: The food was awesome and It is a must go for every trip of mine. It is one of the nicest halal chicken rice ball which I was able to find in Malacca. At the same time, their assam fish and steamed chicken is so tender and juicy.Although I must say that it is a little bit pricey as the portion seems little but at the end of the meal, it provides a satisfying feeling!We stayed at hotels nearby this area so it is really convenient for us to pop by during lunch or even during dinner time.Show less

Author: brownbag68Geelong
Title: Kept us coming back.
Review: We went here for the chicken rice balls and were hooked. I have to admit that I haven't tried the other chicken rice ball places in Melaka but I don't regret it as these were so good and there was no queue to get in. The chef makes all these balls by hand - we read about it on the wall. The chilli is mild and delicious and the chicken is cooked to perfection. I'd recommend the roast chicken - a bit more tasty than steamed.Show less

Author: Growler888
Title: Pricey but food is nice
Review: We went to this restaurant after we failed to eat at our favourite Teo Chew Ba Ku Teh at Melaka Raya 4. Boss is friendly and you can ask for a parking coupon because the parking wardens are very active in patrolling and issuing summons.We ordered half white and half roasted chicken, 30 rice balls, veg, sambal squid, drinks. 6 pax RM88. Compared to Chung Wah, the chicken is less oily and salty, rice ball is smaller and less oily and more grainy texture. Also more expensive than Chung Wah.Show less

Author: Gnoskcoy
Title: Good, tender and flavourful chicken
Review: The chicken is very well cooked and flavourful. Definitely comparable to those found in SingaporeI found the rice ball too soft and wet, as I would personally prefer something drier. The chilli is a must have!Also ordered the sambal squid and prawns, which tasted great, though I find the portion smallShow less

Author: Kevin B
Title: Average chicken rice
Review: We are from SIngapore so perhaps it is just average to us. But nonetheless still a good chicken rice place.

Author: NOR AISAH AKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: okay food
Review: We ordered 1 roasted chicken rice (RM 5.50),1 steamed chicken rice (RM 5.50), 10 rice ball (30 cents each), kailan (RM 6), sambal squid (RM 12).The chicken rice was tasty but the chicken portions were really small. We didn't get the soup accompanying it, didn't ask because we were so hungry at that time. The kailan was very nice but the squid wasn't worth a try because of the burnt sambal taste.Show less

Author: Noob123
Title: Decent meal
Review:
Not as popular as those at Jonker.

Rice and chicken meat were ok, compared to Hainese chicken rice elsewhere. The rice balls are just a gimmick.

Author: Valerie CPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: The rice ball made a difference for Malacca Chicken Rice
Review: Why Chicken Rice is so famous in Malacca? The "Rice Ball", besides that just like the normal chicken rice. Many people queuing under the hot sun at the famous Chicken Rice shop in Jonker Street, waiting for tables just for the chicken rice. As tourist, some time I did that as well when I was in Malacca. This trip we discovered Ee Ji Ban just nearby our hotel and we attracted by their big sign board. We decided to have lunch here before we departed from Malacca, we have a pleasant time here. We didn't need to wait for the table, we can take our time to order our food, the place is comfortable and not hot. The good thing is we don't need to rush, we just have great time with our friends chatting without people stand around you waiting for the table. Some said the chicken not as nice as the Jonker Street one, but I feel it is not bad. Personally I still prefer the chicken with a plate of rice, but it is fun for the children and they really love the rice balls. I will choose to dine here in my future trips instead of queuing in Jonker Street. Another good point for the restaurant is "Halal" and our Muslim friends able to try the famous Chicken Rice in Malacca.Show less

Author: Mohd C
Title: Good but expensive
Review: Ee Ji Ban serves Halal chicken rice and chicken rice balls. The food is good but the price is on the high side. If you are looking for Halal chicken rice ball, this is probably the only place that serves it.

Author: Sophia G
Title: Tried the chicken rice ball and chicken rice
Review: Didn't like the taste of both the rice ball and rice.  I feel that any of our local chicken rice stalls can beat this famous one.

Author: MalRosEaSingapore, Singapore
Title: Halal Chicken Rice Ball
Review: If you would like to try a halal chicken rice ball, you may wish to try Ee Ji Ban. The roasted chicken tastes nice. You have a choice to order either chicken rice balls at RM0.30 per ball or a plate of chicken rice (if you wish to have normal rice). Not to worry about the heat as place is equipped with fans. Price wise is ok, not too expensive.Show less

Author: zt1978Shah Alam, Malaysia
Title: Halal Chicken Rice Ball
Review: I dunno where else to have this that is halal, only here. Must eat here everytime i come to Melaka. I don't know what is the difference with non halal or good about chicken rice ball except it's in a ball, but end up ordering rice, than the balls. Chicken was great although ordered half seems the portion isnt like half, maybe the chicken was small? Ate for 2 and that wasnt enough (or bot of us was pure gluttony?).Show less

Author: ellikhoo
Title: Good chicken rice ball without the crazy queue
Review: Chicken rice ball is nice and aromatic. Chicken is good. Price is reasonable with a receipt showing what you are paying. Don't need to queue under the hot sun. Definitely better than those over-rated touristy shops.

Author: PeterD8Newcastle, Australia
Title: Hand Made Chicken Rice Balls
Review: Found this place on our wanders around the area and looked quite busy so we called in for Dinner. Tried the Chicken Rice Balls and found out that they are one of the only places which rolls them by hand - most are now done on a machine. They are a tasty morsel, a bit different in texture to the normal chicken rice. Also enjoyed a Sambal Sotong (Cuttlefish). Very good value at RM 18 for 3 people including a drink. Enjoyed it so much we went back a few days later for lunch and had regular chicken rice which was great too.Show less

Author: AuJusCoTucson, Arizona
Title: Good rice and average chicken
Review: We walked out of our massage appointments at Scents and Senses and saw a big "Chick Rice Ball" sign. We thought, why not. The two of us ordered half a boiled chicken, 10 rice balls, Nyonya chili shrimps, and 2 drinks. The bill was RM42. The chicken was good, but not as tender as Chung Wah's, but the rice balls were much better. They were more "al dente" compared to the mushy ones at Chung Wah's. I like that there were other menu options.Show less

Author: MiminazilaKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Not the usual Chicken Rice
Review: No this is not chicken ball...they are rice made into small balls...They are Chicken Rice Balls and they are fun to eat... something different than the usual chicken rice...the service is super fast.. the staff and owner are friendly...the place is small but clean... the price is reasonable...they also have sambal prawn and squid and fried veggies... the food are all tasty...For quick, tasty and fun lunch...try this place...Show less

Author: RoselohSingapore, Singapore
Title: Good food, exceptional service.
Review: We happen to visit this chicken rice shop as the one we initially wanted to visit was closed. Very nice food. Exceptional Service. When the owner's boy saw us sharing a plate of chicken, he proactively asked if I needed a plate. I declined because I didn't need 1 but the observant and attentive customer service was commendable. The owner also helped to carry my things as we needed to shift table. There was an air cooler at the entrance. The restaurant was quite cool despite the scorching sun outside. The owner definitely went the extra mile to make their customers comfortable. Food wise, I love the chicken as the meat has just the right amount of tenderness and the well-roasted skin was heaven. The chicken rice is soft and fragrant. The rice ball is small and cute. The rice ball cost Rm0.30 which I initially thought was a bit expensive for the size. However, in actual fact, there is a lot of rice in there as it is all compressed so the price is still justifiable. I would definitely patronise Ee Ji Ban again if I were in Melaka again.Show less

Author: vapelle19
Title: Normal service.
Review: Rice ball. Very nice. Soup very good. The place is a nice small place. We had the chicken balls rice. And the soup is nice too.

Author: Rachio2014Singapore, Singapore
Title: Enjoy a taste of Malacca
Review: The shop selling Chicken Rice balls is simply furnished. Even though it is not air-conditioned, there are enough fans and a cooler to keep the temperature sufficiently comfortable for a quick lunch. I'm impressed with the efficient use of space. The place for food and drinks preparation is located in the same compact space as the cash register.We did not have to wait long for the table to be cleared, food to be ordered and dishes to be served. The steamed chicken was tasty and the rice balls was perfectly shaped though a little starchy as compared with the usual chicken rice. The local kai lan was fresh and nicely cooked. Best of all was the chilled F&N lychee canned drink, which was an instant thirst quencher.This family-operated business truly lives up to its name of being No. 1 - Ee Ji Ban!Show less

Author: eezie
Title: Delish chicken rice balls
Review: Fast efficient service. Food served piping hot. Rice balls is something different and taste great. Has other dishes to complement the chicken rice, we had the kangkung which was good.

Author: Zakwan HPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Ball for Lunch
Review: Ee Ji Ban is one of famous chicken rice ball restaurants in Malacca and it is suggested by one of friend. We ordered 30 rice balls with steamed chicked and vegetables. The chicken rice ball is awesome! Similar taste with typical chicken rice, but it is ball-shaped. Size is not that big, yet not too small. Service is good and quick, don't have to wait long for your food. Located near to Menara Taming Sari, this is really a place to have a lunch and feed your stomach.Show less

Author: ciska_fJakarta, Indonesia
Title: The Chicken Rice Ball
Review: Suould you want to give a try on the Melaka's famous chicken rice ball, this is the perfect place to go.Large serving of chicken, should be perfect for two.The ice lime tea is also refreshing.Service is good, the waiter speaks malay, english and mandarin and kind to children.We also tried their sambal udang here, but it wasnt as good. Show less

Author: amoy_fenderKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Delicious
Review: Love the chicken rice ball with steam chicken & roasted chicken.. The Udang petai was good n awesome.. I love the Longan drink.. so good and I can drink even 10 cups. The location at the town near to Menara taming sari.. Need to find the parking.. Their staff are friendly and fast service. Keep it up guys! I will come back again..Show less

Author: CarplaneshiptrainSingapore, Singapore
Title: good local food at reasonable prices
Review: Non aircon restaurant that serves good local food. If you want to try Melaka's famed chicken rice balls, you can give this place a shot. The rice balls are handmade(you can see it when its served due to the imperfect shape). Tasted delicious. A normal person can eat 10 rice balls I think. The balls are small. Try the sambal sotong as well!Show less

Author: Liz J
Title: Halal Chicken Rice Ball
Review: Only halal chicken rice ball in Malacca. Thumbs up for the delicious chicken Rice. It's just a walking distant from Hatten Hotel.

Author: sophiaJohorBahruJohor Bahru
Title: Nothing to shout about
Review: We were looking for chicken rice balls, not in the Jonker Street area, because there were long queues there. There were 6 of us (adults) and a toddler. We ordered a plate of chicken rice balls (5 per person @ 30 cts each) and a chicken (RM38), a plate of 'siew pak choy' (RM11) and fishball soup ((RM9 for 12 fishballs and some choysum). The taste was nothing to shout about and prices are rather steep. I wouldn't recommend it at all.Show less

Author: FanazmiSingapore, Singapore
Title: A nice change.....
Review: Went to the place for an early dinner. Easy parking all around. Friendly and attentive staff.Ordered half a roasted chciken, Assam fish head, Sambal prawns, Kangkong belachan, chicken liver and of course, the rice balls. The chicken was really nice and tasty. Very memorable. Fish head was a tad too small and the kangkong was too overwhelmed by the excessive amounts belachan used.Come here for the chicken and rice balls.........that much I will recommend. Also you'll need more rice balls than you think :-)Show less

Author: hasmalinik
Title: Halal chicken rice ball
Review: Nice foods, love their salty sambal  prawn & squid. Friendly & very humble owner.Next trip to Malacca i will definitely come back here..2 thumbs up :)

Author: HannyBunnyKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Something new but average
Review: It was my first time trying the chicken rice ball. Tasted pretty average. They do serve other dishes besides chicken rice and chicken rice ball.I also tried the steam fish - portion was too small, and the fish sliced very thinly, hence expensive. The fried veggie was good. In fact all the portions were small. We ended up ordering 2 extra servings of chicken and rice balls.Service was fast though and friendly.The overall experience was good but will probably not go again.Show less

Author: Christian J
Title: Above average chicken rice ball
Review: From so many chicken rice ball restaurant in melaka, this one is above average. The taste and the portion ,also the price, is just match. Worth to try when you visit melaka. The location also in the center of the city, with very easy to see- shop.Show less

Author: Paul YSingapore, Singapore
Title: Halal, close to the Hatten Hotel but fare was average
Review: Our lunch on the afternoon we arrived in Malacca. With everyone hungry and anxious to eat, no one was prepared to drive around to look for food. So we settled for something near Hatten Hotel where we were lodging. One of the must-dos for the trip was to try the chicken rice balls and so we discovered Ee Ji Ban just next to the hotel within easy walking distance. They had well-placed banners along the main road which screamed "chicken rice balls." They also had other dishes and there were plenty of banners which showed their eatery being featured in newspapers, etc.There was a crowd and signs proclaiming it "halal" attracted Malay tourists. The chicken rice balls are small, something like large fishballs at dim sum places. The chicken was average, a little to wet for my taste. The proprietor speaks English & Mandarin so that may be a plus for foreigners.Show less

Author: themushroomsociety
Title: A memorable first time to eat rice balls!
Review: Great food, great host, and a lot of potential to be the best place to eat chicken rice balls in the town center! The lady host wasnt able to give us roasted chicken rice on time as it was still being prepared and we were delighted to get a complimentary small serving of it. Awesome! Worth the trip. Show less

Author: ahmadshazerainShah Alam, Malaysia
Title: The Best There Is!!!
Review: great host, great food at affordable prices. I have never missed an opportunity to have a meal here everytime I'm in Melaka. it seems like for the past 3 years, this has been my go to food venue whenever i'm in Melaka. recommended dish; sambal garam sotong/udang.Show less

Author: aha181Scheveningen, The Netherlands
Title: The only Halal chicken rice ball in Melaka.
Review: Over rated i think. 1 ball of rice size of ping pong ball cost 30 cents. Average person consumes about 5 balls. The chicken costs extra. Total cost for 3 pax about RM23 include chinese tea, ice lemon tea and mineral water. But overall it was worth it cos it was the only Halal chicken rice ball stall we could find in Melaka.Show less

Author: LadyjennerinSingapore, Singapore
Title: Not as fantastic as its name
Review: Obviously this eatery received a lot of media coverage. But im puzzled that the place was not packed with people. The chicken rice comes in balls, not the typical plate of rice we usually see.The balls of chicken rice were small. For a medium size man, he'll probably need at least 10 to be full. We ordered the mix chicken (roasted & steamed) and some side dishes. The roasted chicken are pretty good but i wont give it a must-try. There are better options at Melaka.Show less

Author: Odyssey8888Singapore, Singapore
Title: Not worth the money. Lousy Chilli
Review: Fundamentals of a good chicken rice meal. Solid Chilli and Nice Rice.The boss is a perfect salesman. He said his Asam Pedas is better than the Parit Jawa one. I didn't bother to try.Their chilli was very dilute and watery. Rice not as fragrant.There were 9 of us. we ate 80 chicken rice balls + 1 chicken + 1 veg. Total $84RM.compared to the old corner store of Jonker walk, this one is no where near.The rice balls are not as compacted as the Jonker walk, so that's why we ate 80 balls.Very expensive. Will not return for more. We spent only half that amount at the corner shop the next day.Show less

Author: MichelleLee0717
Title: I will never come back again!
Review: The service sucks. We ordered 4 set chicken rice ball and they didnt allow us to get some extra plates as we wanted to share we other friends. One of the waiter spilled the sauce on my friend's leg and didnt even apologise. Waiter talked in an arrogant style. No manner. The taste is so lousy. Not nice at all. Price is so expensive. Postions are just so little. People please dont come here.Show less

Author: Whitters80
Title: Delicious and great value!
Review: We stumbled across this little restaurant by chance, and we gave it a try! Definitely glad we did, it was so good! The friendly owner was very courteous and helpful, and the food was amazing! I'd really recommend sambal sotong ! The squid was delish!!

Author: h4niMalaysia
Title: Halal Chicken Rice Ball Restaurant
Review: Rice ball chicken rice is a speciality of Melaka and prior to this, halal versions were difficult (if not impossible) to find. Ee Ji Ban's version is tasty, although I would say the portions are smallish. They also have plenty of vegie dishes to accompany, and a choice of soups. We had the cincalok omelette but thought it was not worth it for the price; will not have this omelette again though we do want to come back for the chicken rice!Price is also a bit on the higher side for chicken rice but the taste makes up for it.Show less

Author: satoyurikosingapore
Title: Average rice ball but tasty chicken
Review: It was an accidental find ... we were rejected by a nearby Peranankan restaurant and one of the group member wanted to have chicken rice ball. The boss is friendly and told us to trust him in terms of quantity of food to be ordered.We had chicken rice balls, chicken (half steamed and half roasted), Peranankan style squid and prawn, cinchalok omelette, sambal sweet potatoe leaf, and refreshing lime juice (Thai lime)The rice ball was so-so but the chicken is tasty! esp the roasted ones - with maltose taste and not dry/tough at all. The steamed ones are yum too. I also liked the omelette (unique with cinchalok) and sweet potatoe leaf.Price wise - it's not as economical as other food in Melaka. We spend arnd RM 15 per pax.It's still worth trying if you don't want the long queue at other Jonker Street's stalls and happened to stay nearbyShow less

Author: ray tKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Expensive!
Review: We stopped by this restaurant to allow my kids to try 'chicken rice ball' - famous in Melaka.Yes yes, one would most probably say, it's halal, what do you expect? But it is 'chicken rice' after all... and it's either it's good, or it isn't. In the shape of balls or not.It was quite an expensive experience, we had the set (which was ok) but we ended up ordering a few more side dishes (another plate of chicken included) and spent about RM35 for 1 adult and 2 small kids!I did call to make a 'reservation' just so that there won't be disappointment. Getting there, I realised that they made the rice balls there and then, hence the wait.Show less

Author: NOR AISAH AKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Not worth the money
Review: I went to their 'halal' outlet near Melaka Raya. We just wanted to try the authentic chiken rice ball but we found out that it didn't justify the hype. For RM7.00 I got 10 fish ball size rice balls (quite ok with this), a small portion of chicken (this is a ripp off) without a bowl of soup which is a normal accompaniment of chicken rice and no limit to condiments-chillies and soya sauce. I think they expect us to order other side dishes which we didn't do. I'm just curious, it is just that when I eat at any Chinese restaurant, the owner is always concern if not so much of the taste (different people have different tastebuds-can't satisfy everybody) but the portion is always enough. This one is a let down.Show less

Author: cochleartraveller
Title: Chicken Rice
Review: I didn't find the taste that great, nor did I find the portion worth it, infact I was hungry just shortly after! Dissapointed.

Author: wearethekids
Title: Just average.
Review: Not a particularly fantastic place to enjoy the famous chicken rice balls. Also the balls are poorly made and are of uneven sizes, making it quite unsightly.

Author: YmgPhilippines_
Title: Something different...rice balls, literally
Review: Great food, their specialty is the chicken rice ball, very tasty chicken served  with rice ball, good combination. They also serve  spicy  squids and veggies . Simple yet very delicious. Quick service, very friendly  and homey atmosphere. Had a great time!

Author: leecK9330OU
Title: Overated
Review: One of the popular local street food in Malacca. There is no seating, only offer take away & limited parking nearby. Taste ordinary

Author: MadelineFoong9988
Title: I'm in Putu Piring heaven
Review: Finally had my first bite of this infamous and widely spoken about snack or dessert. In fact, the first whiff is already a sign that it's worth the queue and the looooong wait for it to open in the evening. Every bite is generously filled with fragrant gula melaka in the midst of the fresh and fine rice flour. The freshly grated coconut added to the aroma and texture. Best eaten fresh when it's piping hot.Show less

Author: ginachow
Title: Nice but be prepared to queue
Review: Super huge Putu Piring that we queued for an hour, so be prepared to queue but at least you won’t be disappointed by it. Soft and fluffy rice powder with grated coconut in between, and generous filling of gula melaka. Definitely thumbs up!

Author: rain498Singapore, Singapore
Title: One of the must-eats in Melaka!
Review: The shop opens from 6pm to 10pm and we were there early around 620pm on a Friday evening and already there was a queue formed. There was a person in-front of us who ordered 60 pieces hence, needed to wait for a while. The cooking time was not too long and at one-go, there is a batch of about 20 pieces were being steamed simultaneously.This is by far, one of the larger pieces of putu piring that I have ever come across and at just RM1.20 per piece, this is quite a steal. Taste amazing and the gula melaka in it was really good.Must eat in Malacca.Show less

Author: Treg_SingaporeSingapore
Title: Putu Piring - Worth the Walk from Jonker
Review: Having eaten the ones from Haig Road in Singapore, these ones are larger and tastier. Not just my view but most of my friends who were with me. Got to eat it there and then (within an hour) to taste the best of it. There was no queue as we arrived when it opened at 6pm on a random Tuesday evening. It’s a short 15-20 minute walk from Jonker Street. Show less

Author: alansxi86
Title: Uniquely Malaccan delicacy, a must try.
Review: Steamed rice flour cake with gula melaka (palm sugar) and grated coconut. Made upon order, it's moist, sweet, slightly salty, and fragrant (from the banana leaves). Best eaten while still warm, contain generous amount of ingredients (at RM1.20 per piece).

Author: onghm6950
Title: Tasty
Review: The putu piring sold here is very big, double the size I have seen. They put a lot of malacca sugar compared to other putu piring makers. Reminder, have to queue long to get to eat the food.

Author: melmeleats
Title: Generous sixes of putu piring! Must-go!
Review: At only RM1.20 a piece and each comes piping hot, there's no reason for you to skip this stop at melaka! Super delicious putu piring with a copious amount of gula melaka within and just eat it when it's hot.. it's really good..

Author: Patrick Terence LSingapore, Singapore
Title: Worth the wait!
Review: I usually do not queue up for food but this was an exception. The stall opens at 6 pm and when we arrived, there was already a long queue. However, the wait was well worth it. It was piping hot, generous fillings and they did not stinge on the coconut. DELICIOUS! Truly a must-eat when you visit Malacca!Show less

Author: happydevo55Portland, Oregon
Title: Great little treats at only 1.20 MYR each
Review: Great little deserts. We got there just after they opened so we did not wait long. They are 1.20 MYR per piece for these delicious little treats. We bought 8 of them so we would have some for a couple of days. They are so good fresh. Only thing I wish is that they had somewhere there where you could sit and enjoy them, but we took them over to the waterside and enjoyed them. I would go back here regularly if I lived here. Highly recommend going to get some. Also fun to sit and watch them make the Putu.Show less

Author: zacstone08
Title: Best putu piring I had so far
Review: Small shop along the road with the bright signboard. I was pleasantly surprised with a short queue and bought 8 pieces in one go for snacks for the evening and the cake was really yummy. Whilst queuing, we decided to buy a pack of the gula melaka as well and it should make some yummy food judging by the taste of the same gula melaka in the putu piring. Worth the time to head there and queue.Show less

Author: EnochmingoKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Best Putu Piring in the town
Review: I only ate putu piring in pasar malam before. But once I tried this, no more putu piring can amaze me. They serve the fresh and tasty, not too sweet putu piring made by gula melaka. Eventhough you have to queue up for maybe around 15 mins to buy it but it totally worth.Show less

Author: yeeping87
Title: Recommended by relative from Melaka, queued for 1hr+
Review: Had been wanting to try this dessert since it was recommended by locals. Decided to come during PH, ard 8pm. Queued patiently for more than 1 hr - for just 6 pieces (for 2 person). The gula melaka is too sweet to my liking (they’re generous in it) but the shredded coconut save the day! Mind u, this dessert is a killer for supper as the ingredients include rice flour, gula Melaka, & shredded coconut. All in all, if u r there at 6, u might be able to get them quite fast! Not bad for one timer! Won’t be back for more.Show less

Author: jeffchia88Singapore, Singapore
Title: Delicious but nothing to rave about unless it is your first time
Review: I was referred to the shop by a relative and had actually wanted just buy the Coconut palm sugar(Gula Melaka). Observing the long queue I decided to have a try. It was a 15 minute queue before I could order.Well, the steamed rice flour cakes with Gula Melaka inside with a sprinkle fresh grated coconut melts in your mouth but really nothing of the extra ordinary as I can better ones in Haig Road Hawker centre in Singapore. I guess it must have been the best there as I did not come across anther stall during my stay.The cakes were prepared by two guys and a lady with another helping out in the packaging. Anyway that was tea for me and I manage to buy what I wanted - The Gula Melaka. To get there one needs to have a car just like much of the places in Melaka or take a trishaw or get a Grab car. Forget about the taxis unless you are feeling rich or desperate to get there. Perhaps you could rent a bike somewhere and cycle there too.There is no sitting area to consume the cakes so we drove down to the Portugese Settlement to sit by the seafront to enjoy our cakes.This shop is closed on Sunday.Show less

Author: garetjax72Singapore, Singapore
Title: Excellent putu piring, best eaten fresh
Review: The best putu piring in Malacca from a stall run by a husband and wife team. It only opens after 6 pm and is located along Jln Tengkera, right beside a shop that sells Toto lottery. The putu piring are of a good size, and the gula melaka used is of excellent quality, not too sweet, which indicates there is no added white sugar. They are best eaten fresh, and indeed are prepared only to order.The stall sells the gula melaka used in the putu piring, and it is excellent!Show less

Author: kiangggSingapore, Singapore
Title: Delicious!
Review: This stall has relatively short working hours, and only open at night from 6pm to 10pm. We heard about the Long queues but when we arrived at 945pm we were pleasantly surprised that there was only 1 patron ahead of us. The putu piring is freshly prepared and steamed, with a perfectly balanced mix of flour, gula Melaka and grated coconut. Each piece is RM1.20. Best eaten fresh! Most patrons park along the roadside by the side of the stall. Show less

Author: M30_MOLLYKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Best Putu Piring Ever!
Review: Have always loved putu piring but could never find a great one such as this anywhere else. The stall operates in the front of a shop where they steam and prepare the putu piring on the spot. Then it is placed on a banana leaf and packed when it is piping hot. The size of the putu piring is big with generous amount of gula melaka and grated coconut. The grated coconut is salty therefore tastes very well when eaten together with the flour and gula melaka. The taste was simply out of this world! A must try! Show less

Author: EatnPlayallDaySingapore, Singapore
Title: Piping Hot!
Review: There appears to be only one putu piring stall opposite the Lao Qian Ice Cafe. The putu piring here is worth trying - they do a perfect balance of ground rice flour with gooey gula melaka - yummy!Be prepared to wait as the stall prepares only 1 order at a time - read: 5 putu piring (!) even though they have a 10-unit steamer. Not sure why when they can effectively double productivity that they choose only to steam 5 at a time. This is with 3 people manning the stall! Ah well - the Q is manageable as long as the people in front don’t do multiple boxes! If you have to wait, I’d suggest you buy a coconut shake from next door - it is delicious and you’d be happily sipping until it’s your turn! Putu Piring 5 for RM6 / Coconut shake RM4Show less

Author: ttye0Central Melaka District, Malaysia
Title: Super sweet
Review: This hype stall was always crowded with customers queuing along roadside.Since when we liked over sweet stuffs？The gula melaka was totally out.Lack of aroma and flavour,only sweet,sweet and sweet(sweet from the extra sugar, not from the original gula melaka.ok).Sorry,not for me to queue.If u like super sweet putu,go there.Show less

Author: Louis Y
Title: Great tasting, but wait not so much
Review: Easily a half hour wait to purchase RM12 worth of putu piring. But pretty tasty nonetheless. Come after dinner for a late night snack

Author: chrischoong007
Title: Consider the best in the country
Review: I have never missed coming to this place when ever I am in Melaka. Nice steaming hot putu piring. There's always a queue but not to worry, service is fast. Don't mind the price if the food is good.

Author: OneLena
Title: Fresh, delicious, queue a long time
Review:
This place is famous.  I waited 45 minutes to get my putu piring.  Well worth the wait!  I have not had authentic putu piring in years!  

Locals queue to get 36-45 pieces to take away, so be patient!

Author: salini01
Title: Must try for everyone
Review: Third time coming back to Melaka and this place is always a must for me. I just LOVEEEEE the putu piring here. It's like potato chips, 1 is never enough.

Author: Choo NIpoh, Malaysia
Title: freshly steamed putu piring in Malacca
Review: One of the best putu piring I have ever tasted which located at jalan tengkera,something you cant miss in Malacca.It is a bit too far by walking from the city centre.queue is long but their service is pretty fast.Did i mention this was cheap and good?Yup, it is!Show less

Author: Kg TSingapore, Singapore
Title: Steaming Piring Fragrant Perfumed The Air
Review: Was just riding past and noticed a queue and distinctive steaming Putu Piring smell caught my attention. So I made a u-turn and joined the queue. I observed the efficiency of the family team, with 1 making the dough, 1 steaming, 1 packing and last one selling. It was perfect team. No airs.At RM1.20 a piece, I thought it was decent pricing. It comes with generous amount of Gula Melaka and fresh coconut shavings, it just hit the right note. Makes me crave to make another trip there (but that's more than 200km away).Show less

Author: Yap KNegeri Sembilan, Malaysia
Title: Hot Putu Piring!
Review: Located at Jln Tengkera along the main road. Drive slow to get there or you can see a queue with uncle & aunties cooking with steam flowing around outside the house then this is the destination. Place your order & collect your number. Wait till your number is called for your collection. It could take about 20-30mins. It is circular cone shape, quite big, hot, sweet & good. Eat when it's still warm but not cold. It won't be nice. Try it if you haven't & enjoy your food!Show less

Author: elaynecswShah Alam, Malaysia
Title: Must-try if you are in Malacca
Review: It's the best putu piring in Malacca and many people travel far to try it. Drive slow as you might miss this tiny stall in front of a house. Tricky to buy because of their short opening hours and limited pieces for sale each night. Que can be long but you'd see many people willing to wait (smelling the wonderful aroma of hot sweet gula melaka while waiting makes you salivate in a heavenly bliss). Suggest to buy some of their uncooked raw gula melaka cubes back to make sweet desserts - goes well with anything!Show less

Author: candiesssSingapore, Singapore
Title: One of Malacca's food trail highlights
Review: You'll smell it as your come close to the stall. The putu piring is big, so the 2 I had left me with little space for other food at the Jonker night market. Fluffy and very generous with the gula melaka. We queued for about 25 minutes at 6.30pm on a Saturday, watching the sunset behind us. Would recommend trying this if you don't mind queuing. :)Show less

Author: samanthas792
Title: Good puti piring
Review: One of the best tasting putu piring i have tasted. Wish the putu piring is smaller in size so that can pop into the mouth in just one or 2 bites, it would taste even better!!

Author: pinkgiraffeKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Most amazing putu piring in the world
Review: Soft, fluffy full of fragrant gula melaka goodness!! It's so yummy and worth the queue by the roadside. Book online via their Facebook page if you are ordering a lot. Must try if you are ever in Melaka. According to my knowledgeable Malaccan friend, the gula melaka (palm sugar) used is made the traditional way by a seller whose shop is opposite the putu piring place. Bought a packet of the gula to make my own ondeh-ondeh at home.Show less

Author: HelloChrisTanSingapore, Singapore
Title: Made from home where the heart is...
Review: i realised that there are so many mixed reviews about this little humble home food stall, and i have to say that taste is very very and extremely subjective. It's amazing how a putu piring which is simply made of 3 ingredients - rice flour, gula melaka and shredded coconut, can turn up the senses of many to such a high note, suddenly making anybody such a food connoisseur. Too bland...too sweet....too anything or everything....blah blah blah. #seriouslyFor the many years that i have visited this stall, i don't think they have ever claimed to be the best or like many food establishments, hang up printouts, plaques or photos of celebrities visiting. Every evening (except Sunday), they just go about doing what they always do - open the front door, set up the stall, prepare the fresh ingredients and start steaming some hand made putu piring-s. Despite how the world was judging them online - they probably are somewhat aware or not aware at all, they just carry on this family business which has probably put all their kids to school. If they can still be standing after so many years - from just catering to the folks in the small town of Melaka, to gaining such international audience, they must be doing something right.For the many years that i have been to Melaka, this putu piring has always been THE dish that brings me back to Melaka. i might not have eaten that many putu piring from around the world but quite enough from Singapore, but being a creature of comfort, if i find something i really like, it will stick to me for a long long time. And i am sure taste is something you don't really forget - just like how you will remember how bad something tastes from a certain stall and you vow never to go back there again, you will always remember the good dishes that you had somewhere that made it up to your very personal list of favourites.For the many years that this family putu piring has been on my personal list of Melaka favourites, it really is a taste i reminisce. For that, it's a 5 for me.Show less

Author: Panda6551Singapore, Singapore
Title: Divine
Review: You must eat the Putu Piring from this stall to know what is "REAL" Putu Piring. The gula melaka is fragrant as it should be as it is from Melaka and be a bit too sweet but then may be due to my cut back on sugar as my other companions felt otherwise. So save some stomach space for this desert. Worth the wait. Difficult to find good Putu Piring these days. The one at Bedok in Singapore comes close but the gula melaka is not as tasty or fragrant.Show less

Author: Yeoh M
Title: 1 day trip.. Cari makan.. 👍👍😍😍
Review: Taste as nice as before... QC pass!!! N Q as long as before.. Yummy yummy!!! A sure must visit destination next time!!!

Author: David T
Title: A little too sweet
Review:
The gula melaka a little too sweet. 

There was a queue when we were there at around 8.30pm. 

The lady and her family members were  quite efficient.

Author: Grace WSingapore, Singapore
Title: Average Putu Piring
Review: I read about the famous Putu Piring on Jalan Tengkera and decided to walk to the shop after dinner from Jonker Walk. As I was with a Caucasian friend who had no idea what Putu Piring was, I started to describe it as something so delicious that he had to try it. It was drizzling and by the time we got there, there was already 10 people ahead of us in the queue. I queued for almost 40mins because the Putu Piring makers seemed to be making a whole lot and putting away for some people who have ordered in advance but would be collecting later as they were not physically there. So those in the physical queue had to wait doubly long as a result. Luckily, I ordered only 2. We ate them while they were hot as recommended but couldn't finish them. The Putu Pirings were so tasteless. The flour tasted bland and the gula melaka was not fragrant at all. Honestly, I've tasted better Putu Piring at the pasar malam on Jonker Street (even though people claim that the place is a tourist trap).Show less

Author: TaroSgSingapore

I was there when there, there were customers who arrived like 10mins before 10pm and all the putu piring were already sold out..Show less

Show less

Author: PS12345678000

Author: prasanas
Title: Nonsense
Review: I really don't understand how this place is voted the best PUTU piring... Clearly many don't know what is the ACTUAL TASTE of putu... Putu fist and foremost is an Indian delicacy... You want to know the REAL puttu taste like you have to go to Alor Setar, KedahIn this shop, whn I tasted it the flour was not properly cooked... The taste is MASKED by shoving in a lot of brown sugar [gula melaka] ... So people think it's nice... NONSENSE! The REAL PUTU is nothing like tht.... The FOCUS taste is on the rice floor NOT on the brown sugar [Gula melaka]... The floor has an aromatic rosy smell and a slight rosy taste... The gula melaka and the coconut is VERY MINIMAL... Putu here in Tengkera is just about loads of brown sugar [gula melaka] and lots of coconut that's all... It's edible but it's not the best putu please Show less

Author: Dolphania

Author: JasmyinKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Putu piring galore
Review: Putu piring is steamed flour with a filling of gula melaka. It is soft and warm and sweet and superbly yummy. This stall is actually in front of an actual lived in house. The house is located between the Sports Toto shop and the pet shop - Perniagaan Sayangku. The putu piring they serve can only be taken away (there is no place to sit down and eat) and parking is not easy (unless you park by the side of the road and run in to get a couple of these yummies). Sometimes there are unimaginable lines and it will take forever to get your share of these. Other times, it is fairly okay and you'd get yours in less than 5 minutes. The putu piring are usually packed hot in a box with holes so it won't get soggy. It comes on a piece of banana leaf, fluffy, packed with sugary goodness of the gula melaka and has sprinkles of grated coconut. Currently it is priced at RM1 per piece. Opens everyday except Sunday. 6pm till I guess when they run out of putu piring to sell. Go earlier (7 plus) to avoid disappointment.Show less

Author: ganadelineSingapore, Singapore
Title: Good Melaka version of putu kiring
Review: I got to know about this stall from a food show on tv which featured their famous putu kiting. We drove there and was surprised to see there was mo queue yet as it was 7.30pm, still early. Could smell the pandan way before I approach the stall. A couple and their daughter were preparing these kuehs with wellpractised and deft hands. The putu piring was rather big with generously serving of coconut and gula Melaka. I find the Kueh texture a bit rough and dry due to the type of flour used . It didn't taste as fragrant as it smells. Overall it is still good value at 90cts each and it is a refreshing change from the version we get in Singapore. Will eat them again if I have the craving for it when I'm in malacca in future.Show less

Author: altytudeSingapore, Singapore
Title: Tasty And Fragrant Putu Piring.
Review: Read about this stall on some foodie's blog but sorry, can't recall whose blog so can't accord credit here.Went looking for it while visiting Melaka. Walked from Jonker street, approximately 10 minute worth of walking. Just as i was feeling less than confident whether we were on the right track, a whiff of steamed rice flour and Gula Melaka fragrance found its way to my nose, thus confirming its location.It is a stall outside the vendors' home, looked clean and well-organised. the vendors were pleasant despite being always busy making Putu Piring. It was also quite surprising to see the vendors were Chinese as i've always assumed Putu Piring is a fusion product of Indian Putu and Malay pandan leaves/gula melaka. The Kuih/Kueh is made upon order while the customers wait and look on. Very fresh and piping hot.Customers were from all walks of life -- we walked there, some came by motorbikes, others cycled and there was a guy who came in a Porsche Cayenne SUV looking quite excited to get his Putu Piring. The Putu Piring was delicious, there was a nice, clean rice fragrance and the gula melaka filling had a pleasant natural sweetness which could only come from good quality gula melaka.However, for those from Singapore, i think the famous Haig Road Putu Piring in Singapore has an edge over this version. The Haig Road version is more moist, has more grated coconut and stronger pandan fragrance.Having said that, this was a Putu Piring with its own merits and very enjoyable too. Open from 6pm till approx 10pm. Closed on Sunday.Show less
