Title: Surprisingly family friendly satay celup restaurant
Review: This seems to be the most famous satay celup in town according to the taxi driver who drove us there.What impressed me was their warm service. I only found out the sauce for cooking the satay was spicy upon arrival. So I asked if there was non spicy sauce available for the kids. The lady boss offerred to cook the satay in their kitchen for me. Thumbs up for the thoughfulness!! At time of payment, I checked with the boss if it would be easy to flag a taxi here. He offerred to call a taxi for us! I was grateful with his help as we were tourist n not familiar with the place.Drive your own car to this restaurant if u can. The traffic is not as congested as the central. Otherwise Uber n Grab is cheaper to move around in Melaka.Show less

Author: JGOH25Subang Jaya, Malaysia
Title: One of my fave and MUST HAVE
Review: This is a one of its kind steamboat/shabu with SATAY sauce as the soup. It is one of the BEST in town vs the overrated Capitol. This is my go to each time i am in town for business or leisure. If you are facing it, go to the one on the right side. There are 2 shops with the same name but if i remember correctly, the one on the right is the original one. It starts only in the late afternoon till late nite.. Make sure you go try this.Show less

Author: chrischoong007Penang Island, Malaysia
Title: Want to go and eat BUT
Review: Have to get there early and parking is not easy along the street. And there is always a queue by 7 pm. Nice choice of 'satay' and the gravy is nice and thick. Price is just right, service is good and efficient and you will be spoilt for choice. Just come early, try to get a parking space and you will be alright!!Show less

Author: KirRoyaleSooKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Must try in Melaka
Review: Local cuisine, so tasty and not pricey. There is 2 Ban Lee Siang next to each other. I believe they are family . Is a must if you visit Melaka. So yummy, just needs to drink a lot of water after the meal if you don’t want to get sore throat. Show less

Author: tadboonMiri, Malaysia
Title: Worth a try
Review: I tried d left one w blue sign board becus when I go the right one is closed. I like the sauce flavor is good. Be careful this is not hygienic & v unhealthy. But this is definitely a must try for tourist. The boss is intentive & does not ignore when they are ppl queuing up. Show less

Author: MelanieQ59
Title: Local Favorite
Review: Nice gravy and fresh ingredient served. Efficient service and good hygiene as they will cover the satay gravy once the customers finished the foods

Author: MacPau
Title: Opens at 3.30
Review: I was on my way to JB, and stopped by for my satay group fix. Ban Lee Slang was already open. The gravy was better than Capitol's, imho. I will definitely come back again!

Author: macplastikKuala Lumpur
Title: Enjoyable but
Review: Really enjoyable from start to finish, until we asked for the bill whereupon they placed a lid over the boiling soupy gravy, suggesting that they don't clear out the soupy gravy and recycle it for the next batch of customers. That's unhygienic. That's a very easy way to spread and contract diseases. That's disgusting.Show less

Author: cynmaine
Title: Love the satay celup
Review: good customer service as the boss is very friendly.  Look the food as well, easy to get parking and you can get the table quite fast.

Author: Maxteo919Singapore, null, Singapore
Title: Locals recommended and okay for supper place
Review: Went to this restaurant and saw another one side by side. We went to the one on the right as there were more people in the restaurant. The satay celup was okay. The satay sauce was okay, not too thick. However, the same pot of sauce at the table was there, unchanged, for all the patrons eating at that table. We were to boil our sticks of food in the pot of satay sauce till it was cooked. Not too expensive at around 1 RM per stick of satay Celup. Good for supper but it was abit out of the city area. We went using Grab. If you want some supper place, do pay this restaurant a visit.Show less

Author: Lady_Lyn18Chengdu, China
Title: Popular among local
Review: Recommended by local, we visited this restaurant, apparently there are two similar restaurant side by sideWe tried the one on the left side because there are more people thereEach satay cost around1 -1.2ringgit Half of my family likes it, but half of them doubt about the hygiene of the sauce they are using, because they are using the same sauce pot for the customersShow less

Author: Gina T
Title: Famous Satay celup at Melaka
Review: Even though the waiter is very busy but they insist to provide a good service, smile and friendly. This is my first for this satay celup. Their satay celup is just so so only, not so special. Reccomended for high tea or supper.

Author: Tino898Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Good Satey Celup
Review: This is the first time we visit this restaurant. Along the road have 4 satey celup restaurant. 3 Ban Lee Siang. 1 Mc Quek. Finally we decided to try the yellow sign Ban Lee Siang. At 830pm, weekday, it also so crowded. Luckily we can get a table where the customer just finish. 8 of us, enjoy the food here. Rm1.10 per stick. Show less

Author: Star_dust_rainbowKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Not worth it
Review: This is not a place for young children as there is nothing suitable for them to eat. Each skewer cost RM1.10 and the portion on the skewer was actually pretty small. I remember eating this about 10 years ago and the food on the skewer seems to be bigger. I know the price of everything has gone up but 1 tiny prawn for RM1.10.... that's ridiculous. And not forgetting 1 piece of round fish cake, 3 very thinly sliced sausage, 1 piece of fish ball and the list goes on and on.Show less

Author: WOO GPenang, Malaysia
Title: Satay Celup Experience
Review: There are 2 satay celup shops with same name and there are side by side. We went to the "yellow sign board" Ban Lee Siang and there was a written notice at the wall saying this is the original shop before they split their business which refer to the next shop "Blue sign board of Ban Lee Siang".During dinner time, it was packed with people and table fully occupied but the service were fast. Taste : Average. The satay sauce was sweet although it "look" red and spicy. Not many food choices.Price : Affordable, for once a while experiences. We spend RM90 for 5 adult as we did not like it much compare what we had before. Show less

Author: Frank_Png
Title: Excellent!
Review: Had a couple of dinners there. Satay sauce make the food more appetizing and yummier, i suppose. However, this is not a meal for the faint hearted. So put aside your hygiene standard and dig in!

Author: candiesssSingapore, Singapore
Title: Affordable and worth trying
Review: Satay Celup or satay sauce steamboat restaurants can be found in many parts of Malacca. You need to forget about hygiene when you dine in these places as the Satay sauce is reused and topped up in the same pot for the next customer. Please do not double dip!Each stick is RM1.10, making it so easy to grab dozens. The staff count the number of sticks you have when you have finished your meal. Service is prompt and you get a table fairly quickly even with a queue. Worth a try just for novelty sake. I didn't find the Satay sauce absolutely amazing and the variety can be better. Show less

Author: ellxy
Title: Yummy yummy
Review:
Love this place! A definite must visit! 
Sauce is yummy and very affordable! I would say varieties are ok.. could be better but I'm happy!

Author: JohnstannoSingapore, Singapore
Title: Can't stop eating!
Review: Very tasty satay sauce and food are fresh + a variety of choices. A must must to try and eat like locals when you are in Melaka. Each stick cost around RM 1+. Throw hygiene out of your mind and enjoy the food. You will love it.Staff are very prompt in their services. Missing it already!Show less

Author: Carbo tPuchong, Malaysia
Title: Satay sauce steamboat
Review: Place is always crowded and have to wait for your table. The satay sauce is among the best in Malacca and they have a good variety of meats, vegetables and seafood on skewers. A favourite place for the locals to eat so it must doing right...Show less

Author: V00DooKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Specialising in Satay Celup (steamboat satay)
Review: Good selection of chilled skewers (meat and seafood) in the 2 HUGE glass fronted chillers. Too many to describe. Grab yourself a tray, fill it up and dunk them into the pot of sauce to cook or reheat. Scoop some sauce into your own plate. NO DOUBLE DIPPING!! At the end of your meal, one of the staff will tally up your skewers and work out your bill. Each skewer costs RM1 - we managed 70 sticks between the 4 of us. Including drinks, the bill came up to RM88.85.Show less

Author: Lil Ly c
Title: Unhygienic, not worth the time!
Review:
Been there once n will not patronize this restaurant again.

Pots of satay sauce kept boiling n reused by the next customers. Skewers of seafood, meat, meatballs, fishballs lay on wet n bloodied trays. 

If hygiene is your concern, give this a miss!!

Author: zysonlee
Title: Overall it's nice, worth a try.
Review: We went with empty tummies but ended up finishing only 15 sticks of satay per person. Reasonable price (RM0.90 per stick) and a variety of choices of fresh and clean satay. The Satay Celup's paste can easily fill your stomach, take it slow and enjoy one by one, take your time. It's worth a try.Show less

Author: sinnyiKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Still my favourite satay celup
Review: Been eating since young, tried another famous satay celup but still find ban lee siang the best. Service is fast too. Just that it is getting more pricey now - RM1 for a stick which I find quire expensive for the portion served. Avoid peak hours if you don't have the patience to wait for a seat. Plenty of seats available after 9pm.Show less

Author: MK_Lai
Title: Favorite supper choice
Review: Great choice of variety satay in peanut sauce...!! Very crowd during weekend or public holiday. Serve some beer too in restaurant..!!

Author: 398limwSingapore, Singapore
Title: Satay Celup - a typical Malaysian dish
Review: The smell of a hot steamboat bubbling with peanut gravy is a magic potion to us. We always visit this restaurant when we are in Melaka. It is like part of the food culture here. Last night's visit was pleasant. All sticks cost only 1 ringgit and if you are a big eater you will need about 20 sticks. They are generous with the gravy making sure it is piping hot and full of peanuts. Show less

Author: 341angelinesMalaysia
Title: Average stuff
Review: Peanut sauce was average, nothing to shout about. There were skewers of meatballs, quail eggs, mushrooms and other processed foods (eg: sausage). Nothing super yummy. Less variety compared to Capitol but the environment is definitely more comfortable & hygienic. Price is ok, 90 sen per stick. Go there for the experience if that's what you're after, otherwise skip this if you're on the hunt for genuinely good melaka food.Show less

Author: swift1984Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Must Eat When in Malacca!
Review: This is one of the two popular satay celup joints (the other being Capitol), there is another one of the same name down the street which the owner claims is his as well. This joint is packed at 8PM while the other satay celup joint beside this one is seeing little to no customers.Food selection is not bad and the satay sauce is not too spicy (maybe I'm not that picky about food quality). They do change the satay sauce daily as it cannot be kept overnight. If you are concerned about food hygiene, find some place else to eat. This is just how the place rolls.Favorite celup items: taiwanese sausages, quail eggs, seafood tofu, otak-otak and kangkung (water spinach).Show less

Author: Natlooi
Title: Average
Review: In my opinion, the squid is the best as it is fresh and cost Rm2. The rest are just normal and I felt it kinda costly for each sticks cost Rm1.

Author: Michelle L
Title: Nothing to shout out for
Review: The food was so so and not worth the price. Satay sauce taste diluted, and some of the meat balls not very fresh.

Author: MrJLim
Title: Satay Celup
Review: Average in taste. Not as good as before. Selection is not a lot in comparison. Can be better. The satay sauce in the middle table did not change. Dirty and unhygienic.

Author: shemin61Singapore, Singapore
Title: Avoid! Disgusting and unhygienic!
Review: This place is at top 22nd place to dine in Malacca. How can this be?! Doesn’t anyone care about hygiene? I’ve tried Lok Lok from a mobile van before but it was way more hygienic than this place. Avoid! Avoid!They call it a restaurant but there is no air-conditioning. There were some fans around and at each table there is a tank of gas to cook the pot of satay sauce. Somehow I fear the tank might just burst beside me while I’m eating. We were quickly shown to a table but there are no instructions how to order. I had to stop one of the busy waiters to find out how to order/get food on the table. There were 3 young boys around the age of 12-15 years old helping out at the stall (possibly a family run business). They are sure how much each skewer cost, when or how do they charge, if it’s a buffet style or not. I had to ask other staff to get info. Basically, take a seat and order your drinks (before you know it, the drinks are served), put your belongings down, go to the fridge and take the skewers of meat/veg that you want, go back to your table and dip the skewers into pot of satay sauce to cook it and eat. Skewers are charged $0.90 per stick at the end of your meal. Things like prawns have double skewers, means its $1.80. Service is fast!The sight of the food in the fridge is rather turn off. The meat are just flimsily hanging on the skewers and placed on a bloodied tray. While trying to take a skewer, there is a chance you might touch other skewers as it is tangled in the tray. Who knows if the meat has been touched by other patrons? Satay sauce was really watery and the choice of skewers was mainly processed food, meatballs, cuttlefish balls, fish balls. Deep fried dough sticks are left in a basket, in the open for houseflies to feed on. Usually in Lok Lok style they would help you to deep fry some of the items and serve but here there isn’t. We didn’t take much of the food as the meat were unlabeled and bloody. Went elsewhere to eat after 1 round. Refer to photos. No one ever told me how disgusting it is to cook the food in that pot of satay sauce. I only found out at the end of my meal. The minute we stood up, the staff took a plate to cover the pot and cleared the last bit of the table (drinks). And another staff showed other patrons to our table and removed the plate, showing the satay sauce. Omg! I’m really praying no one double dip in our pot. Or hopefully no one was sick and passing bacteria through the shared sauce. I’ve tried other Lok Lok on mobile van and we each get our personal satay sauce, maybe Satay Celup is different concept. I reckon Lok Lok is more hygienic than a common sauce which who knows how many years it has been cooking. I will not return to Ban Lee Siang nor recommend to anyone. Overrated and disgusting!Show less

Author: AlvindharmawanJakarta, Indonesia
Title: Sate Celup!
Review: I went here with my friends as this is the closes sate celup restaurant nearby TBS as I had to catch my bus ASAP. Luckily, we were the first customer to use the dipping spicy peanut sauce, so my friend told me that it is still fresh. Tried every satay skewers, and love especially the pork sausages one!The spicy peanut sauce for some people may be too spicy, however, I love it!Too bad I cannot eat more satay skewers as we were eating in such a hurry. Show less

Author: CrystalT1171
Title: toooooooo spicy
Review: very spicy if compare to capitol satay celup but the queue is shorter but overall is a good try but warning is very spicy

Author: LittleLatteKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Nice & cheap but prepare for the queue
Review: There are 2 Ban Lee Siang next to each other and so I choose the first opened Ban Lee Siang (blue)..I was there at 5.30pm so queued almost 45mins..the owner and workers are very friendly..if one wish to change a new pot of sauce will cost rm60..so everyone is dipping into the same pot and you just pray that those previous customers are all good hearted not to re-dip the food into the pot again..but the sauce is very nice! Each stick cost about rm1. Love their lime & sour plum drinks. Best is you can purchase half kilo (1/2kg) of the satay sauce back home for rm20 (just add 500ml-a small bottle of mineral water). Show less

Author: DayleePaleta
Title: Delicious and fun!
Review: We had never been for satay so an older waiter had to explain how it worked. He was so helpful! We probably ate more than we needed to, but that’s not unusual for us.

Author: kriyalekshmiJohor Bahru, Malaysia
Title: Can go for the experience
Review: We visited Ban Lee Siang for supper. There will be a pot of peanut gravy in the middle of the table, we pick our food and cook it in the gravy. I find the choices little and the peanut gravy was average. It was ok for a first time experience. I might want to try other satay celup restaurants in my next visit. Show less

Author: golfpaths6Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Dipping delight
Review: Satay celup... Satay what? That was my first reaction to an introduction to kebabs dipped in a special boiling, peanut sauce in Malacca. Pork balls or seafood on bamboo skewer sticks, and more, can be chosen from the fridges. I personally love the quails eggs! It is like lok-lok, except that you boil your food in that heavenly peanut sauce instead of water. Remember to order the bread to dip in the sauce. Its hot and crampy here on weekends though. Of course queues are a norm. Come here by 6pm if you want to get a seat. Enjoy! Show less

Author: samanthas792
Title: Yellow signboard Ban Lee Siang
Review:
Yellow signboard Ban Lee Siang is the original one. $1 per stick, nice alternative place to try satay celup should Capitol has a long queue, which usually does! 

Came here twice in 2 days.

Author: weelijing
Title: Good Alternative!
Review: Prices are affordable and reasonable. Have your satay celup here in peace and no rush! 10mins walking distance from the bustling Jonker Street after your shopping and stuff. Recommended!

Author: TTC_214Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Used to love it but not anymore
Review: I used to love this so much and it is a must when I travelled to Melacca. But this is my last visit i think, ya before this I knew about the hygiene problem but since it does not cause discomfort to my stomach therefore I never feel a thing. However, during my last visit, I discovered stomach discomfort after the meal, I feel like vomiting. I think I won't be going in the near future.Show less

Author: lengying
Title: Satay celup best choice!
Review:
If you do not want to queue for Capitol, this is another good place to drop by! Make sure you go to the right shop, the one with Orange colour uniform staff!

The vege and tau Kee is must try!

Author: josd704
Title: Somebody told us we cannot leave Melaka without sateh culup
Review: We went here based on the recommendation of the owner we rented an apartment. Sateh Culup is sow thing like steamboat but then using a kind of spiced peanut soup to cook with. Very nice and tasty.

Author: Natasja_8Rotterdam
Title: Delicious and fun
Review: Satay celup is very tasty and great fun! We went twice. The food was all fresh and staff was very friendly and helpfull. This place has a very nice buzz with lots of families and groups of friends coming here for a relaxed dinner. The restaurant is close to the historicAl town center but we were the only tourists there on both occasions. Show less

Author: aflame_SG
Title: Satay Celup at its best!
Review:
Satay Celup here is one of the best in melaka. Definitely better than dunno-why-so-long-queue Capitol.... There's a huge varieties of food to choose from, but please do order the bread+cucumber. 

Oh, there's limited food choice for toddlers/non-spicy eaters.

Author: Belinda WKuala Lumpur
Title: Best satay celup in Malacca
Review: One of the oldest & best satay celup in Malacca town. There're 3 outlets on the same row of shops ie.McQuek & Ban Lee Siang with 2 shops different owners if I'm not mistaken. We went to the last one with staff in Orange uniform.Each stick is MYR1.00 (the ones on plates are different price) which is reasonable for more expensive food, it'll only be 1 serving per stick. So it's much likely depends on what type of food you would like to pick. They're a huge varieties of fresh food stored in the fridge from veggies, seafood, meat to even internal organs like pig intestines & etc. It's a non-halal place (serves pork) for sure!There'll be staff walking around assisting you with the satay hot sauce as they need to come around to stir them from time to time to avoid it getting burnt. Service is pretty good I must say.There's no parking space as it's located right on the main road. Not too convenient to grab a cab here as this area is usually quiet at night. Business is from 6pm till late night.Show less

Author: qiwen21Segamat, Malaysia
Title: Delicious. Always crowded
Review: This is where my satay celup cravings satisfied each time. This shop has more seats than the others and provides a variety of choices. The taste does not disappoint me in every visit. And this place is always filled with people from evening til night. No long queue such as Capitol, I still find this place a better alternative to satisfy the hype. More can be done for the hygiene in this place. Overall, I still love the satay celup here.Show less

Author: dennylkh
Title: Nice One
Review:
It's new concept of steamboat.

The food is variety and the price is justify.

They did offer normal soup for kids that can't take spicy.

Author: tango122008Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Delicious
Review: Delicious satay celup, good variety of choices of sticks, sauce is thick and peanut-y, very easy to overeat as the food is yummy and is a good place to chit chat with friends and family while dining. My tagline for the place would be 'Just one more stick...'Show less

Author: derekang1980Singapore
Title: Great alternative to satisfy the hype
Review: This is mostly known to the locals, but trends have shown that tourists are starting to notice this place. It's a little far out from the city centre but still within the city limits. Probably a good 10 mins drive. The hyped up stall Capitol probably serves a better satay sauce and better consistency but considering the long queues, this place offers just as good an alternative. Price wise it's also cheaper than the Capitol stall, and also have a long history in Melaka. This is the original stall but was subsequently split into two, where the stall next door is operated by the other family member. Great place to have some late night supper as food are mostly satisfying that crave and not exactly a fulfilling meal. Show less

Author: sam lKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Good sate celup
Review: My first time trying sate celup here in malacca and it's surprisingly good. Staffs were friendly, the herbal tea was great! Will definitely return. Please beware of the shop with the same name next door. Don't go to the one with blue sign. Go to the one with orange shirt crews Show less

Author: Cikgu
Title: Retro meal
Review: I visited Ban Lee Siang on the recommendation of Makansutra website. Our driver also recommended this restaurant as his previous group had been sick after they ate at the other famous satay chelop restaurant!We were ushered to a table as soon as we arrived at about 7.45pm. One side of the restaurant were the fridges where the skewers of food were kept cool. As expected there were the traditional offerings of sliced pork, liver, fish ball, quail eggs, kang kong, cuttlefish, tau pok alongside the more 'modern' offerings of tofu fishcake, meat ball, mushrooms and angry bird fishcakes! Prawns were peeled and skewered - most helpful!The sauce was a little watery in the beginning but it got thicker along the way. The servers came around several times to stir the sauce to prevent it from burning at the bottom. Skewers of food were dunked in the sauce and cooked. Plates of bread and cucumber were available to soak up the yummy sauce.Good value for money, all sticks were priced at RM1 each. A plate of bread and cucumber also cost RM1. Trays were provided for the raw food and separate plates were available in the fridge to place raw meat. I titled this review retro as I remembered eating this more than 40 years ago in Singapore. Then skewers of food were cooked in boiling water and the satay sauce was dip. I guess it has become more efficient to cook the food in satay sauce!Show less

Author: Jennyf00Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Simple but interesting concept
Review: If you wish your gravy to be "first-hand" then you should arrive earlier. We went there around 5pm, it was still half empty seats in the shop. Not recommended on peak hours, as those waiting will be standing right beside you. Wear thin clothes as it would be hot when you started to boil the gravy and dip-in the foods.Show less

Author: Sizuka W
Title: Melaka local signature food
Review: I went to this shop at 4.30pm to avoid the crowd. Ban Lee Siang well-known for satay celup. It's bite size food put on a stick then let it cooks inside a hotpot which filled with satay soup. The aroma of the satay soup is amazing. Watch out if u allergy to peanut because peanut is the key ingredient. Price is reasonable only cost rm1 per stick. There is another shop just next door which owned by his brother. I tried the one with blue color signboard. I would recommend that and personally I love the Fu chew meatball. The meatball has filling of another small meatball inside. PS it's little bit spicy. Show less

Author: linweisingaporeSingapore, Singapore
Title: Dinner
Review: 1 Day Malacca tour.Dinner was the famous "Lok-Lok". The rest of the Malaysia state serves clear soup base but it's here that they serve satay gravy sauce (peanut, spices and condiments sauce). Really different. Dare to be different. It's little spicy but tasty. For those with weak stomach best to avoid.This shop serves Lok-Lok and drinks only.No WiFi. Small not so clean squatting toilet. Indoor and outdoor seating. A little warm, as everyone cooking their own hot pot of food. Waiters and waitresses always busy topping up the gravy, taking orders and collecting payments. Slow service. Be prepared to queue during peak hours, 6pm - 9pm. Limited parallel parking space.Estimated about MYR 40-50 per person inclusive of drinks.Enjoyed this dinner. An unique experience.Show less

Author: Fengli
Title: Good satay sauce
Review:
Went there around 11pm. 
Quite a crowd but managed to find a place.
Food is great and lots of variety. 
Satay gravy is splendid. 
Will come back for more

Author: AcuraMelody
Title: Never let us down
Review: Every time we at Malacca we never miss satay celup. We reach there around 5.35 & you can see the restaurant is pack with people. The staff is friendly. The food & gravy is awesome 👍🏻 I prefer this than Capitol satay celup

Author: U556DLjessicabLeeds, United Kingdom
Title: Great satay but no chicken!
Review: This place is a great find. Luckly when we arrived it wasn't extremely busy and got seated straight away. The prices are great- 1 ringget per skewer. They range from tofu to crab sticks to wontons but no chicken!! The coke is 2 ringgets and it makes for an enjoyable experience. I would recommend just for the novelty and you are not having to part with a lot of money.Show less

Author: MEENA1012
Title: Nice Satay Celep
Review: Not crowded like other restaurant, fast & service. Taste of the satay gravy feels the same as other restaurant.  RM$1 cost each piece and my son also like the Angry Bird Yong Taufu .

Author: HO DKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Satay Celup
Review: Restaurant normally quite pack with diners yearning for satay celup. Surprising, its quite pricy to dine here.....also they have GST charges. Per stick of average size and all at same prices. The service OK as they have many staff. Not many of this sort of restaurant servicing this cuisine in Melaka. Another shop is downtown but that area is small.Show less

Author: Swee Hiang P
Title: Friendly Reception
Review: Satay celup, the original is here. You have to come early to be seated comfortably. The staff are friendly and even allow outside food. The food is delicious.

Author: WeeWeiYangMelaka, Malaysia
Title: Cheap Yet Good And Tasty
Review: Ban Lee Siang at Ong Kim Wee is the original branch for satay celup. Compare to Capitol satay celup, it's satay sauce is little watery. However with the price at 1 ringgit per stick, it's so much more affordable and you need not queue like crazy with its ample table. Parking is easier than Capitol as it is just in front of the establishment. When in melaka, try different places for their famous satay to suit your taste buds as everyone have its favourites. Overall rating is very fresh and good.Show less

Author: simono611Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Tasty and delicious
Review: Located at Jalan Ong Kim Wee in the very heart of Melaka nearby Jonker Street. A delicacy known as Sate Celup where by the base of the soup is made from peanuts and thick spicy gravy. Please be aware of a long queue before hand but due to the fast service you are able to get a place in no time. Show less

Author: lui_py86Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Dissapointment
Review: My husband and I was looking forward to have the satay celup of Malacca prior to our arrival in Malacca. But what a disappointment. The satay gravy is not the same anymore. It is terribly lacking in flavour and grounded peanuts. Service however was fast and efficient.Show less

Author: Sammy792Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Best Satay Celup in Malacca
Review: The boss and staff are friendly and fast to serve. We went for dinner at 6pm, the restaurant was almost fully seated and whoever came later in the evening have to queue for table.The satay celup are really delicious with plenty of varieties to choose. The essence is the sauce that make the stay celup taste even better.The restaurant will not replace, instead refill the sauce, hence the rule of thumb is the sauce is for you to cook and add to your plate, but not dip your satay celup after you have eaten partially or put in your mouth to ensure the hygiene for others. I would recommend you try the satay celup at this restaurant if you are visiting Malacca.Show less

Author: Ngan H
Title: Best satay celup in Melaka
Review: Truly recommended! You must try all the food-in-stick that are prepared for you. Nice to super nice. I especially like the "mengkuang" and "balled water spinach". Dipping them in satay sauce makes the taste even tastier! The quail eggs are also not to be missed. The restaurant can get crowded especially on weekends & public holidays. Try to eat in one of the weekday and you will see more locals eating there.Show less

Author: ThingYanTShah Alam, Malaysia
Title: It was above my expectation
Review: There are many satay celup restaurants in Melaka and this is really recommended by me. The sauce was above my expectation, YUMMY! If you love spicy, this is totally a house for you. I just love it. But you have to bear that the sauce will not be changed every after customer comes and goes. Some people who have weaker tummy should prepare some medicines in case it might upset your tummy to ruin your whole trip! So lucky my friends and I were all fine after eating there. So a big like from me! (Y)Show less

Author: Melanie_YeohSemenyih, Malaysia
Title: Unique Combination
Review: Have you tasted satay before? We usually dip satay in a bean- based sauce. So what Melaka people did is to combine steamboat with this sauce. Instead of a pot of hot soup, they substituted it with a pot of bean-based sauce. They skewered all the meat and veggie on bamboo sticks and dip these half- cooked sticks of food into the sauce and let it cook some more. Once it's cooked, you can eat it right away without having to add any other sauces. The sauce is nutty and slightly spicy and savory, it smells great and it tastes good. The pot is set on the centre of each table and everyone will dip their sticks in and wait for it to cook like what people normally do when they have steamboat. It's nice for big family and also picky guests, you cook what you want to eat only. Do come early as it's always packed.Show less

Author: BellaDearestMelaka, Malaysia
Title: My usual for Satay Celup
Review: The actual name is Ban Lee Siang, and there are two shops (they were once a single business but had a messy family feud so here we are with two). One is run by a couple and the other by the rest of the family. Been eating here for the last decade or so. I am from Melaka and have tried almost all the satay celup restaurants there are; by far this is the most consistent in taste.To those who are unfamiliar with Satay Celup, it basically is various surimi (fishballs, and other processed seafood), meat balls, pork, seafood and some vegetables that are on skewers then dipped in a thick spicy peanut sauce that's constantly brewing in the center of the table. For those who cannot handle the heat, just asked for a bowl of hot water to wash of the peanut sauce (parents used to do that when we were kids). IT IS A MUST TRY IF YOU ARE IN MELAKA :)Which one? Go either, it's difficult to say which is the best as they were originally from the same business. Try to go before 7pm and on the weekdays, as the weekends are too crowded to really enjoy the food.Show less

Author: FromKluang
Title: Normal food
Review:
The restaurant is very crowded during weekend and public holiday.
One of the famous restaurant in Melaka. The foods is just simple.
The environment is a bit warm. Can give a try if you never have Stay Celup before.
Only serve dinner no lunch.

Author: Ajith R
Title: Good food
Review:
Enjoy the food. Will go again. Easy to find . Staff friendly and speak English.
Could be cleaner .....................................

Author: al_review365Singapore, Singapore
Title: Satay celup in Melaka
Review: The restaurant is crowded even before 6pm for dinner. There are two shops next to each other, according to one of the owner, they used to be in partnership but now separated. The satay sauce and tastiness of the food at this place is over rated, tasted a lots better satay celup in the residential neighborhood near bachang and taman merdeka.Show less

Author: chong s
Title: Worth a try for satay celup
Review: It is crowd packed during holiday and weekend. Other days you can get a seat easily. The food is average, in fact I feel all the satay celup tasted more or less the same. Previously only has one Ban Lee Hiang. Then the brothers quarrel and separate out. They divided the shoplots into 2 with a gate in between. Both of them claimed their recipe were the original. In fact both have the similar taste. Thus No matter with shop u choose, it is the same type of satay celup. Show less

Author: Eric_loves_tripsSingapore, Singapore
Title: Better variety of menu items but dip can be better
Review: Read reviews on this shop and thot to have a try while visiting Melaka... The queue is not as Long as the other big C*** and they have more variety of menu items ... However feel that the sauce is not as flavourful ... Can be a good alternative in case you find the queue on the other side unbearable :)Show less

Author: shirleychau
Title: Very friendly service
Review: Good food, good service and owner is very helpful and friendly except the place is a bit warm, but will definitely go again.

Author: canberra421Singapore, Singapore
Title: Interesting experience for first timers
Review: We drove over from Aeon Melaka as the google map doesn't reflect a correct direction. Thus we spotted the branch first (only after our meal, we found the main branch further down the road). It was a rainy evening, thus when we reach the shop, it was not crowded.Eh we were a bit taken off by the idea of not changing the sauce, they simply add some more when the new customers take the table. So you can imagine how thick the peanut is at the bottom of the pot. Thus the staffs has to constantly go round the table and stir it so that the sauce doesn't burnt or the soup base can boil...anyway, there are fridge to store the food, some cooked ones on the far end of the 3 big fridge. Each stick is priced at RM0.90, so not too costly.. example, hotdog were sliced into 5mm thick and 3 pieces were placed on the stick, 2 rolled up kang kongs on the stick, 1 shelled prawn on the stick etc. The bacon were priced at RM5 per plate, consisting of 3 pieces. yes as one reviewer wrote, coke were cheaper than the plum/lime juice. btw, you could order plate of ketupat(rice) or cucumber to eat with your meal.Show less

Author: kingsguardRawang, Malaysia
Title: Not worth the fuss
Review: The queue maybe intimidating but largely due to tour buses groups. They come in droves, go in droves so if you are unluckily caught when they are visiting, wait a while. In 2015 Sept, they charge 90sen per stick so being a thrifty traveler with kids, I tried to be prudent. It was never my intention to eat until we are full so we just had about 20 sticks. 1 stick portion can be as little as 1 meatball so go figure.Hygiene-wise, ok...nothing to be shouted about or condemned, typical Malaysian eatery management. One word of caution, the water spinach is rolled into a fist and overcooking it will unroll it and create a mess. I made a mistake of undercooking it and spend 2 times that night in the toilet toiling.One unique feature here is instead of the regular peanut satay sauce, you have sesame seeds in place of the nuts. The spices were in the gravy which you can actually eat. Show less

Author: DougF895London, United Kingdom
Title: A must if visiting Melaka
Review: We were taken here by Malaysian friends and queued with friendly locals in the street to get an table in this busy restaurant, but well worth it.A novel experience sat around a boiling pot of satay on a table have way into the street being constantly refilled by the staff. You simple go up to the fridges select from a multitude of small dishes on skewers and drop them into the pot. Great food and way of eating with friends. At the end they simply count up the many skewers on your plate and it's amazing good value.Show less

Author: flhl82Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: hygiene is a BIG issue !!!
Review: We visit here with a group of friend at 5pm to avoid the crowd as we went there on Sunday. There is actually 2 similar shop next to each other but we pick this one. There are variety of food for u to choose and u also can add on the slice cucumber & bread in order to indulge with the satay sauce. The satay celup look like the normal steamboat ....here comes the problem ie. the hygiene !!! It doesn't bother us very much as we are friend BUT how about the others ? they don't change the gravy instead they add on and stir it all over again !!! Imagine from 5pm until the shop closed the same sauce is repeatedly used ....from the moment we start eating that issue floundering within my mind !!! The quality & value of the food was fine for me BUT i will not going back again simply because the hygiene is a BIG issue for me. It is the enthusiasm of my friend brought me here and there to try out Melaka local delicacy that render me not giving a terrible rating !!!Show less

Author: Jian Chen T
Title: It's just average if you had tried once
Review: Well,it would be a big shock experience for anyone who hasnt try satay celup before. The sauce is awesome, but the selection of sticks are like normal stuff. So you definitely have to try it if you never check it out!

Author: beeb9Pak Chong, Thailand
Title: New Premium Items
Review: Arrived at about 6pm for our dinner yesterday. Food choices, no changes from my previous visit in Jan this year. They just added a couple of premium item which I find it too pricy.My son took a squid and it cost RM4.50. A plate of bacon (3 slices) cost RM5. Other than that most item cost RM0.90 which is still acceptable.Another feedback, a glass of watermelon juice (quite diluted) cost RM2.80 while a can of coke cost RM2. hmm... I thought the coke should be more expensive.Show less

Author: VLKJSingapore, Singapore
Title: Interesting experience of eating food with the satay sauce
Review: The thing l like is the ability for a group to share one pot of satay sauce with yr choice food in the stick. There are 3 refrigerators of food selection and each stick is only RM0.90. The cons is that the satay sauce is not changed since the first customers using it!!!The satay is reused n new sauce is added to the old one and cook again!!!This practice is probably not accepted else where. Show less

Author: Jessica TJakarta, Indonesia
Title: considered the long queue, the food was just average
Review: It was a unique way to eat the satay by boiling it in peanut sauce. The satay taste is just so so, for it's just a variation of fish balls etc. The price was average but the queue was too much. we need to wait around 30 minutes to get a seat.Show less

Author: whatsupwhatsupwhatsuPerth, Australia
Title: Only average for me
Review: It really was only average, didn't live up to my expectations, but it wasn't bad. If you think RM0.90 per stick is cheap then you might be wrong given the size and portion of the food is small. A fishball for 90 cents? Two pork skins for 90 cents? A small prawn for 90 cents? Was it really worth it? I think not. Would I return? I probably will give it a miss.Show less

Author: biofreshKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Try Out of Curious- NOT BAD
Review: During my Family trip to Melaka we always heard that JLN ONG KIM WEE is a famous street for Satay Celup. We had not try before so we drove there after our Afternoon TEA in TBC. Not bad but hate most is TOO CROWDED. Maybe this is the reason it was famous. Waited about 15 minute and to me it is worth a wait. Good for those who love spices but to me it is so so. I still love the one in JONKER Streets. My boy love it most as he had many varieties for him to choose. Not bad for tourist as this is one of the attraction in this historical state of Malaysia. Give it a TRY!!!Show less

Author: Ssoong Y
Title: Good services and nice taste
Review: A lot of choices with all Of them are same price. Thus, it is quite worth when you take seafoods 😆😆 better go at 5pm and be the 1st one use the sauce 😋😋

Author: Kathleen_Leong
Title: Nice Sauce
Review: Love the satay sauce and there are many variety food to choose and go with the saty sauce. THere are long Q after 5.30 pm. Good to go there by 5 pm if you do not want to wait. Worth a try!

Author: jesuistinaTaipei, Taiwan
Title: Restaurant name should be "Ban Lee Siang"
Review: OK! it's a must try in Melaka. The celup has strong flavor made of Sate/peanut/dried fish and smells yummy.A very wide variety of food in refrig will make you feel excited. You can also find pork in the refrig because it's from China. Almost every customer is Asian. As a Taiwanese, calories of the sauce is too to try it twice. :)We paid RM55 for four people, so I think the avg consumed amount in this restaurant is not high. Note: Most of restaurant is off on Monday, double confirm availability via phone before your visit.每串都一樣價錢但是山葵鑲肉最好吃Show less

Author: FrancescaU535Singapore, Singapore
Title: Good, not great
Review: Heard a lot about Melaka's famous satay celup, so just had to try it. Plenty of variety of fresh ingredients such as meat balls, prawns, fish balls, kangkung, tau kee etc to choose from. The satay taste is quite mild and the only thing that enhanced the taste was the prawns. The home made drinks were nice especially the Liang Teh and sour plum drink. Overall, a different experience to eat lok lok boiled in satay sauce. Go for the experience, once for me is enough. Show less

Author: SingaporeRon
Title: Our preferred choice
Review: We like coming here cos the 2 shops have good food & sauces & reasonably clean. It helps that the numerous customers ensure good turnover that promotes fresher food selection.

Author: drag0nb0iSingapore, Singapore
Title: Awesome food and prompt service
Review: Was on a family road trip to Malacca and first stop for dinner was Satay Celup at Ban Lee Hiang. As we were early, seats were plenty and parking was`t too difficult to find. As i was traveling with my wheelchair bound brother, the stuff quickly gave us a table nearer to the walk way and helped me carry the wheelchair over the steps. Selection of food was good, although their selection of drinks can be better. Its a must when you visit Malacca. Crowd start pouring in slightly after 6pm and the whole place was packed! So do be early if you are planning for dinner.Show less

Author: sheronlee
Title: The best satay celup
Review: This shop provides  the  best satay  celup in Malacca. The gravy is thick,  nutty and spicy. The staff constantly add pounded nuts and sauce to the  gravy.

Author: yeauejenJohor Bahru, Malaysia
Title: You've never been to Melaka unless you've tried this!
Review: Came here about 2 days before Chinese New Year. There are two shops of the same name just side-by-side (We went into the one on the right). Heard that both shops, despite the same name, were run by two different people and use different sauces. Food items are charged at RM0.80 per stick. The spicy satay sauce is superb. Food items are of great variety and very fresh. Some food items may not seem worthy at that price (such as mushroom), but there are some that certainly worth the price (such as bak kwa, meat skewer, etc.). Staff were very attentive, and overall service greatly exceeded our expectations. Will definitely visit it again in the future. Heard that there may very, very long queues on weekends.Show less

Author: Jess218
Title: Worth a try
Review: Went there with a group of friend at around 6pm. But only spend about 10minutes waiting for a table that can suit 9 of us. Lots of variety and vege are fresh too. The gravy is awesome, just that they only refill instead of replacing a new one for every customer. Something to share is that, try not to dig ur food in immediately after u get your seat. At least wait for the gravy to boil a while before putting ur stick in.Show less

Author: TeeCheeSengSingapore, Singapore
Title: Satay celup
Review: As what we learn from the hotel staff who introduce us to go there instead of Capitol satay celup due to long queue, there are 2 shop with same name next to each other due to the 2 brothers had dispute that why they are separated.We tried the one with red coloured gate. The taste is good but due to business is too good, they didn't change the satay gravy for the new customer, they only refill the satay gravy.Show less

Nicely tucked in a quiet corner near the touristy zone. Can get a lil crowded though. My 2-year-old daughter had her very first stick of satay here and immediately fell in love with it. :) Show less

Author: Ashley S

heard a lot of good reviews abt this place, went n tried it

limited choices compare to the other famous shop.

prices are cheap, BUT other than that, the lack of choices is really a letdown

Author: Surendaran CKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Good food but limited choices

Tried the one that is on 45E. The run down looking place. The food selection here is not much. The price is about Rm0.80 per stick. I tried several items and find the items on a stick was a bit too little. The gravy sauce was just fine. I find it abit annoying that they just come and stir my pot without asking anything. Some of the food just falls out the stick and drowns in the sauce. And this later will be discovered by the next guest. LOL!!.Show less

Author: Lalat79Kuching, Malaysia
Title: The same good taste for more than a decade
Review: Been more than a decade I've been to this shop. Mind u. It started with one shop, later expanded to two shop side by side and later unfortunately some internal family dispute ( I heard) separated the two side by side shop selling the same thing with a grill in between ha... Still the same good old taste of spicy peanut sauce for dipping of assortment of satay-styled vege, meat..... I still love it.... Come try.Show less

Author: SmileForYouChatswood, Australia
Title: Isn't this supposed to be Ban Lee SIANG?
Review: We went here for dinner after walking around Jonker Walk with my husband. Place is recommended to me by a Malaccan acquaintance. It is located in the outskirts of Jonker Walk and takes about 10minutes to reach the place by foot. However, when we went there, we were directed to the longer route and took us about 15-20minutes to reach the place and I was sweating buckets! The place isn't air conditioned btw so prepare to keep yourself hydrated if you'll be eating here during daytime. It was my first time to eat satay celup and I'm only familiar with the traditional satay, and I was expecting something similar to it. But it was more of skewered yong tau foo stuff that you have to cook in peanut sauce. Hubby and I both agree that food was worth the long walk that we did. Since me and my husband were walking for the whole day, we weren't surprised that we ate so much! I just wish that they have more fans around as I was sweating profusely while eating. Oh and don't expect much on the service, just enjoy the food ;)Show less

Author: FeraEs
Title: good cheap satay
Review:

We had 24 pieces and 2 drinks for 22 RM.

Author: dogtrekKuala Lumpur

The ingredients are mainly processed meat/fish pieces skewered.. the taste of blended peanuts and pineapple is overpowering, the place is hot and sticky.. Just not to my taste..Show less

The one on the left is generally busier. Both are clean with good speedy service.If you are hankering for some satay celup and don't want to wait in line do give this place a try.Show less

Author: Karynn-YH-TanKuala Lumpur, Malaysia

Review: It's not bad but it's not super good either. The boiling sauce was alright, but the seafood was not all fresh. The processed meats like fishballs and all are ok but fresh seafood could be better.At least we didn't have to queue miles long like at Capitol.Show less

Author: souchyfamilySunbury, Australia

Staff had limited English and tried to help with what was in the fridge, but after a few sticks you don't really care as long as it tastes good. Worth the experience.Show less

Author: NeeNee_ChoPenang
Title: First timer
