We arrived at around 7pm on Monday evening, even though there is no queue but the restaurant is still fully occupied. Easy rule to follow, every stick count at 80 cents and there are quite a big variety of choices. The satay sauce is not so spicy so that we can eat more. For people like me who hate long queue, this restaurant can be an alternative choice.Show less

Author: YukieLily
Title: Best satay celup
Review:
The best satay celup in town.
My piece of advice, should celup with their "yao tiao" which goes best with their gravy.
Best combination ever.

Author: PinkyJane88
Title: Be early to avoid the Q
Review: Worth a try but not worth the queue. If u are early, u might not need to wait but if you are late, u gonna cry for the wait. Nice boss and lady boss. However, it's just normal satay celup, nothing to brag about.

Author: Andrew KSingapore, Singapore
Title: So So Satay Celup
Review: This coffee shop style makan place serving Satay Celup was packed with young adults when we visited it about 5:00pm. It's kinda of dangerous dining there if you think about all those rubber hoses piping out from LPG cylinders lying on the floor in between the tables...you could accidentally tripped on it and burst one of the LPG hose. The Satay Celup here is done quite differently from the Singapore version, instead of dipping the skewered food in the hot boiling pot to cook then in the Satay sauce/gravy for dressing...you dipped the skewered food directly into a pot of boiling hot satay gravy. Just don't sit down for your meal immediately after the table has been cleared from a previous dining by other customers. Some customers maybe turned off by the pot of satay gravy which matter of fact is recycled and topped up for the next customer...just enjoy the local flavour and not to think too much about the previous customer table etiquette while dining. Good dining experience if you have not tried Malacca Satay Celup before.Show less

Author: wakeupcall_07
Title: No complaints
Review: N complaints about the freshness and the taste of the sauce. Did not have too queue for more than 5mins - I arrived at 6pm. I went to the shop on the left

Author: Setay168
Title: Very good satay cellup!!
Review: First time having satay cellup..very yummy!!  I wish they can sell the satay sauce :)  You need to be early before the crowd forms. Price is reasonable!!

Author: Cammal_BrownBoyKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: You should try, at least once!
Review: "You should try satay celup!" That is what my Melaka friends have been telling me all this while. So we wanted to go to Capitol satay celup but diverted to Ban Lee Hiang due to heavy traffic. According to my friends, the outlet on the left is the original one. Apparently one has to queue to eat here but our luck was good on that day as we managed to get a table in few minutes time. You have to choose you own ‘satays’ from the chiller. You can choose from a wide selection of fish balls, sausages, fresh seafood, cockles, vegetables etc. Best to take as many as you can consume first, if you want more then get refills. The price of each of the satay is counted based on the number of stick it has ie each stick is RM0.60. Similar to ‘lok-lok’, you will be cooking those items which you have taken in the pot of peanut gravy. If you want it spicier, you can add the chili flakes placed on the table. Overall I would say it is average. I like the idea of cooking your own food and eat it while it’s hot. I do not like the gravy as doesn’t suit to my liking. Some says the Capitol is nicer as they have thicker gravy and tastier. I wouldn’t know that until I try it the next time I am in Melaka.Show less

Author: tmark338
Title: Satay Celup
Review: Opposite hotel. Very special local delight. Apparently this is the original satay celup store. Cheap and good. But crowded so must wait if you go late

Author: hongwii
Title: One of the good satay celup
Review: Although not the best satay celup in melaka, it is one of the choice when u come to melaka. try to eat the Red sign board one. the sauce is more spicier.

Author: TraveleddictSingapore, Singapore
Title: Choose the white signboard stall
Review: There are 2 Ban Lee Hiang side by side, heard is because the 2 brothers owner split because of some family issue. But we went to the shop with white signboard, recommended by local. Good service and great gravy, they charge by per stick so try to control. You can always take more after that, do be there early before 630pm especially on weekends. They opens around 5pmShow less

Author: NuttyCheeseSingapore, Singapore
Title: Watery sauces.. novel experience only
Review: We didn't have to queue as we got there around 5pm, and the place was already getting crowded.The variety is very good, with lots of different satay skewers to choose from. But everything we cooked in the satay sauce just didn't taste that great. We found the sauce too watery and we couldn't really taste the sauce much. We did stir the sauce up, but that didn't help at all.We ate less than 20 skewers (RM 0.60 per stick) and were out of that place in 20 minutes, probably the quickest table to vacate that evening.It's an interesting experience, but not for the food.Show less

Author: MissAdriennely
Title: Not bad
Review: Not bad if you like satay celup (I don't). As compared to Capitol,you do not have to wait an hour for a table here and the sticks are only RM0.60/stick.

Author: Elena WSingapore, Singapore
Title: Satay Celup!!! Sedap!!!
Review: We tried the one on the right hand side as it looked slightly "cleaner". Had plenty of variety of seafood and meat at RM0.60 / stick. Satay sauce was pretty alright with a bit of spiciness.Satay Celup basically is satay steamboat, naturally they don't replace the pot of satay that will cook the satay pieces. Well, unless you are a hygiene freak, you do not mind the sharing of satay sauce with other patrons, it will be pretty good to have it if you visit Malacca.I particularly like the Otah here =)Show less

Author: JoanLee88
Title: Not so clouded
Review: I come here with my friends. The place here not so clouded. So, I can enjoy the satay at Rm0.60 each~~

Author: Dylan1980
Title: must try
Review: a food that u must try when you're in melaka, kind of oily (might be not suitable for people who prefers hygience cause the broth /sauce were been used over & over by different patrons

Author: ECKLKualaLumpurKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Less is More Part 49 - Worst of Melaka
Review: I am actually dumbfounded that this street food is so popular (and actually famous?) here in Melaka. There is indeed a plethora of other wonderful street foods to celebrate in this historical city BUT satay celup?!? Apparently it isn't something even several Melakan friends want to be associated with. These pair of identically-named shops belong to squabbling siblings NW of Jonker (according to a local) is less touristy and more favored by Melakans.At midnite on a Saturday, both establishments are still packed with people still queuing for tables. (Surely there must be something better to eat at this hour?) There is no service so hover near any table which looks like the people there are finishing off their meal. Once seated, you may have to signal for a someone to clean off the inevitable mess left behind by the previous patrons. There is a hotpot built into the center of the table where you "cook" your skewers of seafood and other meats. The hotpot is filled with (here lies the big difference) a thick concoction of spicy, greasy curried peanut sauce instead of the customary boiling water/soup stock. Hence you are literally cooking your meal in your dipping sauce - a somewhat innovative (lazyman) approach?While all this so far may still sound fairly acceptable, the BIGGEST PROBLEM is that the hotpot of hotsauce is NEVER replaced but merely topped up with more "fresh" sauce. While "hotpot etiquette" dictates NO double dipping, there are no guarantees here. Our "personal" pot which presumably had been simmering continuously all night, had the consistency and appearance of bubbling molten lava. Please watch out for scalding splatters of hot oil! Since it is all self service here, we selected our skewers arranged in plastic baskets inside a bank of refrigerators. None of the skewers of assorted fishballs, meatballs, tofu, sausages, seafood was remarkable. Perhaps it is the entertainment value (fun factor) that keeps some people coming back - it certainly isn't the taste nor food value for this reviewer.Show less

Author: LimbbatokSingapore, Singapore
Title: Poor hygiene. Eat at your own risk!
Review: Took our party of 4 a while to locate the premise when we left Jonker's Walk. Upon arriving, we were dismayed at the crowded and unhygienic conditions.We were seated at what was obviously used to be a kitchen area converted into another dining hall. As soon, we had to make through the now smaller than usual kitchen areas. We can see the manner in which the kitchen helpers prepared the food and I already filled like walking out. What took the cake was that we were led to a dirty recently vacated table. The helper proceeded to wipe the table of the satay gravy. In the middle sat a pot of half filled gravy sauce, obviously left overs by the previous occupants. The kitchen helper then simply lit the fire and pour more gravy into the existing one in the pot. When we ask for a new pot, he flatly refused saying that this was the standard practice.I wanted to walk out, but my brother in law wanted to try; particularly having walked quite a distance to locate the place.Let's just say I hardly touch the food. This contravenes basic food hygiene and is really a poor business model. I just can't imagine dipping into the same sauce left behind by don't know how many other occupants before us. I wouldn't mind paying more if they bother to observe simple food hygiene. Shocking!Show less

Author: MagteMalaysia
Title: Food definitely at par with Capitol but cheaper, better ambience and less queue
Review: Why go to Capitol Satay Celup when most Malaccan locals come here to enjoy their food? Slightly further from Jonker Street (located on the same road as HSBC). In my opinion, Capitol caters more for tourist customers. Price wise it is so much more reasonable at RM0.60/stick vs RM0.80/stick. You still get the same food such as fish balls, sausages and so on. The peanut gravy tasted average and slightly more spicier compared to Capitol. Don't have to really wait long for a table. There are plenty of car parks at the opposite of the restaurant.However currently there are 2 restaurants by the same name competing each other. Don't be fooled that it is the same establishment side by side. The original owner (Restoran Ban Lee Siang - left hand side) and the competitor (Kedai Makanan & Minuman Ban Lee Siang - right hand side). The competitor is actually the former staff of the original owner. The former staff learnt all the satay sauce recipes and decided to start his own business. I would say both are equally as good. Competition is healthy so the price will remain the same for a while.Show less

Author: otyewSubang Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Nice satay celup but....
Review: Well this restaurant is growing since yrs ago. It wasnt the best either but wasnt bad too. The problem is that the sauce was not replaced all the time, so hygenic wise....if you dont mind, it is still ok. As compare with Capitol, the sauce is a bit spicier but not as thich as Capitol. For some, me especially...I think Ban Lee Hiang is more worth it compare to Capitol.Show less

Author: mostlyharmlessSingapore, Singapore
Title: Satay celup without the queue
Review: Having been to Melaka twice, and both times witnessing the tremendously l-o-n-g queue outside Capitol Satay (*nothing* can be worth queuing for 1 hour!), we decided to try this place on Jalan Ong Kim Wee. We drove - it's a little way out from the historic town centre. Arriving at 615 am, most of the tables were taken.. but at least there wasn't a queue. Food on skewer's is placed in self-service refrigerators. The sauce is served in a ever bubbling pot placed in the centre of the table, and you dunk in the skewered tit-bits. A reasonable variety of food, with most sticks at standard price. Some food choices felt like less value than others.. Ambience was noisy, and it was sometimes congested around the fridge area. The sauce was nutty, with spicy notes. It was less rich and creamy than traditional satay sauce. Overall, we enjoyed the experience and the bill came to RM$60 for four adults.The sauce is definitely recycled between diners. However, having said which, as it's continuously boiling throughout, there aren't any microbial issues - it's just a matter of the "yuck" factor.Not having ever made it to Capitol Satay, I can't compare it to the ever popular standard - some blogs say the variety and size of the skewers is better at Capitol. But for me - the lack of a queue is the main selling point!Show less

Author: g0_f0r_itSingapore, Singapore
Title: plenty of locals having their satay celup here
Review: Having read some negative reviews about Capitol Satay, and not wishing to queue and and fight with the crowd, we decided to try satay celup here. There were many locals eating here. Next door is Teow Chew Satay Celup, which, for whatever reason, had not a single customer while we were there. Most sticks cost 0.50RM each while some cost 0.60RM. At the end of the meal, the sticks were counted in front of us. Overall, a good experience if you wish to try the local satay celup. The restaurant is located along Jalan Ong Kim Wee, which is a one-way street.Show less

Author: whiterose39Sri Kembangan, Malaysia
Title: NOTHING TO SHOUT ABOUT
Review: I told my family about the dinner area in the Portuguese Settlement and we decided to visit there for our Christmas Dinner. We had wait for a bit for them to prepare the table for us. We than orderd Fried rice, Baked fish, Squid Fritters, Kangkung belacan, Kailan, Chicken Debal Curry and drinks. We had to wait a bit, we asked them how long would it take to get our food. The lady said "if we are patient, we would get nice food" now i dont think its a proper way to answer your customer. the Baked fish was not very fresh, tasted like mud. Squid Fritters was okay and that was the only thing on the menu for kids, as we had 2 children with us.Kangkung belacan was normal too. Debal Curry chicken also was not that great, they gave us more potatoes and gravy and not much chicken. We wanted some hot drinks and they said it was not available at all which was quite disappointing. Now when we finished, we realized that our Kailan never arrived. We called for the bill and the boss came and to collect our money, as we went through the bill with him, we told him we never got the Kailan, at that moment he asked us "Do you want the Kailan now" ??? We had finished our Dinner what are we going to do with the Kailan, utter nonsense la. As we were walking away, new customers came in and were seated, the lady boss was asking away to one of the waiters for hot drinks to be served, how come they could get hot drinks and we couldnt get it. Quite unfair service. While eating the baked fish, i got a bone that got stuck in my throat and started coughing, my brother in law immediately ran to the lady boss to ask for some rice, knowing quite well my situation, she took her own sweet time to get the rice for me.....haizzzz dont want to say about your service la. You are busy trying to serve Portuguese food, but have lost quality of real portuguese food.Show less

Author: yiliyuli
Title: Best thing is the juice
Review: We visit every time we go to Malacca.  Funny enough the thing we miss the most wasn't the food, but their mango juice.   Best not to go during festive season as it's a terrible wait. Other than that, it's nice to chill.

Author: dwinty123Cambridge, United Kingdom
Title: A Scallop Like No Other
Review: The Portuguese settlement is a place like no other I've been, but if one place embodies the familial, lighthearted and culinarily expert nature of the 2,500 people living there, it is Monterios. We went to try the mysterious Debal Curry (which you have to ask for) and we left eight hours later, supremely spoiled on spicy and flavourful Debal, rich and scrumptious dry butter prawns, and garlic and butter scallops that were dropped on our table straight from heaven. I am not normally a scallop enthusiast. Thankfully a divine voice in my subconscious implored me to order them. I'm ever so grateful. After finishing our unparalleled meal we were lucky enough to join Janet and friends for a chat; so wonderful the company we stayed for many more hours. I wish we'd have stayed for many more. Thank you Monterios for a remarkable meal and a remarkable evening!Show less

Author: goh_ginnySingapore, Singapore
Title: Good food and value for money but be prepared to wait
Review: We came here for dinner on a saturday night as part of a big group of a few tables. The staff are friendly but there is only one cook so be prepared to wait for your food. Time from reaching the place (we booked beforehand) till finishing our food was about 2.5hrs. Show less

Author: hazinheiraSingapore, Singapore
Title: Flavourful food, but only remotely portuguese-inspired
Review: The cooking style is not Portuguese, but we nevertheless enjoyed the food. We had the water spinach, fried rice and clams. We found that the spices overpowered the flavour of the clams and that we should have ordered them less spicy. We sat in the courtyard outside – the setting is simple but clean, and prices are very affordable.The staff speaks English.Show less

Author: JoakimD
Title: Great value for money
Review: Great seafood and great value for money. We had plenty of clams, prawns, calamari and a baked fish for 200 RM (4 pax)

Author: aishwariyah
Title: Terrible Experience
Review: These people ruined our Xmas eve dinner. We were made to wait for 1.5hrs for our food. We did not make a fuss as it was the eve of Christmas and the place was busy but what put us off was that these people were unreasonably rude and arrogant. We were told after 60mins that the chef can only go "table by table" and there were 4 more tables to be served before us. I asked if they could just serve us 3 bowls of plain rice and 1 simple vege dish so the children could start eating first while we wait but was very rudely told off by the lady who runs the place that she cannot "disturb" her chef. We carried on waiting patiently and after 1.5 hrs we realised that the 4 tables before ours were not served yet and we decided to leave. I made my way to the cashier to pay for the soft drinks we had ordered earlier and the man at the counter ,also someone who runs the place, was unhappy that we were leaving. He held on to my 50 ringgit note and refused to give me my change until we gave him an explanation about why we were leaving. We were then told that they only had 1 chef. I then told them that they should downsize and not try to serve more than 25 or 30 tables at a go with just 1 chef in the kitchen. The rude lady then came up to us and simply rolled her eyes and walked away when she learnt that we were cancelling our order.This place deserves no rating or good reviews. A food business that treats their customers so badly should not be supported at all.Show less

Author: imagine6572Balmain, Australia
Title: This family run restaurant has great hospitality and delicious food
Review: Janet and Helen the owners/hosts/cooks are lovely and will put together a selection of dishes to suit you. We visited as a large group (4 tables) and all the dishes were consistently good. A special treat in the Portugese Settlement precincy at Christmas-time are the Christmas lights and carolers on the weekend.Show less

Author: josefklng
Title: Fantastic Portuguese Seafood
Review: Tasty seafood I'd ever had. Recommend creamy crab added with salty egg and fried clams with garlic and ginger. Don't forget to order morning glory and you can appreciate the difference between the same dish usually available in Thailand. Blended lime with plum is a good choice for cold drink. The only disappointment is that the chef (Janet or Helen?) was unwilling to disclose the recipe of any of her dishes to my wife who enjoys cooking food merely for the consumption of the family.Show less

Author: SunnySussex21Brighton, United Kingdom
Title: Melaka visit.
Review: We were being hassled by the staff in the nearby food court so decided to find a meal somewhere else . Luckily we found this delightful place nearby . Basic surroundings but lovely to sit unded the stars. This family run restaurant is clean, friendly and well run with flavoursome fish dishes at a very reasonable price . The family I visited with spoke highly of the chilli crab .Show less

Author: TanM458Singapore, Singapore
Title: Best Seafood Meal Ever!!
Review: I chance upon this place a few years ago and the food was good. After 3 years we decided to make a trip to Melaka for this seafood feast again! The food is simply fantastic!! We went all out and ordered Fried butter prawns, baked scallops, garlic ginger clams, stir fry balachan kangkong, crispy squid, crabs done 2-ways, salted egg and chili crab; the salted egg crab was the bomb!! All of that for just 5 of us!Our forks just zoomed in to every dish, we forgot to take photos of them! The meal was soooo good and it was worth every cent!! If we could lick the plates, we would ;p Price is extremely reasonable!! The service was great with smiles that added the warm to the meal!! Definitely will go again if we return to Melaka!!Show less

Author: peinit2015
Title: Nice place to date
Review: I’ll come back again. The boss is very friendly while the food is really nice like the others recommended. This restaurant is like perfect. Halal food.

Author: CelineCleeMelaka, Malaysia
Title: Super wonderful dinner
Review: Me and hubby decided to try seafood for dinner, drop by Portuguese settlement at Ujung pasir, we decided to stop by Monterious seafood restaurant, the seafood was stunningly wonderful, we had pepper crab, fish, garlic lala & vege! Oh and not forgetting the devils curry! the devils curry was super wonderful i can't forget it. We are planning to have our dinner again here this weekend!Wish all population of Malacca & the world come visit this restaurant to try the authentic taste of Portuguese dishes!Show less

Author: jacqqqNCL / KUL
Title: Thanks Helen
Review: No encounter of any hassle as we entered the Portuguese Square. We got dropped off at the car park behind the statue of Christ. No aggressive touts whatsoever.Found Monterio easily. It was to be a very fishy evening for us. Scallops, grill fish, dry butter prawns and a vegetable dish. Simple but delicious.Helen who tended to us was wonderful. Not altogether cheap but a very enjoyable meal nonetheless.Show less

Author: greenham01San Jose, California
Title: Unpretentious but good food, friendly service, good value
Review: We have not had "Devil's curry" for the longest while (like for 30 years) and made it a point to look for it when we were in Melaka recently. We decided on Monterios for dinner and luckily we called up to make reservations and to confirm if they had that dish. Turned out, they only serve Devil's curry on the weekends, and it was a Tuesday when we called. However, the lady was so nice to make an exception and went out of her way to cook the dish for us! What a nice gesture!Besides the curry, we had their 3 flavored fried fish (very fresh and flavorful), clams, crabs, and vegetables. All the dishes were very tasty, and delicious - the Devil's curry was excellent and very memorable, and so it will now be the new standard for the latest memory of this dish - hopefully not another 30 years before we get to eat it again!As mentioned, service was very helpful and friendly, great recommendations for what to eat, reasonable prices.Show less

Author: GloriaSomeHobart, Australia
Title: Superb meal and very friendly service
Review: We walked to Monterios from our hotel and we were the only people there at the time so we had a lovely chat with Janet, one of the owners and also the chef. We had a drink - a beer and a beautiful lemon drink with sour plum, highly recommended, and then ordered butter prawns, chilli squid, garlic clams, kangkung and chilli fried rice. When it all came out we thought we would never eat even half but in a fairly short space of time we managed to eat virtually everything! The food was magnificent, fresh, flavoursome and clearly cooked with great love. It was really pleasant sitting watching the passers by and also hearing the mass at the local church commencing, it really added to the whole village atmosphere. I would heartily recommend Monterios, I hope we get to visit again.Show less

Author: Mattjack8Singapore, Singapore
Title: Dinner with Parents on road trip
Review: This is a nice change from the hectic hawker center round the corner run by an extended family who genuinely care about your meal and are careful to not over spice the food for European tourists. Good seafood basic surroundings and sea air .... Highly recommended its a 15 minute walk and 30 years from the new Hilton Hotel. Show less

Author: travelman020
Title: Tasty, but not so special.
Review: Fresh seafood flavours and a good kway teow with friendly, attentive service. But not special enough to bring you out of town. Clean and tidy, but location is tired and down at heel.

Author: Rajeshwary
Title: Yummy!!!
Review: The food was very tasty and just divine ... the butter prawns was soooooooooo good ... a must try and the garlic Lala just wow ... and the otak otak OMG!!! To top it off great service !!!

Author: travelbug_July1968Singapore, Singapore
Title: Did not live up to expectations
Review: We went for dinner here in the Portuguese settlement given the good reviews. While the service was good and staff friendly and seafood fresh, I have to say that we were very disappointed with the flavours. Overpowering use of spices, pastes and butter / oil which ruins the taste of the dish. We would have been better off eating at the stall at the neighbouring food court recommended by our driver I think.Show less

Author: ilovetravelling123india
Title: Awesome Portuguese food
Review: Awesome food. The butter garlic prawns, chilli grab were awesome. The baked otak otak fish was a complete surprise as it was out of the world. Just loved every thing. The lovely lady helen served us with great love and it was a beautiful evening spent well.Show less

Author: shuyi c
Title: Good service and nice food
Review: A very peaceful place to having our dinner and the host is welcome for our arrival. The food is nice and price is reasonable. Although the prawn not so fresh but it is acceptable. Highly recommended.

Author: mandya162Singapore, null, Singapore
Title: finger licking
Review: loved the food. the restaurant is no-frills and is in the portuguese settlement. it is run by three sisters and one of their husbands. we met two of the four - very personable. had to wait a looonnnngg time for our food but couldn't really carp given the apologetic-ness and explaining-ness of the owners. in the end it was well worth the wait. we didn't mind because it's in the open (with a roof), close enough to the sea to feel (or imagine you feel) the sea breeze, and the music (owners' selection) was delightful (mostly old 70s hits). we ordered chili crab, black pepper crab, baked portuguese fish and stir fried, assorted veggies. the last were the best stir fried veggies i've ever eaten anywhere. each dish was delectable. the baked fish was swimming in oil and we almost felt like we had to dig and delve to get to the fish. that apart, it was all good.Show less

Author: rubenesk
Title: One word to cover it all. Excellence.
Review: Great food, great service, great ambiance, affordable pricing. What more could one ask for? Keep it up sisters and family.

Author: 875rajag
Title: Super Portuguese!
Review: A group of 10 of us had dinner and tried a variety of their dishes ranging from two types of crab preparation (pepper and salted egg), two types of fish (Pomfret with Garlic and butter) and the red snapper with sweet and sour sauce, chicken curry t, the fish cake(yummy), and so on. The atmosphere (oldies music) and the food was excellent. A beautiful team of sisters working hard to keep the Portuguese tradition alive! Well done all around..!Show less

Author: TzargalahadKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Monterios' Food Are Delicious and Good Value!
Review: A family dinner suggested by a cousin. Decided to give it a try since we are in Melaka. Why not try it's historical dish of Portugese descend?It was clean environment. The food was delicious. We order the stingray Portugese dish and jenahak garlic steam fish, butter prawn, kangkong belacan, lala dish and a round of drinks.The food is reasonable and delectable. All in all cost us less than RM200.00 for a meal for 6.The owners are friendly and welcoming. Special thanks to Danny for his hospitality. Will definitely bring our family again on our next visit. Good food Monterios sisters! Show less

Author: KH_LyeKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Authentic Portugese Seafood with Gerat Service
Review: We sought this out amidst all the other restaurants / stalls given its high reviews and it exceeded our expectations. The service is very friendly and has a family feel (we think the waiting and serving staff are family members). The proprietor, Janet, came over to say hello and told us she will personally cook herself for us. Her sister took our order and made fine recommendations. MUST try: Butter Garlic Scallops and Garlic Ginger La La - freshest seafood, fantastic gravy and so memorable ... savour them! The steamed Otak Otak was equally great - so smooth and delicious. Kangkung Belacan - nice but very spicy. Baked Fish with Special Portugese Sause - very fresh fish but the spicy sauce was too much for us - so fiery it was a fitting end to the gastronomy delight. Ice water was free flow and so was the rice. When the bill came we could not believe the great value for money. Highly recommended. Tip: for those not used to spiciness, ask to tone down the fieriness, and eat the non-spicy dishes first (before your taste buds get overwhelmed).Show less

Author: teh s
Title: Portuguese fare
Review: We visited this place based on reviews. It is nestled in the Portuguese settlement. We have very interesting glimpses of the houses beautifully decorated for Christmas on the way there. As for the restaurant, am quite disappointed despite the rating. We ordered their specialty. Was wrongly served the baked fish. Only realised when the actual baked fish came when we had already done with our meal. The proprietor who is also the cook then kind of berated us for not telling them beforehand about the wrong order. No sincere apology given and we were also billed quite exorbitantly for the wrong order. Anyway, that aside, we felt the meal is also so so. The fish was not fresh and generally the cooking is home styled. Ok for a simple meal out but that is about it. Show less

Author: Alex_Singapore_15Singapore, Singapore
Title: Portuguese Seafood
Review: Place is easy to find via Google Map. Restaurant opens at 5.30pm. Ordered, Fried Rice - Small portion, serves 3 pax. Chilli crab - Crab very fresh and spicy Baby Kai Lan - Though small portion, the serving is for 4 paxButter Scallop - Very fresh and niceThe price is reasonable and will come againShow less

Author: AugustineA68
Title: Seafood
Review: No words to describe friendly and best food in malacca.. the exterior is not indication of the food... a place not to be missed.

Author: Siraj29
Title: An awesome restaurant
Review: Good food, good service, good price, perfect!!! Great place for a family dinner, good variety of seafood and dishes.

Author: Mohamed IKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Re-visit with outsiders
Review: This time we brought along visitors from Sarawak with us.Dishes ordered were buttered garlic prawns, squid fritters, baked otak-otak, kailan and bean sprouts. No salted crab as our guests don't take crab...and the prawns. What a miss!They commented the food was good and they were surely satisfied, seeing the rice re-fills they had through the dinner.A speciality on the drinks are the juices, really among the best I have had for dinner.Show less

Author: 56natliet
Title: Exceeded our expectations. Thumbs up!
Review: We ordered 2 crabs. Delicious! One of the best butter crabs I've tried. Finished almost one whole crab by myself! And the service is fantastic! Friendly people. Price is good too. A bit hot of where we sit, but overall is excellent :)

Author: kiwi-traveller-PS
Title: It was so good we went again
Review:
So much better than eating around jonkers!

Only a Myr5 taxi ride away to get simple seafood done well - very tasty and reasonable prices - great service - the 3 sisters will look after you

Highly recommend

Author: Stajin
Title: Excellent
Review:
Excellent food, good price, friendly service. Crabs were good size and cooked well
Really no complaints or issues other than maybe I wish there was a better view/location? Definitely would return here !

Author: Melissa zKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Delicious Meal
Review: It is located in a square that has many other restaurants nearby. The restaurant is quaint facing a disused stage which I guessed at one point, held dances or the likes. But the highlight are the food. There are three sisters and we spoke to the one who prepared the food. We especially requested the meals to be non-spicy with zero chillies because we had young kids who were sensitive to overly spicy dishes. And oh, my, lord, those buttered oysters were divine. The clams were delicious that my not so curious daughter thinks it is yummy. The chicken were also pretty good. The fried rice was also absolutely nice. And our baked Portuguese fish was also had a sufficient oomph. Only thing that startled us were the squid. It was hard for my husband and I to appreciate a dish where the sambal overwhelmed our taste buds. Were we impressed? Yes, we were. If we weren't living so far away, we would go here for a weekly basis.Show less

Author: ChristopherC4640
Title: Surprisingly good food, great service, nice people
Review: We decided to get away from the city for a few days and headed out to Malacca. Going to the Portuguese Square was something of an accident. After viewing the long queues at the more popular Chinese seafood restaurants, we gave up and decided to take a longer drive. I must say that it was probably the best decision we made the whole day. At first glance, the Portuguese square is looking rather run down. it is no longer the tourist attraction it once was with nightly cultural dances etc. But it was cool and windy, not crowded or busy...exactly what I was looking for.Monterios is a small, family run restaurant directly opposite the large stage. We found the people to be pleasant and friendly. It is apparently run by three sisters, and as they prepare all the dishes, they could make the best recommendations based on the quality of produce that they received. I decided to trust their recommendations and never regretted it. The cooking was very good, quality of produce was excellent. It was probably the best meal I had throughout the entire few days we spent at Malacca. In fact, we enjoyed it so much, the wife and I are thinking of another over-nighter with the kids again soon.Good food itself is not enough to make for an enjoyable evening. The simplicity of the setting was more than offset by the warmth exuded by the family as we were greeted more like old friends than customers.Show less

Author: IvanT2882
Title: Seafood restaurant
Review: They serve the best seafood dishes. Coming all the way from Singapore, we would frequent their restaurant and their standard of cooking is maintained with quality. I highly recommend dining there. They have good customer service and closes late after 1am.

Author: Mohamed IKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: The Right First Impression Wins
Review: Walking through the Square, we passed by Helen on the way to the sea front stalls. My wife turned around and asked her some questions and decided to give Monterios a try.Night 1 was for supper only since we already had dinner else where. The squid fritters were very appetizing. Even I could not resist. So was the chicken wings and the kailan vegetable.For me the apple-lemon was very tantalizing, the best one for this year.Night 2 was the big dinner for 4 of us. Salted egg crab really opened the night. Followed by the wet buttered prawn, baked otak-otak and steamed otak-otak. Of course our dinner was not complete without the garlic kailan and chicken wings.The juices of apple-lemon and honey-lemon really help us wind the night.A place worth a re-visit! Thanks Janet, Helen and the team.!Show less

Author: GreenieSingaporeSingapore, Singapore
Title: Scallops with butter garlic! Family like service!
Review: This place is in the middle of the settlement building areas. It is not by the sea. The owner related that they decided on this spot as it was easier to keep the kitchen clean. We called before visiting to ensure there were tables as it was a long weekend holiday. Janet who picked up the call was very warm and friendly! When we arrived, we were met by her just as friendly sister and a gentleman. Just as other reviewers said, the service was very thoughtful. Eg we sat at a big table, they asked if we wished it removed the table top so that it will be a smaller and more cosy table size for us. Most zhi cha spots will just leave it instead of doing the extra work. We had butter garlic scallops, salted egg crabs, dry butter prawns, steamed fish (with this really nice sauce!), otah and veggies. The food was all very tasty. The butter garlic scallop sauce was a surprise... The scallops are small but the sauce was really nice! Our kids loved it! Saw horse shoe crab shells in the rubbish bin and asked if they had it. Apparently the brother operates another joint in front and specializes in this and other shell fish! Can order and ask them to bring over. Would recommend this place! Had a memorable dinner! Show less

Author: HunyBunySuny
Title: Terrible!!
Review: As soon as you step out of your car, representative from each stalls compete with one another by harassing the guest (which really agitated me and annoyed me). They surrounded us in a circle, demanding us to pick a stall number immediately! Highly unprofessional and rude! Food was worth coming all the way to try. Nothing special. Promoted so highly on the crab but the portion of crab turned out so small and not worth the money. Terrible place. Show less

Author: AndyD729Paradise Point, Australia
Title: Fantastic food and service.
Review: This is the second time we have visited this restaurant and both times sensational food and service. We have travelled Malaysia for the last couple of weeks and this restaurant came out a clear winner from all we ate at. It is way better than any out the front in the big show which we tried last time we were here.The 3 sisters that own it are just so attentive to your requirements. The La La dish as snack amazing. Then came vege dish, butter scallops and salted egg prawns with a Portuguese fish to complete the meal. By the time we got to the fish we were really full. Show less

Author: William W
Title: Great food. Great host.
Review: Great food. Great ambient. A hidden gem in Portuguese Settlement, Malacca. Will differently come again.

Author: Pioneer397669
Title: Fantastic!
Review: Food was good. Place is simple but with good ambience. Felt relaxing because of the oldies music they played. Loved it!Food portion was big even thou we ordered small for everything. Seafood was fresh and flavour is amazing. They served the fattest crab I ever had! Other than that, the service here is really good. Will definitely come back again. Show less

Author: Carson L
Title: Cill out
Review: Monterios restorean is the best food that i have ever had the seafood then the owners were very frendly and kind

Author: 238quenting
Title: Welcoming and nice staff
Review: This little restaurant is just a few steps from the Portuguese square restaurants on the seaside.We went there to have some drinks after dinner and we wish we would find it earlier.The three sisters that run the place were really amazing, and really caring about the quality of their products and the well being of their customers !I recommend!Show less

Author: barbarita2011Melaka, Malaysia
Title: Delightful Portuguese Dinner evening.
Review: The family operated restaurant has a warm, cozy atmosphere. The service is very personal. Chef came to our table to discuss the seafood dishes. Excellently prepared fresh seafood with very tasty sauces: clams, prawns, grilled fish and vegetables. Highly recommend. Two Canadians really enjoyed the entire evening. Thank you Helen and Janet.Show less

Author: kevinn7
Title: Excellent portuguese food
Review: The salted egg crab and mango juice is a must have. Seafood was really fresh. The recommendation was perfect for the family.

Author: HarleyclarkeyCounty Dublin, Ireland
Title: Not great
Review: This is more expensive than the stalls and to be factual our meal was not as good.It is more expensive for both the fish, sides and drinks.We were quoted 6-7 MYR per 100 grammes for our fish. We were charged 8 MYR with no notice to us. Not a huge deal but this should be stated upfront. (next night we paid 6 MYR for the same fish in a stall)The fish was small with little flesh and regrettably bone, and I mean bone, dry so as to totally lose all of its flavour. It was also covered in far too much of a sauce. Service was friendly and good.Show less

Author: A3355800Kuala Lumpur, Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Love the taste of home cooked traditional portugese food!
Review: Had a great time celebrating Christmas eve at Monterios. love the cosy atmosphere and the family run business. Everyone was friendly, and even though the restaurant was closed for their own family celebration, they still hosted a couple of us for a great seafood affair. Must try their fried chicken and their butter cooked scallops. Their crabs are also fresh and cooked in their salted egg sauce, it was yummy! I personally loved the salted fish kailan. The portugese grilled brinjal was unique. I would hav prefered it with a bit of sauce to go, but it was nicely grilled. They allow BYO with no charges at the time i visited. We celebrated my Dad's birthday and we had a blast. Highly recommended for those who are tired of the commercialized restaurants in Melaka. Show less

Author: Max T
Title: A Howlin' Good Time at Monterios Portuguese Seafood Restaurant
Review: Malacca has slowly been gaining a reputation as a bastion of food innovation. And I don't doubt that for a bit. I have been dining in some of Malacca’s best-kept secrets for many years now, and I must say it's quite an experience. This so-called food revolution happening in the Portugis Square has seen many of the country’s best new restaurants sprouting like mushrooms in this lush Bay. And for those of you searching for a culinary experience like no other, look no further than Monterios. Nestled amid the lofts and showrooms that pepper the city’s trendy Portugis Square, Monterios is the brainchild of Janet and Helen, sibling who grew up on the Portuguese-Chinese fusion cuisine they’re bringing to the restaurant. The restaurant is located in a rather unassuming converted community centre with a stage that almost blocks the restaurant from the car parked view (that’s quite easy to miss). However, the interior will remind visitors of a minimalist, Cast Away-esque tropical paradise. The decor allows the simplistic beauty of the food to really shine, though beauty isn’t the only thing bringing folks to Monterios. The restaurant buzzed with excited energy and was comfortably full with seemingly satisfied patrons. We started with Monterios’s famous deconstructed ranging from salted egg crabs, prawns, scallops, lala, steamed/baked fish, vegetables, otah and the list goes on. We certainly could have shared a second order, though that is more a reflection on the otherworldly taste than the portion size. Though I would love to be selfish and keep Monterios all to myself, the work of Janet and Helen are too good to stay hidden for long. There’s no doubt a table Monterios at will quickly become the hottest reservation in town.Show less

Author: Cheryl TSingapore, Singapore
Title: Very fresh seafood, friendly staff & nice ambience
Review: I was there in early Sep and had the most memorable dinner at the Monterios! We had differently cooked seafood ranging from prawns, scallops, lala, steamed/baked fish, vegetables, otah and the list goes on. The staff were very friendly and recommended what was their best dishes. Highly recommended in Melaka if you have a seafood craving.Show less

Author: Evelyn Chin Y
Title: Good seafood
Review: Food here is really awesome. But the hawkers are too desperate for business. Didn't expect them to surround us when we got out from the car and try to convince us many times to go to their stall and eat. And spicy crab is not worthy to eat cause they just cook with curry powder. The rest are good.Show less

Author: June N
Title: Delicious and fresh Portugese seafood
Review: Friendly staff, great food with reasonable price! Spacious compound suits children to play around safely. Definately will visit this restaurant again.

Author: flyingace28Malaysia
Title: Great Portuguese food
Review: Family run business, the sisters were very nice, friendly. Recommended very good dishes. We had the Devils chicken (have to preorder), the steamed lala, chilly oil steam fish - all of which were really amazing. Fresh and full of flavor dishes. Highly recommended for those who want to try good Portuguese food. Show less

Author: hayes1313
Title: Great fresh Portuguese seafood
Review: Friendly staff. Great food. I especially like the otak otak, the Portuguese fried Brinjal and the scallops. This restaurant is quite new at time of review. Open for approx 1 year. So there is no long queue and not crowded.

Author: JanlklSingapore, Singapore
Title: Delicious dinner
Review: First time here despite many trips to Malacca. Very friendly, laid-back place run by 3 sisters. Reasonably priced. Food was very fresh and good. Even the kids enjoyed the dinner very much as they can take some level of spiciness. Will certainly be back. Was advised to call ahead to confirm that they are opened for business, in case the family's traveling.Show less

Author: ttp1111Toulouse, France
Title: Take your time, its open till 2am
Review: we didn't arrive early in the Portuguese settlement, due to the flight in. We did want to have Portuguese food though. Wow, were we not disappointed. We may have slightly over ordered but they were so accommodating, and said "take your time, its open till 2am". Good food, i would highly recommend it, i wouldn't even bother heading into the stalled area. since as soon as you head to it, you are swamped with proposals of which one to go to. It wasn't very pleasant. What to have - salted egg crab, the otak otak.Show less

Author: tony12cuKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Great Value for money dim sum, taste average
Review: This is a dim sum restaurant with a history and recommended by many websites. The dim sum is below average, while the service is good. The stand out dish is the otak-otak.The only thing great about this restaurant is its great value price.Parking is quite difficult.Show less

Author: jokl78Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Taste ok but cheap
Review: Come here early like 8am if you want to avoid queue. Not really practicing social distancing as we were forced to share table with 2 other people on a small table. We are 3 in a family. Taste wise ok. KL has much better dimsum. Price is cheap. Servixe is fastShow less

Author: leecK9330OU
Title: Old Shop
Review: This kopitiam is offering dim sum at morning. Price reasonable & popular to tourists. There is no car park & service can be improved

Author: senfaaaMalaysia
Title: Not bad~
Review: Woke up in the early morning and walked to this restaurant.This place serves dim sum and the food taste good.However, it could be better if the food was hot or warm enough (because some dim sum were quite cold, even it was just served on the table).Show less

Author: sze2276
Title: Worth Trying
Review: Nothing to shout about. Tasted normal like the others. Worth trying though. To me, it is considered pricey.

Author: leecK9330OU
Title: Dim Sum
Review: The dim sum are taste ordinary at reasonable price. Always crowded with tourists after 8am & required a wait for seat

Author: Stephanie S
Title: Great place for breakfast
Review: Cheap food,  fast service and friendly staff.  The yum cha was amazing. Great value for money... try the steamed pork buns

Author: Liam K
Title: Typical simple Dim Sum
Review: Dead cheap. Open early in the morning. Fast and frequented by local. No frills. Excellent value for money

Author: hxhxhx
Title: Good place for Breakfast
Review: It is a convenient location with a wide variety of dim sum, it is a good place for a nice breakfast. Their tea taste good too,warm and fragrant. For more variety, you may need to visit earlier.

Author: emilyr395
Title: Good
Review:
Everyting came in small portion.
Their tea was good too. Very nice fragrant.
Place was almost full.
Try gg early so tat u dont miss out on their food choices. I wen abt 9am plus.
Everyting was nice.

Author: GoochmasterSydney, Australia
Title: Great for the Family
Review: Yes this place gets really busy and so why is it you have to wait if the food is average. Well depends where you come from as nothing beats Sydney yum cha but for 80 MYR feeding a super hungry family of 4 it’s a great deal. It opens at 6am and Singaporean’s come here to eat and love it. Get here by 7:30am to avoid a queue on a busy weekend for breakfast. Lunch sells out by 1pm and they close so don’t get there too late for lunch.The speciality here is Xiao Long Bao and Mango Mochi. I don’t like durian but they have a mochi equivalent too.In all convenient and good tasting food, I’m not sure there are better options for dim sum in Malacca.Show less

Author: Lugosi915
Title: Normal...
Review: Came here to order some takeaway after reading some good reviews here but, kinda below expectations. Dim Sum was normal, Loh Mai Kai taste weird, and Pao was... hrm... The 3* gain from the price. Will i return again? Probably no...

Author: random010
Title: convenient location
Review: Location is convenient if you stay around jonker street area. Website stated opening hour as 8am but when we reached at 8.06am, it was already full house. Queued for about 10mins, service was not as bad as I thought. Food tasted normal, liu sha bao and chicken feet was quite good, xiao long bao is bad no soup in the dumpling at all.Show less

Author: Miketwz
Title: Nice place to have breakfast
Review: Although there are a lot of people waiting in queue, we manage to get a seat quite fast. Staffs are friendly and tried their very best to serve us. Food are nice and fresh too.

Author: LionrocksSingapore, Singapore
Title: So so Dim Sum
Review: I'm not sure what's the hype all about this restaurant. The quality and varieties of the Dim Sum is not what I expected it to be. The Bao is quite nice. The rest of the items I find is only so so or below average. But there is one item which I find Very nice is the tofu. Very smooth and the taste fantastic.Show less

Author: EYeoSingapore, Singapore
Title: Worth a visit
Review: I’ve eaten here numerous times before. I eat here more because of its central location, it’s a Melakan institution than because the food is particularly delicious. The food isnt bad, but it’s not spectacular. I like the big pau and the otak, but the rest of the dim sum dishes are so-so. The coffee shop can get crowded and warm, so be prepared. The service is quite prompt.All in all, an enjoyable and reasonably-priced meal.Show less

Author: clayden_tan
Title: Bad service and food
Review: Food mostly serve cold. Bad attitude when taking orders by some of the staff. Food is not up to standard of the long queue..

Author: Best127
Title: Nothing to Shout About
Review:
Other than is reasonably priced and speedy service, the dim sums here are really nothing to shout about. 

Undoubtedly it is popular among locals and tourists alike due to there are not many dim sums restaurants available in Malacca.

Author: Hugh M
Title: Super fantastic
Review: Ok so we went with me Janine and our 3 boys. Even the fussy one loved it. SUPER speedy service and excellent breakfAst at a FANTASTIC price. Think fast, eat fast, start your day off right.

Author: SunnyDream_DreamSkyJohor Bahru, Malaysia
Title: An average dim sum place
Review: A crowded place for breakfast. Go early to avoid the crowd especially on weekends and public holidays.Dim Sum is average. Worth a try: Glutinous chicken rice (Lo Mai Gai), Meat Bun. The others are just average.Quick service but servers can have a bad attitude at times.Show less

Author: Hwee Min LSingapore, Singapore
Title: Dim sum hell
Review: The only thing going for this place is its location. Food and service seriously can’t get any worse. They yell at you if you take more than 3 seconds to decide what you want to eat. Which would be forgivable if the food was exemplary. The truth though is that the har gow skin is so thick and gooey it clumps up once your chopsticks touch it, totally detaching from the meat filling. If that doesn’t count as dim sum failure, then I don’t know what does.Lin Heung Lau this place is not.Show less

Author: ClassyrcIlford, United Kingdom
Title: Definitely worth a visit if you fancy some dim sum
Review: The service here was ridiculously quick. We sat down and they immediately came over with trays full of steamed and fried dumplings which you take and eat. No need to order and wait. It was so quick we were a little taken off guard but the steamed dumplings were good. Not the greatest I've ever had but definitely worth a visit if you fancy dumplings. Also the pork steamed bun was the most full bun I've ever had. Also it's all very cheap! Show less

Author: pauljerSingapore, Singapore
Title: A reliable choice
Review: In Hong Kong, dim sum is almost like a religion. If you’re already a devotee, you are likely to have burned your tongue on many a pork bun and dumpling.Hidden near antique and vintage Jonker street, spot, opened since 1947, knows a thing or two about dim sum. It’s a very traditional coffeeshop and unsurprisingly the menu consists of resolutely traditional Dim Sum. The fried turnip cakes were competently done, if not especially exciting – and free of excess oil. The skins of the siu mai were a little fragile and there was precious little prawn, but the chunky whole pieces of meaty pork made up for it. The lo mai gai (Chinese Sticky Rice Wrapped in Lotus Leaf) was far more impressive.Most of the basics are done well and – some of which are surprisingly good. But despite this Low Yong Moh is still one of the better places to have morning dim sum in Melaka. This is the true truth as I say it as it is…Show less

Author: Wongeileen
Title: RUDE TO HELL
Review: Those who rated above really really really have never tried dimsum before. Plus, service and attitudes is rude to hell.

Author: nikselaAmsterdam, The Netherlands
Title: Amazing dim-sum and bao breakfast - get there before 10am. Closed on Tuesdays.
Review: Amazing dim sum and bao breakfast, be there before 10am, as the bao start selling out around that time. You will find your own seat or the staff will help you if busy. Servers will come along with trays filled with dim sum, bao’s, crispy deep fried items and desserts, and you can just point to what you like, they will explain what it is, and you can pick and choose what you’d like to eat. When paying, the boss will check the plates on your table and you pay accordingly. You can have top ups on your tea! Try the pork bao and the mango dessert: amazing! Note: closed on Tuesdays!Show less

Author: Lenard L
Title: Abomination
Review: What a joke. Such as joke. It seems like those who rated above 1 have never tried dimsum before. J.O.K.E

Author: AliciakhyKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Cheap dim sum
Review: The prices for each dim sum ranges from RM 3-4 something, which is pretty cheap as compared to KL. But do note, the dim sum here is also much smaller. This place would be pack in the morning as dim sum is a morning food. There isn't a lot of seating and you might have to wait, we waited about 15 minutes for a table. If you decide to eat here, get a cup of tea and just sit while they bring about trays of full of various dim sum and you get to pick off the tray. There are some things you have to order with the waiter such as loh mai kai and custard buns. Do try their loh mai kai and siew mai! It is amazing, both of them have really porky flavour which I love. Service may not be on the best side, but honestly, they are really buzy.Show less

Author: jocelyn_smi
Title: So so
Review:
Went there as it was near hotel i stayed.  Weekend needs to queue but waiting time not that long.  Food wise not that tasty, just for a meal to keep stomach full.
 Perhaps the place is the only dimsum offered. Others are local delights.

Author: allanonthego
Title: HERD MENTALITY
Review: Went on a monday morning, having search tripadvisor it was good dim sum.Hold & Bewarned, they dun make the dim sum themselves. They probablygot it from a mass dim sum manufacturer or wholeseller. They re-steam it and serve..All dim sum dishes were cold and salty. Quality? None - when u have no control over the manufacturing process.The skin of har gau was too thick & filling salty.Siew Mai was bland/ tastelessChar Siew Pow flour was rough and filling was a llittle fat pork slice and salty.Nothing was good.You could eat better at any chinese roadside coffeshop selling din sum.Why queue for something that you can have very much faster & better at anysmall chinese coffee shop offering the same .Herd Mentality is so TRUE here.Show less

Author: Contented13
Title: Not opened till 29 Nov 2018
Review: Can’t say much since I didn’t get to try!! ʜᴀʜᴀʜᴀ! So we asked a local for a recommendation and was very pleased!! (See my other review on Pin Pin Hoon)

Author: The_Traveler010710Shah Alam, Malaysia
Title: Dim Sum Shop at Jonker Street
Review: This shop basically run by a family. If you except great service, then this is not the shop. The food was good, but don’t expect a warm welcome or hospitality from the people there especially the young girl (when you asked her or wanted to order for more food, she will show the unhappy face as though you are asking for free food!).It still keep the ‘traditional taste’ of dim sum, not like many dim sum shops in Klang Valley. Price was also cheap. Show less

Author: Tigerlily752Manchester, United Kingdom
Title: Delicious :)
Review: We visited this place twice on our stay in Melaka after it was recommended to us. Both times it was absolutely amazing. The steamed pork buns are unbelievable as is the salted egg bun and radish cake (+ so much more). We also tried the mango mochi which was so yummy. Service was really good and the staff are so friendly! Can’t wait to go back to Melaka so I can come here for breakfast :)Show less

Author: Koo YKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Good dim sum selection
Review: We Have a morning walk looking for nice food in Jonker Street for breakfast. Suppose my plan is to look for Heng Huat coffee shop but not able to locate it and we came across this dim sum restaurant and give it a try. We reached early at 8am and the place is almost full.lucky we have a small table for 6 of us. To bring for small children to dine in at coffee shop is not easy and the friendly staff there make me feel welcome and they are very helpful , always remind the kids to sit aside as they holding hot dim sum around. Small gestures does make me feel good to dine in here. We ordered lo mai kai, har gao, saltee egg bun, braised chickeb feet, fishball, fried food,braised pork rib, porridge and lots more. Delicious dim sum, love the authentic taste and i will highly recommend the salted egg bun. It was the best since i have previously from Opium KL.Yum.total bill RM 44.not bad.Portion might be smaller within that reasonable price.Show less

Author: eylmikSelangor, Malaysia
Title: AMAZING FOOD ANS SERVICE
Review: I'm a BIG fans of dim sum and always craving for it. Found this restaurant via google map and saw some review online so I decided to try it out. Well, I waited for 20 minutes in the line because this place is crowded !!! The Staff was so friendly that I can tell them I need another dim sum via eye contact even though the restaurant is pack with people. We had so much dim sum for just RM 70+ , you might think that's a bit expensive but trust me, you will feel like a pregnant lady after you finish your meal :DShow less

Author: yeeping87
Title: Good among a few others in Melaka
Review: Been here for more than 5 times. This had been the most expensive visit - price range RM 3 per small plates of 2 pieces - Xiao Long Bao is sold for RM2.50/ pc (tiny one without much soup). 2 person we ate abt RM35. Quite long queue at about 930 in the morning but their turn over was quite quick (there’s a stall with old lady selling fried sweet potato and banana fritters if u r hungry and ur kids couldn’t stand the wait). Staff were very friendly and organised and know exactly which table to attend to! Lovely 3 generation in this business and great to see everyone in harmonious duties. Selection was limited but essential to fill the tummy before you go for more food in the town! Good start of the day!Show less

Author: OkoklahT
Title: Bad service and food
Review:
I been type twice and my record all gone.

Author: Derrick6971
Title: Best Dim Sum in Malacca
Review: Owner's is helpful and friendly.  Dim sum is cheap and delicious. Location is inside Jonker Street. By Grab/Grab Taxi about RM4-RM20 depending on location you stay. My Kid like most of Durian mo chi. Overall experience is great.  Will come again.

Author: CelynJuiSingapore, Singapore
Title: Popular Dim Sum nearby Jonker
Review: Place is crowded when we reached. Waited for about 10mins before we get a table. Missed out a number of food as they are sold out, overall food is good, service is good also. Choose from the tray the staffs bring around you and order those that are not in the tray. Hot water is self service.Show less

Author: engy2017
Title: Poor service
Review:
Food is good but not services are not
not friendly. Come if you only care abt good food but not good service.

Author: jeffchia88Singapore, Singapore
Title: The average Dim Sum stall to eat when you are at a loss of what to eat for breakfast
Review: For some reasons many of the restaurants in Melaka are packed. There was a need to queue to get a table at this place. I guess people follow people.The Dim Sum here is average for a decent breakfast or brunch. Coffee or Tea except Chinese Tea is made from 3 in 1 packets. I did not find anything special in their offering but the food tasted ok. The facilities are clean at the shop front and place is accessible for wheelchair.Show less

Author: leecK9330OU
Title: Popular Dim Sum
Review: It's an old dim sum restaurant in the heritage city. Dim Sum are selling at very reasonable price & popular to local & foreign tourists. Always crowded after 8am & prepare to have a wait for seat or sharing table

Author: FLBBPCMM
Title: Not much choice.
Review: This place is near to tourist attraction in jonker street itself. Very crowded need to queue. Dim sum taste ok nothing to shout out. They don't have the very basic one that is chee cheong fun. Price not cheap. I will recommended Man Ting Siang at Kota Laksamana more choices n nicer. Show less

Author: pamtjhSingapore, Singapore
Title: Yummy Dim Sum
Review: Good place for traditional dim sum. Slightly difficult to order if you haven’t had dim sum before as their menu is very vague. Went there around 11am and quite a few items were already sold out. Would recommend their salted egg bao as it is very soft and fluffy.Show less

Author: junesingSingapore
Title: Must try - Tua Pow, lotus leaf glutinous rice and chicken feet
Review: A 30 plus year old traditional dim sum restaurant. We got there at 745 am on a saturday just before the crowd’s formed. The siew mia (pork and shrimp dumpling) was dry and hardly any shrimp, the ha gao (shrimp dumpling) was hard, not succulent, the carrot cake was quite nice, crispy on the outside soft on the inside, the chicken feet was soft and nicely marinated, the nor mai kai ( glutinous rice in tin cup) was oily and hard but the lotus leaf glutinous rice was nice. But the best is their Tua Pow ( big pow) which is filled with stewed pork and marinated egg, its juicy and the skin is soft.Show less

Author: ChangKaHinkSandakan, Malaysia
Title: Very vintage, and traditional!
Review: The place really takes us back to the olden times when dim sum is just a coffee shop of the neighborhood. As we were there quite late in the morning, it wasn't necessary for us to queue up (it was also a weekday).Foodwise, there was nothing to really judge, but enjoy! Especially the siu mai served there, which is both flavourful & fragrant, not like the typical meaty one.The other recommended items there are: liu sha bao (salted egg pau) and fish balls with curry soup in the centre. However, the others are still delicious too.Basically, go and try out how the uncles and aunties had their dim sum for breakfast a few decades ago! Show less

Author: leecK9330OU
Title: Cheap Dim Sum
Review: It's an old chinese kopitiam, which selling dim sum at morning. The outlet is located in front of Masjid Kampung Kling. Good selection dim sum. Priced very reasonable but taste ordinary. Service can be improved. Always crowded with tourists & travellers

Author: alanthegreatSingapore, Singapore
Title: Busy dim sum cafe
Review: Expect long queues even in the early morning, however, the turnover of seats are pretty fast probably due to the fast service and limited variety of dim sums available. It serves mainly the traditional dim sum, so you won't too many of new flavour in here. But the food quality is good. Recommended if you are around the area.Show less

Author: yomamemo
Title: good food
Review: good traditional dim sum place. Recommended to try the salted egg yolk bao, big bao, steam pork ribs and steam chicken feet. the glutinous rice is a bit more salty than normal.

Author: X2452GGvanessatSingapore, Singapore
Title: Second visit, food is still so good
Review: Limited seating but turnover for seats are fast. Restaurant is hot as it's not air-conditioned so guest tend to leave immediately after eating. Food gets sold out by 10am. Gotta b there early to ensure u have their full selection of dim sum. Lor Mai Kai and their big meat bao is a must eat.No chilled drinks serve. Only chilled 100-plus without ice. Mostly hot drink are available.Show less

Author: Thomas T
Title: No frills dim sum place
Review:
Family business, daily freshly prepared food. Liked the lo mai kai, pau and the kopi.
Old school serving concept.

Author: lihyenno
Title: Quintessential local Chinese breakfast
Review: Love the ambience and the food, dim sum were freshly prepared, steamed and served.  All good stuff are gone by 11am. So, please be early.

Author: CGUrbanaIllinois
Title: Fantastic!
Review: We saw a long line here one morning and so tried it out. We returned several times, as everything we tried was truly excellent. Plus, very reasonably priced. Would go back in a heartbeat.

Author: Linda CToronto, Canada
Title: Delicious steamed pork dumpling!
Review: Eating dim sum on your own is not ideal but if nothing else, stop by for their steamed pork buns (dumpling). They have two sizes, normal and small...they are full of delicious juicy pork with 'gravy', very tasty and filling. I tried a few different things over a few visits; pork, shrimp and chicken choices and found them up to normal dim sum standards. Service was good and staff friendly. Reasonable prices, three or four choices plus tea, 10-12mr.Show less

Author: Alice SSingapore, Singapore
Title: Don't Expect Too Much
Review: Was there on a Saturday morning at about 9 am. There were some early birds but several empty tables were still available. Wanted to sit at a round table but was quickly directed to a long bench leaning against the wall. Well, I didn't mind that at all. There was a young Asian guy sharing that bench with me.A hardworking Indian (or maybe, a Nepali) staff followed me all the way to my seat. He offered to steam the egg tarts for me and claimed that there were very nice. But I didn't order what he recommended. Instead, I ordered the Big Pau, Lor Mai Kai and Milo. Glad that he was not pushy and he brought the food I ordered within a few minutes. Well done, man, keep up the good work!The Big Pau was O.K. but the Lor Mai Kai was miserably small (both were of the same price). I do agree with other members' reviews that you can get much better Dim Sum in Singapore. The Lor Mai Kai I always buy in Singapore is about the same price but in SingDollars and the amount (portion) is 4 times more. And it has lots of ingredients, such as chicken, chestnut and mushroom - definitely much more YUMMY!!The young Asian guy sharing the long bench with me turned out to be a Japanese student on holiday in Malacca. He asked me "How do they charge?" He seemed to be a bit worried, as he had quite a number of small plates of Dim Sum in front of him. He told me that he had problems communicating with the staff. I guessed they simply gave him one plate of each type of Dim Sum. All the items he had were from the big serving tray, none were specially ordered. He asked me "What are these (pointing to a couple of plates of Dim Sum) he had?" I really didn't know since I did not order them. I waved to the staff trying to get help for the poor chap (not knowing what he was eating). One of them was Yam but he didn't understand "Yam", and I didn't know how to say it in Japanese. He told me he didn't like it (the Yam). When I asked for my bill, he said he would like to have his bill too. So I simply relayed the message in Mandarin to the staff (an Ah Soh). She was standing near the cashier. She turned around and asked me sarcastically if I was going to pay his bill too. I shot back and said "This poor chap had problems communicating with you all, so I am just trying to help". My firm and fierce voice was enough to shut them up. I wanted the bill to show all individual item price and not one lump sum. My bill came first and yes, they gave me exactly what I wanted. When the Jap's bill came, I saw he was billed for everything, including those he couldn't finish. I looked around to find that Indian worker who had given me very good service from the time I stepped into the restaurant. I got him to pack up whatever the Jap wanted to take away, after all he had paid for all of them. That Indian worker did exactly what I told him to do (immediately).Back in the hotel, I was thinking if we had treated this restaurant just like a coffee shop or a stall in a food centre, then we might feel better because expectations of food quality and service standard would be much lower. After all, there was no service charge in our bills. I don't think they meant to be sarcastic or rude, it is just their "normal" way of communication.Show less

Author: Mia FSingapore, Singapore
Title: overrated, no-quality dim sum
Review: do not expect much decent service rendered here at this restaurant. just get your own table and wait for them to come to you "randomly" with big serving tray of just any kind of dim sum (fried or steamed) and you just take whatever you want. Pau (steamed buns) would have to be ordered/requested for though, never seen any being displayed on the serving trays. food are just ranging from being average/mediocre to BAD (for that ONE rice roll wrapped thing which tasted absolutely disgusting in my opinion). initially you may feel that prices are dirt-cheap (comparing to much how you would have to pay for the same quantity ordered in Singapore). But if you take into account of the quality, you will know, what you pay is what you get.Show less

Author: ThriftyAlwinLee
Title: Overrated and expensive
Review:
Food was bland. Don't know why there was a queue. Price is expensive as compared to other eateries in the area.

Don't come.

Author: chshan37
Title: Bad experience, Food was soso
Review: We went on Sunday morning, where we need to queue up to wait for our turn, it might not taken a long time. For the food, the dim sum offered there are so so, not really worth the wait unless you have nothing to eat or choose from. The price are affordable enough but when come to service, they are rude enough. Especially when we ask for bill and the person didnt response and we plan to call again due to long queue and we would like to leave to let the other customer get in and have a sit. Then the person scolded my friend claiming that he is not deaf. It is OUT of the must list.Show less

Author: 235micheleqNew York City, New York
Title: No frills
Review: Authentic dim sum spot that was no frills. Come early or expect to wait in line, as the restaurant gets packed. Once you're seated, you're brought tea and then wait around for the servers to come by with (literally) small plates of a variety of your typical dim sum options. At the end, they add up the number of plates (depending on size) you've had to charge you. Note, you have to go refill your tea kettle yourself. Food was nothing to write home about but I enjoyed the atmosphere of the local joint.Show less

Author: Babymuji
Title: Must eat when in Melaka
Review: Authentic dim sum which is tasty and reasonably priced. Especially enjoy their chicken glutinous rice!

Author: GanLKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Must have the tai pao
Review: Went here for breakfast. Simply loved the wide selection of delectable dim sum and piping hot Puer tea. Our favourite is the tai pao. The tai pao here is similar to a siow long pao which has a soupy presence. As you lift the tai pao up, you will feel the heaviness at the bottom. Once you bite into the pao, out spills the soupy substance that is so flavorful. This pao only consists of pure lean meat. This restaurant has been around for 60 years and is now run by third generation Lows.Show less

Author: ivykuang98
Title: Okay
Review: Food was quite okay, not exceptional good or bad.Custard bun, durian mochi, carrot cake and lotus leaf rice was goodSmal portions but low priceWent on a Friday so no queue no wait.Note that coffee is not freshly brewed but with coffee and tea bagsOverall okayShow less

Author: OliverL751Singapore, Singapore
Title: Decent food with good service
Review: We were a group of 14 and there was a queue when we arrived.However we got acknowledged promptly and got seated in 10 mins.Good variety of dim sum and drinks. They frequently checked in on us to see if we needed more food.Within walking distance from JonkerShow less

Author: Ktbh21Singapore, Singapore
Title: Worth the visit!!
Review: Great Breakfast place featuring amazing dimsum which is served right up to your table. The variety and price will leave you satisfied for sure and its one of the best breakfast i had in awhile! Do plan your trip to the place early as it gets to full house really quickly! It is also prominently located at the jonker street area so its really accessible if your hotel/ apartment is near there!Show less

Author: alistair15Singapore
Title: Authenic Breakfast
Review: If you miss the good old days of the yum cha culture. This place is what you looking for. Average foods and services. You have to come early to avoid the crowd. Finish off with a early stroll down the streets of Melaka in a beautiful morning.Show less

Author: Janbroviz
Title: Great Dim sum and Custard Bun
Review: Good place to have breakfast like a local. Tasty dim sum and custard bun with reasonable price. The staff are very friendly and recommend us a delicious menu. Highly recommend!!!

Author: Karan K
Title: A taste of nostalgia
Review: It's a really busy breakfast place, so come early and be prepared to queue. Dim sum selection is very common, nothing out of the world, but you do get good old fashion dim sum that is affordable and made fresh everyday....

Author: TakoTako
Title: So-so though, for the food.
Review: More for the old school concept instead of the quality. But a couple of items are not bad though. I suppose good for a visit for the experience, but not really for the food.

Author: beeti tKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Tasty Big Buns!
Review: My father frequent this place during our childhood days and Malacca is our hometown. We have always love their big buns. We recently went back to Malacca for a short break and decided to come back here for their big buns and siu mai. Big bun was good but siu mai was a little of a let down (think it is not as nice as before).Show less

Author: BenYorkieKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Delicious Dim Sum. Perfect Pau
Review: Forget the breakfast included in your hotel price - go down to Low Yong for one of the best local breakfasts that you can find in Melaka. The dim sum are tasty and fresh, and we think the char siu pau are some of the best we have ever had; anywhere.Good strong local coffee, basic local café but good prices and good service.Very very good.Show less

Author: sky369369
Title: Stupid and rude action boss
Review: This dim sum restaurant i visited last my vacation on 2015. Since is so early at 6am. Im hungry so i visit again this dim sum. The older boss is ok. I think the boss i mentioned is thier son is so rude and no manner. Talking so rude and attitude also. Service so lousy.scold customer. Mind problem ya.. their foreigner worker is more better attitude than this stupid boss..Show less

Author: JuliaVWeissSao Paulo, SP
Title: The best dim sum and awesome people!
Review: Mainly local Chinese people when we were there (that's always a good sign!), the dim sum was fresh and there was a lot to choose from. The family who runs the place is lovely, helped us with our order and was super friendly. We even went back the next day for more! Show less

Author: 656ivanav
Title: Breakfast like a local
Review: Low Yong Moh is a dim sum coffeehouse just a walking distance around jonker street. The coffee shop offer varieties of dim sums, fried tofus, pao, lotus leaf rice, and delicious lo mai gai.I personally really like their lo mai gai (it's a dim sum dish of steamed glutinous rice topped with soy sauce chicken and mushroom), the char siu pao (Chinese barbecue pork filled-bun), and fried tofus. The coffee also nice (they only serve hot and warm drinks).As mentioned by other reviewers, the food comes with cheap prices ranging from rm2.40 to rm3.20, and don't expect the dim sums taste up to high standard dim sum restaurant.Expect for a long queue and be early to avoid disappointment from finished dim sums.Show less

Author: IchigoKurosaki55
Title: Custard buns, LohMaiKai, HeYehFan
Review: Very old school desert with very nice salted custard bun, lohmaikai and leaf wrapped glutinous rice are my favourites .. arrived around 930 just a short queue and we were quickly seated .. must visit

Author: X2452GGvanessatSingapore, Singapore
Title: Dim sum is cheap
