Review: Small restaurant in a strip mall, parking nearby hard to come by but around the corner, there is a side street, and another less congested road where there are parking lots - just be prepared to use parking coupons (can buy the coupons at one of the shops, ask the coffee shop for directions to the shop nearby).Food is good - we had their otak, kiamchye soup, mango kerabu, pie tee, and taugeh chicken. Except for the kiamchye soup, the dishes were delicious. The kc soup was ok, not as fragrant as the ones I am used to. Prices are reasonable for nyonya food, although the portions are not terribly big.Show less

Author: michaelc679Singapore, Singapore
Title: Too sweet
Review: Not sure if we are not use to Malaysian Nyonya food or it was just too sweet for that day.We were a group of 4 friends on a foodie trip and decided to try some local food and decided to try this place compared to the many other restaurants.The only comment we could conclude was the food was not as authentic as it should be and. It was way too sweet for all of us.We had the Chap chye, Asam fish, fried chicken, prawn petai sambal (Super tiny shrimps at market price) , hee peow soup (tons of sugar), chengdol. Will definitely try other places.Show less

Author: angely_angel
Title: Authentic and yummy!
Review: The food here taste very good! Try the chendol! Very fragrant! Had Chap Chya, Ayam ponteh, fried chicken and we wiped our plates clean!

Author: poonam05
Title: One of the best
Review: One of the best nyonya food I ever had. Suitable for families and friends. Every dish we ordered was delicious. My fav was the fried japanese tofu. Must try.

Author: audreyxjySingapore, Singapore
Title: Good food and good price
Review: We visited on a Sun and called for reservation 45mins before dropping by. It was not crowded and there really is no need to reserve in advance. The Ayam Buah Keluak is a must try, the chicken is tender and savory. The cendol is a disappointed especially after we tasted what was offered at Jonker88. Show less

Author: GerardWWSingapore, Singapore
Title: Perfect place to try local Peranakan and Nyonya cuisine. Make a reservation though!
Review: Its all about the food here. Simple restaurant, nothing fancy. Deco is limited, but the food is really great. If you want to try true local Malaccan cuisine, then Amy's is as good a spot as any. Do make a reservation though. Prices are cheap and dishes are copious. It's a little off the well-beaten tourist track so be prepared to walks 10-15mins from the Jonkers Street area to get there. The head chef/owner came and spoke to us as we had a small problem with a dish, but she took time to sort it out and we then learnt a lot from her about the dishes, ingredients and techniques. Highly recommended, but do keep everything in perspective: you come for the food not the ambiance!Show less

Author: foodienandaJohor Bahru, Malaysia
Title: Go with a reservation
Review: So we looked this place up after a decent review on tripA. Came here for lunch on a Saturday. It was packed, and we immediately turned away saying, sorry only for bookings. Didn’t even give us an option of waiting. But there was a tiny little table outside the resto which we tot was good for 2 and somehow convinced the foreign waiter(poor guy was scolded by the lady boss for entertaining this request haha) and we said we didn’t mind. We ordered ikan gerang asam, bendi and pie thee. All were super awesome and I can’t believe how good it was. One of the best tasting nyonya food I have ever tasted. Only thing is the place is small n loads of people kept getting turned away during peak hours I guess. So go with a plan. Can’t wait to try the food again. Show less

Author: KLCLCC
Title: Yummy food but poor service!
Review:
Pongteh chicken and fried chicken were really yummy but the service was really poor. 

Hope the team can serve customers better in future.

Author: charhugkissSingapore, Singapore
Title: Surprisingly good
Review: Friends made prior reservation, we were lucky as it was fully booked the day when we dined. Sadly otah was OOS. The asam fish was super food that i had 4 plates of rice with the gravy over it. The food was so good that i totally forgotten to snap pics. :'(Show less

Author: christyc1963
Title: AUTHENTIC AND AROMATIC CUISINE
Review: The Nyonya food here is of very high quality, with generous ingredients in the spices, the aroma of the food is exhilarating. The taste of the food is authentic and the fish we had was very fresh. Definitely must return to try out other dishes.

Author: fujiapple79
Title: Nice small restaurant with great food
Review: Small restaurant that serve great food. Must try if you are in malacca. Chendol was ok but chendol from Penang is better.

Author: Ozab0utManchester, United Kingdom
Title: Best Restaurant in Melaka
Review: Food was sensational - best restaurant we have been to in Melaka!!Fantastic Nyonya cuisine - Amy is passionate about her food. We had Ikan Assam Rebus (Fish) and Udang Lemak Nenas (Prawn with Pinapple) and the Ayam Buah Keras (chicken) - they were excellent. You can also see Amy on Rick Stein.Show less

Author: inlyonSacramento, CA
Title: Awful service, acceptable food
Review: We walked in and they seated us and took our order, then a party of at least 30 people who had preordered showed up. They informed us our food would be delayed because of other guests. They should have told us first. The group was so loud we could not carry on a conversation. They should have closed the restaurant for a private party.They made no attempt to help us find something our 5 year old would eat. Other restaurants have been very helpful.Be forewarned they do not serve alcohol. I don't care but I have been in many halal restaurants in France on North Africa where they were happy to serve their non religious guests beer or wine.Show less

Author: Wenxi CSingapore, Singapore
Title: Another Nyonya Cuisine Worth Visiting in Melaka!
Review: Finally, we had visited Amy Heritage Nyonya Cuisine before leaving Melaka. This is one of the popular Nyonya Food that have good feedbacks on the media. It is Halal and just as what was written by everyone, reservation in advance is needed. Being walk-in customers, we were only offered one of the outdoors tables out of the two, non-airconditioned but there was a ceiling fan.As we settled down on the outside seats, the servers were quick to service. Service was friendly and efficient when handling their menu as soon as we sat down.We flipped through the menu and notice that there were only medium and large portions. As the dishes does not contain pork and lard, it is suitable for Muslim's consumption.The crispy top hat with shredded turnip filling and served with chilli sauce. Glad that it was not too oily.Pie Tee - RM 2.00 / EachLime Juice, Barli & Lime, Cincau - RM 2.00 EachWas looking forward for a bowl of Duck Soup with Salted vegetable and sour plum but it was not available, thus we order their recommended Hee Peow Soup. It is noted as "Nyonya Wedding Soup" with dried fish bladder , quail eggs, fish ball and vegetable.Hee Peow Soup - RM 25.00The Nyonya style mixed vegetables was indeed tasty with carrots, black fungus and cabbages..Chap Chye - RM 13.00 (Medium)Ayam Pongteh is a classic chicken stew with soya bean paste, chinese mushroom and potatoes. The portion was generously served with couple of chicken drum sticks and delicious. I love its gravy and perfect to go on our plates of fragrant white rice.Ayam Pongteh - RM 21.00 (Medium)Amy's serving of rice was quite different from the rest of the Nyonya Shops we went in Melaka. Rice was kept in a traditional old hand held basket.Rice - RM 1.50 / PaxAs the basket was quite big and space was rather limited at the outside seats, the servers placed the basket using another table.Our finisher for the Nyonya feast was non other than the MUST HAVE dessert, Cendol. The green jelly has a soft texture soaked in gula melaka and coconut milk.Cendol - RM 3.00 Amy Heritage indeed has a given a homely taste to all the dishes. Coming to its portion where minimum order is medium, its not recommended for small group to dine. In addition to things to take note, do make advance booking to avoid disappointment.Show less

Author: ThriftyAlwinLeeSingapore, Singapore
Title: Very good fried sotong and nyonya cuisine
Review: Very strict about reservation so remember to cal them to book. opened exactly at 6pm. Waiters were polite and quick. We ordered a few dishes which include pie tee, chap chye, Ayam Keluak, tofu. Food was good especially the sotong, we ordered 2 servings. Give this place a tryShow less

Author: jasonngan
Title: Excellent Peranakan Cuisine
Review: Good food, reasonable price, and friendly service staffs.Will definitely dine here during our next visit to Melaka.

Author: tcakohSingapore, Singapore
Title: Good Pernakan Food
Review: The location is easily found if you are staying around Mahkota Parade area. Its being a while since I have tasted good peranakan food and I thoroughly enjoyed the food, especially the ayam buah keluak. It reminds me of the food I had in my younger days.Show less

Author: 207normansSingapore
Title: Excellent Nonya Cuisine
Review: The best restaurant cooked peranakan food I've had after a long time. Portion was large enough for 4 persons. Only medium or large. We chose medium. Generous amount of buah Keluak (8 pcs) and plenty of chick thigh. The Sambal kang kong was very good - Not too spicy with 'hay bee'. Must try place when in Melaka. Bring at least 4 diners to sample more variety of dishes. Show less

Author: tauruspel
Title: Good food
Review: Most of the food we ordered are quite yummy except for the otah. Price was reasonable. 11 dishes include drinks cost RM339. Will definitely come back again. Restaurant is just opposite the famous Tong Seng Restaurant. 5-10 mins walk from Hatten Hotel.

Author: Angie L
Title: Have to make reservation - no walk-in.
Review:
apart from the reservation required issue - The basic Nyonya noodles and fried rice are really good. Cendol is also awesome!!

Prices are okay for simple dishes of those that I have mentioned.

A seriously must visit shop.

Author: name-annie-81Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Bad services👎👎👎👎👎👎👎👎
Review: Terrible n bad servicehighly recommend to walk in customers, dun go in. Wil hv an aunty (if not mistaken, she is d Bos)come out to scold d staff n reject us Insisted d staff allow us to sit!!!! So rude n no respect at all! If earli b4 v waiting, jus dun accept us. But wen v oledi sit down n ready to order.. then been reject n asked to leave! Wat d hell!!!!! Reali annoying!!!! Bad services . 1st time ever In my life been like tat treat by restaurant. Pls share d bad manner of d aunty... Show less

Author: chandra kumar V
Title: Excellent food at affordable prices
Review:
Was hoping to try this place and thankfully we got an opportunity! Food was great. Ordered the Asam fish and tofu and prawns. Dishes were rich in flavour and portions were adequate.

Have to make reservations or else you will be disappointed!

Author: Navin AKuala Lumpur
Title: Delicious but expensive Nyonya food
Review: The food is first and foremost, delicious. I must say that.The restaurant was not crowded during weekdays however we were still required to place a booking and be on time or they booked table will be given away. Service was ok. Nothing special about it. The price....well, it's ok for the non-seafood dishes. Portions are big however be wary of any dishes that does not have pricing. It can get quite expensive. It doesn't help that the owner only talks to foreign tourists during my visit and doesn't even bother approaching a table of locals. Maybe I'm just asking too much.Overall, not bad but I won't go back.Show less

Author: Kitsc
Title: Good service, yummy Food, Reasonable prices
Review: The food at Amy Heritage was very flavourful.  Love the curry chicken and Ayam Pongteh.  Service there was excellent where the service staff were very attentive, refilling our drinks promptly.

Author: FoodReviewerSGUK
Title: Amazing Nyonya Food
Review: Definitely should not miss this place. Award winning restaurant which serves excellent Peranakan food.Try out their Kueh Pie Tees, Curries and Assam Garang.

Author: TravellerfromSINSingapore
Title: Our fav dish - Udang Lemak Nanas
Review: Food was slightly slow in coming but it was compensated by friendly service. The soups (itek Tim and Hee peoh) were average and the itek tim didn’t have enough ‘kick’. The pie tee was good but we found the chilli too sweet. We were disappointed that there’s no buah keluak for lunch on a Sat. The best 2 dishes by far were the prawn nanas and chicken pongteh. There’s no pork so it’s not quite true Peranakan but overall we enjoyed the meal. It was very reasonable but some in our group found the dishes a tad too sweet. Show less

Author: DanWee555Singapore, Singapore
Title: Not Authentic Baba Fare.
Review: So very disappointed..heritage ? No pork on the menu, so no Babi Pong teh, nor Ayam buah keluak and the most painful blow was the Chap Chye..it's was stir fried!! I asked the boss and he admitted it. So cheated. However, the Ayam Buah Keras was quite tasty and saved our dinner.Show less

Author: 62melvynnSingapore, Singapore
Title: Average Nyonya Food
Review: Came here on recommendation but I find the food just ok, portion only in medium or large, not ideal for small group as we couldn't try as many dishes as we wanted. Ordered Ayam Buah Keluak (chicken with black nut) which came without any black nut. Service was slow and not exactly friendly. Show less

Author: cpr2exssydney
Title: Authentic and delicious food
Review: Visiting Malacca and staying at the Hatten. Amy’s was recommended to us and was only a 5 min walk from the hotel. We had the Itek Tim (salted veg duck soup), Kerabu Mangga (mango salad), Assam fish and taugeh Ikan masin (bean sprouts with salted fish) . All were really well done. I especially liked the Assam fish - the consistency of the gravy was very good with the right amount of spicy and sourness. Pricing was good too. Highly recommended. Show less

Author: TinyRedDot
Title: Melaka version
Review: Note that I am comparing dishes with those from Singapore.Pie Tie: chilli could do with a little more lime. Not enough 'kick' for me. RM2 eachUdang Goreng Assam: I tasted shrimp paste (hae ko) rather than kecap manis. A little over-powering. RM45 (6 pcs)Nyonya Mee with Rojak: good. RM5Chap Chye: first time I see carrots in a chap chye dish! No belachan was served to go with this dish. RM13Our dinner costed RM104.50 with drinks for 3 paxIt was supposed to be one of top five Peranakan restaurants in Melaka but overall quite disappointing.Show less

Author: lei_lentzakisSingapore, Singapore
Title: Great tasting & enjoyable Nonya cuisines
Review: Went to Amy’s Heritage Nonya Cuisine as my husband saw pretty good reviews about it. Of course with the benefit that it’s location was within walking distance from our hotel too. We ordered Kueh Pie Tee as an appetiser. It’s hard to come by really good kueh pie tee nowadays and Amy’s Heritage pie tee was crisp and fresh! We had Ayam Buah Keras (Candlenut chicken) - something we havnt’ tried in a Peranakan restaurant. This dish blew our tastebuds =) My husband loves it so much. Aroma of the lemongrass, lime leaves and the gravy itself is pretty near perfection! We also had udang sambal petai and udang lemak nenas. I personally love the latter. The gravy of udang lemak nenas although had a little too much of coconut, the spices in the gravy pretty much redeemed itself!Chap Chye was per standard. Itik tim was more sweet than sour for our tastebuds. Overall, this is an excellent place to head for great homemade Nonya dishes with good size portions! Show less

Author: d_reenrPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Delicious Nyonya Food
Review: Pls make reservations because seats are limited. Food served are Nyonya style something different from what you get in Kuala Lumpur. Service was fast. Dessert chendol is a must because the sugar used for this recipe is pure coconut sugar called Gula Melaka. This sugar is famous in Malacca. It is thick like brown molasses. Don't miss it. A other dish I liked was Ponteh. It's a Baba Nyonya chicken dish. Not to miss this dish too!!!Show less

Author: Jim Angie T
Title: Too sweet for my liking
Review: The food served is authentic enough although I find all the dishes too sweet for my liking.  Not one but every dish seems to have much sugar added.  Overall the food is good if you have a sweet tooth

Author: MrGoh
Title: Not Great
Review: The restaurant is rather small and setting is simple. Food quality is so-so. Not worth the visit. There are many more peranakan restaurants with better food.

Author: Larissa O
Title: Horrible
Review: The Nyonya food was terrible, the ayam buah keluak was hard and expensive. The udang masak lemak was too milky, no sour Rastenburg just plain santan. The ikan cili garam was soooo sweet and not pleasant The other dishes were very sweet. The cendol is horrible, the ice were in chunks, had to bite my ice. One of the worst nyonya food I had. Show less

Author: Ultraman87Singapore, Singapore
Title: There are better option elsewhere in Melaka
Review: Normal foods. I think there are many option elsewhere in Malacca for nyonya foods. We just happened to walk in for dinner as the restaurant was not too packed with diners on a Saturday night. Ordered some typical nyonya foods which we know such as pontek chicken etc. It was edible but not "wow"Show less

Author: oscar_oz37
Title: Overall positive & pleasant experience but quite expensive
Review: Recommended to us by family freinds. Staff was helpful and friendly. Average portions for family of 8. Food as compared to other nonya places was acceptable.

Author: jasperjwb
Title: Great food, low prices
Review: We were lucky to get a reservation for a table and were more than happy with the food, while it's not at all expensive. Best Nyonya dishes we had in Malaysia!

Author: fooalarice
Title: Just average
Review: Went to Amy's after seeing positive reviews. The food is decent but I feel that it is just average. I have been to other nonya restaurants which taste better. Pricing wise, it is very reasonable.

Author: SweetiebunMalaysia
Title: Good food at Amy's - a must try
Review: Had lunch and ordered Asam Fish, fried chicken wings and their ladies finger in prawn sambal. Food was sumptuous n a thumbs up to their Chef. Fish was fresh n succulent; on the other hand the Asam Fish was not spicy not too sourish. The dish was into perfection. We ordered cendol for dessert n it was heavenly for a hot day. Will come back wt the family to dine here. A definite recommendation to those visiting Melaka. Show less

Author: Tania A
Title: Sumptuous food at Amy's
Review: We had lunch here and ordered their best - Asam Geram Fish. It is definitely a Chef's recommendation and everything in the outlet has an opulent taste from the fish to the fried chicken wings to the kangkong belacan. Portioning of the food was also generous for a small portion. Their dessert cendol was heavenly! Price was a little pricey for two, however you are paying for the quality of food served and will definitely come back with my family to this outlet. Well Done Amy and Team! Show less

Author: Winson_ChuaRongsenSingapore
Title: Go early or make a booking!
Review: Went there around 6.15pm on a Sunday evening. We were lucky to get a table as there were only 10 tables in the restaurant and most of them were booked.We had prawn, chap chye (mixed vegetable), chicken wings and otah. Food is good but I will try other Nyonya restaurant if I am in Melaka again.Halah restaurant so no alcohol served in there.Show less

Author: FoodEnthusedKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Excellent, Soulful Nyonya Meal!
Review: We booked for dinner a few hours ahead with reminders not to come late as the table would be given away. Arrived early and table was ready for us. The menu had a good variety and we wanted to order everything! We finally chose the Pie Tee, Buah Keluak Chicken (excellent), Itik Tim Soup (a bit too sourish for me, but everyone else enjoyed it), Sambal Prawns with Petai (delicious), Fried Chicken Wings, Vegetable Titik Lemak (so yummy), Cincalok Omelette and the Ikan Gerang Asam - all went perfect with the free-flow white rice. The cendol was unfortunately not the best we have eaten, as the gula Melaka was very diluted.Located a bit further out from the tourist centre, you would need a car to get to the restaurant. Streetside parking is ample. We honestly cannot wait to come back and try the rest of the menu! Show less

Author: KeekSengBeeKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Delightful lunch
Review: Arrived at 1.10pm on Tuesday afternoon and the restaurant was full but a family just finished lunch and we were ushered to the table. Food was indeed very good. We ordered the pineapple prawns, asam fish, belachan kangkong and chilli chicken plus pai tee as starter and of course the cendol. Every dish exceeded our expectations.Show less

Author: Lilian580514Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Sunday School Teacher's Retreat
Review: Ambience is simple and nice. Rice is served in the traditional Nyonya basket. Food is tasty. The appetizer of banana flower with carambola fruirt or buah belimbing assam is so appetizing. There are "ponteh", "lemak santan vegetable" and many more Nyonya authentic dishes to try. I place worth trying if your are in Malacca.Show less

Author: Maxteo919Singapore, null, Singapore
Title: Above average nonya food
Review: Amy is often fully booked and it is best to make booking before heading down for a meal at the restaurant. This restaurant serves better nonya food than the one just few shops beside it (Amboi). Ponteh ayam with potatoes and fried chicken were good. Chendol and tau hu were so so. I remembered that its menu only has medium or large portions. The food was not too bad, do swing by if you are near. Don't expect the service to be fantastic. Show less

Author: Chow ESingapore, Singapore
Title: Best Nyonya food in Melacca
Review: Many Singaporeans went to this authentic restaurant for traditional nonya food. Well worth the wait. We order 5 to 6 dishes for 4 persons to share, and the food was totally fabulous. Be prepared to wait for more than half an hour for food to come, as there are many customers waiting and the service is rather slow.Show less

Author: HappiMummiSingapore, Singapore
Title: Dinner
Review: Finally I get a chance to eat at Amy's - after much raves from bloggers and friends.They did not take out reservation initially but my husband went to take a look, they are ok with us as walk-in.The food was ok. I love the Ayam Buah Keluak, fish maw soup, fried chicken wings.The Chap Chye was disappointing. Overall, a pleasant dining experience. Show less

Author: yliktat
Title: Yummy Nyonya Food
Review: We were there at 1.50pm and waitress immediately take our order as the chefs will be off at 2.30pm. Like their chap chye, ayam pongteh, assam prawn, otah. Assam fish so so only. Chendol is good too!

Author: NgCnalKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Not bad
Review: I love the cendol!The asam fish is alright. Everything taste as how it should.HUGE portion..so bravo to that. Reasonable price.Best to arrive real early and make reservation at night if you want a place for gathering with acceptable nyonya food with large portion.Show less

Author: darenlee
Title: Yummy Nyonya Food - Must try Cendol with Gula Melaka
Review: Lovely Nyonya Food. It was really delicious and style is home cooked style. The Cendol with Gula Melaka is a must!

Author: 34pangseSingapore, Singapore
Title: Great food
Review: I visited the place with my friend. The place is packed. We managed to get a table outside the restaurant. It was warm. When the food was served, the food was great. I like the assam fish and the chicken. Nice food. But they serving size is big for 2 person. Nevertheless the food was enjoyable. Show less

Author: Gene CJohor Bahru, Malaysia
Title: Go for the yummy Nyonya food, reservations would be advised.
Review: Arrived there in the evening around 8 without a reservation, on a weekday night. The bulk of the place looked to be taken by a large group so we were told no available seats, and the last empty table was for a reservation. Fortunately a kind couple who had just concluded their dinner beckoned us to have their table. So reservations might be a good idea if you're planning to dine here as they have limited seating. We ordered Pie tee for starters, followed by fried chicken wings (not bad, nice marination), fried squid, nasi goreng (ok) , cincaluk omelet (yum, was quite liked by my Japanese friend), and the real revelation for me was the sayur masak titik lemak which had me going for me and really drowning my rice with it (and I'm not usually much of a vege person too), the sauce which is santan (coconut milk) based was just sooo sinful & good!Will try my luck next time I'm in Malacca and hope to sample their rendang as it was sold out that evening.I found the prices to be slightly on the high side and had chalked it down to the tourist factor, but perhaps they do charge something of a premium due to their popularity. Show less

Author: JaneJeyarajKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Very Rude
Review: We went there for lunch, the moment we arrived the waiter asked us whether we had any pork in our bags. He was very rude and I didn't think what was the big deal if we carried pork. We told him we didn't have any pork but he was so rude and kept on saying this was a Muslim restaurant. At the back the owner was shouting at her cashier so loudly. Honestly don't think she needed to do that in front of her customers. Anyway we walked out of the restaurant which only had one table occupied ! Definitely not going there anymore ! Don't think that they should impose their religious beliefs on others and it's not like we didn't know that ! We are Malaysians and we do wonder whether they do that to foreigners ! Show less

Author: jenyxzzjennc
Title: Taste was moderate, bad service
Review: Taste is just ok, limited choices in the menu. Attitude of the waiter needs improvement.. They were very impatient

Author: Wan-Ling NKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Horrible service and arrogant staff
Review: Even though we did not make any reservations and we are willing to wait to be seated, the staff would not even let us sit down and wait. There were approximately 30 empty chairs, both on the empty tables and some chairs stacked up where nobody is sitting and they just refused to let us sit down and wait. Horrible service and super bad attitude to treat your customers like that. Will definitely not come to this restaurant no matter how much people rave about it.Show less

Author: scampytails
Title: Amazing flavor!
Review: We just enjoyed our first experience with Nyonya cuisine today at Amy's. The restaurant is charming, the food presentation is unique and the flavor outstanding. Every bite was an explosion of different flavors. The washrooms were also clean. We would definitely go back!

Author: EricChai
Title: Average Nyonya Food
Review: I have a 1 nite stay in Melaka during my business visit to Muar this month and I was looking for a place to have comfort food for dinner.In Melaka first thing pop up in everyone mind will be Nyonya cuisine and been a average person of course same. After much of searching I decided to this restaurant which is 5 min drive from my hotel. Cuz of the weekday nite and non school holidays period the restaurant is quite with 3 tables of customers quite a slow nite I guessed.A one person I ordered a fry noodles and chicken. Food looks colourful and big portion for medium size. Food is a bit salty side and taste is average which I have been better Nyonya food before.If you are hungry and nearby hotel is a place to be and price is at the very comfortable band.Show less

Author: kAkaLowSingapore, Singapore
Title: good food, friendly staff!
Review: This was one of the better reviews of Nyonya Cuisine in Melaka so we decided to give it a try! It was fully book but luckily we they had 2 tables outside the store so we took it anyway.They really serve great Nyonya food and the services they provided was great! To be frank, it is not costly at all.If you want to have Nyonya cuisine in Melaka, be sure to visit Amy Heritage.Show less

Author: SwaneeTehShah Alam, Malaysia
Title: Delightful... AGAIN
Review: We were at Amy's again today, our second visit. Knowing how essential it was to have a booking, we called the day before as we were travelling from KL. Making a booking was easy. Getting there today was hassle-free. Food was excellent especially the ayam goreng and yam buck keluak. The restaurant even made available small spoons to dig out the yummy contents of the buah keluak (Indonesian black nut), pure ambrosia to me what with its nutty, slightly bitter tar like consistency mixed to perfection with the sauce from this chicken dish.Having read the other comments here, my view is that if you make a booking and are on-time (we were half an hour earlier than expected), there is will not be any expected problems getting a table. We were here for the food and we got excellent food served within a comfortable environment, served without undue delay.Although stuffed, I could not resist the yummiest cendol I have ever tasted (wasn't even a fan before) again right before we went on our merry way around Malacca.Go for the food. Go for the experience. Go without reading the reviews here which focused on ranting about how they were turned away because they were late. This is Amy's Restaurant - embrace it.Show less

Author: Kerry SKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: A Great Place for Nyonya food
Review: Knowing how fastidious the owner is, and how popular this place is, we always make sure we observe 2 simple rules:1. Make a reservation; and2. Be on time.Follow these two rules, and the menu opens up to a wonderful presentation of fine nyonya cuisine served the way it has been for generations.The pai-tee, ayam buah keluak, cendol ... are but a few must haves. The house special: Nasi Kemuli - requires at least a weeks" notice. What the Kings' dishes are to the Thais, the Nasi Kemuli to the Nyonyas. (Although a stretch of imagination, you'd get the drift).Enjoy!Show less

Author: yll79Bangkok, Thailand
Title: Horrible service
Review: The moment we arrived and it's at 2pm noon. Your board says that you are open from 11.30 to 2.30pm. Immediately your waitress hand me the menu and required me to place order that instant. I wasn't even give at least 1 min to look at the menu since this is my first visit.Then the food arrived and within the same instant my cendol was sent to my table while we are still half way eating out main meal. By the time I get to my cendol it was already diluted.Then at 2.40pm you send your waitress to start sweeping the floor while we are still eating and it's a aircond place.Congrats you won the award of providing the worst service ever. Doesn't matter how good is your food but this kind of service is really bad. My first and very last.Show less

Author: pauljerSingapore, Singapore
Title: This is damn shiok
Review: Nyonya cuisine is intensely rich, gutsy and accented with tangy, pungent and sour flavors. What makes Amy Heritage Nyonya Cuisine so fascinating and different is that it exemplifies the tenets of Slow Food. Peranakan recipes do require time-consuming preparation.The food at Amy Heritage Nyonya Cuisine bears the hallmarks of the best of home cooking. The extraordinary kangkung kobis keledek masak titik lemak (water convolvulus, cabbage and sweet potatoes in coconut milk) was a superb dish which has a flavor quite unlike anything I’ve ever tasted. The ikan geram asam (fish cooked in aromatic spicy tamarind gravy with ladies finger) was well balanced and deliciously rich. The udang goreng asam (succulent prawns sautéed in thick tamarind juice) was heavenly with a nice asam dressing to finish it off.This is damn shiok. Shiok translates as conveying strong pleasure or tingling of the taste buds. This is the true truth as I say it as it is…Show less

Author: Mun Onn LSubang Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Still the best!
Review: We visited Amy's for the first time in November 2015. We were there again in November 2016. The main regret we had the first time was that there were only 2 of us (plus our toddler) so we couldn't order too much.This time round, we went with another couple and they were locals who ordered the good stuffs for us.The highlight was the fried chicken (Amy's Ayam Goreng). We also loved the Udang Nenas Lemak and the Ikan Cili Garam. Of ourse we had the Pai Tee. But we were so caught up eating and chatting that by the time we wanted to order desert, the cendol had run out.We will be back there again if we are in town!Show less

Author: lingsue123Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Reasonably priced Nyonya dinner
Review: After reading all the food blogs, we decided to make a reservation and thankfully we did, as every table were booked out when we arrived at 6.30pm on a Friday. We also decided to have dinner early as we read that it could be a long wait for food when it's crowded. True enough, service was pretty quick and we were done with dinner within 45 minutes. I loved the pai tee, hee peow soup, kangkung in lemak (not for those who aren't a fan of santan as the broth has a very strong taste of coconut milk) and assam fish. My hubby loved the chicken though I found the flavour mostly on the skin while the flesh was not so tasty. Also to note, the fishball in the hee peow soup weren't too fresh. However, generally speaking, our meal was satisfying and price was reasonable.Show less

Author: hannah3107London
Title: Poor customer service
Review: My friend booked for all of us at this restaurant. The taxi driver and all of us were completely lost as was not able to find the restaurant despite using different search maps. Called the restaurant and was informed that everyone seemed to have the same problem as their website did not provide clear instructions. My friend called the day before to confirm the booking and was not informed of directions. As we were 10 minutes late, we were informed that our table had been given to someone else!Show less

Author: 881tayk
Title: Overrated and ordinary
Review: I've tried a number of Peranakan restaurants in Melaka but a friend told me that I should try Amy Heritage and so I did. Booking a table wasn't easy and they make you feel like they are doing you a great favor if you get a table, reminding you that you need to be there on time or your table will be given away. Customer service is not foremost in this restaurant. They must have enjoyed too much success in the past and have now grown arrogant. Despite all the hype about the place, I found the standard of food there to be poor. Every dish was too sweet and lacking in traditional Peranakan flavors. I was so disappointed with the lack of authentic flavors that I wanted to drown my food with sambal chili. Guess what? You have to pay RM $2 to get sambal chili. Some chairs in the restaurant had wobbly legs. We had to try a few before finding safer chairs. Do be careful when you're there. Overall, it was a very disappointing visit. Food is not good and not cheap either. I would not go there again.Show less

Author: xiaoxuanSingapore, Singapore
Title: Arrogant boss
Review: I am giving 1* without even tasting the food. We tried numerous times to make reservations but no one answer the phone. After a long walk and found the place. We were told place was fully booked. They told us they were short of staff to answer calls ( Then why bother to put up a phone) we saw 1 or 2 tables were finishing and are willing to wait but was told not to wait around as they "do not like to rush their guest". Arrogantly we were told if we needed to eat Nonya food, we can try another restaurant next door. There are so many NonYa restaurant in Melaka. We can give this place a miss and won't be back. Show less

Author: TravellinG_SGSingapore, Singapore
Title: Excellent service, excellent food, very reasonable price
Review: Ok, first of all, this is not like any other nyonya restaurant, this requires reservation. Walk in, dun bother.... saw few been turned away....Was within walking distance from Hatten Hotel and just opposite another famous thong seng restaurant. They gotten one of the dish wrong as we want the CHILLI and fish to be separated, the boss immediately asked the waiter to change it, saying that it was their fault. Well I guess this is what you call customer service!! Impressed.I was pretty impressed with the stew chicken. Really nice....bill comes at the end and it was well lower than my expectation. Well done Amy restaurant! Now I know why so many people goes to you....Show less

Author: TimothySohSingapore, Singapore
Title: As usual great! Reservations a must! But do not walk in
Review: Delicious is the word to discribe. Without reservation, I have seen a family of 13 persons turned away. They open on the dot and not earlier . Their clock is a little slow. They told me if I was late by 5 min , my reservation would be gone. Such attitude must be backed by fantastic taste.My group of 14 were not disappointed at all. The rojak Mee, chicken buah Keras, chicken pongteh, mango salad, chap Chye, Assam fish are must tries. Overall, excellent and tasty. One of the few good Nonya food left in Melaka. Restaurant is halal so no pork.Drinks like lime juice and Chin chow are blend and bad. The chendol is so so. Forget it. Show less

Author: 555Ted
Title: Authentic Nyonya food
Review:
Large selection of  local food. Seafood was very good.
Good prices for the quality of food and service.
Make sure you make a reservation.

Author: ellybethSingapore, Singapore
Title: Dinner:)
Review: They were rather understaffed as there was only a woman waitress who solely attended to the customers. Space was rather limited so quite a few people had to leave:( Food however was worth everything! Must tries are the Ayam Goreng and Fried Rice for kids:) The soup was absolutely delicious that my family practically devoured it. The chicken wings were . The chendol was good too but too sweet. Order more chicken wings as all my family members ate at least 5-10 each! One comes with the chicken wing and the . The restaurant was nicely clean. Pie tee and rendang was ✌.Show less

Author: gckaryKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Overpriced and Arrogant Boss
Review: The food here is ok but the price is expensive. We have booked this restaurant earlier and lucky we got a table. The boss sitting at the counter is arrogant. Maybe his business is too good and he thinks that service is not important. He is rude when talking to customers.Show less

Author: 394ahl
Title: Walk-In customers, don't bother.
Review: If you don't entertain walk-ins especially during on the weekdays, don't bother having foreigners patronising your food. Driving hundreds of kilometres just to review on your popular Nyonya Delicacies is all wasted. We have other places to do reviews on. There should be something you guys are able to do. Booked for the whole day? No time slot just for 1 table? Rude form.Show less

Author: 1john316Singapore, Singapore
Title: Inconsistent Quality
Review: This restaurant is still popular and attracts quite a crowd. We've patronized this restaurant a number of times over the last two years. Our experience is that the quality of food is inconsistent and the level of service can certainly be improved. The staff needs to be more courteous in dealing with customers.Show less

Author: archmageMelbourne, Australia
Title: Consistently Good
Review: I've becoming here regularly on my trips to Melaka. If you are looking for authentic Nyonya food, this is it. Would recommend it on any trip to Melaka. Only recommendation is to book ahead as they are notorious for turning away customers during busy seasons. If you are particular on trying out certain dishes, please book those in advance to avoid disappointment.Show less

Author: Powerpuffy88Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Very Rude Boss and lousy food
Review: Visited this place recommended by a friend. Is not worth to try. The food is not up to its quality. They don't taste like any nyonya food. They are more like THAI FUSION. Besides the food the service is terrible. The lady boss is so RUDE and arrogant. We requested a simple meesiam for our diabetic aunt to be served first. She came to us and said that they can't do it. She said we have to sit and wait. Come on.. is for a diabetic person. Not for all the food. This place is not worth to even try. Don't bother. There are many nicer nyonya food restaurants in Malacca.  Show less

Author: Hawker78Burlington
Title: Review #2... WHAT HAPPENED??
Review: I came to Amy's in March of this year, and had the door's blown off my expectations of what Melakan Nyonya Restaurants could offer. Namely, the banana blossom salad, and the smoky, creamy chicken stew with buah keluak (black nut), blew my mind as very few dishes in my 6 or so years of visiting and eating around Malaysia have--such a richness and symphonic construction of flavors, it was everything I hoped Nyonya food would be like, but rarely lived up to. Fast forward to December. WHAT HAPPENED? Ikan Asam Pedas (sour/spicy fish)--a Malaysian staple, and a Melakan Nyonya specialty--was thin, watery, a little sour, and bland. Absolutely no depth, and we're pretty sure the fish was cooked seperately and chucked into the kuah at the last minute. I've had all kinds of asam pedas around the country. This was the worst. Another favorite, sambal petai udang (prawns with "stink beans"), was made with tiny, precooked shrimp, without shells and without flavor, another "worst" rendition, and I'm simply shocked how pedestrian this was, after offering two of the best Nyonya dishes I've ever eaten. I'll be back, for sure, but I'm calling ahead to see if the bunga pisang dish is available.Show less

Author: kingnyuk
Title: Disappointing food quality
Review:
The duck soup was tasteless. Mixed vegetables was undercooked. Fish tasted like eating paper. Crispy chicken wings were ordinary.
 Over priced menu with overrated reviews.
We do not recommend this restaurant.

Author: colink987Singapore, Singapore
Title: Good Peranakan food but not the best
Review: My advice is to reserve first before you go. We made a reservation and had to TT a deposit to the owner. Fair enough cos I understand this restaurant is always full house. The restaurant is quite small so it quickly fills up during meal time. I hv read quite a few complaints about the owner. My opinion is that he's alright and don't expect the PR sort of person who will ask you how's the food etc.Generally the food is good and authentic Peranakan. Pity they don't serve pork cos some of the Peranakan dishes are better with pork than with chicken meat. I also felt that the sambal chili is a bit too salty. The consistency of the fish maw soup is also too 'thin' and can hardly taste the fish maw in it. My favourite is the fried fish with chili topping.Show less

Author: Tene17
Title: Worth it
Review: First time trying baba nyonya food here recommended by my sister. The food was really delicious especially the asam pedas fish and the tauhu. But gotta reserve here for large groups coz it's always house full.

Author: PennyPngSingapore, Singapore
Title: Arrogant boss, bad service attitude and lousy food.
Review: The owner was arrogant and he was making a fuss throughout about the no. of chairs down to the numbers of plates and utensils we are using as we have few children (4 in exact) who requires proper seats and serving plates. The food were served very fast but the taste was lousy and cannot be customized when we asked for non-spicy fried noodles for the children. We do not feel the taste was authentic and the juices were all syrup and diluted, simply tasteless! And the staff were full of attitude and rushing us when taking the orders and chasing us to finish the food. It is an expensive and lousy experience after all and we will definitely not want to go back ever again!Show less

Author: BorneoJessieKota Kinabalu, Malaysia
Title: Delicious home cooked Nonya food
Review: Took a taxi out to Amy's as it was located in Melaka Jaya, far from our hotel in Jonker Street. We arrived around 6pm without a reservation as it was mid week. We were VERY LUCKY to get a table as the places was very popular with both the locals and the tourists. We saw people who have booked being turned away through out the evening.The layout was simple and the service was polite and good.We have the Sambal Jangtung Pisang ( Bud of the banana flower in a tangy salad dressing) to start. I finally get a chance to try the Ayam Buah Keluak which was very tasty - the chicken is tender and the gravy is tasty and thick. Then we ordered the Fish in Chilli and Garlic topping with the Prawn and Pineapple Curry. I also ordered a portion of the Mee Siam to try. I have not have Mee Siam for a very long time. It was not bad. I finished with the Cendol.. which was not as good as others in Melaka. Overall, the food was well prepared and quite huge in portions for the 2 of us. It was tasty and we would recommend them to others. We will tell them to book in advance to be on the safe side.Show less

Author: PA- C
Title: Bad Attitude
Review: Owner has a lot of air in him.Even though restaurant closes at 2.30pm, we arrived at 1.15pm and our last order was at 1.30pm.After that we could not order anything else except for rice and plain water.Full of attitude when taking our order and was rushing. The sambal was salty, lime juice was syrup based and not fresh,the prawns lemak was average and we could not even top up the gravy even though we were willing to pay extra.He treats his servers like a dictator and scrutinises their every move.Even declined to serve us chendol.Turned down a family entering the restaurant at 2pm even though sign says 2.30pm.Severely overated restaurant overall!!!Show less

Author: W3407BYkevinsLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Bit out of the way but worth it
Review: There's not much else nearby by ways of tourist attractions so it took us a while to find this place after we got a recommendation from our contact at the hotel.Despite this, and judging from the reviews, we may have got lucky to get a table despite having no reservation. Arriving at around 1pm, it was quite busy.I thought the restaurant was very clean and the decor was simple but effective. The menu contained a small insight to Nyonya food in general and the history of the resturant, which I found interesting. Food wise, the menu choices stayed in line with the decor, simple. I wasn't overwhelmed with choice but that didn't matter as the menu contained local food which all looked very tasty.We ordered an Assam fish dish and a Prawn dish in a curry sauce, the name of which escapes me right now...! In any case, both dishes arrived looking like a lot of care was made in preparing. Though it took a while to arrive, we overlooked this as it was pretty busy with a couple of very large groups... The food was tasty. No further complaints were made after.Price was not the cheapest but was still good value due to the quality.I'd highly recommend this restaurant, it was a real highlight to my short stay in Melaka. I just wish there were more like this within the old town district. Tourists deserve to taste this local food instead of being fed generic chain-restaurant rubbish in all the malls.Show less

Author: SarmilaA5
Title: Interesting
Review: Helpful and friendly staffs. Managed to accommodate my reservation even though we were a bit late. Food was nice and nice place

Author: Cin_Fab_JJSingapore, Singapore
Title: bad service
Review: had placed a phone reservation at 7pm for table of 3+1 while in singapore. should have double confirmed n make sure the owner heard me correctly. dear advisers. please make sure you reconfirm the time with the owner. arrived at 708pm. made to stand with my kids more than 10 mins and being told off by the owner that they have given up my table be cos I made a booking at 630pm. smmore he said that even if I did indeed made a 7pm booking, I'm already late. we are only 8 mins late and by the time we were made to stand and wait, a further 10 minutes more have gone by. can you imagine my husband n I having to cross so many busy and dangerous traffic streets from hotel equatorial go get to this restaurant. at least he should have bothered to suggest we wait for a while more to see if the next booking does turn up at 730pm. why would I walk all the way over if I'm sure my booking is at 630pm n not 7pm. sweating n panting.serving nonya cuisine and getting mostly good reviews doesn't make your restaurant an excellent if you are not an empathetic ownerShow less

Author: VeldsparSingapore, Singapore
Title: Lovely.
Review: This restaurant represented Malaysian cuisine on a global scale, and the standard makes it easy to see why.Book early if you want to eat here? There is only the one chef, and there is limited seating (we were amazingly lucky and got in due to an unexpected cancellation, or we may not have gotten a place).Everything was pretty amazing. The best items of what we ordered were the special fried chicken (amazingly juicy yet crisp, and surprisingly not oily), the itik tim duck soup (savoury, with a sweet lingering aftertaste due to the addition of sour plum), and the sotong goreng (juicy fresh squid deep fried to perfection).The place is clean, well-kept and quiet (they do not encourage queueing or loitering), and the food is well worth it for a very affordable price.Definitely worth it if you are going to Malacca.Show less

Author: YogananthanD24Bangalore District, India
Title: Dissapointing
Review: Arrived there at 1130am, the restaurant was empty, but we were turned away on the grounds that they were fully booked, and upon inquiring how long we have to wait to get a table we were told that they are booked after that also. If they are booked, a closed sign has to placed on the door indicating that its not open for walk in. Instead of giving ridiculous explanation. Show less

Author: ScubaDy
Title: Best nyonya food in town
Review: If you haven't tried Amy's you should. But you need to call up and make a reservation otherwise you will be disappointed. The food is nyonya style and every spoonful is a burst of flavors.

Author: Aqeil A
Title: Good place for lunch/diner
Review: 1- always make reservation prior to coming here..*read: compulsory.2-the food served was nice n tasty3-choices are limited but who would've ordered everything on the menu anyways?! 4-clean n neat premise5-the owner has a great accomplishments thru out her 9yrs business6-food are priced fairly reasonable.7-u might gotta wait awhile before being served as they're short of staffs.Show less

Author: DoreenC292
Title: Authentic Nyonya food
Review: The nyonya food served here are good and authentic. Love the Lemak udang nenas, ayam pongteh, buah keluak and pai tee. It is advisable that you make reservation well ahead. This restaurant if popular and they seldom take walk ins. Because they are popular, the person taking reservation may sound a little unfriendly. Overall good nyonya food served here and at a reasonable price too.Show less

Author: yss97Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Excellent Peranakan food
Review: Went for lunch and the manager said she was about to give away our table as we were late! But, after that, things went much better. We had ayam pongteh, prawn curry with pineapple, otak-otak, pie tee & chap chai (mixed veg). All were excellent. The style of cooking was more home-style but delicious. The chendol was nice also but for some reason did not have red beans. Would recommend especially if you like unfussy but good tasting food. Show less

Author: flyingace28Malaysia
Title: Very nice peranakan food
Review: Very delicious nyonya food. We had ayam pong teh (Braised chicken with potatoes in bean sauce with ‘gula melaka’)- very nice, thick and full of flavor, nicest pong teh I have ever tasted; Prawn goreng Asam (mediocre) ; ayam buah keluak (chicken in Nyonya spicy gravy with black nuts) - amazing taste and gravy. The steamed rice is served in the traditional nyonya red & black basket. Very unique. Thumbs up aunty AMY!Reservations recommended, as it gets crowded.Show less

Author: medsp3cSingapore, Singapore
Title: Great dinner
Review: Amy Heritage serves great food. We ordered 4 dishes and there was nothing to complain about in terms of quality and quantity. The best dish we had was the fried rice and definitely worth a try! This restaurant has a rather small sitting capacity (30~35 pax) so better to make a reservation ahead of your visit. We saw the staff turn away many patrons who did not make resevations.Show less

Author: jeannie wSingapore, Singapore
Title: Rich & satisfying dinner!
Review: The night that we had dinner at Amy Heritage Nyonya Cuisine, it was full house! Good thing we had a reservation. Restaurant was filled with tourists and locals, which is a good sign! We ordered Ayam Buah Keluah (Chicken stew with "black nuts"), Udang Lemak Nenas (Prawn with pineapples & coconut milk) & a vegetable dish for the 2 of us. Serving portion is big! All 3 dishes are yummy and very well cooked. We're so busy eating that we forgot to take pictures of the food! :)Show less

Author: Lina_TanSGSingapore, Singapore
Title: Over-rated and disappointing food
Review: We visited the restaurant for lunch. The quality of the food was disappointing. We were served cold rice which we rejected and subsequently replaced hot steaming rice. The fish otar just fish cake wrapped with curry coconut paste - one of the worst otar I ever eaten. The chendol is also lacking - dilute coconut and no red beans. All their dishes paled in comparison to the dishes in other Nonya restaurants that we visited in Malacca. Show less

Author: ahmedeA4934GDDubai, United Arab Emirates
Title: Worth the hype
Review: I was a bit cautious after reading some bad reviews regarding the service. Then, when I was making the booking the guy answering the phone seemed a bit rude, so I went expecting the worst. I was proved wrong. First of all, Amy is a legend! She cooks all the food herself (she is a descendent of peranakans) and is a very warm and lovely lady. She welcomed us and took the order herself.The other guy serving at the tables (I think same guy who answers the phone) was polite and nice enough as well.The food was just so good! No fuss, just home-made-style delicious Nyonya food. We wanted to order the whole menu.Prices are quite affordable.Be sure to reserve a table at least a day in advance if not more. Show less

Author: Long MKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Nice place away from down town, but...
Review: Called up to make a table booking for 20 people for dinner.The person taking the call said a deposit of MYR200 is required. So was given their bank account number and did the deposit transfer Also letting him know the time we will be there, 7.00 - 7.30pmAfter doing so, in order not to wait for food, we place the order for food too.Since the ordering and negotiating is done through whatsapp and phone calls, we were given a menu list. The menu list was without picture and description as well as price. This was a little bit of work needed to find out what they have and also the description and picture as example.For that have to refer some where else for picture and description.Once confirming the order and also the estimated total bill amount. We went ahead.Came the day for the dinner, we arrived around 6.43 pm. Well, we were earlier than expected. They still accommodate us as there were not that busy and it is also a week day.Met and chatted with the person who took our orders and booking. The down side is he is not tactful in telling people that any items with pork are not allowed to be inside the restaurant premises. Drinks were ordered on site, as this is rather individual preferences.As we have pre-ordered our food, the food came quickly.Dishes ordered were 01 Pie Tee02 Hee Peow Soup (Fish maw soup)03 Kangkong Kobis Keledek Masak Titik Lemak04 Ikan Gerang Asam05 Sambal Udang Petai06 Udang Lemak Nenas07 Ayam Pongteh08 Chap Chye09 Otak Otak10 Ikan Cili GaramAll our ordered dishes are pretty average. The Sambal Udang Petai is good, but too little petai. The Udang Lemak Nenas is okay, but very soupy. Can take the gravy like soup. Even the Kangkong Kobis Keledek Masak Titik Lemak and the Ayam Pongteh's gravy were rather soupy too.The interior is well decorated but not too much. Just that when the noise levels goes up, it echoes.It is a nice little nyonya restaurant away from down town with ample parking, but the human relations and food is just so soShow less

Author: eirikl2016
Title: Lousy service
Review: I hv booked a table at 12noon n was told twice by the staff tat my table will onli b reserve until 1230 noon. I hv arrived at 1225noon n was informed that the first rule is to arrive punctually n there is no such thing as keeping my table for certain period. The male black face staff is extremely rude n implying tat i m lying!! The staff also didnt offer any solutions...yes ur arrogant because your biz is dann good but nothing last 4everShow less

Author: jamietheincredible
Title: Tantalizing food. Definitely going back.
Review: Absolutely lip-smacking food. Everything was up to my expectation and there are always ppl waiting in line. Booking in advanced is highly recommended.

Author: jolttSingapore, Singapore
Title: Call to make reservation before going
Review: This is a small restaurant which is very popular with locals and tourists. We visited without any reservation and was almost turned away. Fortunately, the owner agreed to let us sit on the table outside, as all the tables were taken up by reservations. We turned up before 6pm and after we ended our dinner around 6.40pm, only half the restaurant is occupied, as the rest of the reservation have not turned up yet. Maybe the owner should try to do more business to sit guests with no reservation, but promised to finish up in time for the next round of guests. The initial feel that I got from the owner was a bit of rude, but then again, I can understand as he was all alone in taking orders, making and serving drinks and the food. But my suggestion is to be nice and patient as we are customers who have come far to try at your restaurant, hence, be nice. Food wise, the kueh pie ti and the Fish Rebus were really nice. The chap chai (mixed vegetable in bean paste) was different from the usual chap chai I had. I think I still prefer the usual ones with lots of cabbage, vermicelli and black fungus type. The chendol is also average as the ice shaving was not fine. So overall, I would rate it average, not die die must try.  Show less

Author: Cikgu
Title: Managing expectations
Review: I visited Amy's at a recommendation of an office colleague. It was billed as the best he's eaten and that reservation is a must. The same was confirmed by the driver of our van and he volunteered to drive to Amy's to make a reservation. The restaurant is very easily accessible especially for those staying at Mahkota or Hatten. It is alongside Mahkota and behind Hatten and Estadia Hotels.We booked a table for 6 at 6.30pm. Arrived there punctually as we had been told that if we were late, our table would be given up. All tables had reserved signs on them and some walk-in customers were turned away. We felt they could have been accommodated as the tables remained unoccupied even when we left the restaurant.We ordered some nonya staples like chap chye, ikan chilli garam (which was recommended by other reviewers) hee peow soup, fried chicken and ayam pong teh. The ikan chilli garam was quite disappointing as I expected a quick fried chunky chilli sauce rather than a bowl of finely ground sambal. The soup was clear, quite tasty. The ingredients were a little unusual for hee peow soup. Very little hee peow (fish maw) and they were not puffed up at all. Apart from the de riguer cabbage, carrot and fishball, the soup had angled loofah, quail eggs and fresh mushroom. Fresh shiitake mushroom in soup is not too good as it had turned sour. My friends were not keen on the chap chye because they felt it was not braised enough and felt alot like stirfried vegetables.Ayam pongteh was good and the chicken was well cooked and tender. The fried chicken was also good but nothing spectacular.Service was so so. The menu only has two sizes - medium and large. When we mistakenly said we'd take a small portion, the manager impatiently pointed out that they only had medium and large, no small. He did not repeat our order and hence one of our vege dishes did not arrive. We were quite happy for it and did not complain since we were not charged for it either. No other sambal was served at the table. Sambal chilli was charged at RM2 a portion. We asked for it in the middle of dinner but the sambal did not come till we had eaten most of our food. However the server apologised and took back the sambal. All in all, a so-so experience. The ladies in our group did not ask for name cards hence it will not be a place we will return to.Show less

Author: jenlauwlKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Nice food but bad service
Review: Recommended by friend to try out this restaurant and booked a table. You need to book in advance or else it’s hard to get a table. The nyonya food here is nice. We ordered few dishes and one of the dishes served was not what we wanted. We told the boss that is sitting in the counter but he refused to change and even showed us one kind of face.Show less

Author: Juni1984Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Reservations is a MUST to not be disappointed
Review: Amy the owner is a nyonya lady herself and does not hire that many help to keep the quality of the food. You see her around taking orders and chatting with guests. Highly recommended dishes at this pork-free restaurant is the chilli salt fish and chicken pongteh. Portions are generous and they are not stingy with the ingredients used. Make sure that you make reservations at least 1 -day in advance to ensure you get a place at the restaurant. Lunch is from 11.30am to 2pm, and they only serve one round of lunch. Example if you reserve a table at 1pm, the table will be kept empty from 11.30am until you arrive. So you can arrive earlier but if late by 10 mins, she will open your table to walk-ins. Same goes for dinner time as well.Show less

Author: Linda TSingapore, Singapore
Title: Sedap (Delicious) Nonya Food
Review: It was a weekend of makan (eat) and shopping spree in Melaka and Amy Heritage Nonya Cuisine) was on our check list. Having made advance reservation via a phone call. We were not disappointed with our lunch there. The kueh pie were tasty. The assam ikan was sedap too and so was the udang (prawns) masak nanas. The nonya mee was very sedap very similiar to my mum's home cooked version. The chicken cooked with candle nut (buah keras) was yummy. But the otak was a disappointment, as the rempah has a very strong kunyit (turmeric) taste which overwhelm the flavour. The chap chye was disappointing, the gravy was too sweet and the cabbage was hard. We had chendol for dessert and it was ok. The gula melaka was very wangi (fragrant) but quite diluted. Using freshly squeezed coconut (santan) would have enhanced the flavour further. Overall we enjoyed the lunch very much. And will return to try the buah keluak and other nonya dishes. A note of advice. Do call to make reservation at least a day or two in advance.Show less

Author: WeiHanLai
Title: Clean. Comfortable nyonya dinning
Review:
Very nice restaurant suitable for local and tourist. Lady boss is friendly to serve. Do note that once you order they prepare and serve accordingly. If you have extra order, you have to wait a while. 
Toilet is clean, if that's your concern :)

Author: patriciakoh1974Singapore, Singapore
Title: No.1 Favorite Nonya Rest
Review: This has always been my MUST have whenever I dropped by Melaka. Had dinner with a friend on last visit...Yummy..... It's been 2 years since my last visit. The taste always stay in my mouth and memory. And please don't forget to have the chendol to end the wonderful mealShow less

Author: k7cqPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: A nice place for trying Nyonya cuisine
Review: It is a small but clean and well done restaurant. I had never had Nyonya style food before and I liked most but not all. There are a number of Nyonya restaurants in Melaka, so do your research and pick the one that sounds right for you.Show less

Author: katrineangSingapore, Singapore
Title: One year on and still good!
Review: I had dinner at Amy's again, a year since my last visit and review. The Kueh Pie Tee is still the best and there's no regrets. They have since given their menu a new look - a sign of good times!I'm a Nonya and we are generally fussy eaters. I packed the Buah Keluak, since the portion was generous and it's better than when I had it there. It has to do with Nonya style cooking - once the dish is well stewed, the flavours just blend and works great. They used a little more assam (I think), but it's still delicious.Show less

Author: barryf975hong kong
Title: Family restaurant worth finding
Review: Jn Melaka Raya stretches out through one of the city's least attractive areas, part of a massive reclamation zone dotted with high-star hotels and boring shops. Amy's tenement shophouse is one good reason to take a fixed-price taxi (RM20) out there. Arrive early, pre-reserved if possible, for lunch or dinner, before menu items are sold out. We ended up with a fine fresh vegetable soup (Hee Peow) and a rich black-nut chicken stew (Ayah Buah Keluak) that was admirably both tenderly tasty and chewy. Fair, average prices (RM 25/27, medium portions, with lime juice at RM2.It closes in the afternoons, last orders at 1:30 pm.Show less

Author: jazzng2015Singapore, Singapore
Title: Different taste and bad service!
Review: Very disappointed with this restaurant. 2 years ago, a group of friends and myself came for their food, the elderly boss recommended us for their signature dishes and it was really nice and a real authentic Nyonya food in Melacca. Another selling point needed to highlight to this shop was their friendly service and off course the elderly boss friendly recommendion. Therafter, I strongly recommended to all my oversea friends and relatives who visited Melacca. However yesterday,we came with disappointment. The taste of their authentic nonya food has gone. Pee tee was one of their signature dishes and most customers came for this but was not available.The Hee peow soup was over putting sugar. We seems like taking sugar water instead of soup. The Sambal Petai prawn taste like "chili sugar prawn",the fragrance and spicy taste have gone. The taste of Nyonya cooking was totally disappeared and totally different from what we had it before.During the whole dinner course,we didnt see the elderly boss but only can see all new and young inexperienced stuffs chasing customers away and have double standard service.We reached there at 5.40pm and was told all tables were fully reserved. We asked for alternatives such as having a quick 45mins meal since a few tables were reserved for after 7pm. One of the waiters said their policy is since a table is reserved for dinner, they will not allow to give to another customer even the reservation is after 7pm. Since we crave go the food, we requested to sit outside the restaurant which has a small table. One of the waiters accepted us with very reluctant and no smiling face. During our 45mins dinner, 2 caucasian ladies came without reservation. We overheard their conversation. Initially they were being rejected, and when they left the restaurant, the waiter offered them to come back at 8pm for dinner. We were surprised that the waiter provide double standard. In our customer's eye, it seems like change of management. Last but not least, no matter how this resturant changes their service policy, food is still important to customers.The authentic way of cooking must keep instead of the changes and the original taste of it also missing and disappeared.Show less

Author: AidanEmily
Title: Nyonya cuisine - Make your way there!
Review:
Simple and Delicious cuisine with reasonable price. Restaurant may close earlier than the signboard time and do make your way there early to find a table.

The waiting time is reasonable even for full house. Near Hatten Square and easy to find.

Author: LowylMalaysia
Title: Food below expectation
Review: Need to queue to get a table, but the foods served were not up to my expectation. Fried chicken wings taste good. Cincaluk omelette taste ok. Ordered assam fish and it not aromatic, with sour tastes only. Not only that, the fish is not fresh. The cendol has only 3 ingredients in there which were ice, cendol and brown sugar. Thus, it's only sweet tasting . Utter disappointment. Show less

Author: huiyel
Title: Best Nyonya Food I've ever had!
Review:
We had a very satisfying meal here.
All the dishes are sooo delicious and we enjoyed every single dish.
Will be back for sure when I visit Melaka next time!

Author: Kittychat28Singapore, Singapore
Title: Peranakan Cuisine
Review: One of a number of restaurants serving Nonya food. One of the better ones too. Only disappointment was that my ayam buah keluak had only 3 nuts and one of them was empty. When I mentioned to the owner, he just said it fell out while cooking and did not want to replace it. Come on boss, it's only US 20 cents at most!.I hear they turn away couples as they only want larger groups.Show less

Author: Hyoga83Bordeaux, France
Title: Elaborate and different
Review: Although we missed the wow factor I was hoping to get, we enjoyed our dinner here. Being European we have no idea how Nonya food should be, but our dishes were tasty and the portions generous.I did find excessive the difference in price between the chicken we ordered (17 rm) and the fish: 40 rm!! This was not known during the order as it was "as per market"....Show less

Author: Angiebee7577
Title: Nice food nice people
Review: Great finger licking food. Very friendly staff that is good at recommend food. Will be back again for more !

Author: Leesukim
Title: Delicious authentic nyonya food in Malacca
Review: I'm always being asked where to get good and authentic nyonya food when in Malacca. There are lots of Nyonya restaurants in Malacca some of which are good , some disappointing and some passable. Currently I 'd say the best is Amy Heritage Nyonya Cuisine. Nyonya dishes here are delicious and authenitc, cooked and supervised by Nyonya Amy herself. It gets very crowded though and resefvations should be made to avoid disappointment. A good range of nyonya dishes to choose from followed by the wonderful dessert of chendol. Prices are reasonable too considering the labour involved in cooking nyonya food. Show less

Author: ZoakiesMalaysia
Title: Nice home-made food
Review: Going there after reading some review in TripAdvisor.... Didnt hold up high expectation in such a highly recommended nyonya restaurant in Melaka coz i been to few but its just over-rated in my honest opinion.This is something different!!The taste of their Nyonya food is kindda homely made type... Not too commercial and their taste suit to my taste bud.Love their fried chicken wings and Pai-Tee... The taste is just awesome... the brinjal taste good too but too bad the fish sambal is not too into my style. If you into dessert, the Nyonya cendul is a must try... They put in sago into their cendul is something different.. Well, after i have tried few nyonya restaurant in Melaka, i would recommend give this Amy Heritage Nyonya Cuisine Restaurant a try. It's not hard to find...it's located in Melaka Raya, right opposite road of the Allianz Insurance office... Tables are limited, so making a reservation is preferably. Parking shouldn't be a problem as right outside the restaurant got plentiful of it. Be there early...as their last call is 9pm...Show less

Author: Panda6551
Title: Almost like grandma's cooking
Review: Of course everyone's grandma food is the best.  I think Amy comes close.  They also have food that we seldom get like Nasi kemuli.  Make reservations to avoid disappointment.

Author: CheokHorPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: Authentic Nyonya food
Review: Highly recommended by a friend who is a local baba. Tried the following dishes. Asam Prawn - somewhat disappointed. The Asam paste is not authenticItek Tim soup - this is tasty although the serving temperature is a bit low. Teluk dadar cincaluk - this is the best Kangkung kobis keledek - very good and authentic.Overall I have good experience and would recommend this place to friends. Need reservation to avoid disappointmentShow less

Author: Aaron NSingapore
Title: Reservations recommended
Review: We heard about Amy's from a few people, and we thought why not try to make reservations. We had the good fortune of getting a table one day in advance, as it was only the 2 of us.The restaurant employs a reservation system which gives customers the assurance that they don't have to wait for a table if they had make a reservation. This also allows customers to eat at their own pace, without being hurried or chased off by the wait staff. (Although we did see many potential customers arriving and leaving dejectedly, because they didn't reserve a table) This system probably ensures that the food is freshly prepared and not produced en masse.All in all, homely Nyonya flavours in a no fuss restaurant. You'll have to try it yourself!Show less

Author: JoshChuiSingapore, Singapore
Title: Freshly cooked nyonya food
Review: This restaurant serves freshly prepared food. It is not up to my taste buds but thats very subjective. Contrary to the remarks made, our visit was pleasure. Amy explained why the restaurant can't take in anymore customers despite the reserved tables are for customers who are coming an hour later. If you want to eat at this restaurant, just book a table a few days ahead. Food was ok. No wow factor.Show less

Author: Ericalow
Title: Yummy food!
Review: Their food is superb. The best nyonya food among the few I have tried. Highly recommended. Please ensure you make a reservation.

Author: BrotherDragonSingapore
Title: Highly Recommended But Food Quality Is Unacceptable
Review: Foodie friends of mine in Singapore and Malacca highly recommended this restaurant to me. Being a huge fan of Peranakan food I was in all anticipation. Phone reservation for a table was made a week earlier for I was told the place is always fully booked.For the three of us, I ordered the Kueh Pie Ti, Ayam Buah Keluak, Item Tim, Otak Otak Panggang, Ikan Cilli Garam, Telur Dadar Cinchaluk, Chap Chye and Udang Goreng Asam.The Kueh Pie Tee starter kicked off to a very good start. Flavourful and delicious, the pastry shell was crispy and fresh tasting.But after that, it was downhill all the way.Next to arrive was the Itek Tim (duck with salted vegetables soup). It tasted ducky and it came warm, not hot. And it was served in a chipped bowl.The Ikan Cilli Garam, fried fish slices topped with a spicy sauce. While the sauce was delicious and not too salty, the fish meat was soft and mushy. Certainly not very fresh fish. Quality control failed badly here.The Otak-Otak Panggang was just a slab of fish cake coated with a coconuty rempah (spice paste). Fish cake? Maybe that's their style, but it is the first time I have eaten this version in a Peranakan restaurant. And it came steamed not grilled as advertised. Usually, the fish meat is minced and mixed with the spice paste and then either steamed or grilled.The Udang Goreng Asam tasted right but why so much gravy? Isn't it supposed to be drier? The highlight of a peranakan meal is usually the Ayam Buah Keluak, chicken cooked with keluak nuts in a spicy sauce. Again, the sauce was great but three of the six buay keluak nuts were one step away of being rancid. How could this be allowed in a nyonya kitchen? The cook would have been banished from the kitchen for life!The Telur Dadlar Cincaluk and Chap Chye were okay but nothing to rave about.After this bad experience, we didn't dare order any of the desserts and waste more money.I don't know what happened to this restaurant as I trusted my foodie friends' tastebuds. But never again will I step into it.Show less

Author: Wheelers7Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Overrated !
Review: 1st visit. We are really excited when we managed to secure a table for dinner on sunday night (phone booking a day earlier).Food is only average ! There are other good peranakan restaurants with friendlier service than this much hyped place. The greatest dissapointment are chendol (ice is coarse and can't really taste the fresh coconut milk) and titik lemak (bland and some vege not properly cooked) !Show less

Author: Gerald KSingapore
Title: Still the best nyonya food I've tasted in Melaka
Review: Best nyonya food that I've tasted so far in Melaka! Please make a reservation before you go. Everytime I eat there, I always see people get turned away. We went there on Sunday lunchtime hoping to make a reservation for Sunday dinner, but it was already fully booked. They were closed on Monday, so the soonest we could eat there was Tuesday lunch before returning home, and so we made a reservation for Tuesday lunch.Basically, Amy serves only one sitting each time (lunch/dinner) because she wants to maintain the quality of her food rather than to earn more money by getting as many people into the restaurant. I respect that of her.My wife and I ate the pietee, chicken pongteh, and udang (prawn) nanas lemak, and we enjoyed it, and almost slurped up all the gravy. Just having plain rice with the gravy was already so good. The food is rich, tasty, and flavorful. Will definitely return again!Show less

Author: Mun Onn LSubang Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Best Nyonya food I've ever had
Review: This place was recommended by a friend who lives in Melaka. We were advised to make reservations and it was a good thing that we did for it was fully booked.When we tasted the food, we understood why. To me, the food was excellent!The pie tee was the best i've ever had. It looked normal but it tasted so good. The "basket" was so light and crunchy and this went well with the "stuffing".I love the chicken pongteh - i actually finished up al the gravy. Sweet and savory at the same time, the chicken meat was nice and tender.The assam fish was pretty good too. So was the mixed vege. Fresh vege cooked the nyonya way.The hero of the night was the cendol. This was the best cendol we have ever had. Sure, the ice was a little coarse but taste wise, it was simply delicious! The gula melaka was soooooo good!My only regret was that there were only 2 of us with our toddler so we could not order more dishes!Amy herself attended to us and made us feel comfortable and at home - like we were visiting her house and having a meal there.Show less

Author: Aidanaj
Title: Overrated eatery
Review: Went on Tuesday, for dinner pasted on door "for booking only" disappointed we went day 2 Arrived 1130am greeted by a lady owner who's hospitality is something that needs to work on. She seems to be keen to have patron that is local and elderly and main priority is to share her business stories that she forgets other patron around. Let's talk about food 1.
