Fried chicken - normal and tad dry easily could get anywhere 2. Goreng Asam Udang - great 3. Ladies finger - great.. a tang of sweet, slight spicy and an array of herbs and cincaluk4. Buah Keluak chicken - taste great unfortunate a bit overcook even then chicken thigh a slight tough. 5. Cendol - gular Melaka was superb 6. Pie tie look great presentation but a bit oily on bottom Definitely overrated and too hyped up about the establishment. Owner lacking the passion to serve food and too haughty to be on food serving industry.Show less

Author: Christina_tankySingapore, Singapore
Title: Will Return for Pie Tee
Review: My husband and I had a sumptuous nyonya feast here. We had pie tees, hee piew soup, ayam pongteh, udang masak nanas, and telur dadar cincaluk. We enjoyed every single dish and even order second helping for pie tees. Amy's pie tee is one of the best I tasted so far. We made reservation a week ahead. The restaurant only take in the number of customers that they can manage especially during weekends, even it means to leave the tables empty for the guest who will come later. So, please please please - call in advance to avoid disappointment. Show less

Author: DarhicrKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Over rating of yr outlet
Review: Our family group was there last month with high expectation to saviour authentic Nyonya food. Regretfully, most of the food we ordered, tasted average only. We believe your outlet was over rated. The most memorable incident was when our cendol was served straight from the fridge. (cendol was frozen and the grated ice was coarse).Show less

Author: Winnie_L_123
Title: Must book before go
Review: I did not able to try. Since been told by owner that we must make booking before go. But this is something should not happen ! How can a restaurant fully booked with empty tables. Only do one round of business???

Author: 1_OrangMelaka
Title: Dinner with wife's sisters
Review:
Kerabu Mangga is my favourite since I first tried this dish Thai-style in Kelantan back in 1993.

After that I continue to hunt for this dish.

Now, Friday 9 October 2015 8:07, I am again enjoying this dish at Amy Heritage Nyonya Cuisine Restaurant.

Author: EricK388
Title: So So La
Review: We had Fried Rice, Assam Fish, Fried Mee, some Prawns in chilli source. Food so so, may be we are not a Nyonya Food lover

Author: DrRachael
Title: Excellent authentic peranakan food and friendly service
Review: We visited the restaurant as it was our first time in malaysia and were searching for authentic local food. A sign on the door said "bookings only tonight", however they were kind enough to let us straight in anyway and seat us. There are lots of certificates and accolades on the wall highlighting Amy's expertise in this cuisine. The food was absolutely delicious and reasonably priced. The decor is basic but it doesnt matter, its all about the food.Show less

Author: Tee_MalaccaMelaka, Malaysia
Title: The boss has WORST manner
Review: My family and I arrive here around 7:30pm at night. All the tables are occupied. But the workers are cleaning two combined tables, which another one family is waiting for the tables.The boss said there is no empty table, and ask us to leave. Okay, I can leave, no problem. Then, the family who is waiting said that they only need one table. So the two combined tables can be separated and we can use another table.Buy the boss just looks at us in very angry and impatient mood, tells us that even the family is okay to only use one table, but is not okay for him. He just uses the rude body language and the words "no no no" to chase us out.I got shocked on the spot, what is this kind of manner in the world? We ask him politely but the respond he gives us is so bad and rude! If he wants to close the shop early today, he can just tell us, instead of making excuses with such bad manner.My family used to visit this restaurant always few years back, but now I will definitely not come again!Show less

Author: ChanMLPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: We had 11 pax gearing to have a great nyonya lunch in Malacca
Review: We were recommended by a fren to make sure we go to Amy's for a real nyonya meal. We booked a day ahead but was turned down, so we opted for the following day. We ordered at least 11 dishes as there were 11 adults that day. What came out great was the fried noodles served with sambal. This was the first dish and we were full of praises for it. Once the rest was served, we all agreed it's just average. The prawns and fish was not fresh. The otak(steam fish with spices)was a real let down. We could get this from the stalls in town. The soup and vegetables was also nothing great. I must say the cendol thou is nice. We left the restaurant, all agreeing we won't visit this place again. BTW, within the group there were a few nyonya among us.Show less

Author: ChanMLPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Grossly overrated nyonya restaurant
Review: It was highly recommended for us to have a meal at Amy's. This was a constant reminder from my frens aunt even before we reached Malacca. We were asked to book days' ahead to avoid disappointment.Making a phone call to Amy's already din impress us, a group of 11 frens. We were told she can't take bookings for 11!!!My friend was speechless since she was informed maximum she can accommodate was 10. The phone was passed to me and I finally managed to obtain a booking for lunch on Sunday. All geared to try out this place, we were there sharp at 12noon. We ordered majority of recommended dishes to try, alas to our disappointment more than half of the dishes were below average. Don't order seafood at Amy's, all was not fresh namely fish n prAwns. What we all agreed was good was nyonya fried noodles, chendol and ladies finger. The rest were mediocre and some were not palatable. Don't order the otak otak(steam fish wiv spicy paste). You can get the same thing at Baba Charlie's. It was a real disappointment. Show less

Author: Eeling LKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Absolutely Fabulous Authentic Nyonya Cooking
Review: I have been on various food trip to Melaka and I have tried a few peranakan nyonya food places in the past years but nothing is as good as compared to Amy's. Once you tried Amy's, you will know what is authentic peranakan nyonya food and the average peranakan nyonya food. This is a small privately owned restaurant with limited tables. Do your reservations early with them (i.e. one week before your trip) or else please expect to walk out disappointed. I walked in at 6.30pm and the "CLOSED" sign is already at the entrance. The place is fully booked for the night. I am one of those who made my reservations early!!During my dinner session (roughly about two hours) noted that they only serve one round of crowd. From how I interpret this, the owner would like to maintain the food at the best quality and highest standard. If you are a fan of Asian food (hot, spicy and flavourful), there are no words that you can used to perfectly describe the food at Amy's until you have tried it yourself.Show less

Author: flowi fKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Excellent Peranakan Food
Review: Was recommended by local friends and was sceptical as most peranakan's food tasted the same. Expectations was not overwhelming at that time but trust me ... IT'S AWESOME. Small restaurant managed by family members and service is so so but attentive. They could have recruit more staff to improve our dining experience but its OK coz the place is small and probably can seat about 50 diners at any one time. My best dining experience in Melaka so far ... food is simply fantastic. Amy was there to serve us and she is such a darling! friendly and never stop smiling. Cendol and Pai tee is a MUSTShow less

Author: SkyegerlSingapore
Title: Arrogant Dining Place!!!
Review: Totally disappointed with the arrogant attitude!! Reached at 130pm hungry and refused our business when they stated 230pm as closing. Amy herself was so arrogant. Didn't even tell us nicely why they are closed and just signal and ask us to go. Will never come back ever again. Don't think I want to pay and see faces. Will spread this news around and make sure all my friends visit others than them.Show less

Author: Hyden F
Title: Badman and beyond rating.
Review: This is beyond rating. Service barely exist as you'll be whisked away by the arrogant server when you just step in. Not a word of sorry and they just give a hand gesture of shooing u away. Kindly revoke their award until they up their service. This is criminal!Show less

Author: pandb2London, United Kingdom
Title: Malaka doesn't know how lucky it is!
Review: Excellent original cuisine. People who want commercial tastes and fast food please don't bother as this is quality. You need to book and you need to appreciate the experience and those negative reviewers don't have much of clue. I suspect they probably expected something much more ordinary. Its very simplicity is a selling feature. Good food purchased at the morning markets prepared on day for those sensible enough to book.The owner is informed, friendly and delightful, the manager efficient and helpful, oh,and the freshly prepared food with all its interesting and unique tastes is a perfect fusion of styles and tastes. Really it is a jewel in the crown and Amy Heritage Nyonya Cuisine could happily sit along side the best eateries found in London or New York.A delicious experience.PHShow less

Author: Ratcool69Singapore, Singapore
Title: NYONYA FOOD AT IT'S BEST
Review: Tried our luck and went without a reservation at 11.15am...initially was told full house..Amy said there was 1 table that didn't turn up..wow..Amy the owner easily turned away at least 50 people when we were having lunch. .the food was really good...satisfying. .Nyonya Food Hall of Fame..thanks Karen Cheah...you are right..Amy told the walk ins that the place is full..and asked them to make a reservation or come back the next day..Amy's is closed on Mondays. ..Show less

Author: Michael C
Title: Worth the trip
Review: For all the excellent online reviews, Amy is quite a small cozy restaurant tucked away in a quiet corner.  Food is first class, and service is warm and fast.  It's certainly worth the trip there.

Author: Ayimbun
Title: The Best Nyonya Cuisine in Melaka !
Review:
Excellent Food with Wonderful Service.
However need to make advance reservation or you'll be rejected to dine in.

Author: JansonC14
Title: Very bad service
Review: Spend time to the place, enter the restaurant quite lot of empty table but the waiter just tell you that all are reserved. Very poor service.

Author: e78n11
Title: Sumptuous food
Review: Very authentic nyonya food, servicing was good but very limited tables and you can't do walk in. So is a must to call to book before head down.

Author: BrianTongKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Moderate food and poor service
Review: Poor service. Serving food have to be table by table. Food quality is moderate. How can they be best Nyonya food in Malaysia as some review. Have you ever tasted the best real nyonya home cook food? I am fortunate because my wife is a nyonya and i get to test it from her mother and late nyonya auntie from Singapore.Show less

Author: mozilla_monsterKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Good food in a simple setting
Review: Nice, simple place.The good:* Owners takes your order very carefully, and takes time to explain what you will get, and does some thinking for you (eg considers the appropriate portion size)* Taste wise, very little was under expectation - everything tasted good and the portion size is also appropriate.* Reasonable serving time, considering our big group (20+ people)All in, nothing to complain about, very good food in a simple setting. I'll come again!Show less

Author: MY58Singapore
Title: Great Authentic Homecooked Nonya Food
Review: We had a wonderful dinner at Amy's. We thought we had over ordered, but we ending up finishing everything because it was so good. Everything was freshly cooked and had that wonderful taste of authentic homemade Nonya food which is getting hard to find. We loved the crispy tofu, Chicken Pongtay, Ikan Assam Rebus, Chicken Buah Keluak, otak, chap chye, etc. Best to call ahead and make a reservation before going otherwise you could well be disappointed. They are very short handed as Amy and her son are the only servers in the restaurant, so they cannot cope with too many diners. When we were there, we saw many people without reservations being turned away.Show less

Author: ernichanKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: One of the best Nyonya eateries in msia
Review: This is not a joke, the title befits this restaurant, excellent authenticity coupled w true attention to culinary detail, peranakan food just like how it was prepared by our grandparents, if they were babas and nyonyas...don't miss the buah keluak chicken, Kuah lada fish and the masak lemak vegetables or the fried chicken to name a few...Amy is a wonderful hostess,,one thing to remember pls book well in advance, they only hv limited numbers and are always turning away customers that show up unannounced....enjoy...Show less

Author: TravelatorsHeartlander
Title: A Peranankan Feast
Review: This is my third visit to Amy over the past 3 years. Her food is superb and a real treat. We had kids who were not used to spicy food and Amy recommended dishes that were well suited. Everyone loved it and I noticed the entire restaurant was reserved by different groups. Do ensure you make reservations as well! Try to go there earlier so that you can get parking outside the restaurant. Show less

Author: Enilecmak
Title: Waste of time and effort
Review:
Eager to trY out due to the favorable responses.

However, once arrived, we were made to feel like beggars seeking alms as they gave us the cold stare and told us fully booked despite many empty tables.

Truly bad service that deserves a minus 1.

Author: Kath KHastings, New Zealand
Title: What a great dining experience
Review: We actually met Amy while wandering around the Sentral Market and after talking to her decided to visit her restaurant. Yes you need to book and yes it is a little difficult to find but it was so worth it. We got there early [6pm] and Amy recognised us from the market. She gave us a rundown on the different dishes and some recommendations then left to run the kitchen.The front of house staff were attentive and helpful. The dishes we had were Pie Tee for entrée followed by Chicken Pongteh and Prawns in curry coconut sauce. It was so tasty. What a find. Thank you Amy and staff for a great dining experienceShow less

Author: fredd0Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Don't bother
Review: After trying to find the place, arriving at 7.45pm (at a shop entrance prominently displaying hours until 9.30pm) we were told it's closed and full - all this while there were empty tables around and only 1 reserved. Clearly a restaurant that doesn't want business. They should change their opening hours signage. Show less

Author: Li H
Title: Surprised and Very Pleased
Review: We had to book a day in advance, and already had to beg for a table. Call at 3pm to book if you want someone to answer the phone! Amy herself tends to customers - nice touch. She says they cook for one table at a time, and I believe it. All fresh. So be prepared to wait, but you will be rewarded.Found the blend of spices for each dish very well balancedDishes are very well put together - you can tell it is not mass produced, like the other restaurantsWe ate :Ayam Sek - surprising, but v delicious!Ikan garam asam - shiok! The quah was so good we couldnt stop drinking itAyam pongteh - also very finely doneBelimbing - wah delicious! We were lucky she had it in stock that day - a special orderSambal Belachan - worth every extra cent! Finished! Cendol - no kachang, but really well put togKeep it up Amy - please don't compromise the quality for mass. We will be back!!Show less

Author: dgohpg
Title: Nice nyonya food
Review: Tried this restaurant after being recommended by the hotel. Nice nyonya food and you need to make a booking in order to eat there. If not, it will be very packed with people.

Author: NGUYETD
Title: Ok only
Review: We came as this restaurant is ranked in the top 5 penarakan restaurant in Melacca. However the food is just so-so. Not impressed! Can get better food at Singapore Keppel Club.

Author: FelixH374Singapore, Singapore
Title: Very Authentic Peranakan
Review: Wonderful Food ; great service if Amy herself serves you ..... Not if you're unlucky and her son serves you ( grumpy face !) they are terribly short handed. So, if you can overlook the slipshod service , you're in for a wonderful dinner . We didn't make a reservation and the place was fully booked so after pleading with Amy who was so so nice she told us to sit outside and as soon as the first table cleared she'd seat us ... We waited about 6 mins . Yay !!! Assam fish , steamed lady's fingers with Sambal , Sambal belachan , pie tee and Sambal timun are excellent . The buah keluak dish had a very easy gravy unfortunately she doesn't take out the keluak flesh , pound it with spices and prawns and stuff it back into the shell like the authentic dish calls for . So the flesh in the buah keluak comes out in chunks which is unusual and not my favourite. The Chendol was disappointing .... Coconut milk was watered down and no red beans . Overall a nice dining experience. Show less

Author: SFJCWongPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: Fine dining made affordable.
Review: We had a good dinner at Amy's. We managed to secure a table by calling earlier to book. The service was good in a clean, modern, minimalist setting. We were told that we had to wait for our food (20-30 minutes) as they were all freshly cooked (two thumbs up).We didn't mind the wait at all knowing that our food was personally prepared by an award-winning veteran chef, Amy herself. We had pie tee as appetizer (a small aromatic crispy cup of pastry), followed by otak otak (clean, homemade taste). We had white rice with ayam buah keluak (good stuff with generous amount of thick gravy), fried chicken (savory & tangy), & kangkung kobis keledek masak titik lemak (water spinach, round cabbage, sweet potatoes in coconut gravy all soaked in unparallel creamy goodness!) & itik tim soup (compensates forgivingly for the mediocre drink selection). Unfortunate for us, sambal jantung pisang was unavailable. We enjoyed our gastronomic encounter at Amy's so much, we packed Nyonya mee jawa (tender noodles in well balanced gravy) and Siam bihun (non-over spicy rice vermicelli), topped with more fried chicken (for the craving Wife) the night after for supper. Our verdict: each dish (dine-in and takeaway) was prepared with passion and a personal touch of Amy's individuality, constantly reminding us of the uniqueness of Nyonya cuisine refined for an unforgettable dining escapade.Show less

Author: WantedToTravelKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Yummylicious!!!
Review: We had asam pedas, curry chicken, pai tee, chap chye with white rice. I blame my tummy for not big enough to eat more!!! Everything taste so good. I can easily finish 5 pai tees on my own. Sorry, no sharing on this dish. Must make a booking before you make your way there. Me and hubby are lucky as we didn't get rejected when we walk-in. All the tables are fully booked and only 2 walk-in (including us) are entertained. At least 6 groups of walk-in is sent away. Show less

Author: poopshooterPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: yummy Nyonya treat!
Review: Stumbled upon this place researching for good Nyonya spread. There is just too many in Melaka these days & most end up disappointing. However this was a gem of a find. Do make reservations as during weekends its always fully booked. Do note that it takes awhile for food to be served so if in a hurry go elsewhere. However good things come to those who wait. ;)The 4 of us tried 6 dishes & they were all rich, fragrant, spicy & simply yummy. Notable mentions would be the Pie Tee, Ikan Asam Rebus & the Kangkong Kobis Keledek Masak Titik Lemak. There are many others but we didn't get to try this time around. Prices were decent for the type of cuisine so no complaints there.The restaurant itself is nice & cozy. Simple set up nothing fancy. Service is organized & friendly. Would say the best Nyonya restaurant in Melaka right now. Highly recommended!Show less

Author: KhinLayKhaing
Title: Reasonable price with nice food
Review:
We have 16 paxs and ordered 7 dishes. Most of us loved Asaam Fish and Buah keluakchicken. You must try.
For appetizer , their pai tee and awesome.

Author: irene lSingapore, Singapore
Title: Good food, homely feel
Review: Quite value for money. We went on a Tuesday, didn't make reservations but arrived before 6pm. Lucky we could get a table.Menu listed medium and large portions. The boss proposed small portions for us, seeing we are just 2 adults and a child. Prices were also adjusted for the small portions. We had hee peow soup, fried chicken wings, squid rings, ayam pongteh and chendol.Show less

Author: kmquek
Title: Great Nonya Food. Light, fresh and delicious
Review: The food here is really nice. Amy herself oversees the kitchen and ensures that quality of food is not compromised. Whilst her son manages the restaurant. I'll definitely come back again and also reservation is a must.

Author: Leesa DJakarta, Indonesia
Title: Lovely comfort food
Review: We were staying at the Holiday Inn and they managed to secure us a table at the last minute, thank you! We saw people turned away and once inside we understood. Amy isn't here to turn people over quickly like in KL restaurants. It's about the food, executing it well and not rushing you out. Unfortunately 2 dishes we selected were not available but we understood. If ingredients aren't available you don't compromise. The alternatives we did order were delicious. You could taste the layer of flavours and it felt like I was eating something that the chef had lovingly prepared in their home. Next time we would probably come for lunch as we do like to have a drink with our dinner and there is no alcohol served here but we would definitely come back. Felt the prices were very reasonable too. We couldn't eat dinner like that for that price in KL.Show less

Author: beeb9
Title: Yummy Food
Review:
Returned here after 3 yrs with the same group of friends savouring the yummy food.

Ordered Ayam Pongteh,  telur chincalok,  bendi kukus,  hee peow  soup, saliva drooling.

Author: Pat C
Title: Fabulous Food and Service
Review: Make a reservation!  They keep it small to keep the food and service terrific, so reservations for dinner are a must.  You won't regret it!

Author: David HMelaka, Malaysia
Title: Always Excellent
Review: Whenever I have out of town guests visiting I always take them to Amy's. Her food is always excellent and very authentic Nonya cuisine. The curry sauce's are so tasty that you almost want to take your spoon and finish every last drop from the bowl.Always book ahead, especially on the weekends as she is always very busy.Her cooking is so authentic and good that the Malaysian government twice sent her to New York to represent Malaysia at the UN and to cook for the ambassadors from the various countries.Show less

Author: chuahonlyAuckland Central, New Zealand
Title: Overrated
Review: Extremely overrated in the sense that I heard from a colleague at work about the "best nyonya restaurant in town" The food was good but I expected much better . Service was average although the female staff who served my table was rather blur . My wife ordered the fried fish which was pretty ordinary however the masak lemak was excellent .Overall an average place .Show less

Author: 288thiruaKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Good food but overstated
Review: No complaints about the food itself, they serve pretty good dishes. We were group of 10 and we booked in advance as we heard that it gets full fast and that they don't take in any customers once it's full. The chendol was good, but the ayam ponteh was a hit sweet for my liking. Overall I would rate the food as decent nothing outstanding. Show less

Author: Ron JPerth, Western Australia, Australia
Title: A good dining experience but could be better!
Review: We visited this restaurant at the recommendation of a close friend who lived in the area. Upon our arrival we were quickly shown to our table. There were a few large vacant reserved tabled so we were lucky to get a table.We advised the restaurant manager of the friend's recommendation but he did not show any interest in the introduction and more interested in showing us the menu.The meals we have ordered were of a good standard which we enjoyed. The service was efficient but we did not feel any warmth which was a disappointment as the little extra 'love' would in our view have made a vast difference for an award winning restaurant.Show less

Author: chew cSingapore, Singapore
Title: good food, service and value
Review: On 10th December just few hours before my coach was scheduled to picked us up from Hatten Hotel I decided to have a last minute quick lunch at Amy Heritage .It is very near to the MakhotaMedical Center which is at Syed Abdul Aziz Road. When I was there at 12 to 1 pm it was not that crowded and i managed to get a sitting. The dishes mostly come in medium and large sizes.I decided to try their ayam ponteh and chendol. As i have just taken my breakfast I asked the gentleman there (not Mr Lim) whether I could have a smaller portion and he obliged by recommending me a 3 pieces of chicken in the ponteh. I found both the chendol and ayam ponteh both okay with the ponteh a bit sweet, However I was very pl.eased with the service and the value for money. Will visit again to try more of their food if i return to Malacca.Show less

Author: Peggy LLondon, United Kingdom
Title: We enjoyed the meal, not sure if it's 'the best nyonya' food
Review: Having attended Guan's supper club in London - http://theboywhoatetheworld.com/my-malaysian-nyonya-supper-club/ I have a pretty good idea of what spectacular nyonya food should taste like and on this occasion - I haven't found this at Amy's.Overall, we enjoyed our meal and there were flashes of brillance to remember. My grandma, mum and I shared the otak otak, ikan cili garam, prawns with pineapple, Kangkung Kobis Keledek Masak Titik Lemak and a cendol for dessert. We loved the quality of the sambal on the ikan cili garam and the cendol to us was great simply for the quality of the gula melaka and fragrant coconut milk that has gone into it. The otak otak was tasty and pretty special as the body was the texture of a springy fish cake with well balanced tasty spices to accompany.The prawns with pineapple and kobis titik lemak were like big bowls of spiced coconut milk soup to me. There was way too much gravy for the amount of food in the bowls. I was expecting to find a wholesome portion of al dente vegetables in the kobis titik lemak but what we had was more like a soft vegetable stew in a tasty enough coconut milk soup. The team were courteous enough though not the warmest bunch . They were ernest and could tell they take pride in the restaurant. I hope to see the restaurant improve and grow as if this restaurant was to be one of 'the authority' on Nyonya food in Malaysia - it certainly should impress and wow. It hasn't done so today.Show less

Author: Jillian L
Title: So so..
Review: Buah keluak was not bad, however the gravy is on the sweet side, also the flesh of the nuts were not pounded.

Author: mrsdoo10206Singapore, Singapore
Title: More than 15 cockroaches on dinning table
Review: I was at Amy on 13 Dec for lunch with my family and relatives of 32 pax (3 tables, age range 8 to 80+ Years old). I have read so much about Amy but never have a chance to try it. So for this family trip, I was excited and proud to introduce Amy's Nyonya Cuisine to my family. I made the reservation about 2-3 weeks in advance and even went down to the restaurant one day in advance to make deposit and order dishes. We were there at 12 noon. As lunch was not ready, we sat down and started to order our drinks first. While deciding what drinks to order, my niece started to scream when she tried to pick up the fork and spoon on the dinning table. We walked over and thought there were many ants on the table. But to our horror, it turned out to be baby cockroaches. I went over quickly to tell the waitress. She came over to take a look and then walked away. I thought she was going to report what she saw to the lady boss. NO. She did not. She continued with her drinks-making and act as if we were over-reacting. I was pissed off. I walked straight to the kitchen to get the lady boss out. My brother lifted up the folk again to show the lady boss and more baby cockroaches crawling out. The lady boss just cleared the cockroaches from the table and kept mentioning that she always keeps her restaurant clean. NO APOLOGY words at all. I did not get out of the restaurant immediately as i still want to give this restaurant a benefit of doubts. ( I must be out of my mind then). When the food was served, it was not hot. It was just a little bit warm. We were worried about the hygiene of the food and hence expected the food to be real hot. ( to give us a peace of mind that the food are okay). When I asked the lady boss why the dishes were not hot, she said that we were early for lunch (the first dish was served at about 12.30pm, shop open at 11.30am). And continued to say that the beauty of Nyonya food is that the food can be eaten cold/room temp. (Testing my limit again). And then continued to mention that she keeps her place clean. (still no apology).We just wanted to finish our meal and get out of the place. It does not matter anymore whether they are serving the best Nyonya food in Melaka. The whole incident just spoilt our appetite. When it's time to settle our bill, the guy at the counter was not friendly at all. It was like we have made him unhappy instead of they made us unhappy. We paid about MYR986 for the lunch .If it happens in another country, the restaurant would have been heavily fine and might need to close down for a clean up. But here....... That's all I can say. I hope more restaurants can pay more attention to their cleanliness. No point talking about how good the food is when the most important hygiene is not there.I need to mention this: we paid full and forgot to deduct the total bill against our MYR300 deposit. The restaurant called us in the evening to ask us to go down and take our deposit back. For this, I must mention that they are honest.Sorry Amy. This will be my first and last time going to your restaurant. Do continue to work hard on the restaurant's cleanliness.Show less

Author: jeannietung81Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Worst peranakan food
Review: After reading the good review in tripadvisor do we decide to give it a try. And the taste of the food is very normal and nothing special about it. My husband said I cook better than them. The fried chicken( forgot the dish name)The cendol is worst than a Indian stall who selling it. And the boss face is stuck up type. I would not recommend it to anyone. Show less

Author: nathanjef
Title: Great Food
Review: Brilliant cuisine. I love the food and the service here. Price is reasonable and the food is tasty. Easy to get parking and in fact it is free.

Author: kennperrPerth, Australia
Title: Great Food and Service
Review: Before we left Melaka for Perth we tried the Nyonya cuisine at this restaurant. First and foremost, the restaurant had great ambience. The food was great, please try the otak otak amongst, sago gula melaka. Rich and sweet food. Got to work out when I get back to Perth. Thank youShow less

Author: LeeLeeMelakaMelaka
Title: A friendly face and ambience, with homely prepared cuisine
Review: The first time I tried Auntie Amy's place, I fell in love with her sambal jantung pisang. To me this dish is a must whenever I visit this restaurant. I also love her lemak titiek keledek. Authenticity is being reassured with Auntie Amy herself preparing the dishes, with pride and passion.Show less

Author: FlyingbertKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Found! A good Peranakan makan place in Melaka.
Review: Made reservations for 12, but party of 19 turned out. Food was really good, one of the better Peranakan restaurants I've tried out the years. Ordered the standard fare - ayam ponteh, ikan cili garam, chap chye, prawns with pineapple, otak-otaku....all good, prawns & fish is fresh. Tried the sambal pisang jantung - it was new to most of us. This is one restaurant that you can just turn up and expect a table, reservation in advance is a must. Will surely return again. Show less

Author: farscope
Title: Good but can be better
Review: I have been to a few Nyonya restaurants in Melaka. I decided to try Amy for my recent visit after reading some recommendations online. The dishes prepared are carefully prepared and clean. Ingredients used were also good as the ladies finger we ordered are not too old and chewy. You are able to feel the details of the dishes prepared. However, the fried chicken is a bit undercooked. Probably didn't thaw properly before frying. It didn't taste as good as I expected as I have higher expectation for Amy but overall it's not bad either. Perhaps I need to order their signature dish next time. Cendol is just plain. Cendol has slight pandan taste but that's it. Coconut milk and gula melaka is not generous enough. I will recommend a pass for their beverages.I will try their signature dishes next time when I'm back with a bigger group of people to share.Show less

Author: angry_customer0111Melaka, Malaysia
Title: Terrible attitude!
Review: I went to the restaurant with my family but unfortunately it was fully booked.However, the restaurant is still empty so I suggest the uncle boss to let us have a quick dinner.With hesitate, he kept giving plenty of excuses but I am still fine with it.The worst thing was he replied in a really unfriendly way to me and blaming me for not listening to his explanation.I understood you might have limited capacity and you might be rich enough or have more than enough customers to forgo me and my family but the terrible attitude is what I couldn't accept!Sorry to say no matter how good is your review I will definately boycott such impolite service, and please be assured this experience will be shared with my friends and family.Good luck!Show less

Author: ShaliinPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Superb Sunday family lunch
Review: First visit to this authentic Nyonya restaurant at Melaka Raya on 19th Oct'14, Sunday with total of 8 pax. We loved all 8 dishes ( including cendol dessert) that we had especially the Ikan Gerang Assam & Pie Tee. Chicken buah keluak was very delicious too. Would strongly recommend this restaurant to those genuine & fussy Nyonya cuisine lovers.This restaurant has been in operation for 8 long years by a lovely couple: Mr & Mrs Lim ( Amy the chef). Both are in their seventies but they are still very enthusiastic and gusto! And they do not entertain tour groups in order to maintain their food standards according to Mr Lim.You have to make reservations especially during weekends.A must try restaurant in MelakaShow less

Author: David HMelaka, Malaysia
Title: Authentic Nyonya Cuisine By Celebrity Chef
Review: Yes, there is an Amy and she was recognized by the Malaysian Government to prepare authentic Malaysian Nyonya cuisine at the United Nations in NYC. The menu is Halal so there are no pork dishes, but her chicken and fish dishes are perfect. Her curried vegetable and sambal fish dishes are amazing. It is better to make a reservation as the restaurant is usually very busy. I always take our out of country guests there for a meal to experience authentic Nyonya cuisine.Show less

Author: MonkeyAhMoSelangor, Malaysia
Title: Nyonya Food that you should try when visit Melaka
Review: Highly recommended.... been here twice and food it's still delicious , staffs are friendly and it's not expensive too.We really really love the Pie Tea and Chincalok omelette.But please make your reservation before you come even on weekdays and please be prepare that they take long time to prepare the dishes too (at least 30 minutes).Show less

Author: mrmin1
Title: Incredible culinary experience
Review: Wow Wow Wow. What amazing food, we let Amy choose the dishes and we were not disappointed. The whole meal felt made with love in every bite and we tried dishes we have never seen in Australia. Amy is a national treasure and we could see why famous international chefs come to cook with her.Show less

Author: DazzaRBKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: So good we went twice in 3 days
Review: We went for a weekend break in Melaka and like with all our getaways, it tends to revolve around food. The location of Amy's is just out of the city centre among some shophouses, which is a good thing because you dont get stuck in the city traffic and it's easy to find parking at night and on the weekends. We went the first time on Friday night - perhaps because we went a bit late (around 845pm), it was easy to get a table but I strongly recommending calling ahead to book as we found out on the second visit that they can be fully booked. We were willing to wait it out until a table vacated, which actually did not take so long - about 15 minutes.They are clearly very passionate about their food and dont upset the uncle by ordering fried rice to go with the dishes! We left it to the uncle to recommend the dishes and we were not disappointed. Just a word of caution that the portions can be quite big so on the first time we had actually over-ordered.They also sell pre-packed homemade pineapple jam tarts by the counter. They really do taste like they were just baked in your aunty's house! I loved the uncle's response when i asked how long do the tarts last? He said, "depends, if you open it and start eating you will finish it within 2 days!" He was right.Show less

Author: huajernMuar, Malaysia
Title: A bit of a letdown.
Review: Decided to try out Amy's based on a friend's recommendation and favourable online reviews.Luckily a last minute dinner reservation was possible. *Do make one as it may not be possible to squeeze in without a reservation.Service was friendly and the food came promptly despite the fairly packed dining room. Decor is simple & pleasant.Sadly the food quality was below expectations after the effusive praise of most reviewers here. 3 of us ordered a soup, fried chicken wings, bean sprouts, asam garam fish and rojak noodles; with cendol as dessert. The dishes were too salty for our taste, the seafood wasn't fresh, and we didn't really taste the spices classical of nyonya food.The dishes were not bad, just not memorable enough to make me come back for more. Even the drinks were nothing special. Prices are reasonable for Melaka.Judging from the crowd, many don't agree with me on the quality of the fare here. Come try and decide for yourself. Show less

Author: lekkykim
Title: Excellent!
Review: My friend brought me here. At first I wasn't expecting much. But when the food came, I was in awe. Beautifully decorated and very appetizing. You can tell that the cook put in a lot of love and care. We were lucky that my friend made a resrvation, becuase it got really crowded at night. Excellent service. Will come back.Show less

Author: Manoj1973
Title: Great food, prepared with lot of care and love
Review: The food was mindblowing.  It was simple and we loved all the four dishes we ordered.  Have to visit again.  Slightly more expensive than usual restaurants in Melaka.  But then, the presentation is great and the preparation quite unique.

Author: jo_chaMalaysia
Title: Good Nyonya food
Review: We had no reservation as we simply browsed through the internet for best Nyonya food. When we called up at 1.30 pm Madam Amy took us in even though it was a last minute request after we said we just found out about her shop. The food was good and Madam Amy's husband was really friendly and was checking on our food to see everything was in order. Will definitely go back there again with a proper booking first :)Show less

Author: katrineangSingapore, Singapore
Title: Amy's - Authentic Nonya Food
Review: To dine here, a Reservation IS A MUST. Tables are limited because in my opinion, to maintain the authenticity of the serving with the cost of the serving, it makes sense. Most times, when going commercial is in question, something gets 'lost' along the way. A humble shop house they may be operating from, but they win on Quality, Price and Serving portion. They are closed on Mondays. If you call and no one answers, keep trying - this is a 'family business' and usually they are busy cooking, serving and chatting with the diners.I am Nonya and I grew up in a full Baba household, not one where a lot of Chinese food/habits are incorporated. This is as home-style as any commercial establishment can serve. Of course, for those who can cook Nonya food, you will know that the difference comes in how thick or thin the family prefers the gravy/sauce to be. The authenticity comes in the ability to discern the spices that goes into the dish and how sometimes just one spice more or less makes it a whole new Peranakan dish.Show less

Author: SchrodiSunSingapore
Title: Delicious food!
Review: We made our reservation for lunch, just before our drive back to SG. Really good food. The friendly owner (Amy's husband) was helpful in recommending dishes, and chatted with us near the end of our meal. It was one of the best meals of our trip! The Pie tee appetiser was mush better than any i'd ever had, crisp and freshly fried outer shell carrying a filling of vegetables. Ayam pongteh was a deep flavoured chicken stew with a slurpable gravy. The coconut curry vegetable dish was the best of its kind I'd had. No joke. I don't think the gravy was calorie-light though- I bet Amy pours bucketfuls of coconut milk in there-though that didn't stop me from drinking up the rich creamy gravy. The Assam fish had a light sour tomato broth, done well. Chinchalok omelette was just that, eggs with prawn stuff in it. Soup was light and complemented our meal nicely. They don't use msg, Mr Amy told us, but that didn't tone done the food's flavours at all!We were too full to try the chendol, and waddled out satisfied and happy.Show less

Author: Joesop168
Title: Worst Nonya restaurant
Review: The man with the tattoo is the most obnoxious service personnel to be put to front the restaurant. The food is really bad...right from (Milk in ) prawn nanas to chendol...no red bean no shave ice...it is just a complete waste of time and money.

Author: KiznicolenigelSingapore, Singapore
Title: Worst Nyona Food!!! Biggest disappointment!
Review: It was highly recommended by our friend who visited last when it the chef was an elderly lady and the server was an elderly man. This trip was run by 2 fairly muscular men who obviously was really uptight and just not pleasant and somewhat obnoxious. Every single dish was just way below par that it was a waste of calories to eat there. We ordered quite a number of dishes for our big group of 10 pax. The chicken Ponteh was the only decent dish that could be repeated. Every other dish from Assam Fish to soups were ..If I may blatantly comment- awful. But the worst of it was the chendol- no crushed ice and very weak coconut with only the green jelly strips. It made us really so disgusted at how anyone can serve chendol of this standard and in Melaka. Our last trip there...Most certainly! Show less

Author: Zozo10
Title: Will definitely be back again!
Review:
Best nyonya food I had so far!   We had it at lunch, no booking is needed at 11:30am.
The owner's husband, helped us to select our food choice and it was perfect.  Love every dishes!

Author: drsfr
Title: Good nyonya food
Review: We booked ahead as we were a group of 9. The restaurant had to turn people away who had not booked and this was on a Tuesday night. Food was good. Service was reasonable. And it is super convenient just opposite the mahkota medical centre.

Author: Hedgiebunny
Title: Authentic Peranakan food at decent prices
Review: Best to reserve as the place was packed on a Sunday evening. Closed on Mondays. Order the ayam buah keluak (my fav), lady's finger and Kueh pie tee. Yummy!

Author: LowLCSingapore, Singapore
Title: Turning away customers before official closing hours!
Review: Based on reviews about how good the food is, my family of 5 travelled all the way from Singapore to patronize this restaurant, intending to take our lunch there. We arrived about 1.30pm and was prepared to wait for a table as we did not make any reservation. Upon arrival, all the tables were occupied but one kind family informed us that they were done and was settling the bill and we could have their table. We were grateful but to our shock, the proprietor I guessed, a senior man, turned us away by saying that the restaurant was closed for the afternoon as they were expecting a dinner group that night. What has it got to do with our lunch? We didn't understand further when he said they were leaving for the afternoon. We were quite pissed off because the official closing hour was 2.30pm and it was only 1.30pm! Besides, there was a table available for us!My family was utterly disappointed with the attitude of this restaurant. Even if it has good reviews, we will NEVER return again!!My family was disappointed with the attitude of this senior man.Show less

Author: EdwinT819Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Visit to Malacca
Review: We were on a day trip to historical Malacca and our goal was to eat and eat as Malacca is not only famous for its historical setting but the food as well. Since there are so many nyonya restaurant, we were spoil for choice and decided to try Amy Heritage Nyonya cuisine. We were there for lunch and we did not make any reservation but fortunately there was a table ready. Since it was our first time there, there was an uncle recommended to try their 'pie tee', otak-otak, assam fish (sweet and sour), chicken with black sauce and mixed vege in some sort of soup base. Sorry, I can't remember some of the above dishes name. The ambience of the restaurant is nice and modern looking compare to some of the nyonya's restaurant that we have visited. The pie tee was good and the rest of the dishes depend on individual taste. Its either you love it or you dont. Otak-otak was totally different from what we have eaten. The price is reasonable and the service is good and we have an uncle that keep asking us how was the food and whether its ok and even recommend us to drink the assam fish, chicken and vege soup based. Personally for me I have yet to really appreciate the nyonya food in Malacca as I am more use to the nyonya food taste in Kuala Lumpur or Petaling Jaya. As I say before, it is more of a personal taste whether you love it or you dont.Show less

Author: sheronleeMalacca, Malaysia
Title: Tasted like how my Grandma used to cook.
Review: The food is quite good. It reminded me of my Grandma's cooking. I especially like the "jantung pisang salad" and "ayam masak buah keluak". They are really good. However, I would prefer some of the food to be spicy. The owner indicated that they have to cater for some of the patrons who can't take food that are too spicy. I personally feel that they ought to ask the customers how they like their food. I was disappointed to see their "lemak masak udang" looked so "whitish" instead of the normal colour of "orangey". Nevertheless, I will always bring my friends who are visiting Melaka to this place.Show less

Author: Gerald KSingapore
Title: You must make a reservation!
Review: I went there this time with a big group of friends, so I called Amy to not only order the food dishes ahead of time, but also reserved the number of seats for lunch. I arrived earlier than my other friends, and as I sat in the restaurant, I saw quite a few people being turned away because they did not make any reservation... so please make a reservation if you are going!The food, as with all my previous visits, was great! All my friends enjoyed the food, especially the pineapple prawns (udang nanas), and the chicken pongteh (ayam pongteh).Show less

Author: Sean T
Title: Favorable.
Review: It's okay. But a big let down for spicy fans. The food is a little too sweet, just a little above the human tongue could handle. But, I can say that the service and ambience is very very good. The uncle will not rest until the customers are satisfied, which, to me, is quite good of him to do so. Food specific, the Pie Tee was extraordinary, as well as the sambal prawns with petai. The asam fish was favorable, but it doesn't quite fit the picture of asam fish. In a nutshell, it's an okay experience at Amy's. Show less

Author: dttx_84Singapore, Singapore
Title: Amazing nyonya food!
Review: I visited this place on the last day of our malacca before heading back to Singapore. Having been turned away 1 day earlier due to a fully reserved place I decided to try my luck on a Sunday afternoon around 2pm. Was lucky enough to get a table as those who came after were promptly turned away. As the owner himself put it, this is a family run restaurant it doesn't serve tour groups to maintain food quality.The wife and a few staff did the cooking. I can understand why they choose not to overwork themselves. Most food were cooked from scratch except the ayam ponteng which was prepared slightly ahead I was told. Nonetheless I had a wonderful meal consisting of prawns, jackfruit in lemak gravy & ayam ponteng. Would definitely be back nxt time & make the necessary reservations.Show less

Author: SusangermanyNew York City, New York
Title: Amy Nyonya....
Review: food is a place you should not miss in Malacca. The Restaurant looks more like a Coffee shopthan a Restaurant. Simple and clear cut.The owner Mr. Lim is very friendly and the "Chef" Amy knows how to cook!We choice our dishes and Mr. Lim explained every course to us.You have to try the Pie Tee, the Ayam Lada is very good and I think all others are good too. Theprices are very reasonable.Don't forget to make a reservation, without is only a slight chance to get a table.We took a taxi to Amy and the Driver did know his way.Show less

Author: nigelskelchyKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Gruff Beginning but a Sweet Ending
Review: Uncle Lim who takes the reservations and orders is particular about doing things in a particular order. He's also gruff over the phone. No brownie points for phone manner but in person he's lovely, helpful and very friendly. Every inch the proud Maitre D'! Lovely to watch someone who's proud of what he's putting in front of his guests.From his assertions that Amy's does everything in-house from the spice pastes to his instructions about ordering and eating dessert at the end "Cendol nanti, Makan Dulu" he's large and in charge! Just in case you're reading this Uncle Lim, it's all good! ;-)Unfortunately, the bad part of our experience was that there were only 2 of us, which for Nyonya food is not always the best thing as what you can order is very limited. We had the Udang Goreng Assam or Tamarind Prawns, Sayur Masak Lemak (Water Spinach and Cabbage lightly braised in Coconut Milk), and the Ayam Pong Teh (a Chicken Stew braised in a sweet broth with fermented bean). All were delicious. As my friend said about the Sayur Masak Lemak, "it was a 'lemak' orgasm!" Recommendations for the best experience;1. ALWAYS reserve a table for your party. Never show up without one or you could be turned away. Yes, this happened while we were there. And show up on time or risk having your table given away.2. Waze doesn't always get you there. It got us near but it was about 200m further up than where Waze said it would be.3. Pre-order. They do have a menu to take away at the restaurant. They run out of dishes quite early on as they make a limited amount to keep things fresh.Other than that, prepare for a great, authentic, delicious experience.Show less

Author: Hantukomkom
Title: nyonya food
Review: sedap bangat!!! and good service too. better book in advance to avoid disappointment. amy and her managers are always friendly and ready to talk to u about your food.

Author: Aidanaj
Title: Could not locate the place
Review: Even with GPS it's a dead end pointing direction to Jalan Melaka Raya 23. Tried calling the restaurant no answer . Have been driving around locating the place few times even in google map could not find Melaka Raya 24.

Author: Sen RPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: Best Nyonya Food in Melaka
Review: The place to eat if you are craving for Nyonya Food. You can also meet Amy in person if you are lucky. Simply authentic & delicious. Their interior is simple and minimal but clean. Free flow of rice is served in a thingamajig basket. If there’s you are planning to visit a nyonya restaurant, make sure you have this one on your priority list! Tips : Compulsory to make reservation becoz it is packed all the time !!!!Show less

Author: nahs731Singapore
Title: Authentic Nyonya Food
Review: Being a nyonya whose hometown is in melaka, i think amy's nyonya food is authentic.Though not the best in my opinion, still a must try!We had kueh pai tee (good!), fried chicken (which was average), ikan goreng chili masin (chili was not satisfactory for me but the fish really fresh and value for money), chap cai, chicken buah keluak (a must have and best dish i had that night) and last but not least, chendol (too thick for my liking, they use ice cubes instead of the usual shaved ice).Do note that the place is not really easy to find as we couldn't find it on the gps. And the place is too busy so owner was kinda stuck up and took a long time to seat me even though i made reservations.Also, once you order on the phone when making reservations, they do not allow you to change orders so do only order if you are very sure of what you want to have there.Show less

Author: ianwyjSingapore, Singapore
Title: Authentic enough for me
Review: We came in a big group of 23 family members and friends on an organised pre-Chinese New Year shopping trip to Malacca. With most of us having a Perenakan background, it was a no-brainer to be here for our lunch stop. Restaurant was crowded, unsurprising considering its reputation. Staff were busy throughout bringing out dish after dish after dish. We started with kueh pie tee which didn't come with prawns, so that seemed a little odd. But the rest of the meal was lovely. I especially enjoyed the cinchalok (shrimp paste) egg omelette, which I hadn't had for a long time, and the sambal prawn. What was interesting was that the Chinese tea came infused with pandan leaves which gave it a mild scent, not easily detectable. So, overall, quite an authentic and satisfying meal - just don't tell my Perenakan aunts who had a fun time dissecting the good and bad about every dish.Show less

Author: joetan76Singapore, Singapore
Title: The best in melaka
Review: This place serve the best nyonya cuisine in melaka, you have to book in advance to get a table. Their taste is authentic and price is reasonable. Their udang masak nenas has to be the best i ever tried. Their boss Amy is friendly and she share some of the way to cook peranakan food and she herself is the cook!Show less

Author: seabreezesblowSingapore, Singapore
Title: Amy's..for those who know good Peranakkan food
Review: Those who know their Peranakkan food go to Amy's. Of the five dishes we had, the fried fish with sambal was a standout -- fish was done to crispy perfection on the outside but just succulent inside (unlike most crispy fried fish which are dry and hard inside). This is one of few Nyonya places that serve sayur kangkong lemak (water spinach) in coconut-based gravy, which also had cabbage. Also good were the buah keluak and udang nanas lemak (fat, fresh prawns in chilli-coconut gravy). Also to faint-for at first taste: the sambal belachan. The belachan or shrimp paste is fresh and of quality and the chilli is without seeds -- very rare nowadays, when people grind very "rough" and eating sambal belachan is like eating chilli seeds. If you are on a budget but want to try authentic Baba food, go for the fish, the kangkung lemak and buah keluak, with heaps of sambal belachan at every mouthful. Mmm, mmm...Show less

Author: 123Lim456Singapore, Singapore
Title: Bad attitude!
Review: We went to this nyonya restaurant to test on the foods because of the reviews are good. But, we were very disappointed on the attitude by the uncle boss and get very pissed off! We booked dinner on a Saturday. We went to order a few small/medium portion of the dishes just to taste on the foods given the reviews are good. But, the uncle boss kept comparing to us the prices for a medium and a large portion of the dish (please bear in mind all the prices were listed in the menu) and it makes us feel like we got no money to pay! The worst thing was when the uncle boss said " Don't come and eat when you are full of stomach", and is not only one time he said that. When asked for bill, we even praised to the uncle boss that the foods were nice but end up we were repeated by "Don't come and eat when you are full of stomach". Can you imagine how affected your mood and feeling was when the uncle boss said that again and again in front of you? So what your review is good but is that the right way to treat your customers? Does it mean that we shouldn't go there and eat if we got no intention to order many dishes?? We will not go back to this Amy Heritage Nyonya Restaurant again. So, please remember, next time if you want to go to this restaurant, think twice and make sure you are starve the whole day.Show less

Author: Harwant R
Title: Superb food
Review: The freshness of the food and each and every taste felt with each bite taken is just such a mind blowing experience. The home made touch to the food is not lost. Great value for money too. Will deffinately go back there again..

Author: theawsumpawsumWolli Creek, Australia
Title: Amazing food
Review: Food is bursting with flavour and fragrance, the dishes taste of the best home cooked variety and no expense had been spared when it comes to serving up a meal of the highest quality. Definitely worth a stop whenever you're in Malacca. The elderly owner and his wife were beaming from ear to ear as we wiped every dish clean. Highly recommended: udang goreng masam, kangkung masak lemak udang, pai tee and ikan masam rebus.Show less

Author: jlnkcSingapore, Singapore
Title: Doesn't live up to the hype
Review: Being peranakan myself and having an extremely strong peranakan heritage I was really looking forward to this meal, especially since it was fully booked during my last trip. We booked dinner on a Sunday and when ordering, found that many items were sold out. Of the items that we did order, they were unspectacular and overall quite bland and lacking in flavour, spice and kick. With all the hype surrounding this restaurant, it made what probably could have been an OK meal feel sub par, especially given the weight of expectation.Show less

Author: donutnomorePenang Island, Malaysia
Title: Live up to its reputation and more!
Review: We read so many rave reviews and they are right. Food is delicious. It has the home cooked taste, flavorful and yet not overpowering. Chef Amy personally recommended dishes to us, she is very thoughtful to suggest dishes that complement each other. She is so sweet to make smaller portions just nice for two of us so that we can try more dishes. We really appreciate that, at other restaurants we could only have 2 dishes as they don't do smaller portions. The Fish in sweet and sour gravy is very delicious and fish is very fresh ! Thumbs up. We also love the kueh pie tee, Ayam ponteh and chap chai. Lastly, it is friendly on the pocket, not too expensive. She is truly a chef with a passion to share nonya heritage with her cooking. Show less

Author: sarahhobartHobart, Australia
Title: Great Food, nice place
Review: Having read that bookings were recommended, I booked our lunch about a week in advance since we intended to go on Boxing Day. The man I spoke to was quite unfriendly, bordering on rude, and was not happy I couldn't give him a local mobile phone number. I explained I was not yet in Malaysia, and would let him know my local number once I arrived, which I did. He was no friendlier on our second phone conversation. However luckily I booked, because when we arrived right on time at 12.30pm there was a "full house" sign already hanging on the door, and a bunch of people waiting outside.The restaurant is clean, air-conditioned, and plenty of staff on hand. They have traditional Nyonya tableware on display on the walls. We were promptly shown to our table and the menus in English with pictures were very helpful. An elderly gentleman which must have been the owner came over to take our order. I recognised him as the person I had spoken to on the phone. I have read previous reviews about him, and unfortunately must agree. He was both arrogant and dismissive, the only reason I have given a 4 and not 5 in this review.We ordered for the two of us Tie Pee, Otak Otak, Belacan Kang Kong, Assam Fish, and Ayam Pongteh. He tried to discourage me from ordering that much, but we are big eaters, and I wanted to try their famous dishes, so I ignored him. Luckily, we were able to finish everything !!Tie Pee - I had never eaten this before, and did not think it would be anything special, but I was wrong. It was great, cruchy, tasty, delightfulOtak Otak - the fish paste was nice and firm, almost like a fishball texture, but with lovely coconut and rempah spice taste. WonderfulBelacan Kang Kong - my favourite vegetable dish, and they did not disappoint, very niceAssam Fish - this was magnificent. The gravy was really something special. The elderly gentleman was worried I was ordering too much so he made a "small" size for us. Therefore, we had to share a piece of fish, and it was not enough. I could happily have gulfed down my own piece of fish, so I ended up guzzling down all the sour, hot, tasty gravy instead. Just magnificentAyam Pongteh - the only dish that did not wow me. If you have kids then this is a good dish for them. However, I like a bit of spice and chilli, and this dish was quite bland for my taste. Should have listened to my partner and ordered an alternative more spicy chicken dishI finished off with a chendol. It was the BEST chendol I have ever had. It comes with ice cubes not shaved ice, lovely thick coconut santan and gula Melaka with plenty of chendol. GREAT !!Show less

Author: robby321Burnaby, Canada
Title: Order everything
Review: Came here with family, who had local friends that took us here. Met Amy herself who came out to personally take our order AND cook the food. Order everything, especially the 'tophats' and the excellent curries and meat dishes. My goodness, just a fantastic meal that I didn't want to ever end...Show less

Author: 640herbertl
Title: Great food
Review: Once you sitted down and having your food, the owner will make sure you have a peace of mind while enjoying what you eat. Superd recommendations by the boss. Thanks.

Author: Abikoh
Title: Good food
Review:
A bit pricey but worth the visit.
The location is not that convenient if you are staying at jonker street. However, it's worth making a visit down here.
Advance book is recommended

Author: ShiouSingaporeSingapore
Title: Enjoyable dining, reservation recommended
Review: We were there on a weekend for lunch with our friends who made reservations the day before. Some walk ins had to be turned away unless you arrived nicely when some people leave. The host's recommendation were good and the dining experience not rushed and enjoyable. We had Kuey pitee (they seem to run out so prior order may help), Otah, hee peow soup etc. My only disappointment was they do not have my favorite ngoh Xiang.Show less

Author: Hui CSingapore, Singapore
Title: The tastiest homestyle Nyonya meal I've had in years!
Review: We went to this restaurant without any expectation and were totally bowed over! When we arrived at 7.30 pm some of the more popular Nyonya staple dishes were sold out. We went along with the owner/ host's recommendation and ordered the sour Assam fish, otak otak, ayam ponteng and the restaurant's signature kang kong dish. And boy, these dishes really hit all the right spots and left us clamouring for more. So we ordered the curry chicken and it was the best we had in years - the chicken was tender and favourful and the curry was rich, aromatic, smooth and not the bit oily. To top it off, our host was warm and gracious. He even introduced us to his wife and chef, auntie Amy. It was a wonderful evening of great food and great company. We will definitely be back soon for more.Show less

Author: braydenlim123Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Amy's Nyonya cuisine
Review: We arrived at the restaurant around 8.30pm and the old man said kitchen was closed. However as there was only the two of us, he let us in, and decided to 'reopen' the kitchen for us, which was thought was really nice of him. Food was good. The waiter was really good at recommending us dishes and we were quite satisfied with the dishes. The dishes were nice and unique. Would return again if we had a chance.Show less

Author: derrcheung
Title: Nice Nyonya Food
Review:
Was recommended by our hotel to this restaurant.
We tried another nyonya food near to our hotel in Jonker Walk but this is nicer. The taste is better and it's actually very nice especially the sour fish. Price is reasonable.

Author: Singapore313Singapore, Singapore
Title: excellent Nyonya food
Review: we make a reservation for Saturday afternoon 1pm. We were late due to jam and reach there close to 2pm. The owner had informed us when we made reservation that the last order is before 2pm. So it was very nice of the owner, Mr Lim to quickly take our order as we plonked into our reserved seats at a nice table. The Hee Peow soup was so yummy and invigorating after a long drive. The pineapple prawn is heavenly and we had extra rice to go with it. The owner was fast t serve us the food and it taste better than anywhere we have tried before (eg Nancy's, Ole Sayang). The Asam fish gravy is so delicious after Mr Lim taught us how to appreciate it..and he was right! We just have to drink it instead of going with the rice. We wanted to order another serving past 2pm..but Amy came to explain to us that her food is cooked from scratch and we have to wait for another 20 min as she has closed her kitchen, but she was prepared to do it for us...and that's nice of her. Overall, it was a good makan session - good food, nice & clean place, spacious and owner is so hospitable to recommend the dishes to us, and replenish drinks and rice promptly even with full house of other guests. BTW, they are strict about reservation because we witness how he had turned away other walk-ins as well as those who came in past 2pmShow less

Author: icebaby0Singapore, Singapore
Title: Food isn't as fantastic and yes, the elder owner is abit rude
Review: The food isn't fantastic. The food we ate at another place was better. I think my late grandmother-in-law make better Nyonya food. What I dislike was the elder owner who is abit "proud" and told us we had to "reserve" cos they are very booked. But the best joke is, when we went at night, there wasn't any other table except us thru the night! And it is a weekend by the way.Show less

Author: GeochongPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: worth a try
Review: visited on a Sunday night. it wasn't crowded and service was prompt. However as they prepare food enough for the day so some of the dishes were not available at night. better to come for lunch. The prawns and vegetable masak lemak were good. Fried chicken was average. would come back again.Show less

Author: applejaneongBatu Caves, Malaysia
Title: terrible services...
Review: after read the review , my cousin sister is decide to go there have lunch with our families .We had reserve the table for 30 person , and when we reach the restaurant , an elder"rude man" said we had no making any reservation on that day , so make my family all cant have lunch at there and amy told my cousin sister that my cousin sister din make any reservation , so she give up our order , this make all my family members very dissapointed and make us need to find other place to have lunch , and the most important is that day is my cousin sister wedding ceremony and we very sure that we had call them 2 times to make the reservation and confirm the reservation..really so disappointed with they service and attitude..Show less

Author: vivted56Brisbane, Australia
Title: Died and gone to Heaven!
Review: This is a restaurant that MUST be visited for those who have a love of good Asian food. The place abounds with customers which attests to the quality of the food. Our interaction with an older gentleman/ waiter enhanced the whole occasion as he suggested that we wouldn't really like the combination of some dishes that we had ordered and he steered us to a selection that would be fitting for a 'Last Supper'. Make sure you have the pineapple curry!Everything including the price was amazing!Show less

Author: kuaychapSingapore, Singapore
Title: Local recommendation
Review: Amy's was recommended to us about 2 years ago, and we make it a point to return each time we are back in Malacca. Booking is essential at weekends, and advised at other times. The restaurant is usually full and the acoustics make it a very noisy place. Those looking for a fiery curry experience should go elsewhere. If you are looking for peranakan food in a restaurant as close as possible to homestyle then this is the place to find it. The only minuses are no pork, and no shaved ice for the chendol.Show less

Author: Dina21monstersssSingapore, Singapore
Title: Small resturant, reservation recommended.
Review: Was there on Sat around 12pm to make reservation for Sunday lunch, but was told is full house...We change our plan to have lunch there instead of Sunday, was told is full house too..Nice boss suggested us to wait, as the 1st round customer almost finnish.We feel lucky to have our sit as have seen a few beening turn away.We had Pie Tee(nice), otak, chap chye, Kangkung Kobis Keledek Masak Titik Lemak (boss recommended, as only his shop have this, but we dnt find it fantastic) then the Ayam Pongteh, our family all time favourite(very nice)Another Nyonya restaurant that you may want to try if you have been to Nancy Kitchen. Both are nice,Show less

Author: CeciltongSingapore
Title: I strongly suggest making a reservation.
Review: This was the place of our last meal before our 3 hour trek back to Singapore, and we made the right choice. I called at 11 am to reserve a table for 12.30pm, and I was thankful for my wife's foresight in wanting me to do so. The place was full when we arrived and we would have been turned away if not for the reservation (call: 06-286 8819).My wife (a Peranakan and a competent cook herself) raves about Amy's. She kept telling us (the non-Peranakan side of the family) over lunch about how Amy offers dishes not often offered elsewhere, which reminded her of her parents' cooking. Yes, if you are not aware of this fact, some Peranakan men are very accomplished cooks and my late father-in-law was one. Amy and her husband run the restaurant and she takes the trouble to talk to you when you order, to tell you what fresh ingredients she was able to buy from the market that day. We were hoping to order "kueh pai tee" (braised radish in a crispy shell) but another table ordered most of it before us. (We should have ordered when making the reservation, as the other table did.)To "compensate" Amy offered us a complimentary serving of "onde onde" (coconut covered glutinous ball with a smooth filing of rich gula Melaka). The complimentary water tasted unusual but we soon realised that they had added fragrant pandan leaves to mitigate any possible taste of chlorine in it. We had the fish maw soup (a clear soup) which was a pleasant choice before the far heavily flavoured main dishes. For the mains, we had the "kangkung kobis keledek masaaki titik lemak", which was delightful (for me as I love coconut). Its kangkung and sweet potatoes with a soupy coconut gravy. The "ayam ponteh" (chicken braised in a soy sauce and spices) came with potatoes and was my younger daughter's favourite, as she is not too keen on spicy food. We also had the assam fish (fish in a sourish soup base and served with tomatoes and lady fingers). The lemak, ponteh and assam are very distinct flavours and eating them all at one sitting made my taste buds work overtime. Don't get me wrong, it was a delightful experience. And it made me reach out for more rice to accompany those exquisite flavours. We also had the chinchalok omelette, which was good. We also ordered the otah, which was a piece of fish cake covered in rempah (a coconuty paste). We obviously over ordered but we finished everything and belched all the way home (haha). The other thing that made Amy's special was the fact that you had to wait a little while for your food, and that's because every dish that she serves is cooked when you order. And that feast (with drinks) for 4 only cost us RM$122 (S$50).Show less

Author: Lauren H
Title: Excellent fresh tasty delicious food with fantastic and attentive sevice
Review: Amy's was definitely worth tracking down, the food was delicious, the portions generous and the service excellent. We were greeted so warmly and continued to be spoken to by the owners throughout the night, it was a lovely experience. I saw a comment stating this was an expensive restaurant, this was anything but expensive and truly worth a visit.Show less

Author: DTan TSingapore, Singapore
Title: Average taste but generous servings
Review: As we arrived 2 hours late due to traffic jam on the NS highway, we were pleasantly surprised by the warm welcome f food all laid out on the table. The service staff were cheerful and, knowing how hungry we were, quick to meet all our needs. We liked the cendol, made on the spot, at a stall set up just outside the restaurant.Show less

Author: ihawk98
Title: Authentic peranakan food, friendly owners.
Review: Forget the touristy peranakan food at Jonker Street, the food at this restaurant is arguably one of the best in Melaka. Must try is the Titik Lemak. Cendol here is served with ice cubes which does not hardened the cendol although it wasn't as sweet as I thought it would be. Owners are friendly and will stop by your table for a quick chat. Show less

Author: PapuacragratVancouver, Washington
Title: A feast for the eyes, and o yes, the stomach!
Review: Nyonya food has become popular and "normal". With that in mind, it helped to be with local Malacca folk who know Amy as we were treated well. It also helps: to make reservationsthat it's quiet on a week daythat we had a large group, so we could have more dishes and variety.Amy's seating isn't huge, which means that food comes out quickly, is tasty and good. But expect noise rebound when it's full of people.Warning: Two of our group asked for regular water (as opposed to bottled water). The water tasted weird - perhaps straight out of the tap?!Show less

Author: KylieTong
Title: Satisfied with their foods...Nice!!!
Review: Their service was very good especially the boss.He was very friendly and nice to giving suggestion to us while ordering our foods.I love their dishes very much,especially their Sambal petai udang and desserts.

Author: SingaporeRonSingapore, Singapore
Title: Good Find
Review: On this trip, we were delighted to have been directed to Amy's. The food quality was excellent, though it's halal.Appreciated that they limited their reservations so as to maintain standards.No long queues n ppl hovering ard yr tables. Loved the overall setup & cleanliness.Show less

Author: earl9reyKuala Lumpur, Wilayah Persekutuan, Malaysia
Title: so nice meh?
Review: for me it's just normal. the boss didn't let us to choose our own menu. when we said we want certain dishes, he said not nice la this one more nicer, Kangkung Kobis Keledek Masak Titik Lemak other shop don't have lar. we order 4 dishes for 6 person and he keep insist that the dishes is not enough for us, we should add more. it's kinda piss me off when he force like that and saying if u add later, u need wait long time for the food to come again. we want peacefully choose our own food also cannot?Show less

Author: NatKLKL
Title: Write-up and awards on the wall-a truly disappointing affair!!
Review: After my nephew's graduation in Melaka, he booked at Amy Heritage Nyonya Cuisine Restaurant for dinner for all of us. I was looking forward to introduce an authentic nyonya meal to my mum and my nephew's family. It was on Saturday night, restaurant was fully booked, soon as we entered the restaurant, it was very noisy with a group of Chinese families presumably from SG with their children(both adults and children trying to outdo each other in talking and screaming at the same time!!!) after half an hour or so, they are still as excited, I asked the waiter if he could let them know to reduce the noise down a little but I was told, it was not his place to do so. Eventually, politely I had to ask one of the diners in the group to lower the noise down a little.. BUT to no avail! We had a big order for 11 of us, pai tee to start with, chicken buah keluak, masak lemak prawns with pinapple, kangkong kobis keledek masak titik lemak(yellow curry with cabbage, morning glory, sweet potatoes), telur dadar cincaluk(preserved shrimps omelette), bendi kukus (blanched ladies fingers with sambal), sambal jantung pisang(banana flower sambal/salad) and chendol. We were given 3 complimentary small helpings of 'fermented rice' which were already going sour!!!(past it's due date???) The food was very bland and disappointing.. I must say, I would not be dining there again.Show less

Author: MadamkMelbourneMoreland, Australia
Title: Bland food a disappointment
Review: We were visiting Malacca and relied on TripAdvisor to find authentic nyonya food for dinner for the one night we stayed. We finally found Amy's and were delighted to get a table, although it was a Tuesday night. We went through the menu and asked advice from the waiter (maybe Amy's husband). He recommended one main dish, which was a chicken dish with potatoe and mushroom, in a nyonya gravy. We were looking foward to a nice, tasty, spicy meal using the local spices. The appetiser was very nice (the little chef's hats), the chicken wings were simply fried chicken, which was a little disappointing. However, the chicken main meal was very disappointing - as soon as I tasted it, it was exactly like an apricot chicken dish we used to make at home (chicken cooked ina tin of apricot juice with a packet of dried French onion soup). Maybe we chose the wrong meal, but it was disappointing.Show less

Author: fire-tower
Title: The Food Did Not Disappoint
Review: Nonya restaurants are a dime a dozen in Malacca, and preferably, you should be recommended to one by someone familiar. Amy Heritage Nonya Cuisine was recommended by a friend as well as by our hotel. It was closed when we last visit Malacca and this time round, we arrived at the restaurant on a Saturday afternoon for lunch. Guess what? They were fully booked! We requested for a Sunday lunch reservation and again, they were fully booked. However, there was table available on Saturday evening, and voila, we are back to Amy's for dinner.
