Review: Went for dinner as recommended, but disappointed at limited fare on offer (set dinners) despite this, the service still managed to be dreadful - 3 dinners arrived within 20 minutes, then one more 15 minutes after that, whilst the other 2 (same as previous orders) had their rice brought after an hour, then the curries when the microwave had heated them at 10 minute intervals. No apology, and accused of having more desserts than entitled to. I'm live in Malaysia, and am used to food arriving when ready, but this was just clearly forgotten orders and dreadful service.Show less

Author: Dedee3
Title: Views are ok, the rest forgettable
Review: Food was bad, service really average, waiting time too long, they forgot one dish (which they tried anyhow to charge), one serve of rice arrived 5 mins after the first one, really the basics aren't there!

Author: Ivan L
Title: Kitchen is a disaster...
Review: Nice concept and good location, but kitchen is a disaster. 6 people standing around and 1 cooks order by order. No wonder it took 45 mins for some basic lunch dishes chicken rice/laksa). Completely clueless.

Author: SharmilaG8
Title: Terrible service
Review: Seemed more interested in serving foreign tourists than locals.I wouldn't recommend this place to anyone. They got my order wrong after I waited an hour for my food.I was deeply disappointed after reading positive reviews.

Author: Waddy W
Title: Relaxing river scenic experience
Review:
No nothing were so impressive except place & ambiance.

Sat by the river bank with light drink and a couple of curry-puff + cigarette. 

Dont forget to raise ur hand every times the boats pass thru u! Hahaha enjoy n experience it! XD

Author: Robin R
Title: Breakfast yuck!
Review:
Breakfast was awful, instant coffee with fake creamer and sugar
Without even asking if I take sugar.  And remember "sausage" 
Is hot dog in these parts.  Hash browns were greasy and out of a box.
Expensive too, what a disappointment.

Author: Kesh K
Title: Good dining experience
Review: Had dinner with my family here. Food was good and prices reasonable. Had the set meals as that was the only choice during the weekend. No ala carte. You can sit either by the river bank or indoors. Friendly staff. Good place to dine!

Author: Austin_fr_tawau
Title: nice view
Review: we stumble on the restorant , nice and friendly place, lots of nice food with exceptional of the satay. Don't order the satay, the worst satay in Malaysia.

Author: mayL91Klang, Malaysia
Title: not worth the money
Review: nice ambience but the portion is small, food was so-so, not worth the price at all..service was pretty poor as well..will never return to this place again! the only good thing about this restaurant is that we can dine by the river of malacca,really windy at nightShow less

Author: Dantes GKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Lousy foods
Review: Here is a list of why u should go to Dutch harbor cafe: ambience and nothing else. I went there for dinner and since it is a cafe by the river, so expect cool breeze while u are having your meal. It is a good place to sit down and chill. However the menu at night is of limited options and all of them are set meals. No alcohol is served in this place. So if you are looking for someplace to sit down and have a drink, head to other place instead. I would rate the foods 2/5. I would strongly advised against this place. Show less

Author: auntybibHunter Valley
Title: Bizarre menu - no options and guaranteed indigestion!
Review: I am not sure who the menu planner is... but whoever thinks a set menu of pumpkin soup and chocolate pudding with ice cream (no options) can sit well with...sate, or portugese chicken curry has shares in indigestion remedies. Maybe the western options for a main course were a better fit.. I passed on the pumpkin soup ( it was a hot and humid night!!)Regardless of three option of passwords. no joy on the wi fi, and no help from staff pleasant to be sitting near the river but left as soon s possible... and never to return!Show less

Author: AustraliaAthenaPhnom Penh, Cambodia
Title: Much promised, little delivered
Review: We actually searched this restaurant out based on previous reviews, and thought we'd have dinner there on our last night in Melaka. The advertised free wifi was an added attraction.What a strange experience - for a start, there was only a set menu being offered, with very limited options. The set included pumpkin soup (no option) which came even though we said we didn't want it it, some Asian themed mains including satay sticks, and chocolate pudding with ice-cream ( no option). Bizarre and nearly inedible overall.The wifi didn't work, and the staff couldn't have cared less.Show less

Author: 566singapore
Title: Meal By The River
Review: Saw this place during our 2008 trip but did not have the opportunity to try their foods.So this round trip we decided to try it due to their good review.What I can say is that their foods come with reasonably priced menu but very small portion.We sat by the river, watching the boats go by.Nothing impressive except location and ambiance.Show less

Author: Atikah R
Title: Nice view, nice place
Review: Apparently I'll visit this cafe again if I had a chance to visit Malacca in the future. My husband and I were warmly greeted by the staff. It has two area;back side and front side. But I'll definitely suggest you to go to the back side of the cafe to have your food as you can sit by malacca river. Food wise I rate it 4/5. It has variety of cuisine including local and western food. I'd tried asam pedas and it was nice. Show less

Author: skogs1Wellington, New Zealand
Title: good riverside cafe
Review: Nice place to take a break from strolling around the historic centre of Melaka, and recover from the heat. Great (and strong) brewed coffee plus a good and interesting range of cakes, such as apple pie and ice cream, and bread and butter pudding (I kid you not!). As well as watching the river boats, you might also see monitor lizards swimming up and down too.Show less

Author: 9M2RT
Title: Scenic by the river cruise breakfast joint
Review:
Dutch & American Breakfast served. 
Monster Burger hilights @ Wall of Fame. 
Shaded from the morning sun blocked by the building makes a perfect location for having a cuppa.

Author: RuthC460Andover, United Kingdom
Title: Excellent find!
Review: We stumbled upon the cafe on a very hot day when everywhere else seemed closed. So did not know what to expect. Wow, we're we pleasantly surprised. The menu was varied and we plumped for a traditional dish, not really knowing what it involved apart from Chicken. There was a little wait but only because it was freshly prepared, so no complaints there, much rather that than hear the ping of a microwave! The staff were friendly and the slight breeze from the river welcoming. We sat and watched the river boats while refuelling ourselves, even the iced tea was freshly made. Show less

Author: NazhirahSingapore
Title: So far e Best tasted ribs in Msia!
Review: When we first entered this recommended restaurant located along the river at Jalan Laksamana, Malacca, we thought that the place looks a little bit aged but as the saying goes, never judge a book by its cover! The ribs we tasted were ever so good thus far in Msia! The meat were tender & succulent, not too undercooked or too dry, served with an excellent herbal-infused sauce. Its a must try! RM48 for a big chunk of lamb ribs is worth the spending. Service was excellent (very friendly owner) and our food came just in time. We will definitely be looking forward to return in our future trips to Malacca.Show less

Author: aamirjavid
Title: Tasteless Food by River
Review: Ordered Asam Padas , a recomended local dish which lacked proper seasoning.Nothing impressive except location and ambiance

Author: sarijmiller
Title: Nice food in good setting
Review: We both had curries that were really delicious. We sat by the river, watching the boats go by. The mango shakes are seriously yummy and the staff nice and friendly. We would recommend to anyone visiting the beautiful city of Malacca.

Author: pupsie m
Title: splendid!
Review: love the foods...their service...we get to know the owner..plenty of variety...just 15 min walk from my hotel..

Author: Beijingfolks
Title: Quaint spot by the river
Review: Child-friendly place, warm welcome, prompt service, reasonably priced menu and good view of the river.

Author: Noraliza BShah Alam, Malaysia
Title: Delicous "halal" food @ romantic atmosphere
Review: The first time we came in 2012 we met the owner and had a great meal there, by the riverside. It's chicken lasagne is my favourite and hubby adores the carbonara pasta. Very nice pizza too. We promised to come again and early this year (2013) we spent the evening there on my birthday for my favourite lasagne (again??? hehehe...yummy) and also trying out the asam pedas there. I would recommend to all locals and foreign travellers to try out this place and enjoy the variety of menu the cafe has to offer. The local and international dish they are serving are equally tasty and value-for-money. Next time we are in Melaka....this cafe is a MUST stopover.Show less

Author: Bernddasbrot2016CHVerscio, Switzerland
Title: BBQ your own satay sticks
Review: We had drinks and satay sticks there. Nice place on the river, friendly staff. We went in because the idea of having our own satay stick bbq was nice. The sticks were ok, though with 6 for about 20 RM more than double the price than in other restaurants in Melaka.Show less

Author: tinarossPerth, Australia
Title: A Long Wait
Review: Situated on the murky river where the ferry shuffles up and down, you will locate the little restaurant known as the Dutch Harbour Cafe. The prices were reasonable so I selected Thai Green curry Chicken for 8.8ringgits. I waited and waited for over 40 minutes, even though the place did not seem overly busy. Finally after a long duration of watching Santa throw goodies at the cruising ferries, a gentleman finally noticed the empty glass and nothing else on the table.Within 5 minutes, my meal was delivered. Taste was just okay and I guess I was a bit disappointed after the anticipation of finally having the meal arrived. Great spot for watching the world go by if you have nothing to do all do and simply, wait.Show less

Author: Xbrit2004Songkhla, Thailand
Title: A peaceful meal by the River
Review: I have lived in Melaka for almost 6 months now and Dutch Harbour is far and away my favorite place to eat. The staff are friendly and speak excellent English, the variety of food spans everything from simple local fare to Beef Stroganoff and Shepard's Pie, and you can eat outside, by the river under an umbrella, inside under a fan, or outside surrounded by walls but with an open roof. (I prefer the river when it's cooler, or inside when it's hot. They have a bunch of fans inside and also a "Swamp Cooler" for rally hot days).Prices are a step above "Street Food prices" but lower than Hotel prices, so expect to pay around RM 10-20 for a meal with a drink. Well worth it given the location and the quality of the food.They serve a great breakfast for RM 12 at any time of the day but don't expect them to open before 10 am since they tend to stay open pretty late into the early morning. (Tell Nina, the manager, that "Mr. Douglas" sent you and she'll probably sneer at you and complain that I don't eat there often enough). They also have a "Burger Challange" - a triple (quad?)-decker hamburger loaded with everything but the kitchen sink, plus fries ,for RM25. People who order this get to sign their name on "The Wall of Shame" listing their name, country of origin, the date, and how long it took them to eat it. I have avoided that particular challenge but the regular "hamburgers" taste great, The owner Azahar, can usually be found there on weekends. He is an excellent host and speaks flawless English, so expect to be pumped for tales of your travels and opinions.All in all a great place to eat a quiet meal by the river. A bit beyond the usual backpackers budget but the perfect place to take a break from "Noodles and Rice" if you want to splurge a bit.Show less

Author: asia2go
Title: Special and romantic!
Review: Special location to spend a tranquil and romantic candlelight evening on the water's edge. Very special menu and warm staff.

Author: WaniSalehin
Title: Romantic monthsary dinner
Review: Spent our 29th/last monthsary dinner before getting back to a 9 months long-distance relationship. Dining by the riverside is so romantic. Excellent spot of opening up a restaurant

Author: Choy9w2pck
Title: Pokok Melaka (Melaka Tree)
Review: Wonderful boss and the madam... tried the Laksa Melaka.. wonderful part was relaxing under the Melaka tree at the backyard of the cafe.

Author: MVLVA
Title: Really nice spot by the river
Review: Had already been in this restaurant in 2008. Being again in Melaka, I wanted to return because I have liked it a lot. Good cooking with tasty dutch specialities. Superb staff. Also there is free internet.

Author: Lll6033
Title: Good environment good food
Review:

The foods are great and the cake not that sweet which I can finish it without sharing. 😋

Author: amalziaqKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Suprisingly Amazing!
Review: Went in to try after walking around Jonker and was attracted by the exterior.We ordered the Nasi Lemak, mee goreng, otak-otak and a few other dishes.Complimentary cheese cake because our otak-otak came late Overall experience was great and food was delicious. Author: Jasminetea53Cambridge, United Kingdom
Title: A great find

Author: Kevi9812

Title: Great atmosphère, better food and friendly people
Review: Peacefull place, with old but stilysh fourniture, Little garden and local food. Super cakes and good coffee.

Title: Good

Chique place

Author: Carole HMelbourne, Australia
Title: Great Cakes
Review: We dropped into ChopTiang Bee after walking around the Jonker Street night market. We had cool drinks , carrot and orange juice for me and ice hazelnut chocolate for him, both were really good! Our cakes were dad's carrot cake and the original chese cake and they were delicious, I wish my dad could make a carrot cake like that! The service was friendly and prompt and the air con was nice and low. I wish I was staying in Melaka longer so I could go back for a full meal.Show less

Author: ArtoMoira
Title: Beautiful Peranakan food
Review: Great friendly service and beautiful food. We had the Nonya Laksa, OtakOtak and Beef Rendang and each dish was just absolutely massive.
Restaurant: Chop Tiang Bee Cafe and Restaurant

Author: Paradise795648Singapore, Singapore
Title: Delicious Local Food
Review: This place has a very calm atmosphere,and the food was delicious! I especially recommend this place's Laksa and Nasi Lemak, a local delicacy in Malaysia. The building was very hygenic, and looked very nice. The building was very well air-conditioned. I recommend this place to anyone who likes Laksa and Nasi Lemak.Show less
Restaurant: Chop Tiang Bee Cafe and Restaurant

Author: thtareka
Title: Lunch
Review: Lovely shop if you like to eat traditional Malaysian dishes. What had is 02 CTB Nasi remak with ayam goreng berempah There are side dishes, fried fish, roasted peanuts, and fried chicken drumstick. 04 CTB Laksa Laksa noodles (noodles in spicy coconut milk curry with fish ball, shrimp, fried tofu. What you should try is a homemade carrot cake it just comes out of the oven still warm. It's the most delicious carrot cake I ever had.Show less
Restaurant: Chop Tiang Bee Cafe and Restaurant

Author: Travelbug880Los Angeles, California
Title: A foodies delight!
Review: On a street just off Jonker, the restaurant can be found in a building that exudes peacefulness. The walkway to the entrance passes through a zen feeling garden which has a small patio with low tables. Orders are place at the front counter. This place can be busy so don't be surprised if you have to wait not only to order but to find a table. The tasty food makes any wait worth it. The place is not very large.This is the place for a modern rendition of Nyonya cooking. Even the desserts are a delight. Run, don't walk to experience the food here. Monday the restaurant is closed, so plan accordingly. The prices are not street food prices but affordable. When I go back to Melaka I will be making a beeline to have a meal here. As it is, I was only in town for 4 days and ate here twice. Would have eaten there a 3rd time but one of my days in town was a Monday!Show less
Restaurant: Chop Tiang Bee Cafe and Restaurant

Author: laladabCambridge, United Kingdom
Title: Hidden gem
Review: This pretty little café has a lot of charm and really good food! In fact, it served some of the best food we had in Malaka. Our children enjoyed it too! Overall, it’s a shame our stay in Malaka finished and we didn’t get the chance to go to chop Tiang Bee again! I highly recommend it! Show less
Restaurant: Chop Tiang Bee Cafe and Restaurant

Author: richardwarwick1969
Title: Great little place
Review:
Wonderful little cafe just off Jonker. Beautiful l, calm garden with great food and smiley service. Try the 5piece chicken. 

Only comment is shame there’s not more shade in the garden as it’s a lovely oasis. 

Recommended.
Restaurant: Chop Tiang Bee Cafe and Restaurant

Author: itsyyyyy
Title: Newly opened cafe
Review:
Food was average. 
Price is alittle pricey.
Ambience is chilled and cozy. 

Overall, i will not recommend.
Restaurant: Chop Tiang Bee Cafe and Restaurant

Author: SanfordCheeSingapore, Singapore
Title: Retro cafe w/ air conditioned comfort
Review: This is a beautiful Cafe. The entrance looks inviting and the interior is spacious with retro chic. Somewhat similar to The Daily Fix in terms of coziness but less crowded and with a more toned down retro influence. But the best thing is that it as cool comfortable air conditioning to beat the Melaka heat. Nice place to chill over iced coffee and quiet reading. Show less
Restaurant: Chop Tiang Bee Cafe and Restaurant

Author: SohyinSingapore, Singapore
Title: Interesting Brand New Cafe in Jonker
Review: My Singapore hairstylist recommended this cafe as her Friend was one of the partners. We decided to try it and we are pleasantly surprised, Food wise, I would say it is quite good. It serves good local Malaysian food like nasi lemak and laksa. And my boy said the laksa was the best out of the 3 restaurants that we tried out during our trip. It also serves interesting ‘fusion’ type like pasta with a local tinge.WeShow less
Restaurant: Chop Tiang Bee Cafe and Restaurant

Author: roxanner2018Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Local Malaysian food
Review: Saw the beautiful entry of this restaurant while walking through China town in Melaka. They have fresh products and make tasty local dishes with chicken or sea food. They have fresh detox fruit juices and delicious homemade pastries!The only thing odd is that you need to pay before receiving your order. Show less
Restaurant: Chop Tiang Bee Cafe and Restaurant

Author: Vacation825132
Title: New Tasty Food Explore at Malacca
Review: Excited!! Finally found another tasty local food at Malacca! 1st image of the restaurant which we found that it was previously a furniture shop which our furniture been bought from.Wow! what a unexpected transformed into a Fusion Local Nyonya Restaurant!Nice environment,Friendly crews,Tasty food recommended their Signature NasiLemak and Curry Laksa!Appreciated on their Free Christmas Cookies too!Definately will come back again when visit malacca!Thank you.Show less
Restaurant: Chop Tiang Bee Cafe and Restaurant

Author: dr_ganlt
Title: Good Clay Pot Food
Review: Nice and authentic clay pot food. The fish fillet, roast pork in clay pots are delicious. The fried eggs onion is good too. Good dinner.

Author: ck kSingapore
Title: dining @ Restoran LSM
Review: This is a place that is totally hidden away from civilization! You won't be able to see or smell it from the main roads. Its along the seaside road towards Holiday Inn. It's a small little establishment tugged away. From all the quiet lanes and shophouses, we drove and the GPS led us to this jostling and bustling place. WE arrived there at 6.45pm and had to wait till 7.15 for a seat. And another 15mins for thee food. Seating is limited and service is not too bad even tho it was packed. Food is GREAT and price is reasonable too. Parking is avail. Their curry dishes is a must try. And veg dishes get sold out rather quickly. Show less

Author: JohnNg636
Title: Excellent dishes served mostly in clay pots
Review: Food quality is very good but one needs to go early. They won't take reservations and don't even bother calling them. I think they ignore all calls.

Author: jontravelsandeats
Title: Yummy fish curry! Would recommend
Review: Yummy fish curry! Would recommend this if you’re into lemak (creamy) curries. Everything was served in clay pots, so they stayed warm throughout our meal.

Author: Joyce T
Title: Great food at reasonable price
Review:
Expect to queue as the food is good. The chicken in black sauce is very good.Locals often come here for their daily meals.

I would recommend to stay away from the red/rice wine chicken soup, unless you like it really potent.

Author: Lee S
Title: Nice dinner
Review: This is my 2nd time visit, the food is nice and cheap. Unfortunately most of the dish is not available and sold out due to holiday period. Will come back again with my family if I visit Malacca.

Author: chiachiang
Title: Disappointed after great first visit
Review: First visit was three years ago and it was great experience, and this time the food did not live up to my expectation. I find it normal taste now. Anyway for those who have not try the clay pot style local tze char, please try.

Author: Trail09349759567
Title: all claypots
Review: This is where the locals would dine instead of the cut-throat overrated baba nyonya restaurants. Anything you ordered bound to taste good and the best thing of all, the price is pocket friendly. Not really sure about the crowd though, the restaurant seems small and they do give out waiting numbers. We were there early so we have no problem getting table. Show less

Author: RebReuSingapore, Singapore
Title: Everything in claypots!
Review: You may need to wait in line or some dishes run out if you don't go early. I particularly enjoyed the cheese prawn beehoon - not too cheesy. The omelette otah was new to me and I quite like the taste of it too. The chicken dishes were gone by the time we ordered so we took the braised pork and the buns. That didn't disppoint. It was good!Show less

Author: 780margaretySingapore, Singapore
Title: Dinner
Review: Excellent seafood served in claypots. The cheese prawn mihun is a must try. Curry sliced fish was not too spicy. The omelette with otak was palatable with the children . Fish maw soup is definitely a winner . All the dishes were piping hot as served in Claypot. Good portions for the small sized Claypot. Systematic queue with queue number issued and after waiting 1/2 hour in queue, the food was served in about 15 min. Show less

Author: jamestan1410Singapore, Singapore
Title: Did not meet my expectations at all.

The dishes does not have the “claypot” taste. They are basically the same as any zhichar stall. In fact I have tasted even better similar food in Melaka or in Malaysia..Show less

Author: bennyvectra
Title: Everything claypots, Everything delicious

Every item we ordered was in claypots. All yummy and delicious. Generous portions.
Pig stomach soup, Yam chicken, Sweet vinegar chicken, Salted fish bean sprouts

Author: 615trinalCheras, Malaysia
Title: Good food
Review: Delicious food, we order ginger fish, curry fish, vwge, han yu hua lan , and prawn eggs. The food was super , so delicious . Worth the wait. if reach 6pm should be better. we take grab , We reach 645 pm already long q, take no 31. waited 30 minutes for a seat. will come again next time. Show less

Author: davehuangSingapore, Singapore
Title: good food at value for money prices
Review: visited Restoran Lee Swee Meng in a party of 4 and we ordered 5 dishes (all size small, including one cheese beehoon). we were pleasantly surprised by the amount of food and were glad that the food served here is delicious!i prefer the cheese beehoon over the ones served at other restaurants (those tend to have a strong pepper taste). Show less

Author: lsk701125
Title: Reasonable price
Review: All foods in clay pot and service very fast although many people.  The foods is delicious too, will visit again.

Author: Jaime N
Title: Nice dishes @reasonable price
Review: Located at some remote obscure shoplot with no other shops around. Reached at 7pm, queue was no.12 already however waited got a table by 7.30pm. Once seated down, waited as dinner is cooked based on table number. Food came around 8.10pm.Ordered Fish head soup (soup is sweet & yummy), ginger fish fillet (suoer yummy), lala soup, salted fish pork fillet & potato leaves for my family of 4.Price came to about close to RM150.00 only. The fish head soup is RM50.. A very big pot indeed. Happy to gave this place a try.If u have the patience to wait at least 30mins for your table and another 30mins for your food to arrive, then by all means give this place a try.Show less

Author: DomokirisakiBrunei-Muara District, Brunei Darussalam
Title: Everything in Claypot? AMAZING!❤
Review: Many varieties of chinese food cooked in claypots! Its very unique and the food cooked is very delicious! Loved all the food we ordered!! We had Curry fish, Otak omellete, Pork belly salted fish, Yam chix, Tofu w/ mushroom, sweet potato leaves and Pork stomach pepper soup~Show less

Author: Lennon N
Title: Not open on time
Review: Went there on a Thursday 5:30pm. Sign board clearly stated they are open today and shop not open, phone nobody answer. Totally waste of time.

Author: jeffchia88Singapore, Singapore
Title: A recommendation for lunch that caught us by surprise.
Review: We had arrived in Melaka around lunch and were looking for a meal when our driver suggested we try this place.To our surprise the food they served in claypot was fabulous. We enjoyed the Pepper Pork Stomach Soup which was pepper hot and tasty. Also on top of our favourites is the Pork Leg with Vinegar. This is a sweet and sour dish prepared with black vinegar and normally lots of ginger. The Pig leg is stewed in this sauce resulting in a sweet and tangy sauce. The sauce together with the stewed meat is simply yummy when eaten with plain rice as the flavoursome sauce helps build up a healthy appetite. The location when we visited was clean. Do look out for the parking warden if you are driving and parking there without a ticket. Their business hours are: 11am to 3pm / 5pm to 9pmShow less

Author: marvin_ngrwSubang Jaya, Malaysia
Title: CLAYPOTS HEAVEN!
Review: OMG! You must try this Claypots Restaurant, everything is so good! Please be there as early as 5-5.30pm. There will be huge crowd over the dinner time. I have tried most of the dishes and all are awesome. My favorite dish are the Claypot Clams... and many others from the menu. If you are dropping by Melaka, you must not missed this restaurants besides going to fancy shopping mall restaurants or other trendy cafes in town. Recommended LOCAL FOOD! BEST!Show less

Author: WeeWeiYang
Title: Words Fail Me
Review: Just simple but delicious. Me prepared for crowd though. Advisable to come before 6pm. Affordable prices and good for bringing friends or large groups

Author: Cristine_02
Title: Good food
Review:
Was searching for seafood, found this place. Location is abit deserted but it’s a place for the locals. 
Food was fantastic, ex the cheese prawn and Lala.

Author: KLCLCC
Title: No regrets
Review:
This restaurant was highly recommended by a friend of mine so we went there on our off day. The food was amazing at affordable price and big portion! 

We will be back!

Author: Pang O
Title: Claypots galore
Review: This restaurant serves all its dishes in claypots.  If you want a good, nice, wholesome meal, this is the place to go.  It is a popular and busy restaurant and the service is not bad.  BYO allowed.

Author: dominiqueng
Title: Great chinese cuisine at reasonable price
Review:
I love the claypot sea cucumber , clay pot pork tendon and the claypot curry fish fillet. 
Not many restaurants serve pork tendon, thus i would recommend it is a MUST TRY dish.

Author: MARKW8357
Title: Excellent food in claypot
Review: We visited the place on a weekend and the place was packed. We have to take a number but surprisingly the wait was not too long. The staffs were friendly & attentive, keeping everything moving like clockwork so that the waiting customers do not need to wait too long for their table. We ordered a variety of dishes but the black pepper pig stomach soup & claypot lala were to die for and are highly recommended. All dishes were delicious and come in claypot even our egg omelette. Service was efficient & fast and pricing very reasonable. Will definitely recommend this place to our friends & relatives. A must visit on our next trip to Melaka.Show less

Author: sy3717Subang Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Need to take number to wait for a table
Review: Must go early for dinner during weekends and public holidays, otherwise need to take number and wait for at least 20-30 minutes for a table. Delicious authentic claypot food. Service okay and reasonably priced, Can make use of a parking place on an uneven site if the street parking is full.Show less

Author: MayTan21Shah Alam, Malaysia
Title: Early dinner recommended
Review: The restaurant was highly recommended by a friend, so we took the chance to come when we do a trip to Melaka. The dishes all comes in a claypot- a novelty. We tried their highly recommended pineapple prawns, pepper pig stomach soup, curry fish fillet. I must say the pineapple prawns is a must try - sour, sweet & a tinge of spicy sauce really tweak our taste buds. The curry was not our thing, if you like the over powder curry flavour. The pepper soup was ok, we prefer "oomph" to our soup. Since all dishes comes in clay pots so the dishes were piping hot when it were served - a plus points compare to our cold lunch. Definitely coming back if we are in town again!Show less

Author: hirocmp
Title: Delicious Food with reasonable price.
Review: Food taste good and fast delivery to table.Price of food also reasonable. Located at place with a lot parking. This restaurant with 2 shop-lot space but it will be crowded when lunch and dinner time so be sure reach there early.

Author: jeannie wSingapore, Singapore
Title: Yummy food cooked in claypot
Review: We went on a Tue evening, got the whole place to ourselves except for 1 more occupied table. We went there by taxi, only MR12.00 from Estadia Hotel, hence we arrived early. People started coming in when we're half way through our meal, that shows how popular the eatery is.Food is tasty and all dishes are cooked in claypots. All are so good that we forgotten to take pictures! We like the crab cooked in the local flavor/style, tasted some salted fish in it. However that did not made the dish overly salty, quite an unique taste. The crabs we're very fresh & meaty too. Definitely good value for money. Happy that we ate there.Show less

Author: chengjenni56
Title: Dinner at Restaurant Lee Swee Meng in Malacca
Review: Good food, reasonable pricing and great company. The only drawback is that you have to either go early or queue. Not sure if they take reservations. Very crowded as usual so take note. Almost all the dishes are tasty😋😋😋

Author: faithgay
Title: Love the authentic dark noodle, simply irresistible
Review: Tried cray pot la-la, traditional dark noodle, cheese bee hoon this round, very satisfied. young and old everyone happy.

Author: RoyThia
Title: Excellent food. Must try!
Review: Great dinner at the place. Must try their cheese beehoon. Their claypot dishes are very well cooked, though portion may be small. Location is within 10 mins drive from Hatten hotel.

Author: ernstdorfer
Title: Tasty food for reasonable prices
Review:
Found our restaurant of choice closed, a local guy was very supportive and brought us to Lee Swee Meng. Food was very delicious, we tried vaieties of fish, seafood, ...
Staff was friendl and fast. We will come back.

Author: Jesuislafille
Title: Yummy but portion a little small
Review: Go early as there is always queue and to avoid running out of ingredients. The restaurant closes at 9pm, all chickens were sold out by 7pm. Food is good. Portion a little small.

Author: kok kim l
Title: Good Clayport Delicacy
Review: Did enjoy the yummy food with reasonable prices. Staff are friendly and quick response. The food taste were good especially the seafood. I'll definitely come back

Author: Kenn LKuala Lumpur
Title: Lovely place filled with locals
Review: Had heard about this from a local friend and decided to give it a go on a late Saturday evening. We arrived at 7.45pm and had to wait for another 45 minutes before we were seated and served with dinner. This demonstrates the popularity of this restaurant. Patrons were mostly local and from the looks of it we were the only tourists. The rest were strictly Malaccans. You had to be local to know this place. The 45 minutes wait was worthwhile in the end. My wife concluded this after her first spoonful of the four dishes of food we had ordered for that night. I concurred after tasting the food and had to do a reality check on myself to see if the feeling of being famished had somehow influenced our evaluation of the food. I'm happy to report that the food here is simple but wholesome. Most, if not all dishes were served in claypots. There is a very fine line between simple cooking and the food you get off caterers. By cooking and serving their food in claypots, the food continues to cook while you are dining. This enhances the flavour of the ingredients and ensures that certain ingredients that may be difficult to cook at the right temperature continue to thoroughly cook itself. We had four dishes that were heart warming - (1) fish fillets with ginger and spring onion, (2) pork fillets with salted fish, (3) eggs with onions and spring onions and (4) Chinese watercress with fish and shrimp paste. I especially liked how the spring onions were cooked to a perfection and the onions were almost caramelised as they continue to cook in the claypot. The portions are good and the cost of the meal was very reasonable for the quality we were served. You can safely dine here with your entire family. While we're were here, we noticed that 95% of their clientele were in parties of five or more. Our group of three was the smallest group here. This place does not disappoint and I definitely recommend it.Show less

Author: Charles TPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: RE: A real let down meal of Portugese cuisine
Review: We had looked forward to having an authentic Portugese meal on our visit to the Settlement.Restoran De Lisbon was named as one of the most popular, according to Trip Advisor.We ordered three dishes, and, disappointingly, not one of them turned out satisfactory.I think the chef needs to pay closer attention to using quality seafood They need to serve customer fresh seafood and ensure that customers are not short-changed in value for money.For example, the crispy battered squid we ordered tasted terrible. All we got was a lot of batter wrapped around tiny little squid tails and tentacles. What happen to big round juicy squid rings? We get better quality, quantity and tastier squid/sotong from some seafood restaurant for less than the prices charged here.The butter garlic clam was swimming in a pool of melted butter in a cream sauce. It was simply too rich and milky. Any Chinese or Malay seafood restaurant could have done a better job.The Devilled Chicken curry we ordered was very ordinary in taste as well. The chicken pieces were very roughly chopped up, with bones sticking out, and the meat tasted like frozen chicken, rather than farm fresh chicken.Given the higher prices charged here compared to other ordinary roadside seafood restaurants found everywhere in Malacca, Restoran De Lisbon needs to pay closer attention to the quality, taste and presentation of its food to retain customers and attract new ones.Show less

Author: jaynec763Jurong, Singapore
Title: Great Food, Sincere Owner
Review: We went to the Portuguese Settlement because my husband's friend had said we had to visit it, and were excited about having dinner there because it's supposed to be great for seafood. We walked past the big Jesus statue and into a white building (I cant remember what the name was) and there was this nice uncle that came out telling us they are famous for authentic Portuguese food. He says they have been around since the 80s ; 40 years! We ordered the baked fish, brinjal (fried eggplant with black pepper), fried mushrooms, Assam squid, clams, cincalok egg, and the prawns.The food was really great! The baked fish was fantastic, and reminded me of sambal stingray but there wasn't sambal but it was this nice paste( that tasted like lemongrass and turmeric and a bit of spice) coated over the fish and cooked on a banana leaf. The brinjal was nothing I've tasted before. The taste was good and it seems they cook it with some salt and black pepper. The mushrooms were battered shitake mushrooms and great for kids and adults as well. Assam squid was appetizing! We ordered 2 portions of the mushroom and brinjal because it was done well and so different from what we have eaten before. The portions are big, and the price reasonable. The owner Albert, is a real nice sincere guy, and he even let us taste achar, which is a pickled vegetable dish that is hard to find, and which he made himself. Love that place, and would definately head back there when we go back. Because we were ordering mainly for the adults, we ordered pasta for my 5 year old from the store next door, (Albert's relative owns the place) The pasta really tasted good, the quality of the food is really restaurant standard. I mean, I've paid more for really crap pasta, and my 5 year old ate it all up, no need to remind him to eat. I tasted the left overs and you could taste that alot of effort went into the meat sauce. Show less

Author: Norm216Sydney, Australia
Title: Simple, Tasty and Reasonably Priced
Review: It has been years since we visited the Portuguese Settlement and that was our only intention. But we were there around lunch time and had the opportunity to visit the Museum, which was located next to the restaurants in "Portuguese Square". We were really impressed with the efforts of the caretaker, Christopher De Mello, who, together with another person, looks after the museum in a purely voluntary capacity. The place needs a lot of work to get it to a standard that would attract more local and foreign tourists, but I am sure that with local support from the government and locals, it will one day be a place "to visit" when in that vicinity. I would encourage visitors to pop in and say hello to these gentlemen who are doing such a great job. They are humble and down to earth and would appreciate all the encouragement we can give them. Keep up the good work guys!!After the casual stroll around the museum and a very informative chat, we adjourned for lunch at Restoran De Lisbon. We were sceptical at first as the ambience of the place was pretty average and it was not quite a seafront location. HOWEVER, we were far from disappointed with the dishes that we ordered. Excellent is the only description for the baked fish, dabel curry and fried bringal. Albert was friendly and very helpful with the choice of dishes which turned out to be just the right amount for the 4 of us. Compliments must be given to his smiling wife, Julie who prepared the dishes in excellent time. And the price? Very reasonable and far below what we expected. Keep it going guys - maintain your standards and word will get around. A highly recommended restaurant.Show less

Author: MalcolmM1947Richmond-upon-Thames, United Kingdom
Title: Basic but very good
Review: We were looking for Nyonya Portuguese influenced food in Malacca and so took a taxi ride down to the Portuguese Square. There are many restaurants here with open air tables by the sea front. Unfortunately, as soon as you arrive in the car park you can be pestered by touts trying to get you to their restaurant. We decided to go behind the main area to look for something less crowded. The Restoran De Lisbon has a largish sign so shouldn't be missed.It is a basic no frills out in the open (although covered) place with about 6 tables. There were a few local families eating and the food looked good. We ordered baked Sea Bass which is a speciality of the house which is cooked in foil with spices (not hot) and some wine. It was delicious. We had a mix of other small dishes to start which were also very good. Everything was fresh and hot. The proprietor was an England football fan so as Anglos - we were made very welcome. The lady proprietor speaks very good English and was very helpful in choosing the food. Well recommended.Show less

Title: Authentic cuisine we had
Review: We came to this place in the quite side of the Portuguese settlement close to papa joe,The food we had was the normal. Author: puspanathan
Title: Good Satay even for breakfast
Review: Ample space. The satay is good with a heavy turmeric flavour. Service is fast. We were told to wait 30 minutes as the crowd was big but our satay arrived earlier than that. The sauce has a unique flavour. Definitely a must return.

Author: 901stanleyl
Title: Simple and delicious
Review:
Manage to find the shop after wander off the normal Jonker Walk trail.

Reach the place around 11am. No crowd ..
 Take note that you have to go to the counter to place order with your table number.

The sweet and sour pineapple satay source...More

Author: hiiong888
Title: Pineapple Peanut Sauce Satay
Review:
The sauce is quite special because it made of pineapple peanut sauce. A little bit spicy and sour.

I personally like the pork satay. Taste as if the satay well marinated.

I ordered chicken satay, pork intestines and pork liver satay as well. All satays...More

Author: melaka13
Title: SUN MAY HIONG SATAY HOUSE
Review: i was there on 29 Dec 2018 at around 2 pm plus. No crowd. Ordered 10 chicken and 10 pork satay.  Cucumber and onions are charged at RM1 per plate. Sour Sop drink 2 glasses, 20 thinly sliced satay, 2 plates cucumber and onions at...More

Author: findingnemo82
Title: Costly
Review:
taste not bad, but the porky meat portion is small looks so "thin" ...Had a coconut cost us rm6.50 not sure if this considered as normal price. 
Services is not bad but is a bit costly as the meat is thin compared to normal ordinary...More

Author: Wyvona
Title: Delicious satay!
Review:
It’s one of the best satay in malacca! We are lucky that we don’t have to wait for table at all. Tip is to go there before 12pm!
Must order their pork satay and intestine satay!

Author: BLYC
Title: Long wait
Review: It’s one of those places in Melaka where it got too famous for it’s own good. The long wait is a turn off. The satay is alright and the sauce has a sweet and sour taste which is rather special. Would go if the wait...More

Author: OngA
Title: So so only
Review: The pork satay I would say tasted average. The intestine satay taste better, probably because of the small chunks of pork lard they put in between. The sauce is slightly sweet probably due to the pineapple being added. Cost RM0.90 per stick. Given a choice,...More

Author: ceboulter
Title: It was OK but service was slow.
Review: Que time was 15 minutes. Satay was nice but took some time to be served. Peanut sauce was different from what I've tasted before. I wouldn't rush to go back there the next time.

Author: agoh69
Title: Can be better !
Review: I found the meat is too dry. Came around 3pm on Sunday and was packed. Waited for 15 mins for food and chicken satay was running out of stock. Ordered pork and liver instead. The satay sauce is less sweet but with pineapples.. tasted quite...More

Author: cityangel78
Title: Something different from normal satay
Review: First time we eat Pork Satay. At first don't like it as it doesn't taste sweet like normal chicken satay. But after few bites, taste not bad. The Pork Satay come pineapple slide in between the pork meat. The satay sauce with pineapple taste. Not...More

Author: Happyzeus2019Singapore, Singapore
Title: Charcoal grilled juicy satay
Review: Visited this from old place near the Chinese temples till they shifted to this laksamana street. The pork satay were so juicy n flagrantly BBQ it's alwsome and most important is the gravy is so delicious with full of pineapple extracts and I even drank the gravy after finishing the satays.Show less

Author: KLCLCC
Title: Overrated
Review:
The satay was average. Meat really dry! 
The sauce was just ordinary!

Not worth the time to queue up!

Author: ailee98
Title: BBQ Satay..
Review: Recommend by the guesthouse owner, she mention must try it due to Melaka dipping satay peanut sauce was slightly different, it was a bit sour (contain pineapple). Overall, he love the sour taste but I still prefer "Kajang" spicy sweet peanut sauce.

Author: AmmyY14
Title: Delicious Pork Satay
Review: This is a quite famous Satay Restaurant in Melaka. The satay is very nice especially pork intestine. Beside the sauce are quite sweet which we don prefer sweet things (which this is very personal). Overall very good.

Author: Mumseword
Title: Overrated
Review:
We came with high expectations. The satay was ordinary, in fact, we found the meat quite dry. 
The sauce was also ordinary.
We aren't sure why the place was so crowded and why there was a long queue for tables.

Author: notfussy2012
Title: The only difference is the dipping sauce
Review:
we visited the satay shop just few days back in Malacca.
The taste of the satay was ok. The sauce contained more pineapple and thus different from what we have in Singapore.  Overall still prefer Singapore satay and our thick peanut sauce.

Author: wandererforever21Malaysia
Title: Not Impressed
Review: Heard that Melaka has good pork satay with unique pineapple sauce. Came here after reading the good reviews. Came on a Saturday afternoon, almost 5pm. It wasn’t crowded. The pork satay tasted normal, it wasn’t amazing, but the pineapple sauce was a saving grace. I loved the pineapple sauce, it tasted very different from the peanut sauce. I believe there are better pork satay with pineapple sauce in Melaka.Show less

Author: Vijayan P
Title: Very disappointed
Review:
Waited 1 hour to get my order.

Satay was dry and almost tasteless.

I come from Kajang where satay is famous. Kajang satay still better. Cheaper too. 

Not worth the wait and experience

Dr. VJ

Author: ThriftyAlwinLee
Title: Pork Satay ftw
Review: Came here to eat pork satay. Meat was tender and just enuf pork fat. Drinks were bland. 90 cents RM per stick.

Author: JTCruz69
Title: Pork Satay Restaurant
Review: You have to come early to have all varieties of satay. Came around 2pm had pork satay only. The pineapple satay sauce needs some getting used to. Had to wait about 20-30 mins for the satay due to peak season. Drinks was good.

Author: 559tany
Title: Satay was slightly salty
Review: Satay waas slightly salty for my taste buds. Only sells satay and the kuehtupat. Quite far away from jonkerwalk as well. At residential estate

Author: John CBali, Indonesia
Title: A bit of a disappointment
Review: Prior to going here we thought we may have found a great satay place in town. We live in Bali and have many places to eat top notch satay.The service is fast but the taste comes up short. A little after 1PM when we arrived, we were told they were out of chicken...we had the pork satay with some boiled rice and purple onion/cucumber vegetables. The sauce was quite tasteless while the satay left us wondering why this place was so packed with local patrons. We would not recommend the place or go again. The staff however are friendly and helpful.Easy walk near the river. No new pics to add. Ours look the same.Show less

Author: wallawSingapore, Singapore
Title: Average fare. Can find much better satay all over Melaka.
Review: Went there after reading all the good reviews and quite disappointed with the food.Satay (Pork and Chicken) are dry (not sure how they heat the satay as did not smell/see any charcoal fire). The satay are quite small too.The rice is a little wet and mushy.The sauce is quite mild (need extra chili) and the amount of pineapple is very little. Not much peanut too.Overall not worth the effort and the price is not that cheap (RM0.90/stick).Show less

Author: SylvienD10Petaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Overrated pineapple satay sauce
Review: My family and I had the pork, chicken and intestine satay. Quite small portion per stick. The satays were lacking the charcoal grilled aroma and taste. The highlight supposed to be the special pineapple satay sauce which is unusual for a normal satay dish. Unfortunately, the sauce was lacking the nutty flavour that satay sauce needs. The sour element from the pineapple does not add value to the taste, in my opinion. I still prefer the original taste of satay sauce, sweet and most importantly the nutty flavour from the groundnuts that defines what is satay sauce.Show less

Author: ConundrumMiaoKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Average Satays
Review: Pork satay - not as succulent and tender as per the review. not much taste in the meat itselfPork intenstine - slightly more fragrant than the pork satay and can tastes the charred flavourChicken satay - a lil dry for mePineapple satay sauce - sweet, slightly spicy satay sauce. prefer to have more nutty taste thoughShow less

Author: ysl_juniorKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Pork satay with pineapple based peanut sauce
Review: We went around 3+ in the afternoon and they have run out of chicken satay. Hence, we ordered pork and liver satay. The satay is a bit small size. Taste ok. The sauce is slightly sourish as it is pineapple based. We still prefer the regular peanut sauce.The shop is quite near to Casa del Rio Hotel, and facing the river.We searched for the location in Waze and it shows that the shop is closed (on a Monday). But we decided to call the shop and found out that they are open every day. So, do give them a call if you are unsure.Show less

Author: consultantckSingapore, Singapore
Title: Overrated place, can give this a miss
Review: I read reviews that the satay here was highly recommended. I got to the restaurant at around 2.10pm. I asked to place my order and was told to go to the window at the wall to place my order. I could not see the purpose of doing that, when they did not even collect the money when one was placing the order. I was told that there was only pork and pork liver satay left for the day, and I took both. Pork Satay skewers were small and relatively blandPork liver satay were dryThe satay sauce was pleasant though; tasty and tangy with lots of pineapple, but the sauce is merely to complement the Satay and not mask the taste. Tons of houseflies all over till it got really annoying that I had to cover my food portions with extra plates. I’m sure there are better satay options in MalaccaShow less

Author: oztraderPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Pork satay
Review: The new premises has ample parking and plenty of tables. The service is good and friendly.The chicken satay slightly on the dry side, the pork satay is pretty delicious but a tinge of too salty. The innards are clean and tasty. The sauce with peanut, pineapple and orange peel is delicious with tanzy stimulation, we love the sauce.Worth a try..Show less

Author: alistair15Singapore
Title: Satay Yakitori
Review: Be prepare this restaurant is really crowded with people from all walks of life. It show how good is their satay. Charcoal grilled to perfection. The aroma of the charcoal is lightly grilled onto the surface of the meat. Imagine the style of the japanese yakitori grill and that what you get from this succulent satay.Show less

Author: John-C_EWSingapore
Title: Good savoury pork satay
Review: Melaka is the only place I am able to find savoury pork satay.... can’t find it in spore or jbI simply love Melaka version of pork satay. Eventhough the crowd not bad we receive our quite fast Honestly I had better Melaka pork satay elsewhere....the meat could be charged a bit more but my biggest gripe is the peanut curry sauce is too sweet and overwhelm with pineapple such that I can’t taste the savoury marinate of the pork nor the peanut curry sauce.Most of the time I am enjoying it without the pineapple curry Show less

Author: Zuee75Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Yummy in my tummy
Review: Came to Malacca just for a day trip. First stop, satay for lunch. Easily one of the best satay houses I had even tried, meat is just perfectly skewed and taste just right, drowning them with peanut pineapple sauce. Whacked a whole lot, food coma now..think I would just sit right here and not move. Show less

Author: Kelly P
Title: Delicious pork satay and the pineapple sauce
Review: The pineapple sauce was great! There have pork and chicken satay, and other pork organ satay. Prefer the pork satay! I may visit again if I come Melaka next time.

Author: Jim Angie TSingapore, Singapore
Title: Delicious pineapple peanut sauce
Review: The satay and sauce is excellent! The right combination of pineapple in peanut sauce. The satay is succulent and delicious with the right amount of fat and meat. They serve liver satay and intestine satay as well. However, be prepared to wait as the Q may be long.Show less

Author: TakoTakoSingapore
Title: The best satay to be had in Malacca!
Review: We reached there at 4pm on a PH Sat, and they were almost sold out. We couldn't smell the satay because the stall got double expanded in terms of floor area and the satay is now done behind in the kitchen area - it used to be done in front of the stall and we can smell it from afar. Yummy, as always, even after 3 years!Show less

Author: PiggyAngSingapore, Singapore
Title: Best Satay in my experience.
Review: 3rd visit to this place and it was the last place for us to go before leaving Melaka. Do check their opening time and days as i saw they were closed till the 9th of August and i had to change our itinerary. Reached the place at around 11am, after a hearty breakfast at the hotel. Place was not difficult to find, always use Google Maps or Waze if you do not want to go random places. Parking was ample infront of the restaurant. Ordered 40 sticks to try and my family was stunned by the satay and its accompanying sauce.The pork was tender and grilled to perfection, with a piece of fat in between each piece of meat. It wasnt too dry nor too big a piece. It is meant to be eaten a stick at a time and with the tangy peanut sauce (with pineapples), it is quite a snack. Parents were too full to eat too much but they were insistent to return if they came back to Melaka again.Do take note that the Kerepok sold in the store were also fantastic, a mere RM2.50 per packet. The prawn crackers were better in my opinion as the fish ones were a tad too fishy in taste. Satay, be it pork, chicken, liver or intestine, was priced at RM0.90 per skewer.Show less

Author: TravellerfromSINSingapore
Title: Great satay sauce
Review: The pork satay was good and juicy (with the standard piece of fat in between) but the liver and intestine ones were rather dry. The chicken sticks were average but the key success factor of this satay joint is the good old traditional Chinese satay sauce that's flavored with pineapple.The location was a little hard to find and the cab driver had problems finding it. Service was efficient as we were there early before the lunch crowd came. Show less

Author: Lilian580514Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Sunday School Teacher's Retreat
Review: This satay house is non-halal as it is famous for pork satay. The also have pork parts ( intestines and liver ) satay and chicken satay. The sauce for the satay is different from the usual satay sauce because instead of using peanut, it uses pineapple in the sauce which is very nice and you will see customers asking for more sauce. Place is always packed. Business hours are from 10am to 7pm but they usually finished selling by around 6pm. The satay sticks are not very big so you can eat a lot if it is for lunch. We ate around 600 sticks ( 36 adults and 4 kids ) with some great eaters and some not so great eaters. Give it a try if you are in Malacca.Show less

Author: CharmaineSwiftSubang Jaya, Malaysia
Title: LOVED IT
Review: Super reasonable and tasty pork satay!! Will definitely be missing this place when im back in KL the sauce is sweet n spicy (it has pineapples in it) and the satay was so so good omg super sinful. Kept ordering more service was nice and fast , ate here at 5pm and some meats ran out. Show less

Author: Yv0nneSGSingapore, Singapore
Title: Nice satay!
Review: Visited at 1.45pm on a Friday and there was a family just about to leave so we didn't have to wait for a seat. Once you've gotten a table (self service), proceed to the counter to make your order. As it wasn't busy, the auntie came to our table to take our order. They ran out of chicken satay so we ordered 40 pork satay, 2 plates of rice, 1 plate of cucumber, 2 coconuts, 1 honey with aloe vera (not freshly made type) for 4 adults+2 young kids. Actually we ordered 30 sticks and decided to add on 10 more after quite sometime but they were nice enough to give us the additional 10 sticks first.The satay arrived after about 10-15 mins. It was good! The satay was well cooked and succulent with good distribution of meat and fat. It's on the savory side. The satay sauce has strong hints of pineapple and was quite watery. Perhaps I'm not used to the taste, I think I still prefer Singapore's version, especially for our peanut sauce. My husband and mum likes their sauce though and it was refilled once (no additional charge).I might come back again to give it another go. But definitely when there's no queue. Show less

Author: sinnyiKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Sauce is special
Review: Expect waiting time of at least 20 minutes after your satay order. Sauce has a very rich pineapple taste which is very different from the typical satay sauce. Satay tastes okay for me as I have tried better pork satay somewhere else. 40 satays and 2 drinks cost RM43, price is reasonable, worth trying. Arrive before 12pm to avoid long queue. Show less

Author: Suryn SKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Disappointing HOUR LONG WAIT!
Review: This place was highly recommended but turned out to be a far higher disappointment than I ever thought possible. Really sad. We had to brave Melaka's nightmarish traffic to find a park where many cars were double parked, then found ourselves in a queue waiting for tables, for about half an hour before we got a table. It was self-service so we had to queue to provide our order at the counter cum kitchen area- then WAIT for what seemed like hours to have our tables cleared and cleaned, before a RUDE waitress came by to DEMAND that we give her our order for drinks or have our food order further DELAYED- we came all the way from Selangor to sample their so-called famous intestines' satay and when our order finally arrived with people standing all around us waiting to take on our table, they had RAN OUT of the delicacy and told us to just take what they had or leave- others were waiting for our table. Not wanting to waste our table, we took our share and left with a terrible distaste- their famous pineapple sauce was watery and too sweet, and chicken, liver and pork satay nothing to shout about at all. I can't even believe how much it pains me to share this but SUCH A DISAPPOINTMENT!!!Show less

Author: arvinAWDSingapore, Singapore
Title: Pork Satay Specialist
Review: Walked quite abit to find this shop. Very old school setting. I loved it. Tried their pork and chicken satay. The dishes came in quickly. I really loved their pork satay. The peanut sauce had a pineapple twist. Slightly unconventional from the traditional peanut sauce. Definitely worth the price and the walk. Will I go back again? Most definitely:)Show less

Author: TiongTiong
Title: Nice Satay Sauce
Review:
Came here for pork satay. one of the famous shop in town. The satay sauce is very appetizing and nice. 

Do note that its always crowded during weekend and prepare to wait for your turn.

Author: albertwee1977Singapore, Singapore
Title: Belimbing satay gravy
Review: We ordered the chicken and liver satay which was grilled perfectly. However the marinade could be a lot better. Every stick had a little piece of fat in it so for those who enjoy that, you can go for it. The outstanding element was actually the satay gravy which was truly home made. Thick, sweet and unique, it had hints of pineapple, onion and berlimbing. The liang teh was also a superb thirst quencher. What we also loved was the nostalgia of the place. Our friends were rhe ones who took us there and we found out that the uncle who was grilling the satay had been doing so for 30 years. Truly a hawker legend. Show less

Author: 225matthewn
Title: Quality on the downhill
Review:
We ordered pork, chicken, liver and intestine. The portion seemed to shrink and came out dry. 
The saving grace was the peanut sauce with pineapple purée.

Author: Jooellee
Title: Disappointed
Review: I've been here three years ago and came back now. Realising that they reuse their satay stick and straws. Totally disappointed and not going to come back here anymore.

Author: rachellin8Singapore, Singapore
Title: Delicious pineapple satay sauce!
Review: The satay place is about 10 min walk from Jonker Street. As it was closed to the shop closing time, we could only tried the pork satay when we visited. I think the satay is rather different from the one we had at home in Singapore. The meat is fresh and not so much marinated. The best is actually the pineapple satay sauce that makes the meal delicious. Show less

Author: Mike T
Title: Satisfying Satay
Review: This place is relaxed, homely serving freshly made Satay.. Pork, Beef,Chicken.. be warned.. the place gets really full between 12-3pm. A little understaffed so please dont complain about the lateness in cleaning your table. The Satay and sauce is 5* plus.

Author: poopshooterPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: worth the stop!
Review: Heard about this place and decided to make a quick stop to try their pork satay. Ended up having 2 rounds of it! Very simple restaurant where you order at the counter & wait for your freshly grilled satay sticks. They have pork, intestine, liver & chicken. On the side they will come around with the cucumber & onions or ketupat (rice cake) & the super addictive pineapple peanut sauce.The pork satay is layered with meat & fat. Taste so good with its charred smoky bits. Good on its own but even better with the tangy & spicy sauce. Wash it all down with some chinese tea or even better their homemade lemon ice jelly. Refreshing & helps cut the fattiness of the satay. Prices are decent. Does get crowded but turnover is quick. Definitely worth the stop.Show less

Author: shiroangSingapore, Singapore
Title: Best pork satay (and sauce) in Melaka!
Review: Pork Satay (per stick) – 0.9 RM ($0.3 SGD)The pork satay is good and combined with small pieces of pork fat in between the meat, makes the overall balance between lean meat and fatty meat (pork fat) just right (not dry or sloppy). The grilled is just nice too (balance) with sufficient smokiness.Is this the best satay I ate in my life? I will say no, but probably the best in Melaka.But I will say the sauce is one of the best I ever tasted, which makes the whole dish shines.Initial thought it’s spicier than other restaurants’ sauce, but yet the peanut and (pineapple?) in it balances the spiciness out.Eating the satay with the sauce, its a smooth harmonious blend of taste. I just can’t stop to keep wanting to dip the meat into the sauce, and immediately into my mouth.30 sticks of pork satays went down both of our stomachs in no time…Meat Rating: 3.75/5Sauce Rating: 4.25/5Conclusion: If you like Satay, just drop by here to eat it! It’s just about 10 minutes walk from Jonker Walk. Better come early, it gets sold out early in the afternoon. When we reached at 3pm, only pork satay left. But pork satay is always our preference to benchmark satay, and apparently their best also?Compared to the other highly reviewed satay restaurant in Melaka, Xiang Ji Satay House. Xiang Ji is honestly decent, but Sun May Hiong just wins Xiang Ji in every aspect.Show less

Author: omega123Singapore, Singapore
Title: Worth the try
Review: The Satay or BBQ skewered meat on a wooden pick. The dimension is about 3 inches by quarter inch. There is only chicken and pork satay for selection. If one of the meat type was to be sold out, then it is your choice. Other than meat satay, the shop also sells liver and intestine skewers. All four types of BBQ skewers were tried and were tasty. The satay gravy was different in terms of viscosity, taste and punch if it was to be compared with other parts of Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia. The gravy had been influence by the Peranankan to a small extent thus it had a slight sour from the tangerine and less of the peanut for viscosity. The taste was sour and spicy mixture but was a good combination and taste. The pineapple was grated into the gravy as opposed to the compared which served as cut pieces on a dish.Different location different eating culture, try and appreciate, you will never be hungryShow less

Author: chungfeeSingapore, Singapore
Title: Food is satisfactory
Review: Went to try due to the reviews of the special pineapple sauce they used for the satay. Only pork available when I went. The food and sauce are ok and nothing out of the ordinary like other reviewers had described. Perhaps my expectations were raised by the other reviews. Show less

Author: wokra1Halifax, Canada
Title: First try on pork satay
Review: Reached there at about 4pm plus and there was only one table occupied, so the order came pretty fast. Minimum number of satay sticks is 10. RM 0.90 per stick. Pork satay was a bit salty for me but the sourish sauce complements it.Good to try.Show less

Author: marcellor613
Title: Good satay
Review: They have beef chicken and pork satay. Completely on jonker street attractions. You may find a nice malacca style satay in this place. Running by the family and must try the wayer melon juice that fresh from the fruitself

Author: ahleongsanSingapore, Singapore
Title: Pork satay with pineapple sauce
Review: I used to patronize this eatery at Jonker Street. A very simple shop house with just two charcoal grills and as the seller finished grilling you can just take a few sticks. Now the young man I knew is an elderly man with lots of helpers to help skewer the pork, liver and intestines satay. The grills are now indoors due to government ruling and hence no more smelling your way to find this shop which is now two shop houses wide. Overall the satay is still good and it's hard to find an eatery like this. It opens only from Thursday to Sunday and from 11 am onwards. Show less

Author: Hawker78Burlington
Title: Pineapple Sauce and Perfectly-spiced pork
Review: I've had great Malay satay in KL, that I thought could never be equalled. Most of the Chinese satay I've had in Malaysia just lacked spice and any distinct flavor, so I'd been neglecting it on my visits to Melaka. Finally cracked, and gave it a shot--and WOW. The pork skewers were suprisingly tasty and spiced but without the Malay sweetness (which I also like); and when bathed in that pineapple kuah, Oh My God--it had the heat, the acidity and sourness, and nuttiness of perfection. I wanted to spoon-feed it to myself and then offer my first-born for the recipe, but I don't have kids so that's a no-go. Basically, come eat this stuff. It's quite unique and absolutely worth the short walk from the old town center.Show less

Author: wong450Singapore, Singapore
Title: Sun May Hiong Revisited
Review: Things have changed a bit since my last visit since a couple of years ago - well the bad part is that this place is a little out of the way near the Ranger College - and is a fair walk from Jonker Street - especially in the hot sun unless you have a car .Now you have to get a table number and then go to the counter and order your satay , stating your table number to the order taker - they do serve Chicken / pork / intestine ( pig ) and pig liver satay at 80 SEN a stick - the condiments of kueh tupat / cucumber / onions are charged at I guess RGT 2.5 per head ( very fair ) - as the for drinkes and anything else the roving table cleaner will take your orders The satay sauce is what is the magic with generous mixture of pineapple . go early so that you can have your choices - I wanted intestines satay - and was told sold out - well I was there about 1500 hours on a sunday . and by the way they now operate Thursdays to Sundays - closed Mondays to wednesdays .Show less

Author: KLH47
Title: A new experience
Review: Went in the late afternoon so not much choice, only pork satay were available. But was pleasantly surprised by how well the salty pork satay went with the pineapple laden peanut sauce.

Author: Lee D
Title: Nice pork satay
Review: Tasty and i love the gravy. Easy parking. Place was packed so there was some waiting. Easy to find location.. Just google...

Author: Winnie Lbatu caves
Title: Special pineapple sauce but..
Review: Few years ago, I went and tried out the satay. It was really GOOD and DELICOUS!!It make me felt it is the best satay I had ever tried. Because the sauce is special. The satay is juicy. The sauce has pineapple in it and this match perfectly with the satay,That makes me miss it a lot whenever I think of Melaka food.Yesterday, 12 Sep 2016, I went again.The shop had expanded to two shops. They make satay in the kitchen not outside anymore. And I get a 2nd chance to eat the satay again.But I am disappointed this time. The taste had changed. Satay become small and dry. Pineapple sauce is a bit different. Not as good as previously.Is it now they are popular and famous so they produce satay with strong fire without quality control?Show less

Author: garrodhutchisonKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Disapointing
Review: We went to this place as it was recommended as a good place for Satay. In our opinion it was certainly nothing special and we have had much better satay at many other places in Malaysia. The satays we were served were small and the texture very dry. Staff are not friendly or helpful in anyway to foreign visitors. Drinks choices are very limited/ We would not recommend this place or ever go there again. Looking at other reviews I would said its reputation is highly overratedShow less

Author: Mrs Ivy Xiuli L
Title: Best Satay House
Review: Satay is not dry, satay sauce is thick and tasty. it comes with all the necessary ; cucumber, rice cube, onion. Were there at 3pm ,waited about 30-45 mins.  Expecting waiting time for lunch or dinner will be much longer.

Author: Levin LKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Not worth the long wait.
Review: We went on a public holiday, which probably made things much worse. There was a long wait for a table, and once seated, a long wait for a waitress to come over, and once she did, she told us that she only takes orders for drinks. For food, we'd have to order at the back- at the kitchen itself, actually. There was no sign saying "order here", either. A short queue formed at a window to the kitchen, but staff ignored everyone. We eventually figured out that we'd have to go into the busy kitchen itself to order. Now for the food. We don't eat pork, but we went for the chicken satay (they don't have anything else on the menu). Barely any fat on each skewer, but there wasn't enough meat. As for the satay dip, they used some sort of sweet/sour sauce. We're more used to peanut sauce. I may be speaking for myself here, but when it comes to satay, when it comes to the dip- it's peanut sauce or bust, unless the satay is so well marinated and roasted that no dip is required.Show less

Author: MfamilysgpSingapore, Singapore
Title: Excellent Satay
Review: Visited on a lazy afternoon around 3 pm. Not many pple but waited quite a while for the satay. Well, it worth every minute of the waiting. Satay was excellent, well marinated and very yummy. The satay sauce was very good too. Try the pork satay.. Very very good...shld have ordered more.Show less

Author: JamesKwok
Title: Best Satay in Malacca
Review:
it is very good with tasty sauce. 
We tried the pork satay and it was fragrant. 
Friendly staff is a bonus.

Author: Yeohgeokpheng
Title: Must try satay when you are in Melaka
Review:
Nice pork satay in town, never over burnt, juicy and tasty. Open on Sunday, close at 7pm. Weekend pack with people, have to wait at least half an hour.
       It's more savoury thansweet. Parking is much easier.

Author: weiminn2018
Title: Very good pork satay
Review:
Another must visit in Malacca,  a bit difficult to find the place but look out for the north bank of the river.

You must try the intestines satay, and of course eat it with a good mix of satay sauce and pineapple.

Author: 653AndrewSSingapore, Singapore
Title: Pineapple satay sauce
Review: Was there at about 4pm. Although managed to be seated immediately, waited for more than half an hour for our satay because the restaurant was packed and there were only 2 staff barbecuing the satay. There are only pork, chicken and some pig organs satay. The pork satay is very good. The sauce is slightly sweeter than others, guess it's because of the pineapple added into it. Overall, quite nice.Although the restaurant closed at 7pm, customers were turned away before 6pm because they ran out of satay. So, try to be there early.Show less

Author: 2074BCSingapore, Singapore
Title: An institution in Melaka!
Review: I never fail to stop by Sun May Hiong for their style of Chinese Satay.The pork satay has the right amount of moistness, taste and grill(ness). Together with their peanut+pineapple dipping sauce, it is a match made in heaven.Parking is easy out front, lots of tables (if you go early) and friendly service staff.Show less

Author: FindTravelPartner
Title: Nice satay but not the best in melaka
Review: avoid come here during lunch time because you need to wait quite long(30-40 minute) for your satay. found that the satay sauce quite watering due to pineapple. still prefer the thick peanut sauce for satay.

Author: Lim LSingapore, Singapore
Title: Perfectly grilled satay!
Review: We had 20 sticks of satay for tea. It came quite fast as there is no crowd at that time. The sticks of satay were well grilled, not burnt, and there wasn't too much fats on them. The satay sauce is unique, not quite like the usual peanut heavy ones. This one has a pineapple taste and I understand from my friend, that berlinbing is used. Show less

Author: 919DISAPPOINTEDGUESTSingapore, Singapore
Title: Yummy Pineapple sauce
Review: Wow! It is closed Mon, Tues and Wed. That is how good business is at this satay house lots of preparation for our satay crave. Its sauce is very different from the spicy peanut dip. Here it is tangy pure pineapple sauce very slight chili to dip your well fired satay pork.Next satisfying taste is the small intestines and tripe innards. The liver pieces are skewered with fat pork to give a moist taste. We arrived after 2.30pm which is most unfortunate as we got the last intestine skewer after a 10yr reminiscing trip.Show less

Author: alex tLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Over hyped Chinese pork satay place
Review: We had this satay as our first stop in Melaka and were not to impressed - the skewers of pork, liver & intestines were well cooked but minuscule in portion per skewer. If you like this version of satay, the stall beside the Kong Heng coffee shop in Ipoh does it far better. Show less

Author: Wheelers7Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Craving for the sauce but not the pork satay
Review: Another crowded eatery which took us 20 min to get a table, another 15 min for the satay. Highlight is the appetizing satay sauce with bites of pineapples but not the pork satay.The meat is quite lean, texture is a bit dry (over cooked) and slightly salty. I prefer the meat to have hints of lemon grass marinate and sweeter taste.Thumbs up on the generous additional serving of sauce when we requested for more.Ventilation is poor. Be prepared to walk away with strong lingering smoky smell on you.Will try out other shop in my next visit to Melaka.Show less

Author: Meng Lai Y
Title: Taste so so only. But slow serve.
Review: Satay taste so so only. We order 40 pc, wait 30mins only serve 20pc and wait 20mins again for another 20pc. Not worth to wait for so long just for a so so taste satay.

Author: yktangphotographyKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Great pork satay with pineapple sauce
Review: Great place, and easy to locate with waze. When we arrived there on a Thursday afternoon around 3.30pm, and was expecting less crowd, and we were wrong !!! The place was crowded. We waited for about 20-30min before our satay arrived.Excellent pork satay with unique nyonya style pineapple sauce!Highly recommended !Show less

Author: CarmenJJMalaysia
Title: Great food if you have the patience (Non-halal)
Review: Ever-crowded place, nice satay, especially the sauce for it. Lack of ventilation, and satay smells tend to fog the interior. Be very patient in order to wait for your food as limited number of satays prepared each time/ almost an hour worth of waiting this time around :(Show less

Author: Weng Meng K
Title: Most delicious
Review: This is thus far my fav pork satay. But the downside is during non peak or low season, they only open Thurs - Sun.

Author: Christine T
Title: Nice Pork Satay
Review: Is another must try satay in Melaka. The meat was so juicy and the sauce, was so so so yummy. They added pineapple in the satay sauce. I will never want to miss this if I were to visit Melaka again.

Author: babyxan88Subang Jaya, Malaysia
Title: My quick fix of "Pork Satay" whenever I'm in Malacca!
Review: Everytime without fail, I must have my quick fix of "Pork Satay" whenever I'm in Malacca!Sun May Hiong Satay House @ Malacca! My 2nd favourite place to be. 1st is Restaurant Xiang Ji (because near Jonker Street). The thing with "Pork Satay" is the way the satay is being marinated and then grilled perfectly with tender loving care. They'll serve you the freshly grilled pork satay that is juicy, succulent and really tender. Not too much of the fatty layer of the pork and not too much of the dry meat of the pork. Just perfect! Is like eating 5-layered pork at every bite!Show less

Author: ChanMLPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Must try if you crave pork satay with pineapple gravy
Review: Liked the pork satay here, especially the sauce rich with pineapple! The flavour of the satay is nice, they are not chunky pieces but dip it in the sauce makes one wonder how well the combination was. Must try if you have not been there. They also serve chicken and spare parts but I would highly recommend the pork satay!Show less

Author: ChanMLPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Never miss this satay whilst in Malacca
