Review: Excellent activity for kids. Booked the workshop. Our son was able to make his own noodle snack and packaging. Workshop advertised to take 90 minutes, however finished after 1 hour.

Author: louiso723
Title: Nice place for lunch
Review: Good place a cheap and decent lunch. Come at week day, the set meal are sold at RM5. Services are quite decent as well. Show less

Author: ReinaJ27
Title: Mamee Making Class
Review: Beside shopping Mamee products, can visit mini museum about Mamee, eat at their cafe and also joint the class to make Mamee from scratch till put in the packaging.

Author: OnAJolidaySingapore
Title: Design your own cup noodles
Review: We wanted to design our cup noodles but happened to have met with a group tour (about 30pax) who occupied all tables, so we had to wait until they are done, which is about 30 minutes. Only there then we realise that adults are able to participate in the Mamee workshop to make our own Mamee, which we initially thought are for kids only. The staff clarified that anyone above 6 years old can join the workshop, but the timing is fixed. Didn’t get more information as we didn’t have time for it. So we headed to the Mamee restaurant for lunch first, most tables were reserved for the same tour group and we took the counter table.After lunch we went upstairs and almost had the whole area to ourselves. It wasn’t clear that we hand to purchase the container for the noodles downstairs, had to decide what flavour noodles at the point of purchasing the container and the staff will indicate it below. Bought Chicken, Curry and Tom Yam, 4 for RM20.80. Recommend the Curry and Tom Tam as they are more flavourful. Had an enjoyable time colouring and designing our containers.Overall this activity is enjoyable although don’t feel the experience exceptional.Show less

Author: safety_pin11Singapore, Singapore
Title: Nice place to visit
Review: This houses a eatery, food is normal and average pricing. For families with kids, do note that most food items contains mild spiciness. There is a 'workshop' on the 2nd floor that encourages activities for kids. Good place to visit to keep children entertained. Show less

Author: merk_kl
Title: Good fun for the kids
Review: You can spend maybe an hour or 2 here with your kids either making their own instant noodles or decorating it.

Author: IzzatulShah Alam, Malaysia
Title: Worth to visit if you have a kids
Review: We came here because of the Little Monster Kitchen workshop which is only be held every Saturday and Sunday. I registered my 5y kid to this workshop and she seems to enjoy and be excited about making her own noodle from scratch. The fees is RM20.80/pax. We came early so its not crowded and we get to wait inside the workshop area and no need to pay extra. We spend around 1.5-2hrs here.The restaurant downstairs is not bad also. I think their chicken rice ball is good, the asam laksa also nice. Parking is very hard to get, we park somewhere nearby and took grab.Tips - if you need to go to the ladies, the password is in your receiptShow less

Author: Meow94Johor Bahru, Malaysia
Title: Mamee monster
Review: One of the halal restaurant to eat chicken rice ball in Jonker Walk. Its connected with mamee merchandise which is interesting to look around. The restaurant staffs were very friendly. We ordered chicken rice balls which, for me, is okay. But their matcha green tea is one of the best! Show less

Author: bucketlisttravellersSydney, Australia
Title: Niche store, museum and cafe
Review: The Mamee brand with its cute blue monster mascot is a popular and well loved brand, but I had no idea until I came to Melaka that there was a store dedicated to it. You can buy their chips and noodles there (although not individually but only in specific sets) as well as other merchandise. There is a mamee monster statue you can get your photo with and if you pay extra there's a museum, workshops and a cafe.Show less

Author: DupermanSouth Australia, Australia
Title: Ranking is Relative to...
Review: Ranking is always subjective, because the number of stars it will receive is in relative comparison to others. If Mamee Jonker House is being compared to other attractions in Melaka, this comes up as 5-stars. This is because it is relatively innovative, inexpensive and yet gives and intense (and compact) experience. The creating-a-cup-noodle experience and going through the museum for interesting selfies – are indeed the 2 highlights of the entire place.However, I have been the real Cup Noodle Museum in Osaka. If that is a 5-stars experience, the Mamee Jonker House might only come in as 3-stars, because of the lack of hygiene and the somewhat copycat experience.Nevertheless, this place comes in top amongst the places to visit in Melaka, especially if you have children that needs an activity as a form of 'entertainment'.Show less

Author: elliet163
Title: Great place to go in Melaka especially during hot weather, get yourself air conditioner place!
Review:
The kids like the making of their own names so much!
The whole process takes about 1.5 hours. The kids dressed in little chef outfit and step by step making their own mamee. With their own coloured packaging.

The named can keep for 1 week.

Author: KTCathy
Title: Workshop and Lunch
Review: There is a DIY workshop to colour our own packaging for the instant noodles. Food wise from the cafe is appropriate too.

Author: bamboolaCoralville, Iowa
Title: Not for Adults.
Review: I had never heard of Mamee noodles until Melaka. Apparently, the ramen noodles and snacks are quite popular. Our hotel suggested that we tour Jonker Street and Mamee. We took off our shoes and entered the ramen-making room. We had to wash our hands after each step of the process. Then, we decorated our ramen packaging and took our handiwork home. How did it taste? I don't know. We gave the ramen away. I can see this place being entertaining for young children. Instead of decorating my ramen cup and the packaging, I spent most of the time sorting through the magic markers and putting the correct caps on the markers. Look carefully. The red cap on the market might turn out to be a blue marker.Show less

Author: zamrudnishanaz
Title: I love Mamee!
Review: If you love Mamee, you should come down and learn more about the history of Mamee! Entrance for the gallery is free if you spent rm $20 for their merchandise; plenty of spots for you to take insta-worthy pics. Kill two birds with one stone by purchasing Mamee noodles cups which you can customised by doodling on it and choose 4 condiments to be included in your very own Mamee cup noodles! Tgey even had a restaurant there for you to indulge if you are feeling hungry. Show less

Author: 779waimunlPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: The place for kids in Melaka
Review: If there is one thing my 7 years old will remember about Melaka is the Mamee Jonker House. He loves it because you get to make your own instant cup noodle. He enjoys coloring and writing message on it. Making his own cup one of a kind. I must say it's an enjoyable activity even for the adults. It's a great place to make memories together between parents and kids.Show less

Author: BenBelYenSingapore
Title: A Good Distraction For Kids
Review: A good distraction for kids (if they ever need 1 in interesting Melaka) or a great place to park the hub & kids while you trawl the many shops in the vicinity for 2hrs. Well, my kids visited with expectations from their Yokohama Cup Noodles Museum memories. This place fell short (though not flat) upon that. In comparison, they opined that Yokohama's was educational as staffs painstakingly explained & elaborated on each step of the many processes in the making of the noodles. Here, although friendly, staff were mechanical in taking them through the processes. They felt hurried at each stage & minimal explanations were given. In Yokohama, participants were given their self-made ramen plus a few more packets of factory made ones & a cloth bandana at the end of their experience. Here, participants were given their packet of self-made mamee & a bag of 10 plus the chef hat they wore. Comparatively, RM20.80/pax is costlier than the ¥300 kids/¥500 high sch we paid in Yokohama. Plus the experience fell short.The cup noodle activity was disappointing in several aspects. The cashier insisted my kids MUST go for the Little Monster Kitchen activity before the cup making. No issue with following instructions if crowds at the cup noodle station were better managed. The crowd at the Little Monster Kitchen were somehow better-managed due to the limitations of number of equipment. However, the cup noodle activity was free for all, own time own target. As such, when my kids were ready for the cup noodles activity, there happen to be huge crowd at the cup noodle station. While some were legit decorating, there were a sizable number of companions taking up the seats. There were pockets or empty tables & seats but insufficient markers to go round. Several others hang around, waiting. When it was time to select the condiments, it was sorely disappointing - you get to choose a soup base out of 3 (chicken, curry or tom yam) & 4/6 condiments (corn, cabbage, chilli, carrots, chives & green peas). In Yokohama, there were sinks for complusory hand wash before the activity & you get to choose 1/4 soup & 4/12 ingredients which included eggs, chicken, crab & cute cartoon fishcakes! Each cup noodle also came with a special air bubble bag to protect it, making it a pretty package upon completion. At ¥300 a cup, that was pricer than the RM5.20 (min 4 cups), BUT worth the price for the higher standard of hygiene, better crowd control (there is a managed queue to enter the place), 5460 possible combination of personalising your cup noodle, not to mention the irrisistibly cute cartoon options. In my kids words, Mamee Melaka is a fun activity, once is enough. (Yokohama Cup Noodle Museum is an awesome experience, we should return to every time we are in Yokohama!!)Show less

Author: SamuelOngKajang, Malaysia
Title: Only the Instant Cup making worth going for.
Review: My family went for the custom made instant cup noddle for RM5 each cup.Note that a minimum of 4 cups are required for the workshop. Now i was a bit disappointed on the amount of condiments they had and allowed. Only 6 (On the day we were there) condiments were there (Corn,Chopped carrots,chopped lemon grass,chopped chilli,chai and one more I forgot), they allow you to choose what type of soup flavor you want (Chicken, Tom Yam and Curry/Laksa). Now you can only choose maximum of 3 condiments and then they will pack the cup for you and seal it. It was fun to watch the whole process. However, the cafe was too expensive and also too commercialized. One chicken rice ball for RM1?! I can get 3 balls for RM1. I High discourage dinning in the cafe. Overpriced and inadequate.During that time, there were a promotion stating that every RM20 spent, one complimentary ticket to the museum is given. The museum ticket cost RM5 per person no matter the age. Now the museum is too small given the amount you pay to visit it. You can finish the entire museum within 5 to 10 minutes if you read all the text but lets face it, kids only look for the illustration and arts so you can finish it within 5 minutes. The rest of the shop sells normal MAMEE products that you can find outside.Overall its a place to visit the workshops including the noodle making although I didn't get the try that I heard it was RM20 per person, but dont try the cafe.Show less

Author: mrskskwSingapore, Singapore
Title: Nice food at the cafe
Review: Brought kids to the museum but was disappointed at the SMALL museum that cost 5RM. nothing much to see there but the cafe food was not bad. Chicken rice ball was tasty.Show less

Author: Rina1961Singapore, Singapore
Title: Lousy place
Review: The food is lousy. The chicken rice is served cold not even warm. Ordered Chendol...was disappointed. The items in the Chendol is kept in the freezer and served directly to you without defroze. Not worth the money and time spent. Totally sucks.Show less

Author: Hamonangan N
Title: Lunch
Review: The place itself is very good, classic. The food was okay. Reminds me of the old days of school because they make instant snacks... Hahhaha...

Author: Hwee Mean T
Title: Not worth to spend time here
Review:
Came all the way to see Mamee Museum, ticket cost RM5 per person. The museum is less than 300sf. Nothing much here.
Think twice before you come.

Author: samhisyam
Title: Mamee Workshop!
Review: It was a great experience for us as a parent who grew up with the product and for our kids to explore and understand the process with lots of fun! Great staff with patience and full of knowledge! :P

Author: 559tany
Title: Noodle doodle workshop
Review: Had fun colouring. Tom yum or chicken or curry soup. (Chicken soup tasted v weird though). Can choose 4 ingredients too

Author: Seana L
Title: Disappointing second visit
Review: Went 2 years ago and enjoyed the session even though prior booking is required. This time round, no booking is required, just walk in. So I guessed popularity has decreased. But it doesn't bother us a bit. Then came the most annoying part. My group consist of 6 young kids ranging from 3 to 9 years old. They said they only allow 2 to 3 parents for my group of 6 kids! And some of them are the only child. I told them this wasn't the case 2 years ago! Who is going to handle my 3 year old kid! The answer I received was RIDICULOUS. "What if 1 kid bring 20 adults into the class?" Excuse me, we only have a set of parents for 1 or 2 kids each. I believe the staff should do more observation. In addition, which is the most impt thing, the staff there are obviously not trained to handle young kids. I think my 3 year old will surely get her fingers "rolled" into the noodle machine if I didn't insist my presence in the class.I hope either the management could step up to review the rules or train up their staff to be responsible for young kids' safety. Show less

Author: ch8wongKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Disappointment weekday visit
Review: Frankly there is nothing much to see during weekdays. Probably weekends have more activities. Asked us to buy min 4 cups to do some artwork. We only have 3 persons. Each cup costs some RM5+. Doesn't make sense. Buy snacks have to be in combo. Ours was RM13. Cannot buy individual packet. Doesn't make sense. My neighbourhood kedai runcit (grocery stores) offers more customers-friendly service and flexibility. Staffs are friendly and speaks good English. Store is clean and pleasant. Products offering are decent. Show less

Author: remusang
Title: Educational tour Mamee
Review: Visited in 30Dec. Nice education tour for young kid to learn to make Mamee noodles and understanding process of making noodles. Free goodie bags. Highly recommended. Young Kid will love it . :) Go 4 it.

Author: HockLye
Title: Fun
Review: RM22 for 4 personalised cup noodles. It’s a unique gift and fun to personalise each cup with a message and ingredient. The staff are well trained, so there are full of rules and inflexible.

Author: tauruspel
Title: Great for kids
Review: Be prepared to spend 2 hrs here if you are going for the Kitchen workshop. Workshop was quite disorganised. There is a cafe at the ground floor with limited tables. The fried rice was not bad.

Author: aeyreinnPerak
Title: More activities needed
Review: We were greeted by friendly staffs. There's a merchandise store, museum and cafe on the ground floor.Entrance fee for the museum is RM5 per person, free for 3 yo and below. Limited exhibition items. You'll get to see the history behind Mamee's success, fun facts and the evolution of their packagings. Took only 10 minutes to finish the tour.Didn't have the chance to experience the cafe as we made plans to eat somewhere else. Activity rooms are located at 1st floor. You can try doodling your own Mamee cups, perfect for gifts. You can also try making Mamee noodles in their workshop. Comes with a fee though.Show less

Author: 556ngk
Title: Mamee making
Review: Great for kids to know more about traditional snacks. Not the most healthy option but they will go thru the process of making those snacks

Author: KenYap55
Title: Great for Kids and Educational
Review:
This was a surprise for me and it has a cafe and workshop to teach kid about noodle making & the history of Mameee.

This is almost what i saw in Japan...Kudos to the management

Author: nohp13Singapore, Singapore
Title: Not worth a visit for the Mamee Museum
Review: Visited the Mamee Museum at Jonker street and it was a disappointment that it was that small and nothing much to see...visit only if you have spare time and willing to pay the RM5 for one pax. If you want to get your own cup noodles done, you would have to pay RM22 for 4 cups, yes, that's the min.qty one has to buy.Show less

Author: sgsleepwalker
Title: Making cup noodles
Review: Kids had fun coloring the cups and staffs will help to pack the noodles into vacuum packs. Suitable for younger kids too.

Author: Michael Y
Title: Extremely Bad Service
Review: Waiters are basically more important than customers. Don't have a place to sit and waiters are sitting on a table enjoying the view of me looking for a table. The bald Manager is also not bothered. Finally when there is a table vacant, bald manager says it is reserved. Might as well just close the place to inform walk in customer that your place is already fully booked!! Will not come here again!!Show less

Author: bezybSingapore, Singapore
Title: Lousy service
Review: If not for the limited halal restaurant along jonker we will not be dining here.We wait long for the rice and drinks.. Chicken came early but no rice.. no one care to ask. Reason being they overlook our order.. No apology given..Will not recommend.Food is average.Show less

Author: Nomadman411978
Title: Mamee co. noodles
Review: Mamee Jonker House is one of many fine heritage houses which line Jonker Street. It has a fun cafe for kids specializing in noodles as Mamee is one of the biggest Malaysian companies which specializes in snack foods.

Author: Beatrice_Ayeong
Title: Good family restaurant
Review: It's located at Jonker Street. You can eat there and buy various snacks. The restaurant is perfect for family. The food is various and tasty as well.

Author: AliAzzamShah Alam, Malaysia
Title: Excellent for young kids
Review: Colouring...noodle making...it is all fun time for your young ones. After a bit of shopping at the Jonker street ,do drop by and let your kid enjoy for a change. It is a real family time enjoyment, And do take a small step into their mini museum and understand how it all started.Show less

Author: hiiong888Singapore, Singapore
Title: All about noodle and mamee
Review: This place located at jonker street, melaka. An interesting place for young children especially age 5 and ups. We did some activities as follows:1. Mamee noodle workshop at monster kitchenThis activity located at 2nd floor, however, we need to pay at 1st floor. It cost RM 22 per pax. This is good edutainment for children as they can make the mamee monster noodle from the scratch. I feel that this activity quite safe for children as the instructor quite hands in and some activities like steaming and frying are done inside separate room and children only can watch from outside.2. Decorate cups noodle at noodle doodle.This activity located at 2nd floor. However we need to purchase the cup noodles at 1st floor. We need to purchase minimum 4 cups cost RM 5.5 each cups. There are 3 flavour that we can choose. After we finish decorate, the attendance will fill the noodle and wrap it nicely for us.3. Visit mamee museumThis activity located at level 1. Ticket price is RM 5 per person. It is just a small room with all achievement of mamee company and not too interesting for the children.4. Shopping mamee monsterWe bought quite a lot mamee monster and mamee biscuits for souvenir.Show less

Author: LimJoey1996
Title: Mamee Snack Lover Heaven and Kids Learning Place
Review: A lot of Mamee snack and have a restaurant inside. Inside this shop also got sell T-shirt of Mamee's character. Upstairs is workshop for kids to learn and play how the process of making Mamee snack and coloring the Mamee logo.

Author: pOtAtOeMESingapore, Singapore
Title: A nice Saturday afternoon event
Review: We went with our kids to Mamee at Jonker Street to attend the Lil Monster workshop. There were insufficient signage to guide participants to the workshop area. The cashiers at the merchandise area are too busy with customers hence not available. Had to find our way to the workshop room. When we arrive at 115pm which the the scheduled slot 130pm, the class had already begun. No staffs were at the waiting area to guide. But Charlotte, the In Charge was quick to rectify the situation. She even hands on with the group to make up time. Overall the event was interesting and my kids got to make their own instant noodles, end to end. From making the dough to packaging.Show less

Author: Lilian580514Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Sunday School Teacher's Amazing Race on 15th July,2017
Review: One of our amazing race clue is at Mamee Jonker House. We liaise with Ms Charlotte who is the person in charge. She is friendly. Some of our groups had their lunch there and said the Hainanese chicken rice balls are nice. I tried their satay which I find is okay. The sticks are big and price reasonable. What I find interesting is they have two types of workshop on the first floor. One is you buy the cup at the counter for RM 5 and you do your coloring of the Mamee cup, choose your own condiments ( 4 types out of 6 ) and the staff will put it in for you. Then the staff will put a paper slip on top of the cup and you are to press the button to seal your cup mee and after that they will cling wrap for you and you have your personalize cup mee. The other workshop is making noodles which need pre registration. My group of adults and kids enjoyed the cup noodle workshop and find it interesting and fun even as adults.Show less

Author: pywong100
Title: Food and snack
Review:
With warm weather out at the street - this is good place to queue (with aircond) since all places waiting area under hot sun
Food average rate

Author: lilithian
Title: Refreshing and unique
Review: The food was delicious considering it was made with instant noodles. The actual attraction itself wasn't really interesting.

Author: HappiMummiSingapore, Singapore
Title: Last stop in Malacca
Review: We were recommended to visit this place by a friend. There's a cafe, a shop that sells all the Mamee products and merchandise, they host workshop for kids (but it was fully booked when we were there.)We just got the biscuits and noodles and left. Show less

Author: Star_dust_rainbowKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: For the whole family
Review: Heard so much about this place from my friends with small children. So this place is a must for our Malacca trip. Mamee Jonker House was not very big but it was just right for a family outing. My children couldn't participate in the workshop as there were only 2 of them ( we were there at 10am ). We went into the Mamee museum ( which is not big at all ) but it did bring back some childhood memories. I like the museum visit so much. We had our breakfast at the cafe. The menu might looked simple but the food was good. The fried chicken served with nasi lemak was well marinated and yummy. The curry laksa was creamy and delicious. There was a water self service counter for free. The cafe and toilets were so clean. And last but not least , we were served with a warm smile by the wonderful staffs there. We will definitely visit Mamee Jonker House again on our next Malacca trip and hopefully there will be enough participants for the workshop activity on our return trip.Show less

Author: 34pangse
Title: Lunch at mamee
Review: First time to visit this place.  Nice and cool place to get away from the heat.  Staff is friendly.  Not much choice of food but ok.

Author: GTti_72Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: For young children who know Mamee
Review: If you're not familiar with the products, give this place a miss. The activities and displays are targeted at a very young audience. Despite loving the snack, both my 13 & 9 year olds were not attracted by the limited displays.The top floor is catered for activities. Whilst we were there a large group of children (I assume from a school/kindie) were busy in one section while the other section where actual creation of the snack is being carried out had a few kids (and their parents) participating. The staff didn't seem too motivated and didn't make it more enjoyable. Nobody came up to us and offered advice or asked questions.Some of the products on sale could only be bought in sets so you spend more than you planned for.So overall, skip this place unless you're a HUGE fan of Mamee...Show less

Author: danial8704
Title: the museum is too small. can finish tour is less than 10 minute
Review: small place too visit but if you love to eat mamee product shouldn't be a problem. Recommended to go during weekend because have workshop of how mamee product are made

Author: uninvitedguest82Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: "just a small shop that sells mamee product in it..."
Review: located at the jonker street...quite crowded inside...nothing much to see...just a small cafe/restaurant and snacks shop under mamee product for souvenirs ...there's a workshop upstairs but there's a long queue for the entrance...hope they will find the new places or enlarging the existing store to accommodate crowded...Show less

Author: Esther P
Title: Nostalgic place
Review: Lots of mamee noodles varieties,  there's offer at with reasonable prices. There's free carrier with certain purchase. Great to take photos in the shop too.

Author: candiesssSingapore, Singapore
Title: For Mamee lovers!
Review: I ate lots of Mamee as a child so seeing the blue monster everywhere in the shop was fun for me. There's also a short "museum" walk-through where I took more photos with the blue monster. I'm surprised there weren't more Mamee souvenirs besides t-shirts and cups.There wasn't a workshop going on when I visited but looking at the workshop space, I think it'd be fun to design and create your own flavour. Not sure if adults can participate in the workshops or if its kids only.A good hideout from the hot weather outside. Would spend about 20 mins here. Show less

Author: Hicks_GAMarseilles, Illinois
Title: Nothing much to see and do here
Review: My wife loves her mamee snacks. So, when we went to jonker st, she wanted to go to this place. However, she was somewhat disappointed as there was not much thing to do or see here. They had a restaurant inside the house, but the food menu did not whet our appetite. After looking at their store, we decided to go out. Mamee jonker house should make more efforts in making their house more interesting for people of all ages and the first timer knowing your products. My wife was happy, but she also thought it was an average experience for her.Show less

Author: josephcH9554PCKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Great activity for the kids
Review: A great workshop to escape the hot weather in jonker street.We missed the morning classes and the girls were clearly disappointed. Having re-arranged our schedule for the day, we manage to squeeze in the 1.30pm and the girls loved it ！Thanks for the experience and good job to the staffs.Show less

Author: PhoebeL865
Title: Good food but lousy 'museum'
Review: Food is good except the nasi lemak was a bit too rich with santan. Atmosphere is comfortable... worth to visit. The only imperfection was the museum. RM5 for 5 mins...i can't belive when i arrive the exit.. i was telling my husband, should be some other area we have missed it.. we go round and round... THAT'S it!Wow... RM5? Perhaps i will think it better if i pay it for the air-cond. :XShow less

Author: AsrulJ11
Title: Awesome
Review: As we walk into the Mamee House, my daughter can't hold her excitement, Mamee is everywhere. Since we were hungry, we went straight into the restaurant, queue at the counter and later proceed to the table.Foods arrived about 10 minutes later. The mamee mamak ala thai and hainan chicken rice ball were awesome. Give it a try!Later, we went to Monster Kitchen for Mamee cooking experience. My daughter and nephews love it so much. You have to book for the slot upfront.Overall, its awesome.Show less

Author: wm1509Singapore, Singapore
Title: Interesting experience
Review: Stumbled upon this place where my friends and I could purchase an empty cup noodle and design it accordingly to how we want. After that, we could customise the ingredients of the cup noodles as well. Even though there was a crowd waiting in line, the staff was patient and did not impatiently urge any one to quickly finish up so that they can let new customers come in. Air conditioned setting was also a cool respite from the sun. Recommended for family, friends and couples to spend about half an hour of their time here.Show less

Author: EzLiivaPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Perfect for Mamee lovers
Review: It was okay, a very novel idea to have a themed cafe based on Mamee, brings back memories. I studied in Malacca and the smell from the Mamee factory tells me I'm almost there. However, I'm afraid that was the only charm. The food and drinks are okay, everything was okay! I wish there is something else to add on to the business, but I have no idea too!So I guess it is what it is, a tourist attraction. Malacca definitely has tonnes of other amazing places for foodies. I would recommend this venue for the experience, not for the food or desserts.Show less

Author: L4803GLdavidpSingapore, Singapore
Title: Great workshop, but a bit long
Review: We attended the workshop and our daughter found it great. it was a good experience to get hands on and understand the full process in making the noodles. The only downside was that the class was full but not all tools/machines were used, so kids had to wait a very long time for their turn. what was meant to be an hour+ workshop ended up a 2hr+ workshop, which was too long for kids who lost interest and patience. And it also spoiled the rest of the day plans for some parents.Show less

Author: Evelyn Chin Y
Title: Funny and friendly service
Review: Had a team building activity here and the staffs are friendly to give full and detail instruction to me. I love the concept of drawing and coloring on the noodle cups before watching them to process my noodles. Nice souviner that i would love to bring back to my hometown. Show less

Author: Mizznur
Title: Tasty meal
Review: I was ate Mamee Chef Lontong for my brunch. Wow! I'm so impressed. It was so delicious and I love it . I give 5 star for it.My tummy was happy till night. You guys must give it a try. And also easy to get here, just walking.The other day I tried Mamee Chef Ala Thai with satay. Not bad. For your information, Mamee Chef Bolognese also tasty. Perfect combination between the sauce and mamee (I tried it 2 years ago lol). So what are you waiting for? Do not forget to stop by :) Show less

Author: LitaK72Yogyakarta Region, Indonesia
Title: Interesting place for kids
Review: Mamee jonker house is on Jonker street. Easy to find out. I get lunch there with noddles. Almost the menu about noddles. When you enter the restaurant, you will find a mamee doll welcome you. You can buy a bundling mamee products and t shirt too. If you want to enter the mamee museum, you ask the cashier n they charge each person RM 5. First in the museum is about the rich history of mamee then the second place is about how do u make noddles. There is one interactive chair that you sit and seen on TV. The last part is about the second product that you can play around with football ambiance. The experience bounce back your kids time.Show less

Author: albeechuaSingapore, Singapore
Title: Not much but Interesting
Review: Small shop with a restaurant built in but if you are interested to know more about the snacks that is there since young, it's great place to head to. RM5/person to go through a small lane to read about the history. RM5/cup noodle to customize it. You can color the cup. For ingredients, there are 3, or 4?, flavors to choose from, and about 6 veges to choose from. Too little options in my POV. Most important component that made the visit pleasant are the staffs. They are extremely friendly and helpful!!!It's about to close when we visit but the staff stayed and tried their best help us out anyway. Thumbs up for them. Show less

Author: bshim7822
Title: Favourite childhood foods
Review:
The place is very suitable for children. Foods very good and lots of cartoons around. 

The foods served are Asian favourite, mamee mamak goreng etc

Author: BH C
Title: Photo taking spot...
Review: it is a good spot to take photo with our local mamee hero....kid will love it, but the museum is quite small....

Author: idie Z
Title: Giftshop and cafe
Review: Shop that offer merchandises of Mamee product (famous Malaysian junk food). Taking photo are allowed in the premises, they event have place like a photo booth. Further inside the is a cafe with very nice ambience.

Author: wendytay39Singapore, Singapore
Title: Suitable for young children
Review: Got cafe serve mamee related food. Must pay to enter museum. Honestly nothing much to see. Have workshop that teach you how to make mamee. My children loved it. Must pay for the workshop though. Can decorate own mamee cup noodle too. Also must pay. Overall we had fun. For mamee fans. It's a must to go. We spent almost half a day there. Show less

Author: NurulHashimSingapore, Singapore
Title: They have the newest revamped mamee lontong
Review: Long awaited release !!! I have been looking high and Low in sg and Malaysia for the newest release of the revamped mamee lontong instant noodles !! Finally I found my old Favourite ! Yet to devour it though , bought like 20 packets to bring back to sg :) cute quaint shop. They even have instant noodles making class if you are interested . Show less

Author: foto_melakaMelaka, Malaysia
Title: More To Offer
Review: Perhaps this is one of the least publicized attractions here in Melaka as not many visitors to Melaka are aware of this place. Located smack in the heart of Melaka's Chinatown or Jonker Walk, Mamee Jonker House has a lot to offer than just a place that sells snacks produced by Mamee.Even the facade of the building which it occupies is enough to turn one's head. But do not be misled by the traditional looking exterior of the building as what you will find inside is hardly anything traditional.Being one of Malaysia's premier manufacturer of snacks, one will be able to travel down memory lane in the Galeri World of Good Taste which showcase the history of Mamee since its formation. Visitors will also be able to try their hands at the making of instant noodle at the Noodle Doodle and Lil Monster Kitchen.However, for me, the highlight of the visit is definitely the opportunity to savour various delicious meals served at the Mamee Cafe. If you are thinking of trying out the dishes here, do try out the chicken rice ball which is reputed to be made using traditional recipes passed down through the generation.And a little note to go with it...all the food served here are certified halal by the National Council of Islamic Affairs of Malaysia (JAKIM)Show less

Author: StanleyFoo
Title: Wholesale mamee products
Review: This shop sells mamee snack and other potato chips that their company manufacture. Nice little educational shop that also shows you the process of manufacturing Mamee snacks

Author: Lim LSingapore, Singapore
Title: Make your own Mamee Monster snack!
Review: This shop is located in the Main Street of Jonker Walk. It conducts workshop everyday but on weekend, it has the Mamee Monster snack workshop. From the most basic ingredient of flour, you get to go through the whole process from making the dough, all the way to frying the noodles in 1.5h. It is a very enriching and engaging process. It is very popular, need to pre-book and cost MYR15 per pax. Show less

Author: Sparklesorbet
Title: Good, cheap food
Review: Just went to the restaurant, didn't do the tour, but surprisingly good food, one of the cheapest meals on Jonker street. A couple of good vegetarian options. Good chicken rice balls. They also let us fill up our water bottles for free :)

Author: BenjaminYap427
Title: Small Museum
Review:
The Museum is very short distance, just for those who like cartoon or taking picture. Maybe some MU Fan.

Make sure your beloved likes it crazily, or not it won't be a very reasonable place to go.

Author: Levin LKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Museum is an afterthought
Review: If the thought of a museum for a snack and instant noodle manufacturer tickled your fancy, don't bother. The 'museum' is just a small showroom which you walk through before exiting into their restaurant.Tickets aren't cheap, but at least you get a voucher that you can use at the restaurant- just as some other reviewers have said, it's a nice place for a quick break (that you have to pay for) from the heat.Show less

Author: Jusong
Title: Good spot to rest and fill-up
Review: A nice relaxing lunch when walking along Jonker Street.  Food quality is not bad and service is excellent.  Nice layout and deco.  The mamee workshop looks interesting, although we did not have time to experience it.

Author: Lynnchoy
Title: Interesting find
Review: Nice place to hop in to have a meal and walk down memory lane to childhood days for me.  MAMEE... speaks it all. We had a pleasant meal and bit of lepak time before we headed back to hotel to pack and head home.

Author: inyshen
Title: Disappointed
Review: Paid RM18 (2 adults, 1 x 6yrs old, 1 x 7 months old baby) nothing much to see.. Daughter was hoping to go to the workshop as advertise on their TV but was told need to book earlier and only open on sat and sun..

Author: LKT2171
Title: Mamee Jonker House
Review: Paid RM5 to enter and but need to improve on the overall feel. The tour is short and I think the managements need to give some Mamee snacks for those paid the tour.... Overall, average only for me.

Author: Alex_yong98Johor Bahru, Malaysia
Title: Design your own instant noodles cup
Review: This is a awesome place to bring kids and young children to. They provide classes for how to make dough and make it into noodles. Moreover, you can buy the instant noodles cup and coloured it yourself with creative ideas. After that, you can choose which ingredients you wanna put in and see the process they packed your instant noodles cup. It's is quite fun and exciting. A thumb up for them.Show less

Author: kianglong81Malaysia
Title: Make your own cup of instant noodle
Review: It was something new to me, while visiting jonkers walk in melaka. Perfect place if you loves art, drawing and instant noodles of course. Location: easy to spot. Look for MAMEE sign as your enter jonker walk. Payment: RM18/adult, hv discount rate for kids. The simulated kitchen and classroom on level 1, here you can do the noodle cup's label, choose your flavours... the staffs will guide you through. After done your session, you will get your own version of cup noodle, with 1 week expiry date. After that, you can visit the mamee museum at ground floor. Bring your own camera and enjoy some photo taking there. If you have children (preferably at the age where they able to color with colour pens), This is a perfect place to unleash their creativity and expose them to the science behind the instant noodle :-) Show less

Author: nellielimKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Mamee brands concept store
Review: This is the Mamee brands first concept store. Offering activities for young children, there is also a workshop where it is taught how to make the noodles snack. Mamee merchandise like tee shirts and soft toys are on sale here and the Mamee cafe has quite a good selection of noodles. Food served here is tasty and priced reasonably. Worth a visit.Show less

Author: xiaodingtangSingapore
Title: A good resting point in Jonker walk
Review: We come across the Mamee Jonker house while we are walking in the Jonker Street. The merchandise area wasn’t big but it’s a good resting spot away from the heat. There is a museum which need to pay for RM5 (we didn’t went it). And we are hoping to join in the workshop but found out that it only available in the weekend.Show less

Author: airavata1998Mannheim, Germany
Title: Good place for a rest
Review: We visited this place for lunch.. although it is not as packed as the other restaurants, it offered delicious food as well. We ordered laksa, nasi lemak, mi goreng, abc and chicken rice ball. The restaurant is convenient and air conditioned (the outside temperature was really hot) and the toilet was clean. Come by if you want a good food with a reasonable priceShow less

Author: blinkable
Title: Stop by even if don't want to pay to visit the museum
Review: You can still take pictures and have a look around on the decorations such as huge size of mamee noodle cup, Mr. Potato etc.

Author: Stargal82Singapore
Title: Fun workshop .. Yummy
Review: Visited this place with friend , as we have our childhood memories on having a pack of mamee in hand .. hehehex..We spend RM5 to go in the museum , but the museum is very small , nothing much to see except to take some cute picture wit the deco and mr mamee..But the RM5 can be use to debate for the items purchase at the souvenir shop, so dun mind go in have a look if you want get anything can use the RM5 voucher.And we booked a workshop on sunday for DIY making of our own pack of mamee. We enjoy the workshop ... FYI the workshop only on weekend and you may need to make reservation in case full house , as seem like can only accept less den 20 or 15 pax each time . The workshop take 1.5hours , and they will give you a big pack of mamee after the workshop too.Show less

Author: danielrajesh
Title: Quick visit for young Malaysian adults
Review: Growing up as an 80s kid in Malaysia or Singapore, mamee was part kid our lives. This museum brings a piece of the memory to live. Worth your 10 minutes air con break .

Author: WhoppeR2015Asia
Title: Workshop good to entertain the kids for a few hours
Review: Foods served in Mamee Jonker House was surprisingly decent. We had chicken rice balls, and some noodles dishes.For RM5, you can experience Mamee house decoration- which is not worth it. Don't pay for it.The workshop where you learnt how to make mamee noodle was good to keep the kids entertained for 2 hours- although the quality of the instructors could be improved. RM15Show less

Author: pclee88Penang, Pulau Pinang, Malaysia
Title: Extraordinary experience in Malacca
Review: Nice menu and foods serve in Mamee Jonker House. You can experience Mamee house decoration with purchase RM5 ticket which you can spend to bought for souvenirs, snacks or foods serve in the Mamee house! Besides you can make your own mamee cups mee with three different flavor. So great !!!Show less

Author: Mizznur
Title: Nyummy
Review: The combination between mamee and bolognese sauce impressed me a lot. I like it so much also good crew and service.

Author: KaiBoon
Title: A simple cafe with Mamee decoration
Review:
It is a simple cafe selling melaka food like chicken rice.

Nothing much to shout about unless you have booked the session to make your own mamee cup noodle.

Cup noodle and snacks there are cheaper than supermarket.

Author: Pinkytham
Title: Fun workshop and good food!
Review: I love the workshops that are available in Mamee Jonker House. Love that I could customize my own Mamee instant noodle cup and the cafe serve awesome chicken rice ball

Author: ccjy2001
Title: Favourite to-go place
Review: Ever since the first visit, my family and I have been going back frequently for dinner. Highly recommend the porridge as well as the steam rice with pork ribs.

Author: rachelcM8940IAKajang, Malaysia
Title: Clean, cosy and comfort food
Review: Stumbled upon this place while searching for dinner. The place was clean, air conditioned and well presented. The soup was served piping hot and the choices were plenty ranging from the cheaper ranges of soup such as lotus root, water cress to extensive choices of more expensive range such as bird's nest and abalone. The portion of the dishes were quite big as well. Customer service was good. Show less

Author: mysuite21Milan, Italy
Title: Nothing more than acceptable
Review: It’s a local restaurant of Chinese food, it’s one of the few restaurant in this area of the city.Now the food is decent no more than this, it offers same menu than the rest of the country Quite clean and safe given the local standard Show less

Author: FromKluang
Title: Good chinese food
Review: Good local Chinese foods with reasonable price. Good environment, comfortable and good services. Foods are tasty and worth to have try.

Author: PatYKC
Title: Lunchy Lunchy
Review: Lovely food. Especially the Mee goreng. Great meal except for the noodles portions. Like the mee goreng was enough for 2 but there were like 6 of us.

Author: VOgy72
Title: Great tasting food
Review:
We ordered chicken feet lotus soup, abacus, roasted pork, otak and a few other dishes. All listed are really nice. Came piping hot too. 

The price is also very reasonable whilst the setting is restaurant type. 

Will definitely come again

Author: Bunnyng
Title: Excellent chinese food
Review: We went there for 2 meals. Very satisfied each time. The soup is good, comes piping hot. We also try the ngor hiang, fried egg, steam tofu with meat and leek with roasted pork. Very good.

Author: aikichin
Title: Found this gem accidentally
Review: We were headed to Makko which is a few doors down from this restaurant and were horrified to find out it was already closed, at 2pm. We saw quite a few diners leaving Soupy Licious and thought to give it a try. We were not disappointed. Ingredients were of a high quality, soups were delicious, the Chinese tea was fragrant, and the food was reasonably priced. We will definitely be returning to dine when we are in Melaka.Show less

Author: LennieCSingapore
Title: Delicious Food! Soups are so so..
Review: This restaurant serves Chinese cuisine and is located at a convenient location along Jalan Merdeka, very near the Dataran Pahlawan shopping centre. This is one of our favorite haunts everytime we come to Melaka as it is very near the Novotel Melaka where we often stay, and it is less crowded than the nearby Nonya restaurants. The food here is excellent and the prices reasonable. The environment is also very clean and suitable for kids and family. There is also wifi available, which is a bonus!We always love the guava appetizer and generally anything you order will be of a consistently high standard. Ironically, if there is any dish we have to complain about, it would be the soup dishes which we feel are not as good as when we first started coming here. Tonight, we ordered the Leek with Roasted Pork (Rating 9/10), Chicken in Dry Curry Sauce (9/10), Chicken with Chinese Sausage (8/10), and the Pork Rib Soup (5/10).As you can see from my ratings, the dishes were all delicious, except the soup which was ordinary. ￼ The other dishes we like to order at this restaurant would be the Otah and the Minced Pork Patty with Salted Egg. Show less

Author: sy3717Subang Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Tasty authentic soup
Review: A restaurant which really provide you variety of authentic home taste hot soup. Range from reasonable to expensive prices, depend whether It is a bowl of ABC soup or scallops herbal soup. Sunday evening the restaurant was packed with customers but service quite fast. We tried the Hainan mee, not bad. We were satisfied.Show less

Author: Lll6033
Title: Good food!
Review:
Nice interior design which very heritage.
The foods were super nice especially the mee goreng got the wok hei!
The Nyonya kueh is fantastic!

Author: Jtan8992
Title: Charming hidden Gem
Review: Found this charming restaurant hidden in a quiet part of Melaka. Was mesmerized by the colourful Peranakan antiques tastefully decorated around the restaurant. We had a delightful Peranakan breakfast with authentic taste and flavour. Will definitely recommend this place and will visit again.

Author: apeklim
Title: Nice interior design but average
Review: Nice interior design but average food. Better to head to another place if you want a kite authentic nyonya cuisine

Author: KK_travels123
Title: Nice cozy place
Review: Stopped by for a late lunch on Saturday. The place is cozy with good food. The butterfly pea (a type of flower) drink is refreshing. The cendol not too sweet, just the way we like it. Satisfied with the food, service and price. Good place to visit.Show less

Author: Jack101213Johor Bahru, Malaysia
Title: Lunch during Chinese New Year holidays
Review: Stumbled across this place while looking for a place to eat lunch. Nice and cosy place. As it was the CNY holidays, the place was crowded and the staff frazzled by many customers but yet managed to smile and make small friendly talks. Orders were taken fast and food served with not much of a wait. The food is tasty and delicious. Highly recommend the Pai Tee.Show less

Author: mjohnkam
Title: Good Food
Review: We ate at this little cafe over the weekend, great food (love their mee siam and desserts!). Price is reasonable.

Author: jennik2988
Title: Nice cafe
Review: We were there for the laksa and nyonya kueh and they were very tasty. They do serve tai bak which is a dessert which is not commonly available nowadays. Cendol is very nice also with nice aroma of gula melaka. We can purchase the gula melaka from their shop in front and they do sell other local products which are quite nice.Show less

Author: jintanll
Title: Great Meal
Review: We are very happy with our meal at heritage flavours. Their service is good and their food is tasty (We ordered their Mee Siam and Laksa). We love their Cendol & Tai Bak! Overall a nice cozy cafe with great food

Author: mmleo80Singapore, Singapore
Title: One of the best laksa
Review: We stayed at courtyard hotel and this cafe just across the hotel belongs to the same establishment, as part of the hotel guest we were given discount. The have a a selection of kuih kuih and hot food and desserts!. We tried their laksa and oh boy its one of the best laksa we had! Cool it down with a sweet bowl of Tai Bak! Highly recommended, cozy little cafe!Show less

Author: Bsoonmh
Title: Delicious meal
Review: We stumble upon this little cafe while walking along the street next to jonker. Cafe is cozy and nicely decorated. The food are delicious, love their kuehs and cendol! Will definitely come back when we are back to melaka next trip.

Author: TomGuppySherborne, United Kingdom
Title: Fantastic cafe, shame it hasn’t got more reviews
Review: We wanted a quick bite to eat and all the cafes were busy at lunch so we stumbled across ITs.We are glad we did! Super food, great service in a warm and friendly environment.Drinks were superb - iced coffees and lemon teas.Food was great too! Duck pasta was tasty and so was my wife’s chicken rice bowl.Children had popcorn chicken and sweet potato fries fries. Cakes looked delicious too. So pleased we found this cafe. Very accommodating.Show less

Author: joshpZ691BO
Title: Ontbijt
Review: Lovely restored building, very friendly staff, prepared breakfast with much love, the tropical smoothie bowl looked like a painters palet. And tasted delicious. Great coffee, enjoying this whilst on the background the sound of easy listening music.You will find this cozy place in Jonker Street.Show less

Author: RonaM_11
Title: Lovely Coffee
Review:
Cool and spacious cafe. Friendly staff. Lovely coffee, perfectly made, and very good cold drinks. 
Would highly recommend.

Author: TeyWT
Title: Nice cafe
Review: Ordered the IT'S big breakfast set that comes with a coffee or tea. Nice food and coffee. Good service. Good atmosphere.

Author: KLCKent
Title: Excellent coffee on Heeren Street
Review: Excellent coffee and very good service, with a relaxed vibe. It’s peaceful and spacious. The people speak perfect English, and I felt very welcome.

Author: jingxian0623
Title: Little nice cafe beside Malacca River
Review: Good and relaxing place for a coffee and brunch. The fruit tea smoothies here are really good. Plus it's situated at the side of busy Jonker street so it's good for chilling while looking at the river of Melaka.

Author: angelinecappul
Title: New Hidden gem In Jonker Street
Review: Located beside the river, we had a good brunch while looking at the river view. Really good coffee served here and price is lower compared to the whole Jonker Street. Staff are friendly and food are simple and nice. Drinks are more special and it’s a good place to relax with soft music in the background. Overall worth a visit if you are in this area.Show less

Author: macaiwar
Title: Chicken rice balls
Review: A great option for Melaka native meal in a cosy surrounding. The spicy chili condiment was a lovely addition. Chicken was tender and juicy.  Would be better if the kitchen ventilation improved.

Author: CynAV
Title: Looking for juicy steamed chicken with rice balls in a comfortable ambiance? Go to Hainan Kitchen
Review: This was a company trip of 15 people to Melaka, and Hainan Kitchen was our first stop for lunch. I coordinated this reservation with the owner, Ms Irene, who is a pleasure to deal with right from the beginning, with her kindness and patience. She provided us with the menu and pricing so that we could give her our orders in advance.When we arrived, Irene and her family had laid the table for us and their attentive service made us feel welcome. The servings of the juicy steamed chicken, adorably cute little rice balls, and the delectable braised mei cai pork paus were very generous. The rice balls do not taste the same as the rice that is served in Singapore; probably because it is infused with some herbs/spices, but a dash of chilli and ginger with some chicken shreds should make it enjoyable.This restaurant is very apt for families, couples, friends and any group gatherings. Thank you Irene and to your family for your great service, and hope to see you again. :-)Show less

Author: 434edmonds
Title: Excellent steamed chicken and rice balls
Review: Visited this restaurant to avoid the crowds in town centre. The steamed chicken was perfectly cooked accompanied by soup with well balanced flavours. The rice balls were infused with chicken stock and tasted lovely, served as an excellent accompaniment. This was the best Hainanese chicken rice I have tasted. Staff and host were very friendly. I would strongly recommend a visit.Show less

Author: JiggyKikiMalaysia
Title: Simple Hainanese Place to eat
Review: If you want to avoid the long que in town,at another place for Melaka famous chicken rice ball, you should try this place.The shop is roomy and very less hectic. There are parking lots right in front of the shop.Tried the steam chicken rice and the chicken is just sublimely tender and soft. However, there is this missing mashed ginger accompaniment that you would usually find served with this Hainanese dish. Perhaps it's just their version of this but the chicken rice still tasted fantastic with the chilli.The braised pork rice is also tender and very tasty albeit a wee bit salty but the white rice balance it up nicely.Drinks are generous in size too.IT's great for brunch too as you can find the traditional hainan toast bread here too.Show less

Author: sharontK2979YN
Title: Must try chicken rice ball!
Review:
Good family-run food like chicken rice ball, variety of chicken and pork one dish meals, toast, etc. Near Tong Hup, same row as Notre Dame church. 

Good pricing and delicious!  😋

Author: cherylwA1293IQKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Good honest Hainanese food in a comfortable environment with attentive service
Review: We visited on a Sunday for brunch - thinking that we were early, about 1030am - and it was packed! A good sign since empty restaurants are dicey....we managed to get a table for our party of 4 fairly quickly, with the menus being distributed swiftly. We realised later that swiftness of service must be one of their USPs! To order, select your menu items and write it on the paper provided at your table. The menu items are decent in terms of variety, so they're focused on a number of good things without over-doing the choices. We had the signature fried pork with rice, chicken with rice balls, porridge with braised pork and the pork with preserved vege in a steamed bun. The signature fried pork was super soft and tasty, albeit rather oily; the steamed white chicken was pretty good although I would have preferred the rice balls to be less soft; the porridge was tasty even on its own as it had a hint of ginger; it was served with the braised pork and a hard-boiled egg - mix the pork with gravy and egg into the porridge. The pork with preserved vege (mui choy kaw yoke) in a steamed bun was my fav. We later had their Hainanese coffee which was pretty good too - strong but not overpowering with no underlying sourness which I find in Starbucks coffee which I can't stand and makes me nauseous. All in all a good meal with really attentive, helpful service. Worth another visit!Show less

Author: Joyce L
Title: Excellent Service and good food
Review: Excellent thick gravy on the Pork Mui Choi. Can top up gravy too. Honey Kaya toast was good too. Excellent service and value for money

Author: Patz82Singapore, Singapore
Title: Nice Hainanese Chicken Rice
Review: Had our meal at Hainan Old Street Cafe. Recommended by our driver. The food was served was great. The chicken and the rice ball. And they have this Mui Chye pork if I can remember, is nice too. As I’m not a Hainanese chicken lover, I must say the chicken they cooked and served is nice. Highly recommend if you visit Malacca. Is a must try. Show less

Author: Lil Ly cMalaysia
Title: Simple, home cooked food
Review: Just like having your home cooked meals without having to wet your fingers !! Love the kaya butter toast and milk tea. For lunch I always enjoy the mui choy pork n oily rice. You can opt for plain rice too or even porridge to go with mui choy. My friend enjoys the chicken drumstick rice and insists that the drumstick comes whole. She says it's succulent, tender n just yummy. Show less

Author: seekatetravelNorcross, Georgia
Title: Great find!
Review: Found this place on Trip Advisor, walked about a 1/4 mi from my hotel in search of pork baos. They were everything I wanted and more! The staff is wonderful, the place is charming and the food is affordable and delicious. I will be back for sure! Show less

Author: Akinobu-RayPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Simple, no fuss comfort food, great value for family dining.
Review: Dropped in for brunch. Had the Steamed Chicken rice. The rice ball style chicken rice that is a famous Melaka specialty is also available. Chicken was tender and rice was fragrant. Chilli sauce was spot on.They also have porridge to go with the chicken if you don't want rice. For a family, it is possible to order a quarter, half or whole chicken. Other lighter foods include bread with coconut jam(kaya), fried chicken burger, etc.The place serves simple, no fuss comfort food. Prices are very reasonable. Many families were there too, during the visit, great value for family dining.The restaurant is very clean, including the toilets. The staff are accommodating and cheerful.Show less

Author: AndersonL763
Title: Best Chicken Rice Ball. Love thid place
Review:
Love this place! A definite place must visit! 
Hainan Chicken Rice Ball is yummy and very affordable! Authentic roti kaya, half boil eggs and hainan kopi - best choice for breakfast! So many variety of foods and drinks are so good ... friendly service too!

Author: IreneXinni
Title: Best Hainan Chicken Rice Ball
Review: Varieties of food and great ambience to have breakfast and lunch. Come and taste it and you will love it very much

Author: ziyutanSingapore, Singapore
Title: Nice durian chendol
Review: Super hot weather in Melaka. My mum and I went to Lao Qian Ice Cafe to beat the heat in the air-conditioned.We saw people were buying the durian chendol. So we decided to try it for the first time.Wow. We liked the tasted. It was full of ice and had got to mixed it. Nice!Show less

Author: Ivan K
Title: very special and delicous cendol
Review: Everyone comes here for DURIAN cendol, but their normal cendol is amazing as they put GULA MELAKA INFUSED NATA DE COCO inside, making a very unique and delicious cendol. -

Author: globetrotterCKYSingapore, Singapore
Title: Refreshing from the outside heat
Review: Each serving had a layer of icy durian frozen over the top. So it doesnt look good for pictures. We just mixed it up with the rest of the bowl of chendol. Refreshing and reasonable for less than RM6 each! Located right at the junction of Jonker Street, it provides a convenient respite from the crowd and heat outside. Show less

Author: Jack FBandung, Indonesia
Title: A Thirsty Reli
Review: The location of this restaurant is not far from the Melaka River, their typical dish is a variety of drinks, especially cold drinks, maybe take advantage of the situation from the temperature of the hot Melaka City. Cendol Durian is one of the beverages to try in this place, as a thirsty reli ...Show less

Author: EatnPlayallDaySingapore, Singapore
Title: Best Chendol in Jonker
Review: Forget any other Chendol if you had only one choice - choose this one and you won't regret it.For one, it must be one of the cheapest-money-for-value Chendol in town. The Chendol comes with a cute durian cardboard cone (too much packaging if you asked me) and a decent hard plastic spoon (which I appreciated - it doesn't cut like the thin white ones). The ice served with ththe Chendol is delicately fine. Very generous with their ingredients which includes jelly, Chendol, red bean, attap seeds (I counted at least 4!) and durian purée.I had to go back for seconds. Nuff said. Do try!Show less

Author: Al-Net-Olo
Title: Best durian chendol
Review: Ok. So I know everyone writes about Jonker 88 and the like. I beg to differ. Hands down the best tasting durian chendol. Finely shaved ice with tasty gula melaka and durian paste.Like the fact that the cafe was air conditioned. Located in the 老叔公 main store Show less

Author: witang67
Title: Durian Cendol
Review: While we do shopping, don't miss out their Durian Cendol, best and yummy. Don't forgot to buy some local product from here..

Author: KH_LyeKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Nice Cafe for a Pit Stop at Jonker Street
Review: This cafe shares the same building with the San Shu Gong shop. Order your drink / dessert and go up to the comfortable air-con first floor to savour it. Ideal as a pit stop while exploring Jonker Street ... we visited twice to rest and recharge. The main dessert is the Durian Cendol - we liked it although the durian content and hence taste could be better. Nonetheless it is full of the requisite ingredients and makes a great refreshment.Show less

Author: lechmanrTurin, Italy
Title: 1000 year old frozen cendol
Review: First of all...its nothing close to authentic Cendol (local dessert made of palm sugar n coconut milk). The cendol looked as though it was frozen for 1000 year! Secondly i find the cardboard decoration to hold the bowl is not environmentally friendly at all.Lastly...(I keep the good thing as last) the iced cold white coffee ( they called it so) is really refreshing with good coffee aroma.Thanks for the dessert though but seems to be too commercialised...Show less

Author: salini01Petaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Best durian cendol ever!!!
Review: Previously, I prefer Bibik House durian cendol than this cause I felt like the place here is just overrated. After 2 years, a lot has changed. The durian cendol here is sooooooo good now! Even if you don't like durian, you can try their gula melaka cendol, so damn good. Came here twice during my trip cause I just couldn't get enough of their durian cendol.Show less

Author: Patrick L
Title: Ice cafe?
Review:
This cafe has a lovely and delicious durian cendol. 
It's great for an afternoon and better after a meal and makes for a good break away from the Malaysian heat during the day.

Author: wong450Singapore, Singapore
Title: Revisted Lao Qian Ice cafe
Review: Needed something cooling to kill off the heat of the afternoon - so revisited this place to have a Durian chendol - seems to me that the standards have gone down - not sufficient Durian paste - and the chendol itself feels like it is not as good as before - not that it is a big price at 5.90 RGT a portion but disappointed - although I have not tried the surrounding equivalent shops that sells this similar item - it certainly not as good as before Show less

Author: EYeoSingapore, Singapore
Title: The best
Review: Was chatting with a patron at Aunty Koh's famous cendol, and he recommended Michelle’s dumplings. Not really a shop - it’s her home just a short drive from Aunty Koh’s. No retail shop - you basically pre-order and go there to pick your order up. A discreet sign at the main road points you to her home. She sells various kinds of kuehs, but we only bought her nonya dumplings. We didn’t pre-oder, but she thankfully had some extra for us to purchase.In short - the best nonya dumplings in Melaka, or anywhere, that I’ve tried. Taste is personal, granted, but I prefer Michelle’s dumplings to the others I’ve tried elsewhere in Melaka. A bit out of the way, but try it and see if you agree with me.Show less

Author: Jack101213Johor Bahru, Malaysia
Title: Dumplings for Tea Break
Review: Michelle Soo Authentic Nyonya Chang, Melaka. Had nothing much to do as was raining all afternoon, so decide to go off-the-beaten path for tea. This is the place to buy home made nyonya bak chang if you are in Melaka. It may be way out of the touristy area but definitely worth it. They sell pineapple tarts too which is tasty and delicious. Price wise, you know I know how much a good bak chang costShow less

Author: wong a
Title: The Best Nyonya Chang
Review: This is the best nyonya chang I  have eaten. Tried so many still this is the best. The rice and the meat is consistent and valve for money.

Author: Susan188Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Very good nyonya dimplings
Review: What a discovery .. otw to Aunty Koh's for a bowl of her delicious cendol, we stumbled upon a signboard "authentic nyonya dumpling" tt directed us to the home of Michelle, David & their 6 children .. we sampled the freshly made nyonya dumpling, chatted w Michelle who's so likeable, and came away w loads of dumpling .. :)) .. for everyone at home .. Michelle's quest is not only "to preserve the taste of her grandma’s chang but to reintroduce the goodness of the Nyonya Chang to the new (younger) generations .. & to lv behind the legacy to her children and their children’s children" .. .. Authentic Nyonya Chang .. by Michelle Soo Malacca City .. Kampung house in “SK Bukit Rambai” area .. Show less

Author: Josephine T
Title: Awesome Chang
Review:
Seller pleasant to deal with over whatsapp. The Nyonya Chang is the best, filling is generous and yummy.
Bought the home made kaya and yet to try.

Author: elvinhuangSingapore, Singapore
Title: Excellent!
Review: First day, i drove in without advance ordering, i just want to try it so i purchase two back.2nd day, i drove back and order 20 to bring back! It was so delicious. Filling was filled evenly whereby i chew more meat than rice. I ate 2 straight and wasnt enough! I have not try other sellers yet. Price for this was $6.50 which i felt affordable for the ingredients and never taste any in SG. Show less

Author: bennyvectra
Title: Excellent nyonya chang...
Review: Excellent nyonya chang... but need to travel to her place to collect. Only possible if you have a car

Author: cherwyny
Title: Nyonya Chang
Review: Very evenly cooked glutinous Rice and a generous amount of filling that makes every bite heavenly and fulfilling 😋

Author: JIA SHEN LJohor Bahru District, Malaysia
Title: Best Nyonya chang
Review: In comparison to most shops offering Nyonya changs (e.g. East and West, Baba Charlie and Nancy's), Michelle Soo offers the best Nyonya chang at RM6 per piece in Melaka. Their Nyonya chang is stuffed with seasoned minced pork, mushroom and candied winter melon. Glutinous rice was evenly cooked and wrapped with good coloring.One problem for this shop is that it is located at a suburban area, and one could approach Michelle Soo with personal transport. It is advisable to get their GPS location in their FB website as the entrance to Michelle Soo can be easily missed. Their Nyonya changs will be a good souvenir to others in my opinion.Show less

Author: MKXVII
Title: Any other local eatery
Review: Nice, tasty and delicious food at affordable prices.  All the local fare can be found here.  Good place to get a teh tarik.

Author: sy3717Subang Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Pure Gula Melaka makes a nice cendul
Review: As we were feeling thirsty and just want to try the cendul. Just unbelieveable, the cendul we ordered were blended with pure gula Melaka, made it so tasty. The big red beans made a plus to the cendul. The soursop fruit drink was equally pure and good. Though many other delicious Asian food were served here, but we were unable to taste, will come back again. The restaurant is clean and service satisfactory. Friendly lady boss.Show less

Author: Niels1905
Title: Nice place, great food!
Review: Good, and really cheap restaurant. Vegetarian, but i do that a lot in the morning. So this is a good restaurant for your start of the day. Service is fast and the place looks clean.

Author: rtwfof
Title: Delightful lunch
Review:
Most meals are around 7RM... though our children both ordered the calamari fritters 14.90RM 😂
Delicious and very quick service. Very convenient - located at Bus terminal (we just arrived in town from KL)
Highly recommended.

Author: HPWuSingapore, Singapore
Title: Vegetarian options
Review: This restaurant serve vegetarian food. Remember to remind them if you don't take garlic, onion and fish. I tried a few dishes. We love the fried rice and the pattaya fried rice. The pattaya fried rice is non veg but we asked for vegetarian version. They're flexible. Just tell them what you need. The noodles and others gravy are salty. The owner is a Chinese Muslim. Show less

Author: Andre_Herzog
Title: Fresh food and great service!
Review: The restaurant was a pleasant finding in Melaka's bus station. The food is freshly prepared and the owner is a really nice guy that makes you feel quite comfortable.

Author: Jason E
Title: good to find vegan and vegetarian food in malacca!!
Review: i went here three times and always had the same dish! not very adventurous - fried rice and mixed veg - but it was very good and just what i needed before and after a bus trip. the owner is a nice chap as well! good value food, i should add!Show less

Author: shajipapa
Title: Just if you"re really hungry and not fussy.
Review: Just a normal fried stuff.Nothing special to shout about.Located in Melaka Sentral Bus Terminal.Pricing is ok but thats it.

Author: Mynameisrick
Title: Not a fresh prawn
Review: Im.choosing this restaurant cause their selection of menu quite interesting and clean ..I choose Mee Bandung Johor because from the.menu the picture.look.tempting..BUT  the meal.taste terrible plus they using not realy fresh prawn..i can taste the prawn.almost spoil...I hope.the page manager read this and check.back.ur SOP....

Author: MelakaLady
Title: Excellent range of menu
Review: The only restaurant I will go if I am at Melaka Sentral. Wide range of noodles and rice dished to choose from. Good value and service. They have another outlet at AEON Ayer Keroh foodcourt.

Author: wintrmanShanghai Region, China
Title: I love the mee (noodles) here
Review: The restaurant is not big while have rich dishes on the menu. Especially I'm impressed by the different kinds of mee (noodles), made from wheat or rice, with soup or not. My family and I had a dinner and a breakfast at this place when we arrived at Malacca and left there. The owner is very nice and introduced the ingredients and styles of the noodles to us. If you like noodles, go to here to enjoy it when you are at the station. (There are also other dishes in addition to noodles, while I haven't got time to try them yet)Show less

Author: Stretch_G1069Quesada, Spain
Title: Best food ever eaten at a bus station !
Review: What a host, Ridzuan the owner couldn't do enough for us, a real gent. He explained what ingredients were in the dishes we were interested in and the spice levels, the food was freshly cooked and tasted great. So a must if you going through Malacca Sentral bus station, don't even think about McDonalds a few metres away.Show less

Author: EmilyMiltonSmithSydney, Australia
Title: Great vegetarian options!
Review: After a tiring bus trip down to Melaka we took respite at this friendly and bright restaurant. The owner had a very great conversations with us (and gave us plenty of advice on transport and things to do in Melaka) and was incredibly accommodating of our dietary requirements. It is incredibly difficult to get good vegetarian food in South East Asia due to the prominence of meat and this was a welcome chance! Ridzuan, the owner spoke to us about the local chillies and they are a great accompaniment to our dishes! I had a fabulous flat noodle mushroom dish (with no animal byproduct sauces which is incredibly exciting!) and my partner had a wonderful sweet and sour prawn dish. The food tasted wonderful, presented well and the Owner and staff were incredibly friendly and helpful! Definitely recommend stopping by this place! We will be back very soon (and who would have thought at a bus station as well!) and ridiculously good value! Cheapest eats ever! Thank you Ridzuan, we really enjoyed the food! :)(oh my goodness and the fresh, healthy juices without all the sugar rubbish usually found in all juices in SEAsia!)Show less

Author: Fahad AAbu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates
Title: Amazing Food and service
Review: We were in Malaysia few days ago and came accross this restaurant situated in the Melaka bus station. Me and my wife were very satisfied with the experiences we had. Food was very taste and there were plenty of choices. We had a great conversation with the owner and he was very helpful with our selections. He explained how all of his juices are made with all natural flavors with no added sugar. The restaurant owner is a chemist major he knows what he is doing...I definitely recommend trying their juices. We tried some of the other places in this location but this was definitly the best.. Thanks!!Show less

Author: IbizaDave86Ibiza
Title: Great food, even better owner!
Review: We stopped here for some food on our way into Melaka. This restaurant is at the bus terminal and you have to jump on another bus to the centre.The food was lovely (a very common thing to say in Malaysia), but what really stood out was the friendliness of the owner, Richard. He was so chatty and nice. And was very willing to make recommendations for food and music! Haha.We enjoyed his company so much, we went back the next day on our way out of Melaka too!Thanks Richard!Show less

Author: JJMN4lifeFort Collins, Colorado
Title: Healthy and Delicousios
Review: Best restaurant in Melaka Bus Terminal! The fresh and tasty vegetables used in the soup and rice dishes will leave you satisfied and happy. Tasty cuisine and worth the stop. The owner spoke fluent English and welcomed me with a smile. Make sure to tell him where you are from. Show less

Author: Nai BShanghai, China
Title: Great for Families Dining
Review: A nice restaurant with many big tables for families dining. Need to make reservation few days early especially for weekends. You might need to wait for more than 15 minutes during peak hours.The service was attentive and orders repeated. Green tea was offered promptly and good refill followed up. Food portions and presentations were excellent. The pricings were competitive.Will definitely visit again when next in Malacca as were given returned vouchers.Show less

Author: Aldert VSouthsea
Title: Great experience
Review: Although we are familiar with Japanese food, we aren’t experts. That does not matter because the waitress was very patient with us and gave helpful explanations. I did not expect such a personal approach given the size of the restaurant. All dishes we chose, fish, beef, chicken and seafood were great, although I don’t think one really stood out. It was very reasonably priced. Show less

Author: annpK7508VK
Title: Value for money
Review: Had lunch here. Chunky pieces of sashimi.  Food is tasty.  Total bill very reasonable. They have better seats on other side of restaurant. You may want to request for this.  We only found out on the way to toilets. Staff quite attentive. Will visit again.

Author: Yuric D
Title: Not that good
Review: Okay food. Terrible service. The waitress forgot to order one of our food. Called another waitress to reorder. Waitress ordered the wrong food. Called waitress to ask for toothpick and bill. Takes a long time for the waiter to come.after that needs 3 waitress to do it right. First one just said okay and didn't come back. Second one brought the bill but no toothpick. Third one brought the toothpick. Didn't enjoy at all. Not thinking about coming here again.Show less

Author: JiggyKiki
Title: Nice, fresh quality Japanese Restaurant
Review:
Went there for dinner during CNY. Food was fresh and not like others ice cold from freezer and tasteless. The pizza was nice and warm with generous portion for 2 or 3.
Place could be rowdy at times when it's crowded with families.

Author: 875rajag
Title: A Pleasant Surprise for Melaka..!
Review: Malacca (or Melaka) I presumed would be starved of good Japanese cuisine. Well I was wrong..! Iche Zen a bustling restaurant with not only locals patronizing it but most importantly many Japanese were walking in just as we were ushered to our table. The seafood was fresh and well presented.. Would recommend this restaurant highly.Show less

Author: Wendysltan
Title: Worth it!
Review: Cosy environment delicious food, quiet hideaway from town. Reasonably price and quality of food and taste is good.

Author: Lil Ly c
Title: Excellent food
Review: A good and extensive range of Japanese food.  Very authentic and tasty.  Price is on the high side but if u have the Parkson card u are entitle to 10% discount. Pls present card before payment.

Author: blackhorse007
Title: Nice food tucked away from the tourist crowds
Review: If u are looking for  a place away from the tourist areas and joint the local.... this is a place for good food with nice comfort

Author: toledocupra
Title: Good Japanese food
Review: Third time here at the restaurant. Sashimi is fresh and nice. Set lunch is value for money. Plenty of staff and they are all very attentive and helpful. Decent portions for their ramen. Can't ask for more in malacca for Japanese food.

Author: MimathRebecq Rognon, Belgium
Title: Good food but poor service
Review: Restaurant visited with a business Team of 10.Food is fresh, good and well presented but service is highly disorganized and when anything like a dessert or a beer is needed be ready to have to ask 2 or 3 times for it.
