Review: Booked a Nyonya cooking class for our colleagues as part of our team building event but it did not happen because of a miscommunication with the staff. Their website is slightly misleading so I would suggest you call them up and double confirm your booking for the cooking class. They only put us down for lunch and not the cooking class. Oh well, lunch was delicious anyway but would’ve been more enjoyable if we had managed to get the cooking class too. Staff apologised and gave us a discount for our food so that was a nice and well appreciated gesture. Show less

Author: Jacko2017Wacko
Title: Best Nonya food ever tasted.
Review: Well, Chicken Rendang, Chendol is a must to try. Service was totally fine as well. Nice food always has crowds so your patience of waiting will definitely worth it. Will be back for more.

Author: eng00703
Title: Melaka family holiday
Review: Great food, excellent Peranakan flavours. Must try to sample local cultures. And best of all; affordable and reasonable prices!

Author: nanz31
Title: Aweosme food and great service
Review: We got our sitting after waiting for 10 mins ( we were there at 2pm) ordered the food and was served in 15 mins by our waitress Ruzia. she deserves a special mention- So patient and so cheerful despite the crowd. Food was nice as well. Will definately go again.Show less

Author: Lena YSingapore
Title: Superb and AUTHENTIC Nonya Cuisine & Nonya Chang
Review: Location has moved to another part of Melaka (original location at Jonker Streer). Food and service as good as before! Highly recommended : Curry laksa, kueh pie ti, popiah, fish maw soup, bush keluak Ayam, petai n shrimps, Assam fish, NGOs going, Chao cai,and Nonya Chang!Show less

Author: ze_succubusSingapore
Title: Glad we went ahead
Review: So looking at the comments I didn't want to waste my time but 2 friends recommended it so it became a must try and I'm glad we went. We made a reservation online, didn't have to queue on a Sunday and the meal was delicious. They sold out of the popiah which was disappointing but the Otak, Squid, Babi Pongteh (kids fav) and etc more than made up for it. Service was totally fine as well.Show less

Author: ChongSengIpoh, Malaysia
Title: Better than I expected
Review: At first, I was a little bit worried after seeing all those polarized comments online about this restaurant. However, my concern quickly disappeared after seeing the decent food being served on the table. Tips: Better make a reservation (online) during weekends and public holidays or else you will have to face a long queque. Tips #2: You get 10% off if you use Maybank card for your bill. Show less

Author: Snoopy S
Title: Dec 2017 Family Trip to Malacca
Review: The restaurant served good food but the service is not to standard. Waiting time for lunch is about 1.5-2hr. Very slow in service.Very unfriendly staff at the front counter (waiting to get seat). I could say the price is not cheap. Went once and will not patronize again. Anyway, good to try for the first time.Show less

Author: JasonC7231
Title: Overrated at best! Too touristy & not authentic
Review: There's no integrity in running the business. Rang up on a day earlier to set a reservation, was told only walk-in. Came for it the next day and was shocked that there were multiple tables with reserve sign and was told I had to wait 45 minutes to be served.In short, left the place and went to a better restaurant after consulting the locals.There's a better baba nyonya restaurant by the name of Aunty Lee, close to the Portuguese settlement @ Jalan ujong pasir. Skip this & go for that.Show less

Author: 751tankSingapore, Singapore
Title: Late Lunch at Nancy,s Restaurant
Review: As our family of 4 were not able to find a parking space, we missed having lunch at Makko's Restaurant which closed at 2.30pm. We decided instead to go to Nancy's Kitchen which seemed to have some pretty good reviews, reaching the restaurant at just after 3.00pm. Considering that it was already passed the lunch hour, we were somewhat surprised that the restaurant was still quite crowded at that time but we were able to get a table immediately We ordered only a few light/small dishes namely current chicken, assam fish, chap chye and a mee goreng as we had our breakfast late in the morning. In spite of the restaurants popularity from the number of customers seen, we found the food just so so and somewhat overrated and also relatively expensive. For example, the assam seabass has only half of a small fish weighting perhaps 200 to 300 gms and costs about Rm 30. The fish gravy was just a watery assam solution and very sour (overly sour) while the mee goreng seemed undercooked and not tasty, a far cry from the normal mee goreng we have eaten. The chap chye consists of mainly cabbage stewed until very soft just like what we get from the mixed rice hawkers in Singapore. Only the chicken curry was good and tasted nice. Melaka was supposed to be well known for their peranakan food but we don't find that what we had was anything to shout about.Show less

Author: 882tifft
Title: Dinner
Review: Favourite among the locals .. hotel staff will recommend but it’s a decent nonya meal.. that’s it. Good to book before going to avoid disappointment.

Author: E_ng1972
Title: Nancy’s Kitchen
Review: First time to Nancy’s. Made reservation hence don’t hv to queue.  Food is a little ordinary.  Ordered our fav Petai Udang but was disappointed as there were v few petai. Chendol is not as wat we have expected too. 😔

Author: clementb564
Title: Good nyonya food
Review:
We went to this place once for dinner. The place itself has a nice atmosphere and the food is very good. Prices are correct.
Yet, it is recommended to book in advance as it can get quite busy for dinner.

Author: elisa gKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Overrated
Review: Arrived at 6pm for dinner before the crowd sets in but all tables were quick to fill up and queue started to build up outside the restaurant. If wish to try, best to prebook. Lobak was tasty, cendol was good, pai tee's filling was coarsely julienne while i prefer matchstick size but this is just my personal preference, some people might like the thicker cut, the taste was ok though. The biggest let down was the babi pongteh where the pig skin was rather hard and flesh dry, taste was fine. For any braised or stewed pork with skin, the skin texture should at lest be soft to the bite and a little sticky, although there are people who like them melt in the mouth but not many like dry hard skin. We also ordered vegetable curry and cincaluk omelette. Generally, this place is good enough for a decent dinner if you happen to be around the area and there is no queue. Otherwise, there are many similar restaurant that offer the typical nyonya cuisine. The total bill was around RM20-30 per head in average as we didn't order any seafood.Don't think I will go again.Show less

Author: AdeleneT
Title: Nothing great
Review: Had lunch here having read some good reviews. Ordered a curry chicken, prawns with petai, spring rolls and ngoh hiang. The curry chicken was just passable. The sambal prawns with petai were slightly better but the prawns were tiny and the petai sliced too thinly.

Author: Sally T
Title: average peranakan food
Review: Walked a long way to this restaurant but found the food to be just so-so. The pictures looked better than the actual food! Was quite disappointed. The otah tasted quite good though.

Author: Alok8686
Title: Something nice!
Review: If compare to Donald and Lily, I would say both shops have they own speciality. This particular shop, the nyonya noodles and cendol are superb!

Author: mia7janeKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Favorite nyonya restaurant
Review: Nancy's kitchen is my favorite nyonya restaurant. The taste, flavour, spicyness are very consistent everytime I visit. I will visit this restaurant every time I visit Melaka. My fav dishes are their signature assam fish, lobak, cencaluk ommerlet, paitee. Now I Feel like make a trip to Melaka this weekend!Show less

Author: shuxianivyPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: The authentic Nyonya Food
Review: One famous food in the historical city in Malaysia. Most foods cook with chili that you hardly can get one without it. Most of the signature nyonya dishes are good but the pongteh (stewed pork/chicken with yellow bean) however just so so likes normal braised pork. Chicken candlenut and sambal petai prawn are good.Show less

Author: 796vijayp
Title: Very nice food
Review:
Good food and nice ambience. A bit a walking from jonker’s walk. Quick service and attentive staff.

We had local Peranakan food and they were reasonably priced.

Author: sarah_3YJ
Title: Great Authentic Food - Don't Miss
Review:
Great varieties of authentic food.  There was a short queue when we reached but we were lucky to get a table in a relatively short time.  Serving portions were good and fast.  

A great place to have authentic Nonya food.

Author: MELAKABAGUS
Title: Thank God for Reservations.
Review:
We made reservations, 1 to 2 days before, thus luckily we were able to swerve in without much hassle.Need to be prompt though, as the crowd is fierce and unforgiving.

Food is served hot and fast. 

No disappointment second time round.

Author: JUDYLEE2003Kuching, Malaysia
Title: Nyonya Food
Review: This restuarant do not accept reservation, for walk in customers only. We came on a weekend lunch time, it was already full so we need to put our names for the table queue. We manage to get our table after half hour. I love the food here and I find it cheaper than the other popular Nyonya restuarants. The service is fast and I love the fried fish with sambal paste, do refer to my photo. There is a 10 % discount if you pay by Maybank card. When we left at 2.00 pm, there is still a long queue of customers waiting for their turn.Show less

Author: Wong C
Title: Standard of food has dropped
Review:
Unfortunately the food was bland tasting. Not worth the wait. I first visited the place many years ago at Jonker Street & food was better then.
Many other places with better tasting nyonya food.

Author: vitxho
Title: Worth to try
Review: Second times come, taste still stand good! Service good, price acceptable , if don't like to queue, avoid lunch time, school and public holiday...

Author: Irwyn NKL, Malaysia
Title: Good Variety with Small Portion Options
Review: If you like to savor various types of nyonya dishes, just order the smallest portion. Even for 2 pax, you can order 4 or 5 dishes cause they're really small. Pictures in the menu look really salivating but none of the dishes look like the pics. Seriously, they don't look good when they arrive but luckily they still taste good. I would not order the tamarind prawns though cause the prawns look big in the pic but you actually get much smaller ones and it is not worth the price.Show less

Author: WengC85Singapore, Singapore
Title: Worth the wait
Review: You have to plan your visit. The queue for the walk-in can be longThe night we visited, we arrived at 630pm and were number 14. So the word is out. I did notice that there’s now a sign informing patrons that they can book a day ahead. The 13 people in Malaysia ahead of us didn’t know that, nor did we. You want to book!Food - awesome Enjoyed every dish. I really mean every single morselSolid 5 stars - better if you book a day ahead Show less

Author: paulP1155SHBrunei Darussalam
Title: Delicious and affordable food
Review: Recently have dinner at this restaurant. It is just 10 minutes walk from Jonker street. Ordered a few dishes and also starters for 9 pax for only M$135. Restaurant has a second floor. Service was Ok and place was clean. This is a non-halal restaurant serving nyonya food. Would come back again the next time I visit Melaka. The chinese hot tea come in a jug.Show less

Author: Praviny M
Title: Poor service
Review: I'm aware that this place is famous and melaka is a place you have queue for food. But this famous restaurant been having this many crowds for a very long time and they should be able to cater these amount of ppl well. There was a family before us waited for 1 hours place and still have not been seated. To be noted: there's a upstairs portion that they refuse to open in order to seat their customers.Show less

Author: GogogoC
Title: Jalan-jalan cari makan
Review: Good and authentic nyonya foods and kiuh. Food service is fast and not pricey like other peranakan restaurant. Just need to wait a bit for seat, but a good system in place by the owner to avoid jump Q. Definitely will come back.

Author: Vera A
Title: Delicious food
Review: after tired photos, we had lunch at this restaurant, there is a good onde- dde here. Almost all the food we ordered was all delicious. Food prices are also still reasonable. The dining area is 2 floors and full AC. His service is fast and friendly. I recommendShow less

Author: SockrateezScarsdale, New York
Title: Worth the trek, reasonably priced
Review: It's a bit of a walk from the Jonker Street area but worth it. The curry chicken, candlenut chicken, braised pork and pork fried with bean curd we had were very tasty. It took a while to get seated; it seems popular with regular locals. The small/medium/large serving options are a great idea. Show less

Author: 987reginahSingapore, Singapore
Title: Aromatic and Heavenly
Review: Two dishes stood out for me at this restaurant frequently by the locals. The spicy Nonya Fried Rice and fried pork balls. As I do not see any tour groups in the restaurant, the food came piping hot. The fried rice was aromatic and delicious you can even eat it on its own. The pork ball with a crispy coating was tender and juicy on the inside. The flavour was just right. A nice contrast in texture. Service was fast and efficient on a Friday night. The toilet flush was broken. If the toilet was in proper working order, I would have given it 5 stars.Show less

Author: aukenn
Title: Friendly Nyonyas !!!
Review: Good food with good friendly host. Enjoyable experience. Food portion might be small for some but taste is 10/10. Do make reservations and try all their signature dishes!

Author: fuzzytravellermelbourne
Title: Average food
Review: It was recommended to us as the most famous Perangkan (nyonya) Restaurant. It was busy on the day we visited. This was the second nyonya Restaurant we had dined during our short trip to Malacca. We felt the food was just average and overpriced. The service was ordinary. Show less

Author: Darron1970
Title: Well worth the visit
Review: We went out of our way to get to Nancy's for lunch. It was pretty busy so booking in advance I would say is safe bet. Our food was delicious and we were really happy with our visit. Highly recommended.

Author: 687kevina
Title: Nonya Food
Review:
It was a nice place to sample some so-so nonya food.  Was all hyped up to try the food with all the rave but somewhat it fell short of expectations. 
Orders taken but some items were forgotten.  Service could be better.

Author: LindaL834Singapore, Singapore
Title: Great Nonya taste
Review: We ordered the meatballs , pie- ti , beef rendang, Ayam buah keluak, Babi ponteh, otah, ngioh heong... just about everything on the menu! An hour later, all 8 of us were utterly defeated by the food attack! Everything was just too good ... missed out on the soft shell crab though- we’ll be back!Remember to book a table to avoid disappointment, we arrived at opening time and downstairs was already full and was shown to an upstairs table promptly. By the time we left which was around 1 pm , there was a huge crowd waiting Show less

Author: slepyvon
Title: yummy lunch
Review: super long queue waiting for tables during lunch time. best is to call & reserve tables a day before. love the beef redang. popian was also good. Able to accommodate for large groups. Price was ok

Author: JasonLow2307
Title: Excellent food and kuih
Review: The nyonya dishes is great. It taste good especially the sweet and sour fish. I also enjoyed the cendol that have strong Melaka sugar taste. The onde-onde is also tasty

Author: Jwpgoh
Title: Over-priced and not worth the wait
Review: The food is rather expensive and over-hyped. Rather average peranakan food. With so many competing options in the city area, there is nothing much to rave about.

Author: Ju_juPerthAustralia
Title: Excellent local cuisine
Review: We were recommended this restaurant and it didn’t disappoint. Great service, great local home cooked food.

Author: CeciltongSingapore
Title: One of the best Peranakan restaurants in Melaka
Review: My family always dine here on every trip, and we can say that the standard has been consistent even after they moved to this new location.Highly recommended dishes : babi ponteh, chinchalok omelette, kueh pati, and the bee hoon goring.This is the place for kuehs and bak changes. We have eatern bak changs from 3 different places in Melaka and we think that this is the best. If not, why would we buy 20-30 on each trip to give away when we get home?Show less

Author: swkwan
Title: Long queue. Nice food.
Review: Waited long. Food are nice. Should make booking before coming. Due to too many customers the waiters were impatient.

Author: jadedsoonSingapore, Singapore
Title: Standard has dropped, and overrated!
Review: We have always enjoyed food at Nancy’s when they were at Jonker. But we visited their restaurant at the new location and found the food to be sub par and standard has dropped. The duck soup came cold, steamed fish was dry, and one of their buak kuluak seed was missing content. But they insist it is like that! Horrible service.Show less

Author: GraceN1010
Title: Lunch
Review: Reached at 11am and there was already a Long queue outside. Friendly staff, though they missed some orders but quick to replace. Food is nice as usual.. 👍

Author: chinyih66
Title: Amazing Peranakan Food
Review: One of the popular Nyonya Restaurant in Melaka among the locals and tourists. Environment was so much better since they moved to the current location from the previous Jonker Street. Must try the different type of Peranakan curry cooked with fish, beef, pork, mutton and vegetable. They all tasted differently although they are all curry. Now this place had a big public car park not far away compared to while they are at Jonker. Price are reasonable. Great place to have Peranakan food while in Melaka.Show less

Author: Kailee_TN
Title: Disappointed & over-rated
Review: It's our first time to Melaka and we decided to have lunch at this place due to Tripadvisor's rating. Boy... are we really disappointed. We ordered chicken candlenut, fried meehoon, ngoh hiang, and cendol. Only ngoh hiang was a bit tasty, cendol was good, but the first 2 dishes were completely tasteless. Strongly urge Tripadvisor to review the rating.Show less

Author: blessedwoman08Singapore, Singapore
Title: Overrated...Can give it a miss
Review: Recommend to make reservation as it gets really crowded.Be prepared to stand at the door way like a lost fool because no one cares about your existence. You gotta catch the staff to attend to you. Food quality is so so and portions are really little for small orders. There are better nonya restaurants around, can give this a miss if you have limited time in Melaka. Show less

Author: TerryTeoKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Nice and easy...
Review: I came here upon friend's recommendation. Booking is essential and the best time I would say is around 1130am - 1230pm and thereafter can get a bit busy. Plenty of Peranakan foods to choose and the taste is quite good compared to some Pernakan food you could get in town. Price is reasonable. The only let down for me was the cendol. Others were great.Service was quick and friendly during my visit. Plenty of parking around the corner. Would definitely come back again.Show less

Author: PknowlesiSingapore, Singapore
Title: Nothing To Rave About
Review: Had a reservation for a lunch party for 12. The restaurant was full to the brim. There was no hostess at the door and there were other guests who were just standing around trying to get some attention. Finally, when I managed to get some attention, I was told that the assigned dining area was on level 2. I had 3 elderly folks and conquering that flight of steps was impossible. I explained the situation and the host just retorted back:”You didn’t state this when making your reservation.” How the hell was I suppose to know u have a level 2??? In the end we split into 2 separate tables. Lose 1 ⭐️.There was nothing to rave about with regards to the food. I think there are better ones in malacca. The udang nenas was very watered down and it lacked the oomph and most of the dishes were only warm and not hot probably due to the lack of service staff bringing out the dishes to the diners. Lose another ⭐️. If u have limited time in malacca, it’s ok giving this place a miss. Show less

Author: fqtravellerndSingapore, Singapore
Title: Over-rated and definitely not as authentic
Review: Was good years back but success got over their heads... its too overrated and definitely not as authentic as it used to be. Staff is rude and nobody cares about the customers. Their goal is to have as many customers as possible, so they rush you through your meals. Can definitely get much better Peranakan food at cheaper prices elsewhere in Melaka.Show less

Author: Eileena_2005Pontian Kecil, Malaysia
Title: Nyonya Dinner
Review: Can't go Jonker street due to heavy rain and came here for dinner due to introduction from trip advisor.Many is queueing up and have to wait for some time.The staff there is too busy to introduce what famous or must-try dishes, I guess.Food slightly a bit salty but the price is okay.Show less

Author: jeslin2018
Title: Authentic Peranakan Cuisine
Review: Authentic Peranakan CuisineWe had dinner at Nancy’s Kitchen on 18th May 2018, and this was the first time here since we had it a few times at her previous location close to Jonker Street. There a plenty of available free (no parking coupons required) parking space which was important to us.The three of us ordered the Chicken Rendang, Sambal Udang Petai, Cincalok Telur, Ayam Buah Keluak, Cincalok Ulam with Nasi Lemak and Buah Kedondong and Sour Plum drinks.The Chicken Rendang was delicious and fragrant, so was the Cincalok Telur which was nicely fluffy but can taste better with a bit more cincalok. Both these dishes went well with the warm Nasi Lemak.The Sambal Udang Petai was OK but could have been better with more petai. Also, the petai was cut into pieces that were too small to be discernable – the petai should have been just halved to give it a stronger flavor.The Ayam Buah Keluak was good but you will have to order the nuts separately. I think previously in the former location there were three or four nuts per small bowl. The nuts were of a good quality in taste and texture,The Cincalok Ulam was a bit too dry for my liking but was served in a reasonable portion. The ulam should have a bit more of the cincalok wetness and saltiness to improve the taste.Overall, it was a good dinner and my dinner companions were satisfied with the taste, portions of the food and ambience of the restaurant. Hope to taste the minor improvements on my next visit.Show less

Author: 44garyrYork, United Kingdom
Title: Nice, you would not be disapointed
Review: We stopped off at a recommended restaurant for some nice Nyonya style cuisine. We had a selection of food from fried rice to chicken curry. The service was good and the food was tasty. I would not say I was blown away however I would say it wasn’t that bad and I would go again.Show less

Author: 901stanleyl
Title: Delicious lunch
Review:
Took grab from hotel to hv family lunch there ard 2.30pm

As it's a weekday and off peak hours, not so much lunch crowd.

Food is consistently delicious.
Price is reasonable.
Our frequent place to hv a nice meal whenever we visit Malacca.

Author: kclooiSingapore, Singapore
Title: Never fails to be consistent
Review: A meal at Nancy's Kitchen can be expected to be good. It won't blow your socks off but you will not be disappointed. Moving out of Jonker Walk did not affect the business at all. A restaurant that does not rely on location is a restaurant to follow.Show less

Author: Dharshini86
Title: Fantastic food
Review: Highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for authentic peranakan food. The restaurant is clean. Can be very busy at lunch time with people queuing up until outside the restaurant, the food is well worth it. Price is also reasonable.

Author: joannebC6713DPTairua, New Zealand
Title: Super great cooking class A1
Review: My daughter and I attended a wonderful cooking class at Nancy’s today. Nancy took the class and there were only the two of us. What was very good is that as she has travelled to NZ and knows what’s available there so was able to give hints for making the food at home. We made the Candle nut chicken and the Prawn and pineapple curry. Both were delicious and highly recommended. When we had finished cooking we took our meals down to the restaurant and ate also were provided lime juice, morning glory (veg of choice) rice and spring roll.Show less

Author: JeSGoh
Title: Food not great
Review: The Pie Tie here is yummy but the rest of the food wasn't fantastic and the restaurant didnt feel very "alive".  Our orders also came wrong.  We were served 2 other dishes that were different from what we ordered. Can give this place a miss.

Author: travelbug_July1968Singapore, Singapore
Title: Don't bother eating here
Review: Given that this restaurant made it to the Top 5 restaurants for Peranakan food in Malacca, we decided to visit. Boy did we regret our decision! Frankly, I am really not sure what the hype is all about. Firstly, there is always a long queue to get in. Secondly, the staff is unaware about service with a smile and are very abrupt. We could have forgiven all this if the food was good. But sorry to say it was atrocious!! The beef rendang was so tough that it was impossible to chew. The beef should have been soft and tender and melt in your mouth. The candlenut chicken was ordinary to say the least. The vegetable dish was so spicy that it ruined the dish. Please don't waste your time visiting this restaurant. Hopefully so many bad reviews will make them spring into action to clean up their act.Show less

Author: jarainSingapore, Singapore
Title: Authentic food at very reasonable prices
Review: Come early because the place tend to get crowded even at 12 noon. Make a reservation if you could. Their assam fish was super good with some other dishes such as kueh pie-tee. Chendol was nice too. Try the bak- chang.. nicely steamed and soft glutinous rice! Show less

Author: Jade8KUalaLUmpurKUala LUmpur
Title: peranakan food
Review: customer service could be better especially over the phone.understandably there will be a long queue over the weekend. however, the owners were busy at the cashier counter and not bothered with the people coming in.food is average and small in portion.there is a corner selling melaka delicaciesShow less

Author: GraceLimVelistsikhe, Georgia
Title: Service with an attitude
Review: We did not make a booking and arrived after the lunch hours about 3pm.Still there was a queue and we wrote down our names waiting for them to call and allocate the table number.The lady in charge of the queue was rude and unwilling. We waited for about 20 minutes and we were told to go to the 2nd floor. It looked like a store room with about adhoc three tables. We were disappointed with the food served. We specially made a trip to Nancy’s Kitchen after we read many reviews but we feel that it did not live to its reputation !We will not visit again. Show less

Author: dzafrana
Title: Worth the cisit
Review: Believe the hype. While we had to wait close to 45 mins for a table, the service provided was very professional and food experience was one of the best I’ve had in Malaysia. Tasty and large portions.

Author: ginrey
Title: Bad Foods. Disappointed to the max!
Review:
Just came out of Nancy’s Kitchen. Small serving, bad customer service, and lousy food. 

I used to eat here a couple months back and now its quality has declining. 

Sad

Author: johnnyxtSeremban, Malaysia
Title: Very decent Nyonya food
Review: Decently large restaurant with upper floor seatings as well. Didnt need to wait despite having no reservations on a Friday evening even when there a was a crowd.Food was served quickly and one of the most memorable dish was the assam fish. Just the right balance of spicy and sour, and the size of fish was quite large, and fresh.Show less

Author: Siang Teng LSingapore, Singapore
Title: Poor food. Disappointment.
Review: It is supposed to be one of the better Peranakan restaurants in town. However, I found them pale when compared to the other known restaurants in the same league. The cooking is poor. The reason could be that their kitchen could not turnaround fast enough to meet demand and at the end, they short changed their customers. For example, we asked for “sayur lodeh” and were told that it was still being cooked in the pot. We told them that we were willing to wait for it but at the end we got half cooked “sayur lodeh”. Their ngoh hiang and pie tee are hopeless. It was a big disappointment.Show less

Author: cyrillim
Title: Authentic Nonya food
Review: Came here with family to have a quick lunch. Ended up ordering quite a lot. The food was great. Service was good too. Came about 3pm on a weekday. Did not have to wait for a table. Will visit again.

Author: FLBBPCMM
Title: Too spicy too eat
Review: Most of the dishes is spicy. For me is too spicy. All dishes served in very small portion. The small size is like good for one person. The nyoya fish we order is so small n cost RM35. Kueh pie ti is not so crunchy. Very expensive. Not my likingShow less

Author: Cassandra ZKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Decent food with poor staff
Review: We walked in to the restaurant. And the man who took orders just left us at the corner, asking us wait without any other words. However, when the next group of visitors arrived (who didn't make reservations in advance as well), the man suddenly became another person - warm, friendly, helping them register.As a result, even we were there earlier, our sequence was behind the next group. Title: Yummy Nonya dishes

Author: Wenxi CSingapore, Singapore
Title: Finally here!
Review: Nancy's Kitchen is one of the popular places to go for authentic Peranakan Food in Melaka. Looking at its crowd, walk-in customers need to have some patience in the queue.Today's Nancy's recipe has been passed down from generations and this is the 3rd generation. With the precision towards quality of each dish being served and practices strict cooking skill, it is no wonder that the authentic Peranakan dishes bring new and as well as returned customers.Looking at the lunch crowd on the lower level, we waited for quite a while before getting our seats.Interior was homely and air conditioned. The reason why we visited Nancy's Kitchen is because of its popularity and that it is non-halal.Being Non-Halal, we get to choose more variety to certain dishes like with pork than chicken.With the lunch's crowd, we only managed to get seats on the upper level. The kitchen transfer all cooked food using a elevator from the ground level to the upper level.Upper LevelSteamed Spring Roll aka Popiah is served with turnips , cucumber, fresh bean, coriander leave, eggs, garlic and many other vegetables. It is one of the popular starter before meal and is a must try.Spring Roll (Popiah) - RM 4.00 / PcsKueh Pie Tee came in crispy hat cone form and filled with vegetable. The fillings are similar to what we have in the spring roll but in a different serving.Top Hat (Pai Tee) - RM 6.00 per set (5 pcs)Having their last appetizer on the menu, they have this pork fried with bean curd skin on the menu which we often called it Ngoh Hiong. The pork is wrapped with bean curd skin and deep fried to obtain its crispiness on the outside with sweet tasty juicy pork on the inside.Pork Fried with Bean Curd Skin (Ngoh Hiang) - RM 6.00 (Small) / RM 9.00 (Medium) / RM 12.00 (Large)Chap Chai is anohter classic Peranakan dish that we will often order. Its a combination of black fungus, lily bubs, cabbage, glass noodles, bean curd sheet and cook with preserved fermented soya bean. It is a stew mix vegetables filled with natural sweetness of the vegetable simply irresistible for young and old. However we find that the style of Chap Chai was too dry for us and was not soaked with gravy.Nonya Mixed Vegetable (Nyonya Chap Chai) - RM 8.00 (Small) / RM 10.00 (Medium) / RM 12.00 (Large) Ayam / Bak Buah Keluak is a truly Peranakan classic dish. The black nut (Buah Keluak) is sold at additional cost of RM 2.00 each. Buah Keluak is originally from Indonesia and taste like truffle. Nut is cut open allowing the dish to have a sweet spicy and sourish taste.Chicken / Pork Rib with Black Nut - RM 15.00 (S) , 1 Nut RM2.00Ladies fingers can be served 2 ways, either boiled of fried with chilli. We had chosen the steamed version and it was served with lemony chilli paste.Boiled / Fried Ladies Fingers (Bendi Celur) - RM 8.00 (Small) / RM 10.00 (Medium) / RM 12.00 (Large)This is scrumptious! Duck soup was cooked on slow heat with salted vegetable and white wine, giving the taste of sourish to the dish. The dish has been passed down for 3 generations.Duck with Salted Vegetable Soup (Sup Itik Tim) - RM 15.00 (Small) / RM 18.00 (Medium) / RM 22.00 (Large)Last but not least, we had the classic dessert, Cendol for a sweet ending touch to the meal. Savour with Gula Melaka, coconut, green bean and coconut jelly.Cendol - RM 4.50Overall, Nancy's Kitchen has a home style Peranakan Food with reasonable pricing. To be honest, I am impressed by most of their dishes and will recommend to anyone who goes to Melaka and looking for Nyonya Dishes.Show less

Author: Phyllis P
Title: Good peranakan food
Review: Our must-eat during each Melaka visit. During this trip, we learnt that it has moved out from Jonker, new place has bigger seating capacity. Prices remain reasonable and good food quality. Recommended!

Author: 140angelinak
Title: Authentic home cook
Review: Loves the food. Remind me of my grandma's cooking.  Definitely will return. Lo bak, pork cincaluk and steam okra with special chillie sauce are my favourite.

Author: CLYlumSingapore, Singapore
Title: Delicious peranakan food
Review: Our family of 6 managed to get a table after 10 mins of waiting with less than 5 customers in the queue @ Taman Kota Laksamana. Why? Our lunch @ Nancy’s Kitchen was around 3 pm. Perhaps, it was after the normal lunch crowd.Food was great. Especially sambal belachan fried rice, prawn roll and chilli (need to pay). All other peranakan dishes were delicious! Show less

Author: EatnPlayallDaySingapore, Singapore
Title: Eat if you must
Review: Seriously average- couldn't feel the heart and soul in the cooking. Very crowded and commercial. Could have been that Nancy was at the cashier and not the kitchen? ;) The best thing here is the seriously good sambas belachan - RM3 per dish.Eat here of you must and be prepared to wait. Go really early before they open if you don't want to wait too long.Show less

Author: Al-Net-Olo

Review:
Like everyone else, we waited an hour for a table sans reservations.

The pie tee was good but the addition of the sambal (extra RM3) made it better.

Rest of food was ok. Dunno if it was worth the wait in the end

Author: C7964ROkarendCairns, Australia
Title: Locals’ Retreat
Review: This place is popular with the locals so the only way to get a table is to either reserve in advance or go there, add your name to the queue list and wait. We visited once during the Christmas period and it was busy so we reserved for the next day. The restaurant has three floors. We ordered a variety of dishes, mainly small size and left full. The prawn coconut curry was delicious as was the braised pork. Our son (who is vegetarian) chose mixed vegetables and was happy with his dish. Our other son ordered duck and was disappointed that there was so little meat. The lady fingers were very spicy. Rice portions were extremely small - we had to order twice and there was a mix up with the drinks. But, all in all, 100 RM for 4 was good value.Show less

Author: JTCruz69Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Good Nonya Restaurant
Review: We had to wait 40mins for walk in that wanted Grd Flr seating for the elderly persons in our group. They have wide range of Nonya dishes which included Pork, beef, fish. We ordered sambal petai prawns, pork curry , otak-otak . All turn up well except the chapchai needs improvement. Cendol for dessert was good. Wait staff was attentive. Show less

Author: cweitatSingapore, Singapore
Title: Pretty average (for me)
Review: Had this as our first meal when we reached Melaka and this was around the corner from Hatten Hotel. They served all the food in one round so that you don't have to eat dish by dish. The taste is very flavorful and i recommend their Otah and their fried rice! Show less

Author: bakupakuSingapore
Title: Delicious food;very helpful staff
Review: I went online to make a reservation, but the timeslot that I wanted was full. The staff was very nice to accommodate our dinner reservation. The peranakan food was nice, and portion was appropriate for sharing. Food was served in about 15mins. My only complaint is that the petai was cut into very tiny pieces and very few.Show less

Author: szeweieng
Title: Great Nyonya Joint
Review: Love it. Still got room 4 improvements. Queue can be very crazy. Took us 1 hour plus 2 get our seats. Other than that, its dishes are great. Highly recommended 4 lunch getaway and dinner getaway on Fri Sat and P Holidays.

Author: derricklwySingapore, Singapore
Title: Lunch
Review: So long wait. 2 of us arrived at 12:55pm and did not get a table until 2:05pm!!! There is no proper waiting area or seats and everyone crowds around the entrance. Seems quite chaotic.Now the food....1) Patie - frankly one of the best we have tasted. It is a little bit spicy, which we find to be very good. 5/52) chap chye - we are disappointed with this dish. It appears that this dish is cooked in a big batch and the cabbage is clearly over cooked. 2.5/53) Ayam buah kelaur - very fragrant and delicious. Quite a number of pieces of chicken was served, together woth 2 bial kelaurs. 4.5/54) fried four corner beans with prawns - fragrantly done with a little bit of sambal chilli. 4/55) Fish maw with meat ball soup - refreshing and tasted very good. 4/56) Chendol - can’t be eating peranakan food without chendol and the serving here did not disappoint. Small bowl but packed with gulam melaka and cocunut milk. Extremely good. 5/5.Show less

Author: KH_LyeKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Average Food, Poor Value for Money
Review: Sought this out due to its good review but hugely disappointing. The quality of the food was not per expectations. We asked the staff (looks junior) for recommendations on their signature dishes but he could not offer any definitively ... so we went on our own. Ayam Buah Keras (Candlenut Chicken) - we ordered a small size, the gravy was good but regrettably the chicken pieces were very small and lots of bones and bits, with a couple of wings, no excuse for giving so little for a small size! Sek Bak (Braised Pork) - quite nice but a tad too much fat. Sambal Udang Petai (Prawn) - this was very disappointing, prawns were not fresh, was frozen and treated - you can taste it! It's no different from what you get in kopi tiam. And the petai - all cut into halves and so very few! Nyonya Chp Chai (mixed vegetables) - what mix?? 90% cabbage only! And tasted very ordinary. Well at least the Kedondong drink was a little saving grace. We felt that this restaurant was overhyped and we can certainly find better Nyonya food at better prices elsewhere.Show less

Author: 901stanleylSingapore, Singapore
Title: Delicious Nonya food
Review: Hv lunch at Nancy Kitchen after checking out from imperial Heritage hotel.The food taste is consistently delicious from the frequent visits some time back.We order the small dishes but the portion was generously big.Food was served quite fast Wifey was too tempted to buy the home make nonya Kueh .Overall, satisfying mealShow less

Author: SylvienD10Petaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Did not enjoy the food
Review: Pai Tee - The best dish that I ordered. Crispy skin and fillings was good.Pork buah keluak with curry base sauce - slightly salty and curry sauce was watery and lack of the oomph flavour.Assam Nenas Prawn - Not the freshest prawns. I can find better elsewhere.Show less

Author: ivykuang98
Title: Quite good
Review:
Food was quite good. Went on a Friday afternoon, queue was short and staff was friendly.
Candlenut chicken was good

Author: ToddlerTalesPerth, Australia
Title: Delicious
Review: Well worth a visit. We didn’t have to wait for a table but have been told weekends are a different story. We were there just after 12 on a Thursday. Quick, friendly service and delicious food. We had the popiah, nonya curry chicken, braised pork and fried rice. More than enough for three of us. Very reasonable prices and great quality food. Highly recommend. Show less

Author: ConundrumMiaoKuala Lumpur, Malaysia

Author: lynndolphiny

Author: jusoh64

Author: leeyan80
Title: Food so so
Review: Not sure is Nyonya food taste sweet , somehow I don’t fancy sweet dishes.. however I like the popiah much.

Author: MARKW8357
Title: Authentic Nyonya Cuisine
Review: Delicious and tasty food with reasonable pricing. Clean and comfortable environment. The asam pork was to die for, in fact all the dishes we ordered were good & delicious. Service was fast & efficient maybe because we went on a weekday and the place was not really packed with customers. Will definitely return. Highly recommended.Show less

Author: Willis J
Title: So so and very oily
Review: Super oily. That day was a packed day. Our orders were wrongly taken. Super super oily. Not as good as per reviews

Author: Betty KWestfield
Title: Best Nonya food in Malacca
Review: We came here especially to have lunch. The food is outstanding with generous portions. The steamed fish of the day was delicious- perfectly steamed with a good dollop of chili on top. The curry chicken was very flavorful as well as the pork dishes. We also ordered a local veggie cooked with shrimp paste. The dishes can be ordered by size (small to large) so you can gauge how much food you want.The place was full- many customers. They also have a small area where you can buy some packaged goods.Show less

Author: aaronthamPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Half way between lunch and dinner
Review: Lovely food and still very authentic after so many years. But these days Aunty Nancy is not there too often. Her personality and friendliness adds to the value and visits.Still a nice place for food. By the way it’s in a new place now and no longer near Jonker street, which is better really. Show less

Author: derrickawcwSingapore, Singapore
Title: Not too impressed
Review: Popiah was shocking - skin was so soft and soggy. Ayam rendang - only one piece of thigh meat?! Egg omelette with prawn - nice but mediocre; ngor Hiang - delicious but not outstanding; meatball soup - meat balls were tender, but overall so-soMaybe we had come with inflated expectations... :-)Show less

Author: gnyrretSingapore, Singapore
Title: At last, decent Nyonya food the way it should be! Thanks to
Review: After visiting a few nyonya restaurants in this world heritage city, I began to despair as I sensed that the cutting of corners for mr profit had become too rampant. TA to the fore then as a few readers mentioned Nancy’s as worth a visit although away from town. And it certainly was! First of all, they serve pork which I feel is part and parcel of authentic Nyonya cuisine. Second, their kitchen is kept busy not only cooking for their many clients, but also conjuring up a myriad of snacks and munchies to be bought as gifts. Try their peanut butter love letters. Also their walnut cookies. Mmmm! We started off with a popiah (spring roll) which had me concerned. It was only half filled and the skin overpowered the flavour. But the Babi Pong Teh, Ngoh Hiang, Assam Fish c Brinjals and Okra had me concentrating on the food. The mee goreng was not worth ordering. NB the sambal belacan here is chargeable RM 4 per portion. Home made a’la Minute. The chendol lived up to its name. Perfumed with coconut sugar and milk, all of us enjoyed the final lick of the dessert spoon. Price was RM100 for three of us. Friendly n helpful staff. Show less

Author: Jenny CKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Downgrade
Review: This is nothing like the food from the old shop at Jonker Street. New place but yucky food. If i cook blindfolded it may turn out better than what we were served. Loads of msg. Only the gula Melaka, kuehs, bachang and biscuits managed to retain some former glory.Show less

Author: Vijay R
Title: Delicious food and efficient service
Review: Nancy's kitchen supplied us with some wonderful pernakan dishes. We had a chance to meet Nancy herself who seems to take great pride in her business. It's a short taxi ride away from central Melakka but well worth a trip.

Author: ElnieLSingapore, Singapore
Title: Decent food for a very reasonable price

The bonus was the little shopping we could do within the restaurant for some cakes, pickles, sweets, dumplings and crackers. Free WiFi was a plus. Next to it or a few doors down, is a lovely little bakery/cafe (Yeast Pastry House) where you can have a nice cup of coffee with some dessert if you aren’t stuffed already. Show less

Author: jojoccbSingapore, Singapore
Title: So so nia
Review: We were there at ard 4ish for some small bites. Ordered po Piah, Ngo Hiang, salted veg duck soup, fried calamari. DumplingPo piah - I dun like. Skin is thickSoup & calamari- not badNgo Hiang - so so Note: belacan is chargeable. Find it salty and not spicy enoughDumpling (Kee Chang) goes well with Gula Melaka Show less

Author: aarontham
Title: Late lunch at 3pm
Review:
First time at their new location, neatly done and sure have more space for seating and car parks.

Author: Charles TSingapore, Singapore

The shop filled up after we arrived at 11am. Prices were reasonable and service was prompt. Loads of nonya snacks and condiments at the counter for sale too.Show less

Author: 62melvynnSingapore, Singapore
Title: Authentic Nyonya Cruisine

There are so many dishes we wanted to try but as there's only 4 of us, we order 7 dishes, will be back again if I'm in Malacca. This place is super crowded on weekend, reservation is recommended and that can be easily done online, just google. Show less

Author: SumiologyLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Used to be good but now its really bad
Review: I am from Melaka so I am highly familiar with Peranakan food. Nancy Kitchen several years ago was good, then it was average as it became more popular. However, since it has moved from Jonkers to Kota Laksamana, the food is not at all Peranakan. Rendang was more like chicken curry and the prawns overcooked with hardly and chili paste for taste. Kangkung belacan was easily the worst kangkung belacan I have eaten. Not going back.Show less

Author: Cyanne L
Title: Will be back
Review: My family enjoy3d the dinner well, we have ordered 9 dishes, and finished everything except the rendang chicken which was too lemak. We like the cendol, portion was just nice for 2 person sharing after the meal. Overall price was reasonable, our bill approximately at RM208 with 9 adult proper dinner.Show less

Author: LNE1976Singapore
Title: Still my fav Nonya in Melaka
Review: Clean, very affordable, and still the best Peranakan food you can find in Melaka. It has moved from it's original site along Jonker St. to the address above. I went to Jonker to search for it, and had to walk quite some distance to it's current location.Show less

Author: Peroni10Edinburgh, United Kingdom
Title: Yum Yum
Review: I'm a picky eater ( chilli n spicy is no good for me - wish it was). So, scanning the menu I'm thinking - eeeech - what can I have. Well, I did find something and had a very nice lunch. My partner doesn't suffer from my debilitating dietary dilemmas. She scanned the menu and tucked in. The place in really nice. Clean, spacious, think there may be an upstairs! We were the only 'tourists' in for lunch - that's a pretty good sign. Show less

Author: Yamuna G
Title: Not Fantastic
Review: I ate here 3 years ago, the taste and food quality was much better. Now I don't think so it's up to the standard. Expensive for the quality

Author: ackay2016
Title: Nonya
Review: Helpful staff at busy lunchtime.  Enjoyed traditional pernanakan chicken and duck dishes along with excellent fried rice.  Fresh mango juice a real treat.

Author: IvanT2882
Title: Nonya cuisine
Review: We have visited here more than 4 times and it has never disappointed us. One of the best dishes tried is the hee pew soup and ayam buah kulat which is very authentic and tasty. They serve delicious nonya dumplings, nice petai with shrimps. Just that the rengdang stew meat was not soft enough. It would have been perfect if rengdang dish beef was simmered over low flame for hours till tender. Other than that, the restaurant dishes are really of good standard! Highly recommended restaurant to dine in! Show less

Author: Echo C
Title: Average
Review: We are not the first time visit for this restaurant, compare to last time, the food is average only.

Author: Jinyu2015Singapore, Singapore
Title: Awful lunch-won't be back
Review: We were here on a company trip and Nancy's kitchen came highly recommended.There are 2 areas that made the lunch rather unbearable- and all 9 of us agree!Firstly the service : the waiter taking the order was really condescending. He also did not warn us that the portion for small serving was actually miniscule. We told him that we would be ordering many dishes so portions should be good. We didn't expect everything to come in tiny plates- the type Chinese restaurants use to serve peanuts. We intended to order more if the food was not enough anyway. But we didn't for the following reasons.Quality of food- at best, some of the dishes were mediocre, at worst really not palatable.The Babi buah keluak was the best of the lot- gravy was tasty but the pork was Super tough. It was served without the small spoons for the nuts, and we had to go to the counter to ask- then it took a Long while before the waiter brought the spoons by which time lunch for us was more than half way through. The sambal was watery and with hardly any taste of belacan - by the way the restaurant charge for a tiny saucer. Rather unusual given that sambal belacan is a staple in Peranakan dining.We also ordered a jug of lime juice @ 22 rm. other than the colour, it was so diluted there was hardly any taste of lime. I asked the waiter to taste the juice. After tasting it, he said it was diluted but it was not prepared by him.Maybe tourists not familiar with Peranakan food would not be able to tell the quality of cooking, but for us the lunch was such a let down.Show less

Author: modacostaSingapore, Singapore
Title: Crowded, small portion
Review: We came on a Saturday, it was a 20-30min wait for walk-ins. Food came fast after ordering. We had the Babi cencaluk (not bad but lots of oil), Ayam buah keluak and prawn petai. We had to pay extra rm2 per buah keluak and the dish is nice. Disappointed with the prawn petai, the sliced the petai to small pieces and lack ommph. Small portions. Show less

Author: Jeremylol
Title: Just ok
Review: Everything is ok, average, don't expect is traditional way to cook like home food. The cendol is tasty, with the mixture of fresh coconut milk and gula melaka

Author: Jing Ming GSingapore, Singapore
Title: Melaka's Famous Peranakan
Review: An hour wait for a decent meal. The meal was rather pricey, and there was a charge of $3 for the chilli. I really love the otak, and it was 10RM for a piece. Other dishes were good but certainly not worth the wait. I will agree to visit this restaurant if im around the vicinity but will not travel specially for it. The whole meal on the table cost around 134RM.Show less

Author: hiiong888Singapore, Singapore
Title: Nice nyonya food
Review: This restaurant open for lunch about 11am. Since we are around the area, we decide to drop by. We try the following dishes1. Bean paste chicken or "ayam pongteh"Ordinary bean paste chicken but slightly salty2. Shrimp omelete or "telur cincalok"The taste is quite standard. No special flavour. 3. Meatball with crab meat soup or "bak wan kepiting sup"Meatball taste nice while the soup have quite strong of bamboo shot smell. 4. Spring roll or "popiah"The difference with other popiah is the lard. 5. Fried squidOrdinary fried crispy squidOverall nice food, good service and reasonable quieing time.Show less

Author: GanLKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Must try the nyonya laksa
Review: Be prepare to q. After writing down your name on the waiting list, you would have to wait for the staff to inform you when is your turn to dine in. A must try is the nyonya laksa. The broth has a subtle sweetness and spiciness giving the laksa that unique tantalising taste. Have fun trying it. Another must try is the sek bak. After the meal, we bought five nyonya bak zhang to take home to try.Show less

Author: quincyl862
Title: Good food but slightly expensive
Review: We had our dinner there, waited for quite a while for our tables. The food is delicious however you need to wait for long time for foods to be served. Maybe we were there at the wrong time. Price is slightly expensive

Author: Enleng L
Title: Different cendol
Review: The cendol here is a little bit different, it's got a more santan taste and the Melaka sugar is not as thick as the others I tried. I would say the taste is more balance, with the very nice santan milky taste, and not too sweet, love the cendol here. But it really depends on each person's preference, my mom preferred the ones with a thicker Melaka sugar taste. Dishes here are nice too :) Price: not too pricey, we think it's reasonable. Show less

Author: YK TSingapore, Singapore
Title: Pricey Restaurant
Review: It is a very popular restaurant for many Singaporeans, but it is quite over-rated and expensive. I may be biased as I had tried the Nonya Restaurant in a nearby hotel, where they served their dishes with real, authentic and rich ingredients. Yummy.Perhaps, for the benefit of Nancy, the place was too crowded.There is ample parking behind the restaurant, and please book in advance before you come.Show less

Author: jwee92Singapore
Title: Authentic Nonya Food
Review: Nancy's Kitchen Restaurant is no longer located at Jonker Street (as shown in GPS map). Went in circles looking for it. They are now located at 13 13-1, 13-2, Jalan Kl 3/8, Taman Kota Laksamana, Seksyen 3, Melaka. They take online reservations. Glad to have found Nancy's which served authentic Nonya food. We had the Duck Salted Veg soup, Pai Tee, Spring Roll, Ngoh Hiang, Buah Kelua seeds, Bak Pongteh and Deep Fried Soft Shell Crab. All were delicious and home made. We had a satisfying meal at Nancy's. It was reasonable too. We will return again.Show less

Author: huetan
Title: Nice nyonya foods with reasonable price
Review: Crowded on Saturday dinner, we waited 40min for a table for 5 pax. The price is reasonable and the foods taste good. Must try kuih pie tee, nyonya laksa and cendol!

Author: LimJoey1996Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Nyonya Food
Review: This place have free parking. Preferable make the booking one day before dine in while public holiday due to personal experience have to wait 3 hours to dine in and fortunately my hotel just beside this shop so I can walk to beside check how many person I have to wait. If you no make the booking, you have to write down your name, contact number and number of person that will dine in on their queue list. They will call you once your turn to dine in. The taste of food just normal.Show less

Author: I8838OFannasJohor Bahru, Malaysia
Title: Still a local favourite
Review: Since moving out of the Jonker Street area, Nancy's Kitchen hasn't lost any of it's authentic local flavour and is as popular as ever. The babi pong teh is so good and the curry chicken has a nice kick to it. Worth the longer trip to have real Nyonya food!Show less

Author: mogadan
Title: Delicous food
Review:
probably there will be a line when you arrive, but the waiting is worth it! Delicious and affordable food, although I am not a local... Not that far away from the center.
In my opinion, worth trying!

Author: josephinec42
Title: Appropriately priced Peranakan food
Review: It was a short getaway for the family and we decided to have lunch due to it's reviews.Food was appropriately priced for it's portions. Be prepared to wait to be seated during peak hours without prior booking. Due to the crowd, we were seated on the 3rd floor. Not suitable for the elderly and disabled as it was quite a climb. The Fish in Tamarind Sauce is highly recommended. It was the highlight of our meal. The rest (Sweet Potato Leave Fried Belacan, Brinjal with Chilli, Sambal Zu sang Petai and Ngoh Hiang) were mediocre.Show less

Author: JennyY856
Title: Food so-so
Review: my family and I went on last Saturday. the food was far different from original peranakan taste. We ordered belacan kangkung, pongteh pork, cincalok egg and some other dishes. all tasted totally out, and was not cook by locals but foreigners. Foreigners doesn't know our nyonya food taste. my whole family is really disappointed with the food. we will never go again to this shop.Show less

Author: EuniceOngSingapore, Singapore
Title: Peranakan food
Review: We booked a lunch here in advance and headed here after exploring Jonker street in the day. It is a far and tiring walk, esp if it is midday and you walked the whole of Jonker street. Next time would recommend taking car, but cabs somehow weren't easy to find in Melaka. Go Grab or Uber. The restaurant isn't hard to find, use Google Maps. And obviously walk towards where the shops are all together you'll have higher chances of finding it. Good Peranakan food, their sotong was cooked till so soft! Recommend to try their Popiah too. They were out of kueh pie tee when we reached. After your meal i actually recommend stopping by Yeast Bakery just two shops (or one) down for some fantastic bread and pastry home.Show less

Author: Mervyn33Singapore, Singapore
Title: Day eating trip
Review: A day visit to Malacca town for good peranakan food and a little sightseeing and shopping around Malacca Jonker Street.Lunch was at Nancy's Kitchen at 13, Jalan KL 3/8, Taman Kota Laksamana, 75200 Melaka, Malaysia. Although the foods isn't quite what my grandma cooking is but it is still acceptable.We had the Fish maw soup, Ayam buah keluak ..(my granny gravy is slightly thicker even my wife version is slightly better) is still ok. We had some Popiah and Ngoh Hiang.Small restaurant with efficient service and we end the meal with some chendol, overall everyone enjoyed the meal.This is the first time our friends from England tried Peranakan food and they enjoyed it.Show less

Author: AlbertwcsBrisbane, Australia
Title: Good nyonya food, prepare for a long wait without reservation a day ahead
Review: If you do not have a reservation (only allow to take reservation one day in advance), be prepared for a long wait for seats. We went there during lunch hour, around 12 noon, and the place was already packed. We were lucky that our waiting time was cut short to only about 30 minutes, as compared to what was told (1 hour at least). Also, it is about 5-7 mins drive from Jonker Street depending on traffic conditions. Plenty of parking lots around the restaurant. The food was good. I recommend to try their otak-otak, the sambal kankung, chilli sotong, and the chicken curry. The other dishes we had were only average ( soft shell crabs, pork curry, ngoh hiang). Show less

Author: salini01Petaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Don't waste your time
Review: Seriously, don't bother wasting your time queuing up just cause of the hype. This place is just too overrated. 2 years ago this place was actually quite okay, the food was good too. Now, sucks so bad. First, you have to wait approximately 20 to 30 minutes. Then when the food arrives, it's not even hot plus the food is just so so. If you realize, the locals wouldn't have their meal here.Show less

Author: Oon_mac
Title: Worth a visit!
Review: A little way off the normal tourist trail but well worth a visit. Very busy on a Saturday night but I only had to wait about 15mins for a table. I had the chicken rendang, acar and Ngog Hiang, all of which were delicious and fresh. Service was fast despite how busy they were.Show less

Author: 343elainelPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Never a disappointment
Review: My all time favourite for nyonya food. They have moved to bigger and newer shop. 10 min from jonker. Do go early to avoid long queue. Kedondong juice is saviour in the typical hot day in Malaysia. Tamarind pork , cencaluk omelette and nyonya curry chicken is a must try! Show less

Author: ANG-POHAIMINSingapore, Singapore
Title: Utterly Disappointing Melaka's Nancy's Kitchen Nonya Food
Review: Terribly overrated Nonya food.The male host was impolite and arrogant. Made customers feel unwelcome. Waitress lacks finesse and slams bowls on table while serving. Can't find the X-factor in any of the dishes. We ordered many dishes - 9 to be exact, for only 3 of us, as we were upbeat to wanna try as many dishes as possible. None of the recommended dishes we ordered were good - they were in fact below average.1. Only angel bean (四角豆）with chilli belachan was a tad nicer than the rest of the dishes. 2. Basic Nonya staples like Chap Chye (mixed vegetables) was not cooked sufficiently and the vegetable was still hard and raw. Lacks basic umami. My maid's home cooked one tasted and smelled better. It should have been cooked soft and tasty. 3. Babi Pongteh (Kong Bak) did not have the right cut of pork and was far too tough. Lacks umami.4. Chicken rendang was really so-so at best. 5. Coconut Prawn Curry was normal. Taste was kind of flat.6. Otah was like run of the mill. No fragrance nor texture. My frozen Kukop otah tastes way better.7. Fishmaw Meatball soup has funny smell... meatball was so-so and fishball was worst than market fare... not springy or tasty at all.8. Ngoh Hiang was far too starchy ... only thing nice was the accompanying Chilli sauce. 9. Fried egg with prawns was just normal that you would expect from any Restaurant.10. Chendol concoction was not balanced - too sweet with too much Gula Melaka and insufficient coconut. Lacks fragrance!Honestly, I have never been to a more overrated restaurant than this. Most of the 9 dishes we had were basically below average. The best part of the meal was the chilli sauce for the Ngoh Hiang. No joke! Show less

Author: MELAKABAGUS
Title: GOOD NONYA FOOD.
Review:
As the saying goes, if there is a queue outside the restaurant, the food must be good.

This is very true for Nancy's kitchen. The food IS good.

Price wise, mid-range. However, considering the quality, it is worth the wait and price though.

Author: Kelly NSingapore
Title: Decent Nyoya Food restaurant and we will be back again.
Review: Went there first time last Friday around 8pm. Registered our name and waited approx. 15-20 minutes (considered fast) and ordered 4 dishes. We are quite satisfied with the food and service. The staff is polite and the utensils are cleaned. Overall the dishes are yummy can be better as the portion is small. One thing I don't like is we have to pay for the sambal. Comfortable place for makan. Will return again.Show less

Author: jackie_a007Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Long Wait for Poor Food
Review: We tried this restaurant on the recommendation of a friend who assured us that this is a MUST TRY in Melaka. The wait was inexplicably long - over one hour - and this restaurant has three floors to accommodate patrons! The food was so underwhelming however because we were hungry from the long wait, we ate it all up to fill our grumbling tummies. Everything was bland, dumbed down (to please the palates of foreigners, I presume) and tasteless. Nancy let us down. Most restaurants in Melaka flourish because of the hype and the standard of food diminishes almost immediately after they become famous. Not worth the wait and not worth the money.Show less

Author: Winston1831Singapore
Title: First visit
Review: The place popular to the local and tourist. Need to wait about an hour before get a table. We need to write out name to get a table ( which is ridiculous). Some items we ordered was salty and some is not tasty. Maybe due to the crowd on that day which they need to rush thru the cooking. Show less

Author: KhooyeoSingapore
Title: Lunch
Review: Waited about 1 hour on a Monday afternoon. I would say their standard of food has dropped. The Beef rendang was too tough same as the pork rib bua keras. The cendol is worst than those bought from the street. Would not recommend to come here. Show less

Author: KiddySing
Title: Quality Nonya Food
Review: I think everyone will have their opinion about good Nonya food, but haven't eaten in hundreds of such places, I must say that their food is really good and authentic. Despite the restaurant being full, service was adequate. I would eat here again.

Author: ngofamSingapore, Singapore
Title: Crowded but below expectations
Review: This place you need advanced booking otherwise you might have to wait for 1 hr to get a seat during peak hours. The food choices were like the menu in their own premises. The meat dish with 'bucalak' was tough(probably not cooked Long enough). The chicken dish was covered with a layer of oil and saltish. Keep to the usual fare. When crowded you have patrons standing just next to you. Could have been better. Won't be returning. Below expectations.Show less

Author: Geraldine S
Title: Let down
Review: The food was such a let down, over ratedAssam Nanas Udang - the portion is small, prawns not top quality Chicken Buah Keluak - doesn't comes with the nut, have to order separately. I was looking forward for the nut but was disappointed, not fragrant compared to those I ate at Amy Heritage and Suan. Fried Egg Cincalok - just regular omelette Fried Bee Hoon - worst dish of allDeep Fried Fish with Chilli - the fresh water fish is tasteless. Am sure there are better authentic Peranakan food in Melaka. Not worth my calories. Show less

Author: DavidK9699
Title: Poor service
Review: Went there this evening 11/6/17 , food was quite good . Ambience was great !! However service staff was rather poor . No advice whether food order was sufficient or too much . When asked why our Brinjal , Boiled Ladies Finger and Cincalok Ulam came rather late , the rude and curt reply was that it was a late additional order . Yes , the only late order was the Cincalok Ulam , and actually plus the F Fish SO , however the rest were ordered earlier . I think they must have forgotten about the veggies, and they came only when the rest of the dishes were almost finished !! Thereafter this particular slim lady staff with a baseball cap (Carol) gave a rather sulky face and attitude and didn't even say " thank you" or " goodbye " , let alone apologise for the delay . What a lousy experience and I certainly won't go back there despite the rather ok dishes . Show less

Author: arvinAWDSingapore, Singapore
Title: Amazing Nonya Cuisine
Review: The food is simply delicious. Served fast and hot. My Favourite has to be the braised pork. If you are planning to head there, do make a reservation online. It gets really crowded and you got to wait. Apart from that great service and affordable food. Will definitely return back. 10min walk from Jonker street. You may try Uber to get there too.Show less

Author: stanleynguSan Sa Ho, Vietnam
Title: Best nyonya food
Review: We were pleasantly surprised with the quality of the food ...I give top marks to to the salted vege duck soup...buah keluau is very special (ate it for the first time) ....was expecting more cincalok taste in the egg omelette though...best nyonya food we had nevertheless Show less

Author: alj_travelsTucson, Arizona
Title: Fine food, touristy atmosphere
Review: Enjoyed a lunch here in May. As a vegetarian, the Nyonya cuisine doesn't leave me many options, but my husband had a great time trying some of the local Melaka dishes. The operation is professional, full of tourists. It was highlighted in our Lonely Planet guidebook and I imagine the operation has benefited from this mention. There is a fun shop with spices, pastries, and other items to take home, as well.The food itself is fine, though not memorable. I'm not sure how it is better or worse than another of the other Nyonya restaurants in Melaka, but it has a touristy vibe that can make it a fun spot to stop for lunch, if you're in the area. Show less

Author: TayJ_12Singapore, Singapore
Title: Cheap and good authentic nyonya fare
Review: It was lucky I made a reservation before heading down as there were long queues outside the restaurant at 6pm. Food came pretty fast and it was delicious. Total bill for 4 pax came up to about 100RM, which is really affordable considering we ordered so many dishes. Will recommend others to give it a try when visiting malacca. Show less

Author: Grace WKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Decent meal
Review: We ordered stir-fried sweet potato leaves, otak-otak, fishballs & veggie soup, chicken pongteh, egg omelet cincalok and chap chai (mixed veggie). It was just okay for me. Portion was just nice for 5 adults and 3 young teens. The kedondong and lemon tea juices were nice. Show less

Author: JoshShoeString
Title: Decent Peranakan dishes
Review: Decent Peranakan dishes. Pong Teh and Chap Chai are pretty good. Jug of juice without ice is thick. Portion a bit small.

Author: eeynis13Johor Bahru, Malaysia
Title: Quite okay Peranakan food selection
Review: We got this place from the tourist guide book and decided to try it out since it was on the way out to the highway. It had said to make reservations ahead of time but we wanted to test our luck since it was way past lunch hour around 3.30pm. The restaurant had arranged its tables quite close to one another so we were lucky that we were there when it was not so crowded but the spices used to cook the food left an odour in the sitting area. The menu was extensive and we ordered a few signature Peranakan dishes like the "achar" and "babi ponteh". The food was satisfactory.Show less

Author: AsianWorldTravellerSingapore, Singapore
Title: Very cramp & crowded,food average
Review: Went on a wednesday afternoon around 1pm and there was a queue outside.Had to register and the wait was about half hour.Inside the restaurant was very small with only about 7-8 tables.Smaller tables sitting 2-3 people at the side and 2 big round tables in the center.Off to the side was where you could buy their snacks and dumplings which made the whole place really cramp.Typical peranakan food on the menu.If you cannot take spicy better let the order taker know.Food quality was average nothing special.Personally it was just to cramped and crowded to have a pleasant meal.Show less

Author: Letranger90Hong Kong, China
Title: Excellent Peranakan food, get there early
Review: We were lucky to get here early: patient crowds (something less common in Malaysia than in Hong Kong or New York) waited to have the excellent Peranakan food at Nancy's. Far superior to some of what you'll get in Singapore or KL, the value too is outstanding: more than we could eat for RM100 (about USD25) I've reviewed Amy's here very favorably: don't visit Melaka without eating at one of these two restaurants.Show less

Author: AussieMahoBrisbane, Australia
Title: Traditional Malay Food
Review: It was such a privilege to eat lunch at Nancy's Kitchen. Located away from the main tourist areas, it was a refreshing surprise when our private tour guide took us here instead of to one of the standard tour food troughs that we had experienced on other group tours.My garlic allergy was easily catered for and the level of heat in the food was modified to our western pallet. The flavours of the spices rang through and we enjoyed everything we tried. In particular I can recommend the prawn dish and the chicken curry. Make sure you leave room for the local dessert cendol. It was delicious! Show less

Author: 201kamhIpoh, Malaysia
Title: Nyonya dishes with reasonable price
Review: My first time experience for traditional Nyonya food. I was Queuing up for more than an hour for my lunch. The fish was fresh, the food taste good. I have ordered 2 Cendrol, 2 popiah, 1 asam fish, 1 Nyonya curry chicken, fried pork ball, prawn omelette and 1 jar of Chinese tea. It cost meRM125.00+. I recommend those who want to go for a try call up and make a reservation to avoid long queues in front of the shop under the hot sun.Show less

Author: happypeople888
Title: Standing strong !
Review: Nancy Kitchen has been around for ages. Their food taste better at the old location. They are now at new location near the Swan Garden Hotel. Reservation highly recommended. It is always packed during weekend.

Author: sheyengKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Food was good but the waitress have zero knowledge on the serving portion
Review: Went there with 7 friends and got a quiet table on the highest floor which is nice cuz me made reservations. Have no idea which food on the menu is good so can only order randomly. Asked the auntie that helped us take order about what portion of the dishes we should order for 8 person but she say she not sure about that. Ask her about the jug of herbal tea can serve how many person she also say she don't know. We ordered their famous rendang chicken which was really nice but the portion served is for 2 ppl only ‍♀️ every dishes portion also damn small cuz the person who took our order doesn't know how to estimate the portion to serve. Overall they do serve good nyonya food just the quality of the workers have to be improve. Show less

Author: DavieOngSeletar Hills, Singapore
Title: Authentic Nyonya Food in Melaka
Review: Had an authentic Nyonya lunch on a Sunday at this highly recommended restaurant while touring Malacca recently. It was crowded and you need to call one day in advance for booking.The prices were reasonable but portions were small, but served us well since we have 5 ladies and 2 men. Advisable to order more varieties and don't forget to order the Nyonya deserts (eg. Chen-dol).Nancy's Kitchen is located about 3-5 km from city centre, therefore if you do not drive, call a Taxi.Show less

Author: Jane G
Title: FAMILY LUNCH
Review: We poppped in for lunch while shoppping. we did have to wait a while but this was fine. the food was cheap and cheerful but it is hardly a restaurant more a cafe.

Author: AlvinLah
Title: Good Food
Review: Had a good dinner at the restaurant.  Ordered, Babi Ponteh, jackfruit curry, potato leaf fried with sambal balachan and ayam bua keras and chendol.  Also bought 1 bak chang which tasted good.

Author: Cindy K
Title: Good food
Review: Very good food as reviewed by others. Had to wait 50 mins though, but it wasn't unpleasant as we sat in the cafe on the same row while waiting. Price was very reasonable as well.

Author: Flyn1170
Title: Delicious and Reasonable
Review:
Overall delicious dishes and very reasonable pricing. Enjoyed the pie tee and tamarind pork dish. Pork was not fatty which suited us. 

There was also delicious nonya kueh and cookies. I would return for good Peranakan food when in Melaka.

Author: teok870Bangkok, Thailand
Title: Lunch
Review: Thought we were going to be eating good peranakan food judging from queue. Very disappointed by cooking standards. Maybe expectations a bit too high. Bakwan kepiting and fish maw soup from similar stock. Avoid. Chap Chye too sweet and Assam pork dish too dry when using pork loinOverall will not recommend Show less

Author: Dianakpg
Title: Very Reasonable Pricing
Review:
They serve very delicious Nyonya food. Service was fast and friendly.

The cendol is very authentic. Real gula melaka was used.

But do be there early to avoid having to wait for a table. They have sitting upstairs too.

Author: Tyem32
Title: Nice atmosphere but food is average
Review:
Precook food. Food are serve cold. Not hot. Expensive.
Taste is average. Restaurant setting and atmosphere is comfortable.

Author: Tang L
Title: New setup with old taste
Review: Baba & Nyonya foods available in new shop lot... check out the cendol and dodol, don't forget to check out their local snacks...

Author: Lai Y
Title: Not bad
Review: We love the pai tee and chicken candlenut. The black nut pork ribs is so so. Overall food is not bad but its not a 'must do'.

Author: GlenT870London, United Kingdom
Title: Good Nyonya meal, bit far from town
Review: We had lunch at Nancy's Kitchen when we were in Melaka back in February. This busy local restaurant is little hard to find, located a good walk out of the tourist area in town, with seating upatairs as well as downatairs. We tried the Candlenut chicken, Nyonya fried rice and pork in tamarind sauce, which week all very nice. A very nice lunch out and about.Show less

Author: 905chual
Title: Peranakan food
Review: Decent Peranakan food. But food became cold very quickly shortly after being served. Crowded restaurant. Abit far to walk from city centre.

Author: Vooth
Title: Authentic Nonya Restaurant
Review: tried their various signature dishes, all tastes great! Truly authentic nonya dishes, do go and patronise.

Author: toledocupraSingapore, Singapore
Title: Spicy food
Review: Most of the food here are spicy and relatively decent. Price is reasonable as well and not expensive. Nancy the boss is a good and friendly woman who knows how to make the customer happy. Good place to try Nyonya food though there are better alternatives in malacca. Service and nancys welcoming response to customers deserves a thumbs up!Show less

Author: YX_657Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Okay
Review: I'm not sure if it's because of what we order but it wasn't very satisfying. We had the otak, Assam prawns, fried chicken roll (Ngo Huang), curry vegetables, cincalok omelette. It came up to 70 something ringgit. Including drinks and some crackers. The curry vegetables were good but the rest of the dishes was just satisfactory. Overall, Makko is better. Show less

Author: ferrymulSingapore
Title: Very good Nonya food and quick service
Review: We were there for lunch hours, and expecting long queue, it turned out to be not so bad at all (average waiting of 30 mins). We got table at 2nd floor for 4 people. The food are heavenly, all the items we chose, are very good. Try the buah keluak, it was not bitter at all. The grass jelly was refreshing. The ngoh hiang was also good. The squid is heavenly. The service is fast, and easy ..Show less

Author: C3451ZUmichaelt
Title: Lunch at Nancy's
Review:
Was exited to come again to have a good meal. Today lunch was disappointing. Hee Piou Soup / Assam Nanas Prawn was too saltish. Prawns is not fresh. Sambal Belachan is so so. 
It seems Nancy's is over rated. Won't be back again.

Author: Mike TManchester, United Kingdom
Title: Nancy's is NICE
Review: Many may say 'food is better' elsewhere.
