Maybe so, but I have found out each time i have been to Nancy's.. its MORE than just the food (which I rate highly) its the atmosphere, the service, the general ambiance as well as the truly friendly staff and owners that make this place my first place of call... AND because it has now moved from next to Jonker to Kota Laksamana, (only 5 minutes walk away) it is also almost next door to my other fave - the Sun May Hiong Satay House.... DOUBLE PLEASUREShow less

Author: stefiney
Title: Amazing Poh Piah
Review: I had, Meat Roll, Poh Piah and Curry Chicken. Among all I enjoyed the Poh Piah the most, it was different from the usual I had. However Curry Chicken was a little too spicy for my liking.

Author: peace20294265
Title: Food is average, nothing to crow about
Review:
The place is always crowded but the food is actually so  so. Nothing spectacular.
Don't know why people are raving about this place. Can find better and cheaper food elsewhere.

Author: ericchay
Title: Family lunch
Review: The foods in Nancy restaurant is fairly OK for me, potion is small and the location for the restaurant is abit out from the city. The space inside not big so is abit squeezy if you come in a big group. It will be better if u can make a reservation before heading down.Show less

Author: SumitaKristinP
Title: Yummy
Review: Baba nyonya food. They have relocated but I remember when they were at main street of Jonker. Recommend this anytime. And price worthy. Keep it going but keep it authentic pls. We lack of it.

Author: Keith V
Title: Not in Jonker Walk
Review: Note that this has moved away from Jonker Walk in Melaka! The food is delicious and worth the effort to find. As a tourist in Melaka, the place was not easy to locate on foot. However, once I found it and tasted the food, it was well-worth it. Everything I tried was delicious, recommended by Nancy herself whom I met. The restaurant space is very unassuming. Highly recommended for Peranakan food.Show less

Author: DivyaLeeSingapore, Singapore
Title: Worth the calories intake !
Review: Really must make reservation in advance otherwise waste hours sitting outside for a table.Service was average, took a while before we got our orders taken cos there appears to be only one order taker at that level (we were parked at level 2), I could be wrong... Anyway we ordered a variety of dishes but these are the must orders from my personal opinion - kueh pie tee, babi pongteh, chendol, Nonya dumpling We also had the Ngoh Hiang that was served with this Chili sauce which was so good I had to buy some home. Go down to the ground level and ask Nancy or whoever is at the counter for the Ngoh Hiang Chili sauce !!! Will definitely be back at Nancy's kitchen ! Show less

Author: Vinnyau
Title: Authentic Peranakan Food
Review: Food is great and service is prompt. Only problem is sometimes is can get crowded and queues are long. Go early to avoid the queue. Finish off with some nice Cendol which is damn awesome. Ample parking available.

Author: Audrey T
Title: Cosy Peranakan restaurant, good for family
Review: Our 2nd time to Melaka & Nancy's Kitchen. A must-go as they serve traditional Peranakan comfort food.Nancy's Kitchen open at 11am & we made sure to reach about 10min before to be one of the first in the queue. If you arrive past 11.30am, the service staff may inform you that the wait may take 45min for the 1st round of patrons to clear.Show less

Author: kareneng84
Title: Nice food
Review: Must try when you in Malacca. The food was yummy and the restaurant always full.   We went during lunch time and waited for 45 minutes as we need a big table.

Author: iwantgoodfoodnow
Title: Nice kueh pie tee and cincaluk omelette
Review: Friendly staff and boss. Tried the lady's finger and chicken with tamarind too which was average. Chicken didn't feel very cooked and willing recooked it. Many cookies and chilli for sale

Author: Michael LSingapore, Singapore
Title: Over-rated; Average at best.
Review: We occupied a large table for 12 and I must say service was prompt. The food, however, was disappointing considering the many good reviews I read about it in various websites and blogs. In my opinion, Nancy's Kitchen is grossly over-rated.Every dish (8 in all) is not bad but mediocre at best. None of the dishes excited me but we finished the food mainly because we were all hungry.Show less

Author: LittleLatteKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Nice Nyonya food!
Review: Better environment with more tables after they moved to the new location (not in jonker walk anymore). I preferred ground floor sitting as the ventilation on above floors are not very good as I smell fried oil surrounding the area at that time. The food are so good and prices are so affordable. They even sell some nyonya delicacies at the cashier counter and Nancy were there to explain to everyone who ask her any question about the food and ways to cook. Show less

Author: dominico789Hong Kong, China
Title: Food and services were average
Review: We followed the visitors recommendation to search this restaurant. To ensure getting a table, we arrived 10 minutes before its open hours. It was a bit disappointed that the dishes arrived too slow and not hot. The taste was so and so. However, the restaurant was full with customers queuing outside. As a whole, I considered this restaurant was overrated from tourist information web.Show less

Author: Chun C
Title: Slightly overrated
Review: Decently good food.Slightly overrated and price were average but a place with great ambience and no harm giving it a try.

Author: pigletress
Title: Honestly, bad.. I
Review:
This place is not a good introduction to peranakan food. Sucky and overpriced! Total tourist trap.

Love my peranakan cuisine but can't believe these jokers can call themselves that serving bad food. So no go there unless you want to be disappointed.

Author: Clement Yi Chen... CSingapore, Singapore
Title: Not the best nonya food, and relatively poor service standards
Review: Called 5 days to a week in advance to book a big table to sit 16 persons. Person over the phone agreed to the reservation and the seating arrangements. However upon arrival, they said there no such seating available and we either had to settle for what they have, or leave. Pretty bad customer service I would say. I've been to a number of nonya restaurants and Nancy's Kitchen is by far the least authentic. Probably contrary to the many that have said otherwise, Nancy's kitchen is really nothing to shout about. The buah keluak dishes are so-so in terms of taste - probably more dark soya sauce than anything else. Even more surprising to me was the fact that there were additional charges if I wanted buah keluak in the dish. This is probably the strangest thing and I would only reckon that the restaurant wants to make a quick buck of it. Imagine you having to pay extra for chicken to be added to your rice.The fish otah while meaty, was small in portion and it was lost in its own spice so much so that if you're not a fan of chili, you will probably be downing glasses of water instead. Pongteh dishes were so-so. The chup-chye actually tasted like mixed cabbage. The only saving grace is the chendol, which was delectable to a good extent and just the right amount of sweetness.Show less

Author: EittusSingapore, Singapore
Title: Great food! Please make reservations.
Review: We came by late as we did not know that they have shifted and we went to the wrong place. We had to wait for half an hour for the next table. The guy was nice enough to offer us a table. He gave several other walk in before us as we were late. It is reasonable. Food is great. Dishes are reasonably sized. Not too large or small. One of the better peranankan food around. I will come back again!Show less

Author: jerhewsMorschach, Switzerland
Title: Tasty Eurasian Portuguese Gourmet
Review: Nice set-up and rather friendly place.Good suggestions from staff concerning what to eat. Food from mild to spicy to hot. You can place your request according to your taste buds. Just fire away your orders. Very cooperative. Also recommended though the prices of some dishes are quite expensive. Still worth a try!Show less

Author: Baking_Love
Title: Authentic Nyonya
Review: Loving the food offering at this delightful place and be sure to try the pork leg, popiah, boil okra, steam seabass and many more. The sambal is rocking at this joint including the homemade Chang and pineapple tarts.

Author: ZzzhiyiiiSingapore, Singapore
Title: Good nonya food
Review: Traditional nonya food, which is tasty. The restaurants also sells traditional snacks where you can walk in to buy. Tried a few of it and they are definitely worth it. However, each person is only entitled to one cup of plain water and cannot be refilled. Restaurant has a weird smell too.Show less

Author: thinesdino88
Title: Great food
Review: We went around 4.20pm and thought they going to say kitchen is close but actually they entertain us and was very friendly. The food was good , had a nice classic late lunch

Author: Tene17
Title: Best Nyonya Food!
Review: I highly recommend this restaurant to those who wish to try authentic nyonya food in Malacca... Tried the 'Nyonya Chicken', 'Ladyfingers/okra', 'Assam Fish', 'Mixed Vege', 'Assam Pork' and also Mango Juice. Loved the 'Assam Pork'! Price is totally worth it. We went as a family of 5 pax and the total price was about Rm140.Show less

Author: hcaaliew
Title: LOST IT'S AUTHENTICITY
Review: This was my 3rd visit to the restaurant and I am very disappointed with the quality and authenticity of the food. The Nyonya Popiah is not authentic at all and the food in general does not give justice to the real Melaka Peranakan food.

Author: wxyztraveller
Title: Quality of food is average
Review:
Read about the good reviews and was curious to try out the food.

The restaurant is quite out of the way.

The taste of the food is not extraordinary.

Will not visit again.

Author: DrRubenMalaysia
Title: Melaka Peranakan food at its best
Review: Brought to this restaurant as we are in a wedding entourage. Walked into this bustling establishment and we noticed the pleasant Peranakan ambiance this place has. We were seated at the upper floor, the place is clean and nice. Staff are quick, attentive and friendly as well. The pricing here is fair, but justified with the outstanding authentic Peranakan food. Dish portions are adequate (had about 12 people on the table and it was sufficient). Sotong sambal is a must-try, absolutely delicious and the squid is fresh and not rubbery. The fish curry was lovely and the chicken rending did hit the spot for sure. Other dishes were decent and good as well. Reservations might be needed as this place is always crowded.Show less

Author: Andonjt
Title: Arrived at the last minute
Review: We came a long way from jonker by foot. Long walk with a bag full of purchases and arrived at the restaurant on the last final minute (they close early on weekdays at 5pm). They did not turn us away and waited patiently for our orders. However, I felt the food was a little overrated. They taste nice but not as what I would have expected.Show less

Author: lfyloh
Title: Last customer
Review: Even though we walked in at 9.29 pm they still serve us & inform us last called we need to order what we want. We called pork ponteh, cincalok omelet, duck soup & chicken curry we really enjoyed our food.

Author: pinkgingerbread
Title: Delicious beyond words
Review: We chanced upon this restaurant as it was close to the hotel that we were staying it. Ordered the black nut chicken (ayam buah keluak) and it was sooo delicious!! The pricing was also fairly reasonable and will definitely go again next time.

Author: hannah3107
Title: Good Food and Service
Review:
We did not book and waited in a queue.  Staff really friendly and good food.  
Excellent Chendol and sweet potato crackers

Author: ChooMichaelSingapore, Singapore
Title: Nice Nyonya food in Malacca
Review: It is one of the place we visit when we are in town. Some of the food we usually order are the kueh pie tee, Sayur Loday, Curry Chicken and finish off with Chengdol (its a must)Always busy place, please do your reservation via their website before visitShow less

Author: 2loveN2travel
Title: Make your reservations before going there!
Review: Service is good but there are too many people so do not expect too much. Food is average.  Waiters and waitresses are friendly and helpful.

Author: ivorysingaporeSingapore, Singapore
Title: Decent nyona fare if you are too lazy to cook
Review: Went there with a bunch of ladies who grew up on Peranakan fare and we found it passable. Jackfruit dish was nice but your traditional ayam buah keluak was pathetic, even after taking into account the very reasonable price of RM2 a nut. I like the sambal egg omlette but the chincalok omelette was wanting as can't really taste the chincalok. Kachang Botol and ladies fingers were nice. Popiah and ngoh hiang average..... you can never please Peranakan taste buds that always prefer home cooked cuisine.... even Violet Oon doesn't pass our standards! Show less

Author: TeikBoon C
Title: Still a Melaka Favourite
Review: After sharing notes with some of my buddies I brought them to Nancy's to compare with what they have been accustomed to at the other Nyonya style restaurants. My friends were all impressed with Nancy's offering for lunch and looks like the other places have lost some of their customers. This place serves pork as should any authentic nyonay restaurant. My favourite thing about Nancy's is the sale of the coolies and kuih-kuih on the side. We had some angku kuih and kuih kochi as appetisers. Their kuih bangkit is better-than-sex good.This location now can cater to more customers but it pays to be there before noon as the crowd builds up. Even with a dining hall upstairs, it filled up quickly and by the time we finished and left, there was a long line outside the door.Show less

Author: LeeWJ
Title: average nyonya dishes
Review: Nothing much stick in my memory. In the end, the dishes here felt like any other Chinese dishes (but with Nyonya name to it) rather than having a distinct Nyonya taste to them. However, dining here is comfortable with ample parking lots.

Author: bnicealex
Title: Unexpencted
Review:
We called for reservation but they ask us to walk in, luckily available sits for us. 
Foods is fine, must try pork in tamarind and curry chicken.

Author: VthyaKPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Average tasting and very crowded!
Review: If you are looking for authentic nyonya cuisine, i would say my experience at Amy's Heritage is better than here, maybe perhaps coz i went over a logn weekend but the corwd was horrendous,i made early reservation , went early , was told to return 10minutes before reserved time. Service was good and fast. Very accomodating as i requested for chicken porridge to be prepared before i reached, and they were able to do that. but taste wise,we had their prawn masak lemak nanas, i found it to be bland... there was no sweet,sour or spice... just plenty of turmeric and chilly blended. and we ordered the prawn asam... too much asam,. too thick....but their glutionus rice was really nice and must try! Show less

Author: meimeic626Singapore, Singapore
Title: Don't ever visit this place
Review: Waited 30 min but food didn't come so went to the counter to check and was told the kitchen didn't have our order and must re-order again. Nancy's kitchen moved to a new and larger premises but quality of food was compromised. The old Nancy's Kitchen was better than the new one. Sad...Show less

Author: MarkMcG1956Singapore, Singapore
Title: Disappointed
Review: Ok, it was a Sunday and after waitimg 45 minutes for our table when the dishes arrived the flavours ranged from wow to disappointing.The signature chicken with candlenut was tasty but more bones than meat. Sambal prawns were delicious, fried squid perfect and so so ota. Overall, just above average. Since she moved to her new premises, locals we spoke to say that quality has given way to quantity( of customers). Show less

Author: augustinweeSingapore, Singapore
Title: Good Quality and Quantity, yummy!
Review: Was lucky to pop by for lunch without any appointment made, and manage to get a table for 5 adults! Friendly boss, wonderful foods with good quality and quantity, especially the Asam-fish, not too spicy and sour; ngo-hiam delicious yum yum and chendol for dessert. reasonable price too.Show less

Author: shiroatkl
Title: Average
Review: Went for lunch (packed with people), waited about 20minutes for table. Menu is attractive with lots of choices. We had the 4 angle beans with sambal (just average taste but with fresh prawns), pai tee is flavourful, assam prawn and ayam pongteh taste.

Author: Travelfather59Petaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Overrated
Review: Long queue, waited for almost an hour for a table and after all this ...food just average. This place is certainly overated. Not the kind of food experience you want after an hour wait. We ordered, the nonya fish curry, chicken debel, assam prawns, chap chai, belacan four angled beans, vegetable curry, fried eggs, pie tee cups and popia. The fish was very fresh and would rate this as the best dish. The pie tee cups and popia was also very good. and the rest were down the hill. we left the chicken debel untouched after trying one piece. Chap chai was an insult to nonya cooking. Assam prawns was good flavour spoilt by the low quality prawns (the kind that disintegrates in your mouth because it is not fresh) and four angle beans very average.I was tempted to give this place a poor rating, but maybe it was just the overwhelming crowd that affected the quality of cooking but then again good restaurants have the reputation of being consistent.Show less

Author: mcrulu
Title: Must Eat When In Melaka
Review: When in Melaka city, you must try squeeze Nancy's Kitchen into your To-Eat-List! It's a quaint restaurant in Kota Laksamana offering amazing BabaNyonya/Peranakan food. You will not regret it, and if you are lucky, you might even see "Nancy of Nancy's Kitchen" herself sitting around the restaurant! Some food suggestions: Top Hats (pai tee), Bak Buah Keluak (pork rib with black nut), Fried Prawn Tamarind (Udang Goreng Assam) and the mixed vege (chap choi).Show less

Author: Tay TMelaka, Malaysia
Title: Bad experience and not friendly
Review: I booked on Wednesday for Sunday lunch 1.30. They have taken down my name and phone number by repeating to me and make doubly sure . When reached there at 1.30 Sunday , was told not in their booking system and very unfriendly . Their food not the best in town ,but the attitude will chase customer away .Show less

Author: bridgetp355
Title: Not bad
Review:
The only paranakan place tried in malacca. Thus can't really compare. Quite crowded. Better to make reservation online. Overall food is nice and reasonably pricing. Oneh oneh is good.
Restroom is clean. But tiny flies around dining area.

Author: Evonne T
Title: Authetic Peranakan Cruisine
Review: Nice cosy restaurant serving Peranakan delights. Serving size is small and reasonably priced. Ordered popiah, laska mee, grilled fish, chicken curry and chendol. Delicious with good level of spiciness. Prompt service. Has free wifi and clean toilet. Restaurant also sells Peranakan cookies.

Author: Shiva197710Klang, Malaysia
Title: Worth the wait
Review: I normally do not wait in queue for having my meals but decided to give it a try since their cendol rated one of the best in Malacca.You need to write your name, phone num, no. of person is some sort of a log book.They will give you a ring once a table is ready for you to sit. That isn't too bad then. Alternatively, you also can reserve in advance ( I think is one day earlier).I went there without a reservation, logged my name around 1.15pm, they called me around 1.45 and food was served around 2.05pm.Nice food and as expected, the cendol was yummy and tho, busy and packed, it was a nice environment to hang out. Price is still acceptable for the taste and do check out the prices on the menu before you order especially on those items which labelled "Follow market price".There are plenty of parking lots available, so do not worry about getting a parking there. Will go there again when visiting Malacca.Show less

Author: SanfordCheeSingapore, Singapore
Title: Standards have dropped
Review: Since shifting to a new location, Nancy has not maintained the same standards that have made it famous. The Laksa was disappointing, almost bland and a poor contrast to other places. I would recommend trying the laksa at Calanthe Art Cafe instead.The petai and prawn dish was also disappointing, small beans of petai and shrimps that weren't fresh.There are much better Peranankan/Nonya restaurants around. I would recommend trying Samfu at Hotel Mimosa or Seri Nyonya at Equatorial Hotel. Check out Rebecca Saw's blog on Melaka Nyonya food recommendations they are more spot on. Not worth going out of the way to Nancy's Kitchen to taste food that are past their glory days.Show less

Author: ZacharyMarret
Title: Excellent Peranakan food
Review: I had a really good lunch here. Peranakan-style chicken, popiah, and rice, with some fresh cendol for dessert. The main courses were all hot, flavourful, and delicious, while the cendol was icy and smooth just like it should be. Very much enjoyed the meal overall.

Author: DoreenLoo
Title: Good food, go early!
Review:
Loved the sambal prawns with petai, the pork balls and pie tee!

Price wise: mid range. 3 of us, 6 dishes with dessert, bill came up to slightly over RM100. Service was fast and efficient.

Author: taifookchiaKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Malacca Nyonya Restaurant
Review: Be prepare for the long queue. It may be a good idea to send a buddy to stand in the queue at least 30 mins before your group come in.Once you get a table to sit down your frustration for waiting will be behind your mind. The menu is filled with all variety of authentic Nyonya dishes and the waiter or waitress is ever ready to recommend their specialties and give a brief description of the dishes. The food will be on the table very fast to compensate for the long waiting time. I like the dishes are served in small portion so you can sample a great varieties of dishes. I find most dishes tasty and price is reasonable.For serious gourmet you may need several visits to form a fair opinion on the taste and authenticity of these Nyonya food.I definitely will give it a second try when in Malacca.Show less

Author: wshaprMelaka, Malaysia
Title: Recommended Nyonya Food
Review: As a Malaccan, I normally will not visit the tourist famous restaurant due to long queue and normally the price is much higher. Well, my family and I visited this place at 11 am where other nearby restaurants still yet to open for business PLUS my friend has been mentioning this restaurant due to its famous and delicious nyonya "zhang". There were a few tables when we entered the restaurant instead of long queue outside the main door. Normally, long queue started at 12pm. To my surprise, the price is very reasonable and we also notice some dishes are different and not able to be found from other Nyonya restaurants in Melaka which we are the frequent nyonya food seeker in Melaka. I love its Petai Prawn where it is not as extremely spicy but, the taste is asam with light spicy. What a delicious dish. We also ordered some non-spicy dishes due to our small kid in the family. Further to that, we didn't wait for long on the food serving after our ordering. This is really a worth place to try out the Nyonya food. However, you may need to reach there before 12pm.BShow less

Author: 234keetSingapore, Singapore
Title: Spicy spicy
Review: Arrived 1058 am just in time for their opening at 11 am. Great timing as there isn't queue. By time were done and leaving the queue was at least 5 tables wait. In my opinion it's too spicy for personal an cuisine. The taste was great and intense but way way too spicy. Great pricing and was surprised actually. Fair ! Will be back but didn't think it's worth the queue!Show less

Author: francis_61jbSingapore, Singapore
Title: Good food. Appropriate pricing
Review: As my title suggest, it's good food with appropriate pricing. I will not say that the food is excessively excellent. It was crowded when we went. Just have to register in the queue book. Food-wise. It was comparable to another nyonya restaurant we patronised a day earlier. We had "curry chicken" - taste 'clean' as any curry dish - above average (only). Egg cincaluk was bland with hardly a cincaluk taste.Cendol. Fail in this area again when compared to our prior experience. Red beans are those small ones unlike the soft big red beans in ABC.Chang. The special meat n egg type at RM8.50 was a big Big BIg BIG disappointment. It's not about the pricing. If any of you are chang fans, happen to be in JB, I will introduce you to the best ba-chang in JB, some say in Malaysia and some even say - best in the world.Show less

Author: Stella LSingapore, Singapore
Title: Delicious Peranakan food
Review: If it's crowded, jus need to register your name at the Q book and wait to be called by the waiter. We did not wait for a long time even though it was a Sat night, people just know the queuing system. Food was served fast and it was really really good. Peranakan cooking was different from the usual Chinese cooking. Must try. Price was very reasonable with 3 dishes for about RM50. Show less

Author: zhihongtoh
Title: Decent Nyonya food
Review: Whole family decided to dine here for dinner. Food was good with friendly staff. The chicken rendang is a must try!

Author: R6511QXdavidcBandar Penawar, Malaysia
Title: Good and affordable nonya food
Review: This restaurant has moved out of Jonker Street to a nearby location that requires 15 mins of walk from Jonker Street itself. It was about 7pm for us so the walk was fine. You can find on Google Map and just follow the directions. The food was not expensive and came in small servings. It was good for me as I can order several dishes and still get some desserts.The food is good and I will return the next time I visit Malacca.Show less

Author: DebbieSeowMalaysia
Title: Overrated Restaurant
Review: I heard so much of this nyonya restaurant. And finally I manage to give a try in this trip. But the taste was a bit disappointed as it is overrated. They do selling some nyonya kuih and rice dumpling. We order an Assam Pedas fish, fried kangkung, ngor hiang (meat roll), Portuguese curry chicken and a glutinous rice dumpling (bak chang). The tastes of the dishes are so so. But the bak chang is really yummy. Show less

Author: jeiwongKajang, Malaysia
Title: Delicious and reasonable price
Review: I like nyoya style dishes, spicy but yummy. Nancy's Kitchen is one of our choice when we visit Malacca. There are quite a number of specialty that you must try(you can ask the waiter as I can't remember the name of the dishes).If you visit during weekend or public holiday, kindly call for reservation.Show less

Author: vodkakurant
Title: Average food
Review:
We had a few dishes and found it average.  Location was easy to find.  Parking was convenient too.

Table reservations preferred.

I'm sure there are better nonya restaurants in malacca.

Author: aboozieMumbai, India
Title: Need a huge tummy
Review: We tried this place based on my wife's insistence and boy was in for such a treat, we tried a few dishes as the whole menu is too elaborate and this was one of the yummiest meals I had in Malaysia - Nyonya cuisine. The popiah hats are a must try. We ordered some 4 dishes and each was brilliant. Show less

Author: Maria Z
Title: one of famous Baba Nyonya in Melaka
Review: I brought my friends to Nancy Kitchen, u need to queqe outside while inside full, better nextime call for reservation 1st

Author: BalGill81Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Wonderful little spot
Review: Found this restaurant by chance, apparently the ori spot was somewhere at jonkers and this is a new outlet. I wanted to have my other half try out the nyonya peranakan dishes,I was vegetarian and was prepared to just have rice with cili padi but to my surprise, the waitress was so accommodating and agreed to have the vegetables fried without any meat or belachan. They even the popiah vegetarian friendly and I could not be happier!Tried their pineapple tarts and angku Kuih which can be purchased from the ground floor. Both were good. Point to note, if you are sitting upstairs, get the Kuih on your way up or you might need to come down again as its self service.The only down point for me was that upon entering the restaurant, I could see the tables were all taken and it seemed to us there was no where to sit. No one greeted us, and we were prepared to leave until I saw a staircase on the right hand of the shop. Curiosity got the better if me and we went up and accidentally found the first floor seating space. Come again? For the food,Yes. Next round when I'm not on vegetarian diet! That pongteh chicken lookin mighty good.Show less

Author: Tsb_foodhunter
Title: Nothing special here.many nyonya betters in the town
Review: I listen many times about that in this place you will find the best nyonya food in the city. But this is no true The food is very poor and low in quality. No fresh ingredients. Bad and no taste. No representative for the real nyonya food. Only mix ingridients and add spiceThe place is small hot and noisy and also need clean properly. very difficult for the people walk there if are in the historical area.If you want try the autentic nyonya food please look for other restorant. We never come back.Show less

Author: 207aur_lienm
Title: Good place  (recommended to book table  before coming )
Review:
Good baba nyona food which is a mix of Chinese and Malay food 

I recommend to book your table in advance. Otherwise you may have to queue for 30 minutes

Author: moderntraveler16Seoul, South Korea
Title: Good Food,but needs better service
Review: Good peranakan food, but last 2 times we went there was always things sold out. Disappointing for my mum because she specifically went there for things like the Kueh Pie Tie and it was sold out, we also wanted another gravy dish, but was sold out, and the balutlut drink which my mum liked was also sold out. The staff was not even apologetic. Just said, no more. Sold out.Not sure if we were just unlucky, or did they under order/ or staff stressed, but they are leaving guests unhappy as we have to settle for other food options.Show less

Author: firerooster2009Singapore, Singapore
Title: Yummy
Review: Though it was a Monday, my group of 8 managed to get a table for lunch at 1pm. Shortly after we sat down, there was a queue forming outside the door.Service was efficient and friendly in spite of the crowd. We could eat at comfortable pace, without being hurried.It would have been less stressful if we could make a reservation and be assured of a place.Food was yummy and the portions were sufficient.It was definitely very affordable.Show less

Author: Sherlyn T
Title: Best Nyonya with reasonable price
Review: Trying this nyonya food for the second time and the food is still delicious. Visited once on last June, and I waited for the long queue as it was on weekend and they only accept walk in customers. So this trip, I went there once they open at 11am. This trip I came with my friends, 5 of us ordered their Peranakan curry chicken, fried egg with cinchalok, beancurd with pork, brinjal with chilly,cucumber pork salad with a fried rice and cendol. All are small size and the portions are just nice for 5 of us. The price is also reasonable as it only cost us RM65 with so many dishes. Tried their kuih is also mouth watering especially their ondeh-ondeh is my favourite.Go early to avoid the long queue and is actually worth to queue :)Show less

Author: ConradthorpeArona, Spain
Title: Fantastic
Review: When we found the restaurant there were people waiting outside. You have to go in and register to wait for a table. They told us approximately how long we would have to wait and it wasn't long. The atmosphere inside is quite noisy as there were a couple of large parties in and the kitchen is open. The food is great and the staff were friendly, knowledgeable and efficient.Show less

Author: RobyRadi
Title: Weekend in Malacca
Review: Good local food, very cheap, better to book in advance to avoid a long queue. We went without any reservation we had to wait for 30 min but it was worth it

Author: janicek0hSingapore, Singapore
Title: Nonya Dumpling spoiled
Review: I arrived the shop at 11am and I discovered that the nonya dumpling is delivered by a outsource vendor.This is not the first time I bout the dumpling and the taste is okay but am disappointed to discover that it is not made by Nancy's Kitchen itself.I open 1 dumpling at 11:45 to taste, it is spoiled. I check the rest, all spoiled. It has developed spider like sticky thingy!!!I am disgusted and dump all of them!!!Show less

Author: vampiirec
Title: Not bad
Review: My boyfriend and I ordered otak-otak, fried rice, four-season beans and fried mee. The otak-otak is very nice, others is ok, but the fried rice is not my cup of tea and the beans are spicy. The price is affordable, for the food is below RM50. Will go back again !Show less

Author: DDPCLManchester, United Kingdom
Title: Fantastic family treat
Review: Dropped in at Nancy's Kitchen on the outskirts of Malacca Town Centre, for a simple traditional Nyonya dinner. Being a semi-Baba (Nyonya) myself, found the food authentic and really delicious. Setting of the restaurant is also markedly Nyonya/ Baba. Strongly recommended for anyone trying out traditional Nyonya dishes, one of Malaccan treasuresShow less

Author: samanthas792Singapore, Singapore
Title: Poor in nyonya taste
Review: I have tasted many better nyonya food before. I would not recommend this restaurant at all. The only item that can worth mentioning to probably the otak otak. I will only give 4/10 in terms of taste. Sambal petai was watery, petai still rawBabi poteh - pork meat was hard & dryAssam chicken - salty Ayam buah keluak - just passed the tasteChap chye - fail presentation & colour of the dish, doesn't taste nyonya chap chye.Show less

Author: poopshooterPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: home cooked comfort...
Review: Been hearing about this place and finally tried it over the weekend. The restaurant itself looks rather crowded with tables close to each other, the cashier & goodies counter. They have a 2nd floor but we didn't go up to check it out. Open kitchen concept. Service is pretty good, friendly.We went after peak lunch so we got a table easily. With 6 of us we ordered quite a bit. We had the Hokkien Chang, Nyonya Chang, Lor Bak, Pork w/ Cincaluk, Dabel Curry Chicken, Asam Fish, Duck with Salted Vegetable Soup & Four Angle Bean Fried Belacan. All of them were on point & packed full of flavor. Decent portions as well. Washed it all down with 2 jugs of strong Chinese tea. It didn't end there as we went for some dessert - Onde-Onde, Seri Muka & cendol. Again they were rich in flavor & done right.I've tried close to 6 Nyonya places in Melaka and I have to say Nancy is #1 in my books. It can be a bit of a wait during peak times but well worth it. Prices are slightly high but so is all the other Nyonya joints. Highly recommended!Show less

Author: Halcyon_FlowersSingapore, Singapore
Title: Yummy food
Review: A friend wanted to buy the kee zhang from there so we decided to have lunch there. Our party of 8 had all the usual Nonya favourites like Ayam Buah Keluak, Babi pongteh, Chap Chye, Cincalok Egg, otak otak stim - all quite delicious.We have also eaten at Kochik Kitchen and Amy's but we think Nancy's is way better in terms of taste.We only tried Nancy's ondeh ondeh but weren't impressed.Instead go next door to Yeast Bakery. Very delicious and interesting buns and cakes; especially the Japanese-style light cheese cake. A wonderful sweet end to a good meal.Show less

Author: Baileys_Travel27Singapore, Singapore
Title: Not as good as before....
Review: Nancy's Kitchen relocated from Jonkers Walk to the current place. It's quite a walk from Casa del Rio hotel. You may choose to take the cab if you want.There were at least 7 other groups on the waiting list ahead of us. Waited for almost half an hour before we get a table on the second floor. Ordered a few dishes, the only ones worth mentioning are perhaps fried rice and cendol. I've tried Nancy's Kitchen years back, food then were tasty!If you really want to enjoy good Peranakan food, I believe you are able to find them within Jonkers Walk rather then travelling all the way to Nancy's Kitchen and still wasting time to queue.Show less

Author: yss97
Title: Good Peranakan food
Review: The pie tee, popiah, chicken curry, sotong (cuttlefish) curry & asam fish were excellent. The other dishes were ok - prawn & pineapple curry, duck with tamarind, kangkong belacan. Overall, an enjoyable meal at a reasonable price (compared to city prices).

Author: Mintie LKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Home cook style Nyonya food
Review: Like the bak asam (Tamarind pork ), really enhance your appetite. however the fried vege is way too spicy (although i really love spicy food, but this is a bit too spicy for vegetable).Overall it just simple home cook style dish here, nothing fantastic, but the 'ang koo kuih' (turtle look nyonya traditional cake/kuih) sell at the cashier are quite nice, not too sweet and the skin is just right. If you like nyonya home cook food, here it is, nothing fancy. But it would be very pack if you come at lunch, cause they close at 5pm.Show less

Author: laosiz
Title: Over rated
Review: Sad to say that the place is over rated. The Nonya laksa tasted more like curry laksa. The fried meehoon was over powered by the garlic. The mee goreng was no better. However the queue doesn't seem to stop at lunch time.

Author: onenah
Title: Average Peranakan cuisine
Review:
A wide variety of Peranakan dishes in the menu. Taste was average and was much too spicy (at least for my liking). 
The gem we found was the ondeh ondeh (local dessert). It was very fresh, soft and had full flavor of gula melaka.

Author: Irene_HYP
Title: Authentic Peranakan Restaurant
Review: Omg..... their foods nice & yummy!!!! This is my first time tried Peranakan foods with my hubby we loveeee it so much. Must try their cendol, nice too!!!!

Author: Karan KSingapore, Singapore
Title: Lovely Nonya selection
Review: We decided to walk there from Jonker, which took us approximately 20mins. We arrived around 2pm, lucky for us, the lunch crowd was dispersing so we didn't have to wait long to get seated.We ordered a Nonya Laksa, Popiah, chicken rendang, kangkong, salted veg and duck soup, hokkien dumpling and nonya dumpling for 2 to share. Paid about RM85 for a very hearty lunch.We love everything, especially the popiah and the nonya dumpling.Show less

Author: Jackie_NMLSingapore, Singapore
Title: Can eat but not super good!
Review: I went there with my friends in June. Due to holiday season, we waited an hour for the table and another 15-30min for food despite we gave our order in advance.My friends highly recommended this restaurant over Makko. However, after the meal and we went to Makko another day, our conclusion is their standard had dropped. I personally prefer Makko over Nancy's. Not sure if it is because they had expanded and couldn't cope with the crowd surge hence quality being compromised.Of cos that particular day that we went, we also heard from the staff that 2 of the staffs r on MC hence short handed. We ordered quite a fair bit. I particularly love their Kueh Pai Tee & Acar Pork. Other dishes were so so only. Overall the experience is ok only. However due to so many good reviews from various ones, I don't mind giving another chance if I'm in town again just to make sure that my experience wasn't as fantastic as others due to short handed.Show less

Author: Bee4
Title: Very small but popular place for Nonya food and cakes etc.
Review: We always pop in to NK for a tasty meal when we visit Melaka.  Rather cramped and sometimes too full of patrons to get a table when we want one, but well worth trying.  Pineapple tarts and other nonya treats are Nancy's speciality and irresistable!

Author: Gavin_MarieGold Coast, Australia
Title: The Best Nyonya Food In Melaka
Review: In our four day quest to sample authentic Peranakan food Nancy's come out the best by far. It is about a 30min walk from the Jonker St area but well worth it and would be a cheap ride in a taxi. If you would rather not wait for a table then arrive early as this little gem is very popular with the locals.The staff were cheery and efficient and the food was excellent and full of flavor. They even talked us into a dessert which is a rarity for us and it was well worth it as it finished off the meal brilliantly.Show less

Author: InnekeHSingapore, Singapore
Title: yummy nyonya food, a bit far from jonker area
Review: The location is quite far from Jonker area, need to walk 30-40 mins.Once you reach, register by writing your name in waiting list/paper located inside the entrance door.The staff will call your name once table is available.This restaurant is very crowded.We ordered pai tee, babi pongteh, ayam buah keluwak,kangkung belacan, kedondong juice, ice cincau, mango juice. They charge for each keluwak for 2 ringgit.Pai tee is fantastic, must order. Babi pongteh and ayam buah keluwak is tasty and kangkung belacan is fragrant and mild spicy. Overall, it's a very yummy dishes. We spent 120 ringgit for 4 people.Show less

Author: pitcher723Melbourne, Australia
Title: peranakan restaurant in melaka
Review: this place is one of the peranakan style restaurant that is available in melaka. possibly very crowded, so expect longer waiting time during peak hours; but they have free wifi. food is more or less done in peranakan style; chicken/pork pongteh, laksa, nyonya cang, cendol, pineapple tart and some kuih are also available. non halal food are served. the room is full aircon.Show less

Author: MistressofbooksMuar, Malaysia
Title: Give this place a miss if you can
Review: In the past whenever we think of 'nyonya popiah', Nancy's Kitchen comes to mind. That was in the good old days before the present premises.It is not worth waiting for the popiah that we ordered as takeaway - a great disappointment when we went home to eat. It is not authentic anymore. There is no sweet sauce spread on the popiah skin; no cucumber strips and instead of omelette we find chunks of scrambled eggs. The worst part is the yam bean filling is so very salty. Nancy's kitchen has sacrificed quality for quantity. We saw foreign workers in the kitchen and this place has become too commercialized.Show less

Author: jiamajumotorsdnbhd
Title: Good food deserve
Review: 11.00am open. 10.30am already long que. good food deserve your waiting. Go support and try to get surprise tongue taste. This is real Makanan Peranakan Tempatan!

Author: soule24Singapore, Singapore
Title: Besides the affordability, there are better nyonya places elsewhere....
Review: Nancy used to be crowded when at Jonker, and I would expect the same at this new location given the strong name. Granted the food is good, but it is typical nyonya fare that you can get elsewhere. Service is nonexistent - you can stand right in the middle of the restaurant and the staff don't give a hoot. I would advise to try better nyonya food elsewhere.. I have a good recommendation that is near Jonker.Show less

Author: MummyBluesSingapore, Singapore
Title: Long queue, average food ... Sigh! It used to be good ...
Review: Each time I visited Malacca, I will surely come here for a meal. Perhaps it has been a really really long time or my memory failed me but this recent visit didn't give me a WOW experience. First of all, reservation require 24hours advance booking. You can reserve using their online portal (where you will receive a confirmation email) or call them. If you are coming with big group, it's best to call even earlier as space is limited (mostly 4-6 pax per table although I do see them joining a few square tables to make room for 10pax). Their new location is considered far from their old address at Jonker Street. Plenty of parking spaces located in front of their restaurant. Plus point of this new place is that it is more spacious & offered more tables since it serve two levels now. Ah ... about the food ... I was expecting much more particularly after reading their wonderful review. Firstly, we ordered Pork Buah Keluak (black nut) ... it came with bits of pork rib but no nut. After we ask the waiter, he told us we gotta order separately. I was dumbfounded. The waiter taking the order didn't even bother to ask us if we want the nut or not. Honestly, if I don't want the nut, I might as well ordered stew Pork rib. Anyway, it's my fault for not reading the menu carefully. Next was the "Chap Chai" (mixed vegetable). Sigh! Frankly it was just a plate of fried cabbage w bits of black fungus & tau-ki. There is no taste of the 豆酱bean sauce. This is definitely not Nyonya dish at all. For the salted duck soup .... oh, it is far too salty for our liking. Considering this soup was my all time favorite, I only took a couple spoonful. Utterly disappointed.In short, Nancy's Kitchen should taste all their dishes they served & work towards bringing back the authentic favors of Nyonya cuisine. Show less

Author: karla m
Title: taste so good
Review: this was recommended to us as well and is only a 15 min walk away from our hotel, i didnt know anything about nyonya cooking so we tried it and it was great.. they give big portions of food and it comes really cheap..

Author: Tan WKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: A Crowded Nyonya Restaurant
Review: The atmosphere of this restaurant is quite good, the food is good. There are alot variety of foods. The Cendol is good also (better than Jonker street). You can bought their pineapple tarts here. It will be more better than those pineapple tart selling in Jonker Street. We arrive at the time they start their business, but they already have a long queue. So better do reservation before you visit.Show less

Author: bkobogSingapore, Singapore
Title: one of our favourite Peranakan meals
Review: We dropped by Nancy's kitchen at 11am (when they opened) as we did not have any reservations. In no time, the restaurant was packed and we were fortunate to have our seats. This is a good sign.We wanted to order the top hat but it was not available. quite a bummer as we have read amazing reviews of this dish.We ordered few dishes for our young family with 3 kids and had them with rice.One of our favourite dishes was the Chicken with Tamarind sauce. It is well marinated and the flavour of tamarind is evident but not overpowering.We also ordered the Otah Otah. This was a "common" snack in Singapore. Yet, with the drizzled lime juice, there is a spicy but sour punch which I thought was an ideal combination of taste. This went down very well with the rice.We also ordered the nongya dumpling, It was really pretty and had a dash of blue "colouring" on part of dumpling. The filling of meat is tasty, moist and sweet. The rice was sticky but not too hard. thus, it was a nice version of the dumpling we were familiar with.Before we left, we bought some snacks. Some of them are really delicious and the kids fought to finish the last bits. the popular ones include: kueh koic, bahulu, oneh oneh.This was one of the our best peranakan dining experiences thus far and given a chance, we will return again. The slight down side is the presence of housefly. In the middle of the level 1 dining room, we had to move from the 2nd table to the one closest to the door due to the "cold drift" coming from the aircon unit.Show less

Author: gabrielt198
Title: Good food but terrible hygiene.
Review: Nancy's kitchen does served one of the better Nonya food around and is always one of the stop to make whenever i go to Malacca, but unfortunately, i might have to rethink my choice for the next trip. The whole restaurant and i do mean the whole restaurant was infested with flies. They are simply everywhere and impossible to remove. Flypaper thats filled with flies are left all around. I really hope they do something about it.Show less

Author: kennlaicPuchong, Malaysia
Title: Price not cheap if refer to the portion of foods
Review: During public holidays & weekends -: - advise to book the place before enjoy your diner , cause it long long Q to wait Food quality -: - taste as normal nyoya foods - " sotong cooked with petai sambal" was taste good Price -: - price not cheap if refer to the portion of foods , especially "prawn cooked with pineapple" & "achar" Show less

Author: iceblended
Title: Excellent food
Review:
Dinner with friends and it was about 20 mins walk from Jonker St.

Complimentary Wifi was available.

A range of nonya snacks and kaya were available for sale and it was good!

Author: C33kSingapore
Title: Disappointing Experience
Review: This is my 2nd-3rd visit and the standard has dipped. The food is probably still acceptable for those who are new to Peranakan food but definitely will receive a few frowns from most Peranakans.Ordered chap Chye. It was more 'fried cabbage', the greens of the cabbage were still visible, the stock was not flavourful.The Ayam Buah keluak was a totally failure. The buah keluak was sweet! Like really sweet! The Ayam was probably cooked separately from the nut thus lacking in the rich unique taste of the nut in the gravy.The bakwan Kepiting was overwhelmed by the bamboo shoot 'stench'. An unfortunate word to be used to describe one of my favourite soup. We left most of the Babi assam goreng untouched because of the 'porky smell' from the pork belly. The pork was probably not very fresh. The Nonya Chang was also a far cry from what it used to taste. Not as fragrant and some rice grains were also not cooked. Show less

Author: Rororo97
Title: Nyonya Dumplings
Review: bought nyonya dumplings to take away as there was a long q.. it was superb!! recommend to buy their dumplings RM 5-RM7

Author: AcuraMelody
Title: Disappointed
Review: I have been to Melaka for few times & heard good review about Nancy kitchen hence we decided to try! We order paitee, asam fillet fish, braised pork & also cincaluk egg. Their paitee is awesome taste good. The fish is not fresh & you can know it was taken from freezer where is soft. The egg is salty & the braided pork is cold when they serve. I will not return to the restaurant Show less

Author: LAYLIANT
Title: Overated
Review:
Male and female boss disappeared. You know who cooked or not? 外劳
Veggie over cooked. Samba prawn are cooked only prawn and onion without sambal. I also don,t know can get ranking numbers 12. Must be never tasted no ha food.

Author: rhasvin
Title: Could do with better service
Review: First impression was that the food had to be good as there was a long queue of people waiting to be seated. Everyone had to register their names and number of pax in order to be seated. We arrived on a Sunday, at 12pm, and the waiting time was over 30 minutes. Initial thoughts on the place, it had a nice environment, truly capturing the heritage of Malacca. However, the experience soon turned unfriendly when we were greeted by their staff. They looked overwhelmed by the sheer number of visitors waiting for a table, communication from them on the whole process was nothing short of dissatisfactory. There was no place for those waiting for a table to wait. Everyone crowded the entrance, and there was no one to greet or assist us. When we finally got hold of one staff member, we asked how long we had to wait for a table, we were given a rude response; "you wait, we will call you." And then he walked away. That itself was enough to dissuade me from returning. There was no courtesy nor was there an apology. We decided to leave for some place else. Shame that we didn't get to try out the food. It did look tempting. Perhaps they should have a professional and courteous staff member to handle customers at the registration, as well as a proper waiting area for those on the waiting list. People take time out of their trip, coming from far to try out their offering, so it's sad when they don't get the chance to do so.Show less

Author: louis899Vancouver, Canada
Title: New location but food just as good.
Review: Visited restaurant when it was in Jonker Street area.It is now located at its present premises at Taman Kota Laksamana, a three storey building.We ordered pork chincalu, fried turnip,pai tee ,steamed fish with chilli paste,otak otak and popiah.For drinks I had sour sap and the others lime juice.The pork was a little salty.The rest of the food was delicious and leaves you no doubt why it is one of the best Nyonya restaurant with Peranakan food & cakes.For dessert I ordered chendol which was great !Go early as queues form at lunch/dinner hours.Better still call them to book and order your food.Ample public car parking lots.Just buy parking coupons from outlets like convenience shops,news vendors.Staff very friendly and efficient. Brochure indicated that Kitchen also conducts cooking classes.Opening hours :11am to 5 pm ( Sunday,Monday,Wednesday & Thursday) 11am to 9pm ( Friday,Saturday & public holidays)Show less

Author: MAHA24
Title: Great food!
Review: Chicken rendang to die for!!! A must try! good food with reasonable price. had trouble locating the place as they had relocated from the address that is listed in the website.

Author: Grace WSingapore, Singapore
Title: Most disappointing
Review: The last time I visited Nancy's Kitchen was when they were in their old premises. They always had long lines outside their restaurant then. Now, they have moved to a spanking new place. The hotel staff advised us to make a reservation a day in advance, and we did. It was a Saturday and we were there for dinner expecting a long line. Strangely, not only was there no queue but they had tables for walk ins as well. We ordered Pie Tee, Ngoh Hiang, Chilli Prawns, Tamarind Prawns and plain rice. The Pie Tee was all right but not terribly delicious. The filling was too wet and Pie Tee shells not exactly fresh and crispy. The Ngoh Hiang was soggy and simply unappealing. The Chilli Prawns were flavourful enough but there were only about 6 or 7 small prawns on the plate. The Tamarind Prawns tasted just like the name, prawns fried in tamarind sauce. Nothing spectacular. All the food especially the Ngoh Hiang tasted like they had been heated in the microwave. Even the sambal belachan which should accompany the food had to be paid for at RM3. The chillies were very coarsely pounded and the dish was more seeds than sambal. Perhaps it's because we didn't order the recommended dishes but I was really disappointed with this restaurant because it's supposedly one of the most famous in Malacca.Show less

Author: yichingy2016
Title: Lovely food at reasonable price
Review: Must try their popiah! completely different to the usual popiah available! Nyonya chap chai and assam fish were excellent as well!

Author: Janice_Kanda
Title: Awesome Food
Review: Came here without reservation, luckily they accommodate us. We ordered a few dishes with rice and Chinese tea. The portion of the dishes were adequate. The taste was really good. Affordable and satisfied.

Author: jacfaadKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: The food is not worth the queue or waiting list, disappointing.
Review: We were Google'ing for good food to eat in Malacca. And we came across the blog - Top 17 food in Melaka so we decided on Nancy's Kitchen. Judging by the queue and the waiting list of the restaurant, we were excited for the food ^^ plus we were hungry!We ordered what most people have on their table. Ayam Rendang (was just normal), Popiah (is bad, skin is dry and the content inside is just blah), Pork Bean Paste (nothing to shout about), Omelette, Mix Vegetable (looks like from yesterday's dish, not fresh at all) & Ondeh-Ondeh. Presentation is bad. Taste is not up to a "queue up" restaurant standard. Verdict walking out the restaurant: It is a very disappointing experience. Show less

Author: FonglinMuar, Malaysia
Title: Gone was the good old taste
Review: I always make it a point to dine at Nancy's whenever I am in Melaka. Few months back, I brought some friends there and ordered popiah. It was a disappointment. The popiahs were full of garlic and it tasted terrible. It was so different from the days they were at the old placeShow less

Author: Sandeep_AujlaIpoh, Malaysia
Title: Overrated tourist trap.
Review: As with most hyped establishments, over time, the qualities that got them the fame would slowly fade if not managed well. This is the case, I suspect with Nancy's. Service was good, waited in line for about half and hour due the popularity and was seated promptly once a table was vacated. Hungry and excited, we were let down by the food though. Of the 5 dishes we ordered, only the otak2 starter stood out. The dishes we ordered were mainstay Nyonya food, Like the chicken rendang and Assam pedas fish. It looked more like an oil slick off the Melaka straits! So oily! And the taste was nothing to shout about .. I've had better n that's a guarantee. The Kang Kung belacan was simple and for the price not worth it. Any regular Chinese corner shop could whip that up for half the price. For all the hype , it was an utter disappointment. I regard this establishment as a tourist trap. Never will I recommend this place to anyone heading to Melaka. There are better options out there... Show less

Author: DylanAndrewMartinKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: True Heritage Food
Review: Nancy's is a must for any Malacca itinerary. On a weekday lunch we still had to sit upstairs as the place was full, but one doesn't really go to Nancy's kitchen for the decor and atmosphere anyway — you go for the food. We had heard a lot about the restaurant and so tried a number of dishes with a large plate of rice to share and were certainly not let down. Fantastic food, every dish was a taste experience.Show less

Author: DaleSG
Title: Nothing fantastic
Review: My partner and I find the food here average. Only dish that we thought was good is the chicken buah kaluak

Author: C3451ZUmichaeltVoesendorf, Austria
Title: Went back to try at their new location
Review: Was so exited to go back again to eat at Nancy's. When there early, place was nice & big. Time to order our foods. But was disappointed with the foods that we ordered. Felt that they didn't maintain their food quality as at the old place. Disappointed after tasting the food. Uncertain if we are coming back for more. Show less

Author: Jeannie C
Title: Order a larger Rendang Chicken
Review: Went at 3pm, seated at 4pm. It's a very popular place for Peranakan food.Ordered Rendang chicken, tapioca leaves with sambal, prawns omelette, eggplant with belacan & Mee goreng. Total was RM 68.55 with 4 drinks & rice. The small size Rendang chicken was really small. The rest of the dishes had better portion.Would love to return again in my next trip to try the other dishes. Show less

Author: celine_sernlinSingapore, Singapore
Title: Could be better
Review: My husband and I drove from out of state to Malacca specifically to have Nyonya food. I must say that this restaurant has charm and the waiters were friendly. We ordered chicken rendang, fried rice, pai tee, and eggplant (all small portions). While the food was really good, I was surprised that the bill came up to RM60. A little bit on the high side, considering it's not in Jonker Street or anything. Second thing that bothered me a little was that the lady boss seemed to only want to talk to "certain people". When she saw me raising my hand, she didn't bother to come. Rather, she sent someone to us (note: she wasn't busy doing something at that time). For a restaurant of that size, a little personal touch wouldn't hurt.Show less

Author: andyfromsouthamptonSingapore, Singapore
Title: Would give this six stars
Review: This is undoubtably the tastiest restaurant we visited in Melaka. The prices were reasonable and the waiters very friendly. The location is a bit out of the city now, but worth the walk. Now to the food. It was a veritable exploration and explosion of the flavours of the region. Ginger, chilli, shrimp, peanut. All great examples. I would take every visitors to Melaka here, without any hesitation. I rarely write such one sided reviews, but this deserves the accolade. I would recommend the fish in ginger and garlic, and any of the shrimp dishes. Excellent Show less

Author: mj18_12Seremban, Malaysia
Title: Good nyonya food
Review: Reasonably priced good nyonya food was what we got here. Amazingly we managed to get our seats pretty fast compared to the long list of people who came after us. It's better to book this place if you wish to dine here. Pongteh pork and nyonya fish were very sumptuous. I did not like the popiah here, could get better ones back in my hometown of seremban. Fried egg with cincalok was a below average dish. However I would really recommend this place to newcomers!Show less

Author: andrewjkwong
Title: Very good Nyonya food
Review: Have been to this restaurant several times, since when it was on Jonker Street. Restaurant is usually packed, and a must try when anyone comes to Melaka for Nyonya food. Nyonya chang, babi pongteh and cendol are my favourites.

Author: 1john316Singapore, Singapore
Title: Recommended for Peranakan Food
Review: We visited this restaurant when it was in the heritage area of Melaka in June 2013. This was our first visit in their new location. It is a much better place with ample parking and the ambience of the restaurant is good. As usual, it was crowded with customers indicating that it is still a popular place for authentic Peranakan food. We ordered popiah, kueh pietie, chap chai, fried meehoon, plum lime juice and cendol. They were all delicious. We especially like the plum lime juice and cendol. Be prepared to join the queue and wait patiently for your turn. They also sell all kinds of nonya desserts and chang. We bought and tried the nonya chang. It was good.Show less

Author: Low Z
Title: Relocated
Review: Nancy kitchen relocated. No longer at jonker street, would need to drive here. I like their Popiah, you get your lard but not too much and overwhelming. Nyonya laska not very good. Too much coconut milk and too much noodles, just kill your stomach space... The ngoh hiang was good!! Must try. I don't like the Bak Chang, nothing fanciful and I think my mom does better Bak Chang. The pineapple tart not recommended. Too much dry flour with little pineapple inside. Will be back again for the Popiah :) and maybe for dinner and not breakfast.Show less

Author: IHeise14
Title: Good Nyonya Food
Review: Stopped in here for lunch on a Saturday. It was very busy, but worth the wait. The popiah and pork sausage here were some of the best we've had.

Author: Lwailin
Title: Gula Malacca Cendol is really good
Review: Ordered a few dishes for dinner. overall food rating is average but the cendol is good. Service is good too :-)

Author: BenjaminYap427Selangor, Malaysia
Title: Nice food
Review: Not bad for this place, food was nice, once you had your food, there is kuih, to bring back to your family.Suggested that go in pair, or call in for booking 1 hour earlier.I was lucky that i went with my gf, there is table for 2. Those who reach with family of 4 and above need to wait 40 minute.Show less

Author: Cassfu
Title: Must try baba Nyonya food in Melaka
Review: Best baba Nyonya food in Melaka. Went there twice during our stay. Do ask for recommendations from the order taker. He provides great suggestions. Don't forget to save room for Chendol and buy some Nyonya kuih to go. They can also call a cab for you if you need one. A must try in Melaka!Show less

Author: sianhianooiAdelaide, Australia
Title: Again all the hype!
Review: Tourist trap to say the least. Honestly very diluted dishes and commercialization has taken over. Trying to do volume crowds the food becomes "fast food quality. Service is bad. Attitude and arrogant staffs. Time to shake the wheel and tell netizens to post honest writings. Tourist trap giving innocent travellers the wrong indications. Place is not well cleaned and cluttered with unsightly matters. Imagine it's a food joint. ..how in earth did they pass health inspections.Show less

Author: andybian
Title: Popiah & Ngoh Hang really good
Review: Ordered few dishes for lunch. Popiah, fried fish spring onion sauce, curry chicken has thick curry sauce, fishball soup is so so, mix veg, fried egg with Chinchalok is unique. The best best is the Ngoh Hiang.

Author: seafare74
Title: Many Dishes were Finished Early
Review: The service was friendly and the dishes we tried were alright but we were disappointed that many of their speciality dishes had sold out by mid-afternoon.

Author: F KSingapore, Singapore
Title: Best peranakan food ever
Review: Conversations die when you eat at Nancy's kitchen. You will simply indulge in the delicious food that is both very tasty and refined. The taste of the food will linger in your mouth long after you swallowed it. Be prepared to stand in line because this restaurant is very popular. But, it is worth it.Show less

Author: rickbM4897BN
Title: Some good some not so great
Review:
Signature dish (chicken) was very nice, spicy fish - good. The omelet and other dishes below average. 
Would not go out of my way to get there again.

Author: 650kingtGuildford, United Kingdom
Title: Delicious. Taste of nyonya cuisine.
Review: Nancy's Kitchen was our final stop in Melaka. There was a large queue outside the restaurant and the wait was expected to be about an hour. In actual fact it was around 30 - 45 minutes. I must admit it was well worth the wait. The food was delicious and what I expect original Nyonya food to taste like. We ordered nearly everything and ended it with a delicious Chendol! Show less

Author: jonathan550
Title: Nyonya
Review: Great food and good service - a little hard to find - so cab advisable - try the popiah and the Nancy's special chicken - all good though

Author: chillleeeo
Title: Their cendol is the bomb!
Review: The best cendol we've tasted so far... Nyonya food is nice and reasonably priced. 😊 We will defo visit Nancy's again...

Author: Lee R
Title: It's normal fried rice not nyonya!
Review: The nyonya fried rice is terribly tasteless, so as the fried meehoon. Only the spiciness of the sambal can be tasted in the sambal fried rice. I dun think the fried rice has any special compared to normal fried rice as it was really tasteless. Personally think they shouldn't use the word "nyonya" in front of the fried rice in the menu to mislead the customers. However, the "hat" was very delicious and it really amazed me. Show less

Author: Sia65
Title: New location, more places to park. Food just as good.
Review: The new location is opposite Bei Zhan, the white restaurant. The new place has plenty of parking. Food is just as tasty though I wish the portions could be bigger. Waiters don't seem to know their menu well but service was warm and friendly. Recommended.

Author: zitasharmani
Title: Ok only lah!
Review: The food was ok only lah! Nothing to shout about. Their new location is not impressive, the whole feel of dining is like any other restaurant.

Author: FromKluangMelaka State, Malaysia
Title: Good nyoya foods
Review: The restaurant had move from Jonker street to Kota Laksamana ( near opposite Bei Zhan restaurant ). One of the better Nyona foods restaurant in Melaka.Recommend foods : Ponteh pork. They selling nice Nyona kuey.Long queue during weekend better go before 11:30am for lunch.Price is reasonable but serving was little small.Show less

Author: ShawngohysSingapore, Singapore
Title: Authentic Nonya food at a reasonable price
Review: Patrons need to be prepared to wait. We were there around 12:30hrs and was told to wait for at least 45 mins. Give your phone number and they will call you once ready. The disadvantage is that there is nothing to visit or shop in its current location. However, to me the food is authentic and good with reasonable pricing. We ordered mixed vegetables, Ayam Buah Keluak, prawns in tamarind, fish maw soup and curry chicken. Show less

Author: CarolynCheongPenang Island, Malaysia
Title: Generally good nyonya food
Review: Went here with friends in search of good nyonya food.We ordered their onde-onde, pai tee, otak-otak, asam fish and sweet potato leaf belacan. For someone who doesnt like coconut, i really like their onde-onde which didnt have too strong a coconut taste, and the onde-onde kinda melts in the mouth. Pai tee and otak-otak was superbly scrumptious, that we ordered another round of pai tee. Sweet potato leaf was normal. As for the asam fish, the gravy was good but the fish didnt taste fresh.All in all, definitely worth eating there!Show less

Author: ymLee1991Malaysia
Title: Nyonya Food
Review: If possible go during the weekdays where there are less queue so you wouldnt have to wait for so long. All in all the atmosphere is pretty good in an air conditioned place with 2 floors. Service wise is reasonable and fast. Serving was a little slow could be due to the crowd. Price wise reasonable for a tourist attraction. However the serving was a little small for the price that we paid for. Still have room for improvementShow less

Author: JoyceAw40Singapore, Singapore
Title: Crowded place with nice food
Review: During our way back from Ipoh we stop over at Nancy's Kitchen. As during the time 3 plus in the afternoon we can't hardly find any restaurant open for meal. We decided to try out at Nancy's Kitchen as they open till 5pm. Guess what when I called them the staff told me that I need to wait for an hours as there are 13 groups before me and that was almost 4pm. We have a hard time finding this restaurant. When we reached there the staff told us that need to wait for 45 mins. Since we are second in the queue we wait but only waited for 20 mins we got our table for 8.We need to wait for more than half an hour before the food being serve. Food was good and nice. But the portion were not as big even you ask for large. They sell good nonya goodies and kueh. Cendol sold out by the time we want to order.Overall if not the waiting time is good to try out. Do prepare to wait if you have the time.Show less

Author: GattoMelakaMelaka, Malaysia
Title: Overated and Disappointing.
Review: We were there in December 2015. Here's our verdict:Food : The spread on the menu looks good so we ordered "Jantung Pisang", "Curry Chicken" "Fried Four Angel Beans" "Asam Bak" and "Otak Otak".However, the food turned out to be disappointing -it appeared to have been pre-prepared and microwaved and the taste was mediocre, at best. The jantung pisang was mushy and overcooked. The cook completely destroyed whatever color and texture there was. The restaurant was really busy but I guess the other patrons did not know any better. It comes across to me that the food is mass-produced and the owner of the restaurant does not care about the quality of the food. Ambience: Average decor. No ambience really. Its like "eat and go". Too crowed and cramped. The toilet is quite clean. Service: The ladies accepting the reservations, sadly, do not have a cheerful face or voice. There was no smile or greeting when we went over to enquire about our reservation. It's like a chore to them. Conclusion: Given a choice, I would not return to this restaurant. I have eaten better Nyonya Food in Melaka.Show less

Author: jas0nike
Title: Nyonya food
Review:
Overall not bad. Sambal squid is best of the day. A bit too spicy for the veggie. Worth for a try.

Reminder : not to forget to order cendol

Author: juletckaDubai, United Arab Emirates
Title: Don't understand why it is so popular
Review: Tiny place with canteen like comfort. The food was ok. We have not found it being exceptional. We did not understand why we and many others were queuing there for hours. I would say there many other restaurants in Malacca with better cuisine, more comfortable & with better service at the same price. Show less

Author: 060501Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Authentic Malacca Food
Review: Must try Rendang Chicken & Prawn with Coconut Milk yammyDon't for get Appetizer Spring Roll ( Popiah )Popular Starter before Meal..I don't mind waiting in a Q for a good food Guys Pls Try Check it out...Nancy's Authentic Peranakan Food and the Place very Clean Tum's up ...Shaan Kanda Show less

Author: jessiejamietanSingapore
Title: Definitely overrated.
Review: I found the food mediocre, definitely not the best nyonya food in Malacca as mentioned by some. We had the fish with coconut milk, omelette with cinchalok, sambal prawn with petai and chicken ponteh. Nothing great. It's our first visit and our last. We had better nyonya food elsewhere...give it a miss.Show less

Author: HappyTravelerSarahSingapore, Singapore
Title: Overrated Penarakan Restaurant!
Review: We waited 50mins for a table for 4 on a Monday. Long queue at the restaurant. Came all the way to Malacca and had to try. Ordered 6 dishes, curry chicken, duck soup, fried egg with shrimp paste, ngoh hiang, assam prawns and chap chye vegetables. Didn't like the ngoh hiang and egg. Soup was too salty. The rest were ordinary. Not worth a special visit really. Coffee was 3 in 1 type so don't bother. Overall, it is really overrated. Had much better Penarakan food elsewhere. Show less

Author: pOtAtOeME
Title: Nice food but long queue
Review: Went to Nancy's Kitchen for dinner. We queued for at least 30 minutes before we were able to get a table. Generally food is nice and the price is reasonable. Wifi is available.

Author: PS12345678000
Title: Thoroughly enjoyed the food
Review: Great food and fantastic chendol. Nice that they moved out of jonkers Street and fitted in nice air cond etc. The Nyonya dumpling/chang leans toward being sweet

Author: travelhoneybeeKL
Title: delicious nyonya dishes
Review: very popular restaurant. i have failed to walk-in in past. this time, i visites its relocated outlet which is more spacious to cater more customers. managed to book a table in advance via online. we enjoyed nyonya dishes;pai teepopiahsteamed siakap RM48porkeggcendoltea by jugRM150 for 6pax. lesser than expected price but i could say s size is quite small portion.overall, we enjoyed nyonya dishes. Show less

Author: Eric_loves_trips
Title: Quite crowded and regulars get served first :(
Review: The food is undisputed great  but i think its only fair to serve people based on queuing, rather than reservations or regulars.  There are quite a new up and coming eating places coming up hence it may do well to rethink the approach.

Author: LoveTravelww
Title: Horrible service ;(
Review: Not first come first serve basis but frequent guest first! Food's quality just normal. Wasted time and patient. Not a pleasant experience. Will definitely seek for better food and service elsewhere in malacca.

Author: JustinaLeeSingapore, Singapore
Title: A must-visit Peranakan restaurant
Review: Nancy's Kitchen has always been a must-visit Peranakan restaurant for my family members whenever we are in Malacca because of its well-known delicious and authentic Peranakan food. However, we could not locate the restaurant at No. 7 Jalan Hang Lekir (3rd Cross Street). My husband and I walked up and down the street twice and later found out from a neighbouring shop owner that Nancy's Kitchen has shifted to Taman Kota Laksamana, which is about 15 - 20 minutes walk away from Jonker Street.It was quite a long walk for my husband and I as we were not familiar with the area. When we finally reached Nancy's Kitchen, we were tired but relieved. Nancy's Kitchen has expanded to two floors in a row of shop houses. We could see that the restaurant was doing brisk business as the 1st level was fully occupied with customers. The waiter told us that Nancy's Kitchen has shifted to its new location just 3 months ago. I had a quick glance at the ambience on the 1st level. There were beautifully-framed Peranakan beads pictures on one side of the wall and photos of Nancy and her prominent visitors on another side of the wall. Bottles of pineapple tarts, kaya, sambal, nyonya cakes and cookies were displayed for sale on a open shelf cabinet and a number of nyonya chang (rice dumplings) at RM5.00 each were hanging from a bamboo holder. We were directed to the 2nd level where there were more seating but the décor was much simpler. We ordered otak (steam spicy fish paste with fresh coconut and several kind of spices), sayur loday (mixed vegetable with coconut milk) which were at RM10.00 for a small serving, Ayam Buah Keluak (chicken with black nuts) which is truly a Peranakan classic dish as the black nuts gave the gravy a sweet, spicy and sourish flavour. We also had Bakwan soup (which is meatball, crabmeat soup with vegetable and bamboo shoot). It was rich in broth and flavourful. Both the Ayam Buah Keluak and Bakwan soup costs RM15.00 each for a small serving. Our total bill with steam rice and plum lime juice came up to RM69.00 for the two of us. Fairly reasonably priced as the food was really good. My husband and I finished our food within 10 minutes as we were too busy gobbling down the food, no time to talk. The menu is extensive. Fish and prawns dishes are at market price. A bowl of cendol costs RM3.50 whereas other Peranakan restaurants were selling cendol at RM3.80. As if we haven't got enough of Nancy's delicious food, we also bought 12 nos. Nyonya chang (rice dumplings). Good food has to be shared with family members even if we had to lug it back home to Singapore!We would recommend Nancy's Kitchen for its authentic Peranakan cuisine and reasonable prices. We had our Peranakan meals at Ole Sayang and Makko in Malacca but Nancy's Kitchen stood up on its distinct own, despite steep competition. We will definitely visit the restaurant when we are in Malacca again.Show less

Author: 7DeeweeSingapore, Singapore
Title: Authentic peranakan cuisine
Review: This restaurant was so crowded, people queue up outside and waiting for almost 1 hr to get table. The staffs were really friendly. They served us and don't care about the crowd as they were treated us with their knowledge about their food products in professional way. Food was tasty and fresh, descent price and best chili!!! Located not so far from hotel we stayed. Show less

Author: MartinFitchesLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Worth the walk
Review: We spent some time trying to find Nancy's as it had moved! But it was worth the walk. Everything we ate was excellent. I particularly enjoyed the soft shell crab and the pork and bean curd. The place is super clean, sterile almost. We didn't see Nancy though....Show less

Author: Zenheart
Title: Average Peranakan Fare
Review: Each visit to Malacca for our family must include a stop at a Peranakan eatery. We were recommended Nancy's Kitchen. Having been spoilt by great and genuine homecooked Peranakan food by close Peanakan family friends, we tend to measure the standard of food at Peranakan restaurants with what genuine homecooked Peranakan food should be! We were not impressed by what was served. It was at best Average. We were looking for the extra x-factor in the taste and preparation.It did not have the 'wow' factor to bring our taste buds up a notch or two, that we would want to reorder the dishes!
