Service was also average! Value for money - not really! Worth a revisit the next time we hit town? Will try other Peranakan eateries first to compare!! Show less

Author: 822benjamintMalaysia
Title: Too crowded but good quality of foods was been served
Review: When we first arrived there it was really crowded where everyone have to stand at there to wait for a seat. Other than that, there were almost 12 of us so its really hard to find a seat to sit down, but luckily the lady boss was kind enough to help us find a place to sit down and have our meal there. There a variety of choices to choose from the menu, personally I would recomment that must try their " Ayam Pontrh"(dunno whether I spell it correctly) ...it taste so unique and delicious where you can taste the authentic nyonya flavour out of it. Moreover, another dish that you must try is their cendol but the portion is really smal compare to the ones that selling outside and the price is charging the same....there is one thing make it different from others is that the richness of their gula melaka, which it makes you can't stop eating it.Show less

Author: Warren HSingapore, Singapore
Title: Food and service
Review: Each time I visit Malacca, never fail to patronise this restaurant (since 2003). Peranakan cuisine which is a fusion of traditional Chinese and Malay food. Quality and taste though not exceptional but nevertheless gives the visitors a great sampling of this unique cultural food experience. A must try are the local pastries made up of flour and brown sugar (gula melaka), cookies and cendol (coconut milk and brown sugar).Owner, Nancy (become friends) is always on hand to welcome guests and ensure food are served on time. Go early due to long Q.Show less

Author: DolphaniaKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Will Definitely Visit Again!
Review: The food is superb! We ordered a fair bit of food among the three of us, but nothing was wasted. If only we had more space in our tummy, we would have tried everything on the menu. It is a Peranakan Restaurant that serves mouth watering dishes. We had the Stir-fried sweet potato leaves with belacan, fried homemade pork meatballs, Nyonya chicken curry, sek bak (braised pork), pai tee, and of course ended our meal with cendol. Note: most of the dishes tend to be on the spicier side, so if you are unable to take spicy food, check out the other items available or ask the crew if they can make it mild. We visited the place again the next day to buy local delicacy snacks for the family back home. Only compliments received for the snacks :). Keep it up!Show less

Author: kongsuzen
Title: Good
Review: Try the pai tee and nyonya chang! Price is reasonable, food is not bad but might have some flavouring as my throat was very dry after.

Author: DynLim
Title: Nice Foods
Review: Nice local foods, crowded during weekend, must go early. Very friendly staffs there, will visit again soon.

Author: Michelle L
Title: Love the food~
Review: I don't know why people gave it 1 star or 2 stars. Me and my friend loved the food!! It's rather salty... but other than that, it's delicious. The price is reasonable as well. Love it!

Author: Tan1990Melaka, Malaysia
Title: Pricey. Food okay. Very limited space.
Review: Nyonya kuih are overpriced,compared to Jonker street or other places. The dishes are OK only, the sambal petai with prawn, full of prawn which is not fresh, and will tiny bits of petai.you can get better chap choy in other restaurants. Dishes are overpriced. Limited space even though they have shifted. Show less

Author: jazandthejetsetterSingapore, Singapore
Title: Overrated place, average food and poor service
Review: We were greeted with no service right from the start where there was a short line but no host to attend to us. When we went to the cashier to enquire, the cashier/lady boss told us impatiently to just wait and they will come to us. We eventually found a table on our own since there was no help rendered. Food was average, nothing spectacular. The kueh pie tee is good, the steam fish was bad, the stir fried wing beam was overcooked, the Assam prawns was not fresh, the ngong hiang is not bad and Chendol average. Otah did not arrive even though we ordered. Would I return here? With the wait, rude service and very average food, absolutely not. Show less

Author: BLYCKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Try it, and judge it.
Review: Seeing the mixed reviews here makes me wonder is this place worth visiting.Truth is, i had visited this place even before seeing the reviews here. Just happened to stumble upon this place while it was still in vicinity of Jonker Walk.Queued a while but was it worth it? Yes to my opinion. While i do agree (and disagree) with some of the other reviews, i think this is a place where you should just visit and have a go at it yourself. After all, everyone's taste buds are different. Will i return? Yes, as there are many more dishes which i wanted to try but the stomach wouldn't allow. Haha.Show less

Author: Chell MSydney, Australia
Title: Not worth the trouble to find it!
Review: Everyone raved about the food so we kept looking for the restaurant. It has moved from Jonker Street to a pretty obscure new address. Our Melaccan driver couldn't find it the first day even with the address and I should have listened to JC when he said he could take us to another really good Nyonya restaurant. I was so excited when we found it but what a disappointment! Did we order the wrong dishes? Maybe we did as some of the other dishes brought out to neighbouring tables looked okay but ours were really awful. Every dish had chicken bones even the spicy fried rice! It makes us think the the cooks break up the chicken with a meat cleaver and aren't too careful about leaving little splinters of bone attached to the chicken pieces.The only saving grace was the Cendol (dessert) but I've been told great Cendol is easy to find at lots of places.The wait staff were rude and disinterested although the cashier was friendly and cheerful. The single toilet almost inside the restaurant is woeful and wouldn't be allowed in Australia due to our health regulations. I'm sure there are much better places to eat in Melaka.Show less

Author: Steven C. Y. OKota Kinabalu, Malaysia
Title: Totally over rated restaurant!
Review: I agree with some of the comments made..however, in summary, I'm totally dissapointed coz it's over priced and is a tourist trap! The only compliment is their friendly staff. Food is not exactly as nice as others mentioned in their reviews. There are many of these kind of food standard restaurants in melaka. Show less

Author: Murray JWellington, New Zealand
Title: Nancy's is An Enigma
Review: Although this restaurant comes highly recommended one wonders why. I believe they have bought into their own hype and the standards experienced earlier have certainly slipped. We went for lunch - they are open on restricted hours Tuesdays to Thursday. Longer hours over the weekend. Casualness is the order of the day. The downstairs area is cramped and unremarkable indeed. The waiting staff required prompting, were generally disinterested and offered no service at all. There was no proactiveness and the experience was underwhelming. One wonders about how its ratings have been achieved - a tourist trap, with guidebooks ensuring clientele as their food does not do nonya cuisine justice.We started with popiah, which was not rice paper rolls but a simple crepe, followed by an omlette with prawns which was chilly hot but unremarkable. It needed a genuine flavour boost and decent plating. The whole steamed fish was simply not fresh and a huge disappointment where seafood is highlighted as a notable dish. The braised pork with tamarind sauce was simply sliced pork on an iceberg lettuce leaf with onion and a mass of inedible tamarind seeds. And the plating was effortless. When you look at one another during your meal and ask "what is this food all about" you realise it's either a bad day in the kitchen or the ascribed rating is a phantom and totally unwarranted.We went with high expectations following some reviews and the hotel's recommendation. It did not measure up - it was a very average meal. It felt like the waiting staff could not be bothered and the kitchen was understaffed with no plating effort. There are several cafes nearby that serve better nonya food we found, and are better value.Show less

Author: Elaineyapsc
Title: So so food but pricey
Review:
Disappointed. Kuih muih and food are not authentic. Renovation and decorating are nice but very noisy with too many customers. We can't wait to leave. 

Will try more others nyonya restaurant in melacca. 

Chances of returning: 0%

Author: Paul BStockton-on-Tees, United Kingdom
Title: worth a detour
Review: As others have said, this is not where you might expect to find it if you use the Lonely Planet guide - if you walk from the top end of Jonker Street it's quite a hike in the heat so you might want to get a taxi or one of those Hello Kitty trishaws...One excellent feature is fierce air conditioning, which (for a Westerner) was heaven-sent. The menu is exciting and it is difficult to recommend specific dishes (although chicken and candlenuts is worth trying, as is the banana flower dish, sweet potato greens and fried rice).Everything coming out of the (clean) kitchen looked delicious.For a taste of real local cuisine I would recommend this restaurant.Show less

Author: Sia65Singapore, Singapore
Title: Very tasty food!
Review: Food was fantastic! I recommend the prawn petai dish. The decoration is that of peranakan, which was interesting. When I was there end August 2015, I was informed that Nancy's Kitchen would be shifting to a new location. Best to double check the new location before going.Show less

Author: TaniaKansilSouth Tangerang, Indonesia
Title: High demand resto - worth visit
Review: When we were in Malacca, we decided to have lunch at this resto. Seemed the resto is quite famous, coz there were a number of people queuing to get a table. Perhaps because the resto is quite small, though it occupies 2 floors.The spring roll definitely yummy. The es cendhol too. Other food that we tried were: Fried Nyonya Yellow Noodle, Nyonya Mixed Vegetable and Chicken something. You can ask the waiter the serving size for the food, be it small or large. So, you can enjoy the meal well. Been informed by the waiter that the resto would move to a new location, Taman Kota Laksamana around Sep'15. »TKShow less

Author: Annesofouch29
Title: Great food
Review: I went there for lunch and we had some delicious food!!! It was a late lunch so no queue and we try the top hat , the spring roll and laksa . Every thing was delisious and spicy!!! Loved every bit!!!

Author: CorinneLee35Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Long waiting but food is delicious
Review: We looking place for lunch, finally decide to try Nancy's Kitchen, we been waiting(standing) more than 40mins just to queue for the lunch. The restaurant is small, between table to table fit for 1 person walk through but the food that we order is delicious - Steam fish, Soft shell crab, Rendang Chickeng, mix vege & Kuih Pai Tee (must). Show less

Author: Britt_NomadSydney, Australia
Title: The best nyonya food in Malaysia!
Review: I ate here several times during my stay in Melaka. The depth of spice and flavour in the dishes is amazing. For entrees I recommend the top hats, and for mains I recommend the delicious prawn and bean dish and the candle nut chicken. Everything I ate here was exceptional. This place really captures the essence of nyonya cooking.Show less

Author: josephinengpy
Title: The best taste of Nyonya dishes
Review: Worth the wait in line to get into this restaurant. Ate the nyonya chicken and prawn. Tooooooo yummy that i am dreaming of it again

Author: Bruce FNortham, Australia
Title: Worst Restaurant in all of Melaka!!!!
Review: We went there today under recommendation from our driver, it was busy, the place looked dirty and we were ushered upstairs to a back room which had a slight odour to it. The waiter kept getting our order wrong and we had to ask 3 times for a dish we ordered. The food was bland and uninteresting. I do not recommend this place to anyoneShow less

Author: CarolynLan
Title: Very close to courtyard @ heeren
Review:
passed a few times, this place always have ppl queing up.
tried before we left melaka.
Ithink its the price and the quality makes it popular.
homemade nyonya food is not too bad (not too greesy) quite a selection of meat/veggies as well!

Author: SkyegerlSingapore
Title: Very Good Food
Review: Restaurant is small with limited seats but food is good. The Pai Tee and the sambal prawn with petai are so good!! The pork ribs buah karak and chicken rending is nice too! Fish maw soup is good too!! Ordered small portion for all for 3 persons. Just nice if you are small eaters. Meal came up to RM$88 including 2 drinks and 2 rice.Show less

Author: Hwei36London, United Kingdom
Title: Food is so so, not worth queuing for
Review: We queued for a hour for Nancy's and finally got seated. Service was great, but the food was not as great as people raved about! Presentation was not given any effort and most importantly, quality was not there. Highly disappointed as we thought it would be good!Show less

Author: danny jSingapore, Singapore
Title: OVER-RATED, BLAND AND DILUTED
Review: My partner and I were looking forward to dining at Nancy's after reading the reviews and based on recommendations in some websites.We appreciated and respected the reviews. However, we felt the restaurant is over-rated!And the long queuing was not worth it at all.It is no doubt the restaurant is very popular amongst the tourists but a few chats with the locals, we were told that the standard has dropped very much.And we could not agree more. The management did not maintain the quality of the food. I suspect they may have chosen quantity over quality. We ordered 4 dishes to savour. Each dish may have its own distinctive taste and seasoning. However, the two words to describe it is 'Diluted and bland'. Peranakan food is known to be rich and savoury. It is not supposed to be palatably light. So, my partner and I could not reconcile with that the fact that this restaurant is voted no.1 for its Nonya food. We have expected better.Perhaps, it was the tourists who have voted for it and not the locals. Or maybe this is the only Peranankan restaurant in Jonker Street that serves pork dishes so it attracted the crowd.I would personally not recommend this restaurant. You may have a different opinion and other expectations because everyone has a differing taste bud. You may want to consider Kocik Kitchen which is just a stone's throw away from Nancy. Why not go for both if you are staying for two nights and draw your own conclusions?Enjoy!Show less

Author: chickenluckPJ
Title: Decent Nyonya Delicacies
Review: Second time round dining at this restaurant. Food is great and service is fast. I guess it's because they'd have to pace to accommodate the crowd.There's a perpetual crowd queuing for this but the staff here make sure each table gets to eat at their own pace - unlike some restaurants where they subtly chase you out.Do order they Devil Curry or their Babi Pongteh dishes. Superb. Also, don't forget to stop by the kitchen to see what snacks they have to offer.Show less

Author: WhoppeR2015Asia
Title: Too small and environment not suitable for kids
Review: Small and cram and shabby! As a result of the small sitting area the queue was so long, and you have to stand under the hot sun.Nonya Kuehs were good, especially the ondeh ondeh.Be prepared to cough when you pay your bill- it is next to the Kitchen and it just oozes chilli.Show less

Author: hktraveller328
Title: Convenient location
Review: A compact restaurant. Staff not particularly friendly. Food above average and prices reasonable. Chicken curry worth tasting.

Author: john m
Title: Authentic Nyonya food
Review: Small, popular, busy selling nice local food just off Jonker Street. Be prepared to cough when you go to pay your bill as its next to the Kitchen and it just oozes Chilli!

Author: dostrovsNew York City, New York
Title: Highlight of my meals on Malaysia
Review: We got in line 20 minutes before opening. The place opened for dinner 30 minutes post intended time. The line behind us was ridiculous.They have all the dishes in small portions, which allows you to try a lot of different things. Managed to try about 10 dishes because of this little trick - nice and smart of them!Fantastic popiah. Excellent otak otak. Could not find anything to complain about. Best version of buah keluak ayam I have tried. I want to say few words about this dish: It is one of the things you are looking for as a traveling food enthusiast. It has distinct taste with unparalleled flavor. It is reminiscent of mole, but not quite the same. Liked a lot. Unfortunately Singaporean renditions of the dish did not match the expectations.Show less

Author: Phil_OPKS
Title: Good Food!
Review: Good food and reasonable prices.  It's a small place and you may have to wait for a table.  We ate a late lunch, just before their closing for lunch.  Pleasant staff and very good food.

Author: FrennieB
Title: Best Nyonya Cuisine
Review: This restaurant offers the best nyonya food ever! You got to try the Babi Pongteh and Babi Buah Keluak. The taste is awesome that I can't even describe it here!

Author: Jonathan NKo Samui, Thailand
Title: Very popular
Review: With locals and tourists.I managed to go when it was less busy than usual and enjoyed a good value meal.Good Nonya food is exceptional when done really well and this isnt at all bad and not expensive.I will not be returning here only because Melaka is a place I would not go back to,as in general I would say there are far more interesting places to visit in Malaysia.Show less

Author: Markdicko12Fuengirola, Spain
Title: Closed!
Review: I guess you have to just go with the flow here in Malaysia and accept that things are well a little chaotic. But having said that its bloody annoying when you turn up at the restaurant of your choice bouyed by the great reviews on trip adviser and lonely planet only to find that they are closed. No explanation ......just don't fancy opening.....come back at the weekend!!Show less

Author: PRT2014
Title: Es Chendol and Refreshing Juice
Review: Very refreshing Lime juice with Jaggery - perfect after walk at Jonker street. Also must try is Es (Ice) Chendol to beat the heat of Melaka - a very special combination of ice, milk and jaggery with red beans -

Author: rzsandoval
Title: Go here!
Review:
Great Peranakan food!  I especially liked the chicken curry, pork with kluak, and cincalak.

The dining area is super small, so the line gets long on the outside in the heat.  Go early to save yourselves!

Author: Yap K
Title: Average Food
Review: Restaurant quite small but when there's a big crowd, queueing outside the shop is hot. Old folks not recommended to wait under the sun. Should provide some chairs for them & kids while waiting. Food wise are so-so. Nothing to shout about on their food.

Author: MWeePhotographySingapore, Singapore
Title: Definitely NOT classic nonya food...
Review: We've tried getting a table at Nancy's a couple of times but were unsuccessful as they were always packed. We managed to get a seat this time round though because we waited for them to commence their operations outside the restaurant (which in itself was weird, their facebook profile and a few other reviews listed wrong operational hours?!)So, after reading through numerous positive reviews about this restaurant, and us having tried pretty hard to get a seat the last few times, we were pretty excited. Unfortunately for us though, we did not hold back on the ordering. We had the popiah and the kueh pai tee as starters, with the sambal prawns, chicken "buah kuluak", mixed vegetables, banana flower curry and the nonya "sio bak" (it was a table of 2 to put things into perspective). Firstly, the popiah was probably the worst popiah I have had. The skin was too thick, the bamboo shoot was too soggy and the entire dish was too sweet. To be fair, the kueh pai tee's were not that bad, and the only grievance I had with this starter was that they served it with the wrong chili. The sambal prawns and the buah kuluak was not that bad either (although the chicken was tasteless). The biggest disappointment on the table was the sio bak. I've had the privilage to have tasted some really good sio bak, and this version was no where near the level of anything I have tasted before.Visit this restaurant if you do not mind below mediocre food set in a rustic environment. Any thing else and you would be disappointed.Show less

Author: Tazen_TzKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Great taste
Review: Fine heritage place for lunch break, food are affordable and reasonable price,Belacan fried rice was really good, spicy, tastyNyonya kuih was good alsoAdvisable to take as many dish as possible in small portion and try them all***open for lunch, go early, food finishes fast thereShow less

Author: duoleeSingapore
Title: Early lunch
Review: Were there at their opening time (11am), to avoid quene. Small restaurant with about 3 tables on the first level and 4 bigger tables on the second level. Went with 2 grandmothers and they had some difficulty going up and down the stairs. Food was just average and the white rice had lots of weevils! Not likely to visit the place again as there are many other places to eat at jonker walk.Show less

Author: zaraongSingapore, Singapore
Title: Authentic Peranakan Food
Review: We were waiting for our tour to start at the Baba Museum and were walking around the area nearby to pass time. We just happen to chance to Nancy's and realised it is one of the best eatery around. We had some drinks and dessert and decided to come back for lunch. It was one of the best decision for the day! The food was great! No wonder it was full house during lunch time but worth the short wait. They also sell tarts and dumplings. Highly recommended for authentic Peranakan food.Show less

Author: JaaialigSingapore, Singapore
Title: Nice nonya dishes
Review: Saw good review on this restaurant and decided to give it a try.Went at noon and the queue was long. Hence revisit around 4pm plus. The queue was short and decided to await for the queue. It took about 30mins for our queue. The dishes which we ordered tasted very nice and price was reasonable was Rm 68 plus for my spouse and myself. Well recommend by trip advisor!!Show less

Author: Bellerancic
Title: Liltle nyonya taste
Review: Get ready to queue up for this place if you visit it on weekend. First try for the nyonya food, not bad still. Love the acar the most.

Author: Ellie WNorwich, United Kingdom
Title: Great tasting food
Review: I was a little dubious when I entered Nancy's as I thought it smelled like a pet shop.....not a promising start. (I'm not a seasoned Asia traveller!) However, the food was great. A real mix of flavours (not just hot and spicy) with lovely little dishes, such as the top hats. I'm glad that I went and after spending 2 weeks travelling around Malaysia, Nancy's had some of the most interesting food that I ate.Show less

Author: MxJ1504
Title: Reach early! Good food at affordable price!
Review: Was there during my recent trip with the family and really enjoyed myself! Arrived at 6.15 and waited about 15minutes for a table. Crowd started coming about 6.45 and queue gets really long! Food is good and tasty.. And located conveniently at jonker street!

Author: godzilla_ozSydney, Australia
Title: Authentic & Tasty
Review: The recommendation paid off .The restaurant is in a terrace shophouse on a side street just off from Jonker Street. There were only a few tables & the setting is nice with photos of of ladies dressed in their nonya outfit. Service was prompt & efficient. The poh piah & the peranakan chicken curry was really good & so was the steamed okra served with a special sauce.It was a really an enjoyable dinner to end our wonderful 3 days stay in Melaka.Show less

Author: Stoney7788Singapore, Singapore
Title: Awesome food and consistent
Review: Great variety of nonya food and the staff were very helpful in recommending. If you like gravy this is the place to be. Order as much as you can eat as it's worth the wait outsideWish the restaurant was bigger as lines into the restaurant can be long. Show less

Author: wandersomeCastro Valley, California
Title: Scrumptious!
Review: I finally had my meal @ Nancy's Kitchen after going there on a Tuesday when they are closed. The restaurant looked unassuming, but there was an air and aroma of good food to be have. I looked at the varied menu consisting of Nyonya/Perinakan(Chinese-Malay fusion) food.So tantalizing the menu, but settled with two dishes. The poh piah, a fresh spring roll filled with sauteed vegetables, tofu, shrimp, and crispy pork rind was simply scrumptious; refreshing. The Nyonya laksa, a spicy, pungent/aromatic coconut based curry with noodles, tofu puffs, shrimp was delicious although a bit heavy for lunch. I must say that my experience at Nancy's kitchen was part of the fun of Melaka.Show less

Author: FrancescaU535
Title: Over hyped food
Review:
More misses than hits. 
Hits were the pai tee and cendol
Misses is everything else. Food was too salty. Curry wasn't flavourful and the spices bland.  Kacang botol was old, so it wasn't crunchy. Very disappointing meal indeed.

Author: shenpl02Singapore
Title: Simple dinner
Review: we went early, around 5pm and already there is a Queue. we waited for about 20min, and managed to get a table then.had belacan stir-fried potato leaves, peranakan chicken curry, fried rice and kueh Pieti.by the time we finished our dinner around 6pm+, the Queue has grown much longer.I must say, I don't understand what the rave is about. the food is only average, not worth the time at all.Show less

Author: Martita76
Title: Delicious!
Review:
It is a small restaurant and there is always a line, but we got seated pretty fast. All the dishes we ordered were delicious, especially her
signature chicken stew (can't remember the name)

Author: PavaliaCambridge, United Kingdom
Title: Nyonya Cuisine
Review: We visited to try a selection of Nyonya foods and plumped for deserts, mainly. The very helpful waiting staff made suggestions and brought us a selection of things to try. My daughter loved everything: Kuih lapis - a sweet steamed cake made from rice flour, coconut milk, sugar and various shades of edible food colouring done with many individual layers; Onde onde - small round balls made from glutinous rice flour coloured and flavoured with pandan, filled with palm sugar syrup and rolled in freshly grated coconut), popiah (uber-spring rolls stuffed with shreddded carrots, prawns, chilli, garlic, palm sugar and much, much more), pineapple tarts (flaky pastries filled with pineapple jam) and my favourite; the most fantastic cendol! The best I have yet to try! Yummy!!Show less

Author: silverglazeBaguio, Philippines
Title: Nice to try
Review: I tried the Peranakan braised pork andHog plum juice.. The pork was good and i actually finished it. It also has tofu and egg. It wIs my first time to taste a hog plum juice.. It was sour but not bad.. I could not actually describe the taste.. The staff are nice and accomodating..Show less

Author: WantedToTravelKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Good food, cosy place
Review: We're lucky we do not need to queue up like some other reviewer. We had what recommended here, pai tee, popiah, Chinese dumpling. All food is up to our expectation. Nothing special though. Worth to give it a try but not if you need to queue up for 30 mins or so.Show less

Author: PyecombeEastbourne, United Kingdom
Title: Shut your eyes and eat the food
Review: If you are squeamish you might find the interior and kitchens a little too rustic. Don't be put off, the food here is really good and the open kitchen and decaying walls all add to the charm. Chicken Rendang was great as were the Nyonya noodles. A must visit place. Show less

Author: 341angelinesMalaysia
Title: Simple yet tasty Peranakan food
Review: If you want authentic Peranakan food, this is the place to go! The flavours are great, and the price is very reasonable considering that everything in Melaka seems so tourist-y! The otak-otak was served in a generous portion as compared to the other Peranakan restaurants that are charging the same price. Other dishes like the fish curry had generous amounts of coconut milk too, which we love! The cendol was awesome too! Loaded with lots of coconut milk & gula Melaka, this bowl of dessert can never go wrong! As for the dish sizing and price, they are clearly stated in the menu. So, no worries of over-charging there ;) Oh, and when you are done with your meal, head to the back of the restaurant and check out the treats that they sell. Freshly made Nyonya kuih and pastries are sold in neat packagings and guess what, they taste good too! Very suitable for those of you who want to bring home some of these treats as a reminder of Melaka.Show less

Author: Cecilia11132015
Title: Nancy Kitchen - moved
Review:
New address: 13, 13 & 13-2,
Jalan KL 3/8 Taman Kota
Laksamana Seksyen 3
75200 Melaka

DISAPPOINTED:
Walk to old address & found they have moved.
Took a cab & located the new place BUT was closed.
Very disappointed

Author: kdsydneySydney
Title: Really overrated and not worth the wait
Review: After reading all of the reviews on trip adviser I was really looking forward to lunch at Nancy's kitchen during our recent trip to Malaysia. The food was OK, nothing spectacular and it certainly wasn't worth waiting for an hour in the heat for a table.Show less

Author: SmilesssssKlang, Malaysia
Title: You must try it out if you are looking for authentic nyonya food
Review: You will never regret & definitely will make a second, third visit....I like the rendang chicken & ponteh (pork), and I believe u will definitely like them too. My sister & me felt disappointed when we visited on the 1st day stay in Melaka, where the pai-tea finished at the time we visited and we were told to revisit the next day.However, on Sunday (2nd day) when we wanted to order the pai tea and was informed that they didn't make pai tea on that day.... We were a bit upset when we were not well informed.2days stayed in Melaka & didn't manage to eat the pai tea by Nancy's Kitchen, frankly my sister & me were quite disappointed. Hope we got chance to eat the next trip when we revisit again....Show less

Author: suichabo
Title: Lunch of 5 people
Review: Ordered fried rice, fish maul soup, curry chicken, etc. Not authentic n not nice at all. Very disappointed

Author: KaZsingapore
Title: Worth the wait!
Review: This is peranankan cuisine at its best. The superb taste bespoke meticulous preparation and the food looks good too. Prices were reasonable. Don't miss the ayam pongteh, springroll, otah and cendol!

Author: pangethaSingapore, Singapore
Title: Well Worth the Wait
Review: We have been to this restaurant twice within a year. In June 2014, no need to queue at about 1pm on a Thursday and we got a table for 5 rather quickly; the meal was served very quickly too.The eatery is situated in an old shophouse, sparsely but aptly decorated. It gives a feel of old-time Chinatown. You also get free Wi-Fi.In December 2014, we were en route from Port Dickson to Singapore and decided to make a detour to Melacca for dinner. Queued for almost an hour before the evening opening hours (5pm) on a Saturday and waited another about 45 mins for the meal to be served. It was obviously very packed and under-staffed. Food is simply delicious and we will always finish off the meal with their Chendol.If you have time to spare, Nancy's Kitchen is well worth the wait. If not, perhaps timing your visit to weekdays will help. Make sure you check on their opening hours before going down.Of course, there are other Nonya eateries around and good ones too. But a visit to Nancy's is quite an experience and a hallmark of having been to Melacca.Show less

Author: pinkpj
Title: Excellent Food
Review: Most of the food was brilliant but, to our taste buds, not the starter salad!  Service was great and price reasonable!!

Author: AdaDupont
Title: Authentic Nyonya food
Review: When I'm in Melaka, I always have lunch here. It's casual local restaurant which offers authentic Nyonya cuisine. Foods are not spicy but tastes mild. You can buy Nyonya sweets such like pineapple pies and dumplings with brown syrup and other Nyonya specialities on the ground floor. They are also good taste.Show less

Author: evonny1London, United Kingdom
Title: Much better than expected.
Review: Have just come back from having dinner in this restaurant. We were expecting a long queue as it is Saturday night but we were able to go right in. The staff were friendly, smiling and welcoming. The menu was well presented in English with photos to help choose the unfamiliar food. The food was served promptly and was absolutely delicious. We ate nonya fried rice which is similar to fried rice we see in English Chinese restaurants. We had pork in tamarind sauce, fried fish in ginger and spring onion and vegetables in coconut sauce which was very slightly spicy. All were unusual, tasty and satisfying. We tried a nonya dessert which I can't remember the name of but it was green balls of gluten, like Japanese mocha with sweet gula malaka syrup inside and coconut sprinkled on the outside. Again, unusual and yummy. We had water and lemonade and paid around 80ringgits. We thoroughly enjoyed it and felt we had experienced some true local food. Just to say the place itself is not posh. The tables, plates and glasses are all plastic and there is some peeling paint on the walls but everything seemed clean and well organised.Show less

Author: Merryn1288Melaka, Malaysia
Title: Delicious nyonya food
Review: Available more genuine nyonya food and taste delicious with its food marinated with sufficient herbs and spices. Place is conducive and located at prime area where most tourist visit that is near Jonker Walk. The owner said somewhere in Sept 2015, their restaurant will be shifted to Melaka Raya but new address not known yet.Show less

Author: Travelicious_KKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Be prepared to queue up
Review: We stood in line for about 20 minutes or so before we got a place to sit. We had to share a table with a couple as the restaurant was packed. It's a very small and narrow shop lot with not a lot of space, so there were about 7 tables that could probably accommodate about 30 people at one time. However, there were more than 30 of us as everyone was cramming around the tables to fit in as many people as possible. You have to order your food, eat and leave - no time to sit and linger around. Their popiah and pai tee seemed to be a crowd pleaser. We wanted to order some for takeway, but they had run out, and it was only around 7pm. The food was not fantastic, just ok for me. I liked the sambal squid with petai the best. The prawns cooked with pineapple could have tasted better if the prawns were fresher. I somehow did not like the texture - they seemed soft and funny tasting. The Portuguese chicken curry was also ok, but both the curries we ordered were really thin. It was just two of us and we had small portions of the squid, prawns, chicken and one vegetable dish, which came up to about RM65, which I thought was alright. The food could have tasted better though. The lady who took our order was very pleasant and patient in spite of how busy they were.Show less

Author: Paulk004
Title: Super value
Review: We had lunch at this authentic little restaurant. It is very popular so be prepared to que at weekends. No advanced bookings are offered but the wait is worthwhile.

Author: AutumndewSingapore, Singapore
Title: Not worth it anymore
Review: We used to like visiting Nancy Kitchen for a nice meal whenever we come to Malacca. The food was much much better before.Now, it seems like the standard dropped by a lot.. Seriously by a lot.We ordered the sambal potato leaves, braised pork, Otar-Otar and Nyoh Hiong.The sambal potato leaves are tasteless with no taste of sambal at all. The Otar-Otar is mild, braised pork is alright and the Nyoh Hiong is just average.Food used to be much better here.Show less

Author: 8asiaKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Good but not great
Review: The queue system needs to be updated to make it more tasteful. Although they don't accept reservations but at least tell the customers who are waiting at the opening their queue expectation and if it's in the 1st eating or wait for next table available when customers finish & leave. Yes, it gives a sense of popularity & publicity that customers are prepared to wait but not good PR. The food had a good standard of Nonya cooking but not great.Show less

Author: kajambeCanberra, Australia
Title: Good Malay nonya food
Review: I was frustrated to find TA's top rated restaurants in Melaka at the moment were a mix of western food, cake shops and pubs with a few good Indian options. After a bit more research we found Nancy's with its varied menu of honest nyonya food that went beyond the familiar curries and noodles and ventured into some interesting options including plenty with pork and also some duck. A few nice sweet choices to finish were great - the delicious onde onde and coconut kuih, though I would love to have squeezed in the kaya custard too... Maybe next time. And the big bonus was they also serve beer - perfect!Show less

Author: eMole
Title: Overrated
Review: Positive reviews and herd mentality (the queue) led me to try Nancy's. I don't understand the queue for it. Service is good but the food is just average.

Author: HuiPing HPulau Penang, Malaysia
Title: Moderate food and pricey
Review: Visited at 3pm with a 2-3 groups of queue outside of the shop. Waited for around 15 minutes and got in.Service: service is in a slower pace but friendly.Food: ordered 3 dishes.1. Curry chicken detul (or dentul?): said to be Nancy's signature. Quite nice and chicken was cooked well.2. Prawn asam pedas: the prawn was not fresh. The prawn meat was loose and did not taste good. 3. Vegetable curry: said to have 8 types of vegetables cooked in coconut curry. The gravy was not thick enough and tasted blant. And could not figure out the 8 types of vegetables, only seemed to see a lot od radish-like veggie.Total cost ~RM58 for 2 person.Overall not satiafied. Felt overrated online.Show less

Author: Lovetotravelpj
Title: Nice food
Review: Nice food. Good service. Must try the popiah n cendol. Non halal. Lots of pork dishes. Autentic nyonya food. Enjoy the food

Author: BallVivi
Title: Excellent
Review: Very delicious, traditional one, will try again next time.  Long queue and they close around 9:00 pm, so need to go early to get seats.

Author: Saved_by_TravelBeijing
Title: Great food ... and even greater advertising strategy!
Review: We stayed at a hotel near Nancy's Kitchen and continually saw the very long line-ups at Nancy's so decided to join the queue. Although the restaurant was supposed to re-open at 4 p.m., it opened about 4:25. We were sat at a table with two other couples, who proved to be excellent company. The food that we ordered spring rolls (popiah), sweet and sour fish, chicken curry, fried rice, jack fruit and greens were all delicious (okay, maybe all except the jack fruit)! There was also free internet in the restaurant. Despite the long line-up outside, Nancy's staff did not rush their inside customers at all. In fact, the staff were in no rush themselves to clear the tables and make them ready for the waiting guests outside. The verdict = tasty food, reasonably priced, slow and leisurely pace, long line-ups and exceptional advertising on Nancy's part. We never went to Nancy's if we had not seen the steady line ups! If you have time on your hands, and are in no rush, give it a try. Don't forget to take some Pineapple Tarts home with you ... they were exceptional!Show less

Author: msnakimSingapore
Title: Mediocre Peranakan Food
Review: We enjoy Peranankan food and frequently eat nyonya dishes back home in Singapore. This brings about comparison and we weren't very impressed with Nancy's Kitchen despite it's good reputation. Food is mediocre at best. And with the long wait for a table and the longer wait for food to be served, the dining experience was just so-so.During our visit, we also witnessed the service attitude of the staff. One of the customers politely declined the dish served as he had ordered pork and not chicken. The confused waiter brought the dish downstairs and soon a lady (who took the order) stormed towards the customer. No smiles and no apology. She insisted the customer had ordered chicken, placed the dish back on the table and stormed off.I had no idea who was right and who was wrong. But the staff's attitude leaves a lot to be desired.Show less

Author: mikelarry70
Title: authentic nyonya food!
Review: friendly lady boss owner..asked her to recommend some good peranakan dishes and out came superb meals! must try..

Author: MontanaCyclist
Title: Bad food wrapped up in a fancy bow for tourists.
Review: This place is simply not good. It's not really Nyonya either. Try Kota Laksamana area for much better food.

Author: Gnoskcoy
Title: Nice homely feel...but average food
Review: Perhaps all the review hype up our expectations. But the popiah, nyonya chap Chye, otak and ayam buah keluak all tasted average...The chap Chye cook be cooked longer, the ayam buah keluak also lacks the full flavour of the keluak fruit...Considering the queue time and thereafter the 30minutes wait for food, I will probably try out other peranakan restaurants.Show less

Author: SGPTravellerSGPSingapore, Singapore
Title: Poor Business Practice Average Food
Review: Visited this restaurant since there was quite positive review in the internet. It was absolute disappointment! Opening hours at the restaurant was indicated as 11.30 am but we waited close to 12 noon without any explanation or apology. As a family of 7 (six adults and one child), we waited for close to half an hour under sweltering heat but when it opened its door for lunch, a tour group of around 20 was allowed to cut queue and given priority entry over all others in the queue. It was also evident that they were attended to first. While we were still having our lunch in the restaurant, a noticeably queue was again forming. They could not be admitted as seats in the restaurant were limited. I pitied those in the queue because when another tour group arrived, they were barred entry so that the newly arrived tour group could take up seats from customers who had just finished their lunch. The restaurant defended its position citing that groups with 20 or more are allowed reservation and thus the privilege in treatment. It would have been more reasonable if the restaurant had indicated the remaining available seats (after deducting those in their reservation list) so that walk-in customers can decide promptly whether to select an alternative eating outlet.Food in this restaurant was rather mediocre. Personally, I would prefer Makko Restaurant - better food at more competitive price and it allowed reservation even though we are a family of only seven.Show less

Author: Seahlydia
Title: good food but place cramped
Review: not so children friendly and if you are going on a bigger group will not be easy. food is good but may not be worth the queue.

Author: VTikSingapore, Singapore
Title: Delicious
Review: Was wondering why the long queues outside the restaurant daily when we were visiting Melaka. Finally tried it one day and ordered a poppiah,Nonya Laksa, chendol and kedongdong drink (since there were 2 of us only for brunch).There were no skimping in the fillings or ingredients for the poppiah, laksa and chendol.It was yummy! Reasonably priced too. Would love to be back for more Peranakan fare!Show less

Author: juzatouristSingapore, Singapore
Title: Not sure what the fuss is about
Review: Maybe we didn't order their famous dishes, but the food was really nothing to shout about. Throw in the queue in the sun and I'd rather stay in Singapore and eat at Peramakan, which was better food imo. If you've never been, I guess it is quite charming and fascinating. The pineapple tarts were one of the better ones in Melaka. Not too mention having to navigate the scary stairs (for older folk). Thankfully they're moving soon hopefully to a place more elderly friendlyShow less

Author: SoonhoeLSingapore, Singapore
Title: Nice cozy eatery
Review: We read about the queues and were pleased to get a table for lunch rather quickly, perhaps because it was off-peak on Wed in mid-Oct?The popiah was quite good, and so was the KuehPieTi (they called it Top Hat). The Kang Kong Belacan was somewhat chewy and the beef rending was tough too. The latter 2 dishes would be more enjoyable if they were softer. They also sell a variety of nonya kuehs (cakes) in the inner hall. We bought the pineapple tarts which we felt was a little too sweet.Show less

Author: BerniechiahumphriesSingapore, Singapore
Title: No Standard
Review: We were there for Dinner on the day we arrived in Melaka. Food is so so only, nothing fantastic. After our meal , shocked to see their worker cleared all the the remnant onto a plate in front of us on our table. And there was a big Dustbin at the side of the Eating place which was so disgusting . I thought this is supposed to be a Restaurant but Service is no better than a Coffeeshop.Show less

Author: erinSGSingapore, Singapore
Title: Homemade Nonya food
Review: The restaurant is family run. Tight squeeze at the front of the restaurant but they have more seating space upstairs. Everything appears to be homemade even the kue paiti skin which is delicious. The curry is a must try as well as the chinchalok (small shrimps fermented in brine) omelette.The back of the shop is stocked with more homemade goodies to take home. Definitely worth a visit if you can get in. They don't take reservations and it's almost always crowded.Show less

Author: PinXunSingapore, Singapore
Title: good for kueh, average for other food
Review: a small shop to be missed unless there is a long queue outside. the assorted kueh especially onde-onde is super yummy. mini bite size that burst in your mouth. also the dumpling is worth the try here. other than that I find the food quite average and expensive.Show less

Author: Amanda W
Title: Great Peranaken Food
Review: Very good authentic Peranaken food - basic setting but the food more than compensates for that.  Also interesting to peek into the very busy kitchen from the upstairs eating areas - it's a hive of activity!

Author: Travel_Buff_AsiaSingapore, Singapore
Title: Reached high expectations
Review: Foodie friends of ours had highly recommended this place and our hotel concierge warned of long queues to enter... So we entered this restaurant before 8pm on a Friday. Its just over 5 min walk from the Hard Rock and on the second left down Jonker.We got seating at once and a very patient server who explained each specialty. We chose 4 dishes, the chicken, prawn and okra were superb - delicious blend of spices but not too hot. The atmosphere is simple but service was swift and attentive also with the family photos on the walls it felt like we were in a Peranakan relative's dining room.Planning to try another meal before returning home. The variety of items on the menu and the experience of the first visit requires that!Show less

Author: mrmin1
Title: Must have visited on a off day.
Review: Based on the review we were eagerly anticipating eating at this little restaurant.We visited on a Monday, however felt the food was only average. Maybe after the busy weekend there were different chefs working on the weekend. The Pork was tough and not at all tender, and the Chicken smelt like it had been reheated.The highlight was the freshly prepared spring roll which was bursting with flavour.Show less

Author: sajuzac
Title: Queue up for some tasty food
Review:
1>Stand in line to get seats during lunch time.
2>Food is tasty and pork options available too.
3>Location is accessible from main attraction areas.
4>It is a small area and hence less seating, but worth the wait for your turn.
5> Try the soursop juice.

Author: JessieW74
Title: Authentic nonya food
Review: Too excited forget to take picture before food...the taste is good reminds me of the dishes which my grandma and dad cooked. Is a must to try the food if you are in malacca.

Author: Paolo DRescaldina, Italy
Title: it worth the wait
Review: You can often read that if in a restaurant you have to wait for sit and eat it means that the restaurant is good. This is especially true there! You will wait a lot of time in the street and you will have to suffer the worm, but the food worth it! And it is also cheap!Show less

Author: Martin FColorado Springs, Colorado
Title: AWESOME local cuisine & experience
Review: Go to Nancy's just for the experience. There's usually a line waiting for table any time around 12h00 or after 18h00 in the evenings. The place looks like a hole-in-the-wall, but when we asked a local where he would go for the best Nyonya food in Melaka, he immediately pointed us to Nancy's and he was right. They make popia right in front of the door, you walk in past four or five table in the main area, then right through the kitchen to get to the stairs that take you up to two other dining area. Service as attentive and gave good recommendations, the food came quickly, and the beer was cold. This is NOT a white tablecloth place, but a mom-and-pop locals place that gets by on simple, tasty food with excellent sauces cooked fresh, served hot, and excellent. Overall a great experience! (We're happy that we arrived just before 18h00 and got a table!)Show less

Author: Tijn G
Title: best place in town
Review: A very good restaurant to taste Nyonya dishes. We did a cooking course here. Very special to learn the dishes from a cooking perspective

Author: Cypgrizboy
Title: great experience
Review:
we've been there for our last dinner in town with the familly. 
The food was yummi, we taste new dishes, the quantity and the quality were perfect. 
Highly recommended. 
Very affordable prices. 
We oly have been "disturb" by the too cold aircon.

Author: allerta2016Leiden, The Netherlands
Title: Aside from the popiahs, not impressed
Review: We had dinner at Nancy's on our first evening in Melaka, encouraged by TA reviews praising the good local fare and reasonable prices. Unfortunately, we can not give a great review. On a positive note, the popiah that we started off with was delicious! However, we were somewhat disappointed by the main courses: we had a fish dish (garlic and soy sauce, I believe), which was admittedly tasty, but it was a tiny portion (like 6 very small pieces of fish and some sauce) which we felt was way overpriced at 18 ringgit. We didn't enjoy the vegetable dish (called something like angled beans with fish flavour) and left the plate half-full - definitely the first time that has happened in Malaysia! Furthermore, when we returned a few days later (a Tuesday) to pick up some popiahs for lunch the place was strangely closed, although it had been open for lunch the previous day. There was no signage to explain the closure.Show less

Author: Don T
Title: Great food
Review: It's spicy it's tasty and cheap. It's reL no ya food. Be careful as it has limited opening hours and if you arrive after 6pm you will miss out.

Author: Aurcka
Title: GENUINE NYONYA CUISINE
Review:
authentic nyonya (local race between chinese male and malay female) cuisine
service friendly, do not have to wait long
good choice for evry taste
good value for price paid

Author: bertiekerrLima, Peru
Title: Excellent food and great value
Review: We visited here after doing the night market. We were a little lucky to get a seat as it was busy. It has a great atmosphere and is really friendly.We tried way too much - so that we could try a little of everything and the food was great. Really recommend this to try local food and a greta evening out.Show less

Author: NevillI
Title: Excellent food and price
Review: Randomly chose the restaurant and it was delicious. Staff friendly. Went back for a second meal and it was consistently good.

Author: panadollgalSingapore, Singapore
Title: Really nice Nonya food in Melaka
Review: My first time trying out Nancy's kitchen and i must admit that they serve really good nonya food... best so far as to the rest that i had tried in Melaka. The shop is in a small little lane which you might missed out if its your first visit. A must try Chicken Candlelight... A dish which we enjoyed very much...Show less

Author: barveSingapore, Singapore
Title: For an authentic Nonya experience
Review: Nancy's kitchen seemed to be a popular place in Malacca and after I ate there I could see why. If you want to try authentic nonya food then this is the place to come to. The decor is nothing to write home about, in fact it is quite basic. However the food makes up for that in spades. Plus they also sell local snacks if you want to take home a food memory.Show less

Author: yenlung
Title: Food so so only
Review: Food not hot while serving... the taste is so so only...but cendol is nice. good location.. must try the cendol...

Author: food_heiressMalmo, Sweden
Title: Buah Keluak is excellent!
Review: Actually every dish is very good. I've not eaten anything here that I didn't like. I have to say though their pineapple tarts are very expensive compared to a good one like LW (start of Jonker Walk). One dish you have to try is the Buak Keluak. You can order as many of those truffle-like nuts as you want. But be warned, it's an acquired taste!Show less

Author: drsfr
Title: Not worth a visit.
Review: We went as per recommendation from a tour guide. We tried the nyonya cakes pineapple tarts chendol and laksa. Really average and nothing memorable. We had better lalsa at calanthe cafe and chendol at the food court in pahlawan mall. Go elsewhere for nyonya food.

Author: haihangvncaChina
Title: Excellent food
Review: It was my last time trying Nonya food but my wife tried many Nonya resto in Singapore. We both enjoyed the authenticity of the food taste. Its definitely a must-try restaurant. The queue is long but worth it. We didn't expect much from service because it's a family restaurant. They are authentically care about their foods and customers. We definitely want to go back there one day if re visit Melaca again.Show less

Author: bentong66
Title: Get your tarts and traditional cookies here!
Review: Didn't stop for a meal this time around, but picked up all our traditional favourites here.  Pineapple tarts are highly recommended!

Author: Wendy8088Tonbridge, United Kingdom
Title: Don't believe the hype, over-rated!
Review: We went there earlier than the opening times, staff were adamant that they will be shut and only open at 11:30am, so we tried to find out if we could grab a table and even just browse the menu first. Instead we were told to wait outside and basically stood waiting under the hot sun at that time of the day!! The queue started to form quite long and we saw families queuing with kids and we patiently waited until 11:30am. But there was no sign of opening until probably around 11:40-11:45am! If the food was great it would have compensated for all the unpleasantness that we encountered. We tried the nyonya laksa - being a nyonya myself I know what they should taste like and unfortunately this one didn't make the cut and it was below average, pai tee - quite good, with very spicy chili sauce, popiah - average nothing memorable and apam balik durian - would not have it again, it was not very good. I don't know what the hype were and clearly this restaurant is quite over-rated! Unfortunately, the Peranakan food scene in Melaka has deteriorated just as quickly as the speed of the new hotels mushrooming all across town over the recent years.Show less

Author: vong3333Singapore
Title: Interesting experience
Review: Heard a lot about this place and finally went there for lunch on a Friday. Went there with my hubby and 2 kids. Reach the place around 1145 and there is already a group of 12 in the queue. They opened at 12 and we were given a table for 4 downstairs. Food is so so, perhaps we didn't order the right ones because we ordered those non spicy fried rice, soup and Kang kong. The Assam fish is good and otak is ok. Will recommend for those who have not been there it is not worth queuing for it. Saw a long queue when we left the place after lunch at 1pm.Show less

Author: tomwi2London, United Kingdom
Title: A must visit
Review: Everything one reads about eating in Melaka recommends Nancy's Kitchen so we were a bit skeptical but it really is very good. Yes, it's quite small, and you sit fairly close to other tables, but it's not exactly cramped as some of the reviews suggest. We sat downstairs, right at the front, so perhaps upstairs is more crowded...The staff speak good English and other than a brief mix-up with one of our dishes being delivered to the wrong table the service was fine and the food reasonably priced.The chicken candlenut is particularly delicious!Show less

Author: michaeltang64Hong Kong, China
Title: Food Great, Service Nil
Review: We started queuing for this restaurant at 11:45. We were seated at roughly 12:30 but our food did not come until 2:00. By the time we finished it was 2:40. We had close to a 3 hour lunch!Don't be mistaken though. The waitress's attitude throughout the meal was sincere and nice. They just weren't able to streamline their logistics efficiently to serve their customers promptly. The waitress apologized a couple of times and we accepted it, but those in a hurry might want to consider elsewhere. Food wise it's flavorful but I would not consider it unique. It's typical Nnonya food in a touristy street. They do have a wide collection of Nnonya food in a comfortable setting hence those who are newcomers to Melaka may give it a shot. Show less

Author: kelvincokelite
Title: Be prepared to queue
Review:
Affordable gastronomic peranakan cuisine. The must haves are the otah, kuehs, chendol....the list goes on...

The down side is the long wait for the limited tables. 

Friendly staffs. 

Highly recommended.

Author: Kail1
Title: Affordable Nyonya food
Review: Our group of seven managed to get a table without queueing on a Saturday night. We find the food tasty and affordable. The otah, Popiah, Assam prawns, rendang were good.

Author: mokurene
Title: Tasty Nyonya Foods
Review: Tasty and mouth-watering nyonya foods like Asam Nanas Prawn, Otak-otak & Popia. Like the Popia very much. Spicy but can't resist to take mores of it.

Author: nandychandySingapore, Singapore
Title: Nonya Food
Review: We had to queue quite long to get in and it was almost 2pm where most of the lunch crowd would be gone. Service was a little bit slow but the food was good. Ordered the pongteh, Chicken with Candle Nut curry or something like that. The Chendol was awesome and you can taste the gula melaka in it. Might be a little too sweet for some. Would love to go there again to try the other dishes. Show less

Author: Amanda W
Title: Delicious Nyonya food
Review: Very good traditional nyonya food served quickly in basic surroundings.  Be prepared to queue as it's very popular.

Author: Kelljl
Title: Average nyonya fare
Review: Very average nyonya fare. Only the pie tee made an impression. Chicken ponteh was too oily. Everything else was forgettable. Can probably get better nyonya food elsewhere.

Author: AnnagansyKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: wasting my time to queue for poor food and terrible service
Review: My 2nd visit to Nancy's Kitchen was full with disappointment. Their service are terrible and the food are no longer delicious comparing to my 1st visit (almost 2 years ago).Before their business hours, I went to Nancy's Kitchen to reserve a table. They rejected my reservation and informed that they only accept walk-in customers. I have no issues on this and decided to come back during their business hours.When I went back to Nancy's Kitchen, there are many people queued in front of it and I joined the queue. After 15 minutes of waiting, a group of foreign tourists (almost 20 pax) arrived at the restaurant and the staff said their tables are being reserved & directed them to upstairs. I felt very angry because they told me that they only accept walk-in customers but in fact they do reserve table for foreign tourists. Isn't it a double standard? After 45 minutes of waiting and the queue is not moving, my family and I decided to leave and come back on the next day. On the 2nd day, we went to Nancy's Kitchen 30 minutes before their business hours to queue. When it reached the business hours (as mentioned in their notice board), the staff just taking their own sweet time to pack the nyonya kuih and keep the customers waiting outside. Some of the customers requested the staff to let them go inside but the staff refused by giving the reason they haven't finished the preparation work. After waiting another 15-20 minutes, the staff just willing to open the door and let the customers go inside. We ordered cendols, fried mee hoon, asam fish, asam sotong, veggie, chicken & etc, and we are quite disappointed that it were tasteless.Given the terrible service and poor food, we will not visit Nancy's Kitchen again. It's wasting time to queue for such a terrible service and poor food.Show less

Author: Lafemme_12Luzon, Philippines
Title: Cuisine Full of Flavors
Review: I heard a lot of reviews about this resto & finally get to try it on our 3rd day in Malacca. At first, we just tried the food in hawkers since we knew that if the rslesto has good reviews, expect long queues. Since, we were curious if it's really good, we were patient enough even if we already arrived late, around 1:36 for lunch. As expected, the queue was long & I almost gave up & told my bf that if it doesn't move w/in 5-10 mins we'll try the other resto nearby. For some reason, we were patient enough & almost waited 20 mins to be seated & another 15 mins or so to have our food served. The foods were not that fancy & just served in ordinary dish which was just fine at least serving portion is enough to make you full. We ordered chicken candlenut, chicken in tamarind & chinese fried rice. I highly recommend their one of signature dishes- chicken candlenut. I like the nutty taste of the sauce & the flavor of the lemon grass. However, i didnt know that it was a bit spicy 'cuz I am not really fond of chilli (as it wasn't indicated on the menu) but it was tolerable. The other dish was also good but was a bit sweet w/c I am not also a fan of sweet viands. They didn't have much choices when it comes to drinks. I tried the honey lemon juice w/c was not that good. I was supposed to order either the fresh mango or soursop juice but the waitress told me that they were not available. Only to find out that those same drinks were ordered by the gueata next to us. They also make popiahs w/c we failed to order. The place was not really that comfy since it was not really that huge. We were seated on the 2nd flr & we had to pass their kitchen & saw lots of supplies cluterred everywhere. Also, the same waitress was a bit rude as she raised her voice to a group of Chinese guests when the latter took their seats when the table wasn't cleared yet. She told them that they were not supposed to seat until the the table was cleaned. She should have said it the nice way. Good thing, the Chinese group didn't take her seriously & just smiled. Perhaps, the waitress was just tired since there are lots of guests coming nonstop. Nevertheless, the good food outweighed the bad customer service & I could say that our long wait was paid off. Likewise, price was also reasonable, 1 dish costs around RM12. On the whole, I still recommend it since it was one of the best dishes I had in Malacca.Show less

Author: YingHusainSingapore, Singapore
Title: Good Nyonya Food
Review: This was our second time to Nancy's Kitchen. When we came here almost 18 months ago, we felt that the food was better and we also were able to order what we wanted. This most recent visit felt like a bit of a let down as they had run out of a few of our favorites. That being said, we did have some great vegetables and squid and the flavor was just as authentic as we remembered it being. We waited in line for about 30 minutes before we were seated, and I would say that any longer and I'm not sure the food would have been worth the wait.Show less

Author: Buddymate77
Title: Good place to try Nyonya food
Review: Too many choice to choose. Feel like want to order all. Price is reasonable. Too bad, they closed very early. I will come back to try other of the food.

Author: VguudealSingapore
Title: Wonder why people keep coming?
Review: Food - terribleAmbience - noneCleanliness - rat houseService - more like self service you mean?!?Location - goodPrice - average, let's just say it reflects the quality of the food!Need I say more? Not worth the detour from Jln hang Jebat!!!!Show less

Author: GreenieSingaporeSingapore, Singapore
Title: Food is good...
Review: Well, good peranakan food fix can be found here. We liked the good. For the Singaporeans, order the Babi chinchaluk! Menu says only available in Melaka so we decided to try. We liked it! Yummy... Not for those who are not adventurous or don't like belachan though. The rest of it is classic good home cooked peranakan food! Ayam ponteh is thinner than I'm used to but still delicious... Kids had extra rice just to enjoy the gravy. The sotong sambal petani was nice too! That said for most of the normal food, we found ole sayang richer tasting albeit bigger/less personal set up more expensive! Show less

Author: DanChoo
Title: Good food worth the wait
Review: One of the best nonya foods around malaka. Must try the the house specialities.  Authentic taste. There is always a Q during weekends. Worth the wait.  Not the best chendol around.

Author: Kool123934Singapore, Singapore
Title: Authentic Peranakan Restaurant
Review: This restaurant is situated at a double storey shop-house off Jonka Street and very close to most of the tourist attractions of this historical city, rich in Peranakan (Straits Chinese) culture. The restaurant serves authentic Peranakan dishes. We like dishes such as “Popiah”, “Ayam Buah Keluak”, “Assam Prawn”, “Deep Fried Soft Shell Crab” and “Fish Maw Soup”. Must be prepared to wait especially during holiday seasons, weekends and peak hours. Prices are reasonable, you can typically get a good meal for 2 at less than RM50.00 including drinks.Show less

Author: amy2kChicago, Illinois
Title: Excellent food!
Review: For the rave reviews this restaurant has already received, I was surprised to find a simple store front of a seemingly uninviting place. It is located on a side street near the Geographer's Cafe. It sits right next to a Portuguese restaurant, and a nice bar. All these other places look more appealing than this Kitchen. But don't let the look fool you. Inside, the decor is rather plain, it reminds me of a simple Chinese restaurant. Since I just came from Penang where many restaurant servings seem to be small, I ordered 2 dishes. The waiter said that should be more than enough. Indeed he was right. They were both wonderfully prepared, delicious and in good portions. Besides, they priced them right :-) If you are in the area, don't miss the chance to try some soft wrap rolls, spicy rips, and Nonya style fish.I wish the owner can consider up-ing the decor a little to make the place more memorable.Show less

Author: 123bath123
Title: great food
Review: great food here. very 'local' feeling to the place (despite its popularity). the style is traditional, simple, good value, good food. wel worth a visit.

Author: Karene HVancouver, Canada
Title: not fantastic
Review: most of my Singaporean friends would go here for their Melakan Peranakan fix, but I think the food here is just average -- not the best, and portions generally small. the service also borders on being below average... but their kueh pie tee is one of the best in the area, much better than the overrated ones around jonker.Show less

Author: gavinb340Marseillan, France
Title: Authentic
Review: Very busy small restaurant in heart of town. You have to queue but its worth it. The tophat staters are wonderful and most mains are very good but avoid the pork; tough and tasteless. The service is efficient and friendly and its very good value - £20 for 4!Show less

Author: Rosy CPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Good Nonya Food
Review: The candlenut chicken was really delicious, exactly the taste I used to eat at my relative, who was a nonya, a long time ago. Their popiah is huge for the price of RM4 and the sambal sauce in it was really yummy.They have a lot of delicious Nonya kueh too and Nonya dumpling wihich is equally good. A good place for nonya food in Malacca.Show less

Author: ElleM777
Title: Lucky to get in!
Review: Small space and very popular with good reason.  Nancy helped us select some food (vegetarian daughter) food so tasty and authentic!  Go if you can!

Author: 62Denise
Title: Yummy and simpe food
Review: Was there for the day and my friend and I went in for lunch. We had soft shell crab which wasn't the best Ive ever had but still very good. The laksa was amazing, couldn't get enough of it. Spring rolls also very nice.

Author: Geneveive
Title: Average Peranakan Food
Review: The food was average compared to the last time we dined here. Service could have been faster as we waited quite a while for our food.

Author: Ian MBath, UK
Title: Great place to eat
Review: The decor of this restaurant is fairly basic, more like a cafe. However the extensive menu is great value. Service was also good, which deserves mention because every table was full with a queue of at least 10 people waiting for a table whilst we had our meal. Highly recommendedShow less

Author: 640herbertl
Title: Over-rated
Review: My family and I went on a weekday. So not so crowded. The drinks I ordered are too sweet for anyone to take. I meant I have been in Thailand for some years and able to accept their kind of sweet level, this is really sweet. Too bad that I have a Nyonya Grandmum and mother, I would just said the food is average even comparing to other pernarakan restaurants in Melaka. The good thing is the location in the heart of the old town. Any tourist can reach there easily. Service wise.....slightly lower than average. Sitted for a long time and nobody really bother to serve you. I can excuse you if totally crowded, but as a walk-in and can get a seat immediately. Meaning.....you are not valued. The attitude is like .....not happy....dun come. I would like to state that there was no disputes or unpleasant instances during my dinning experience there. My comment merely from what I saw and feel thru the way the staff run the place. Will not come back.....they probably will not bother also.Show less

Author: Candy L
Title: Disappointed lunch at Nancy's Kitchen
Review: Lesson 1 - long q formed outside the shop far after it stated opening hour at 11am on Sat, allowed to go in at 12pmLesson 2 - Anticipating the food should be nice after what trip advisor commented, turned up to be very disappointed, chap Chye was cold and kang kong was old.Lesson 3 - service wAs poor. Ordered honey lime but tasted like sour plum and they insisted bluntly it was honey lime! Never go there anymore n I shall recommend all to try the little nonya near jonker boutique hotel, at least the food are hot when serveShow less

Author: cmkohSingapore, Singapore
Title: Good nonya food at a good price
Review: A nice little place which you may miss if not for the queue that forms rain or shine outside the restaurant. The signs are not obvious and you will easily be distracted by its neighbours with their more attractive signs. But the queue which are almost always there during the opening hours will lead you to it no problem.The wait isn't that long actually. Turnover is reasonably fast. Bring an umbrella if you can't stand the elements.Don't expect too much of the interiors decos. And don't expect 5 star service too. They won't expect you to pay 5 star prices or even tips.The food is excellent, for the price we paid. So if you are expecting michelin stars worthy culinary then you have to look elsewhere. Maybe KL.There are also baked nonya cookies etc at the cashier if you like. I bought the pineapple tarts which I loved.Show less

Author: vivien02
Title: popian
Review: I bought the popian from their stalls. quite good ! the line for the restaurant is always very long. but if you just go for popian, then no need for waiting

Author: Nwabuike UKuala Lumpur, Wilayah Persekutuan, Malaysia
Title: Good place
Review: Was here with a local and some other people (All friends). We had a very good time trying the local cuisine and it was a good meal. Quite a small place not spacious; you would have to queue before it gets to your turn but the patience is worth, delicious delicacy, good value for money and friendly waitresses.Show less

Author: Abikoh
Title: Good food
Review:
Not the best but it's still a nice place to get your fill of nyonya food.
Their popiah and dumpling are not too bad.

Author: Gil G
Title: Shared table.
Review:
Friendly-ish waitresses. 
Have to share table with another 5 people. So there's an awkward moment of ordering the food. 
Full of signs warning you not to do anything. Spill water. Open window. Closure dates. Mind your head. Etc. 
price wasn't so bad.

Author: MunzterKl
Title: Good local food at a reasonable price..
Review: Local Peranakan food with a reasonable price. Service is non-existent but look past that and you've got yourself a decent and satisfying dinner.

Author: happybaby03Singapore, Singapore
Title: Horrible service!
Review: Read up the review about this restaurant so we decided to give a try. There was no one attending to us when we are at the door. It was the lovely customers whom sitting around told us there were more seats available upstairs since they seen we have big groups. Headed up with the narrow steps and the waitress upstair stop us from going up saying that is full house no place at all. So we went down again and notice one big round table only 2 seats occupied so we wanted to share the table. Just when we are arranging the seats a man came out say sorry you all cannot sit here cos we cannot walk at all. I am so angry and asked my friend loudly have he order anything if not let's go ... is total a waste of time and I will not spend my money here! No point spending money on this lousy service there are plenty of nice yummy food located at Jonker!Show less

Author: Mong2902Singapore, Singapore
Title: Disappointing meal
Review: We always visit Nancy's kitchen whenever we are in Malacca. However this trip to Nancy's proved to be the worst ever. The sek bak that we ordered was cooked so tough I could not even chew it apart. The sambal belachan cost RM3 and it was dry, salty and blah. My MIL could do better. There was no oomph to the chicken curry and the cincalok omelette was not nice.Noticed filipinos cooking in the kitchen.. perhaps tastebuds are different. We used to be able to call to make a reservation but no this trip. Was told to come and queue. We queued for 45 min and there were 16 of us. Surely this is our last visit to Nancy's. What a shame.Show less

Author: Daniel C
Title: Close early and the Indonesia worker so rude
Review: Quite sad when I went there raining with my wife and son.. The worker so rude and said.. sudah tutup, tak nampak.. Only 3.30pm and they close.. operations hour is until 5.30pm.

Author: debubhatnagarGurugram (Gurgaon), India
Title: Nyonya ah!
Review: We visited this restaurant largely due to its internet reviews and we were not disappointed. The good was great from the start. The summer rolls were fairly good and the soft crab was crunchy. The beef was a bit disappointing but the fish was simply great. Don't order the fried rice just stick with the steamed. The chicken came in a rich gravy sort of like what you find in Kerala so one could see the fusion of culture right there on the plate.We ate a lot. This is a restaurant that we had to queue up to get into in the hot weather. But it was worth the wait. Great food.Show less

Author: EllaLeowSingapore, Singapore
Title: disappointed meal
Review: Pretty excited to try after reading all the reviews and also encountered the long q in Aug when we came to Melaka but didnt have a chance to taste it. Finally we were there and no q at all at 4pm on sunday. We had Ngor Hiang (was ok, not crispy), Fried omelette with shrimps (average with few shrimps), Fish maw with meatballs soup (average, soup wasnt hot), Prawns with Tamarind sauce (Prawns were not fresh), Chicken rendang (not bad) and Chendol (not too good, pathetic amount of green jelly and red beans) for dessert.Food was served fast as it was not crowded but kinda cold when served..Price was reasonable but food was so so.Overall: Would rather try other nonya place then returning and not worth the effort to Q.Show less

Author: kuaychapSingapore, Singapore
Title: Prime location, shame about the taste
Review: Had a late lunch at Nancy's on Saturday, basically because it was just around the corner from the Courtyard @Heeren where we were checking in. We last ate there four years ago, though we've been coming up to Malacca at least once a year in the meantime. It was busy, but we got our table for 6 in the front room after about a 20 minute wait. Turnover was quite fast and tables for four were available sooner.The menu looked tempting, especially as it had pork dishes, unlike all the other Peranakan restuarants I have tried in Malacca. The kuay pie tee was good, and the pohpiah ok. But the main dishes didn't do it - the shiokometer barely budged. Those unfamiliar with Nonya cuisine may come away impressed. We remembered why we hadn't been back for four years.Show less

Author: chubbyhugsSingapore
Title: Delicious Nonya Food
Review: We ordered a few dishes including the otah, kueh pie tee and kangkong, and all were delicious. Do try the kueh pie tee which can be ordered outside the shop, but there is a queue for it and if you come at the wrong time, it may be sold out. The eatery was crowded when we went and do not expect first-class service and pristine plates/cutlery as it's a local eatery.Show less

Author: formulafrog GCairns, Australia
Title: A major disappointment
Review: This restaurant had rave reviews in our guidebook, and seems to be relying on that legacy. It had queues out the door everytime we went past it (on the weekend). When we did go it was a huge disappointment. The starter was good, but the main course of duck was a bowl of bones. The staff seemed unhappy and disinterested.Show less

Author: Jackie C
Title: very busy, good food helpful staff
Review: First taste of Peranaken food, really enjoyed it, given good advice from the waiter. Good meal, spicy and tasty

Author: CeciltongSingapore
Title: Have they become too successful, for the customer's good ?
Review: We were in the Jonker Street area and wanted Peranakan food for dinner, and so Nancy's came to mind. We were there about 8.30 pm and they were still serving.
