Nancy, who was sitting at a counter near the kitchen, was too busy counting money to pay much heed to us other than to tell us to go upstairs. Her staff took our order, served it and left us alone. When we wanted to order more rice and drinks, I had to go to the stairs at the back and shout down to the staff at the ground floor, who shouted back curtly that the kitchen was closed. The food is ok, but definitely not the best in Melaka. As a customer, I felt that they were mainly interested in making a profit and not in the customer's dining experience. We visited Amy's Heritage Cuisine on the same trip and had a far better experience - in value, the quality of the food and in the service, as well.Show less

Author: PaulG_SydneySydney
Title: Great food and excellent value in a modest setting
Review: Nancy's Kitchen was recommended by the good people at Heeren Hotel for its traditional nonya cuisine. We ordered 6 dishes and none failed to impress. My traveling buddy ordered what I thought would be a standard pork ribs dish... but the sauce and tenderness of the meat just blew me away. i ordered a stuffed pickled chilli dish and was so amazed i was very reluctant to share... the soft-crab dish was also heaven for the senses. This was a spectacular lunch eaten at a venue that did not really give a hint of the quality food they serve and was all done at a very modest price. A very pleasant outing for my taste-buds and I will be sure to visit again when I next go back... I may even just do a day trip from KL for the enjoyment. Well done guys!!!Show less

Author: Tasfamily2013Launceston, Australia
Title: Nice place - good food and service.
Review: Children were challenged by the choices and weren't going to eat anything but they came around when the candlenut chicken arrived and at it all! Fried rice just OK. Laksa OK. Vegetable curry with coconut mild OK. Candlenut chicken big winner! Service excellent and location in Jonker street convenient. Overall: good!Show less

Author: TrupNew York, NY
Title: Go for the spring rolls!
Review: The spring rolls were outstanding --- among the best I have ever eaten; the duck was not better than average. Cute little place between two primary streets; service was just fine and setting was also fine. But if I were to return, I'd start and perhaps finish my meal with those spring rolls!Show less

Author: KatarzynaPeWarsaw, Poland
Title: Special place
Review: The restaurant offers traditional baba-nyonya food. The names of the dishes tell you nothing, but probably everything you try will be delicious. A perfect place to feel the atmosphere of Melaka, very nicely decorated. You will be delighted, unless you meet a roaring group of Chineese tourits ;)Show less

Author: Steven_TeoTawau, Malaysia
Title: unique taste but could improve on service
Review: There were 9 of us in our group. This restaurant was highly recommended to us when we planned our trip there. We arrived there at about 2:40pm way passed the lunch crowd. We wondered in and the tables were taken except or a table of 4. We were not sure whether we should wait or take the table for 4 and wait for another table to be empty. We waited inside the restaurant which did not have enough room for our group and the temperature outside was blazing hot. So, we were literally standing where we could find an individual space to stand. At that point we were totally lost as to what we were to do and no one came and told us what our status was. By that time more people were entering the already packed place. From nowhere, a sign "CLOSED" was then placed on the glass door. By this time which was 3:30pm we were still not told what our status was. It was until we enquired who we could speak to our status was finally clarified. We finally was seared at about 3:40pm Terrible!Nancy's cooking genre is called Nyonya, style. A number of her dishes were new to my taste buds and therefore I did not WOW over it. But I also have to mention the majority in my group liked the unique taste of the food.Show less

Author: EliiiADBristol, United Kingdom
Title: Super Delicious food, but lack of customer service
Review: The food was super delicious without any doubt and I love to try it again once I go back to Melaka! The owner was very welcoming person.But we have been waiting for one hour in a queue to enter the restaurant. After one hour we entered the restaurant and ordered our food, but we had to re-order after 30 minutes, because the waiter forgot what we ordered. Customer service needs to be improved there not food for sure.Show less

Author: ReiseVacances
Title: Delicious food
Review: Delicious food, but price is on high side. Go there if you are willing to pay. Long queue during weekends for both lunch and dinner

Author: Benjaminrpthomas
Title: Best Malay food we had in our whole trip.
Review: This is a fantastic restaurant. The candlenut chicken, an original recipe, is amazing. Nancy, the lovely owner, also runs great cooking lessons in the kitchen behind.

Author: serenesam
Title: I prefer Kocik's kitchen.
Review: The place is rather run down. Thank God we didn't have to queue up, or else it's a waste of time for the kind of quality of food.

Author: jervis21
Title: Authentic nonya cuisines
Review: Tucked in the corner of a small lane, it is the gem of Jonker street. What I love is the popiah and nonya curry here! Definitely a must try!

Author: lundberg105Beijing
Title: Decent food, more expensive than we wanted to pay
Review: The food was average. I was expecting much more from the packed house that we walked into and the recommendations from a few different people. It was alright. A bit expensive for our budget. A one meal splurge every now and then never hurt anyone.

Author: GwenC875Singapore, Singapore
Title: Order the rice?!
Review: Yes you must have the rice because the dishes were so good with the the rice. We ordered the chicken buah keluak, sambal sotong(squid) and petai, asam pork and chap chai (mixed-vegetable) and we just loved the gravy mixed with the rice. The dishes looked ordinary, however each spoonful of the sauce and the meat just yielded such rich and wonderful taste.I must say having had tried many peranakan food in Singapore, none measure up to what I had in Nancy's. We also tried the popiah(wrap with stewed turnip) and again I was won over by the skin and the ingredients in it. Please do not let the lack of presentation of the food and the ambience deter you from enjoying this true blue traditional peranakan food.Show less

Author: sporestrikerSingapore, Singapore
Title: Tasty Nyonya food.
Review: Heard great reviews and wanted to try this restaurant out for a long time so we were happy to finally get a chance to try it out. Small place with limited tables so you have to queue up for a while. Food was one of the best Nyonya food that we have tried so far. Worth the wait. Will certainly go back again.Show less

Author: sadee_raghavanSubang Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Food is good
Review: This is a good place to eat Baba-Nyonya food. The food is good but the place should be bigger... just a little bigger. I found it claustrophobic but enjoyed the food anyway. I wanted to speak to the owner about the place but she had only enough time to take a photograph with us. And even then, only after I said I write reviews. It was too business-like but I guess that's what it's all about for them.Owners of such restaurants should make time to mingle with their customers who, I'm sure have questions. Nevertheless, a good place to have Baba-Nyonya food. How authentic is it? I honestly don't know. Summary: The food is definitely good but the ambiance needs a lot of improvement. Putting up photos of early Nyonyas is not enough. Hope they improve on this.Show less

Author: NewZealand-7AUCKLAND, NEW ZEALAND
Title: Best food we had in Malacca
Review: This place is sooo good. Incredible value, beautifully cooked. Free Wi Fi. If downstairs is full - which it was -don't be deterred. We had the upstairs room to ourselves. The waiter didn't think we'd be able to eat what we ordered - about 4 dishes for lunch. We got through it no problem. It was so delicious.We tryed other restaurants, but this was by far the best. Just good home cooking.Show less

Author: WessandCorinne
Title: A good recommendation
Review: This is what we'd been looking for. Third generation using old recipes handed down. Cold beers, wifi, limited English but they know what u want when u point on the menu.  A definite must try.

Author: Tim HMelbourne, Australia
Title: Didn't live up to reviews
Review: Tried to get to enjoy the nyonya style of cuisine while in Melaka but couldn't find anything particularly outstanding that wasn't overpowered by oyster sauce. Was hoping Nancy's would excel but in our experience, didn't particularly come out as exceptional. Food was fresh and well prepared, however. Show less

Author: HelenaGuerraWashington DC, District of Columbia
Title: Amazing Experience
Review: Tip: try the onde. A delicous coconut sweet.Pros: delicious food, good value for money.We shared a popiah (4 slices) roll. A lady was cooking them outside. They are really yummy. Then we had a small duck ribs with cilantro and Peranakan chicken curry. Both were terrific.We also tasted the Chinese cold tea. Very refreshing.In the end you can go to the kitchen area and get some sweets. We bought a box of onde. Delicious small coconut sweets.Show less

Author: Christopher KSingapore
Title: For individuals with patience and crave for local taste ....
Review: Distinctive crowd outside the restaurant ... Service standards highly dependent on individual mood swings, you do get kind & warm services from individuals along with disastrous crude remarks from other others.Had tasted much better peranakan food in other locations ... but this is definitely one of the easiest to locate near jonker streetPrice point is considered high by local standards ... costing around MYR$40 per person.A one time visit affair for me ... Show less

Author: Lizardqueen57
Title: Best Otah
Review: I liked the cosiness of this restaurant. It's like eating at someone's house. The otah is so yummy. The opening hours of the restaurant is quite confusing.

Author: Oratory1Singapore, Singapore
Title: best nonya food in town
Review: excellent food with a vast menu to choose from. Reasonable prices and authentic setting. A short walk to jonker street. Be patient as it is a very busy restaurtant and the staff have lots of orders to take. Arrive before 830 as the kitchen normally closes by 9pm. There is always a queue of customers wanting tables which is a good sign.Show less

Author: RoscoeHR
Title: Don't miss out. It's what I expected to find but took a while to come across
Review:
Here is exactly what I was looking for in Melaka. All the regional classics done well.
The dish cooked with the black nuts is an experience, the flavor is completely unique. All the dishes are executed well and the place is cozy and welcoming.

Author: KlokaniPattaya, Thailand
Title: Worth the wait - authentic nonyan food
Review: Well I don't really know what "authentic" Nonyan food should be but I bet its close here, its awesome flavours and combinations kept us ordering more and more food. Small and cosy with an upstairs section, I don't think it seats too many people and its really popular so be prepared to wait for a seat. We went there the first time in the early evening before about 7pm and there were no queues, we decided to walk around the Jonker Street markets and came back about an hour later and the line up was horrendous. Came back the next day for lunch, the line up was smaller and worth the wait of 20 minutes for a seat. We sat near the kitchen and you need to walk through it to get to the bathroom, interesting to watch them put the meals together. This place is a must do when in Melaka.Show less

Author: LEE Jsingapore
Title: Disappointed
Review: My friend found this cafe so we gave it a try during lunchtime about 2pm. Queues were already forming outside. It wasn't really a big restaurant. Food wasn't really fantastic which I expected more as it was highly raved. We tried the kuehs which wasn't to my liking as well. Won't come back again. Show less

Author: Ruby84
Title: Great popiah
Review: Nancy is a bit on the peculiar side and enforces her closing hours strictly.  However, her popiah were the best we ate in all of Malaysia.

Author: GrouchoSydney
Title: Really, really good.
Review: Without doubt one of Melaccas top spots. Excellent menu, authentic dishes, great value, excellent service and not just for tourists with many regulars from the local community.

Author: onglaysanSingapore, Singapore
Title: Good Nyonya Food
Review: A long queue outside the restaurant before its opening hour. Though, the restaurant is one of the old Melaka house, the space inside are quite spacious with 2 levels. The dishes we tried are good and considered quite authentic. However, you might have to bear with limited services due to their constant crowds in the restaurants.Show less

Author: justme439Singapore, Singapore
Title: expensive and disappointment
Review: last week, 2 of us brought our relatives to visit Malaca and went to this place, had the following :-- popiah ( so so ) -- egg cincalok ( above average)-- ayam buah keluak (4 pieces of keluak) (so so)-- prawn petai ( where were the prawn ?? just tiny shrimp and a few pieces of petai)-- chendol ( smaller portion and less flavorful compared to what one could get in Jonker street)we were the only local eating there while the rest were europeans. the way of preparing the kuih pie tee was not hygienic. the lady worker used bare hand to pick up the ingredients. i suspect that our popiah was similarly prepared !! agree with some reviewers that cheaper and better food could be had at some other places.Show less

Author: BradJill THong Kong, China
Title: Nancy's Kitchen - Indeed an excellent local dining experience!
Review: We visited Nancy's Kitchen at recommendation of our guesthouse manager and were very much impressed with the dishes we tried here. This was a very good late lunch meal, one we will specifically seek out next time we visit Malacca. Nancy's is located just off Jonker Street amongst quite a few other bar/restaurants so you have to look for the sign. Inside it is just 5-6 tables with basic decor. This is an unassuming restaurant, serving up some very good local dishes. Staff were friendly and helpful, suggesting that we only order the small size as it was enough food. We sampled two chef recommendations and very much enjoyed them both. First, we tried the small portion of the Peranakan Braised Pork (Sek Bak) - (RM12) that was very good. The pork was succulent and the combination of spices used to marinate and cook this dish made it delicious. Some sweet chill sauce was provided to give it just a bit of kick. Even if you don't like spice, we recommend putting just a touch of the sauce on each bite as it accentuates and enhances the natural flavours of this braised pork dish. Can't think of many ways to improve this one (rating 4.5 of 5), would happily order again. We also tried a small portion of the Chicken Candlelight (RM12) that was a stellar dish. This included some local nut variety that we are not familiar with and a fine concoction of local spices, lemongrass and other ingredients that made this dish - a 'wow' on the taste scale. Chicken was slow cooked in the sauce so the tastes went through nicely. Recommend ordering the medium or larger portion instead of small size as its hard to imagine diners not enjoying this one (rating 5 of 5). Overall, this was a great meal, one we would be happy to repeat with more time in Malacca. Can highly recommend based on our experience at Nancy's Kitchen.Show less

Author: WiserTravellerLondon, United Kingdom
Title: High Quality Nyonya Cuisine
Review: One of our best meals in Melaka. If you want a taste of real Nyonya cooking you can't go wrong with Nancy's. They have slightly odd opening hours so best to phone ahead, check the times and book a table.The Kway Pie Tee, Popiah, Lor Bak and Laksa were all great and authentic. The setting is also very nice in an old style Peranakan house. There is another room upstairs so for larger groups don't think there are only the few tables on view downstairs.Show less

Author: RosiePerth123Dundee, United Kingdom
Title: An experience
Review: We ate here on 23 February, it had been recommended by hotel staff who also suggested which dishes to try....it was very busy and as a result we were given a table upstairs with no windows or outlook lacking any ambience but the ventilation was good....plastic picnic tables and chairs and sharing tables appeared to be the norm.....The food was very good, no complaints but found being so close to the only toilet a little off putting....tables were within a few feet of the actual toilet....Staff were okay and service was prompt and food was fresh and hot.However not sure I would rush back as lots of other places to try.Show less

Author: ClerkenwellLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Prime location and reputation allows them to drop standards
Review: Nancy's is an institution. It serves Nyonyan cuisine and is located just off Jonkers Street. This makes it very convenient for the night market. It sells itself as an authentic Melakan experience. Unfortunately there are a number of other restaurants in the town that serve better food for the same price in cleaner surroundings.The surroundings are cramped and worn. You do walk through the kitchen to get through to the upstairs dining areas. It is quite a challenge to get past other eaters to reach the toilets, which in themselves are poor. The service is erratic because the waiting staff are stretched between the separated dining areas.The food is tasty and varied but, again, I think that they could make more of an effort. Our hotel served a better dish for breakfast. I wouldn't choose Nancy's as my one signature Nyonyan meal during my stay in Melaka.Show less

Author: Chippering
Title: Very Disappointed
Review: Surprised and disappointed by our meal there, given other glowing reports. Waitress uninterested and surly. Duck: bits of scraggy bone with hardly any meat in a glutinous sauce; chicken OK but not special.

Author: dputDallas, Texas
Title: Delicious tasty meal for 2 for under $10 USD
Review: Went here with my wife and got 3 dishes. 2 chicken and laksa. All the food was delicious. Do not go here if you are looking for bland western food. This food is very tasty and spicy. We enjoyed it very much and with 2 drinks it came out to under 10 bucks.The place is not fancy and you will find ants on the walls. However, the food was clean and the ants did not bother us. Definitely a must do in Melaka for local cuisine!Show less

Author: Kathryn H
Title: Not the best
Review: Both the food and fresh juices didn't seem to be prepared from the scratch, it definitely wasn't light on the stomach. We ordered meat in Tamarind sauce and chicken in coriander and it tasted similarly (weird). The ants parading on the wall didn't help either.

Author: Edwina TGeneva, Switzerland
Title: Great authentic food - go somewhere else for luxury
Review: If you want very authentic, delicious Nyonya food you cannot go wrong here. Fantastic interior, like eating in someone's living room, with family photos and antiques all around. Large menu with various portion sizes and all delicious. I think they also do take away.However it's not luxurious and doesn't pretend to be.Show less

Author: Zhenyu LSingapore
Title: Should try!
Review: My mum recommended me this place, asked me to get her some packed Sambal back. We ended up having lunch here instead and it really taste good! From the outside it doesn't look much, but the service is good and ventilation is good. Try the Chilli prawn and the popiah, they r really good. Get some cool drink (lime juice) to go along cos they r really spicy!Show less

Author: DavidDharmaraj
Title: Great food, but waitress was busy counting money...
Review: Food was great. Good insight on Peranakan food. Overhead the next table people (who was kind of loud and rude to the guy who was serving the food) that they came all the way from Singapore to try the place out. The only thing that spoilt it a bit was the waitress who was to busy counting the day's earning than to take orders from two starving people... The food made up for it though.Show less

Author: Sasha MSydney, Australia
Title: Try the chicken with black nut...Devine
Review: This little restaurant doesn't look like much from the outside, but the food is delicious and a must try. We had three dishes here - the chicken and black nut, the popiah and the pork. All were tasty and the servings were large (even for the small size). The cost was reasonable. The atmosphere is like you have stepped into the front room of their home, very interesting. Show less

Author: HLoySingapore, null, Singapore
Title: Good place for Nyonya food
Review: Have seen reviews on this place and decided to bring my friends to try. Was there at about 2 plus on a Friday afternoon and there was no queue. Try the "Ayam Buah Keras - Chicken Candlenut", it's the signature dish and it's very tasty! Good old Peranakan style.Their fried egg with Chinchalok is also a must try, crispy and savoury at the same time! However, their sambal kangkong is quite different from the ones in Singapore, lesser shrimp taste and much more spicier. Apparently they are very busy on weekends, my friend was there and he said there was even no space to stand in the restaurant itself and the waitresses were super busy.Show less

Author: seluarlonggar
Title: Felt like being in a peranakan home
Review: Did not feel like a restaurant but more like someone's home From unpretentious decor to relaxed atmosphere Loved the authenticity from furniture to decor to music to food Must try is the ondeh ondeh - best ones i've ever eaten For lunch we had soft shell crab, assam prawns n special request kailan w garlic, white rice Sambal belachan was served as a condiment Sedap betul Then we had to hv chendol for dessert My meal at this restaurant was the highlight of my malaccan trip Meal for 3pax came to RM56!Show less

Author: 412khim
Title: Delicious kuih
Review: Good pie tee, oneh-oneh is very delicious(got the fragance of pandan leaves not colouring), popiah is yum too. I find that their chendol is good but a bit disppointed as I can not taste the fragance of gula melaka.

Author: buaya40
Title: a wealth of different tastes
Review: We always explore the different taste of the dishes related to the 'Baba-Nyonya' food when we are at Nancy's in Melaka. We had the 'tophead', Sek Bak, Kangkung Belacana, Pork Lard Popiah and Keluak Chicken.

Author: chengann
Title: Standards dropping?
Review: Second visit here. The food was still good but not remarkable. Something seemed amiss. Service and attention was still good despite the crowd.

Author: purple-lallangSingapore, Singapore
Title: Yummy Desserts
Review: We happened to walk past this place after our lunch, hence only tried some of their desserts. Loved the chendol and their bo bo char char (hot). We also tried their nonya dumpling, popiah and kueh pie tee. The kueh pie tee is good. Restaurant also sells various kuehs. Bought a box of pineapples tarts ( 30 pcs ) for RM$15 - nice.Show less

Author: VguudealSingapore
Title: Good food but poor service
Review: We pre-paiid for 30 over rice dumplings and requested that they steam 10 for us for the journey home. Despite explaining to them that it is meant for kids, who should not be eating cold food hung since morning, they did NOT do it, with the excuse that their steamer is spoilt! Try harder next time if you need to lie!Show less

Author: NuttyCheeseSingapore, Singapore
Title: Good food but slightly expensive
Review: We ordered deep fried squid, which was really good, chap chai which was good and the duck soup which I found a little too much on the sour side.Prices were alright, if a little expensive. Portion size was enough for two (3 dishes).I preferred Kocik restaurant for nonya food though. I liked the peranakan songs playing in the background though.Show less

Author: gussanuSingapore, Singapore
Title: Loved!
Review: Nancy's Kitchen was recommended to us by our bus guide and since we had read about it online as well we decided to go have a look. The food is fantastic! the location, brilliant and the pricing is great.We ate there every single day while we were at Malacca and we even took back some of her belachan and curry powder - it was that good!You must try the peranakan chicken curry , prawn sambal, four angled beans and the sour plum juice. Her portions are decent and more than enough to go around.Show less

Author: iron_symphonySingapore, Singapore
Title: Don't miss this place when you're in Melaka
Review: My partner and I had a very easy and light dinner here. It was my first time dinning here so I did not know what to expect and boy was I in for a treat.The retro setting was amazing and even though the kitchen is located right behind where I sat, I did not feel warm at all. The food was just delicious. No other words to describe it. The best time I would recommend visiting this place is around 5.30pm, that would ensure that you have a nice easy meal to take your time to finish, thereby entering the famous Jonker street at around 6.45pm, seeing them set up the stalls and experiencing the night life Melaka has to offer. Also by going slightly earlier, you would avoid the dinner crowd that my partner and I saw on the way back, there was a huge line! Goodness me, you can't go wrong with this place it seems.The snacks that they sell there are all freshly made on the day itself so we went back the following morning at 11am, just when they were ready to grab several boxes for our respective families before heading back to Singapore. So good were the snacks that we almost finished half of them before hitting the highway!My only mark against this establishment would be the fact that you will have to chase away some flies during your meal. Not really a downside but more of an irritation. Oh wells, I was so engrossed with the food, sometimes you might not notice! I'll surely be back when I can!Show less

Author: Roberto-Singapore
Title: Nancy's Kitchen in Melaka
Review:
Nice retro setting and good food. You have a choice of sitting on the ground level or upstairs with timber flooring.....good old feeling. 
Food is good and pricing reasonable. Hosts are friendly and atmosphere good.
They sell Nyonya kueh too !

Author: Y2079
Title: nice dumplings
Review: I did not dine in, but the dumplings are good. Rm5 now. the place is always crowded. the space is rather small, suggest to dine in early.

Author: Elite_Pinoi
Title: Peranakan food
Review: First it is very crowded, the front of the restaurant is not attractive at all.  Indoor not attractive too, taste of food is so so.  Service so so, nothing fantastic.

Author: Lucy J
Title: The best food I've eaten in Malaysia
Review: The food was delicious and the service was good.  We ate Laska and the candlenut chicken and LOVED both.  You have to go here!

Author: Huongwk
Title: Wise price and good food
Review:
Quite lots of selection for a little restaurant. Price is good for the food and drink. Searving is fast. The seats are limited and luckily i got one table while arrived. 

GPS Coordinate: N02° 11.778
                           E102° 14.753

Author: KeepMemoriesSingapore, Singapore
Title: Food is reasonabley good, snack is better
Review: Overall, food is reasonably good but not super. There is limited seating. Not a place that I would return particularly. The spring roll at the front of the shop looks tempting but turned out to be great disappointment. The spring roll skin is just too thick and chewy. And there is nothing particularly interesting for the filling. I love the snack available for retail. It is housed at the back of the resturant. The nonya rice dumpling are available in frozen orders for packing home.Show less

Author: bunnygoeszen
Title: Excellent nonya food
Review:
Must must must have the ayam buah keluak (an acquired taste though). They allow you to order as many buah kaluaks as you want! Heaven. 

The otak was really good too. 

Come in the morning for freshly baked kuehs. Delicious!

Author: Jenn_Woo
Title: Good food
Review: If you are staying around Jonker Street and is too lazy to drive around but wants good nyonya food, this is the place to go to. There is usually a queue but they are quite fast in ensuring you getting a table.

Author: sylveskeAntwerp, Belgium
Title: Good food, nice atmosphere
Review: Following our tourist guide, we had small lunch there and it was good! It's not too big, but there is a pleasant Chinese-noisy atmosphere. We had good food for a good price and also got in contact with one of the other guests, an older Chinese man. He invited us for the typical dessert, which was very good! I liked this place!Show less

Author: HumouresqueSingapore, Singapore
Title: Good food, good location.
Review: One of the few Nyonya restaurants that serve pork. Very nice food in a good location off Jonker St. A bit on the pricey side but most will find it ok. Very popular & busy during lunch & dinner times. When Nancy is there she will make you feel at home. Worth a visit!Show less

Author: SV S
Title: Excellent Nyonya Cuisine
Review: Nancy's Kitchen serves up some of the best traditional Melaka Nyonya food that I have tasted. I particularly recommend their kueh pai ti - delicate texture and full of flavour.

Author: RolandPriscillaSingapore, Singapore
Title: If you happen to walk past
Review: We heard so much about this restaurant and just had to try it when we were there over the weekend! The service is really lousy and they constantly just tell customers they are full without really giving us a gauge when our turn will be or where we can wait.Thankfully we found a big round table at the entrance and squeezed in with 2 other couples. We ordered the duck soup which tasted alittle odd, we found the smell and taste too strong. And the popiah skin was just too thick and the filling was so little.But the best food we ate there was the ngoh hiang which didnt taste too porky but just the right texture of filling and the Sambal prawns with petai. Again the petai portion was really measly but the prawns were pretty fresh with the right seasoning.Would I come back again? I guess not as I think there are better Peranakan food in Singapore and in Malaysia!Show less

Author: Chris R
Title: Even the small helpings were big!
Review: Very, very yasty njonja food.  Careful you don't over order as we did as the helpings are very generous. 2 meals 1 side dish, 2 rice, and 2 drinks came to RM 42. Try and eat downstairs as there is more character.

Author: pamela_flen77
Title: Good and Cheap food
Review: Enjoyed their perankan food, very tasty and yummy. Not expensive too:) after dinner, a nice walk along Jonker street:)

Author: lowchunmengSingapore, Singapore
Title: Excellent and affordable Peranankan cuisine
Review: Though I have been to Malacca many times, this is my first visit to Nancy's Kitchen. The service standards could be better but the food was excellent! We ordered the usuals - poh piah, babi ponteh, chup choi, otak etc. I was particularly impressed with the chup choi. The chef used such simple ingredients but the dish was really good. The babi ponteh and poh piah were above our expectations too.Show less

Author: icypen
Title: Standard has dropped
Review: I've visited Nancy's twice. First experience was gd (love the pie tee and chap cai).. Second was bad, same dish but had dry and salty chap cai. Plate was hot but chap cai is cold. I don't know why.. But pie tee is still good.

Author: Teresaling
Title: The kuih vy nice!
Review:
I go there on mon so not many so crowded at there.
The service attitude not bad.
The env got peranakan feeling and vy comfortable to hear the soft music.
The kuih vy sweet and the taste really vy nice!!!

Author: ChiccuzPGlasgow, United Kingdom
Title: a tasty lunch..
Review: We stopped at Nancy's for lunch to rest from the hot weather outside and we really enjoyed the food. We had two types of chicken and some veggie and of course boiled rice. All the food was good, simple atmosphere! I would definitely go back there and try all the other dishes!Show less

Author: stefanhosk
Title: your Melaka trip isn't complete without "Nancy's"
Review: i was told that chicken rice ball is a MUST try when u visit Melaka.my own humble opinion is that a small portion of chicken rice ball is ok, but must reserve a big stomach space for Nancy's. Nancy's Kitchen is a humble little local restaurant which may not be the fanciest restaurant in town but food is totally beyond the fanciest, Variety of choice of nyonya food on menu. I have tried different dishes, i don't really have a favourite because i just happened to love whatever i ordered on the Menu. And the plus point is, it is reasonably priced, maybe inexpensive to some.I normally visit Melaka during the weekday, which can explain why i never experienced the crowded situation.Show less

Author: Georgie GLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Worth the wait
Review: Rarely in SE Asia do you have to queue for a restaurant but in this case the 20 minute queue was certainly worth it. The food is cheap, the service is good and it is delicious! A perfect way to fully experience Malay food. Arriving early may ensure a shorter waiting queue but our later arrival meant that the staff had more time for us and were not rushing through our service to free our table. Definitely try the Laksa whilst there, it is not to be missed.Show less

Author: Fiona LSingapore, Singapore
Title: Average food, full of tourists
Review: Food was quite ordinary. We ordered the ayam buah keluah, ngoh hiang, shrimps with tamarind sauce, egg plant stir-fried with chicken. Chicken in ayam buah keluah was too tough. Flavor not cooked into the meat. Tasted like they cooked the chicken separately. Egg plant is way way way too salty. Shrimps not fresh. Only Ngoh hiang was crispy and good. Frankly, we were quite disappointed in the experience. Would recommend trying other more authentic peranakan restaurants. Show less

Author: penggu
Title: Authentic!
Review: Delicious dishes.  Love the assam fish, cant get enough of it.  Bought lots of local cookies and kway kway but the kway cannot keep too long as they all uses natural ingredients and have no preservertives but glad I ate quite a bit there.  Yum!

Author: caroistaaPanama City, Panama
Title: Good food but a bit rushed...
Review: Loved the spring rolls here but did not understand why the line was so long when the food was good but nothing over the moon. My waiter seemed to rush me through my food. Too crowded, which is why I give three stars. Based on just the food: 4 stars even though one of the dishes I wanted on the menu was gone.Show less

Author: Kenny K
Title: Over rated in the web
Review: OK food, reasonable price, better food can be found in Melaka

Author: Amybob AKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: okay food, nice owner, pricey, touristy, open til 5:30 pm ?!
Review: We went there two times in the evening until we saw the sign saying it was only open til 5:30 pm. Dont quite get that. Its a tourist area of the town and i think im not the only one who likes to eat this kind stuff for dinner. Anyway, we went there for lunch (or actually it was our breakfast at lunch-time) and had some appetizers which were quite good. Unfortunately they seated us completely alone in an upstairs room, which was kinda dull and the ordered kopi ais (iced coffee) didnt have enough ice in it, so i had to drink a kopi "neither-hot-nor-cold". Still, for (chinese) tourists who like the little extra bit attention by the uber-friendly owner and just want a litte afternoon snack, this is your place.Show less

Author: ASK84Singapore, Singapore
Title: Not as good as it used to be
Review: The quality of food isn't as good as it used to be. But my favourite is still the Spring Roll (Po Piah)! Although the quality of food isn't what is used to be, their Nonya Kuehs (pastries/cakes/puffs) are still as good as they were in the past! Show less

Author: MelindaL893
Title: Basic but good
Review: We are already fans of nonya food, and this didn't disappoint. The decor is a bit rubbish, but the food and friendly funny service is great

Author: love2cookandtravel
Title: return visit
Review: Visited almost 5 years ago and remembered how wonderful it was so returned this time and it was just as good as last time

Author: Fabian F
Title: Nice Food
Review: Good Food but a litle cramped. You must get used to the straight talking Nancy!

Author: ydd60Wollongong, Australia
Title: invigorating
Review: I am not overly fond of very hot food but the waiter helped us out with dishes that suited both my husband and myself. Tastes that I have never experienced before must be the Nonya that everyone raves about. Nancy's is rustic yet clean. Busy but with fabulous personal service and so reasonably priced.Show less

Author: malawi
Title: Interesting food
Review: with some strong flavours, so be careful what you choose. Great place if you can get a table.

Author: CareFreeBlues
Title: Do  not miss
Review: Wonderful  try it. One of  our best meals all holiday , try the top hats and fresh  veg spring rolls. Great for  meat eaters and vegetarians

Author: AmanduhlSingapore, Singapore
Title: Disappointing
Review: I've been to Nancy's a couple of times with my family. This time around we were disappointed with the taste of the food. This is what we ordered: 1) Bakwan Kepiting - Where was the crab meat?2) Itek Tim - Tasted odd.3) Lemongrass chicken - appetizing4) Otak otak - Good. Very generous with the fish meat.5) Lemak Udang Nanas - Bland 6) Sweet potato leaf with belacan - The vegetable was slightly raw. It had a slight sour taste.7) The RM2 belacan - It was DIFFERENT from any that I've seen & tasted.Show less

Author: aungmy
Title: Want to go again
Review: Food is great and nice. Everythings is good. If we got times, want  to eat Nancy's Kitchen again. Thank you for all.

Author: Paul R
Title: Unpalatable and costly
Review:
My wife and I had very high expectations  when we wnt to this resturant. We expected authentic nyona/pernakan food but it was not worth our time and money. The food was sub-standard and over-priced.
I

Author: memoriezzSingapore, Singapore
Title: Can't get enough of Nancy's!
Review: Nancy's Kitchen is TERRIFIC! it was so good that we just polished off every plate and by the time we arrived for lunch over there, they have ran out of Kueh Pie Ti and oneh oneh! price is extremely reasonable. Do note that they are closed on Tuesday - we were severely disappointed when we went there and only saw closed doors on Tuesday (last day of trip!)Show less

Author: Serendipity20Kuala lumpur
Title: The kind of restaurant you expect when visiting a world heritage city
Review: Probably my best choice in Malaysia when looking for a authentic restaurant that keeps its original atmosphere. Being there you feel transported to a different time, back in the 1930s. Decoration, music, staff make you feel like in an old cafe. And what is best is that you won't be disappointed by the food, which is excellentShow less

Author: Kimba GHurstbridge, Australia
Title: Authentic nonya, home-style. Nom Nom
Review: We just ate there tonight and had a wonderful meal. The place was crowded, but upstairs there are two more dining rooms.We had the popiah, so delicious with small bits of crunchy pork belly and fresh coriander.The braised pork was so rich with flavour and the sauce was Delish. Our fav dish was the chicken with black nuts. Oh my goddess what a taste revelation. The nuts are filled with a paste that is unlike anything I have had before. Try it!The only poor dish was the kang kong (morning glory). Totally overcooked and bitter.Staff attentive and friendly, a warm vibe all around.Back for seconds tomorrow!Show less

Author: Aquagal44
Title: Had to Go Back Again!
Review: A re-visit the next day was a must and that is not an easy thing to do when you need to fit in so many recommended places to eat.  Great menu.  Great food. Yum!

Author: PaintcanMelbourne, Australia
Title: Oh my
Review: This restaurant was recommended to us by our hotel, we shared a table with some locals and joked with them about wanting to try everything on the menu. The food here is exquisite, I have eaten Nonya food many times before but this place is a stretch above the ordinary, everything was delicious. If we had stayed in Melaka longer I could have eaten here every night and maybe some lunchtimes as well!Show less

Author: AndyofLondon
Title: Avoid if vegetarian!
Review: Non veggies will enjoy the quality of the cooking; but veggies will struggle.

Author: eblissSingapore
Title: Great nonya food, a place you must try at least once.
Review: Service-wise, the small shop is too crowded and busy to provide 100% attention to each customer. The lady boss is not too friendly, maybe it's because she is busy.Hygiene-wise, two houseflies greeted us at our table and were our unwelcomed guests throughout the meal.We had a few dishes.Assam babi (assam pork) - very fatty meat, otherwise, deliciousFried rice with sambal belachan (local chilli) - spicy but tolerable, I find the prawns not too freshCincalok omelette (fermented shrimps omelette) - nice, fluffy with a unqiue tasteChicken candlenut - rich nonya dishChendol - better than the one from Jonker 88Will I be back? Yes, to try out other dishes.Show less

Author: ymmit
Title: The chendol was amazing
Review: you've gotta try it. the chendol was amazing. really really good. am I at 50 characters yet?

Author: st69com
Title: Not too bad. Worth visiting
Review: We went to the restaurant close to 12 noon, luckily no queue. Nice food, reminds me of my late mum's cooking. Saw a long queue after we finished our lunch. Try to go early to avoid the queue.

Author: Kimmozieto
Title: Good nyonya dumpling and popia
Review: This is a place where you can get good nyonya dumpling and popias. But it's a little expensive.

Author: lynst82
Title: Nice but the queue is long
Review: Very homely food - my dad especially love the curry chicken! But go early - we queued about an hour 0.0

Author: eightysixxxSingapore, Singapore
Title: Delicious Peranakan food at affordable prices.
Review: When in Melaka, you have to eat the Peranakan food. So I stopped in here for dinner with my partner just before the crowds arrived. We weren't hungry at all but this turned out to be a really incredible meal and we ate like we were famished.We looked at the menu and wanted to order everything but eventually settled for the small servings of Ayam Buah Keluak (Chicken Buah Keluak), Bak Assam (Pork Belly in Tamarind Sauce), Sayur Lodeh (Vegetables in Coconut Curry), and the Ngoh Hiang (Minced Pork Rolls in Beancurd Skin). We had all that with steamed rice, and ice lemon tea and lime juice with preserved plum. Everything was delicious. The first mouthful of Bak Assam was mindblowing. And the other dishes lived up to the expectations set by the Bak Assam. Portions were generous and the small servings were generally RM10 each for the main dishes with the appetisers being cheaper.Show less

Author: Liza W
Title: Dabel curry amazing
Review: The curries at Nancy's are delicious and really good value - and the popiah a must try!

Author: Blackheathbloke
Title: A must visit....
Review: ...one of the stalwarts of Melaka, I tried the Curry Puffs and was most impressed.

Author: AnnabelleLamKuala Lumpur
Title: Just an average restaurant
Review: Visited on 18/11 and had popiah, pork tamarind and the chicken nut (or something similar -recommended by the waiter). I have tasted better nyonya food than the ones served here. Hence I do not find this as good as what was raved around. However, the popiah is something that I would go for again. Service was mediocre as we were generally ignored most of the time or told to wait but waiter was very attentive towards bigger tables.Show less

Author: OngP
Title: Excellent Food
Review: Excelllent food but they close @ 9pm!!! Dinner time is at 5pm in Malacca!!!!??

Author: ELAINE KBoise, Idaho
Title: Small but charming
Review: We had lunch at Nancy's on a Monday. The day before they were packed when we walked by so we decided to wait. I'm glad we did. The first floor dining room is small but clean and charming. We tried the popiah which was nice because it was not fried. Also tried a pork dish which was yummy. Prices are very reasonable and service was great.Show less

Author: sofitemeCalifornia
Title: Good Nyonya Food in touristy area
Review: Noticed the long line the night before while dining at a nearby restaurant. Place is AC- a good respite from the hot crowded weekend market. Seating is limited in the shophouse restaurant. We were led upstairs to one of dining rooms. Place could use a little help in decorating-- there were hodgepodges of photos/ decors (including leftover Xmas and Chinese New Year). Staff is friendly and food came our fairly fast. We ordered: the young jackfruit curry, chicken candlenut, house pickles, Peranakan Curry Chicken.Show less

Author: Cassell28Warwick, United Kingdom
Title: Best food in Melacca
Review: Was a little worried when we were shown upsatirs and into a back room but all fears were allayed when the food arrived. The service was incredibly fast for Malaysia, under 20 minutes from ordering to arriving and we even got our drinks without having to chase staff. Poppiah, chicken candlenut all fantastic along with the other dishes sampled. Very highly recommended.Show less

Author: bahamassSingapore
Title: Disappointing food and service
Review: We used to like Nancy's kitchen, making it our first choice for dinners every time we visited Melaka twice yearly. However, this round was a disappointment both in the standard and quality of the food and the customer service. To begin with, we waited around in the kitchen/cash desk area for 15 minutes while the staff sorted out whether or not our reservation was to be honored. When our food finally arrived, it was a miserable portion (only 2 pieces of chicken in the Ayam Buah Keluak and a few measly slices of pork disguised by bean curd slices in the braised pork dish), given that the prices are quite steep for malaysian standards. Taste wise, it also seems that spices were in short supply as nothing really tasted authentic anymore. To make matters worse, there was a piece of rubber in the assam fish! When this was pointed out to a waiter, he promptly picked up the rubber and threw it on the floor, telling us that this must have been a piece of assam! We are not chefs, but we can certainly tell the difference between rubber and assam. The waiter later told us something like "Dun worry its not poisonous, I belanjah (treat) you rice lah". Incidentally, the rice was not on the house as promised either. Suffice to say we will not be going back there again.Show less

Author: btchristensenManila, Philippines
Title: Good Food, Definite Tourist Trap
Review: Nancy's Kitchen came recommended both by our hotel and our Lonely Planet for trying Nyonya food. We had their "top hat" appetizer, one of the chicken dishes, and the nyonya-style mixed vegetables, all of which were very good. Ambiance was minimal/nonexistent, and the primary decor was newspaper articles about the restaurant. The downstairs of the restaurant was packed, so we were sent up to a room upstairs that we had to ourselves. This meant, however, that the staff forgot about us after dropping off our food. We therefore decided to go elsewhere for dessert. Also, worth noting that you pay downstairs in the central kitchen area, rather than the server bringing your check.Show less

Author: dotnahSingapore
Title: Food ok ambience comfortable
Review: My family does not take to spicy food, so was glad that they had various choices of non-spicy dishes to choose from. The Kangkong garlic was very good, so is the tamarind prawn and the fish maw soup. The fried sotong was dissappointing as the flour batter too crumbly and you don't see much of the sotong.The ambience is comfortable with soft bangawang solo crooning in the background. While waiting you can go and buy some kueh and takeaway nonya goodies. One setback was the dripping aircon, which irritates the one sitting in that seat.Overall, the meal is passable, price reasonable, but not one I would seek out specially.Show less

Author: rosandjohnEngland
Title: Delicious, traditional food
Review: Luckily for us we needed to eat early to catch a plane, otherwise we might not have sampled the delicious dishes, particularly the chicken candlenut and pork with black nut (apparently from Indonesia). Even the fresh spring roll starter was adjusted to our taste! Family run, excellent service and a delightful way to finish our stay in Melaka.Show less

Author: Tiwari2509Singapore, Singapore
Title: "So-so"
Review: Visited here in Middle June 2010. Ordered some Asam Pedas, Ayam Buah Keluak & a few more dishes. We expected them to be spicy, as what is was supposed to be for Nyonya Cuisine's dishes. Food turned out to be just "so-so". Other restaurants in Taman Melaka Raya would probably be better.Show less

Author: EYeoSingapore, Singapore
Title: Overrated
Review: Dinner for two in Dec 2010. Pork Buah Keluak was not bad - I was told by a regular that it's better than their ayam buah keluak. The sweet potato leaves was too spicy, and the chicken curry they recommended was only so-so. Many flies bothering us as we ate. Overall, I wouldnt recommend this restaurant. The food was so-so, but we expected better given its reputation. Cost was about RM45 for two. You can get better food & value elsewhere.Show less

Author: Actuarial_MathSingapore
Title: Over-rated nonya food; not value for money. Give it a skip.
Review: The restaurant is very small and the decor is very old (if there is any decor to speak of in the first place). It's more like an air-con coffee shop.The dishes are very sweet. We thought the pork in black sauce is sweet. However, the asam curry chicken gravy tastes as sweet! It's as though the sweet taste is uniform throughout all her dishes. The difference is either is a little saltier (black sauce) or spicier (curry). However, I must say that the pork is very tender.The drinks are pathetic. Don't believe the waitress when she says the mango drink is made of real mango; it's not... it's very diluted syrup. I suspect it's the same for their ornage drink, etc.Price-wise, it's not exactly that cheap to dine here. It's definitely over-rated and not value for money.Give it a skip, and you won't miss anything about nonya food from this restaurant.Show less

Author: Father_of_3_kidsSingapore
Title: ok to us
Review: Overall, it was good for my family & relatives. The order taker was good, polite & patient. As we had kids with us, he took note that dishes ordered were not spicy. However, we still managed to order 3 dishes for adults only. Plain rice came in pot. Total of 10 costs us about RM120.Show less

Author: woody2310Mumbai, India
Title: Nancy's Nyonya Nights
Review: The cuisine which goes by the name of ‘Baba Nyonya’, comes from the happy merger between early Chinese settlers and their local Malay counterparts.If you are in Malaka, you absolutely need to sample the exotic and rare Nyonya cuisine, a delicate art perfected by Nancy's Kitchen , located mid-way through Jonker Street, in a narrow alley. If you can’t find it, just ask any local. The service is warm and the food is spectacular. Miss it and you miss Malaka.Show less

Author: NaggasanSingapore, Singapore
Title: Untidy, disorganized and run down eatery
Review: 26 Jun 09 @ 12pm - was our (family of 3) first visit to Nancy's Kitchen Restaurant. First impression - Outside, to one side of the entrance rested a popiah cart. This is where the popiah are made (not in the kitchen). Entering, the place looks rather run-down, disorganized and untidy. A small dinner area (probably can sit no more than 15 ppl) awaits diners. Walk through a door opening, diners would be greeted by all sorts of nyonya kueh-kueh (some placed on table and some in a cupboard (cupboard partially blocking the entrance and needed to be re-position). The cashier is also located at the same area. This area can be very congested during rush hour by paying diners as well as walk-in buyers selecting and choosing nyonya kueh-kueh. Go further in is the kitchen. Up a very steep stairs are two more dining rooms. Boxers of goods were laid along the walk-way causing it to be messy and untidy. Each room sits about 20+ ppl. Again, the rooms are run-down. Old round and beach-styled tables, chairs and squared-stools fill the rooms. We settled ourselves on a beach-styled table. The dishes:1. Sek Bak - Looks very impressive in the menu. This dish literally is pork in spicy black sauce but not at all spicy. The thin pork slices were so-so and tasted ordinary. Nothing special. In fact it tasted just like any kway-chap pork. Not a satisfied dish. 2. Ayam buah keluak - Our verdict is yet another so-so dish (we had tasted better from elsewhere).3. Ayam buah keras - definitely much better than Ayam buah keluak - highly recommended.4. Kangkong sambah belacan - very disappointed as the kangkong was 'old'. Not at all spicy and lacks the belacan aroma. 5. Popiah - Not too bad. 6. Lime & Sour plum juice - Ultra sweet! I added one full glass of water and it was still very sweet.Total cost about RM50+After reading many good reviews about the dishes, we were rather disappointed. However, the pricing was reasonable. Nancy's Kitchen Restaurant lacks the restaurant atmosphere, cleanliness and service. Old tables, chairs and stools needed to be replaced. This place is desperately in need of some renovation or new paint-work. The whole place needed seriously to be tidy-up and cleaning. Our verdict - An untidy, disorganized and run down eatery that serves nyonya dishes.Show less

Author: SunDownUnderSingapore, Singapore
Title: Good Local-Peranakan Food but...
Review: The waiter/greeter, a local gentleman, was friendly and provided helpful introduction to restaurant food. The local Peranakan food was good, worth the try and we enjoyed it. Total costs for the five-course lunch about RM80.My wife went behind the counter to speak to another staff to enquire about the local food seasonings in packet sachets that was on sale but this lady staff was rude & impatient to answer my wife's queries, that really make the trip there unpleasant...Show less

Author: toymakerltKuala Lumpur
Title: Authetic Peranakan food of Jonker Street Area
Review: Nancy's is so far my favorite restaurant in Melaka, for its great food and strategic location. As our hotel was just a street away from it, we stopped by in the morning (around 10:30am) to get some freshly made still hot kuih (traditional cake). Later in the night, we went to have dinner before heading back to hotel. (Remember to check if you plan to go in the night as it might not open sometimes). While most of the Peranakan restaurants are found in Melaka Raya (the other side of Melaka River), Nancy's make it possible for you to hang around and enjoy the heart of Melaka, the Jonker street area the whole day on foot alone.Worth to try include its aromatic and amazingly yummy kuih of all variety (some have to eat with kaya), Bak Chang (Meat Dumpling), Popiah with its special chilli sauce, and Bakso (Marinated Meat with spices). You could also bring home some bottled sauce as souvernir.No fancy decorations nor over-rated fame, Nancy's offers you great value for money and a amazing experience of taste bud.Show less

Author: MissBlue
Title: First night in Malaysia
Review: Nancy helped us order typical foods with typical flavors of Malaysia.  Everything was outstanding with spices and flavors that were perfect for our first meal in Malaysia.  We had 6 courses with beer and water for $27.  Highly recommend.

Author: Ginachan CHoi An, Vietnam
Title: ANTHONY HAS KEPT THE LEGACY OF AUNTY LEE
Review: My group of 6 were looking for good Peranakan food in Melaka and I remembered Aunty Lee from a long time ago (it is now run by Chef Anthony and his wife as Aunty lLee has passed away)We were very impressed at the food served which was authentic Peranakan and good portions at that. We especially enjoyed the Nyonya Fish, the Lime Chicken Curry, the Pai Tee, the ladies fingers. In fact, every dish was delicious!And prices were very reasonable. Unfortunately none of my group eat buah keluak and I could not try that. A must return the next time we go to Melaka.Show less

Author: ymt888Petaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: One of the best in Melaka
Review: My friend was raving about the Peranakan cuisine here, which is a family run restaurant since 1997. Their fish cili garam is highly recommended and a good choice. We also had bendi (okra) ulam, ayam limau purut and prawns. To finish off our meal, we had their cendol which came separately with thick fragrant gula melaka. It was the best gula melaka i ever had.Show less

Author: hidayahsazaliKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Average food and taste
Review: We come here all the way from KL after read a good review about this place. We ordered all small portion; Ikan Jehanak Asam Pedas, Prawn Sambal, Plain Omelette and Bendi Ulam. Our asam pedas end up very salty. The prawn is just ok ok but prawn size quite big. I think they using XL size. Ok fine. What i like the most is just their okra/bendi ulam. That’s all. I rather eat Asam Pedas at Kampung Baru which i think had better taste.. The cost for all these is RM 122.00 which i personally feel a bit pricey for lunchShow less

Author: BigDaddSouthwark, United Kingdom
Title: Very Good Nyonya Food!
Review: This was a pleasant discovery in a recent trip to Melaka. Located at the outskirts of the city is the family restaurant serving Malaysian Nyonya Food. Food was excellent and prices reasonable. Probably have to book over weekends as it is very popular with the locals.Show less

Author: Jo-AnnKYTan
Title: Simple lunch
Review: I did not expect the restaurant to be empty especially with such good reviews. Food was good. Ambience was simple. Friendly service. They have frozen food for sale too. We bought the curry beef home. Lovely.

Author: shahsampler
Title: Simple but super
Review: In the wonderful town of Melaka this is a simple homely restaurant. Had chicken limau purut, beef rending, mutton curry, daun keledek garlic and chai poh omelette. All plentyful and very reasonably priced.

Author: motiver2018Singapore, Singapore
Title: Below my expectation
Review: First dinner in Melaka after driving for three hours. Saw the reviews was good so drove there to try. We called Beef Rendang, Kueh Pie Tee, Chicken with Buah Kalak, Otah, egg omelette, and another soup dish with Chendol as dessert. The beef Rendang is good, the wetter curry version.The Curry chicken is palatable but only three pieces of buah kalak which is miserable. Otah is ok but cannot beats the Muar type. Chendol is below expectations although the gula melaka syrup is thick and sweet. Cost us almost RM$200 which is above average, cannot considered cheap.Show less

Author: kristym964Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Fantastic Dinner!!
Review: Recommended to us by a local, this restaurant has fantastic food. The staff helped us to select the dishes and recommended the number we would need to feed all of us. It was great to try a selection of different dishes and at such a good price. The food came out really quickly after ordering as well. We will definitely go back to this place again.Show less

Author: adrianlim1968Singapore, Singapore
Title: Really bad
Review: I have tasted Nancy’s and Makko’s and was asked to try this restaurant. Being a reviewer of food I can honestly warn everyone DO Not waste your money on this place. The food is terrible and does not have any umami in them. It feels like it was made by foreign workers and the food was salty and dry at times . First and last time for me. Saw the high ratings and wonder why? Show less

Author: APisME95
Title: Great spot off the beaten path!
Review: Delicious, authentic Nyonya food outside of town. Took a GrabCar about 15 mins. The staff was very friendly. Great spot if you’re looking for authentic, non-tourist food outside of town

Author: janelleyeo_
Title: Legit nonya food
Review: Good portions, really nice nonya food! chendol is okay, but good to order. Love thwir chin cha lok omelette and asam pedas! Generally, good place to go for nonya food!!

Author: pkchoon
Title: Sometimes Good sometimes Bad
Review: We ordered few dishes. I can't remember the dishes name...the fish is not so fresh..But I love the ice cendol. I think it's best Cendol that I had in Melaka.

Author: EittusSingapore, Singapore
Title: Pretty good Nyonya food
Review: I made a reservation but was slightly late. Texted them about it and they were very kind to reply and i have a table when we arrived. Good service. Portion is pretty decent. We had the beef rendang which I find that it is pretty well done. Not overly tenderize. The prawn on the other hand was just average. Sauce is nice but the prawn is not sweet and abit tasteless. Wouldn't recommend. Chap chye is pretty good and tasty. Ayam Goreng is tender inside and slightly crispy outside. It is quite nice. However, a little pink and bloody inside. I think it has potential that the other dishes might be much better. I will try again next time.Show less

Author: Happycookies
Title: Make bookings in advance
Review: Food is quite authentic, better than Nancy and Amy’s. Service can be better. It’s very popular so advance booking is recommended- if they don’t answer the phone, that’s because they are full.

Author: TomGuppySherborne, United Kingdom
Title: A good place for large groups
Review: My wife, daughter and I decided to walk to Aunty Lees as we were staying at a hotel nearby. On entry the room downstairs was packed with large groups enjoying shared dishes. We went upstairs and it was just as busy. A popular place! We got one of the only tables left. The menus had 'S, M and L' for sizes. I was hungry so we were going to order a medium or large. When we went to order the waitress said M 4-8 persons and S would be enough for 2-4 people. When we got the dish it had 4 chicken legs in. Enough for one per person if shared between 4. Can see how this would suit others wanting to share. Food was good quality and tasty. Just left feeling like there was not enough. Not overly cheap either for the amount you get. Show less

Author: JasonC7231
Title: Must Try!!! No regrets.
Review: This is the best Nyonya food in Melaka. Yhr food is very tasty & very flavourful. If you are a foodie, this is a great stop.Don't get me started on cendol! Cendol fans delight yourself with every mouthful here.Each small size main dish is price RM20 minimum. Upsize them if you are in the mood for more.Will be back for more, next trip.Ps: it is better than other Nyonya restaurants such as Nancy's Kitchen.Show less

Author: jennytgoSingapore, Singapore
Title: Authentic Nonya Food
Review: Recommended by a friend. It is not in town so you need to book a transport to bring you there. Do make a reservation as there are not many seats. Food is great and tasty. But personally prefer not so salty food. Only the chapchoy i find it salty. Price is reasonable. Service prompt. Show less

Author: Ramesh V
Title: Amazing food & excellent servicw
Review:
I had dinner with almost 100+ Kiwanis Club members on a Saturday and I have to say the food was amazing & we received excellent service. 

My personal favourite was Sambal Petai! 

I believe reservation is highly recommended.

Author: darlynnSingapore, Singapore
Title: Amazing balls! I came back to malacca just for this!
Review: Amazing food and it was so so delicious! Ponteh was good, pie tee was delicious, Assam udang, chap chye, Ayam goreng all are very yummy and we finished every grain of rice and gravy that we have on the table. Chendol was good too! Fresh santan, gula Melaka was not too sweet which is really great! It is just simple delicious, home-cooked food that won't fail. Just simple amaze balls!Show less

Author: ChongCYSingapore, Singapore
Title: Best Nyonya food
Review: Our phone call to book on day after Hari Raya was not successful so we went anyway but it could not accept in person bookings so we booked for the next day lunch. Food was delicious and delivered promptly. Best dishes - chicken buah keluak, garAm sambal fish, chincalok omelette with enough chinchalok, otah, prawns Assam. chap Chye was a little too sweet for me, chendol had insufficient red beans and ice slightly coarse. Don’t forget to buy their meat curry powder which was very fragrant and their bottled chincalok before leaving. And do book ahead!Show less

Author: Christopher L
Title: Very authentic yummy fresh old school peranakan food
Review: We ordered the chilli crispy fish + limau curry chicken + ladies fingers + salted vegetable duck soup + gula Melaka sago. The crispy fish and ladies fingers are my favourite! The gula Melaka sago is super yummy! There's free parking at a huge unpaved area after the restaurant onion the left turn. Show less

Author: FonglinMuar, Malaysia
Title: Buah keluak dish was just so so
Review: We reached the place around 1 pm. The guy who came to take our order was like hurrying us with our order. We had not made up our minds before he came again to ask what we want. When I asked for buah keluak prok ribs, he was stunned. Then we found out it was a halal restaurant where no pork is served. So we settled for buah keluak chicken and ladies fingers with spicy sauce. The ladies fingers dish was tasty but the buah keluak chicken was a disappointment. It just didn't have the taste. Sauce was a bit thick and the buah keluak itself tasted a bit out. We just didn't enjoy the food. The portion for 2 is also abit too much. We found out later that Aunty Lee has changed hands..Show less

Author: Mumseword
Title: Lots of Locals here!
Review:
We loved the fact that there were few tourists here, and the restaurant was filled with locals having family dinners. 
Authentic and yummy dinner!

Author: WongK1365
Title: Excellent tasty food experience
Review: Excellent food, fast service and friendly staff. Cincalok Omellette is good with a hint of sourish/salty anchovies. Fried fish with sambal belachan, mutton curry and bendi ulam were also ordered and were all very tasty.Another authentic nonya food outlet in Melaka. Shame on you Restaurant Suan for a horrible experience.Show less

Author: ongt2013Singapore, Singapore
Title: 2 day stop over from Genting
Review: 2nd visit, this time with friends and spouse for dinner. Didnt book in advance (Fri) but went ahead , reach there 6pm. The chendol (like my last review --GOOD)This time since we have 4pax, we ordered more dishes. Brinjal, ladies finger, ayam buah keluak, sambal kangkong and fried omelette with CINCALOK, finish off with ChendolLike Terminator said "I WILL BE BACK"Show less

Author: pingpingjoKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Decent Nyonya Food in Malacca
Review: A few dishes that stood out were the Ayam Limau Purut (the sour 'kick' from the lime is a nice twist to an otherwise thick gravy chicken curry), Bendi Ulam (the sambal on top of the steamed lady's fingers are really good) and Pai Tee was nicely presented too (instead of serving them readied, we were able to put them together ourselves with the condiments and Pai Tee shells separated). We ordered the Cincalok Omelette but it was a little too salty. Show less

Author: SLL36Petaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Dinner on Sunday
Review: Tried booking by WhatsApp earlier but said was too late. Despite coming early before 6pm. They put you in a corner. When saying you want to order. The old waiter rudely wave you away and ignores you. Food will be reviewed later but first impressions is snobbishShow less

Author: rlsh07Singapore
Title: Nice food.
Review: We ordered the following items 1) assam pedas MYR 40 around there. The texture of the fish is really nice. There was no bitter taste. The way they handle the fish is good too. We enjoy eating this dish 2) nonya chap chyeThis chap chye a bit too sweet for my liking but still it's okay. 3) cendol, not bad too. I suggest that you go to their online website to do reservation before going down.Show less

Author: dr_ganltSubang Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Flavorable Homecook Food
Review: We have a belated BD dinner for our good and close friend at Aunty Lee restaurant on 28 Oct 2017. We made reservation a week ahead. A small restaurant but well patronised due to the good food and reasonable price. The specially ordered fried noodle is nice (thanks to the owner). The stater pai ti, the deep fried fish with sambal, chicken curry, tau geh, prawns, sambal kangkong, fried grago eggs, salted vege chicken soup are well done and good to eat. The chengdor as dessert is nice. Cheers.Show less

Author: chrischoong007Penang Island, Malaysia
Title: So far the best in Melaka!
Review: I have tried many nyonya food restaurants in Melaka until I found Aunty Lee. We ordered a table full of the nyonya authentic dishes; chicken pongteh, chincaluk omelette, ikan gerangasam, udang masak lemak nenas, pai tee cups, purut ayam, chap chye, bendi salad and chendol. Just simple and tasty home cooked meal done the traditional way! Still the best in town.Show less

Author: Making_a_pointSingapore
Title: Tasty homecooked food
Review: We arrived Melaka on Mon evening. While on our way to Melaka, my friend tried to call many Peranakan restaurants and only to find out later that most Peranakan restaurants are closed either Monday or Tuesday. We are fortunate that Aunty Lee is opened on Monday.We had difficulties in located the restaurant. My friend called up and the manager was kind to come out to the main road to keep a lookout for us.The service staff are friendly and helpful in giving suggestions on the food we can try. We ordered a fish dish with chillies, 2 vegetables dishes (chap chye and stir fried sweet potato leaves, kueh pie tee and durian chendol to end our meal on a sweet note. The food portion was just right. We liked the kueh pie tee and the fish very much. The chendol was fresh but the durian was something we could do without.If you are looking for homecooked food, I would recommend that you try Aunty Lee.Show less

Author: QuatoKuatoSingapore
Title: Good food
Review: They serve authentic nyonya food. Very big portion so choose your dishes wisely or else you will end up having lots of leftovers. Slightly located out of the main melaka area. About 10 mins car ride from Jonker street. Price is slightly expensive compare to other nyonya restaurants i've eaten in melaka during the trip.Show less

Author: AkemiR9
Title: Nice ，but public day please come early or make reservations
Review:
local people introduced me to come here . 
nice food ，come early if u can or booking first，because the seat are limited .

Author: josephinec42
Title: Overrated and overpriced food
Review: Our family decided to have lunch at this restaurant due to its good reviews. It is stated in it's website that the last order would be at 240pm. Although we arrived at 220pm, much to our dismay, we were told it was already closed. Upon further enquire, no explanation was given other than it was closing time.But because of it's good reviews on TripAdvisor, we returned the next day for lunch. However, it was a disappointment lunch as the food was clearly overrated and overpriced. The Adam Pedas fish was not balanced and for a medium portion, it was highly overpriced. There was hardly any prawns in Tauhu Udang Tauchu. From all the dishes ordered, the kangkung belacan was one of the better dishes.Due to these disappointments, it is likely that we will not return.Show less

Author: JoshChuiSingapore, Singapore
Title: Fresh ingredients but taste not well balanced
Review: Ordered Ayam Buah Keluak, sweet potato leaves, tamarind prawns, lime juice and Chendol. The ingredients were very fresh but the dishes were either too salty or too sweet or sour. Lacking in balanced of favour. It is really home cooked food. Much better than the mass produced food in the other Melaka Raya restaurants. Show less

Author: nhenghouBukit Mertajam, Malaysia
Title: Family dinner
Review: Melaka Nyonya Food... since melaka already become a tourist spot, the food also cost higher... food is good! The enviroment can consider a bit noisy as the restaurant mostly packed with people. Make "Reservation" especially holiday seasons and weekend.Show less

Author: Happy832013
Title: Yummy yummy food!
Review: Loved their mutton redang, lemak pineapple prawns & mixed vege!  Just like what our Darling Mum used to cook! Also bought their gula Melaka & prawn crackers!

Author: niktancmClementi, Singapore
Title: Aunty Lee
Review: The place is quite cosy but the eating area downstairs wasn't very big. There was a big parking space nearby. My Friend brought us there and was told that the food standard has somewhat declined. Overall the food is alright.Show less

Author: DavidS24105Singapore
Title: Best Nyonya Restaurant in Malacca
Review: Been going to AL ( Aunty Lee ) for years since 2000's. Recently went there again, the food is still very good despite seeing newer faces. This is the best Nyonya restaurant you will ever find that is value for money. the last trip, i decide to give other restaurant a try, ended up being the biggest mistake. i went to 2 other restaurant ( near Mahkota Parade, dont want to mention name but if you are familiar with Malacca you will know). the price was expensive and the taste is not even close to nyonya cuisine. i did not even finish my food. for example the itik tim tasted like salt water , no kiam chye taste. the ayam buah keluak taste like i also cannot describe. ..it was terrible. on the last day i went back to AL. if you are going to AL, remember to grab the prawn cracker RM$3 ( where to find in SIngapore). i'd grab 20 to 30 packets of these when i am there. paiseh... no more left for others. you need advance booking and that means calling from singapore to book!!. i am serious, try to reach there at 1130-12pm , the off peak. anyway what is a little waiting time,,,after having drove 2 hours from SIngapore right??Show less

Author: winstonlawShah Alam, Malaysia
Title: Nice homecook dishes
Review: Price on the high side. They even charge for cincaluk although you only need to taste a bit. The sambal petai is good. Paitee is nice. But getting there from the city can be challenging as you have to travel along some dark roads.Show less

Author: l_xinyingBugis, Singapore
Title: Don't go there unless you have made a reservation!
Review: My family & i went there on 10/06/2017 & the staff was very rude & asked us to make reservation before we go to their restaurant! There are two empty tables but still he doesn't allow us to sit down.Will not go there anymore.Show less

Author: XavierLSY
Title: Nice restaurant
Review: This is a nice restaurant where you can have good baba nyonya food. Don't ever ask them which is the famous dish because they will say all food are nice. Indeed.. all food are nice

Author: archmageMelbourne, Australia
Title: Quaint Nyonya Restaurant
Review: Don't let its looks fool you. This place serves some seriously good and authentic nyonya food. Although the original owner no longer operates it, the food quality is still good. I recommend the ayam limau purut, probably one of the best curry chicken I know of. Others have stated the chap chai is a bit bland, I recommend you spice it up with their sambal belacan. Its a wonderful combination. Will definitely drop by again when I'm next in town.Show less

Author: MELAKABAGUSSingapore, Singapore
Title: Mediocre
Review: Restaurant a bit far from the town center, though the establishment has been around since 1999 or 1997 in the same location.There was not a queue at all, and the restaurant was only quarter full when we entered.Rice and fish was terrible, others mediocre at best. Not worth the long drive from town to this restaurant,Show less

Author: Kelly NSingapore
Title: So so food and staff quality should be improved
Review: Went there the first time and we don't really like the food and the staff turned us off. We had ordered 4 dishes and the standard is normal zhi char standard and acceptable. Just I found it is a bit oily and dishes not very warm. One thing we don't like is one male staff doesn't has good hygiene awareness. He also sits at the table beside us and facing us, watching us to eat. This makes us feel uneasy and he walked away when I questioned him (is there anything wrong, why are you watching us eat?). It is the most pricey meal we had on this trip. We won't be going back again as I preferred the other Nyoya "N" restaurant (based on service and food level).Show less

Author: blujasAmpang, Malaysia
Title: Authentic Nyonya dishes
Review: 14 of us had dinner here and ordered quite a wide variety of Nyonya dishes - from Nyonya fish to paku veggies, Babi pongteh, otak otak, grilled fish filled with homemade chilies etc. We had their cendol and sour sop drinks too and We absolutely love this place! It's patronized by locals and they have kept it low profile, which is great! But you still need to call for reservation to avoid disappointment! Show less

Author: StanleyGohMelaka, Malaysia
Title: Restoran Aunty Lee Only Operates from 1 shop in Ujong Pasir
Review: I was out for a ride along Jalan Merdeka, Melaka Raya, Melaka when I came across a restaurant named Restoran Aunty Le. I do not understand why the name is so similar ( in fact the Chinese name is identical) but just for the benefit of those who love the nyonya cuisine from Restoran Aunty Lee, Ujong Pasir, Melaka, please remember to tell your family & friends that the original Restoran Aunty Lee operates only in Ujong Pasir, Melaka and the similar sounding restaurant is in no way whatsoever related to them.Show less

Author: bactrulusSingapore, Singapore
Title: Reach early or be ready to queue
Review: Was there on a public holiday, luckily we were slightly earlier than the lunch crowd (around 11.30am), got a seat even though we did not make any reservations. Nice Nyonya food, although it tends to be a little salty. The curry chicken was the nicest I have ever tried though! The sauce is really good, with enough spice but not overwhelming.Show less

Author: ykh_malaysiaAmpang, Malaysia
Title: A hidden gem of authentic nyonya food
Review: My wife and I went there for lunch and it was full, with many more walking in. It is advisable to make a reservation ahead. The food is nyonya cooking, and the few dishes we tried is certainly good and delicious. The prices are a little higher than normal. Service is very friendly and efficient, and the food arrive quite fast.Show less

Author: danny6239
Title: Family trip to melaka
Review: Truly nyonya food, the potato chicken is supperb like grandma used to make. Everything else is exceptionly good, if you come on holiday season make sure you come an hour early as there will be que.Show less

Author: sonicblazerPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Great authentic food with big portion
Review: Food was authentic and cheap with large portion for S size order enough to cater 3 pax.The fragrance and spices used in Asam Lemak Prawns was delicious and memorable and Cili Garam was good!Recommended for people whom want an authentic dish which is not too commercialized.Price on top of that was worth for the portion given . Show less

Author: katiemagpie
Title: Great meal
