Title: Roti canai kayu arang.. Long wait
Review: Came here on school holiday and the places are jammed pack with lots of people, can imagine the for food to arrive at your table. Food taste is just average, the only unique part is how they prepare the food with wooden coal. If you have the patience to wait, then is worth visit the place.Show less

Author: RuffRussBirmingham, United Kingdom
Title: is it worth the fuss this roti canai kayu arang?
Review: Absolutely NOT! we decided to have our breakfast here to check what the hype was all about with this roti canai kayu arang. Service was slow as there was already a crowd of people ravenous waiting for their back-to-back orders. We tried the roti canai kayu arang which didn't taste any different than those you get from any stalls or mamak shops. The dhal looked thick but lack dhal flavour. It tasted more like 'kuah perasa dhal & kunyit'(dhal flavoured gravy with turmeric!). Nasi lemak sotong..the sambal was nothing outstanding, very thin in consistency and watery but not dissappointingly spicy. The meehoon soup ordered..well its just meehoon with some soup, lack of flavour as well. The satay perut and satay ayam was just about edible. Roti tampal dangdut..again, nothing fantastic. I would not be in a hurry to return to this place in the future. Was it memorable? Kind of, but in the least expected way.Show less

Author: Eddy412Kuala Terengganu, Terengganu, Malaysia
Title: Great breakfast location
Review: Roti canai a.k.a paratha is a common breakfast for Malaysian... The uniqueness of roti canai here is cooked on pan heat by firewood instead of modern gas stove.The roti nachos is the best taste like a pizza... just please be early.. the best time to arrive is around 7am. After that, especially on weekend or public holiday, you will hardly get seat.Beside roti nachos, try the sate daging there... yummy... must try. Their nasi lemak also best...Show less

Author: MuhammadA11583
Title: Traditional food with new concept
Review: Traditional roti canai cafe with new concept which using charcoal. Worth to try. Pack with people but be paitent & enjoy

Author: Nur S
Title: good roti canai with smoke from the charcoal
Review: new experience to have a roti canai with the charcoal smoke, their nasi lemak also taste good. it is crowd because it is good. Come early or everything will finish before their closing time.

Author: jacqui c
Title: Great Indian food
Review: My husband and I stopped for lunch. Fast service and great Indian food.Meal was very cheap. We had Chicken Briyani and Chicken Masala.

Author: Lootzemike
Title: Great Indian food at melaka
Review: To me I found this place much better than the other Indian eateries on the same road. They got great chicken masala and bru

Author: raven781Tokyo, Japan
Title: Average Indian Cuisine
Review: Located at Little India of Melaka competing nearby eatery like Selvam and Saravanna. People told me their Briyani is a most sought after dish but when I tasted it's merely so so only and nothing great about it. Evening tea breaks Currypuff, Vadai are piping hot and tasty well goes with Brewed Coffee.Show less

Author: monisa93Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Good food, reasonable price and not pushy.
Review: When you first reached the food court area, the workers from every stalls will try to persuade you to choose their stall. But don't worry, they're not pushy at all and won't curse at you if you don't pick their stall. Just tell them 'no' nicely and they'll move on with their life. Stall no. 2 has friendly workers and even shared with us the history of this Portuguese settlement. Service was fast. They'll serve you peanuts while waiting for your order to come but remember, they'll include the peanuts in your bills. Since we don't want to have heavy dinner, we only ordered Portuguese baked squids, brinjal, one white rice and one large beer. Total bill (including the peanuts LOL) was less than RM60.Show less

Author: Yi Fen T
Title: Affordable Portuguese Seafood Cuisine
Review: You wouldn’t go wrong with ordering dishes (with images) shown on the menu. We even ordered the Portuguese baked fish twice. It’s the cheapest and taste awesome seafood meal we ever had in Melaka.

Author: dr_ganlt
Title: Simply Good Food
Review: We have our Christmas Eve dinner at the Joan &  El Chico Restaurant. Nice sea breezs and nice crabs (we had burnt crabs to retain the nice crab meat flavour). The Curry Deval, Portuguese Brinjals and Garlic Prawns were marvelous.

Author: Primela RSingapore, Singapore
Title: Food by the coast
Review: A family run restaurant by the coast in the heart of the portuguese settlement. They were really proud of their heritage and even encouraged us to walk around to take a look at the settlement. There was a wide variety of food to choose from. Portuguese food is a must try. All the ingredients were fresh and the food was tasty. Their hospitality was the best, such friendly people. Would go there again for sure!Show less

Author: ilovetravelling123india
Title: Delicious Portuguese lunch
Review: I found the variety of food a bit less. We ordered prawns vegetables etc. Then we spotted live crabs and decided to order a butter garlic crab. To my complete surprise its was out of the world. So fresh, so delicious full of meat. The butter garlic sauce was finger licking good. Price wise i will say cheap. Totally value for money Show less

Author: Wendy A
Title: Awesome foods..
Review: Drop by for lunch before check in to our hotel earlier today.. omg.. Muliu brinjal, lady finger belancan sambal.. garlic butter prawns, ikan bakar.. chicken sambal.. very filling and tasty.. the muliu brinjal dish is very flavourful but not spicy.. I luv it..

Author: jessloylmKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: NOT Good
Review: Choose stall #2 among nine stalls, ordered Kangkung Belacan, Fish, Squid and ginger lala. Food disappointed taste especially fish, overcook and soft. No fish taste. Can't feel ginger lala with ginger taste also. Although stalls competitive among others, hope owner can improve their food and get return customer instead one time visit. Show less

Author: Christina G
Title: Not so good!
Review:
We ordered Chilli crab, kangkung belacan, butter chicken and baked fish. 

The food is tasteless and not worth. We did not enjoy the food. Not recommended. 

A  for garnishing  and F for the taste. Very disappointing.  

Price is reasonable.

Author: REX551Penang, Malaysia
Title: Great Seafood
Review: GPS Location : N2.18306 / E102.26635. (Stall # 2) Best time to be there is after 6pm. The stall owners are quite competitive in winning diners right from the car park itself. Do not get swayed. All you’ve got to do is ask for the menu and compare pricing based on what you have in mind. They will leave you alone once you've decided which stall to go for. What I noticed was that all stalls offer almost the same cuisine and dishes. Only the pricing and food quality sets them apart. This spot is a must try experience when you're in Melaka. I’d say the dishes are a fusion between Portuguese & Malaysian specialties. The seafood was fresh and affordable. I liked the Friend Sweet & Sour Siakap & Ginger lala..Show less

Author: JTCruz69
Title: Good Portuguese Food
Review: Went with a Church group. Had Fried Calamari, Chicken Devil Curry, Chicken Sweet in Sauce, Fried Prawns, Lala (mussels) , Mixed Vege, Baked Fish in Spicy Sauce..The baked Fish, Lala was the tops for me.. Overall satisfied..

Author: snodoniaGlasgow, United Kingdom
Title: Handsome, delicious, pretty
Review: The food was AMAZING. We had the clam rice noodles. They cooked it with lard and pork crackling and shallot oil. The salted egg yolk crabs were so fresh. Freshest I've ever had. Crabs were expensive at RM230 (about £38) for 1.6kg. everything else was a lot cheaper. The girl taking orders was gorgeous she could be a model.Show less

Author: David M
Title: Annual Chinese New Year Dinner
Review: There are two restaurants known for crabs. This place is simply looking and affordable. Try the salted egg crab. The Winter Melon soup is the house specialty. We have our annual family dinner past the first day of new year.

Author: Wong SBintulu, Malaysia
Title: Nice food!
Review: The location is not too far from Holiday Inn holidays.. is about 5km. However, the car parking is limited cause the restaurant is located beside the road. Ordered the 2 crab (about 1.2kg) cooked butter salt egg. It is really nice and tasty. Also order winter melon soup. The interesting part is soup cooked inside the winter-melon. Soup taste is great. However, the meat in soup tasteless.Show less

Author: maggieleeisme
Title: Zi Char Food!
Review:
Typical chinese food
Affordable
Crowded - usually after 7pm
Can call in reserve
Have to wait a while after order

Author: celynccySingapore, Singapore
Title: Waited an hour
Review: We walked 45 mins from Jonker Street. The order taker is owner daughter aka blur sotong, we had some communication breakdown, don’t expect for recommendation. We order 2 crab, cook in Marmite & Butter (they call as salted egg), food serve at least 45-60 mins later. The marmite taste like soy sauce; while the butter taste good. Crab is big in size and fresh with reasonable price RM88/kg (for xxl size). We paid RM138 for 2 crab. Although butter crab is good, but not worth to wait for an hour. Recommend for later dinner (after 8pm) as lesser ppl. Show less

Author: CasChen
Title: Seafood dinner
Review: Have a dinner on a rainy saturday night at this outdoor place.  The salted egg crab is firm and nice,  fish , pig stomach soup, melon soup,wine chicken and fried rice is good and has a tinge of grandma cooking

Author: Lil Ly cMalaysia
Title: Needs patience to savour the food
Review: Food is delicious especially the salted eggs version of any sotong, fish or crab. Another excellent dish is the claypot brinjal and chicken. Others are just average.Be prepared to wait for at least an hour during peak dinner time. Make a prior booking if you are not prepared to detour elsewhere for dinner. Prices have also gone up lately. Crab and fish items are really expensive!Show less

Author: ferrymulSingapore
Title: Average Chinese Seafood
Review: I was there after recommendation from a salon trip. The food is average. The place is not clean. The price though is quite easy on the pocket. But nevertheless, i will not return back due to hygiene reason, and there are many other options in melaka.Show less

Author: cxhopeSingapore, Singapore
Title: Best Salted Egg Crab!
Review: Possibly the best Salted Egg Crab we have tasted in Malaysia and Singapore! The Chye Poh Cod Fish is also amazing. This is somewhat off the beaten track in Malacca (just 10min drive from Jonker though), but it is well worth the visit for anyone looking for a good value seafood zhi char dinner!!Show less

Author: 254calvint
Title: Good food worth waiting for
Review: When u have time in malacca. And u have spare time to wait for your dinner. Pls come over to this family owned local seafood restaurant. They served good quality crab, few of theirs recommended dishes must try. ( mee Hoon)..To be frank, their food is only slightly above average. ( but is still better then lots of restaurants in malacca)..But what I like the most about this local restaurant, is that from day one till now the owner still does all the cooking by himself. ( nowadays, u could hardly find the owner still does the cooking every single days) should really support this local handsome cook. Two thumbs up!!Show less

Author: Daenvgiell
Title: Poor service
Review: Food is nice, especially the nyonya fish. But service is horrible. Ignorant waiters and waitresses. Waiting time is horrendously long.

Author: EnZZZoSingapore, Singapore
Title: average tze char
Review: Hmm... heard from locals that this place is awesome so we had very high expectation. It's your typical local tze char store. We ordered their recommended popular dish and waited 20 mins before been served. Well, it's not bad but not outstanding. Nothing worth for me to return actually. Show less

Author: Amanda P
Title: Seafood
Review: Here for their famous butter salted egg crab. Super yummy and creamy. Be sure to come early around dinner time. Good food need to wait.

Author: PYTan8Melaka, Malaysia
Title: Awesome food
Review: A must try if you come to Melaka for holiday especially the butter milk salted egg crab, salted egg squid and nyonya chicken.Would definitely come and have my dinner here at least once a month.Food are reasonably priced except for the crabs which is slightly expensive but other than that it's cheap.Definitely recommended!!Show less

Author: CristalglaceSingapore, Singapore
Title: Superb meal
Review: Heard the black pepper and chili crabs are nice. Unfortunately, they didn't cater any crabs that day :( Love the signature fried beehoon and pig stomach soup so much. And the herbal soup is served in a wintermelon. How creative. You may also call to make reservation and order in advance. Check out my post here for more review: http://cristalglace.blogspot.sg/2013/04/melaka-trip-day-1.htmlShow less

Author: Ursula DLondon, United Kingdom
Title: Surprisingly good Thai food
Review: I was sceptical about eating in what looked a typical mall fast food restaurant, but after looking at the menu we decided to give it a try.A lot of customers were having a kind of steamboat meal, but we just wanted some fairly light and refreshing Thai food. We ordered mango salad, papaya salad, and spicy vegetable fried rice. We asked for it to be proper 'Thai spicy', and when our food arrived, we were delighted to find it was pretty hot and spicy, and very tasty, just as it would be in Thailand. We followed with some ice cream sundays.which were quite yummy.Service was quick and efficient. Most of the waiters were Nepali, ours spoke excellent English, and was extremely helpful and friendly. Full marks. Our expectatation were well exceeded, and we left the restaurant happy. And the bill was actually very reasonable, RM48 including tip.Show less

Author: Gregory WMankato, Minnesota
Title: Affordable Food, Below Average Service
Review: I had the $10.90 rinngit special-- Thai tea, tom yam soup, friend rice, ice cream. The soup was cold, but I was fine with that b/c it was too spicey for my tongue. The main course was okay and served with watered down tea. The best part of the meal was the ice cream. The service was mediocre at best, may be they don't care b/c an automatic 10% is added to your bill for service with the total coming to $12.70. I would rate them higher if the waiter showed some interest and also came to check-in with me. Sadly, this was not the case. The place is clean.Show less

Author: faraorkededek
Title: THE SERVICE QUITE SLOW
Review: Maybe because not much people eating or management problem the service not as smooth as other johhnys chain elsewhere.

Author: zunnur
Title: statisfied with food choices
Review: I kinda like the set menu that were offered to us.  for the price we paid, we had the  main course, drinks & desserts.

Author: Ain A
Title: Bad experience
Review: I had test a few times at this place..very bad service and tomyam sup flavour compare to other branch tasty so horrible.

Author: Khairos
Title: Steamboat
Review: Nice place to visit if you like steamboat. Waiters are friendly and helpful. Just don't order from the ala-carte section, they will usually arrive late. Overall and enjoyable experience.

Author: Mohd CSingapore
Title: Comfortable steam boat restaurant
Review: Marketed as Thai steam boat, what sets this restaurant apart is their chilli dip. With strong presence of coriander and tamarind, it is appetising but not for everyone. They also serves a range of ala carte menu of fried rice, fried noodle, soup, rice and dish, etc.Show less

Author: Weepau
Title: Healthy and tasty
Review: My family visited Malacca just a few days ago and we tried this restaurant after reading the positive reviews. Good as a light meal with tasty soup and chicken balls. Fish glue, beef and vegetables were fresh. We ordered the chicken soup base and had no regrets as the ingredients we ordered ala-carte make a wholesome soup but yet healthy. We ordered 2 servings of the yummy BBQ chicken wings. We love the food though was quite sceptical of the quality in the beginning. The ambience is not fanciful and there were houseflies on every table on a weekday afternoon. Will eat at this restaurant again before indulging in other more sinful food in our next trip. We left happy and guilt-free after the meal.Show less

Author: Chiara_sgSingapore, Singapore
Title: Good Service and spicy food
Review: I had a quick lunch there before departure Malacca, I ordered the Lunch Set with only RM12.90 with Pineapple Fried and ice green tea and mini Tom Yum Soup and a scoop of ice cream, good price for a restaurant in Malacca. Their service is good, the staff is very attentive. I will come again my next visit to Malacca.Show less

Author: MarinaMohsein
Title: never fail us
Review: when we can't decide where to eat. we  always decide have dinner here. good tom yam soup and helpful staff.

Author: limessgy
Title: Fast Service
Review: The service was good and did not wait long for the food. The place was clean and the staff attentive.

Author: BeautyliciousbabeKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Love It
Review: From tasting the food in Johnny Restaurant,it is the best steamboat i have ever had in my life.I enjoyed it alot.Their suki sauce was the best.Their food is not preservative at all.It tasted like heaven.If u haven't try it,u should.That is my favourite shop and it will always be.Love you Johnny Restaurant...Show less

Author: Andrew BBangkok, Thailand
Title: "give it a miss"
Review: Dined in this fast food restaurant with three friends ordering six different dishes. The restaurant incidentally does not serve alcohol. We did not order the "steamboat " which may have been a mistake. Several of the dishes were lukewarm the rice was cold and all the food pretty unappetising. The only advice I would give is "give it a miss".Show less

Author: soemr
Title: Good steamboat food
Review: We enjoyed our steamboat meal in this restaurant. They offered 2 types of soup base, chicken and tom yam. Their chicken soup base is delicious and steamboat platter choices are also quite good.

Author: Tina L
Title: Nice food at affordable price
Review: They have several outlets in Malaysia. The two places we frequently visit Is in Kuala Lumpur and In Malacca. Must try is their fish noodle, their fried rice and chicken wings is yummy too. We usually order ala carte instead of the set meal.

Author: aroelpeterpan
Title: Reasonably priced. Nothing much to hype about.
Review:
Ala-carte choice is limited as the staff promotes their steamboat menu.

Very slow service. And waitress gave wrong info about food item. End up got to wait again to reorder...

Food taste ok only and gets cold quick.

Author: Ylimeylime
Title: Average
Review: It is a nice place to have meals here but is not advisable for ppl who bring along kids

Author: cttclaire
Title: Franchise restaurant
Review: It's a franchise Thai food restaurant. Not so special.

Author: anggia_ratriJakarta, Indonesia
Title: My Shabu Addict
Review: I used 2 eat at Johnny restaurant inside of Sungei Wang at Bukit Bintang..They were so damn great!!!I am their biggest fans..Every day i always eat there..Yes,every day!! (While i was in KL off course)They do have a great and fresh shabu2 stuff..Especially the suki sauce...The vegetables are fresh..The meat balls just made when u order..The bean curd is great!!The waiter and the waitress so friendly..The price is excellent! U must try it!!!I LOVE IT A LOT!!!!Show less

Author: foto_melakaMelaka, Malaysia
Title: Fresh Food
Review: If you fancy food with fresh ingredients, namely vegetable, than you should head over to Johnny's Restaurant. Featuring Thai steamboat meals, this is indeed a perfect restaurant for family and friends.The steamboat meal is considered as a healthy meal as the food are not fried with grease but is cooked by dipping it in a pot of boiling water. And this is done on your very table. How's that for cooking and eating your own meal at a restaurant.One thing I like best is the special spicy and exotic dip sauce is catered for local tastes and the steamboat items are dipped in this irresistible sauce which leaves you longing for more. Simply magnificent.Other than Thai steamboat, there are also a wide variety of Thai cuisine here. Each is bound to capture your taste bud.Show less

Author: Best127
Title: Good Service
Review: We are pleased with the good and speedy service at this restaurant. Special mention to their ginger dipping sauce and fishballs soup other than their worthy portions of chicken rice. Suitable for family dining.

Author: raven781Tokyo, Japan
Title: Good Nyonya Laksa
Review: Had lunch today at Hainamko in Malim Jaya and I've ordered today's special which is the Nyonya Laksa and my other friends had Chicken Rice. The noodle was tastier ever with required condiments and portion size. The environment was better good air conditioned and breezing wind from outside hence creates good vibes to have these meals in Malim enclosure. Show less

Author: Enick_KayKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Average lunch experience with sub par quality food
Review: This place was touted to be one of the best based on online recommendation, However we did not find this place up to mark. The chicken served was cold. The rice ball also was not tasty. The soy sauce provided was diluted (almost watery). The chili place served was average.Show less

Author: MkV28Malaysia
Title: I frequent this place.
Review: the lady at the counter is always with a funeral face. Very Bad vib. Can the owner teach her to be friendly or take a class on the importance of smiling. She looks like been forced to work... even when the restaurant is not crowded she has this slucky face... Pls teach her. There's one more a bit friendly.Show less

Author: uw0tm8Auckland, New Zealand
Title: Food isn't bad, but good be better
Review: Chicken rice set was good, but nothing spectacular. The rice was fragrant, however it was a little bit under. Chicken was steamed nicely and flavour was OK. The chilli however was very good. Chee chong fan was good, and the chilli paste fish was great. Fish was cooked rather nicely. Would come back in the future.Show less

Author: Kyong1977
Title: Weekday trip in Malacca
Review:
Hi all,

Food is delicious & many choices of food like Assam fish head but too early to try it now & will come again for sure as just 2& half hours drive from mine house.

Regards
Yong

Author: ConundrumMiaoKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Average chicken rice
Review: Steamed chicken - average steamed chickenRoasted chicken - fragrantRice ball - too mushy, nothing specialRice - al dente rice and fragrantChilli sauce - watery and nothing muchService - they forgotten our drink despite we only ordered 1 drink and fairly emptyShow less

Author: Weemeister
Title: Halal chicken rice
Review: We were actually on the way to Farmosa (Bendahara branch) when we walked by Hainamko n decided to give it a try. We ordered.... what else but the CR balls n steamed chicken. I preferred the rice to the one at Ee Jee Ban (melaka raya) n the chicken too, as a matter of fact. Tho both were tender, this one was less fatty n thin-skinned. Makes a difference if you enjoy chicken skin like I do! N the sauce was tastier versus EJB's blander version - personal preference.The chilli was better too - spicier. Generally, it's not exceptional but not bad either. The staff were friendly and nice.Show less

Author: FEtravellorIncheon, South Korea
Title: Unique small rice balls
Review: This restaurant set in an old typical Malaccan Peranakan House has a good ambience. It's not difficult to find the place but if you are not a local and it's your first time in Malacca, it will take a bit of time finding it as it is located away from the main tourist attractions. There are some hotels nearby, so if you are staying in one of those, you might see it.I ordered a fried fish and a set meal with 5 small rice balls and a plate of roasted chicken. I did not order any beverage as I had diabetes and had to avoid soft drinks and coffee (in Malaysia, coffee is VERY sweet). So I asked for plain water, and they charged me 70 sens for "sky juice".What makes this Hainanese chicken rice famous is that they roll the rice into a ball. The rice is supposed to be flavoured but I found those sold in Kuala Lumpur and Singapore to be better although theirs do not come in the form of a small ball. The chilli was good but not exceptional as it was the way all the Hainanese Chicken Rice stalls do their chilli. I found eating the rice with the chilli to be more enjoyable than eating the rice without it. And with also some ginger/garlic.All in all, the food did not really wow me, but because Malacca does not have that many people selling this dish, so it's where you go, if you want to eat Hainanese Chicken Rice. The other one is on Jonker Street.Show less

Author: 8twenty
Title: Is as Good and no queue
Review: This was as good i think minus the queue.. not necessary need to eat and queue under the hot sun. We had half kampung chicken and normal chicken and lots of rice ball!! Wouldnt mind coming back again~

Author: nel93Penang Island, Malaysia
Title: Good for Bendahara Branch, Bad for Malim Branch
Review: Hainamko of Jalan Bendahara, Melaka is a lovely place for chicken rice, with the friendly and approachable aunty being there. And most importantly they served great quality of chicken rice.Comparing to the one of Malim branch. The attendant is not so friendly, the food is disappointing. And what disguise most is they played with the bowl just seconds before putting the ice kacang materials in and served the bowl of ice kacang to the customer.Show less

Author: Thiagaraj N
Title: Family holiday trip
Review:
One of the very good halal food is served here.
Tourist who drop by to have a breakfast or lunch will have a tasteful food here.

Author: X4842AYdavidkHampton, Australia
Title: Very tasty roast chicken rice
Review: We had the half a roasted chicken serve and two bowls of rice which was plenty. Chicken was very good, tender and flavoursome. Rice was also very good, although not the best I have ever had. Broth was nice, the accompanying chilli sauce could have been a bit spicier and the ginger and shallot sauce was good without being brilliant. We had missed breakfast which may have influenced our opinion somewhat but overall we enjoyed the meal. Didn't eat chicken rice in Jonker Street so can't make comparisons but I suspect this restaurant would hold up pretty well and perhaps better as some others have suggested.Show less

Author: CHRISLL8Singapore, Singapore
Title: Really disappointing customer experience
Review: We went in ard 11am and we were the only tables that are occupied. Service is excruciating slow & inefficient. Forgotten our orders and waited 15 mins for our chopped chicken and our rice went cold. Fishball is extremely salty ....Only saving grace is the chicken was succulent and delicious kaya toast - suspect they add Gula Melaka in itShow less

Author: roryjdoyle
Title: Famous chicken rice joint
Review: Famous chicken rice joint. Open for many years. Specialises is all things chicken and rice. Cash only

Author: chle0ng
Title: Better than Jonker St. ones....
Review:
The chicken was tender and juicy, the rice was not so oily with great fragrance.

Recommended - also to avoid queues and crowds at Jonker Walk.

Author: Liam K
Title: Ball Chicken Rice with no sweat
Review:
Easy to park, good seating, clean restaurant. Recomended to all specially tourist from outstation.
Try this place and avoid rushing to the clasical chicken Ball restaurant

Author: Zenheart
Title: Overrated Fare!
Review: We were recommended by some friends to give this restaurant a try. We came with high expectations but were sorely disappointed. The chicken was more salty in taste than flavourful. It lacked the flavour expected and we suspect sesame oil was the missing condiment. The soup was bland and had a strange taste. The chicken rice was also not flavorful. Did they leave out the pandan leaves? The chicken nuggets were nothing to shout about. We tried the special coffee and we were again disappointed by the brew. The fare is much overrated in our view. There are other chicken rice outlets that offer better fare for our tastebuds. We don't think we will revisit when there are so many competitors in town.Show less

Author: 276JAMES
Title: Great food and reasonable price
Review: We ate here twice during our stay. We were happy with everything here - service, food, price. I recall we paid about 30-40 ringit for two people - meals and drinks.

Author: Yunos M
Title: Taste great and halal too!
Review: One of the friendliest hostess i ever met eventhough i am a solo diner. Take great length to explain every dish on the menu. The free range chicken (poached) was superb!. Nice and quiet ambience. You do not feel rushed to finish your meal. Ample parking space at the back of the buliding. The only drawback is the price is quite steep for such a small portion. Overall, satisfied!Show less

Author: Sumita CStockholm, Sweden
Title: Excellent Garden Chicken dish!
Review: We had just entered Melaka city and were ravenous. We chanced upon the charming Hainamko restaurant and decided to have chicken rice for lunch. We tried a variety of dishes such as the famous chicken rice ball but it was the good 'ol chicken rice which appealed the most. The highlight of our lunch was the Garden chicken - which was succulent, tender and delicately flavoured. It was absolutely delicious. We also tried out several vegetarian dishes such as the taugeh (sprouts) and it was excellent too. All in all, we had a fabulous meal and can't wait to go back. The service was excellent too - the hostess suggested what dishes we could try and it was just right for a family of 8; food was prompt and the entire experience was hassle-free. the only drawback is a lack of parking space - we were fortunate though to have found a slot just in front of the restaurant.Show less

Author: Lovehols71
Title: Very average...
Review: We were not really impressed by the Chicken Rice Balls here.  They were just ok. We expected something much more authentic since Melaka is very famous for it.  It is rather pricy too.

Author: Aussie_traveller63Mawson, Australia
Title: Melaka's best chicken rice balls
Review: Melaka is kind of famous for chicken rice / chicken rice balls and there are quite a few places you can try. Restoran Famosa (Jongker st) seems to be the busiest, but we tried both and Hainamko was easily our favourite. Its much quieter and the staff were more relaxed and friendly. Not only that, the food was nicer and better presented, and the price was cheaper. Plus their supersized cold drinks were very refreshing - i recommend the fresh lime juice.Show less

Author: Dan333_Malaysia
Title: Different but not necesssary better!
Review: Differently served compared to the traditional satay from other parts of Malaysia or Indonesia.I have to say, you can also eat the peanut sauce by itself.

Author: LS-LR-DK-WLKuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Good enough as a dining experience
Review: Thx for reading. Author: JoeMelaka
Title: Rude Service. Extremely unpleasant visit
Review: We basically reserved a table, well ahead of opening time. When we reached the place, the staffs saw us but ignored us and left us to write down our details and take our own temperature. Author: Wally-SingaporeSingapore, Singapore
Title: Surprisingly Good Food
Review: We were a group of 36 adults and 5 children. We found the Portuguese Eurasian cuisine prepared by Chef Ben to be very very good. Personally, I've been to to Melaka countless times and have yet to come a cross any other Portuguese Eurasian food better than those that we had ordered for lunch on the day day we dined hereSpecial mentioned for the Sambal Petai prawns and dabble.. Mmmm really good.Show less

Author: travelwhileyoucan2Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: My favourite fries ever 😋
Review: Big Ben’s food is well known in Melaka. I have been to events where my family has catered from his restaurant and yes, his food is delicious. In the background though, I have always heard many guests talking about his famous ‘Commando Chips’ but bcoz he didn’t serve it at the events I attended, I could only wonder why the fuss for this particular dish.At his stall at San Pedro’s feast last year, I saw it on the menu, gosh, it did look tantalising so I ordered a plate.Omg!! It was really delicious and we ended up ordering more and more!!Which Malaysian wouldn’t love crispy french fries covered in spicy anchovy sambal?? Now I know what the fuss is about Verdict: Definitely a must try!Show less
Restaurant: Big Ben's Restaurant Cafe & Cottage Industry

Author: BrvergTaiping, Malaysia
Title: Home Cooked Portuguese Food
Review: Big Ben Restaurant was previously located at Lim Kok Wing University Melaka Campus and now it has relocated to Taman Synn (old squash building).A hidden gem indeed. Authentic Malaccan-Portuegede food at a very reasonable price.Condusive environment and very friendly peopke. They're open every day from 5:30pm onearsda till 10:45pm and closed every Wednesdays.Show less
Restaurant: Big Ben's Restaurant Cafe & Cottage Industry

Author: GluhenMelaka, Malaysia
Title: A cozy place to relax and dine. Trully a hidden gem.
Review: This restaurant operated by an Eurasian known as Big Ben. It's situated inside Lim Kok Wing University and it's a hidden gem that is only known amongst the locals. A very cozy and peaceful place to have your dinner giving you a homey feel compared to those outside restaurant lots located at Portuguese Settlement parking (no headhunters to rush at you telling you to dine at their lot and can lead to a heated argument among themselves). Parking is situated directly outside of the university. Do tell the guard that you are here to eat at Big Ben and just walk till the end of the premise as it's located by the seaside in which you can catch the sea breeze and the stunning sunset. Price here are considerably cheal and affordable. Foods served here are Western (chicken chop, fish & chips, etc.), Asians (fried rice, wat tan hor @ flat noodles with egg gravy, etc.) and lastly local Eurasian foods such as Curry Debal, Portuguese style baked fish, etc). The local menus are different everyday except for Western. If you don't know what to eat, you can always ask him to recommend you and he will whipped out something out of the menu. Do call before coming as it's not open sometimes and do booking if you are coming in a group so that he can prepare the ingredients in advance. He also do buffet style for birthday parties, anniversaries and wedding dinners.Show less
Restaurant: Big Ben's Restaurant Cafe & Cottage Industry

Author: 21nazzaSingapore, Singapore
Title: Sumptuous authentic Portugese home-cooked meals
Review: This hidden gem is located inside the Limkokwing Institute and it is known only to the regulars, as there isn't any advertising boards of directions to this place. Upon entering the institute, walk straight to the back of the institute where the canteen is located and you won't miss this place. The chef and owner, Big Ben, is a very nice and accommodating person. Leave the food selections up to him if you feel adventurous or order your preference from the menu. Either way you will be greeted with a feast for the eyes and stomach. Located just beside the more famous eateries within the Portuguese Settlement, this place will much more kinder on your wallet. If you fancy any seafood i.e. crabs, stingray, etc. call in advance so that he could buy them. This is because the place is frequented by regulars and he is more famous for his home-cooked Portuguese food.Show less
Restaurant: Big Ben's Restaurant Cafe & Cottage Industry

Author: esquire838Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Yet another asam pedas outlet
Review: Asam Peas is a tangy soup dish synonymous with Melaka. Fish (skate, mackerel) and fish roe are favourites as do diced meat. At Lagenda, they offer seafood as a selection for this popular dish (different range of prices of course). Apart from asam pedas they serve other malaysian dishes if your dining buddy is not into this hot tangy soup. A few customers rate the dish as lacking in tang/zing but that’s this outlet’s style to cater for those who prefer milder sampling of this popular local dish rather than the super hot and thick soup. We rate it as one of the choices to vary the taste when in Melaka. We certainly can recommend those who want to sample this dish without risking the attack on the tongue and stomach. Service-wise, well.... I dare say its typical of Malaysian non fine dining outlets (you get affordability in return) save only for the rare few.Show less

Author: SomeonePhnomPenhPhnom Penh, Cambodia
Title: Traditional Kopitiam
Review: This open air shop, clearly around for generations, offers up a very simple breakfast of Kaya toast and perfectly done soft boiled eggs, along with Malay coffee or tea, typically for less than 6000 ringgit per person. (I have to admit some confusion on pricing having been charged different rates for the same meal on two visits, although one set of toast appeared to be smaller.) Surprisingly I had one of my best coffees here.... better than some hipster cafes! I specifically came for the house Kaya but the spread on the toast was so thin on the toast it was difficult to even taste. What was discernible was good. While I wouldn’t want a thick slather, the toast could certainly use a tad more of the spread so that it can be tasted. Overall, enjoyable, authentic, quick and tasty.Show less

It was a little bit sourish but pineapple always went well with pork for me.I also had the pork intestine satay which was very nice - only for those who like to eat innards.To wash down the satay on a hot humid day, i had a lovely cup of iced barley.The satay was RM0.80 a stick and you need to order a minimum of 10 sticks.Show less

Title: A Place to Gangout after Dinner

A big screen with video Chinese New Year songs. Decoration ready to usher Chinese New Year boost up the festive mood. No hot drinks are in the menu so I went for a beer. My wife had orange juice. The specialty here is the mini satay with pork, goat chicken meat and seafood like prawns, scalops and mushroom. We had pork followef by scalops and mushrooms and downed 3 more beers. Started kara-ok as more patrons came in. Quite a place to hangout. The boss and staff are friendly and the service is good. There are individusl rooms but need to spend minimun of RM500 to qualify. A place on our card for CNY outing. Cheers.Show less

Author: pearlyhuMelaka, Malaysia
Title: The place to have good food with reasonable price
Review: Our favorite place to have decent Western food with reasonable price in town. Their Chicken Maryland has enlightened my taste buds and given me a whole new definition of it. My favourite of course will be Vegemite charcoal pasta! Just order anything that hits you in the menu and also not forgetting to try out some of their specialty drinks! They serve a wide range of ciders. Last but not least, pick a dessert if you a have sweet tooth like me! I love their rum and raisin cake but you need to try your luck as they changes their dessert menu from time to time. Tried their banana heaven and feel that it's a little too sweet personally. You can taste it if your meal is prepared by people who has passion cooking it. "Good painting is like good cooking; it can be tasted, but not explained." Try it and you'll know.Show less

Author: K SSingapore
Title: As dishonest as it gets!
Review: My partner and I went to Lu Yeh Yen for late night supper on 8 Dec 2014. I had originally Intended to order a large salt baked crab but was told by the waitress they only had "average-sized" crabs (500 grams each) available. I thought of ordering two of those but was advised by my partner to try out one first. Feeling she would probably stop me from ordering a second crab even if the first one turned out to be good I requested the waitress to get us as big a crab as possible from their stock, something in the region of 700 grams if possible.To our great surprise the crab served to us was way smaller than expected - see the size of its shell relative to a chopstick in the picture posted. It certainly looked like it may even have weighed less than 500 grams prior to being cooked - I'm sure any seasoned crab eater could would concur. In addition to being small the flesh in both claws of this particular crab was 35-40% atrophied.The bigger surprise, more like shock, came when we received the bill (which for some reason had to be personally prepared by the lady boss even though there were many restaurant employees around). The price of the crab dish was stated as RM60!!! That's right, 60 ringgits for that tiny crab! When asked how they arrived at the price the waitress took the bill back to the cash counter and after some discussion with the lady boss returned to inform that crabs were priced at RM85 per kg (!!) and the one we had weighed 700 grams! When summoned to our table the lady boss reiterated what the waitress had said. When I told her the price per kg (for crabs served in Melaka seafood restaurants) mentioned in several food blogs was much lower than RM85, she insisted the price she set was already lower than those set by other restaurants and speculated that the prices I had read online pertained to smaller crabs (as if the one served to us wasn't small enough!) She went on to explain that crabs were priced according to the weight category they fell under, and that RM85 per kg was within the ballpark figure for medium-sized crabs, such as the one we were served.Sensing she wouldn't budge as far as price per kg goes, I turned her attention to the weight of the crab in question. I told her I ate crabs often enough to know how big a 700-gram crab ought to be, and that the one served to us was nowhere close to 700 grams. She insisted it was and said if I did not believe so I could check the weight of a similarly sized crab in their inventory for comparison.Taking up her challenge I followed her to the kitchen of the restaurant where there was a box of live crabs around. I pointed to one particular crab which I estimated to be around the size of the one we had (taking into consideration shrinkage after cooking) and asked her to weigh it. She objected and said that crab was smaller than the one served to us. She then went ahead to pick out a marginally bigger crab and insisted it was closer in size to the one we had. I told her the difference in size between the one I had pointed to and the one she picked was insignificant and requested her to weigh both crabs separately. True to expectation, the weight of each came up to within 2 grams of 500 grams. After I returned to rejoin my partner at the table it took the lady boss something like 7-8 minutes to revise the bill at the cash counter before bringing it to us. At one point we were wondering if she was perhaps trying to get hold of some thug to come by to take care of us :-) Anyway when the price of the crab dish was revised from RM60 to RM42, which was still a bomb to pay for such a tiny crab! The bill by the way was no more than a piece of unprinted notepad paper with everything written by hand. I got the lady boss to write the name of the restaurant (in chinese characters), the price per kg for crabs, the weight of the crab we had (she scribbled something that looks more like 52 g than 500 g). That the number 42 was written over the number 60 can be deduced from the revision of the total bill amount from 75 to 57.I should in closing point out that the two earlier reviews of this restaurant are fake. Choonfong wrote that the restaurant is "grand, newly constructed well-decorated". This is utter nonsense. Lu Yeh Yen is nothing more than a coffeeshop-style restaurant that's common throughout Malaysia. They are neither grand nor well-decorated. Carimakanman wrote that the "environment is stylish and cozy" and that it's air-conditioned. Both are untrue. I've taken the liberty of posting a picture of the restaurant from the blog "Carol's Life Journey" to back my words.Show less

Author: Kathleen YPuchong, Malaysia
Title: A Gem of Chinese Food!
Review: A beautiful eatery we stumbled upon while looking for Chinese food for dinner! While staying at Double Tree Hilton, we were searching for a memorable place for our elderly parents to enjoy their dinner as the lunch and dinner we had at well-rated restaurants didn't quite meet our expectations. He' Feng is located on the 43rd floor of Hatten Place and to our delight it was 1 floor below the popular Skydeck. When you enter the restaurant, don't forget to go out to their spacious balcony which gives you a splendid view of the sea. He' Feng serves dimsum for their morning and brunch. However, since we were not into dimsum for dinner, we had a good chat with their chef Ah Man and manager, Lilian at about 6 pm. They came up with an array of delicious food that met our palate, especially our parents by 7.30 pm. Amazing! There were sea-bass with their signature sauce, beancurd with fried spinach topping in pumpkin sauce, lightly stir fried baby romaine, tender chicken in mint and ginger, mixed vegetables with broccoli and winter melon soup with chicken cooked in young coconuts! Overall, the food tasted as good as it looked. The soup, though would I think taste much better if the chef had more time to prepare it. Nevertheless with the short time given to prepare our dinner, I must congratulate the very creative and talented chef. My family enjoyed our dinner immensely that night. I would highly recommend this restaurant to those who enjoy Chinese food in a lovely ambience while holidaying in Malacca.Show less

Author: terryvideo t
Title: Vietnamese Noodles
Review: This stall in a food court run by a Chinese-Vietnames couple. The stall is located at the entrance to the food court. Lots of parking at the back of the building. Sells great pork noodles, beef noodles, spring rolls. My favourite is the signature dish, Vietnamese Beef Noodles. Ronnie the chef says his noodles style from Hue, Central Vietnam. That's where his wife came from. Ronnie is a Malaysian Chinese but speaks fluent Vietnamese and English. His beef noodles is so different from any that I have eaten anywhere in Malaysia. He uses only Australian and New Zealand beef. His cooking style is such that the meat turns out tender and fresh, still reddish in colour. Beef is a meat which is difficult to cook. It will turn out like rubber if you don't know the right way of cooking. But Ronnie's beef is just mesmerising. This guy and his wife are champions with beef and their secret recipe of super appetising soup. Once you've eaten, you will keep coming back. Opens at 8am. Sometimes by 9am it's already sold out. But most weekends, stall still open at 10am. Don't come after 10am, cuz you'll most probably be seeing them cleaning up. They have been running their business for more than 10 years. They have a regular following from the locals. I am one of them. Venue: Rasa Sayang Food Paradise, Jalan Laksamana Cheng Ho (Jalan Panjang) Opposite Petronas.Beside ShellBusiness hours: Friday, Saturday, SundayOpening hours: From 8am (breakfast only)Show less

Review: Sorry but we were quite dissapointed by our dinner. I dislike fast-food but seriously kfc is better than this. I can't believe that the nice setting of this restaurant produces such lack of quality food.

Author: 249robjSanur, Indonesia
Title: Food - good! Service ...?
Review: We arrived hungry and in need of air conditioning. We wandered into Tappers where the friendly waitress served us. Upstairs however the waitress upstairs would hardly speak to us. Why? Fried Chicken Wings - very good. Tappers is fine for a quick snack Show less

Author: sheronleeMalacca, Malaysia
Title: Comfortable Cafe But Mediocre Food.
Review: The cafe is quite comfortable with nice view of the A'Famosa fort.However, the food needs lots of improvement. We ordered nasi lemak and salted egg spaghetti. The spaghetti tasted nice but the nasi lemak is a let down. The chicken rendang and rice are cold.  Show less

Author: Beet_snap
Title: Hidden gem in Melaka town
Review: Been here few times, I just found out they actually have a trip advisor page. This place is just distance walk near double tree hotel. Traditional Chinese teo chew dishes, porridge rice and noodle available. Suitable for dinner with family or chillin with friends during supper with beer available. Wow.Show less

Author: WeeWeiYang
Title: Simply nice
Review: Was over for a simple dinner along melaka raya 20. Tay"s porridge is a self ordered type whereby you tick on the menu and they will bring out the dishes for you. Food tasted good and is worth our visiit

Author: PieterS90
Title: One of the best Chinese Restaurants
Review: I’ve been in Malaysia for one week I am so impressed with the beautiful food. It was very recently priced my friend had fish and I have sweet-and-sour pork both dishes were delicious. Very quick service and very friendly.

Author: chiachiangSingapore, Singapore
Title: Excellent teochew porridge that opens until midnight
Review: This place is very close to doubletree Hilton so it’s far away from the Melaka river. Small size with less than 8 tables indoor and several more tables outdoor. The service is quick but can be friendlier. The baby octopus and braised pineapple with pork intestine and their signature steamed chicken are recommended. It’s really comfort food to eat with plain porridge. Definitely would return.Show less

Author: 8MikeMEdinburgh, United Kingdom
Title: How could it be this bad?
Review: We arrived early to mid evening. There were about 20 diners. My burger arrived, in true Malaysian style, before my wife's lamb chop. The cold fries were replaced without fuss. 5-10 minutes later my wife still has no food. We tell the excellent young waiter. He goes into the kitchen and returns immediately with her meal, which had clearly been forgotten about. It's stone cold. The waiter "voided" it from the bill. A strange choice of word which seems to be in common use in this restaurant. Amatuerish beyond beliefShow less

Author: dr_ganltSubang Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Western Food Outlet
Review: We have not eatern at the Windmill Station for many years. We had our dinner here for a change. The Lamb Chop is not too bad so is the barbecue chicken. The ambience is conducive and spacious restaurant. There is also a choice to dine in open air. Over price is acceptable.Show less

Author: amra172
Title: Has lots of choices
Review: The food was great with variety of choices include western and asian such As scramble eggs and nasi goreng. Portion quite huge. Nice ambience with kids n stroller.

Author: Adamm979Seremban, Malaysia
Title: Affordable western restaurant in town...
Review: Feel like having a little western meal.... for an affordable price... with a good environment and very good customer service.... This is the place.... This is not a place for fine diners who wish to have real steaks as its not a steakhouse.... but its more of a malaysian style of western fusion restaurant.... Food is tasty and worth every penny you pay.... The customer service is something which will bring you over for another visit... The owners might not be there (i don't know) but the staffs are very friendly and very well groomed and mannered.... Many more visits...? YOU BET...!!!Show less

Author: eyegloryBatu Berendam, Malaysia
Title: Good food at good price
Review: I have visited so frequently this western food restaurant. Usually there are many people at this restaurant. I guess they also find this place nice and affordable. The food taste is okay, although it may need some consistency. Dont worry to bring along old people who dont like western foods, since they also serve local foods. The food choices are varieties. This is also a nice place to organize a birthday party, as they can help organizing the surprise. The staffs were very helpful and the service was fast. Show less

Author: Lil Ly cMalaysia
Title: Simple and affordable
Review: I would frequent this place when I need a quick breakfast. Set breakfast with tea or coffee is under RM10/=. I would also recommend their continental meals like mee goreng which is simple but very delicious. If u are sitting inside the restaurant which is air con, choose a table away from the door. I can smell the cigarettes smoke seeping in through their wooden door into the cafe. The verandah are smoking area.Show less

Author: najimudeen
Title: The windmill Station
Review: The Windmill Station is a very good restaurant serves variety of food including East, West and local Malaysian dishes. Very tasty food at affordable price.

Author: syafiq3489
Title: Quite okay
Review: went to this restaurant with fmly. ordered western plus local food. western was quite okay, patayya fried rice and gold fish chop fried rice were delicious. however, tomato fried rice not suitable for my taste bcoz it was too sour.. otherwise, drink was delicious..

Author: suhanashohairi
Title: Quite okay
Review: Been here for dinner. The restaurant space is so comfortable for family with children. All order were on the table less than 15 minutes which is good.We ordered sirloin steak and grilled chicken. Sirloin steak was okey but the grilled chicken was like normal fried chicken. But with that price range, it's quite reasonable. We also ordered the fried rice and the taste is quite good.Show less

Author: happylinch
Title: Western food in reasonable price
Review: Arrived there quite late at night. I ordered fish and chips with hot lemon tea. My friends ordered package with soup. Taste wise not bad but not special. Average. Big portion for me. Reasonable price. And the good thing is they still serving though we arrive quite late.Show less

Author: mohzan hSeremban, Malaysia
Title: Western food and local delicacies.
Review: This review is for their branch outlet in Seremban, located at Seremban 2 infront of City Park. Easy free parking and open from 10am for breakfast and closes around 10pm . For Muslim , not to worry the restaurant is ' Halal ' with proper genuine certificate. Half of the staff / waiters are Muslim too. Chicken chop , steak , etc etc and also the normal local delicacies. First time I had chicken chop with ' nasi goreng / fried rice ' its ok / nice , but next time will stick to either western or local , you can't mixed them , the flavour does not jived. Service is good and price is reasonable. Place is clean and you can have a small gathering / party within the restaurant . Next trip to Malacca / Melaka, will definately visit their main restaurant.Show less

Author: Tr1x1eNg
Title: Slowwwwwwww service
Review: Was there for lunch to celebrate colleague's birthday. The food was nice but i wouldn't say the same for the service though. Another colleague said that service that day was faster than the other time they were there with 5-6 people.

Author: TFaizul
Title: Cozy place, affordable price
Review:
First time I went there for my dinner.  I was so surprised with the size of serving. For me consider big portion. 

They have another place at Jalan KLU 1, Kota Laksamana

Author: Ylimeylime
Title: Clean place
Review: Having food in a clean cooling place like this is advisable. Reasonable price & friendly waiter/waitress

Author: cttclaire
Title: Cheaper with voucher
Review: Normal western food restaurant. Cheaper with voucher. (can get the voucher from city explorer advertising magazine.)

Author: achique_rbh

Author: Timbermad

Author: ChepstowBobChepstow

Author: Jwalker6106Melaka, Malaysia

Review: Western and Asian Foods are available at here, A Place to hang out with family, friends or large group. They cater for Buffet dinner as well, Ideal place for those who is on budget price, The foods here is nice and at quite affordable price. BravoShow less

Author: Mike GPiscataway, New Jersey

The stall operation is disorganized - lots of staff but just messy n slow.Avoid plsShow less

Author: nel93

Title: Review

Author: onishi156

Author: Paik Ling HPetaling Jaya, Malaysia

Here's what we ordered:1) 2 crabs2) Baked fish3) 2 huge plates of fried rice4) Deepfried cuttlefish5) Sambal brinjal6) A chicken dish which I cannot remember the name but it is a house specialty.Best part is that ALL of the dishes were EXTREMELY TASTY!Show less

Author: mrss0malacca
Title: The best restaurant in the whole stretch at portuguese square !!
Review: Was a regular at Sea Terrace with my family as we heard that this restaurant is the best among the stretch of its other competitors. Had mud crabs cooked with cili sambal today with stir fried bean sprouts, baked otak otak and salted prawns. I tell you, the food is da bomb !! Crab was meaty together with the appetising sambal, the stir fried bean sprouts was one of the best that we ever tasted, baked otak otak has the right texture and the salted prawns were tender and succulent( a good change from the usual sambal prawns that we usually order as we can taste the fresh, natural and sweet taste of the sea. Washed it all down with hot cups of chinese tea. Definetely be back for many regular rounds in the future !!Show less

Author: jennylee3456Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
Title: Disappointing food.
Review: I visited this place last weekend and was disappointed with the food. Having frequented this restaurant for the last 28 years, I knew it wasn't the same. Looked around for the owner and was told he sold away his business. Well, definitely, way below the standard. Shall not be visiting it again. I guess tourists go there because of the reviews. A local portuguese friend told me to try Stall no. 4 or 5. If I do go, shall write a review on it. Good luck.Show less

Author: Pixel8Malaysia
Title: Reasonably priced fresh seafood by the sea is worth the visit
Review: Never mind the infamous touting of stall numbers, I guess we will never know how good the other places are. Walking from one end to the other end, looks like no. 1 and last restaurant are the busiest ones. But no.1 is the place we tried and never regret. The young skinny lady on this friday night was quite arrogant but at least she knows to recommend the signature dishes. RM80/kg for mud crabs seems heavy but the freshness and meaty big sizes will change your mind (min. is 2 crabs per portion). Tried the butter prawns (very fragrant), cuttlefish fritters (kids love it), ginger clams (so so), chicken wings (super), burnt with pepper crabs (fresh, meaty and lovely), steam kurau fish (friend couldn't take spicy so we missed the portugese baked, but nevertheless very meaty and tasty), mixed vege and beers ... all in RM270+. Happy burp !Show less

It was sunset, a Saturday night and bustling with customers. We ordered the Portugese Baked Fish, Squid and Eggplant Sambal, washed it down with some Tiger beer for a perfect meal in a real Melakan setting. Couldn't have been better. The staff even called us a taxi afterwards.Show less

Author: Bcda
Title: Best seafood stall at Portuguese Settlement.
Review: Used to recommend people here for dinner, Closed on tuesday, the rest of the day please come at 6.00pm to avoid crowd. The rest of the restaurants no people, they even used touts to tell you to go which stall but ecxept this Sea Terrace without using touts, people just come here automatically come here. Their most recommended food are, Mee Goreng, Baked Crab, Sweet & Sour Crab, Fried Fritters, Kangkung Belachan, fried chicken wing, Otak Otak, Steamfish, Steam Prawn & baked fish.The seafood very fresh in here. But make sure if you order Otak Otak please dont order the baked fish because they use the same type of gravy.Just order steam fish,Show less

Author: kennytan19Sicily, Italy
Title: Cheap and fresh seafood
Review: I purposely drove to Portuguese settlement for seafood. Ordered deep fried squid, salted crab, clam with ginger onion and a vege. Food is decent and it costs about 90 ringgit only. It's very cheap for a seafood dinner of 2. I can never get a similar seafood dinner in Singapore with the same amount of $$. Definitely will return to here next time.Show less

Author: chocolatoSingapore, Singapore
Title: The shrimps were succulent and sooooo fresh
Review: We travelled up to Malacca for the weekend. Went to a seafood restaurant Sea Terrace at the recommendation of a family member. It is THE place to go if you love seafood, we ordered the Black Pepper Shrimps and Black Pepper Crabs. The Shrimps were so fresh and succulent we ended up ordering a total of 3 rounds of it, the first 2 was a small order with about 7 pieces, we decided to place a large order the third time around, there were about 14 pieces. It is the BEST shrimps we have ever tasted. The location in simple, very casual dining. The best part of it, after dinner, you can take a stroll along the jetty which goes out into the sea. Ladies, do bring along a shawl for that stroll at night as it is extremely windy and can get very chilly. I highly recommend this restaurant for all to try although they have about 9 restaurants side by side as the standard of cleanliness is also very good, staff are friendly too. It is one of the few restaurants that draw the crowds so if you are going over a weekend, be prepared to wait for a table.Show less

Title: Very Good Chinese but beware the bus tours.
Review: Very good traditional Chinese fare with usual extensive menu. Best dishes: Steamed Chicken Hai Nam, Spare Ribs, Oat Prawns and Beancurd hot-plate. We found the service good but timing looks to be critical - this restaurant caters for Chinese a Korean bus tours so you need to get in as one tour finishes and before the next one arrives.Show less

Author: Mark TSingapore, Singapore
Title: Good Chinese food reasonably priced
Review: Restaurant caters to tour groups who arrive by the busloads.Very busy and noisy.Despite this they found us a table for 8 and a Hainanese woman recommended us some very good food. The fish which she claimed was caught by "pancing" ( in Malay meaning by rod and line) was unbelievably tender and fresh, we had it done "steamed" and it was magical. The "fusion" prawn cheese beehoon (rice vermicelli) was something we will come back for. Their "long rib" was another dish I would recommend. Prices were very reasonable, and value for money. Place was very noisy until the tour groups left. Wish they would partition up some rooms for non-tour group diners like us who appreciate good cooking in quieter surroundings.Show less

Author: Ronnie L
Title: Nice dinner for two
Review: It ain't easy in a Chinese restaurant to have dinner for two. However, the servings at Keng Dom of egg noodles, pork ribs in yam basket and deep fried squid in batter made a good simple dinner for the two of us. I would certainly order egg noodles again. The mee had a bite to it and the way the noodles were cooked made that a 4-star dish.Cooking squid is an art. I thought that the deep fried squid was a tiny fraction overdone which made it a trifle chewy. The yam pork ribs were fine.Overall, a pleasant dinner at normal restaurant prices.Show less

The suckling was an envious to many lunch patrons from other tables. Unfortunately, this place also served tourists. So it gets noisy at times. Still, highly recommend to go. Show less

Author: E1972LEkarenl

Review: Air-conditioned & cooling, clean & simple furnishing. Very good fried carrot cake, and some other chinese dishes. Recommend their BBQ noodle & fried horfun.

Author: HBLim
Title: A gem in Malacca for gourmet creative nanyang cuisines at affordable pricing
Review: I have had quite a number of meals at this gem, which is a stone throw from Silverscape/Elements Mall and about a 20-min walk from the Dataran Pahlawan Mall. Yee Bao Bao’s Chief Chef, formally from Singapore’s Tung Lok and Lei Garden, dishes out traditional Chinese/nanyang cuisines with creative twists. A rare find indeed in Malacca. Not only is the food served by YBB of good quality gourmet standard at affordable pricing, it is also deliciously authentic and yet unique, refined and yet not too bland or too over-powering in tastes. I particularly enjoyed its hand-made egg noodles topped with its signature barbecued honey pork belly done through sous vide cooking; its mix of mushrooms doused with black truffle oil source; and its own special take on the traditional sweet and sour pork dish. According to the Chief Chef, sous vide cooking is a recommended cooking method favoured by many Michelin restaurants. It is a French inspired cooking technique that utilises precise temperature control (at much lower than that normally used for traditional cooking) to deliver consistent quality results to the exact level of doneness desired. As no artificial colouring or additive is involved, sous vide cooking yields wholesome eating with the authentic taste retained.Show less

Author: Shilalas S

Author: Adam B
Title: Ayam cili set (Chicken set)
Review: The fried whole thigh is fresh out of the wok. Crispy outside and steaming smooth tender juicy inside! The tempe is freshly fried too! Delish.Now... to the superstar of this dish the sambal cili. Which is truly a labour of love towards cooking. Should take some time to prepare, cili is well cooked without any bitterness if u rush the process it will hangus. This reminds me of the chinese style dried sambal udang paste. It is spicy but not super spicy, keep the sambal on the side will let u control the heat level but i end up cleaning up my sambal... licin! I am counting the days for my next visit here.Thanks to qhalifah irwan Faiz and all the staffs.#foodhunt #melaka2015 #sedapdapdap Show less

Title: Ayam cili

Author: jaclynrosaChangi, Singapore

Author: jia_ying_jjMelaka, Malaysia

Author: artieqa
Title: Authentic, old recipe, value to money & consistent taste
Review: This restaurant was introduced by a local Malacca people; located just opposite the "viral" Asam Pedas Claypot. If you are looking for authentic, old fashioned asam pedas, come to this place. It was my 3rd time in few years, and the taste remains the same. Just ask the waiter the selection of asam pedas available that day, select your choice and you will get the selection of asam pedas comes with white rice set, salted egg & raw salad (it can be mixed local raw salad or just slices of fresh cucumber).My recommendation is Asam Pedas Tetel (beef meat that mix with tendon, slow cooked on long hours that makes it very tender); Asam Pedas Telur Ikan (fish egg); and 1 selection of fish dish either Pari(stingray), or any other available fish.The owner is second generation as I was told; and they kept the recipe as authentic as possible. I have tried many Asam Pedas dishes around Malacca everytime i visited this state before i come across this shop, since then i wont dare to change my asam pedas place. If you are a tourist, or just visiting around Bandar Hilir, Malacca, this is the perfect choice to go try the most authentic Asam Pedas. Ignore the fact that this shop is less people than opposite viral shop, just give it a try. Either you like it or not; if you don't like it, it is not because of the shop, it is because it doesn't suit your tastebud (if you are not familiar with Asam Pedas/ any Malaysian/South East Asian food.Shop open 6pm onwards every day. Suitable for early dinner.Show less

Author: BL_LeoPetaling Jaya, Malaysia
Title: Modern Peranakan Cuisine
Review: Modern Peranakan Cuisine - why modern? Because if one mention "Peranakan" and then posted on the dishes, he/she might get backlash from hardcore traditional Peranakan fans. This was what Chef Paul, the talented chef behind The KamCheng, told us as we took our seats. Breaking away from the conventional, they aim to tackle younger market by offering Peranakan food at a twist. A relatively new restaurant located in up and coming Kota Shahbandar in Melaka, we arrived just in time for lunch where Chef Paul Chia and his partner, Fabian Yong, were there to welcome us. Once all of us were seated, we were briefed on how they came up with this concept and started this restaurant. At the same time, I couldn't help but to admire all the efforts that they have put into this restaurant - it was tastefully designed and decorated. Our dishes were pre-planned by Chef Paul, and it was definitely more than we could take: ◾Tauhu Goreng RM8 - fried beancurd on a bed of julienne cucumber, fresh bean sprouts and topped with sweet & tangy peanut sauce ◾Ngoh Hiong RM14 - deep fried prawn & pork roulade with water chestnut, seasoned with five spiced powder (hence the name) wrapped in beancurd skin. ◾KamCheng Salad RM12 - basically a salad filled with chopped romaine, Japanese cucumber, garbanzo beans, cherry tomato, water chestnut, lotus root, crispy wantan skin in coriander vinaigrette dressing. I like the appetising dressing plus the crunchy elements while taking every spoon of the salad. ◾The Kam Cheng Ayam Panggang RM35 - juicy and lightly spices chicken, wood fired BBQ with brush of KamCheng syrup and served with KamCheng chilly sauce. I love the smoky taste of the poultry. ◾Babi Assam RM33 - woodfire grilled pork belly marinated in tamarind juice, served with garlic vinaigrette. Already good on its own, but the addition of the garlic vinaigrette somehow elevate the meat flavour. ◾The KamCheng beef rendang RM38 - 72 hours beef shin braised in traditional spices, fresh Kaffir and bay leaves coated with creamy coconut sauce. It got everyone raving on the texture of the meat. ◾Jenak Garam Assam RM33 - wild caught red snapper cutlet, poached in sour and spicy broth with pineapple slices, and lady finger topped with pink ginger flower ◾Kailan Dua Rasa RM15 - Chinese way stir fried kailan with garlic and crispy kailan floss topped with crispy pork lard ◾Udang Goreng Chilly Garam RM48 - fried fresh fresh prawns tossed in caramelised salted chilly garlic paste ◾Nasi lemak Bunga Telang RM3 - Cooked using real Bunga Telang that Chef Paul personally planted outside his restaurant and using his technique to achieve the uniform colour of the rice. I can eat this bowl of rice alone without any dish. Even their drinks had been given some thoughts: ◾The KamCheng RM13 - an original drink created by Chef Paul◾Honey Limau Kasturi RM8 - love the refreshing flavour of this drink. ◾Iced latte RM11 - sourcing a good roasted coffee bean from a reputable roastery. ◾Local Kopi and Teh - seriously, first time I listened on the meticulous details on how to prepare the drink.. impressed! Desserts:◾Sago Gula Melaka RM7 - all time classic Peranakan dessert, with KamCheng syrup and coconut milk. Again, the bunga telang works its magic by providing the dessert with vibrant blue colour. And it tasted as good as it looks too. ◾Tau Suan Pea Cake RM6 - secret recipe of must green pea cake baked to perfection with caramelised shallot. This is one unique dessert and we were treated with story on how Chef Paul came to create this dessert. And it tasted like tau sar peah too..Show less

Title: Good service !
Review:
Came for dinner with family!

Food was serve fast and delicious.
Restaurant was not busy. 
However, service staff was impeccable and attentive!

Author: TPCheSingapore, Singapore
Title: Lunch
Review: We ordered the chicken rice ball set that that being promoted by the Novetel hotel. It costs RM 18 . Unfortunately we were disappointed upon the first bite. The chicken meat were dry amd stuff. It tasted like chicken meat that had been been around for a few days. The chicken rice balls were not frangant. Show less

Author: tommomelbourneMelbourne, Australia
Title: Good breakfast and cheap lunch
Review: We had lunch upon arrival at Melaka at The Square Restaurant located in the lobby of the hotel.Be aware that the restaurant is Halal so no alcohol is served here. I was told to go to the pool bar if I wanted a drink. Later when I went to the pool bar there was no one in attendance, so not possible to get a drink of any type.I had the Nasi Goreng Meal which came with Chicken Satay (menu said Prawn Satay) and fried egg(no fried egg either) so meal did not match the description. Despite that I still enjoyed my meal which I asked the chef to spice up for me.My wife had the excellent value set menu of Mushroom Soup, Tandoori Salmon, Desert and a drink.The next morning we had the buffet breakfast here and whilst it did mainly have Malaysian options it was quite enjoyable.I especially enjoyed the Char Kuey Teow and Egg Station.Show less

Author: Bubblecat-USATarrytown, New York
Title: Sadly mediocre but with promise.
Review: The hotel is a little generic but clean and well situated for walking into the sights without being too close to the noisy night activities. Room was clean and modern but a little small and several things didn't work (tv, shower blind, safe). Dinner was excellent although the restaurant was close to entry but breakfast was appalling. Cold food limited choice and the bread and butter pudding sauce was off. I wish I could recommend but a good hotel is in the details and these need attention. Maybe our trip during CNY caught them at a bad time.Show less

Author: Ee Ling PSingapore, Singapore
Title: Western choices in Melaka in 4-star comfort but average food
Review: I experienced buffet breakfast there and 2 ala carte lunches and other than mornings, the place is practically deserted. Breakfast was average in terms of quantity and quality but I liked that they bake the pastries there on the spot. The brewed coffee was terrible though - they only allow guests to take from ready canisters and switched off the coffee machines. Ala carte lunches was passable but made a much better deal with my Accor Plus privilege @ 50%. We had burgers (okay), tenderloin (can be better), char kway teow (quite nice), tempura squid (not bad), satay (not bad) in total. A lunch for 2pax each time set us back about MYR80 without the Accor discount for a good amount of food - not a bad deal really. But service can be improved. One time I made an order with a staff, and another staff came over to me some time later to reconfirm if i wanted to order and double checking the item - I found out it was because the first person I spoke to did not understand english. I guess this reflects the real struggles of maintaining a brand reputation with local teams involved. A nice respite from the heat of the area nonetheless.Show less

Author: JeannieW26
Title: Good Array of Breakfast Items
Review: From continental to Asian food, The Square has a good spread of food for all during breakfast. The crossiants are yummy and the eggs are cooked in various ways - sunny side up, fried, soft boiled, hard boiled, scrambled, omelette etc.

Author: Stephen NJonzac, France
Title: No atmosphere, food indifferent
Review: The night I ate there I was the only customer in the restaurant, the atmosphere was non-existent.I ordered rack of lamb. Given I was the only customer, service can best be described as slow. The lamb was cooked as ordered, but it had not been cut into individual chops and the knife provided was blunt making it very difficult to eat. Impossible to ask for a sharp knife as the waitress had disappeared until it became time to pay.It was not possible to order any wine to go with the food as the hotel does not serve alcohol of any description, being halal, something I was unaware of at the time. Otherwise, I would probably gone to one of the restaurants nearby or another non-halal hotel.Show less

Author: Annac12026
Title: Disappointing Service Novetel
Review: We checked in the hotel room and there wasn’t a single towel in the bathroom. Upon calling house-keeping, the staff informed us that they have to wait for the towels to be returned by laundry and will be sent to my room at 7pm. We visited our nieces till past 1am. We returned to the room and there was no towels. Called house-keeping and they offered us only 1 bath towel till We insisted for 2. What kind of service is NOVOTEL offering? Rather disgraceful. We have travelled more than three quarter of the world and this hotel’s service has so much to improve. Novotel, u have a long way to go to improve.Show less

Author: vijayraffi
Title: Good Breakfast
Review: Great breakfast and friendly staff. Food selection was good and the staff was very helpful. They open from 6am to 10am. Try to come around 7.30am, after 7.30am the restaurant was a bit busy. Overall everything was good.

Author: josepho53Johor Bahru, Malaysia
Title: Christmas High Tea
Review: Booked the High Tea at The Square, Novotel Melaka as the price seems reasonable at RM45 nett per person. Senior Citizens and children eat at half price. The High Tea is from 12 noon to 4pm.The choices available was reasonable but not too extensive. Being a High Tea option, not too much food from the main meal courses which was a bit disappointing. There was fried noodles and steamed rice which can be accompanied with cuttlefish, cream muscles & prawns, sauté long beans, grilled sausages and vegetable pie. The Melaka laksa lacks in the taste, quite bland. There is also mushroom soup accompanied with assorted buns & butter as well as salad salads. The fruits, cakes and pastries was the attraction. Lots of variety and color. However again it could have been better. Drinks include coffee, tea, tea tarik and various concocted juices. Overall reasonable buffet at a very reasonable cost. Show less

Author: Yong M
Title: Nice breakfast spread
Review: Plenty of items for everyone. egg station need to queue a while as here is only 1 chef with 2 woks to cater to all.

Author: Evelyn S
Title: Good variety of salads and desserts
Review: Salads and their condiments were plentiful and many local and western desserts to choose from too.  However the meat and cooked vegetable dishes were few.

Author: AreWeSeeing
Title: Wide Spread
Review:
The spread was good. Can still improve in variety of Breads and fresh fruits...
Jam was nice.
Egg section had no meat
Chicken curry was too good.
Toaster needs to be replaced/cleaned

Author: Riptinder SIpoh, Malaysia
Title: An enigma ??
Review: As a member of the Accor Loyalty programme, it is very obvious that we would be availing the facilities at these properties as and when desired. However our experience at this two year old property Novotel Melaka has always been full of challenge/thrill and disappointment.The place is good, the staff are very friendly and the food is often tasty.But what has been enigmatic about our repeated visits has been that either the chef is not present to serve the item from the menu OR the particular dish is not available due to non-availability of the ingredients.As well, the time delay after ordering a dish is too much . If 2-3 dishes are ordered, each one is brought on table almost 20 minutes apart. Its beyond anyone's comprehension what is this service norm ?If three gusets have gone there, then each one either should eat it without others joining in OR let it get absolutely cold waiting for the other dishes to arrive.I would expect a revert from the Hotel Manager on this. I have talked to the chef as well as the F&B manager about it, they are extremely apologetic about it but seem to have no answer.
